# Combwork — Specification (v0.2)

Combwork (renamed in 1.1, HI-2458; this spec names the old name only where the upgrade converts it, §4.1.1 and §4.1.2) is a desktop app for AI-assisted ("vibe") coding. It looks and feels like a streamlined VS Code, but its centre of gravity is the **agent session**, not the text editor. It organises code into Workspaces and Projects, runs CLI agent sessions (Claude Code and Codex, up to twelve agents per active project by default, up to 24 by hand past its workflow's Maximum agents), and manages the skills, MCP servers and shared notes those sessions use.

This document is the source of truth for product decisions. Update it when decisions change.

---

## 1. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**
- Open or create a Workspace; list its Projects in a left-hand pane.
- Run Claude Code and Codex sessions per active Project in embedded terminals, several at once; each agent chooses its provider, so a project can mix them.
- Show per-session stats: tokens, cache use, compactions, estimated re-cache cost on resume.
- Review and edit the agent's memory for a project.
- Manage Combwork skills and MCP servers at workspace ("global") scope: skills with project-level opt-outs, MCP servers with a workspace switch and each project's own choice.
- Per-project model, effort and permission mode, with global defaults.
- Indicate session state (working / waiting / finished) with optional chime and desktop notifications.
- Review changes (git diff) made by the agent.
- Expose an Agent API (HTTP + built-in MCP server) so agents can interact with Combwork.
- Minimise and close to the system tray. Ship as a Windows installer.

**Non-goals (for now)**
- A full code editor. Monaco is used for notes, memory, skills and diffs.
- Providers beyond Claude Code and Codex. The provider framework (§10) is built for more; each needs its own adapter.
- Moving a conversation between providers. Work moves through a handover (**Hand Over to…**, §6.2).
- Automatic session restore. Resuming is always a user action.
- Cloud sync, accounts, multi-user. A remote skill repository is a future idea.

---

## 2. Technology

| Area | Choice |
|---|---|
| Shell | Electron, TypeScript throughout, built with electron-vite |
| UI | React + zustand, VS Code-style layout, `@vscode/codicons` |
| Terminal | `xterm.js` with its WebGL renderer (DOM fallback) + `node-pty` prebuilt (`@lydell/node-pty`, Windows ConPTY) |
| Editor / diff | Monaco (bundled locally, no CDN) |
| File watching | `chokidar` (the workspace's `.combwork`), Node's `fs.watch` (the workspace root, the Files tab) |
| File access (main) | Electron's `original-fs`: `.asar` files in projects are plain files, never opened as archives (#246) |
| Docs rendering | `marked` |
| Packaging | `electron-builder` (NSIS installer) |
| Tests | Vitest (unit, in CI) and Playwright `_electron` end-to-end suites (`tests/e2e`, local: they need the CLIs) |
| Checks | TypeScript, oxlint (`.oxlintrc.json`; typescript-eslint doesn't support TypeScript 7 yet), GitHub Actions on every push to `main` and on pull requests |

Process model: the **main process** owns the filesystem, ptys, hook server, Agent API and agent adapters. The **renderer** is UI only and talks to main through a typed preload bridge (`contextIsolation: true`, `sandbox: true`, no `nodeIntegration`).

**Windows** (like VS Code): one Combwork process, one window per workspace (or the welcome page). Settings, the tray, updates, the Agent API and file locks are shared; each window has its own workspace service. **File → New Window** (`window.new`, Ctrl+K Ctrl+N; VS Code's Ctrl+Shift+N is New Session in Combwork). Open Workspace (or Create Workspace) replaces the current window's workspace; if its agents are running, the quit dialog's *Switch workspace?* variant asks first (per **Confirm on quit**, like quitting and closing a window), then they are stopped. **File → Close Workspace** does the same (*Close this workspace?*) and stops every agent of every project in it, keeping the window open (its tooltip says so). Cancel leaves everything running; a workspace already open in another window brings that window forward instead, so one project is never in two windows. Closing a window that isn't the last stops its workspace's agents after the quit dialog's window variant (*Close this window?*, no "when agents finish"); the last window keeps the old behaviour (tray, or quit). **File → Close Window** (`window.close`, Ctrl+Shift+W, just above Exit; also in the palette) is the window's X: it calls `window:close`, which goes through the same close handler. Quitting covers every window; unsaved files are asked about in each window that has them. With several windows open, File → Exit reads **Exit Combwork (all windows)** (`Command.liveLabel`, from the window count main sends as `windows-changed` and `window:count`), and the quit dialog's title says it closes all N windows, its text that it stops the sessions in every workspace, and it lists the agents under their workspace's name (`QuitSession.workspace`), grouped by its full path (`workspacePath`, case-insensitive) so two workspaces with the same folder name stay apart: each of those also shows the fewest parent folders that tell them apart (`distinguishingParents`, `shared/folderLabels.ts`), and every heading has the full path on hover; a **Close this window only** row in its body (not the footer, which has no room beside Quit when agents finish; the footer wraps rather than overflow) answers quit choice `'window'`, which closes just the window showing the dialog through the Close Window path (`requestCloseWindow`), asking only about what that dialog didn't cover: from the main dialog nothing more (it listed the agents and dealt with the unsaved files); from the unsaved-files question asked first in another window, "Close this window?" about that window's agents, per Confirm on quit. It doesn't save "Don't ask again". A workspace can't be opened inside, or around, one another window shows (a project must belong to one workspace), nor by another name (an 8.3 short name, a junction) for one already open: Combwork compares workspaces by real path (#455); opening the window's own workspace, by any name, is no switch and changes nothing (`alreadyHere`): it is never closed and opened again, and while an open of it is under way (the restore at start) the request waits for that open and gives back its workspace, so what its passes were writing isn't cut off (HI-2141); an Agent API workspace name that two open workspaces share is refused (409) rather than guessed, and one named by its path (`X-Combwork-Workspace`, `?workspace=`) is found by place, under any of its names (`findWorkspace`, `placeMatcher`, #494). Stopping a window's agents also cancels agent starts still being prepared, and turning a provider off lists its agents in every window. The open windows (workspace, bounds) are saved in `config.json` `windows` and reopened at start when *Reopen last workspace* is on; a window opens fitted to the work area of the display it opens on (the one its saved corner is on, else the primary one, centred), so bounds saved on a larger display never run off a smaller one's edge, unless that display is smaller than the window's minimum (900 × 560), which wins (`placeOnDisplay` and `fitToWorkArea`, #812; the developer console's window too, #862); `lastWorkspace` stays the last focused window's for older versions. Events about a project, and its terminals' output, go to the window showing it; app-wide events (settings, updates, plan usage) to every window. **Always on Top**, per window (`main/pin.ts`): the title bar's pin (left of the window buttons, lit while on), **View → Always on Top** (`view.alwaysOnTop`, checked while on), the palette and Ctrl+Alt+O all call `window:setAlwaysOnTop` (`BrowserWindow.setAlwaysOnTop(true)`: above other apps, below system UI; no higher levels). It is remembered by workspace in `config.json` `alwaysOnTop` (lowercased paths), never in `.combwork` (a desk preference, not the workspace's): a window takes its workspace's pin when the workspace opens in it, at start too, and is off on the welcome page and for a workspace never pinned.

Robustness and safety rules:

- **Combwork's JSON files** (`project.json`, `config.json`…) are written to a temporary file and renamed into place, each write with its own temporary file, so a crash or two writes at once never leave a partial file. The files Combwork keeps (`config.json`, `workspace.json`, `project.json`) also get a `.bak` copy of the last good version with every save; a file that can't be read is read again for up to about a second while it is still changing (something outside Combwork saving it in place, which empties it and then writes it, #1598). One still changing after that second, or changed within the last 2 s (a program stalled half way through a save on a busy machine, #1601), is left as it is, nothing reported: that read uses the `.bak`'s settings (or defaults), the next read looks again, and a warning naming it goes to the log. A change Combwork reads such a file for and writes back (to `project.json`, the workspace's record of project names, or the record of whose each handover is, #1600) never uses the `.bak` that way, which would write over the other program's save once it finishes: it reads the file again up to three times in all, and then the change is refused, nothing written, with an error saying the file is being saved by something else (a handover whose owner can't be recorded isn't written either). A kept file that is there but can't be read at all (another program has it locked, access is refused, a disk error, HI-2414) is never taken for a new one: it is read again for up to about a second, and then a change read for (as above) is refused, nothing written, with an error saying the file couldn't be read (three tries in all); any other read uses its `.bak`'s settings (or defaults) for now, with a warning in the log. Settings Combwork keeps in memory and saves whole (`config.json`, a workspace's `workspace.json`) that were read that way (or got the `.bak`'s settings because the file was still being saved) are never saved over the file or its `.bak` while it is there, until a read for them gives them the file's own settings; a read that again gets the `.bak` or a default doesn't count, nor does another part of Combwork reading the file meanwhile, as neither changes what is kept. So a save can't replace settings Combwork never saw. Only a file that isn't there gets the defaults written as new. Only a file that can't be read, has stopped changing and was last changed at least 2 s before is set aside (so a save that stalls half way for more than 2 s can still be taken for damage) as `<file>.corrupt-<time>`, the `.bak` restored and the user told (or, with no good copy, defaults used and the user told), so a damaged file never silently turns into lost settings or session records. Read-modify-write changes to one project's `project.json` or its session records are serialised, so changes made at the same moment (two agents finishing together) are all kept.
- **Session IDs** from the renderer, the Agent API or the file system are checked (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) before they are used in a file name.
- **Starting an agent** is reserved before anything else happens, so two starts at once (a double click, or the UI and the Agent API) start it only once; the other is refused.
- **The window** only uses the clipboard; every other permission a page can ask for is refused, and a build's CSP allows no network connections. IPC calls are accepted only from Combwork's own top-level page (not an embedded preview). Paths from the window are checked against the workspace by their real location too (following links and junctions), for `file:read`/`file:write`, `combwork-img:` and shared notes.
- **Files the renderer may open** outside the workspace are limited to what Combwork shows from each provider's config folder: Claude Code's user `CLAUDE.md` and auto-memory files and Codex's user `AGENTS.md` (editable), and `SKILL.md` files (read-only), never credentials or settings.
- **The UI** catches errors per view: a failure in one tab or view shows a message there (**Try Again**, **Open Logs**) instead of blanking the window, and running sessions are unaffected.

Primary platform is Windows 11. Code avoids Windows-only assumptions where cheap.

---

## 3. Concepts

- **Workspace** — a folder that contains Projects. One workspace is open per window. Combwork remembers recent workspaces: the 12 last opened (`config.json` `recentWorkspaces`), in File → Open Recent and on the welcome page (#144). Each entry says whether its folder is there (checked whenever the list is shown, and when the welcome page's window comes back to the front; one that isn't is greyed, "not found", and kept, since a drive may come back) and whether another window has it open (choosing it brings that window forward). An entry can be removed (its ✕, or right-click → Remove from Recent), comparing paths without case; **Clear Recently Opened** (File → Open Recent, and the palette) asks, then keeps only the workspaces open in a window. Opening a missing one says it can't be found and offers Remove from Recent. Every change (opened, removed, cleared, a workspace closed) is sent to every window (`recent-changed`), which asks for its own view of the list (`workspace:recent`). The welcome page fits a narrow window (#265): its two columns stack when there's no room for both, and an entry's path shortens first, then its name if that alone is too wide (the tooltip has the path).
- **Moved workspaces** (#146, `main/workspaceMove.ts`, paths in `shared/movePaths.ts`). Combwork records where the workspace and each project were last opened (`lastPath` in workspace.json and project.json; recorded the first time a folder is opened with it). When a workspace opens and the folder differs (compared as places, by real path: the same folder by another name, an 8.3 short name or a junction, hasn't moved, #455), Combwork works out in the background what still points to the old folder; if anything does, a banner says **This workspace was moved from …** (or that projects moved, when only a project folder was renamed or moved in) with **Repair…** (also `workspace.repairMove` in the palette while it's needed); if nothing does, the new folder is simply recorded. Since 1.0 Repair also finds the project's slots, copies and retired homes (**Built [#1447]**, §16.10.2). Repair… shows the plan (`workspace:movePlan`) and, on **Repair**, does it (`workspace:moveRepair`), refusing while any agent of the workspace (the Assistant included) runs: **worktrees**: each agent worktree is looked for moved along inside its project or the workspace, moved along in the worktrees folder beside the workspace (`<workspace>.worktrees`), then where it was; the first folder with a `.git` file wins; `git worktree repair <paths>` runs in the project, the result is checked (git lists it and its links are right both ways) and only then is `agents[].worktree.path` updated (`mutateProjectConfig`); one not found is listed with **Recreate worktree** (or **Create a new worktree** when its branch is gone, see below; made at its moved-along place, after the repairs above), **Locate…** (a folder picker; the folder must have a `.git` file; the plan is worked out again with it) or **Remove the agent's worktree link** (`worktree` dropped from the agent; nothing deleted); one still at its old place while the project's old folder exists too (a copy) is left to the original; **sessions**: `cwd`s under the old project folder or an old worktree path move to the new ones (`mutateSessions`); **per-path data**: for the project, and for each worktree now at a new place, kept in project.json (`pendingCopies`, written in the same locked change as the agent's new path) until its copy works, so a copy that fails is tried again by the next Repair, after a restart too, without repeating the git or session steps: the provider adapter's `copyPathData` (Claude Code: `~/.claude/projects/<path as name>/`, transcripts and `memory/`) copies to the new path's name for the project and each moved worktree (the Assistant's home too), never moving or deleting, never overwriting: a file already there with the same size and time counts as copied, one that differs is kept and listed; Codex keeps threads by id and has none; **Open Recent**: the old folder replaced by the new; **Working on**: the projects marked at the old folder (`activeProjects`, kept by folder path) marked at the new one too. **The profile's records by the workspace folder** (HI-2007, from HI-1968's sweep, which found no need for a workspace id; design HI-2007/s40 and s42; `carryProfile`): the window's pin (`alwaysOnTop`, `pin.ts` `carryPin`) moves to the new folder, and the window is pinned again; the close command's ended runs (`close-commands/ws-<name>-<hash of the place>-…`) take the new place's prefix, then the newest `KEEP_RUNS` are kept (`runs.ts` `carryRuns`). Its view preferences kept by folder (HI-2008, `viewPrefs.ts` `carryViewPrefs`: each project's `PROJECT_PREFS`, the Assistant's `<workspace>|<project>` folds, and `ui.panes`' `<what>:<workspace>` keys; a key names the folder only as a whole path, `shared/uiPrefs.ts` `movedPrefKey`) move to the new folder in the same guarded `config.update`, a value already kept at the new place staying, and open windows follow (`ui-pref-changed`, `ui-panes-changed`). A project moved on its own into another workspace (its `project.json` `lastPath` in another folder) has its own keys carried the same way at each open and Repair, before anything records where it is now (`carryProjectViewPrefs`: its path keys, and its Assistant fold `<workspace>|<project>` with its new workspace), while its old folder has no `project.json`; its old workspace's panes and other projects' keys stay, and one renamed or moved within its workspace is `projectRename.ts`'s. Its old folders are its `project.json` `lastPath` and `profileAt` (where its views were last carried, set once they have followed it; `lastPath` stays for Repair), so a project moved again before its Repair is done takes them from where they went (HR2's round 2): the same invariant as the workspace's. Chosen over keying them by project id, which would miss the workspace's own panes and needed every renderer key changed and an upgrade read, while this rides the same guarded, chained, retried carry. The Assistant's old token file (`assistant-api/<hash>.json`) is left as it is: it is written again at each launch, and deleting it could take a workspace's back at the old folder. **When:** not part of Repair's plan. The move is recorded as the moved workspace opens (`config.json` `profileMoves`: one `{ from, to, failed? }` per old folder, never evicted) only when the old folder is gone (no `.combwork`, not open): a copy's original keeps its own. Records about that old folder follow the workspace on, keeping their own `from` (A→B becomes A→C), and the folder they went to gets its record too, only when that folder is gone as well: a copy left there keeps them. Its old folders are `workspace.json`'s `lastPath` and `profileAt` (where its records were last all brought, set once nothing is left to follow it; apart from `lastPath`, which stays where Repair needs it until Repair is done), so a second move before a Repair finds the records where they went (HR2's round 3). Carried at each open (`checkMoved`) and at the start of each Repair until nothing is left at the old folder (a pin there, a run under its prefixes). **Guards:** each change rechecks, as it is made, that the workspace is still open there (its lifetime and path) and the old folder still gone: the pin in the same `config.update`, each rename by `carryRuns`' `proceed`. A close or a switch stops it with the record kept; the original back ends the record, what is left there its own. **What is left:** a run still going (its runner writes there) is retried silently and follows once it has ended. An ended run that couldn't move (`stuck`: a rename's error, a name already taken there, a folder that couldn't be read) is the record's `failed`: a failed row of Repair's report (What: the close command's output) so Repair isn't complete, a row of the plan ("move here (last try: …)"), and `WorkspaceMoved.profile`, which keeps the banner ("Some of Combwork's records of this workspace couldn't follow it from its old folder yet.") and Repair Moved Workspace… in the palette until it is done; at an open it is logged. A plan with files that couldn't be read, or only files already there with other content, still counts (`moveHasWork`): the banner shows it, failures stay pending, conflicts are listed once and never overwritten. The report lists what was done, skipped and failed (logged with `userText()`); Repair is complete only with nothing failed; a project is recorded as repaired (its `lastPath`) only when all its steps worked and nothing is left, the workspace when all are, so the banner stays until then and Repair can run again, repeating nothing done. Nothing at the old location is ever deleted. **Missing worktrees** (`main/agentWorktree.ts`): an agent whose worktree folder is gone, with its branch still in the repository, can have it made again: `git worktree prune`, then `git worktree add <path> <branch>` (no `-b`) at the recorded path (Repair: the moved-along place), or the agent's default worktree location if that can't be used; with the branch gone too, a new worktree on the same branch name from its base (else the project's current branch), as Add Agent makes one. Then the copied ignored files, `needsSetup` so the setup command runs at the next start, and the agent's path updated under the lock; at a new place, the same locked change records the old→new move in `pendingCopies`, so its sessions' `cwd`s and the CLIs' data follow it afterwards (Repair, or `finishPending()` after a Start's recreate) and a failure or exit in between leaves it to retry. Repair keeps a move pending when the sessions.json rewrite fails, too. A project with only such moves left gets the banner's third wording ("A worktree of x was made again at a new folder, and not everything has followed it yet"). Only when the folder is truly missing; refused while the agent runs, while git still lists the folder after the prune (locked), and when the prune would drop another missing worktree's entry (`git worktree prune --dry-run`), which a moved one still needs for `git worktree repair`, naming it (Repair passes the others it is recreating in the same run). Offered by Repair, by Start (New Session, Resume) with a confirm (`agents:missingWorktree`, `agents:recreateWorktree`; with the branch gone: Create a New Worktree or Remove the Worktree Link, `agents:unlinkWorktree`), and named in the error of a start that finds the folder missing. **File → Move Workspace…** was considered and not built: moving needs the old folder deleted, a cross-drive move of a workspace (and its worktrees) while terminals and watchers have it open is fragile, and Explorer does the move better; Repair handles what follows.
- **Repair's plan as a table, and agents' branches** (#1305, Darren's model the project hover's agent table; decision on #1303). The plan is an item table (`ItemTable`, #1317), a group a project then the workspace's (Open Recent, Working on, the board's saved names): **What · Was · Now · Will do**, each path a `ShortPath` (its part that differs from the other; a CLI's folder named after a whole path cut after its common start at a dash, `shortName`), the full path its tooltip and what copying copies; a missing worktree's Recreate · Locate… · Remove link at the row's right edge, compact (icon and short label, the full label its tooltip and name); a coding agent's copies one row (`N folders`, `copy N files; the old ones stay`, kept and unreadable counts after it, their files in its tooltip) with an expander for a row a folder. The table never scrolls sideways (fixed layout, cells cut with an ellipsis; the dialog up to 1180 px). A screen reader reads each row as a sentence (`workspace.repair.sentence`: what, was, now, will do; the table's role and headings left out, its cells' text hidden from it, the choices reachable). **Branches**: an agent's recorded branch in Combwork's full form whose workspace part isn't one of the project's own (`ownSpaces`) or whose project part isn't the project's, is renamed to its name here (`branchHere` in `shared/agentBranches.ts`: the workspace part its new branches take, `chooseSpace`; its agent part kept), never offered: `git branch -m` in the repository (git moves the branch's config, its upstream included, and updates the worktree that has it out), then `worktree.branch` in project.json in one locked change (a workspace part new to the project recorded in `branchSpaces`). Planned for every project with worktree agents, moved or not (`branchesOf`), except agents whose worktree this plan still has to find or make; a branch that tracks a remote is renamed locally and the row and report say its remote keeps the old name; one whose new name is taken is kept and said (`kept: 'exists'`, no work); **one operation a failure never leaves half done** (HR5's #1305 round 1): the rename is recorded first (project.json's `pendingBranchRenames`; a write that fails stops it there, git untouched), then git's, then a `LineRenamed` fact on each card whose work is on that line (`renameCardLines`: so the card follows it, and reconciliation, which waits while Repair runs (`repairingMove`, `reconcilersIdle`), never reads the line in between and records `Gone: line`), then the agent's record and the pending entry dropped; cut short after git's step, the cards follow it before anything else reads their line: reconciliation, finding a card's line gone, looks for a pending rename of it (`pendingRename` in the runtime's config, from project.json) and, when its new name is there, records `LineRenamed` (`followRename` in `reconcile.ts`) rather than `Gone: line` (HR5's #1305 round 2: after a restart or a failed Repair, with `repairingMove` off). **Every observation acts on the card's current line and cycle** (round 4, HR5's and the Assistant's class fix): `followRename` finds `renamed` (this observer wrote `LineRenamed`, or another did first), `unchanged` (no rename covers it, or git still has the old name) or `unknown` (a rename points away but git's names can't both be read: the line isn't observed that run); the caller reads the card again whatever it found; `observeHead`'s write, `Gone: line`'s and `renameCardLines`' each check under their write's lock that the card is still on the line and in the cycle they read, and drop what isn't; no `Gone: line` while a pending rename covers the line. Line references: the `Started` fact, `HeadMoved` and `LineMoved` keep the name they had (history; the fold follows `LineRenamed`); the live ones, git's branch, the agent's `worktree.branch` and each card's folded line, follow in the one operation, the pending entry kept until all have; a queued `prepareSlot` naming the old line (a slot's, P7: never an agent's branch today) makes the rename wait for the next Repair; the next Repair finishes the rest from there (a pending rename is planned whichever names git has; neither name left, it is dropped); a worktree Repair recreates on its branch has its branch renamed in the same Repair; the workspace part a branch moves to names this place now (`currentSpaces`: the workspace's own and its numbered ones; a part recorded under an old workspace name, Scratch-2 once it is Tools, stays the project's for ownership but is no longer chosen, so new branches and renamed ones take Tools or Tools-2); a card's recorded folder following its moved worktree is #1343's; the banner counts them (`WorkspaceMoved.branches`) and says so when nothing else is to repair. Repair refuses while an agent runs, as before. Under the workspace's group, a Microsoft Defender group moves Combwork's exclusions to the new folders (#1302, §4.2.2).
- **Repair's report as a table** (#1313, from the #1307 audit). Repair returns its lines as before (`done`, `skipped`, `failed`: the log, the Agent API, tests) and the same steps as rows (`MoveReport.rows`, `say()` in `workspaceMove.ts`): the project (none: the workspace's), what (by kind: an agent's worktree or branch, the sessions, a coding agent's copies, the board under an old name, handovers, Open Recent, Working on, Defender), where it was and is (folders, or branch names), the outcome and a short result. The dialog shows them in the plan's item table, What · Was · Now · **Result** (✓ done, the warning colour with its reason, ⓘ a choice left), a group a project, problems first, then the workspace's; a row's full line is its tooltip and what a screen reader reads, and "Repair… stays in the banner" is said once, at the foot. A copy's row names the folder that moved, not the CLI's own folders for it (the line names those). With no rows (nothing to repair) the lines are listed as before.
- **Project ids** (#508, `shared/projectIds.ts`). A project's stable id (`id` in its project.json, `p-` and 12 hex digits) is made once, when the workspace opens (`WorkspaceService.projectIds()`, hidden projects too; folders without Combwork's files have none), and goes with the folder; Combwork never drops it (older versions keep it too), and a project.json without it gets a new one, so that project's earlier cards are no project's. What the workspace keeps about a project names it by the id beside its folder name: cards (`projectId` after `project` in each card's document), lanes (`lanes.json`), card watches (`watches.json`: the watcher's project, and each agent an agent watch follows) and the merge slot's record of holds. **The id decides whose a record is** (`projectNow`): read back, it is the project that has its id now (renamed or moved within the workspace since, names swapped or not, whatever project has its saved name now). With an id no project has (its project gone from the workspace), it keeps its saved name, and while another project has that name it shows as `<name>: gone` (never a folder name, so never that project's, nor in its agents' view; saved with its name as it was). Only a record saved before ids (no id) goes by its name. Saving a card writes its project's id; one with an id no project has keeps it, and none ever takes another project's. The ids are listed again when the workspace's folders change: at most once a second, at once after the workspace folder's watcher sees a rename (which also tells the board, `tasks-changed`, when an id is at another folder than where it was last seen while the workspace is open, so the window reads its cards again; compared with where it was last seen, not only with the read before, so a read part way through a rename, which misses the folder, or a project out of the workspace for a while loses no rename; of the projects a read missed, the 64 missed most recently are remembered, and all are forgotten when the workspace closes, #555), and at once for a lane or watch check, so a lane and its cards agree. The folders are compared with their project.json's identity and time, so a folder replaced by another of the same name, or two projects that swapped names, are read again. A rename can't reach a running agent's folder on Windows. A copied folder brings its project.json along: of the folders sharing an id, the one still where it was last opened keeps it (else the one with the same folder name), and the others are given new ids, so the copy starts with no cards. **One-time stamping**, each time the workspace opens (`stampCardProjects`, `stampLaneProjects`, `stampWatchProjects`): a record saved before ids whose name is a project of the workspace gets its id, and one whose project was renamed since gets its name now; a record with an id no project has, and one saved before ids under a name no project has, are left as they are. Cards under the board's lock, each in its own, read again there and written back with every field; lanes.json and watches.json in their locks. Each record changed keeps its content from before beside it once (`<n>.json.before-ids.bak`, `lanes.json.before-ids.bak`, `watches.json.before-ids.bak`, while those were files: since #1018 the files as they were are the import backups `….imported-<time>`; never replaced by a second run or a later change; a backup that can't be made stops that write; removed when the workspace opens once a week old, #1016). A second run changes nothing. A watch whose id is no project's while another project has its folder is set aside in the file (`invalid`), never that project's; an agent watch's watched agents follow their project's id the same way (their marks and fired agents re-keyed), and a watched agent whose project is gone while another project has its folder is marked `gone`: told as stopped, with nothing recorded at that folder (its status, events or replies) taken as its own, even when the new project has an agent of the same id. **The whole workspace moved** (#146): a watch and its agents saved under the workspace's old folder (workspace.json's `lastPath` as the workspace opened: `movedFrom`) are read as under its folder now, then placed by their ids in the workspace's own index, so they come to their projects at the new place (one saved before ids, and the Assistant's, by folder). Wherever else a watch was saved, its project id decides: an id in this workspace's index makes it that project's, at that project's folder now (always one of this workspace's), and the usual checks then apply as to any watch of that project (`followIds`, #536). One saved under another folder with no id, or with an id no project here has, stays set aside: a saved path outside the workspace is never taken as a project. A merge hold left in the record when Combwork closed is told in the project its id is in now; one saved before ids, in the project at its folder (under the new place, if the workspace moved) or else the one project last opened there (project.json's `lastPath`); the holds recorded at the workspace's old folder (the record is by the workspace's folder) are told too when nothing is there now. A hold whose project can't be known (gone, or another project has its folder) is told in the workspace, saying so, and kept beside the record (`<record>.unplaced.json`, the latest 50); the record keeps its content from before beside it once (`.before-ids.bak`) when any hold is placed elsewhere. The Agent API and the board never show the id. **Records left under an old name** (saved before ids, by a project renamed since: the nine cards of website's old name after its rename, 10 Oct): cards, lanes and card watches without an id under a name no project of the workspace has (hidden and removed projects' names count as the workspace's) are given, by Repair, to the project Repair is moving from that name, else to the one project whose agents (project.json, or sessions in its sessions.json) worked on them (`orphanNames`: a card's agent and reviewer, a lane's builder and reviewer, a watch's watcher); one whose agents are no project's, or more than one's, is left alone. The banner and the plan list them (`MoveCards`, "9 cards of old-site belong to website"); Repair moves each card still under that name and without an id in its lock, editing only its project, id and a history line by Repair (its other fields and `updatedAt` as they were, the backup kept as above), and likewise its lanes and watches. Repair also keeps a project renamed in place marked **Working on** under its new name. **What keeps a project by its folder name or path** (#514). Whose a record is goes by the project's id, never by a name alone. *The record of names* (`projectNames.ts`, `.combwork/project-names.json`, a kept file, the workspace's and not the project's, so a copied folder brings none of it along): each project's folder name as Combwork last saw it and its earlier ones, by id, and every rename, numbered, those seen in one read of the ids in one batch. After each read of the ids (`WorkspaceService.onIdsRead`), a project seen under another name than its record's was renamed (by id: two projects that swapped names are two renames, never copies); one not recorded yet is recorded under its folder name, or, one from before whose project.json's `lastPath` is another folder here that is no project now, as renamed from it; a copy just given an id of its own starts from its own name. *Owned by id* (never rewritten): **handovers** (`.combwork/handover-owners.json`: file name → project id, written as Combwork writes a handover, and carried to its new name when it is renamed in Notes (case only too, and to another type and back), in the record's lock, where adoption also lists the handovers, so neither loses it; forgotten only when its file is gone (a case changed outside Combwork keeps it; a folder that can't be read forgets nothing); a handover is a `.md` file in any case, not the README; an older one, or one written by hand, is given its project once, from what it says. Its header's Project line names a folder name, which more than one project may have had (renamed, and the name taken by a new project): the projects that had it are that name's project now and those whose record has it, now or before (`ownersOfName`). The conversation its header names settles which (the one project whose sessions.json has it, if that project had the name); with none, only a name one project ever had counts. With no header, the one project whose name, now or before, its file name begins with (the longest). A header that names another project is never overruled by the file name, and evidence that disagrees or can't decide leaves it nobody's, never a guess, until something tells: a rename, or Repair, which records in the record of names that the project it gives a folder name's cards to had that name (before moving anything, so a Repair that fails part way, or a restart, loses none of it; Repair isn't done until those handovers and comparisons are given to it, and "Nothing to repair" only once they are), and **kept comparisons** (each project entry's `owner` in the index; an older one given its project once by its scope's name, and a choice of baseline and run kept by the project's id). A project's handovers (`handoversFor`: the session guidance, `cw_read_latest_handover` through `GET /v1/shared/handovers`, Hand Over to…, Remove from Combwork's packing) and comparisons are those its id owns, so a renamed project keeps its own, and a project that takes a name another had, or a copy, never gets that one's. These are given owners at the workspace's first follow and after each change of the record of names. Ownership work stays in the workspace it began in: a window that opens another workspace while it waits (for the owners' lock, a file) makes it stop and write nothing. *Followed once, each rename* (`projectRename.ts` `applyRenames`, batch by batch, each batch all at once, so a swap keeps each project's own): the per-project view preferences kept by path (Skills tab provider and folds, Sessions tree, the .combwork notice, the Assistant panel's folds; windows hear, `ui-pref-changed`) and Working on, with config.json's `renamesApplied` for the workspace; Hide or Remove from Combwork (workspace.json's hiddenProjects, and its `renamesApplied`); Progress runs, open and kept, with the kept runs (`renames`); metrics measured under the old names, merged into the new names', with the measurements (`renamesApplied`). Each place saves the number of the last rename it followed in the same write as what it changed (workspace.json's settings change in memory only once saved; the others are saved whole from memory, the number with them), so a rename is followed once, and one a failure or a stop left behind is followed later: a run that fails is tried again after 5 s, doubling up to 10 minutes, while the workspace is open, and at its next opening. A retry follows the projects as last read, never the read that failed: a project renamed again after a failed run has its settings and runs follow its newest name, never back to a folder it no longer has (#555). The Progress panel's filter isn't moved: one on a folder with no runs shows them all. The removal pack restores under the folder's name now, so it needs nothing.
- **Project** — any direct child folder of the workspace, excluding dot-folders (so `.combwork` is never a project) and folders hidden or removed from Combwork (§6.7). Creating a project in Combwork creates the folder.
- **Active project** — a project switched on with its toggle. Only active projects get a terminal, watchers, status indicators and notifications. Activating a project **never** starts or resumes a session; it offers "Resume last session" and "New session". Deactivating requires stopping the live session (after confirmation). Active state is personal, so it is stored in app data, not in the workspace.
- **Provider** — the CLI an agent runs: **Claude Code** (Anthropic) or **Codex** (OpenAI). The UI uses product names, and "provider" where a generic word is needed. Providers are enabled in Settings → Providers; a fresh install has none enabled (a banner links to the settings), and an upgrade from 0.1 keeps Claude Code enabled. With none enabled, no agent can start and none can be added.
- **Agent** — one of a project's session slots: as many as its workflow's **Maximum agents** (HI-2001, §16.6.8: the team size, 12 unless a preset or the user sets another), whoever adds them (HI-2058), at most 24 (#562). **All agents are equal** and a new project has **none**: agents are added (Add Agent) and removed (when stopped) freely, and each works in the project folder or in its own **git worktree** (a separate checkout on its own branch). Agents are named ("Agent 1", "Agent 2"…, renamable), have random ids that are never reused, and always store their **provider**, which follows from their **connection** (chosen when they are added); defaults never move an existing agent. Model, effort, permission mode, context and extra arguments are the connection's (Settings → Accounts & Connections): an agent has none of its own (HI-2108, decision B). Choosing another CLI's connection changes its provider and clears its last session. Each agent has at most one live session. Agents of a disabled provider stay listed, greyed out, and can't start. Upgrading from 0.1 clears every project's agents and layout (their sessions stay and can be resumed by an agent added again).
- **Session** — one conversation of a provider's CLI. Claude Code sessions have a UUID Combwork chooses; Codex chooses its own ID, which Combwork learns from the first hook (with the first prompt). A session can only be resumed by an agent of the same provider. A project has at most one live session per agent plus any number of past (resumable) and archived sessions.
- **Assistant** — one per workspace, in a panel on the right: the workspace's **overseer**, a provider session like an agent's that looks after every project rather than working in one (§6.5). It never takes one of a project's agent slots.
- **Mode** — how the Assistant works: what it puts first and how it hands things back, a Markdown file of instructions in `<Workspace>/.combwork/modes` (`.combwork/personas` until 0.9.3, when modes were called personas: §6.5).
- **Task board** — one per workspace: cards (tasks) in four fixed columns, each belonging to a project and optionally given to one of its agents. The user, the Assistant and agents all work on it (§6.6).
- **Global scope** — settings in app data or `<Workspace>/.combwork/workspace.json`, applied to every project unless the project overrides them.
- **Project scope** — overrides in `<Project>/.combwork/project.json`.

---

## 4. On-disk layout

### 4.1 Workspace (committed to git if the workspace is a repo)

```
<Workspace>/
  .combwork/
    workspace.json        # MCP servers turned on, hidden and removed projects
    shared/               # cross-session notes, handovers, instructions (markdown)
      handovers/
    skills/
      <skill-name>/SKILL.md (+ supporting files)
    mcp/
      <server-name>.json  # one MCP server definition (§7.2)
      <server-name>/      # optional server code
    modes/
      <id>.md             # a Assistant mode (§6.5)
    bundled.json          # which of Combwork's bundled skills and modes the workspace was given, and from which version (§7.1)
    combwork.db               # the task board (§6.6): SQLite, one row a card (#1017), and lanes, card watches and every session host's deliveries (#1018) and session records (#1061, below); with combwork.db-wal and combwork.db-shm
    usage.db              # the usage history (§9, #1106): what each session used, a row per day, model and card; written by the usage worker only; with usage.db-wal and usage.db-shm
    tasks/                # 0.9 to 1.0 left a stub here for older versions (board.json, a README; #1017): none is written since 1.1, and the names upgrade sets aside any card in it and removes it (HI-2594)
    tasks.imported-<time>/ # the cards' files as they were, kept when they moved into combwork.db; to the Recycle Bin 14 days after (#1111)
    .gitignore            # keeps combwork.db, usage.db and the board's backups out of git (written once, if there is none; the usage history's lines added to one an older version wrote before them)
    lanes.json.imported-<time>  # lanes.json, watches.json as they were, kept when they moved into combwork.db (#1018); a project's deliveries.json likewise in its .combwork. Each such backup (`<name>.imported-<time>`: these, metrics.json's, the board's folder, a session host's sessions.json) goes to the Recycle Bin (`trash()`) 14 days after the move, by the time in its name, when the workspace opens (`sweepLeftovers`, #1111): only those names in their own store's folder, a file or a real folder, never a link
    assistant/            # the Assistant's home (§6.5); its own .gitignore keeps it out of git
      .combwork/              # like a project's: project.json (its one agent), backups, launch-assistant/ (its session records are in combwork.db, under `assistant`)
    README.md             # explains the folder to humans browsing the repo
```

`<Workspace>/.combwork/` is intended to be committed so a team can share skills, MCP definitions and notes. The task board's database is this machine's, as the Assistant's sessions are: `.combwork/.gitignore` keeps it out. MCP definitions must reference secrets via environment variables (§7.2).

<!-- old-name: begin spec-upgrade-inputs -->
#### 4.1.1 The move from `.hive` (HI-2462)

Before 1.1 the folder was `.hive`, in the workspace, in each project and in the Assistant's home. From 1.1 it is `.combwork` (another tool also writes `.hive` into repositories). The design is the card's (HI-2462/s21, its state replaced by s65); the code is `combworkMove.ts`, the paths' translation `shared/combworkFolderMove.ts`.

- **When**: as a workspace opens, before anything reads it (`WorkspaceService.opened`), each host's `.hive` of **ours** (holding `project.json`, or for the workspace `workspace.json` or `combwork.db`) is renamed `.combwork`: one rename, never a copy, so nothing is half-moved or lost. A project that comes into an open workspace later with a `.hive` (copied in, restored) is moved by `ensureProject` before anything is made in it. The files inside were then renamed by the names upgrade (§4.1.2).
- **Never moved**: another tool's `.hive`; a `.hive` beside a `.combwork` (**both**: `.combwork` is used, `.hive` is left byte for byte, and a warning names the folder); a `.hive` that is a link, or a project folder whose real place is outside the workspace (a warning: rename it by hand with Combwork closed).
- **Ownership**: the move holds a lock across processes (the repository lock's row, `repoLockCore.ts`, in `<workspace>\.combwork-move.lock`, outside every folder that moves, and kept after the move: a lock's file is never removed). Inside it, a fresh presence marker of any other process (§16.17) refuses the open. The workspace's folder is renamed first: a 1.0 with its board open makes that fail (Windows won't rename a folder with a file in it open) before any project is touched, and the open is refused naming the folder, nothing lost.
- **State is on disk** (HI-2462/s65, after HR1's round 1): before a host's `.hive` is renamed, Combwork's marker (`combwork-move-id`, a small JSON naming it Combwork's move) is written inside it, so it moves with the folder. A host has moved exactly when its own `.combwork` (a real folder at its place, not a link) holds that marker; nothing else records a move. A crash at any point leaves the folders saying what happened: a marker still in `.hive` is renamed at the next open, a moved folder is in the map at once. A `.hive` made again beside a moved `.combwork` (a 1.0 opened since: going back isn't supported, §4.1.2) is left as it is, with a warning, and never read. After the renames come the rewrites, each idempotent: git's exclude lines, git worktrees inside a moved folder (`git worktree repair`), the paths in shared notes and handovers, then (once the board and projects are up) the paths in cards (description, comments, context: in a worker, `combworkMoveWorker.ts`, each batch read and written in one write transaction, so a user's concurrent edit is never overwritten; history is never rewritten) and the agents' folders inside a moved folder (slots, copies, homes, relocated). They run whenever `combwork-moved.json` doesn't hold the hash of the map as it is now, over the whole map, and the hash is written once the last has worked: a host that appears later changes the map, so they run again for it. One that fails refuses the open; the next does them again.
- **The map** is derived from the folders on every use (`deriveMoves`): each moved host's `<host>\.hive` → `<host>\.combwork`, and the Assistant's home's old path under the workspace's old folder only when the workspace's own folder moved (an old outer tree left beside a `.combwork` is never mapped). Paths stored before are translated through it alone, as whole paths (any case, either separator, in a `file:///` link as encodeURI writes it): card text, notes, an old link opened from a card or a terminal (`followMovedLink`, after the file at the old path, if there, is tried), a merge-slot hold's folder and a recorded transcript path. A `.hive` not in the map is never anyone's `.combwork`. Nothing is deleted by the move, in any tree.
- **Conversations**: a session record's folder (`cwd`, the key Claude Code files its transcript under) and `transcriptPath` are never rewritten. A conversation whose recorded folder lies inside a moved folder starts fresh rather than resume (HI-2463's fresh start: what waited for it is carried to the new one, a notice counts them), in its folder's new place; its transcript stays readable.
- **Before the open**: what reads a workspace before it opens (the last run's report, restart's resume, accounts' recent workspaces) reads through `dataFolder()` (`combworkFolder.ts`): `.combwork` only (HI-2594), so a workspace not moved yet has nothing there until its open moves it, and nothing makes a second tree. Only the move itself looks at a `.hive`, as its input.
- **Exclude lines**: the old line for a moved project (`/<project>/.hive/` under its `# Hive project metadata (added by Hive)` comment) becomes the `.combwork` one, only when no `.hive` is left there, and its comment becomes Combwork's (`# Combwork project metadata (added by Combwork)`, the comment new entries get); every other line stays.

#### 4.1.2 The names upgrade (HI-2587)

Darren, 5 Nov: a complete, **one-way** conversion to Combwork's names. What 1.0 and the 1.1 release candidates stored under the old names takes Combwork's once, and nothing reads the old names afterwards. Going back to 1.0 isn't supported: a 1.0 reinstalled finds no `.hive`, no `hive.db` and no `Hive` profile, and starts empty (HI-2461's answer). The design is the card's (HI-2587/s15, with s20, s23, s26 and s40); the code is `nameUpgrade.ts` and the modules it names.

- **Each item on its own**: a step looks at its own item and changes only what is still old, so a 1.0.0 install, a partly converted RC2 (profile, `.combwork` and `cw.*` ids already done) and an upgrade interrupted halfway all end in the same state. Nothing is deleted except SQLite's empty leftovers of the board's old name.
- **Where**: the profile folders by the installer (HI-2460); at start, before what they rename is read, the log (`hive.log`/`hive.1.log` → `combwork.log`/`combwork.1.log`, each only while its new name is free; one that can't be renamed stays in the logs folder, never read) and the run marker's version key (`running.json`: `hive` → `app`); at a workspace's open, under the folder move's lock (§4.1.1) after its renames and before anything of the workspace is admitted, the workspace's and its projects' steps; and in the databases' schema steps.
- **The board's file** (`boardFileMove.ts`): `hive.db` → `combwork.db`. Needed while any old-name file of the board's is there (the file, its `-wal`, `-shm` or `-journal`, a copy in `backups/`). With `hive.db` alone, it is checkpointed and closed in a worker (its log folded in, a crash's rollback journal rolled back), then renamed only if no log or journal holding anything is left beside it (else the open is refused, nothing changed): one rename of a file holding everything, never onto a file that is there. The empty leftovers are removed. Both `hive.db` and `combwork.db`: `combwork.db` is used, `hive.db` and its sidecars left byte for byte, with a warning each open. A leftover log or journal holding data is never deleted: kept with a warning beside `combwork.db`; with no board file at all, the open is refused, every time, naming the file and saying to put the board's file back as `hive.db` beside it (no empty board is ever made over it). The board's copies in `backups/` take the new family (`combwork-v…`, `combwork-before-1.0-…`, `combwork-before-restore-…`).
- **The workspace's files** (`nameUpgradeFiles.ts`): its `.gitignore` (Combwork's head, `combwork.db` lines, and `combwork-names.json` kept out), its README when it is exactly a text 1.0 or an RC wrote, and stored MCP definitions (`${HIVE_MCP_DIR}` → `${CW_MCP_DIR}`, the old catalogue address → the new one). A file the user wrote is left as it is. The board's stub for older versions (`tasks/` with its README, which 0.9 to 1.0 kept; HI-2594, HR1's round 1): the cards an older version saved in it are set aside, intact and each once, in `tasks.set-aside` (the board's notice says how many, and its Review… adds or discards each), then the stub's files and folder go; a `tasks/` without the README (0.8's cards, which the board imports) is left. The board moves its next number past the set-aside cards' at each open, so none is given to a new card, and reads nothing of `tasks/`.
- **The projects** (`nameUpgradeProjects.ts`): the refs Combwork keeps in each repository under the old prefix, `refs/hive/cards/…` and `refs/hive/queue/…`, made again under `refs/cw/` at the same commit and the old ones deleted, one at a time (HI-2593's handoff, HI-2593/s11; its branches stay as they are); skill copies' marker `.hive-copy` → `.combwork-copy`, in each project and each folder the board's `skill_copies` records name (slots, worktrees, copies); in the same folders, Combwork's copies under the old prefix (`hive-<skill>`) retired when provably its own and unchanged (the marker says so and the content is still its hash; `swapOut` checks again as it goes; HI-2594: delivery makes and reads only `cw-` copies), anything else there being the user's; and the old comment lines in the repository's `info/exclude` (`# Hive project metadata (added by Hive)`, `# Hive's copies of workspace skills…`) become Combwork's, whole lines only, and the old copies' lines (`/.agents/skills/hive-*/`, `/.agents/skills/.hive-*/`) go, so a `hive-*` folder left is the user's, which git shows and a slot's removal never takes unseen. Nothing recognises the old wording afterwards.
- **Inside the databases**: every database's `schema_version` column `hive_version` → `app_version` (`db.ts`, as it opens); the board's step 25 (`schema/namesStep.ts`): comments' `hive_text` → `app_text` (`appText` in a card's JSON) and the 0.9 import record's `hiveVersion` → `appVersion`.
- **The window's storage** (HI-2610): the Activity tabs' views kept as `hive.activity.<project>` move to `combwork.activity.<project>` as each window starts, before a view is read (`activityView.ts` `upgradeActivityViews`); one already kept under the new key stays, and the old key goes.
- **Stored values** (HI-2598, its design HI-2598/s9): each `'hive'` value Combwork stored becomes `combwork` (`Combwork` where it is a display name), each where its file is converted, and its runtime reader goes with it. The board's step 26 (`schema/valuesStep.ts`): facts' actor and `Integrated.by`, `Refused.rule` `merge.hiveMerges` → `merge.combworkMerges`, `CheckRan.by` "Hive (…)" → "Combwork (…)", wake actions' `by`, the rulesets holding `finish: hiveMerges` or `commitMessage: hive` (rewritten, their id recomputed as compile.ts does and every fact and lane pointed at it), lanes' builder and starter, card history's and cards' `Hive`, deliveries' sender (with Combwork's own bodies' `[Hive] ` → `[CW] ` and the renamed note added once where they name an old tool outside their quotes; nothing quoted is rewritten), fired watches' lines, metrics' `hive_<tool>` series (merged into their `cw_` one), merge choices, and the Assistant's change records an undo would write back. The journal's step 3: `source` `hive` → `combwork` (its table rebuilt for the CHECK) and the `hive` tag. A workspace's open (`nameUpgradeValues.ts`, under the lock): project.json's workflow options (in force and kept), workspace.json's workflow defaults, When the workspace opens/closes refs and `advanced` ids, and each saved template's workflow. At start, before any of its files is read (`nameUpgradeProfile.ts`): config.json's workflow defaults, When Combwork quits refs and `agentApi.provideHiveMcp` → `provideCombworkMcp`; advanced.json's `hive.*` ids → `cw.*`, `<cli>.override.preApproveHiveTools` → `preApproveCombworkTools`, the two kept for a move (`cw.assistant.otherMcpServers`, `cw.agents.perProject`), and the retired `hive.accounts.preview` dropped; each workspace's kept progress runs (`source`, "Hive (…)" names); and config.json's `ui` (HI-2591): the .combwork notice's dismissals `hiveVcsNotice` → `combworkVcsNotice`, each project's Skills fold `hive` → `combwork`, and the tips seen or used under `hive-folder`, `hive-merges` and `hive-skills` → `combwork-…`, a value already under the new name kept. The workspace's record is version 3, so one recorded before runs its steps again. **A template import** maps a 1.0 export's `finish: hiveMerges`, which would otherwise lose its Git section (the decision's exception, HI-2598/s9 §6). Agents see `combwork` where they saw `hive` (a template's scope, a skill's level, a session's and the journal's source, the console's Combwork source, `combwork:<workspace>`); an old value passed is refused as invalid.
- **Done**: `combwork-names.json` in the workspace's `.combwork` (version 4 since HI-2611's retired skill, 3 since HI-2598's stored values, 2 since HI-2594's steps: one of an older version runs every step again) (kept out of git: a clone elsewhere upgrades its own) once every workspace step has worked; without it every step runs again (each idempotent), so an ordinary open costs only the board's file names and that file. Each project has its own record (in its `.combwork`, out of git with it), written with its steps: a project that comes into an open workspace later (`ensureProject`), its `.combwork` an RC's, a copy's or a new one, gets its own steps once by its own record, whatever the workspace's says. **Nothing of the upgrade is written outside the move's lock** (HR2's rounds 2 and 3): what runs before it only reads whether anything is due; under it, another process's presence refuses it before anything is written (the lock file's own exclude line too), and the records are written there, after the steps. A workspace's open is refused then; a project's upgrade waits (it is used as it is, and its next set-up or the workspace's next open tries again); a new workspace's record (`recordNewWorkspace`, as it is made) is written under the lock too, or left for its next open. A folder or file a step can't read fails the step: only one that isn't there reads as empty, so nothing is recorded done with something old left in it. A step that fails refuses the open (*Combwork couldn't finish renaming …*), naming what it was renaming; the next open does it again.
- **Not stored, renamed outright**: the keeper's pipe (`combwork-keeper-…`) and its state's version key (`app`), the merge queue's job (`Local\CombworkQueue-…`), the launch gate's pipe, temp folders (`combwork-codex-setup`, `combwork-claude-models`, `combwork-copilot-models`, `combwork-antivirus-…`), Copilot's instructions file (`combwork.instructions.md`), drag types (`application/x-combwork-…`), the commit watch's argument (`--cw-commit-watch`). A keeper an RC left running past the upgrade isn't reached on the new pipe: its slot writer stays held until its processes end or Release Slot (the safe way).
- **Exports**: Performance → Compare's files are `combwork-benchmark/1` and `combwork-metrics/1`. 1.0's exports and templates aren't imported (HI-2611, Darren's decision, replacing HI-2587's one import exception): a Performance export from 1.0 (`hive-metrics/1`) is refused, saying it is one; a benchmark's old id isn't Combwork's (those are development runs, made again). A template exports as `<name>.combwork-template.json`; its import reads the content, and one whose workflow holds the old values (`finish: hiveMerges`, `commitMessage: hive`) is refused, saying it is 1.0's, never converted. Only a workspace's own saved templates are upgraded, once, by the upgrade. The upgrade also removes a workspace's copy of the bundled skill shipped as `use-hive-api` (now `use-cw-api`, HI-2463) while it is one 1.0 shipped, unchanged; the workspace's sync of its bundled items no longer looks for it.
- **The runtime readers removed** (HI-2594, its design HI-2594/s7): what read an old name while the app ran is gone, or is now only an input of a step here. The profile folders (§4.3), `.hive` before a workspace's open (`dataFolder` is `.combwork` only; the move's own `treeOf` reads `.hive` as its input, and a 0.9 profile's connection order through it), the `##hive-progress` step lines and the `hive-progress` shims (the profile's old shims removed before the new are written, `removeOldShims`), the MCP zips' `hive-mcp(.example).json`, `${HIVE_MCP_DIR}` and the old catalogue address, the reserved server name `hive` (now an ordinary name; a user's own `hive` server is theirs like any other), Copy Diagnostics' old start line (a log line under any other name is an older version's: more left out, never less), the board's stub for older versions (no longer written, nor read at the board's open: the files step above retires it), and `Hive-…:` lines in merge messages (a commit's text from before 1.1 is history, kept as written).
- **Left to other cards**: the `'hive'` values stored in rows and settings, and the readers that read them now (HI-2598, B2: each reader removed with the step that converts its value; HI-2594/s7); the names of the branches and refs Combwork makes from now on (`cw/`, HI-2593).
<!-- old-name: end spec-upgrade-inputs -->

### 4.2 Project (entirely git-excluded)

```
<Workspace>/<Project>/
  .combwork/
    project.json          # project overrides
    sessions.json.imported-<time>  # its session index as it was, kept when it moved into the workspace's combwork.db (#1061; below)
    sessions/<id>.jsonl   # backup copy of each session transcript
    archive/<id>.jsonl    # transcripts of archived sessions
    attachments/<id>/<time>[_<name>]  # files pasted or dropped into a session (#387; was images/); deleted only by Clean Up… and Purge… (§4.2.1)
    attachments/cards/<card number>/<time>_<name>  # files kept with a card (HI-1700); never a session's: Clean Up and Purge pass them by
    removed/              # only after Remove from Combwork (§6.7): manifest.json, cards.json, handovers/
    project.json.bak      # last good copy (see §2)
    launch-<agent id>/    # Claude Code agents: regenerated on every launch, its skills' copies kept while unchanged (HI-1694) — do not edit
      plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
      plugin/skills/<skill>/...     # copies of enabled Combwork skills
      mcp.json
      settings.json                 # hooks Combwork injects
      sync.json                     # hash of each item copied
  .agents/skills/cw-<skill>/  # Codex agents: copies of enabled Combwork skills (Codex reads skills only here),
                                # each with a .combwork-copy marker (only marked folders are replaced or removed);
                                # git-excluded with a /.agents/skills/cw-*/ line in .git/info/exclude
```

Codex takes everything else from `-c` overrides on its command line (§6.4), so it needs no launch folder.

Worktrees Combwork creates for agents live **next to the workspace**, in `<Workspace>.worktrees/<Project>/<agent>` (e.g. `D:\Dev\Work.worktrees\web\agent-2`), so the project's own tools (tsc, test runners, search, file watchers) don't scan a second copy of the code, and Combwork doesn't take them for projects. Transcripts, backups and images of worktree agents still live in the project's `.combwork` folder.

#### 4.2.1 Storage, Clean Up and Purge

- **Project Settings → Storage** (also for the Assistant's home, from Settings → Workspace) shows the sizes of `.combwork/sessions`, `.combwork/archive`, `.combwork/attachments` and each agent's worktree, and their total; under the backups' and the archive's sizes, what they hold before compression (#1110: `sessionsRaw`, `archiveRaw`, each `.gz` counted by the size its gzip trailer records), when that is more. The CLIs' own transcripts aren't counted. Main measures in the background (`storage.ts`): a directory at a time, links and junctions not followed, yielding to the event loop every few hundred entries; one measurement per project at a time, and the last result comes back at once until **Refresh**. Attachment and worktree folders are cached per folder by modified time (a folder that hasn't changed counts its files as before; its subfolders are still checked); backups and the archive are measured afresh. The Storage pages pass a request with each call and abandon it when they close or measure again (`storage:abandon`, after the new call is sent): the abandoned call fails, and a measurement no call waits for any more stops between entries, leaving no result (the folders it finished stay cached). A request is its window's (by its web contents): only that window abandons it, and closing the window or reloading its page, which run none of the page's clean-up, abandons all of its requests (#260). Calls that reuse a request id while one under it still runs share it: abandoning it stops every one of their waits, and it goes with the last of them (#299). A call without a request (none in the UI today) can't be abandoned and keeps its measurement going. An `.asar` file counts as a file of its size.
- **Settings → Workspace → Storage**: the workspace's total and every project, the Assistant included, biggest first, ten to a page (a data table, #250), each opening its Storage page (the Assistant's opens in place).
- **Clean Up…** runs per project, only when asked; nothing is automatic. Options: attachments of archived sessions last active more than N days ago (on, 90); attachments of deleted sessions and of `run-<runId>` folders of launches that never got a session (never a running launch's); Combwork's backups of archived sessions older than N days, **only where the CLI still has the transcript**; and, apart from that, with a warning, backups of archived sessions the CLI no longer has. Age is the session's last activity.
- A preview lists every file and its size and the total before anything is removed (`storage:cleanupPreview`). Applying it (`storage:cleanup`, with the listed paths) plans again and removes only listed items that still qualify (a session resumed or unarchived meanwhile is skipped and reported); a session's backups go only if every copy of it was listed. Each session is reserved while its files go (a resume of it is refused until then: "Clean Up is removing files of this session") and checked with both of its backups locked, again right before they go (still archived, not running or starting, its copies exactly the ones listed); an image folder is checked the same way just before it goes. Anything else is skipped. A backup goes only after what its session used has been read and saved on its record (`keptUsage`; a session whose only copy it was then moves it to `deletedUsage` as it is deleted), so its totals survive a failure partway; if that can't be read or saved, the backup stays and is reported. Everything goes to the Recycle Bin. Running sessions and sessions that aren't archived are never touched, nor `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`.
- Usage totals don't change: what a session used is recorded in the usage history (§9) before any of its copies goes, and stays there once the copies and the record are gone; a session whose usage can't be recorded keeps its copies. Removing the last copy deletes the session as Delete does (§6.2).
- **Purge…** (#1138, decision 7 of #1106; scope confirmed by Darren, 20 Oct) removes **everything Combwork keeps per session**, only when asked, for one session (the Sessions tab's **Purge Combwork's Files…**, on Combwork's own sessions that aren't running), a project or the Assistant (**Project Settings → Storage**, beside Clean Up…) or the workspace (**Settings → Workspace → Storage**: every project's and the Assistant's). What it covers (`planPurge`, `shared/storage.ts`): each session's backups (active and archived, compressed or not); what is left of them (`.spare`, a half-made `.<pid>-<time>.tmp`, an archive's `.archiving`/`.previous`/`.archived`: the files of `.combwork/sessions` and `.combwork/archive` named for a session, nothing else there); each of its attachments (the plain files of its folder in `.combwork/attachments`); the old usage on its record (`keptUsage`); and what is left of sessions Combwork no longer has: their files, their attachments (`run-<runId>` folders too) and their kept usage (`deletedUsage`). A leftover that may be a session's **only copy** is kept and counted ("1 leftover file is kept…"): one of a session the CLI no longer has, with no backup of it in that folder, which is what Combwork stopping in the middle of a delete or a move leaves (a `.spare`, a set-aside `.previous`); nothing restores it by itself, and it stays until the session is deleted. **There is no option to clear the usage history: it always stays, so totals never change.** Never the CLIs' files (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.copilot`), the session records themselves (but see last copies), the `deleted` list that keeps the CLIs' sessions hidden, worktrees, or anything of a running or starting session (the preview says how many it left alone).
- Its preview (`storage:purgePreview`) lists every file and record with its size and the total, grouped by kind (with the project, for the workspace); a backup that is its session's **last copy** (the CLI no longer has the transcript) is tagged, and a warning says those sessions are deleted from Combwork as Delete Session does. Main keeps the preview as it saw it (each file's size and modified time, each backup's last-copy status), by an id, for an hour (the newest 20), and applies it once and only within that hour (#1158: its age is checked when it is applied; an older one is refused as out of date, nothing removed, and the user opens Purge again): `storage:purge` takes the preview's id and its keys, and works from the preview, not from what it would list now. It goes to the Recycle Bin (`trash()`) unless **Delete permanently** is ticked. Each listed item is checked against a fresh plan: still listed, of the same kind (a key is its kind and path, or its record's host and id: a deleted session's folder that belongs to a session again doesn't match), its file unchanged, and a backup still its session's last copy or still not, as the preview said; else it is skipped and reported, and so is the rest of a session one of whose backups changed. Nothing it didn't list goes: an attachment added since stays, and its folder with it (a folder goes whole only when it holds just the listed files; else the files go one by one, and the folder once empty). A session's things go together (`sessions.purge`), with it reserved (a resume is refused until it is done) and its backups locked, checked before and again right before anything goes, after the waits: not running or starting in any window, its transcript not being read, and, when its last copy goes, not open in a Sessions view (a view reads the CLI's transcript while the CLI has it; the Sessions tab closes its own view first and opens it again after), its copies exactly those listed and unchanged, and the CLI's copy still there or still gone as the preview said. What it used is recorded in the usage history first (`recordNow`, its kept usage too); if that fails, nothing of it goes. A session whose last copy goes is deleted with its copies all or nothing (`trashAllOrNothing`: if its record can't be saved, its copies are put back from their spares, permanently deleted ones too; a crash in between leaves the spare, which the next purge keeps, above). What is left of a session Combwork no longer has goes with that id reserved, once no record or launch has it. Only plain files go from an attachments folder, and only from a real folder directly in the attachments folder. A deleted session's kept usage goes once the usage history has recorded it (`recordKept`).

#### 4.2.2 Antivirus scanning (#316)

Windows only, behind a platform-neutral status (`shared/antivirus.ts`, `main/antivirus.ts`, `components/Antivirus.tsx`): elsewhere it is "not applicable".

- **The folders**, worked out per workspace and always as resolved absolute paths (`realpath`, never `%VAR%` or `$env:`): the workspace root (its projects live in it), `<workspace>.worktrees` only once it exists, and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\combwork-test` only for people developing Combwork (an unpackaged build, or a workspace holding Combwork's repository: a project whose `package.json` is Combwork's repository's: `name` `combwork`, `productName` `Combwork`) and only once it exists. Each is resolved first and checked after resolving: one that is, or holds, a drive or a share's root, the home folder, the profile or a system folder (`unsafeFolder()`), or whose real location can't be established, is listed as not offered and never excluded; duplicates are dropped (`folderPlan()`).
- **Status** (`antivirus:status`): a read-only PowerShell probe without administrator rights (`Get-MpComputerStatus`, `Get-MpPreference`, Security Center's `AntiVirusProduct`, `Get-Volume` for the folders' drives), at most 20 s, off the UI's thread, cached ten minutes per workspace (Check Again refreshes). What scans: Defender (active, not passive), another antivirus (named; Combwork can't manage it), none, or unavailable (said, with why). Each folder: **excluded** or **scanned** when Defender's list is visible; **unknown** when Defender hides it (it shows it only to administrators, the usual case), or **added by Combwork** (unconfirmed) for one Combwork added; once read with administrator rights, the list as of that check. **Dev Drive**: without administrator rights only the volume's file system is known, so ReFS is a **maybe**; the administrator check (`fsutil devdrv query`) says whether it is a **trusted** Dev Drive or one that isn't trusted (scanned like any other), and Defender's `PerformanceModeStatus` (readable without rights) whether performance mode is on. **Slowed**: Defender with real-time protection on and a folder Combwork may offer that is neither known to be excluded nor on a trusted Dev Drive in performance mode. The cached status is probed again when the workspace's folder set changes (a worktrees folder appears); requests share a probe only for the same folder set and workspace lifetime, and an older probe finishing late never replaces a newer one's answer. Defender's hidden-list answer ("N/A: Must be an administrator…") is unknown from whichever read produced it (`readableList()`), never a list.
- **Changes**, only when the user asks, in two steps: `antivirus:prepare` works out the exact operation (the workspace, its lifetime, the action and its resolved folders), the dialog shows exactly those folders (one per line, with a Copy button) and the trade-off (excluded folders aren't scanned at all, `node_modules` and downloads included), and `antivirus:apply` runs that operation once (within ten minutes), refusing it if the window's workspace changed or the folders it would change now differ (a new set needs new consent, never an expansion). **Add Exclusions…** (the folders not known to be excluded), **Remove Combwork's Exclusions…** (only those Combwork added, its exclusions of folders that are gone included: #1389), **Check with Administrator Rights…** (reads the list and the Dev Drives). Each runs one elevated PowerShell (one UAC prompt; `Start-Process -Verb RunAs` with the whole script as its encoded command, the paths quoted literals, never a script file another process could change). The script reads Defender's list first, and changes nothing if that read is redacted (which exclusions already exist couldn't be known); it asks only for what is needed: Add skips a folder an existing exclusion (itself or a parent) covers, Remove takes only exact entries that are there, so the user's own exclusions are never removed; it then reads the list again. What Combwork added (`config.json` `antivirus.added`) is what Defender lists afterwards of what it asked for, never what was asked; the list read with administrator rights is kept only when it was read (a run that couldn't read it leaves the states unknown). Outcomes: done, **declined** (the prompt), **refused** by Defender, or a **policy** (an organisation's settings, or the change accepted but not listed afterwards). Never another antivirus; never silently; paths logged with `userText()`.
- **Where**: Settings → Workspace → **Antivirus scanning** (the status, each folder's, the actions, About Dev Drive with Microsoft's documentation); the Performance view (the workspace) says when scanning slows the workspace, linking there; the palette's **Antivirus Scanning of the Workspace**.
- **The suggestion**: when the window sees a reason (two or more agents running at once, or a command in the Progress panel that ran two minutes or more; and, while that lasts, an agent getting a worktree), it asks main (`antivirus:suggestion`), which suggests only when the workspace is slowed, wasn't declined for good (**Don't Ask Again**, per workspace, `antivirus.dismissed`) and these folders weren't offered in the last day (`antivirus.offered`: per workspace `{ offerKey, count, lastAt }`, the slowed folders as a key; #316's plain key reads as offered once).
