Folders not offered before (a worktrees folder appearing) are suggested at once with a new count; the same folders again as a reminder at most once a day (`REMIND_MS`, `nextOffer()` in `shared/antivirus.ts`), with no limit (#348): closing the toast or reviewing without adding postpones, only Don't Ask Again stops it, and a status no longer slowed (excluded, a trusted Dev Drive, Defender not active) suggests nothing. From the second time the toast says it's a reminder, at most once a day, and that Don't Ask Again stops it. The reply also says when a reminder may come (`remindAt`): while two or more agents keep running, the window asks again then (a timer it checks at least hourly, cleared when the reason goes); a long command is a reason once, each new one asking again, never a standing one. Main checks and claims the offer with nothing awaited in between, after the status is known, so two requests can't both offer and a Don't Ask Again given meanwhile holds. A toast with **Review…** and **Don't Ask Again**; answers for a workspace the window no longer shows are dropped.
- **A moved workspace** (#1302): Repair's plan (§3, Moved workspaces) has a **Microsoft Defender** group when Defender is the active antivirus, read on its own when the dialog opens (`workspace:moveDefender`, a fresh, uncached probe of the new folders and the old: `from` and `from.worktrees`). `defenderMovePlan` (shared) gives the old and new folders by kind with their states, and the change: `remove`, the old folders whose exclusion Combwork added and Defender lists for that folder itself (or, with the list hidden, Combwork's record); `add`, candidates: the new folders Combwork may offer (not unsafe) of those kinds, and any new folder Combwork's removed entries cover now (one moved inside the old folder), whatever their state shows (an administrator read may be stale, or the cover may be the entry being removed): the elevated run adds only those its live list, once the removals are made, doesn't cover; `theirs`, old folders listed by the user's own entries (named, never changed). An entry for a folder holding the old ones isn't stale (it may cover the new ones too): neither. Under the table, where the states come from, as the Antivirus panel says it (Defender's list now; Combwork's administrator read with its date, and that Repair's prompt reads the list again; or that only administrators can see it), and a new folder whose state is unknown is never called scanned. The box **Move Combwork's exclusions to the new folders (one administrator prompt)** is ticked when there is something to remove, and Repair can't be chosen until Defender has been read (the plan shows meanwhile), so the box's default is never skipped; with it (`MoveOptions.defender`, only from the dialog: Repair asked for otherwise never prompts), Repair works the plan out again last and runs one elevated `move` (removes only those exact entries, then adds the new folders the remaining list doesn't cover), and remembers what Defender lists afterwards as for Add and Remove. Its report line is done (*Moved Combwork's exclusions…: n removed, n added*), skipped (the prompt declined) or failed (refused, or accepted but not applied: a policy). `antivirus:prepare` never takes `move`. A move unticked, or its prompt declined or refused, still records the workspace as repaired: Combwork's old exclusions are then among its **exclusions of folders that are gone** (below), not offered by Repair again (#1389). A project moved on its own has no Defender group: Combwork only excludes the workspace, its worktrees and the test area, never a project folder (`tests/e2e/repairdefender.cjs`).
- **Exclusions of folders that are gone** (#1389, the Assistant's decision): the status (`gone`, `goneExclusions()`) lists those of Combwork's recorded exclusions (`antivirus.added`) whose folder doesn't exist (ENOENT, never a folder that can't be looked at), other than the workspace's own folders: with Defender's list known (live, or Combwork's administrator read), those it lists itself (exact entries, **Excluded**); hidden, every one, **Added by Combwork** (unconfirmed). The panel shows them under their own heading, and **Remove Combwork's Exclusions…** covers them (shown for them alone too): the elevated Remove takes only the exact entries listed. Each elevated run that reads the list (Add, Remove, Check, a move) forgets the gone ones Defender no longer lists. No pending move is kept: a declined, unticked or refused move, a folder deleted, an older Combwork's entry, all show the same way.
- **Tests never touch Defender**: a test copy (unpackaged, `CW_USER_DATA`) takes the probe's answer and the elevated changes' outcomes from `CW_TEST_ANTIVIRUS` (a fixture; changes act on a simulated list) and logs every call to `CW_TEST_ANTIVIRUS_LOG`; without a fixture it reports "test copy" and refuses changes (`tests/e2e/antivirus.cjs`, `tests/antivirus.test.ts`).

### 4.3 App data (`%APPDATA%/Combwork/`)

- <!-- old-name: begin spec-profile-folders -->**The profile folders** (HI-2461, part of the rename to Combwork, HI-2458): `%APPDATA%\Combwork` (settings, logs, usage, Chromium's storage) and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Combwork` (accounts and the connections' CLI homes); a dev build's are `Combwork-Dev`, a test profile's `CW_USER_DATA` (unchanged, as are internal areas such as `%LOCALAPPDATA%\combwork-test` and `combwork-updater`). Before 1.1 they were `Hive` and `Hive-Dev` (`shared/appName.ts` `profileFolder`; the old names only the names upgrade's input, `nameUpgradeProfile.ts` `oldProfileFolder`).
- **Which folders a run uses** (`profileFolders.ts`, in `index.ts` before `userData` is set): Combwork's only (HI-2594). The installer moves 1.0's to Combwork's, with the app closed (HI-2460; §11.1, The install identity, says how). Where it didn't (its rename failed, or a dev build, which no installer moves), the names upgrade's profile step does it at start, each of the two folders on its own and by the installer's rule: Combwork's when it is a folder; else, Combwork's confirmed missing (ENOENT, ENOTDIR) and the old one a folder, one rename of the old one to it, never a copy or a delete; neither there, a new profile, made as usual. Both there: Combwork's, the old one left as it is. A Combwork folder that can't be looked at (no permission, an I/O error) is never taken for missing: it is used, and the reason logged. **A move it can't make refuses the start** (*Combwork couldn't move its data folder*, an error box naming both folders and the reason, in English, as nothing of the profile has been read): an old one that can't be looked at, a file under Combwork's name, a rename that fails (a 1.0 still running holds it). Both stay as they were; the next start tries again. No blank Combwork profile is ever made in its place, which would win at every later start. `accountsRoot()` follows the local choice. Nothing is logged until the profile is set; the choice (or the move) is logged then.
- **What the user is told** (`profileNotices.ts`, after the first window loads), **after a move of the local folder**, once: the mover puts `profile-move.json` (`{ v: 1, from, movedAt, by: "installer" | "app" }`, the contract with HI-2460) in the old local folder just before renaming it, so it reaches the new local folder with the rename or not at all (one already there, the installer's from a rename of its that failed, is kept and moves); while it lacks `signInChecked`, Combwork's connections are checked, and those that show signed out are named in one notice, to sign in again in Settings → Accounts & Connections (Combwork never signs in for the user). The record is written back with all its fields, `signInNamed` (the connections already named) and, once every check answered, `signInChecked: true`; a check without an answer, or a failed write, leaves it to try again next start, never naming one twice. A record that can't be read or isn't a mover's is left exactly as it is.
- **The installer's ask to close** (`build/askToClose.ps1`) writes its request into `%APPDATA%\Combwork` when that exists, else `%APPDATA%\Hive` (a 1.0 being replaced).<!-- old-name: end spec-profile-folders -->

- `config.json` — settings, recent workspaces, active projects per workspace, window state. Version 2 keeps each provider's settings in `settings.providers[<id>]` and plan usage per provider and limit. Before the first version-2 save, the 0.1 file is copied to `config.v1-backup.json`, and the 0.1 `settings.claude` block is still written, so 0.1 can read the file again. Version 3 (0.3) moves the Assistant's model and effort, when still at 0.2's saved defaults, to the agents' (§6.5). Written compact (no indentation), with its `.bak` at the first save of a run only (`writeKeptJson`'s options: the other kept files are unchanged), since #1111.
- `ui-state.json` — UI state and caches out of config.json (#1111): each workspace's board folds (`ui.boardFold`), each project's Session tab as this user left it (`ui.projectViews`, HI-1749: Panes or Tiles, its layout and pane placement, by the project's id, else its folder; never in its project.json, so another program holding that file can't make a view switch fail: a project.json from before keeps its view until its first read takes it here, and its next write leaves it out) and each provider's model catalog (`modelCatalogs`). Written before config.json, only when they changed; read over config.json's at start (a config.json from before still has them, and its first save moves them here). Missing or damaged, it is a cache lost: the folds reset and the catalogs come from the CLIs again.
- `agent-api.json` — Agent API token.
- `usage-cache.json` — retired (#1106): an older version kept each transcript's usage here; it is removed once a workspace's usage history has imported its sessions (§9).
- `merge-slots/<hash of the workspace path>.json` — which agents held a merge slot (§6.2), with the folder each holder works in (`cwd`: its worktree or the main checkout, #984), so a hold Combwork closed under is reported when the workspace opens again, naming that folder; after an unexpected close it is a line of that notice (below) instead of a notice of its own.
- `running.json` — **Combwork closing unexpectedly** (#984, `lastRun.ts`, `shared/unexpectedClose.ts`): written by the running Combwork (the copy holding the single-instance lock) once it is ready, every minute (`HEARTBEAT_MS`), 2 s after agents start or stop, and 2 s after a process joins a running launch's job (#1134: the job host tells main with a line `new` from its completion port, `onLaunchProcessJoined`, once per launch until main lists that launch's job again or it starts (a listing never takes back a notice due for another launch), so a build starting hundreds of processes asks for one write; one write at a time, the asks in between coalesced): `{ version, pid, startedAt, lastSeen, app, workspaces, agents: [{ workspace, projectPath, project, agentId, agentName, provider, sessionId, sessionName }], processes: [{ projectPath, agentId, agentName, runId, processes: [{ pid, name, label, created }] }] }` (the Assistant's own session isn't an agent), written beside it (compact, and asynchronously since #1111: it was a synchronous write on every status change) and renamed into place, checked just before the rename with nothing awaited between, so a marker removed as Combwork quits is never put back. `processes` (#987, `runningProcesses()` in `agentProcesses.ts`) is what each running launch's process job holds then (§ leftover processes, #507): its CLI and all it started, each by id and start time (one without a start time isn't kept), at most 100 launches and 50 processes each (as `leftovers.json`), listed from the jobs before each write, one write at a time. HI-2263: a launch whose job can't be listed then (the tracker ending as it lists), or that was running when the tracker was lost, is written with its processes as last listed, until that launch ends; the next start keeps only those still running as the same processes, as for any other. Removed on `will-quit` (every quit: the quit flow, Restart Combwork, an update's install, a crashed window's Quit Combwork) and on a window's `session-end` (Windows ending the session), and not written again. Found at the next start, the last run ended without quitting: Combwork logs it, Copy Diagnostics says so (last seen, started, agents, a crash dump, merges), and once the first window has loaded a warning notice, **Combwork closed unexpectedly**, says **Combwork was last seen on <date> at <time>**, how many agents were running in which projects, **Nothing was resumed** (or how many were, below), that a crash dump of that run was kept (#985: one made since it started), and each merge slot hold it closed under with its folder. #987: of the marker's `processes`, those still running as the same processes (id and start time, checked by the tracker's helper: never by name, a pid alone never counts) and not already listed as left running (`leftovers.json`, #614, offered on their own) are told in a line, **<n> processes the agents started are still running: <labels>.**, with a **Stop Them** button (`session.stopLeftAfterClose` → `app:stopLeftAfterClose`: ends each only while it is still the same process; those that still run after it stay, and the call fails saying how many). #1008: each kept process also has its `parent` (pid) and, on a cw-progress process (Combwork's executable running `cw-progress.js`), `run`: its `--title`, else its command. A cw-progress run is one item of the line, **<title> (<n> processes)**, with every kept process below it (by parent, each started after its parent) and the shell above it that ran the `cw-progress` command; Stop Them ends that whole tree as it is then, what it started since the marker was written too (`endtree`, `PickTree`: from the run's top and each of its processes still running, each only while it is still that process; below them by the parent ids of a snapshot, each child only if it still runs, started after its parent and not after the snapshot; each checked through a handle held until it is ended, so its id can't name another process meanwhile; a root gone or that can't be opened isn't followed). What it couldn't end stays listed with the rest: Stop Them then fails saying how many still run, and tries them again. #1028: a child that runs and Windows lets Combwork neither end nor check (PickTree's `unverified`, its pid in `endtree`'s reply) can't be tried again (with its parent ended, nothing tells it from a process that later gets the id, and Combwork never stops by pid alone or by name), so it is kept apart (`Leftovers.unverified`, `stopLeftovers`, in `LeftoverStops`, whose clicks take turns so one that overlaps another, twice quickly or from two windows, works on what the one before it left and can't drop its ids): every click after fails while any is kept, saying it may still run with its process IDs to look for in Task Manager (`main.unexpectedClose.notChecked`, or `notStoppedNorChecked` beside ones Stop Them does try again), never a quiet success; the roots are still ended (Stop Them ends the run, not keeping it alive for a child it may never reach), and Copy Diagnostics says how many with their ids; nothing is stopped on its own, whatever `agents.leftoverProcesses` says (that is for what agents leave as they stop while Combwork runs). Its buttons are also **Resume All** (`session.resumeAfterClose` → `app:resumeAfterClose`: those agents, once, one at a time, each into the conversation it was in, skipping one running again or with none; the result is a notice) and **Show Overview**. Nothing resumes on its own unless **Settings → Sessions → Resume agents after an unexpected close** (`sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedClose`, **off**; Darren's 17 Oct decision) is on: then they are resumed first and the notice says how many (and which couldn't, with why). Each workspace of that run whose Assistant is set up (`.combwork/assistant/project.json`) gets a `control` delivery from Combwork for its next start: when Combwork was last seen, the agents, whether anything was resumed, how many processes the agents started still run (#987), and to check for stalled card loops and tell the user without restarting or stopping anything. A marker that can't be read is an unexpected close at its file's time, with no agents known. This machine's state: never in the workspace's `.combwork`.
- `restart.json` — **Restarts announced and resumed** (HI-1707, `restartResume.ts`, `shared/restartResume.ts`). **As Combwork closes** (`quitNow`, before the sessions stop): the agents that are working, waiting, `background` or `watching`, or the builder or reviewer of a running lane (`laneOf`), each with its session, card (the lane's current one, else the one it works on or reviews in Doing or Review: its key, else #n) and round (`roundOf`) and lane, are recorded (`recordClosing`): first every running conversation, from the live states alone with nothing read (`baseEntries`), written at once; then, within 2 s, narrowed to those working, waiting, in the background, watching or in a running lane, with their cards and lanes (`enrich`); a read that takes longer keeps every conversation (an idle agent resumed is a lesser harm than a working one lost). The record is **who** and **how** (the Assistant's design call, 26 Oct): its entries are who is resumed, and carry no reason of their own; `reason` is how, one for the whole record, and every close overwrites it, so the latest close decides. An entry leaves only once its agent is ready (`resumed`); one not yet resumed at a close (queued, starting or offered) is `pending` again as it was, with its conversation, card, round and lane: one being resumed is never replaced by its launch, still starting and in no lane. The record: `{ version: 1, reason, entries: [{ workspace, projectPath, project, agentId, agentName, provider, sessionId, sessionName?, status, card?: { label, round }, lane?: { id, name, role }, from, at, state, why?, changedAt }] }` (a record with no `reason` it knows is a quit's). `reason` is `install` (an installer's request, below), `update` (Restart to Update, or Install automatically), `restart` (Restart Combwork) or `quit`; for all but `quit` each is told, best effort within 1.5 s, by a `control` delivery from Combwork: *Combwork is restarting for an update. Your work is saved; you'll be resumed.* A new snapshot merges into the record (`mergeSnapshot`): an agent in it replaces its earlier entry, every other open entry is kept (an offer not answered isn't lost); entries this run had queued, starting or offered go back to `pending`. The Assistant's own session isn't an agent here. **At the next start** (`loadRestartRecord` before the unexpected-close check, `startRestartRecovery` once the first window has loaded): entries the last run left `queued` or `starting` are `pending` again, and one over a day old is `skipped` (`atStart`); `held` ones are offered again. A `pending` entry is decided once **its workspace is ready**: open, read (`info()`: a window sets its path before its workspace is read) and its merge slots recovered (`workspaceRecovering`, from ipc.ts' `onOpened`, as the unexpected-close notice waits for them). It is queued when the record's `reason` isn't `quit` and **Settings → Advanced → Resume agents after an update** (`cw.restart.resumeAfterUpdate`, **on**; a workspace can set its own, as can *Resuming after a restart: ready within*) is on for its workspace, else `offered`: one notice, **Resume the <n> agents that were working?**, naming them, with **Resume** (`session.resumeRestart` → `app:resumeRestart`: queues them) and **Don't Resume** (`session.dismissRestart` → `app:dismissRestart`: `dismissed`, not offered again; the notice's × only closes it, and an `offered` entry is offered again at the next start). **One offer at a time** (HI-2356): a workspace ready later (its slots recovered after another's offer was shown) gives a new notice listing every entry `offered` now, and the earlier notice, its buttons not used, resolves as *Replaced by a newer offer*, so no notice's buttons act on agents it didn't name (both act on every `offered` entry). Resume takes its notice's buttons away at once (*Resuming, one at a time*) and the queue's report then says in it how it went; an offer still open at the report keeps its buttons. **The queue** (one owner of these resumes: `lastRun.ts` leaves out the agents with an open entry, `ownsResume`) takes one entry at a time whose workspace is open (Darren, 26 Oct: one at a time, each after the last is ready; no load check), checks it again just before it starts (the agent still there, `skipped: removed`; not running, `skipped: running`; its conversation still its last, `skipped: movedOn`; no slot hold, `held`, as `resumeAgents`), starts it in its conversation (`--resume`, `auto`) with its note as its first prompt (`resumeNote`: why, from which version to which and when, its card, round and lane, and to re-arm its watch if it was watching or in a lane), and waits until it has taken it: seen `working`, `finished`, `waiting` or `background` in a status change of this launch, within **Settings → Advanced → Resuming after a restart: ready within** (`cw.restart.resumeReadySeconds`, 90 s; not `ready`, which a resumed conversation's transcript gives before its CLI runs, nor `watching`, which a watch it had gives). Not in time: that launch (by its `runId`, never another) is stopped and ended (`stopWhereAndWait`, 10 s) and confirmed gone before the next starts, `failed: notReady`; one still running after that is `failed: notStopped`, and nothing more is admitted until it has ended (a `session-exit` goes on). Its launch ending meanwhile (stopped, or its CLI exited) is `failed: stopped`. **Combwork closing** (`stopRestartRecovery`, `recordClosing`: a generation bumped) cancels the attempt under way: it is checked after every await and just before the start (its workspace still ready, the agent still there and not running, its conversation still its last), starts nothing and changes nothing after (the closing snapshot has put it back to `pending`); its workspace closing puts it back to `pending`. A call for the queue while it works is never lost: it goes round again. Every state change is written at once; the record is removed once every entry is `resumed`, `failed`, `dismissed` or `skipped`. Once the queue is empty, one notice says who was resumed and who wasn't and why, and each workspace's Assistant (set up) gets a `control` delivery saying the same. **Lanes:** while an entry is queued or starting, or `pending` to resume by itself (from when the record was read), at most 10 min, the card stall "isn't running" (`cardStall`, the Agent API's `stalled` and `reviewStalled`) and the merge stall of a builder that isn't running aren't reported for that agent. **The installer's request** (`build/askToClose.ps1`, run by `installer.nsh`'s `customInit` in the outer instance, before the template's check ends a running Combwork): it finds the main Combwork process of `$INSTDIR` only (its exact executable, no `--type=`), opens a handle on it, writes `%APPDATA%\Combwork\restart-request.json` (1.0's profile folder when that is the only profile: a 1.0 being replaced, §4.3) (beside, then renamed: `{ v: 1, nonce: <GUID>, pid, pidCreated, exe, reason: 'install', at }`), waits up to 3 s for `restart-ack-<nonce>.json`, then up to 30 s for that process to exit; no acknowledgement, it removes its request; either way the template's check then runs as before. Combwork (`watchRestartRequests`: the profile watched, and checked at start) takes a request only when it is at most 4 KB, whole, with a GUID nonce, for its own `pid` and start (within 5 s of `Date.now() - uptime`), its own executable (real paths) and at most 60 s old, and its nonce not handled before; it renames it to `restart-request.<nonce>.taken`, writes the acknowledgement (beside, then renamed) and quits as for an update with no dialog (`quitReason = 'install'`). Any other request is removed with a log line saying why, never acted on; what earlier requests left is removed at start. **An older installer** (or one whose wait ran out) ends Combwork without asking: its running marker remains, and when it names another version than the one starting now its agents are added to the record as an install's (`adoptInstalledRun`: no card or lane known), resumed as above; the unexpected-close notice still says Combwork closed unexpectedly, without offering those.
- **A window's page that crashes or hangs** (`main/rendererWatch.ts`, per window): agents run in main, so they are never affected. On `render-process-gone` (except a clean exit) Combwork logs the reason and reloads the page; terminals reattach to their running sessions as after View → Reload, the window keeps its workspace, and a toast says "Combwork's window stopped and was reloaded. Your agents kept running." with how many files' unsaved edits were lost (the window's last report; hot exit would keep them). A second crash within a minute doesn't reload again: a native dialog says "Combwork's window stopped working. Your agents are still running…" with **Reload**, **Open Logs** (then asks again) and **Quit Combwork**. On `unresponsive`, after 4 seconds a native dialog offers **Wait** / **Reload**; `responsive` closes it. Reload ends the hung page (`forcefullyCrashRenderer`) and loads it again, without the crash note.
- `logs/combwork.log` — **Help → Copy Diagnostics…** puts its last 50 lines in a bug report, with Combwork's version and update channel (stable/beta), installed or development build, Windows version, display scaling and locale; each coding agent (on/off, version and path, signed in, update available, anything its adapter adds (`diagnostics()`: Codex's Windows sandbox, default/non-admin/not set up), and its readiness issues); counts (windows, active and total projects, agents, running agents, agents in worktrees, whether the Assistant runs); how each worker thread runs (HI-1880: its own thread, started and not running yet, on main's thread and why, ended and why, or not started yet); and the settings that change behaviour (file locks, merge style, quitting, tray, backups, cache TTL, Agent API, Assistant control, notifications, theme), never free text. A dialog shows exactly what will be copied; **Copy** copies it. It is built and redacted in main (`diagnostics.ts`, `shared/redact.ts`). Combwork marks the user's own text as it logs it (`userText()` in `logger.ts`: card titles, Assistant activity, session, project, agent and branch names, paths; of the arguments an agent is started with, everything but flags and the values of known flags such as `--model` and `--session-id`, whether separate or written as `--flag=value` (`argsForLog()`)), and the report replaces each marked span with `<text>` or `<path>`. Its start line says so (`your text marked`); lines from a run whose start line doesn't (an older version), or from before the first start line in view, keep only their time, level and scope. For older lines and anything unmarked: the home folder becomes `~`, workspace and worktree folders `<workspace>`, including the workspaces in the recent list; workspace, project, agent and branch names, and the project folders of recent workspaces, are taken out of the log lines (not the summary, which has none, so a project called "Combwork" doesn't take Combwork's name with it; each line's time, level and `[scope]` stay); any other absolute path becomes `<path>` unless it is under AppData, a dot folder in the home folder, Program Files or Windows; tokens, keys, everything after a credential's name in a line (`Authorization:`, `token=`, `--api-key`, `password:`, and the lines a continuation carries it onto; a quoted JSON key too), OAuth codes in URLs, sign-in and device codes (`maskText`, #699), well-known key formats, JWTs, long hex or base64 runs and email addresses are masked.
- `Crashpad/` — crash dumps (#985, `exitLog.ts`): Electron's `crashReporter` is started before the app is ready (in the copy that holds the single-instance lock), with `crashDumps` set to the profile's `Crashpad` folder and **`uploadToServer: false`**: a crash of the main process, a window's page or a helper process leaves a minidump in `Crashpad\reports`, and nothing is ever sent. At start Combwork keeps the newest three dumps and removes the rest (#1111: one was 73 MB), as old heap snapshots are, not to the Recycle Bin; the start line is followed by how many were removed, how many dumps the profile has and the newest's time; Copy Diagnostics has a **Crash dumps** section naming how many, the newest by file name, time and size (never the dump itself), and that they are never sent: the user attaches one to an issue themselves.
- **Every way out is logged** (#985, `exitLog.ts`, scope `[exit]`; the logger's lines are written by a thread of their own (HI-1730, `logWriter.ts`: a disk that holds writes up, such as a System Restore point freezing the profile's drive, holds that thread, not the main process; in order, rotated as before; past 8 MB waiting, lines are dropped and the count logged), and at the process's exit what it hasn't written is written at once (`flushLogs`), so a line is on disk when the process goes): `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` with their stack; `render-process-gone` and `child-process-gone` for every page and helper process (reason, exit code, type; a clean exit as info, any other as an error); the PC going to sleep, shutting down, the screen locking and unlocking (`powerMonitor`; waking is logged where Combwork acts on it, `power.ts`); Windows asking to end the session and ending it, with its reasons (one line for all windows); `before-quit`, `will-quit`, `quit` with its exit code, and the main process's `exit`. Every place Combwork's main process ends or restarts the app (`app.quit`, `app.exit`, `process.exit`, `app.relaunch`, the updater's `quitAndInstall`) goes through `exitBy(how, caller, act)`, which logs `Leaving by <how>: <caller>` first; a unit test fails on such a call outside it (the combwork MCP server and `cw-progress` are processes of their own and aren't counted). A run whose log ends with none of these lines was ended from outside (killed) or lost its power.
- **The main process's memory** (#1005, after #988's V8 heap out-of-memory crash; `memory.ts`, scope `[memory]`): an INFO line at start (after the crash dumps line), every 5 minutes and in the `exit` line: used and total heap, the heap limit and the share used, external, array buffers and rss, in MB (`v8.getHeapStatistics()`, `process.memoryUsage()`). When the used heap rises past 70% or 85% of the limit, that line is a WARN saying so, once per crossing (it warns again only after falling back below). Copy Diagnostics has a **Memory** section: the memory now, whether snapshots are on, the snapshots kept (count, newest's time and size, never attached) and the last six memory lines, which the log's last 50 lines may not reach.
- **The main process's stalls** (#1109, `mainStalls.ts`, scope `[main]`): a WARN when the main process was busy for more than 250 ms (every terminal's typing goes through it), at most one a minute (the next counts the stalls left out). The delay is Node's event loop delay (`monitorEventLoopDelay`, a 20 ms timer, so a block between two of the half-second checks counts too), or how late the check's own timer ran, whichever is longer; with no delay recorded since the last check (Node's reset forgets its timer's last turn, so a block begun before the next turn isn't measured: HI-2317), the whole time since the last check. A gap that spans the PC's sleep isn't a stall: the line waits 3 s, and a powerMonitor `suspend` or `resume` from a second before the gap began to then makes it an INFO line instead (`paused for N ms while the PC slept: not counted as busy`), but for a resume before the gap began, and the events before it: that sleep was over (HI-2317, the same for a slow file call's probe); `performance.now()` counts the time asleep, which gave warnings of up to 18 s on an idle Combwork. The warning names the work that overlapped the stall, the synchronous steps first (one held the thread itself; the calls overlapping it may only have waited behind it, HI-1692), then the most overlap first, up to five and a count of the rest: IPC calls (`ipc <channel>`, wrapped in `ipc.ts`), Agent API requests (`api <method> <route template>`, from when the request comes in until its response closes) and hooks (`hook <event>` from the events the CLIs send, else `hook (other event)`, or `hook status line`), and the synchronous steps that can wait (HI-1692, `stallWork.ts`'s `timedStep`: `db open <file>`, `db begin <file>` (BEGIN IMMEDIATE's busy wait), `db commit <file>`, `db transaction <file>`, `kept file read <file>`; and `log write <log>`, noted only when a log write took 50 ms or more), each with how long it took and whether it is still running, or says nothing marked was under way. A stall that Combwork's watchdog thread had too (`stallWatchdog.ts`: a thread that only ticks, noting gaps in its own ticks) is the whole process paused (the PC asleep without powerMonitor telling, the process suspended): an INFO line, `paused for N ms with the rest of Combwork's process … not counted as busy`. Work is named however long it has run (a handler can wake from an await, block, and await again), except the requests that wait by design (`GET /v1/events`, `POST /v1/tasks/wait`, `POST /v1/agents/wait`), which would crowd out the rest (Darren's choice, 20 Oct). Combwork can't see which of them held the main process, so the line is evidence to read, not a verdict: with many long requests open at once, the cause may be among those counted. The work a stall overlapped is kept when the stall is found, so traffic before the warning is decided can't push it out; and the main thread's CPU time over it (`process.threadCpuUsage()`: a stall with little CPU was waiting, on the disk, a child process or a lock). Fixed names only, never the user's text. Tests: `CW_TEST_BLOCK_IPC` holds the main process in an IPC call, and `CW_TEST_STALL_QUIET_MS` shortens the minute (unpackaged builds).
  - **In the Performance view** (HI-1135): every stall the warning would be for (not the pauses), logged or left out by the minute's limit, is kept in memory as it is found, the last 50 since Combwork started and a count of all (`keepStall`, `recentStalls`; `performance:stalls`, read by the window, nothing pushed). Each keeps its end, its length, the main thread's CPU as the line has it (null where Node can't tell; it is measured from the half second before, so it can exceed the length), and its work as the line finds it, copied when kept (labels made, lengths fixed: the work's whole length, as the line says it, and whether it was still running): the synchronous steps apart from the other work, each label once with how many there were and their total (the Assistant's screenshot review: a burst of one call crowded out the rest), the longest total first, five labels each and how many works the rest had. The workspace's Performance page shows them under **Main process stalls** ("since Combwork started": no range or filter applies), newest first: When, Length, Main thread CPU ("mostly waiting" under half the length; unknown CPU is never that), Step and During it (the overlapping work, context rather than a proven cause). The slow file calls (below) aren't in it.
- **The main process's thread pool** (HI-1702, `threadPool.ts`, `mainStalls.ts`): main's libuv thread pool has 16 threads, not Node's 4. Every asynchronous file call of main's and of its worker threads takes one (and so do zlib, crypto and DNS), so with 4 a few slow calls (a large read, a file the antivirus holds) made every window's file work wait, and a step that awaits many calls in turn took seconds: with eight pool jobs always running, a second window's open took 1.6 s instead of 0.25 s, the work after it 6 s instead of 0.2 s and a session listing 400 ms instead of 40 ms; with 16, 0.3 s, 0.2 s and 50 ms. `threadPool.ts` is imported first by main's entry: it sets `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE` (a size the user set is kept), starts the pool with a stat and removes the variable again, so no process Combwork starts inherits it. A WARN when a file call took more than 250 ms to end, at most one a minute (the next counts the ones left out), with the work under way as the stall warning names it (`A file call took N ms to end (timed off main's thread): it waited for the thread pool … or for the disk`). The call is a stat every second on the stall watchdog's thread (`stallWatchdog.ts`), which only ticks, so main's thread being busy meanwhile isn't in it (that is the stall warning's; timed on main, a stall after the probe began was taken for the pool's, HR2's round 1 of HI-1702); the pool's wait and the disk's can't be told apart, so the line names both. A probe that a powerMonitor `suspend` or `resume`, or a pause of the whole process (a gap in the watchdog's ticks), covered isn't counted, decided 3 s later. Tests: `CW_TEST_STALL_QUIET_MS` shortens the minute here too; the stalls suite holds pool threads with reads of a pipe nobody writes to, and holds main's thread with the pool free (no such line).
- **Worker threads** (HI-1880, `workerThreads.ts`): the usage history, git, the repository lock, the WAL checkpoints, the stall watchdog and the log's writer each run on a thread of their own, their scripts built beside main's (`electron.vite.config.ts`). In an installed Combwork those are inside `app.asar`, which original-fs sees as one file, so whether a script is there is asked with `bundledScriptExists()`: a script in an archive is there when the archive is (a Worker reads it through Electron's archive support); elsewhere the file is looked for. Without its script (unit tests) a worker's work runs on main's thread (the usage history, the repository lock) or not at all. A worker thread can't load Electron, so a worker's code imports nothing that does (`tests/workerImports.test.ts`; path helpers it needs are in `places.ts`, not `fsutil.ts`, whose logger loads Electron). Copy Diagnostics lists how each runs; the `packaged-workers` e2e suite checks each is its own thread in `dist/win-unpacked`. Until 1.0.0-rc.9, an installed build ran none of them.
- `heap/` — heap snapshots (#1005), only with **Settings → Advanced → Save a memory snapshot if Combwork is about to run out of memory** (`cw.heapSnapshotNearLimit`, off; applies when Combwork restarts, read from advanced.json at start like hardware acceleration). On, Combwork deletes all but the newest snapshot there, makes it the main process's working folder (Node writes the snapshot to `--diagnostic-dir`, which only its command line sets, or else the working folder; nothing in main relies on its working folder) and calls `v8.setHeapSnapshotNearHeapLimit(1)`: as the heap nears its limit Node writes one `Heap.<date>.<time>.<pid>.0.001.heapsnapshot` before the crash, so the folder holds at most two. The start logs the snapshots there and that they are on. A snapshot is about three times the heap's size and holds whatever main had in memory (card text, transcripts, possibly tokens): it stays on the PC; deleting old ones doesn't go to the Recycle Bin.

### 4.4 Schemas

```jsonc
// <Workspace>/.combwork/workspace.json
{ "version": 1, "mcp": { "enabled": ["github"], "model": 2, "assistant": [], "assistantModel": 3 },   // enabled: #1093's switch, frozen since HI-2059 (read only for projects not converted); assistant: added for the Assistant
  "hiddenProjects": [ { "name": "old-site", "mode": "hidden", "at": "…" } ] }   // hidden | removed (§6.7)

// A card (#12) as the board keeps it: its JSON document, one row of .combwork/combwork.db (#1017); Export Board to JSON writes it as 12.json
{ "number": 12, "title": "…", "description": "…markdown…", "project": "web", "agent": "a-7b21e4aa", "agentName": "Agent 2",
  "column": "todo",                     // todo | doing | review | done
  "order": 3.5, "labels": ["ui"], "blocked": null, "blockedBy": [11], "links": [],
  "comments": [ { "at": "…", "by": "Agent 2 (web)", "text": "…" } ],
  "history": [ { "at": "…", "by": "You", "what": "Moved to Doing" } ],
  "archived": false, "archivedFor": "user",   // user | done | project-hidden | project-removed
  "createdAt": "…", "createdBy": "Assistant", "updatedAt": "…" }

// <Project>/.combwork/project.json
{
  "version": 2,                          // 2 since 0.2.0: reading an older file clears its agents and layout
  "mcp":    { "enabled": ["github"] },   // the project's own choice (#1093); "disabled" is from before it, emptied once moved
  "chime": "inherit",                     // inherit | on | off
  // Before HI-2106: "defaultProvider" and "providers" (per-provider model, effort, mode, extra arguments, context);
  // the accounts migration moves them into its agents' connections and removes them (with 0.1's flat fields).
  "agents": [ { "id": "a-7b21e4aa", "name": "Reviewer", "provider": "codex", "connection": "c-91f0a2d3", "role": "reviewer", … } ],   // none at first; role: free text (#126), empty = its name; connection: a connection's id (HI-2106), provider: its account's CLI
  "migrations": { "accounts1": { "at": "…" } },   // HI-2106's migration, done; connections1: HI-1770's move, kept for its notice
  "layout": "auto",                      // the Session tab's layout (one for the project, #134): auto (the one that shows its agents, up to the 3×2 grid) | single | columns2 | columns3 | grid | grid6; replaces 0.2 builds' sessionLayout
  // Until HI-2106's migration, 0.1's flat model/effort/permissionMode/extraArgs were still written (Claude Code's values) for downgrades.
}

// A project's session records (#1061): rows of the workspace's combwork.db (store `sessions`, under the project's id; the
// Assistant's under `assistant`), one per record, deleted id and deleted session's usage, so a change writes only what it
// changed. Moved in from <Project>/.combwork/sessions.json the first time Combwork reads them (kept as sessions.json.imported-<time>);
// one found later is moved in only if the project has no records there (a folder brought back after Remove from Combwork),
// else kept unread. Remove from Combwork writes them back into the folder's sessions.json (in one write transaction of the database,
// so no change, from any process, is lost between) and marks them exported: while the project is removed, nothing here reads that file; Restore moves it
// back in, with any record made meanwhile; another workspace opening the folder moves it in there. A folder copied or
// moved by hand starts with none, as its cards do. Each in the file's form:
{ "version": 1, "sessions": [ { "id": "…", "agent": "claude-code", "agentId": "a2", "name": "…",
  "createdAt": "…", "lastActiveAt": "…", "archived": false,
  "transcriptPath": "…",        // Codex: where its rollout file is (it can't be found from the folder)
  "titleAtRename": "…",         // the CLI's own name for it (/rename) when it was last renamed in Combwork (null: none)
  "handedOverFrom": "…" } ],    // the session whose work was handed over to this one (Hand Over to…)
  "deleted": ["…"] }              // sessions deleted in Combwork: the CLI still has them, so Combwork keeps them hidden
```
