## 5. Settings resolution

**Skills** — no switches: every Combwork skill in `<Workspace>/.combwork/skills` goes to every session of its audience (§7.1). The 0.1 lists (`workspace.json` `skills.enabled`, `project.json` `skills.disabled`) are dropped when the file is next saved.

**MCP**

```
added(project)    = project.json mcp.enabled                       // converted (mcp.model 3)
                  = project.json mcp.enabled ∩ legacy              // not yet converted: #1093's meaning (legacy: workspace.json mcp.enabled, frozen)
effective(project, agent) = added(project) ∩ agent's choice (all, unless it chose some)
```

- **Available, then added or not** (HI-2059, Darren's decisions of 29 Oct, replacing #1093's workspace switch and per-project switches): "what's available locally and either added or not". A server in `<Workspace>/.combwork/mcp` is **available** to every project and the Assistant and **runs only where it is added**: a project (`project.json` `mcp.enabled`, meaning added once `mcp.model` is 3), the Assistant (`workspace.json` `mcp.assistant`, added once `mcp.assistantModel` is 3). **No switches anywhere**, and no master switch: Add and Remove are the only actions. Two layers: the place (project or Assistant) and the agent (#537, below). `shared/agentMcp.ts` holds the rule (`mcpAdded`, `assistantMcpAdded`, `mcpOnInProject`, `serverOnIn` for a listed server); launches (`sessions.effectiveHere`), the Agent API and the window all use it. A list Combwork can't read adds nothing, nor does a `legacy` list it can't read.
- **Adding one to the workspace** (Add MCP Server from File, New MCP Server, a replace) adds it **added nowhere**, with **no questions** (the name and Replace step stays). **Copy to workspace** (a server a project defines in its own `.mcp.json`) is the exception: its dialog shows what each runs, so it is copied and added to that project only; one whose definition changed after it was shown is copied added nowhere. A server added, replaced or deleted is removed from every place it was added under its name (hidden projects' too, and the Assistant: `removeEverywhere`), so an old choice never adds a new definition. It **fails closed** (HI-2059 round 1): every project's file is read first, strictly (`membershipOf`: only the project's own settings, read and parsed now from its current text, count as membership; one that is there but can't be read or doesn't parse, such as a file partway through a save, is an error, never "no servers", and a kept-file backup or default never stands in for it: HI-2059 rounds 1 and 2), and a project that can't be read refuses the replace, create, copy or delete before anything is written or moved (`mcp.error.cannotClear`), so the old definition stays as it was and no new one runs under an old Add; a delete clears the places before its file goes to the Recycle Bin.
- **Add** (`addMcpTo`, IPC `mcp:add`): a project's MCP tab's **Add Server…** and the Assistant view's **+** open a picker (`McpServerPicker`) of the workspace's servers not yet added there, with search and filter; the one chosen shows what it runs and any literal-secret warning (adding is when it can first run), and **Add** carries the definition and revision shown (§7.2), refused if either changed since ("Check what it runs and add it again"), or if the definition can't run (no `command` or `url`). The target is checked in the turn: a project of this workspace whose `project.json` is there (`mcp.error.noProject`); the write never makes a project's folder. **Remove** (`removeMcpFrom`, `mcp:remove`) is at once, with no question: one Add puts it back.
- **Add to…** (a server's view in the MCP view, `setMcpPlaces`, `mcp:places`): the projects it is added to, ticked, then **Assistant**, with **All projects** and **No projects** (the Assistant only by its own box); **Save** adds where ticked and removes where unticked. Every place it changes, removals too, is checked before the first write (this workspace's project, its file readable; the definition the one shown when it adds anywhere), then one write per place, each checked again: the files are written one by one, so a failure midway leaves the earlier ones written, and the reply (`McpPlacesResult`: `added`, `removed`, `failed` with why) is shown as it is, never as all-or-nothing.
- **Every write** that changes a place's list is the locked read-modify-write (`mutateProjectConfig` with `existing`, `saveWorkspaceConfigWith`), works the list out from what runs now (`mcpAdded`), writes it with the marker (`model`/`assistantModel` 3), and changes nothing else in the file.
- **Upgrading (HI-2059; once per file):** as a workspace opens, after #1093's move and before any launch (`mcpSettled`), each project (hidden ones too) is converted on its own: `added = enabled ∩ workspace.json mcp.enabled`, what ran, written with `model: 3` in the same locked write; then the Assistant's (`assistant ∩ enabled`, `assistantModel: 3`). A choice kept while the workspace had a server off is dropped (it wasn't running). There is no workspace-wide "done": a project whose write fails, or a hidden project that can't be read, keeps #1093's meaning through the same reader (`legacy`, workspace.json's `mcp.enabled`, kept frozen and never written again), so nothing that didn't run starts, and is tried again at the next open; Add, Remove and the deletes convert such a project in the same write as their change. Choices dropped are counted (`mcp.droppedNotice`) and said once, quietly, in the workspace's window (`sayMcpAddedOnce`). **Nothing that runs changes.**
- **Migration from before #1093 (once, when a workspace opens):** `workspace.json` without `mcp.model: 2` has #713's settings, which move so that nothing that ran stops and nothing new starts: a server on for all projects is on in the workspace and in every existing project that hadn't turned it off; one turned on in some projects is on in the workspace and those projects; one on nowhere stays off. The projects (hidden ones too) are written first, keeping their old `disabled` lists, so a move cut short does the same again; then `workspace.json` gets `model: 2` and the old lists are emptied (`migratedProjectMcp`, `migratedWorkspaceMcp`, `WorkspaceService.migrateMcpModel`). HI-2059's conversion follows it.
- **Search and filter** (Darren, 29 Oct, matching HI-545's catalogue): the MCP view's list and the picker search name, description and tags (`McpServerDef.tags`, Combwork's own: stripped from launches with `description`, `toLaunchDef`) and filter by where a server is added (All, Added somewhere, Added nowhere; the MCP view also With problems), `mcpServerShown`. HI-545 adds a source filter.
- **Shown:** the MCP view's list and a server's view say where it is added ("Added in Ambrosia", "Added in Ambrosia and for the Assistant", "Added for the Assistant only", "Not added anywhere"; hidden projects counted, unnamed), from `McpServerInfo.projects` and `assistant` (the window's list, `listMcp(true)`); deleting a server says where it is added (deleting removes it there). The project's MCP tab lists only its added servers. MCP servers aren't Combwork settings, so they aren't in the Assistant's settings catalogue (`cw_list_settings`): the Assistant reads them with `cw_project_status` and `GET /v1/mcp`.
- **The Agent API** (who sees what, HR1's s10 boundary): `GET /v1/mcp` gives the Assistant, scripts and the window `{ name, description, added: { projects: [names], assistant }, error }`; a project agent gets `added: boolean`, whether its own project has it, and nothing of another project's or the Assistant's. `GET /v1/projects/{name}` has `mcp: { available, added, on }` (`on` is `added`'s old name, kept for 1.0, deprecated) and `settings.mcp` is `{ added }`, never the stored list (which, unconverted, means something else). `GET /v1/workspace`'s `config` leaves out `mcp`. Adding servers stays the user's: there is no endpoint.

- **Per agent** (#537, Darren's decision of 11 Oct: for focus and a smaller context, not safety): an agent's settings say **MCP servers: All of the project's** (the default, unchanged: no field) or **Only these** (`AgentDef.mcpServers`, the names; `[]` none), in Agent Settings and a template's agent dialog, saved by templates (`TemplateAgent.mcpServers`), and through the Agent API (`mcpServers` on adding or changing an agent; `["*"]` all again). HI-2059 keeps it: an agent's own subset of its project's added servers. `shared/agentMcp.ts` holds the rule (`agentGetsMcp`): a name chosen that isn't added to the project reaches nobody (the dialog lists it as "not added to this project", so a save keeps it); a value Combwork can't read gives none, never more. It narrows only the workspace's servers: the built-in `combwork` server is always given (`combwork` isn't a name to choose), and the Assistant still gets no project servers. The launch passes only the chosen servers, the same way for every provider (`sessions.effectiveHere`, before the adapters: Claude Code's `--mcp-config` with `--strict-mcp-config`, Codex's `-c mcp_servers.*` with the user's same-named servers turned off, Copilot's `--additional-mcp-config` with `--disable-mcp-server` for the user's), so a server an agent wasn't given is off for it like any other. The choice is part of the launch signature: a running agent shows "restart to apply". Shown in the agent's tooltip, Project Settings' agent list (its own settings), a template's agents, the project's MCP tab (under each server, once any agent has a choice: "Given to every agent", "Given to Tester only", "Given to no agent") and `GET /v1/projects/{name}` (each agent's `mcpServers` and `mcpChoice`). A per-server "only agents given it" option (the card's first idea) wasn't built: an agent with **Only these** doesn't get a server added later, which covers part of it.
**MCP catalogues** (HI-545, Darren's decisions of 11, 14 and 29 Oct; built on HI-2059's "available, then added"; the format is the mcp project's catalog.json v1, MC-1477, its README's "The catalogue" and `scripts/catalog.mjs` `validate()` the reference). The MCP view's **Catalogue** tab lists servers to install; Settings → **MCP Catalogues** says where from.
- **Sources** (`AppSettings.mcpCatalogs`: per machine, Q1): ours first, `https://github.com/Suremise/combwork-mcp/releases/latest/download/catalog.json` (HI-2472; before, the mcp repository's under its old name, which isn't read since 1.1: the names upgrade gave the definitions installed from it the new address, so they keep their updates, HI-2594), on by default, turned off but never removed; then the user's by address (at most 15), each on or off, ordered, removed (servers installed from it stay). Addresses are `https://` or `file://` (a share; Q2), `http://` refused. A source that isn't ours gets a one-time note ("Servers from this source aren't checked by Combwork"), remembered (`noted`).
- **Reading** (`main/mcpCatalog.ts`): only when the Catalogue opens or on ↻, never in the background or at start. One time budget (`cw.mcpCatalog.fetchSeconds`, 15 s) and 8 MB across redirects; an ETag answers 304 from the cache. Checked as `validate()` checks (`shared/mcpCatalog.ts` `readCatalog`): another `schemaVersion`, or no name or list, makes the source show why and list nothing; an invalid or doubled server is skipped and counted; unknown fields are ignored; at most 5,000 servers a source. The cache holds every source listed (16) and at most 32 MB, least recently used out first; a source turned off or removed is dropped from it. A refresh's reply uses what it read, whatever the cache keeps; a search or a next page uses what is kept and never reads (one no longer kept says to refresh).
- **Listing:** each source a category, ours first; search (name, description, tags) and a filter (All, Not installed, Installed, Updates available, Runs on this PC) and a source picker, run in main a page of 50 at a time (`mcp:catalog`; **Show more**), so the window never holds a whole catalogue. A row's badge: Installed, **Update to x.y.z**, Name in use (a server of the name not from it), **Can't run here**. A reply to an older request is dropped.
- **Requirements** (`checkRequirements`): os from the platform; Windows edition (`EditionID`: Core is Home, Professional is Pro…) and build (`CurrentBuildNumber`) from the registry; Windows features only where Combwork can see them without elevation (Windows Sandbox: `WindowsSandbox.exe`), else **?**; Node.js (`node --version`, `>=N`) and Docker (`docker --version`); `apps` shown as text, **?**. Each probe is async with a time budget (`cw.mcpCatalog.probeSeconds`, 5 s), once per refresh; one that fails or times out is **?**, never met. A known unmet requirement refuses Install (and greys it out); **?** only warns.
- **Install** (`prepareCatalogServer`, `installCatalogServer`): the zip downloaded within `cw.mcpCatalog.downloadSeconds` (60 s) and its catalogue's size (200 MB at most), counted as it comes, across at most 5 redirects, each hop held to the source's scheme (an https source only https: never http or file:); a `file://` one under the same budget and end. It is bound to the open of the workspace that asked: its lifetime, taken before any await, aborts it, and a close (or a close and reopen of the same folder) discards what it held. Its size and sha256 must match the catalogue, its zip hold one top folder named after the server (#550's safe unpacking), or nothing is written. Combwork shows #550's Add dialog before it writes: what it runs (and any literal secret) and the name, another one when it is taken, or Replace; held at most 10 minutes, a few at a time, and written only while that same open of the workspace lasts. A server installed from an entry is found by its provenance under any name (Installed, Update). The definition records its provenance, Combwork's own field `catalog: { source, name, version, sha256 }`, stripped from launches with `description` and `tags`. Installed, it is added nowhere (29 Oct decision: no "added off"); the server's view opens for **Add to…**.
- **Update** (`updateCatalogServer`; never automatic): offered when the source's version is higher than the installed `catalog.version`. The dialog shows the versions, where it is added (those places keep it) and what it runs, the changed lines marked. In the MCP turn (the same as Add, Remove and Add to…): the installed definition must still be the one shown (`checkShown`) and the places it is added, read strictly now (`placesNow`, HI-2059's `membershipOf`), exactly those shown; otherwise nothing is written and the dialog opens again from what is there now. Then the new definition replaces the old where it is (#550's Replace without removing it from its places), keeping the user's own `env` and `headers` values for keys it still has (Q3).
- **Uninstall** is Delete, which fails closed (HI-2059). Per-agent access is agents' `mcpServers` (#537). The mcp project's publishing and moving Combwork's own parts out of its servers (#590) are their own cards.
- **Agent API:** `GET /v1/mcp`'s wide reply has each server's `catalog: { source, version } | null`. Installing and updating are the user's: there is no endpoint.
- MCP servers must be deployed to `<Workspace>/.combwork/` before any project can use them.
- Changes (to skills and MCP) apply to **new sessions only**, including restarts. A live session keeps what it launched with; the UI shows "settings changed — restart to apply". For skills that is any change to a workspace skill's files, wherever it was made (HI-2268): the skills folder's watch refreshes the workspace, whose `restartNeeded` compares each skill's revision with the launch's. A skill's revision is hashed again only when its files' sizes, times or entries changed (`revisionOf`, kept in memory, so a change that keeps both is seen at the next Combwork start), and launches take the source's from the same cache.
- If a project defines MCP servers in its own `.mcp.json` that are not in the workspace, Combwork notifies the user that they stay disabled until copied to the workspace, and offers "Copy to workspace". (`--strict-mcp-config` enforces this.)

**Provider** — stored on each agent when it is added, so a change of default never moves an agent. The project's default provider, else the global one (Settings → Providers), is what the quick add uses (the palette's **Add Agent**, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N, and New Session in a project without agents): an agent with that provider and its default settings in the project folder; + Add ▾'s **Configure Agent and Add…** (the session toolbar, #975) opens the **Add Agent…** dialog, preset to it, to choose the provider, where it works and its settings.

**Model, effort, permission mode, chime** — per provider: the global value is on the provider's settings page (Settings → Claude Code, Settings → Codex), the project's in Project Settings under the provider's name, and the project value overrides unless it is `inherit`. An agent's own model, effort or permission mode (set when adding it, or in its settings) overrides the project's; unset, it follows the project. The effort list's first choice says *default* once (#916): "Project's (High)" or "Project's (Medium, default)" in an agent's, "Default (High)" in the Assistant's, and "Claude Code's default" alone when nothing is chosen and the CLI hasn't said which level its default is. A mode that isn't allowed (e.g. Bypass after the option was turned off) falls back to the project's, then the global one.

**Agents** — background task limit and processes left running. *File locks* (default **Block**) and the Card loops options are workflow options since HI-1766 (§16.6.7), inherited Combwork → workspace → project. The files copied into new slots and review copies are a Git workflow default since HI-1765 (§16.10.2: Combwork's, the workspace's, the project's own; default `.env*`), the setup command the project's Slots and copies. The global *Default merge style* went with HI-1765: the hand-merge dialogs (Branches → Merge, an agent's 0.9 worktree, an unused worktree) start from the project's own G6 merge style (Squash for squash; a merge commit for merge, rebase or no workflow), never over a choice made in the dialog. A saved `agents.mergeStyle` is dropped, and a saved `agents.worktreeCopy` other than the old default moves to Combwork's slot default once.

**Number settings** (Settings and Project Settings) save on Enter or blur, once. A blank box saves nothing in Settings (the saved value comes back) and means Inherit in Project Settings; it is never read as 0. Text that isn't a number, or a number out of range, saves nothing and shows the range under the box. Where 0 turns the feature off (*Suggest compacting above*, the Assistant's *Highlight Compact over*, *Warn when a transcript is over*, *Archive Done cards after*, *Pause after you type*), 0 is chosen with a **Never** / **No pause** checkbox beside the box (typing 0 does the same); unticking it restores the last other value, else the default (Settings) or Inherit (Project Settings). A failed save shows the saved value again.

**Permission mode**
- Global default: **Auto** (Claude Code's safety classifier approves low-risk actions and asks about risky ones; Manual asked too often to be a good default for supervising several agents).
- Project dropdown: Inherit, Manual, Accept edits, Plan, Auto, Don't ask — always available.
- **Bypass permissions** is only offered when Settings → Claude Code → "Enable the Bypass permissions option" is ticked (ticking asks for confirmation). Projects using it show a warning indicator.
- If the option is later unticked, projects set to bypass revert to Inherit and the user is told which ones changed.
- **In a running session** the mode can be switched without a restart. Combwork knows the session's real mode from its launch flag, from Claude Code's footer as the terminal redraws (`⏵⏵ auto mode on`, `⏸ plan mode on`, …; read from the rendered screen, a headless terminal per session that keeps its visible screen and one line of scrollback (#1572: with none, xterm 6.0 narrowing and shortening at once could leave fewer lines than the screen shows, and its next line feed threw; after each resize Combwork checks for such a short screen and, if it finds one, logs it and starts a blank one at the new size, carrying over bracketed paste, the alternate screen and pending writes, for the CLI's redraw to fill), since Claude Code may redraw only the characters that changed, as it does with `NO_COLOR` set, which Combwork leaves as it is) and from `permission_mode` in hooks, so a Shift+Tab typed in the terminal shows in Combwork at once. Choosing a mode (the mode badge in the project header, a pane header or the status bar, or **Switch Permission Mode…**, Ctrl+Alt+M) sends Shift+Tab until the footer shows it. Claude Code's cycle is Manual → Accept edits → Plan → Auto; Don't ask leaves it once left, and Bypass is only in it for a session launched in Bypass (it shows Claude Code's own warning the first time), so those two restart the session in the mode and resume the same conversation, after confirmation. A restart waits for the old run to exit as long as its CLI's way of ending may take (`stopWaitMs`, as a stop waits; it was a fixed 8 s) and, in a slot, for that run's writer release before its new run claims the slot (`placeFor`'s wait, HI-1867), so it is refused only if that run's processes are kept or not known to have ended; a CLI still running at the end says it didn't stop in time and starts nothing (HI-1869), rather than "already running". A mode is switched live whenever the provider can switch to it (`canSwitchLive`), a no-guardrails one too after its confirmation (#1014); only a mode the provider can't reach in a running session restarts it, and the mode menu says "Restarts the session; the conversation continues" under exactly those. Not while the agent is asking something (Shift+Tab could change the answer). A live switch affects that session only.
- **Codex presets**: Read only (`-s read-only -a on-request`), Ask for approval (`-s workspace-write -a on-request`), **Approve for me** (`--approve-for-me`: Codex's reviewer approves low-risk actions; the default, like Auto) and **Full access** (`-s danger-full-access -a never`). Full access is treated like Bypass: only offered when Settings → Codex → "Enable the Full access option" is ticked (with confirmation), badged as a warning, and reverted to Inherit when unticked. A running Codex session switches preset live, Full access included (#1014, Darren: "drop restart and keep confirmation": after Combwork's confirmation, as for Bypass, with no restart): Combwork clears the input (Ctrl+U), types `/permissions`, and picks the preset from Codex's menu. For Full access Codex then shows its own warning ("Enable full access?", 0.162.1: Yes, continue anyway or Cancel; not shown when its config hides it), which the user answers in its terminal: the switch waits for the answer (the badge says "Switching to Full access…", Combwork types nothing into the agent meanwhile, at most 10 minutes: Settings → Advanced's `codex.fullAccess.answerSeconds`; before its first message, with no transcript to read the switch back from, Codex has 2 s to show the warning, `codex.fullAccess.warningAfterSeconds`), and only Codex's "Permission selection requested: Full Access" after the answer, or the transcript's settings, confirm it; cancelled, it isn't switched and the badge goes back (the warning's text is the advanced setting `codex.fullAccess.warning`); Plan mode is a separate toggle (Shift+Tab, shown as "· Plan" on the badge).
- **Changing the setting** (global, project or agent) never restarts anything and no longer marks sessions "restart to apply". New sessions use it; for running agents whose setting changed, a notification offers **Switch Now**, which switches them live (or reports which couldn't be). The agents switch side by side, up to six at once, so one waiting for the user's answer to its CLI's own question (Codex's Full Access warning) doesn't hold up the others; the report comes once every switch has ended (#1024).
- **A stopped agent's badge** (HI-2122, the user's option 1): its mode is its connection's (decision B), so the menu lists its account's connections with their modes, the current one ticked and disabled; choosing one moves the agent to it (`agents:update {connection}`, after the no-guardrails confirmation for its mode), nothing made for it; the last item, Edit "*connection*"…, opens the connection dialog. No connection (its CLI has no account here): one disabled line pointing to Agent Settings. An agent has no model, effort, mode or context of its own: `agents:update` and `agents:add` drop them, the project's provider pages are gone (`project:updateProvider` removed; `project:updateConfig` drops `providers`), and undoing an Assistant change recorded with them reports those fields as not undone, saying why.

---

## 6. Session lifecycle

§6.1 and §6.3 describe Claude Code; §6.4 is how Codex differs. Every launch has a **run ID**, so hooks reach the right agent before the session ID is known (hook URL `<hook server>?run=<runId>`).

### 6.1 Launch

On "New session" or "Resume":

1. Resolve effective skills and MCP servers (§5).
2. Rebuild `<Project>/.combwork/launch-<agent id>/` from scratch (copy skills, record hashes) and write the launch's `mcp.json` and `settings.json` to its private folder in Combwork's user data (`launches/<run id>/`, #345: they can hold the user's secrets).
3. For a resume, if Claude Code's transcript is missing (e.g. cleaned up) but Combwork holds a backup, restore it first.
4. Spawn in a pty, cwd = the agent's folder (the project folder, or its worktree):

```
claude --session-id <uuid> | --resume <uuid>
       --name "<session name>"
       --plugin-dir .combwork/launch-<agent id>/plugin
       [--add-dir .combwork/launch-<agent id>/plugin]   (when the agent's folder is a slot or worktree, outside the project)
       --mcp-config <user data>/launches/<run id>/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config
       --settings <user data>/launches/<run id>/settings.json
       [--model <m>] [--effort <e>] [--permission-mode <p>] [extra args]
```

Environment added to the pty: `CW_HOOK_TOKEN`, `CW_API_URL`, `CW_API_TOKEN_FILE` (the file holding the agent's own Agent API token for this launch, never the workspace token; the token itself is never in the environment, HI-2262), `CW_PROJECT`, `CW_PROJECT_PATH`, `CW_WORKSPACE`, `CW_AGENT` (the agent's name), `CW_PROVIDER`, `CW_RUN_ID` and, when known at launch, `CW_SESSION_ID`. Every provider's own session variables inherited from Combwork's environment (e.g. `CLAUDECODE`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`) are removed. **Agents' temp folder** (HI-2496, Settings → Advanced, `cw.agents.tempFolder`: one folder, Combwork's or a workspace's own over it, a `%VARIABLE%` at its start filled in; empty by default, and then nothing here changes): each launch, the Assistant's too, gets its own folder in it, `<folder>\<project name>-<8 hex of its path's hash>\<agent id>` (the Assistant's `_assistant-<hash>\assistant`, apart from any project; equal project names in two workspaces never share), made before the CLI starts and kept, and `TEMP`, `TMP` and `TMPDIR` set to it last, over the account's and server's variables, duplicates of any case removed (Node reads `TEMP` and Rust `TMP` first: both are set). Claude Code's adapter also sets `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR` (read before `TEMP`), over one inherited; empty, an inherited one stays. Only agent launches: `childEnv()` for git, builds and checks, the tests' temp folders (HI-2102) and the CLI's staging (CL-44) are unchanged. It is never inside a workspace's folder (its projects are listed from it, and the Assistant works in it), a project (hidden ones too, wherever they are), a workspace's slots and review copies (`<workspace>.worktrees`), any agent's other folders the workspace knows (slots and retired homes registered elsewhere, 0.9 worktrees, worktrees noted unused: `knownRoots()`), the Assistant's home or a workspace's `.combwork`, in any open workspace, nor the launch's own host and working folder: checked on real paths (its deepest existing folder resolved, so a junction counts) before the folder is made and again after. A folder that can't be used (a variable not set, inside one of those, not made) stops the launch with the reason, translated, never falling back to the system Temp. Combwork never deletes in it (a resumed session reads its scratchpad again): tidying is the user's, with the agents stopped. Sensitive (§ settings): only the user sets it. What each CLI honours (validated on HI-2496, s7): Claude Code 2.1.318 roots its scratchpad at `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR`, else the OS temp folder, with `\claude` after it (its code and its environment reference); Codex 0.166.0 (Rust's `temp_dir`: `TMP`, then `TEMP`) passes inherited variables to its shells unless the user's shell-environment policy changes them, while its `arg0` helpers stay in `CODEX_HOME\tmp`; Copilot 1.0.105 is Node (`os.tmpdir()`: `TEMP`, then `TMP`), with no temp variable of its own. A CLI's private caches elsewhere, and a `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR` in Claude Code's own settings file's `env`, are outside it. The launch plugin is in the project's `.combwork`, so an agent working in a slot or worktree is also given that folder with `--add-dir`: otherwise Claude Code asks before reading a skill's reference file there, and a session nobody watches waits on it (HI-2274).

**A `--settings` in the user's extra arguments** (#330): Claude Code reads only the last `--settings` it is given (2.1.291), so the user's would replace Combwork's and with it every hook and the status line. Combwork instead reads it (the last one, as Claude Code does: inline JSON, or a file relative to the agent's folder) and merges it into its own `settings.json`: every setting of the user's, their hooks added after Combwork's for each event, and Combwork's status line (a session has one; Combwork's reports context, cost and limits). Their HTTP hook allowlists, which Claude Code takes whole from the highest file that sets one (not merged across files), gain what Combwork's hooks need: `allowedHttpHookUrls` its hook URL, `httpHookAllowedEnvVars` `CW_HOOK_TOKEN` (without them Claude Code 2.1.292 blocks Combwork's HTTP hooks, or sends them with an empty token); unset, they are left unset. Managed settings, above the command line, still apply. The CLI gets only Combwork's `--settings`; the user's are dropped from the arguments (`providers/claude/launchSettings.ts`). One Combwork can't merge stops the launch before its folder changes, with a **Couldn't start** that names the argument: a `--settings` given no value (at the end of the arguments, `--settings=` or an empty value, even after a valid one: Claude Code reads the last, and a mistake shouldn't launch with Combwork's settings alone, #361), a missing file (Claude Code refuses it too: "Settings file not found"), one that isn't a regular file or is over 2 MiB (Claude Code 2.1.292 refuses those too; checked before the file is opened and read no further than the limit, #333), a file that isn't JSON (Claude Code ignores it silently), JSON that isn't an object, `disableAllHooks: true` (it turns off Combwork's hooks and status line with the user's, 2.1.292), or an HTTP hook allowlist that isn't a list (Claude Code then blocks Combwork's hooks). `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_HOOKS` in the settings' `env` block doesn't turn hooks off (2.1.292) and is left as it is. Codex has no equivalent: its `--profile` layers a config file under the `-c` overrides Combwork passes its hooks in (0.160.1), so a profile can't replace them.

Each Claude Code agent launches from its own folder (`launch-<agent id>/`), because a launch replaces the folder while the project's other agents may still read theirs (skills are read when used).

Rebuilding `launch/` on every launch means a restarted agent has exactly the workspace's current skills (for its audience, §7.1) and MCP servers.

### 6.2 Operations

| Action | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| New session | New UUID. A live session is stopped first (with confirmation). In a project without agents, New Session (and Resume) first adds one with the quick add, then starts it. |
| Resume | `--resume <uuid>`, in an agent that works in the folder the session ran in (sessions record their agent, folder and branch). Shows the re-cache estimate (§9) first. A conversation that can't continue (HI-2463's rename, HI-2462's move: `shared/sessionFresh.ts`, the one rule the start and the window's lists read) starts a new conversation instead, carrying the agent's work; its Resume says so in its tooltip and session pickers, and pressing it asks **Start a new conversation?** instead of the re-cache question (HI-2540). A start no one was asked about (a restart's, Resume All, a lane's) gets the notice afterwards instead, and the Agent API's reply to a resume says it started fresh and why. If the session has no transcript yet (nothing was typed before it stopped or was restarted), it is started fresh with `--session-id <uuid>` instead. **One conversation runs in one agent at a time**: the main process refuses to resume a session that is open in another agent (two terminals would both append to its transcript), for the UI and the Agent API alike; the UI shows that agent instead. A paused session can move between agents that share its folder (never across worktrees); the record then names the new agent, and any other agent whose *last session* it was forgets it. |
| Stop | Ends the pty. Session stays resumable. |
| Leftover processes (#507) | Ending the pty ends what is attached to its console (node-pty asks the console for its processes), not what the agent started detached or hidden (a preview server, a `tail -f`, a Claude Code background shell, a Codex background terminal), which then outlive it and hold the project's folder and ports. Claude Code's own stop of a background command or Monitor on Windows leaves the commands of its Git Bash pipeline running too (HI-2570: `tail` and `grep` of `tail -F | grep`, the shell ended). Their Windows parents exited when they were exec'd, so they aren't in the shell's process tree, but they are in the job: listed or ended when the launch ends, not at the stop. Recorded as Claude Code's; Combwork doesn't match them to the stopped command. So each launch's CLI (and its worktree's setup command) runs in a **Windows job object** of its own from its first instruction, and everything it starts joins the job by itself, however it is started and through whatever exits since (`agentProcesses.ts`). node-pty can't start a process suspended and knows its pid only once it runs, so the terminal first runs a **gate** (`launchGate.ts`): a hidden PowerShell with no cmdlets (a console program, so it shares the pseudoconsole; Electron's own executable run as Node doesn't), given the command and its arguments in its environment (removed before the command starts). It connects to a pipe made for the launch and waits; Combwork puts the gate in the job (`ptyHost` `track`, which checks the process is still running), then answers `go`, and the gate starts the command with the command line node-pty would have built (`commandLineOf`, tested against node-pty's), on the same console, and exits with its code. The gate starts the command **only on `go`**, however long that takes: `stop <why>`, a failed connection or the pipe closing without a word (Combwork gone, or the terminal stopped) end it with `Error: Combwork didn't start <exe>: <why>` (a failed start), never running the command. A launch stopped while its gate was being tracked is told `stop`, and its job let go even if the assignment lands after (nothing is assigned to a dead or reused pid). **A terminal killed before its gate's word** (HI-1819: Combwork quitting just after a launch) tells the gate `stop` first (`its terminal was closed before it started`), whatever tracking answers after: a command started as its console closes misses the close and runs on with no console. The gate waits for its command, so a gated launch's CLI still running once the gate has exited lost its terminal the same way (`go` said just before the kill): two seconds after, it is ended by identity, not listed as a leftover to keep (it would hold its slot's run, #1434). The CLI is the gate's child and, through `cmd.exe` wrapping it (a `.cmd` launcher, a setup command), the command each wrapper runs, each started after its parent (`orphanedCli`); what the CLI itself started stays a leftover like any other. **When tracking can't work** (Darren's decision B, 10 Oct): a launch first waits until the job host is running (it starts it; `trackingReady`). #1155: the host also starts in the background (`warmProcessTracking`) as Combwork starts with a workspace to reopen (beside its windows' loading), and when a workspace opens later with agents (its `workspace-changed`: a project with an agent, or the Assistant with a session to resume), so the first launch after Combwork starts doesn't wait the 0.35–0.6 s its PowerShell takes (Resume All paid it first in line; measured on a dev build: 0 ms instead of ~340 ms, a Resume as soon as the window showed the workspace); it shows nothing, and a host that can't start is said by the first launch, as before. If it can't run (PowerShell blocked, Constrained Language Mode refusing Add-Type) or doesn't say it is ready within 60 s (it is then killed and given up on for the run), the CLI starts directly, untracked; if a launch's assignment then fails, the gate is told `go` all the same. Once the host runs, every reply is bounded too (60 s): one that doesn't come means the host is stuck, and it is killed, so no launch, End or quit waits on it longer. **A host that ends after starting** (a crash, or killed as stuck) closes its jobs: running agents' launches are no longer tracked (they keep running, nothing is ended); the leftovers listed stay listed by identity, as after a restart (#614, below), and those whose start time isn't known go. A host that held nothing (no running launch, nothing listed but what was restored) loses nothing: only the log says it ended. Otherwise Combwork says so at once through the same once-a-run notice (what was listed and what running agents start are no longer tracked), and Diagnostics keeps it (`; earlier, the process tracker stopped at <time> (<why>): …`) even once a new host, started by the next request, tracks later launches. Either way Combwork never refuses to start an agent over it, and says so once a run: a notification ("Combwork can't keep track of agents' processes": why, and that what agents leave running isn't listed) and a Diagnostics line (`Agents' processes: tracked` or `not tracked: <why>`). Test copies (unpackaged): `CW_TEST_PROCESS_TRACKER=fail` acts out a host that can't run, `=silent` one that starts but never says it is ready, `=mute` one that is ready but never answers (each request it reads noted in the file `CW_TEST_TRACKER_HEARD` names), and `CW_TEST_TRACKER_WAIT_MS` shortens the 60 s waits. One hidden PowerShell per Combwork holds the jobs (C# through `Add-Type`, no files; one line per request); without it (PowerShell blocked) nothing is tracked and agents stop as before. The jobs never end anything themselves (no kill-on-close). Two seconds after the CLI exits, what is still in its job is what it left (consoles' hosts not listed): logged, kept per agent (the newest 5 launches each, 100 in all; older ones forgotten, never ended), looked at again every 10 s while any are listed (those that ended go), and sent to the agent's window (`agent-leftovers`). **Settings → Agents → Processes left running** (`agents.leftoverProcesses`): **Ask** (default) shows a notification listing them with End Them / Keep Running and an **⚠ n left running** chip in the agent's pane header (hover: the list; click: end or keep); **End them** ends them as the agent stops. End terminates the launch's job, so only processes its CLI started are ended, never one started outside it (a process started outside it isn't tracked either, except what escapes it from inside, below; a launch whose job couldn't be ended stays listed and the End fails with a message (the header's End shows it; with End them set, the notification is shown instead, saying Combwork couldn't end them), so it can be tried again or kept; only what was ended is counted. Keep Running stops listing them and leaves them running. Offers whose agent has nothing listed any more are dismissed. Quitting Combwork with some listed asks once in a native dialog (End Them / Leave Running) while a window is shown; a quit with none shown, or to install an update, leaves them running and still listed. **Across a restart** (#614: a dev copy of Combwork a suite started under an agent outlived it and two of Combwork's restarts; that Combwork predated #507, and a later quit to install an update would have forgotten it): what is listed is also kept in the profile (`leftovers.json`, written on every change once within the bounds, so a crash keeps it too), each launch apart and within the same bounds when written and when read (the newest 5 launches an agent, 100 in all, 50 processes a launch), each process by its pid and start time (a Windows FILETIME the host reads with `GetProcessTimes`, `created` in the listing; a process whose start time couldn't be read isn't kept). The next start, once the first window has loaded, lists again those still running as the same processes, each launch on its own (the host's `identify`, which answers with pid and start time pairs, matched as pairs: a record whose pid names another process by then is dropped, also beside another record of that pid that does match) and offers them as when an agent stops ("<agent> left n processes running", End Them / Keep Running; with End them set, ends them). Their jobs are gone by then, so End ends exactly the listed processes, each only while it is still the same process (the host's `endexact`: opened by pid, its start time checked, ended through that handle; one gone counts as ended), not what they started since; they're looked at again every 10 s like the rest. Without the job host, nothing is restored and the list stays for the next start. Test copies of Combwork name their profile on their own command line (`--combwork-test-profile=…`, which Combwork ignores; `tests/e2e/lib.cjs`), so the e2e runner's clean-up of what names a suite's folder also stops a test Combwork whose suite died before closing it, as the one in #614 did. Renderer IPC: `session:leftovers` (the window's workspace), `session:settleLeftovers` (the session host is checked; only that agent's). Windows only. **The real CLIs** (#515, real-tier suites `leftovers-claude` and `leftovers-codex`): a Claude Code background Bash (`run_in_background`) outlives Combwork's stop (its terminal ended) and is listed, and End ends it; `/exit` ends it with Claude Code (2.1.296). Codex ends its background terminals itself as it exits, stopped by Combwork or `/exit` (0.162.1), so they're never left, except that Codex runs commands in PowerShell 7 where there is one, and doesn't end what runs through the Microsoft Store's: that is listed and ended as below (#543). **What escapes the job** (#543): the Store's PowerShell 7 (`WindowsApps\pwsh.exe`) is a packaged app, so Windows starts it in its package's job and its children in none: neither would be listed or ended. The job host takes them in: a live process whose parent is in a launch's job, and that isn't in that job itself, joins it if it is in no job (its later children with it); one already in another job (the Store's PowerShell, in its package's) is followed instead: held open, listed, and ended with the job. Never assigned (#659): Windows would nest the jobs, and the package's job, which every Store PowerShell joins, when it had no parent became the launch's, so every Store PowerShell started after it (any agent's or app's) was listed and ended with that launch. Nor is a packaged app's process, even in no job (#678): Windows puts the Store's PowerShell in its package's job only once it has started (4 to 160 ms after it shows in a snapshot, measured; more under load), and a sweep that caught it before then and assigned it nested the package's job in the launch's just the same (about 1 in 50 loaded test runs). A process with a package identity (`GetPackageFullName`) is followed whatever job it is in; its children (not packaged) still join the launch's job when they are in none. Ids are checked against what they named when seen (#543 round 2): a candidate, or a parent looked up by id and not held, created after the sweep's snapshot is refused (the id names another process by now; Windows stamps creation in ticks of about 15.6 ms, so one created within the snapshot's own tick still passes: a documented limit), the parent must have started before the child, and a process the port reports as joining is held only if it is in that job (a notification read late may carry a reused id). End ends the job and each followed process; one Windows won't end that still runs makes End fail (listed, to try again), and one already gone counts as ended. The host sweeps for them as processes of a job exit (the job's completion port reports each joining and leaving process; the host holds each open until the sweep after its exit, so the exited parent's id and start time stay known; exits are gathered for up to 250 ms and swept for together, since a sweep's snapshot of every process costs a few ms and a build ends hundreds), before listing or ending a job, and every second. Still missed: an escaped process that starts something and exits within a second, before any sweep saw it (a `Start-Process` from the Store's PowerShell that returns at once). The host's C# goes to its PowerShell as the first line of its input, base64 (a command line holds at most 32,767 characters). The log says how many processes of a launch were taken in this way. Unit tests stand in for the escape on any PC (a child started before its CLI joins the job) and use the Store's PowerShell where it is installed; `leftovers-codex` keeps it on PATH. **Agents stop what they start** (#613: one agent's own `tail -f | grep` log watchers, 16 of them, outlived the runs they watched until Combwork quit): the agents' session contract says to watch a run with something that ends with it (`cw-progress`, the CLI's notice that a background command ended), never `tail -f`, and to end what they started that won't end by itself before their card ends, unless the user wants it running; work-on-card (a Finish step, before Review), card-loop (a loop's turns end on a watch, never a watcher) and merge-ready (finishing loose work) say how. The `watcher-stopped` scenario checks it: Combwork lists nothing the agent left once its card is in Review and it is stopped (`session:leftovers` with `settled`, which answers once every exited launch has been looked at). |
| Failed start | The CLI exits while the session is still **starting** (before its first hook, or for Codex before its prompt shows), and Combwork didn't stop it: a missing or broken CLI, an argument or config it refuses. Main reads the CLI's last error lines from the terminal output (`shared/startFailure.ts`: escapes removed, from the first line naming an error among the last 12, at most three lines and 300 characters) and asks the adapter for a hint (`startHint()`: what is wrong and where to fix it: Agent Settings, Provider Setup, or the terminal), and sends them with `session-exit` (`failure`). The pane shows them in place of "Session ended", in red: **Couldn't start:** the reason, the hint, **Retry** (the same launch again: a resume resumes the conversation), **Agent Settings…** (or **Provider Setup…** when that's where the fix is) and ✕; the agent's tab dot and header turn red ("Failed to start"); a toast with **Show** comes only when its pane isn't on screen, and the window's attention inbox lists it under *needs you* ("Couldn't start: …"; the tray's list, built in main, doesn't know it). It lasts until the agent's next launch or ✕, and isn't kept across restarts. The terminal keeps the full output. Not covered: errors the CLI shows without exiting (Claude Code's sign-in screen, an unknown model or expired sign-in on the first prompt). |
| Compact | The agent's ⋯ (#977; a header button next to Stop before), Session menu, command palette. Enabled only while the agent is idle (Ready/Finished) and the conversation has content. A dialog shows the context size and cache state and takes an optional **focus**; empty lets the agent decide what to keep. Combwork sends Ctrl+U (clears half-typed input; Claude Code's Ctrl+Y restores it), then `/compact [focus]`. Status shows "Compacting…" until `PostCompact`, a new compaction in the transcript, a refusal in the output ("Not enough messages to compact"), no `PreCompact` within 20 s, or 10 minutes. A compaction the CLI begins by itself while the agent is idle shows "Compacting…" the same way, from its `PreCompact` until `PostCompact`, a prompt, a new compaction in the transcript, or 10 minutes (#1115: Claude Code precomputes a compaction in the background, idle too, and sends `PostCompact` only if and when it uses it). An agent's footer context turns amber above *Suggest compacting above* (the Assistant's Compact button too) (global, default 200,000 tokens; per-project override; **Never** turns it off). The Assistant has its own threshold, **Settings → Assistant → Highlight Compact over** (`settings.assistant.compactSuggestTokens`, default 500,000, **Never** = 0; it usually runs a bigger context): `assistantProjectConfig()` overlays it as its host's `compactSuggestTokens`, so its header's Compact (highlighted, with the same "Recommended…" tooltip) and its footer's context (amber, "— consider compacting", the `compact-suggested` tip) resolve it through the same `compactThreshold()` as agents' (#290). Until then its footer used the agents' 200,000 and its Compact button was never highlighted. The full pre-compaction history stays in the transcript and Combwork's backup. |
| Archive | Copies the current transcript to `.combwork/archive/` (or moves the backup there if Claude Code no longer has it), removes the active backup and marks the session archived; the archived copy is then compressed (`<id>.jsonl.gz`, #1110). Can be unarchived. Only Combwork's sessions (adopt an external one first), and only when it isn't in use (as Delete). |
| In use (Archive, Delete) | Archive and Delete first **reserve** the session (as Clean Up does): until they finish, it can't start or resume and its transcript isn't read (the viewer, a search, an export wait). Then Combwork checks nothing has it in use (`sessions.inUse`), and refuses (one at a time) or skips it (Archive All / Delete All, saying why): it is **running or starting** in any agent, project or window; Combwork is **reading its transcript** (a read under way: `transcriptReads.ts`, counted around every parse, export and image); its transcript is **open in a Sessions view**, in any window (views register with `transcript:viewing`, and can't register on a reserved session; the tab asking closes its own view first and waits for main to know, opens it again afterwards if the session is still there (skipped, or archived one at a time), and says when it stays closed); **another program holds the CLI's transcript open** (found by opening it to read and closing it at once: the CLI's file is never changed or moved); or its CLI is **still writing** it: changed in the last 5 s and not since Combwork saw that CLI exit (Combwork notes each exit of its own sessions, so Archive and Start New archives one just stopped; a session started outside Combwork, adopted or not, or a Codex guardian review still going, waits). Nothing is ever killed. **All or nothing**: an archive builds the new archive aside (the backup brought up to date from the CLI's transcript), then moves each copy, and any failure (a copy another program holds, the record not saved) moves every copy back; the record changes only after the files. A delete first moves each of Combwork's copies aside and back, keeps a spare of each (a hard link, else a copy), then sends them to the Recycle Bin and removes the record; if one fails to go or the record can't be saved, the copies already gone are put back from their spares (a copy stays in the Recycle Bin). |
| Delete | Any session that isn't running (Combwork's, archived or external), from the Sessions tab or the Assistant's conversations, after asking. Combwork's backup and archive copies go to the Recycle Bin, the record leaves `sessions.json` and its id is kept in `deleted` so it never shows again (not even as external); **what it used stays** in the usage history (§9: recorded before its copies go), so the Overview's and the Assistant's totals still count it (`session:keptUsage`: the history's sessions no record has; lists, search and resume never see it); an agent whose last session it was forgets it. The CLI's own transcript is left alone: Combwork doesn't change the CLIs' files, so the CLI's own resume list still has it. If it runs again (resumed inside the CLI), it is Combwork's again (and its kept usage goes, counted from its transcript instead). Images pasted into it stay in `.combwork/images`. |
| Adopt | Sessions for the project started outside Combwork are listed and can be adopted into `sessions.json`. A sub-session stays one when adopted (its `sub` is kept): never resumed. |
| Add agent | Up to its Maximum agents (§16.6.8, HI-2058: the user too), at most 24 per project (#562), a page holding as many as the layout has panes (§6.2). **Add Agent** is a split button (#286): the main part is **Configure Agent and Add…**, which opens the Add Agent… dialog; **▾** is a menu with Configure Agent and Add… and, in a project (not the Assistant), **Add Agent from Template** (the templates' agents, § Agent templates). The quick add (the default provider with its default settings, in the project folder, named "Agent n") is the palette's **Add Agent** (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N), the project's right-click menu and New Session in a project without agents. The dialog: provider, name, where it works (project folder, new worktree with branch `cw/<workspace>/<project>/<name>` (#703) from a chosen base branch, with the hint "`cw/` marks branches Combwork made, so it can reuse and tidy them up" under it (#702), or an existing unused worktree of the project), optional model/effort/permission overrides (and Use 200K context for Claude Code), and "Start a session now". A page whose layout wasn't chosen by hand shows all its agents (1 one at a time, 2 two columns, 3 three columns, 4 the 2×2 grid, 5–6 the 3×2 grid), and the new agent is focused (the seventh opens page 2). Adding the seventh shows a note that each agent is its own CLI process (roughly 200–500 MB of memory; measured on Darren's machine, 13 Oct: Claude Code about 410 MB working set, Codex 210 MB, Copilot 180 MB) and they share the plan's limits. |
| Agent names (#702) | **Unique across the workspace** (Darren's decision of 12 Oct), case and spacing aside: two projects' B1 couldn't be told apart on the board, in notifications, in Apiary's office or by the Assistant. Refused, never only warned: Add Agent and quick add (the default "Agent n" numbered past every project's names), a rename (Agent Settings, the Agent API's update), a template's load and Add Agent from Template, and a card started with a new agent; the dialogs say so inline before Save or Add ("alpha already has an agent called B1… Use HB1", `shared/agentNames.ts`), and main checks again. **Suggestion:** the project's initials (`projectPrefix`: web → W, web-dashboard → WD) in front of a short code, in capitals (B1 → HB1, then longer prefixes AMB1…), a word with the project after it ("Builder (beta)"), else numbered. **Race-free:** every change that gives a name checks it and writes it holding the workspace's names lock (`withAgentNames` in `main/agentNames.ts`, taken before a project file's lock, never inside one), so two projects can't take a name at once; the listed projects count (a hidden one's agents are flagged if they clash when it comes back). **Names from before** keep working: saving an agent's other settings with its own name isn't a rename; each name two projects share is said once per workspace (a warning with **Rename <project>'s <name>…**, which opens Agent Settings through the `agent.settings` command), remembered in workspace.json's `flaggedAgentNames` while it lasts. The Assistant's name isn't checked: it is never a project's agent. |
| Merge (worktree agent) | Commits the worktree's uncommitted changes (with the message given), checks for conflicts with `git merge-tree` without touching anything, then merges into the branch checked out in the project folder: **squash** (one commit, default) or **merge** (`--no-ff`). Refused while the project folder has staged changes, and while the agent is in the middle of a task (starting, working, waiting for the user's answer, or waiting on background tasks it started: its uncommitted files would be committed half-done; `mergeBlocked()`): Merge… in the agent's ⋯ menu, the Agents settings and the Changes tab are disabled then, with the reason in the tooltip (the unmerged count still shows), and an open Merge dialog says so and disables Merge. On conflict nothing changes; the dialog lists the files and offers to send merge instructions to an idle agent in the project folder, or copy them. Optionally removes the worktree, branch and agent afterwards (off by default; agent must be stopped). After a **squash** that keeps the worktree, **Move the branch afterwards** (on by default) runs `git reset --keep <into>` in the worktree, only when it is on the agent's branch and merging the branch again would change nothing (`git merge-tree`); otherwise the merge still succeeds and a warning says why the branch wasn't moved (`MergeResult.branchMoved`/`moveError`). **Unmerged work** shows on the agent's strip tab (↑ and the count of commits not in the project folder's branch, or • for uncommitted files only; a branch whose merge would change nothing — its commits were squash-merged already — counts as merged, checked with `git merge-tree`), with the details in its tooltip, and as the detail of Merge… in the agent's ⋯ (#977; on a Merge… button in the pane header before). `main/branchWatch.ts` asks git (`branchStatus()`) when the agent's status changes to anything but working or starting, when a window gets focus (at most every 10 s), for agents not checked yet (on `workspace-changed`), for every worktree agent of the project after a merge, when the Merge dialog checks it, and every 60 s for agents with something left to merge; changes go to the window as `branch-status` events (not on the Agent API's event stream). A branch that isn't there (an agent's 0.9 branch gone with its worktree, a card's line deleted after its merge, or deleted while it was checked) has nothing to merge and is no error to log; an agent whose 0.9 worktree the slots took over (#1441) isn't watched on that branch any more; a slot's line with no card target is counted against the project's workflow target, else its default branch (HI-1698). |
| Merge slot (#350) | One merge at a time into a project's branch, so it can't move while an agent checks and merges (#306 made merges check that the base hadn't moved; with several lanes finishing together that meant rerunning the checks each time). `main/mergeSlots.ts` (the logic, synchronous between awaits; one Slot object per project and branch stays registered while anything uses it, so a clean-up never leaves a claim holding an unregistered one) and `mergeSlotHost.ts` (wiring): a slot per project path and branch, in memory. **Holder:** a running agent's launch (project, agent, `runId`; from its own token, never the request), or the user's merge from the Merge dialog (`asUser`, for the length of `mergeWorktree`; refused while an agent holds or waits for it, and the dialog keeps Merge disabled with "B4 is merging #305 into main" until it is free). **Claim** (`cw_merge_slot`, `POST /v1/projects/{name}/merge-slot/claim`) waits in the call up to 240 s (at most 290: Node's `fetch` in the Combwork tools gives up on a reply after 300 s) and the line is first come, first served. A claim that times out, or whose client goes away, keeps its place for 2 minutes. A turn that comes while the waiter is between calls is given as not yet taken (`taken: false`) and lapses to the next in line after 2 minutes. Claiming while holding extends the hold. **Release** naming no branch is for the agent's own hold or place in line when it has just one, whatever branch the folder is on now (merge-ready checks the agent's branch out there after claiming the base's, #586); with none, the branch whose hold it lost; else the folder's. A release that finds nothing to release lists the slots the agent does hold or wait for (`yours`), or says it has none. **Hold:** 60 minutes, kept while the holder's open Progress run reported in the last 15. It ends with the holder's launch (`sessions.onLaunchEnded`, and found out lazily from `runId`), on release, when the user releases it (Overview or Progress panel, after a confirm; the confirm names its hold by id, and is refused if the slot changed hands meanwhile, even to the same agent again), or on expiry (passed on, a warning toast, and the old holder is told on its next call: `lost`). **Shown:** the waiter's and holder's `mergeSlot` note on its status ("Waiting for the merge slot (B4 is merging #305)", "Merging into main (merge slot)"; `statusMessage` takes precedence), the project's Overview and the top of the Progress panel (its merge card, #484; `merge-slots-changed`). **Restart:** agents' holds are written to `merge-slots/` in app data (§4.3); when the workspace opens, a recorded hold no launch has is reported ("check the main checkout for a merge left half done") and dropped. Merges outside Combwork aren't controlled; merge-ready keeps the "has the base moved?" check as the fallback. Agents only (not the Assistant): `AGENT_ONLY_TOOLS`. |
| Worktree branches (#703) | A new worktree's branch is **`cw/<workspace>/<project>/<agent>`**, always in full (Darren's decision on #702: several workspaces can share a repository, even with projects of the same name, and never clash), e.g. `cw/Work/ambrosia/amb1` (`shared/agentBranches.ts` `agentBranch`). The workspace and project are their folder names with their case kept and git's ref rules applied (`refPart`: anything but letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` becomes `-`, no `..`, no leading or trailing `.` or `-`, no trailing `.lock`, at most 40 characters, `workspace`/`project` when nothing is left); the agent is its slug, as before. `uniqueBranch` numbers a taken one (`-2`), comparing case aside (git keeps branches as files on Windows), and never picks one git can't make: not one a branch is inside of (`cw/ws/alpha/x` while `cw/ws/alpha/x/y` exists), and one inside a branch (`feature/y` while `feature` exists) is refused, saying which. **A branch in the way** (round 2): a branch `cw/ws` made outside Combwork, and git can't make `cw/ws/<project>/…` while it exists (case aside: `cw/work` blocks `cw/Work/…`); so the project's new branches take a numbered workspace part, `cw/ws-2/<project>/<agent>` (`chooseSpace`, also when `cw/<workspace>/<project>` is a branch), and the branch in the way is left as it is. **Which parts are the project's** (round 3) is recorded, never inferred from a name that looks numbered (another workspace may be called ws-2): project.json's `branchSpaces` gets a part when Combwork first makes a branch in it, and only the workspace's own part and those count as the project's. A new part is never one another workspace uses in the repository (a branch under `cw/<part>/<project>/`): ws-3 then. **Stable:** once moved, the project stays in the part it moved to while that is clear, even after the branch in the way has gone; its own again only if that one is blocked. The Add Agent dialog gets the part and the project's parts from git info (`ProjectGitInfo.branchSpace`, `branchSpaces`) for its default and its look. **Its own branches** (HI-2593: only `cw/`; branches named `hive/…`, as Combwork made them before 1.1, short form included, are no longer its own and nothing recognises them): `agentBranchNumber(branch, home, name)` says whether a branch is the one Combwork made for an agent of that name, numbered or not: the full form, in one of the project's own parts and for this project only, so another workspace's same-named project's branches are never taken for this one's. For an agent's own default branch, Add Agent also looks for the same agent's branch in the project's other own parts (kept from before it moved) (`reusableBranches`). ### 6.3 Status via HTTP hooks

`launch/settings.json` registers Claude Code **HTTP hooks** pointing at Combwork's local hook server (`127.0.0.1`, random port per app run). The token is sent as `Authorization: Bearer $CW_HOOK_TOKEN` using `allowedEnvVars`. `SessionStart` only supports command hooks (and `mcp_tool`; checked against the hooks reference with 2.1.292), so it is a command that pipes the hook JSON to the same server with `curl.exe`.

**Hook tokens** (#345): **one per launch** (`hookTokens.ts`), made when the launch starts and ended with it (its exit, or a start given up), never one for the whole Combwork run. The hook server takes a call only with the token of the launch its `?run=` names (`timingSafeEqual`), so a token can't speak for another session or outlive its own; a call naming no launch is refused (hooks of an ended launch were already ignored). HTTP hooks read it from the session's environment. **No file Combwork generates in a project, and no argument it passes, holds a secret.** Each launch has a **private folder** in Combwork's user data, `launches/<run id>/` (`launchPrivateDir()`), removed when the launch ends and all of them when Combwork starts (earlier runs' tokens are dead). It holds the hook auth file (`hook-auth.txt`) and whatever of the launch may carry a secret: Claude Code's `settings.json` (with a user's `--settings` and its `env`, #330) and `mcp.json` (the workspace's MCP servers' own `env`, headers and arguments). The project's launch folder keeps only what holds none: the skills plugin, `sync.json`, the Assistant's `instructions.md`, `README.txt`. Hook commands (Claude Code's SessionStart and status line, every Codex hook) read the header with `curl -H "@<file>"` from the auth file. Codex gets MCP servers as `-c` arguments and already leaves out one with a literal secret (it would show in process listings), with a warning; the combwork MCP server's definition names the agent's token file, not the token. `tests/hookTokens.test.ts` scans what both providers write and pass, with a synthetic token, MCP env and header secrets and a `--settings` env. The command is `curl.exe -s -m 5 -X POST -H "@<auth file>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary "@-" "<url>"` for both CLIs (`hookForwardCommand()`): `curl.exe` unquoted and `"@-"` quoted, forward slashes, which works in Git Bash, PowerShell (Claude Code's fallback without Git Bash, and Codex's shell) and cmd alike (Windows 11, curl 8.21 and Git's 8.7.1; before, Claude Code's quoted curl path didn't run under PowerShell). Claude Code's `allowedHttpHookUrls`/`httpHookAllowedEnvVars` in a user's `--settings` get Combwork's URL and variable (#330). 

| Hook | Combwork status / action |
|---|---|
| `SessionStart` | **ready** |
| `PreToolUse` (every tool, since #648) | A call starts (the turn ledger, below: a tool after its turn's Stop carries the turn on). Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit get the file lock check (below), answered before the tool runs; any other tool is answered at once |
| `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse` | **working** (not a `PostToolUse` of a turn that is over: the turn ledger) |
| `Notification` (permission prompt) | **waiting** — notification if window hidden/unfocused |
| `Notification` (`idle_prompt`, "Claude is waiting for your input") | Claude Code sends it once, a minute after a turn ends, only while no turn runs and no dialog is open (2.1.296): an agent waiting on a safeguard prompt that was answered is idle after the stop (*Safeguard stops*, below); an agent Combwork still shows **working** is **ready** again (**background** with background tasks counted), its file locks released, and the log says so with the launch's last eight hooks (kind, time, the status each left), never what was said (#612: HB3 stayed "Working…" after its last turn, so prompts to it were refused; its Stop was delivered, and why Combwork didn't act on it is still unknown). Any other status stands, and so does Combwork's own Compact. Claude Code's compaction while idle (before the prompt cache expires: `PreCompact` with trigger `auto`, `SessionStart` with source `compact`, `PostCompact`) and its recap (an `away_summary` in the transcript, with no hook Combwork takes) leave an idle agent idle (`PreCompact`/`PostCompact` below) |
| `Stop` | **finished** — chime if enabled; notification if hidden/unfocused. **background** instead when the agent has background tasks running that will start it again (below) |
| `StopFailure` | The turn ended on an API error instead of Stop. `error: "authentication_failed"` (`last_assistant_message` "Login expired · Please run /login", 2.1.291) is a refused sign-in: **signin** (below). Any other error (a rate limit, the server) ends the turn as `Stop` does, with the CLI's message |
| `PreCompact` | **working** ("Compacting the conversation…" when it was idle, e.g. `/compact` typed in the CLI); toast for automatic compaction |
| `PostCompact` | back to **ready** after a compaction that started idle (Combwork's Compact or `/compact`); one mid-turn keeps working, and so does a turn begun since (a prompt after the compaction began ends it). Without the hook, Combwork's Compact ends when the transcript shows a new compaction, the CLI says it refused or failed it, or if it hasn't begun 20 seconds after Combwork submitted its `/compact` (typing a long focus doesn't count) or runs past 10 minutes, with the same rule. While Combwork types the command, the agent is reserved: a second Compact or a prompt is refused, and if the agent stops meanwhile the rest isn't typed |
| `SessionEnd` | **stopped** |

Hooks have a short timeout; if Combwork is unreachable, Claude Code continues normally. The same question twice, or a second `Stop`, notifies once. The rules are in `main/hookStatus.ts` (pure, unit-tested for both providers); `SessionManager.handleHookNow` carries out what they say.

**Another conversation in the same CLI** (Claude Code `/clear` or `/resume`, Codex `/new`): its first prompt's hook carries a different session id for the same launch. Combwork then backs up the old conversation, records the new one (as the agent's session to resume) and follows it — usage, backups, the context meter. Only a prompt switches: helpers a CLI runs for itself (subagents) can report other ids.

Hooks are normalised by each adapter into one set of events (start, prompt, tool start/end, needs input, stop, interrupt, compact start/end, end), so the status rules above are shared by every provider.

**The turn ledger** (#648, `main/turnLedger.ts`, pure and unit-tested): status follows the CLI's **turns by their own ids**, so a late or missing hook can't freeze it. Each adapter keeps a hook's ids through normalisation (`NormalizedHook.ids`): the turn (Claude Code's `prompt_id`, Codex's `turn_id`; Copilot's hooks name none, 1.0.95), the tool call (`tool_use_id`), the sub-agent that sent it (Claude Code's `agent_id`) and whether a Stop follows a continuation (`stop_hook_active`). Every hook goes through it before the status rules. **Only a start opens or reopens a turn**: a prompt opens one, and after its Stop a turn reopens only on a start of it (a tool call it never started, or Combwork's own continuation of its Stop); end news (a tool end, an interrupt, the CLI idle, a refused sign-in, a Stop) never reopens one. Every hook that names a turn is that turn's news: one naming a turn that is neither the open nor the latest one (a prompt, a question, a tool, a Stop, an interrupt, the CLI idle, a refused sign-in) is stale: logged, with no effect on status, and never makes that turn active over a newer one. **An id Combwork doesn't remember is stale, never new** (the ledger keeps the latest 10,000 ids, only to say in the log whether one was an earlier turn's): only a prompt opens a turn under an id never seen, since the CLI awaits a prompt's hook before the turn. This holds for every hook that names a turn, launch-wide ones too: a delayed compaction or session end of an earlier turn is stale. Two starts the CLI makes by itself come under an id of their own with no prompt hook (Claude Code 2.1.296, verified in a test home): **a compaction** (`/compact` while idle, or its own), whose start, while no turn runs, opens that compaction, not a turn (Darren, option B), and only its own news (its end, the session's restart and end) follows under that id until a turn begins; it begins and ends once, so its start again (while it runs or after its end) and its news once it is over change nothing, but for the session's end; and **a background task's wake**, which sends its prompt hook (the task's notification) and so opens like any prompt. Should that prompt hook be lost, a tool call the launch never saw opens the wake's turn, but only while the CLI's transcript says a task of it just ended, never merely because one runs (Darren, 12 Oct). And **a turn the user's typing began with no prompt hook** (HI-2673: Claude Code 2.1.319 runs the model on a `!` command's output under that command's `promptId` and sends no UserPromptSubmit), for a CLI whose descriptor says so (`capabilities.typedTurnsWithoutPrompt`): while the user's own Enter into the idle pane still waits for its hook (hooks health's watched prompt, below), a tool call the launch never saw, under a turn id never seen, opens that turn; a Stop or tool end alone opens nothing. Past the bound on the ids kept, none of them opens anything. Hooks naming no turn are launch-wide (SessionStart, a compaction's) or from a CLI whose hooks name none, and are the latest turn's. A turn begins when its first hook reaches Combwork, not when Combwork gets round to it in the launch's queue (the CLI's records are compared with that).
- A **prompt** begins a turn, except one in the turn that runs (the same id: a message the CLI takes mid-turn). One Combwork put into the running turn itself (`expectInjected`, for Messaging 5's socket delivery, which fires `UserPromptSubmit` with the running turn's `prompt_id`) is no prompt at all.
- **A turn under the id of a compaction the CLI began itself** (HI-1916). Codex 0.164 can run the turn after its own compaction under that compaction's id: HR5, resumed into a full context on 27 Oct, had every hook of that turn dropped as "under a compaction's id", and showed "no hooks".
  - A prompt under the remembered compaction's id begins that turn, whether the compaction is still under way or over.
  - Anything else of a turn under that id before such a prompt stays stale.
  - While the turn runs and until a compaction of its own begins, that compaction's late or repeated end (`PostCompact`) and `SessionStart` under the id are stale. A `PreCompact` is the turn's own (a long turn filling its context again, HR6's round 1): from there its compactions are handled as any turn's, working throughout.
  - The fake Codex's `selfcompact` step acts this out (the `turnledger` suite). The unit tests replay the hooks.log sequence (`turns-codex-0.164.0-compaction-turn.json`).
- A **tool end of a turn that is over** is old news and changes nothing: a `PostToolUse` that reaches Combwork after its turn's `Stop` no longer makes a finished agent working (one way #642's Codex reviewer could have stayed working for 37 minutes). So is a tool end naming a turn never seen (its start would have begun it). Without turn ids the same holds for a tool end after the turn's end with no tool start since. An earlier turn's `Stop` changes nothing either.
- A **tool start of the latest turn after its Stop**, for a call the turn never started, carries that turn on (another Stop hook, the user's, made the CLI go on): working again, decided from the ids alone, so a hook that reaches Combwork before the CLI has redrawn changes nothing (Copilot's hooks name no calls: any tool start after its Stop carries it on). A start of a call the turn started before its Stop is no start of it. A delayed start that wasn't one leaves the agent working until the silence below shows its end. With no ids and no turn known yet, a tool start alone changes nothing. Claude Code's `PreToolUse` is registered for every tool for this. A sub-agent's tools are its parent's turn's while it runs, and don't carry on one that is over; a sub-agent's Stop ends nothing.
- A **Stop ends its turn only when Combwork answered it with nothing**: continuations (a block, or context the CLI acts on: `adapter.stopContinues()`) fire no prompt, so a Stop Combwork carried on leaves the turn running (Claude Code 2.1.296 and Codex 0.162.1, verified in #645's spike). The hook server asks `sessions.hookReply()` for a Stop's reply (`stopReplier`, for Messaging 4's drain; none yet) and passes it on with the hook.
- An interrupt, a refused sign-in or the CLI saying it is idle at its prompt (`idle_prompt`) ends the running turn.

**Reconciliation, and unknown ≠ idle.** When a Stop never comes, Combwork looks for the turn's end in what the CLI keeps, never on a timer:
- **The CLI's own record**: Codex's `task_complete` for that turn id in its rollout (`LiveDetails.turnEnded`, written after its Stop hooks are answered), which ends only the running turn of that id; Claude Code's `idle_prompt` notification (above). Copilot's records don't name turns as its hooks do, so Combwork counts when its Stops were answered (its `agentStop` `hook.end`, `LiveDetails.stopsAnswered`, this launch's): more answered since the running turn's first hook reached Combwork than Stops of that turn Combwork got (each one it carried the turn on with counts) means a Stop never reached Combwork, and the turn is over (`unheardStop`). One answered before the turn began is an earlier turn's, also when read in the same lines as the new prompt's hook; a final Stop missed after Combwork's continuations still counts. Either ends the turn as its Stop would: finished, told, locks released, and the log says so with the hooks before.
- **Silence** (Settings has no knob: 5 minutes with nothing heard, no hook and no transcript growth, tool calls open or not, since their ends can be lost too; `CW_TEST_SILENT_MS` in unpackaged test builds) makes Combwork look at the CLI's record again and read its screen with a **version-tested check** (`adapter.turnScreen(version)`: idle, working, or not sure), checked against screens recorded from the real CLIs, alone and in Combwork's terminals. **Idle**: Claude Code 2.1.296's status line above its input (marked "❯", or ">" as it draws it in Combwork) says the last turn is done ("✻ Worked for 12s · done 16:52") with nothing below offering to interrupt; Codex 0.162.1's input is empty, showing its placeholder ("Ask Codex to do anything"), with nothing queued. **Working**: Claude Code's spinner on that line ("✢ Embellishing…"; it shows no "esc to interrupt" in Combwork's terminals), Codex's "• Working (5s • esc to interrupt)".
