Idle on screen: the turn is over, as its Stop would end it. Working on screen (a long reply or think, a long tool): the CLI is heard, so it isn't silent. Older versions, and Copilot, aren't read.
- Failing both, the agent's state is **unknown** (with a tool call open, which may be a long test run, only after 12 times as long a silence): still **working** (so nothing is typed into it and it isn't given work), its pane saying **"Silent 23 min · state unknown"** with **Mark idle**, the log saying what Combwork saw. Anything heard of it (a hook, its transcript growing) makes it running again; **Mark idle** (`session:markIdle`, the user only) ends the turn: **ready** (or **background**), its locks released, not told as finished, and what Combwork thought ran with it (its open tool calls, a compaction, a person asked) is over too. The Agent API's `statusMessage` says it ("Silent 23 min · state unknown: … the user can mark it idle"). A card loop's stall line names the reviewer's real state ("HR3 is watching #6 but hasn't started reviewing it (it shows working, but has been silent for 23 min: state unknown)"; "(it is working on something else)" when it works), not just "watching" (#642).
- **Waiting to retry** (HI-1972). Codex refused a model request (a 429, a failed stream) waits (minutes after a 429: Retry-After) and tries again by itself (5 tries), showing only "Working" and sending no hook. Its only record is a row in its log database (`logs_2.sqlite` in its CODEX_HOME, target `codex_core::responses_retry`, by thread: "retrying sampling request (1/5 in 399.9997619s)… last status: 429"). Once a running turn has had no hook for **Retry wait: look after** (20 s), Combwork reads the thread's newest such row since the turn's last hook (`ProviderAdapter.retryWait`), at most every 15 s and one read at a time. The read is read-only, in a worker of its own (`codexLogWorker.ts`), opened and closed per read (an open file can't be deleted on Windows), with a 200 ms busy timeout. Main gives it 3 s, keeps at most 8 under way, and starts a worker that missed two deadlines again; no answer is quiet (logged once an hour per home and reason). The row's target and message are Advanced settings (**Retry wait: log entries**, **Retry wait: message**). The numbers must be sensible (1 ≤ try ≤ tries ≤ 100, a wait of at most a day, written between the turn's last hook and a minute from now). What a read finds is applied in hook order, only if the same launch and turn still run and no hook came while it read, and only if newer than the wait shown. It is `LiveSessionState.retryWait` (when it was told, the turn's first, when it retries, the try of how many, the HTTP status, and `network` for CLIs that say so). While its retry time (plus 30 s) is ahead, the status is **"Rate-limited (429) · retrying at 15:05 (1 of 5)"** ("Request failed" for another or no status). A turn that had gone unknown is running again, and the silence check doesn't make it unknown. The next hook, the turn's end or its retry time passing clears it. The pane's tooltip adds, under a 429 with the context past the Compact threshold, that a new conversation sends less (a suggestion only). The Agent API's `statusMessage` says it in English. **Claude Code and Copilot** (HI-1973, on the same field):
  - **Claude Code** (2.1.312) writes each try in its transcript as a system entry (`api_error`: `retryAttempt` of `maxRetries` (10), `retryInMs`, and `error.status`, absent when its service couldn't be reached), with no hook meanwhile; it tried 10 times over about 3 minutes against a 429, then ended its turn ("API Error: Request rejected (429) · …"). Its adapter's `retryWait` reads only the transcript's last 64 KB, through one handle, dropping the cut first line and any line that isn't such an entry or whose numbers don't hold up (as Codex's), after **Retry wait: look after** (Claude Code's, 20 s). No status is its service unreachable (`network`: "Can't reach Claude Code · retrying at …"). The entry's kind and fields are Advanced settings (**Transcript: retry entry**, its try, tries, wait and status fields), with recorded samples (`retry-claude-2.1.312.jsonl`, a 429 and a refused port).
  - **Copilot** (1.0.105) sends an `ErrorOccurred` hook for each try, `recoverable: true`, `error_context: "model_call"` (**Retry: error context**), and says neither when it tries again nor how often (5 tries, a few seconds apart). That hook is a `retry` event: the wait is kept from try to try while nothing else is heard (its first try's time, the tries counted), with no retry time or total (unknown, never made up: "Rate-limited (429) · retrying… (try 2)"). With no retry time it has no deadline: it stands until Copilot is heard from again (a later try keeps it), its turn ends or its launch does, through backoffs of any length, so its time counts towards the Assistant's notice (HR6's round 1: a guessed 30 s lost long waits). Why comes from its message (**Retry: error message**: a named `status`, 100–599; `limited`, a rate limit's words, read as 429, since the hook gives the service's own error body with no status, "Rate limit reached for requests"; or `network`). It gives up with a `session.error` of type `rate_limit` (`statusCode: 429`) as well as `query`: both end the turn failed (**Turn failed: error type**).
  - **The Assistant told**: a wait that goes on past **Retry wait: tell the Assistant after** (Combwork's, 300 s; 0: never), counted from the turn's first try, is told to the Assistant once a turn (any CLI's, through the batched control delivery HI-1612's resumes use, `assistantNotes.ts`), never of its own session. A 429 is said as a request-rate limit, never the account's usage limit, with the suggestion that a large conversation sends less from a new one: a suggestion for the user, never an automatic restart. One that ends sooner tells nothing; a later turn's is told again.
  - **The handover**: retrying that ends on a connection error ends the turn failed in the CLI's connection words, which HI-1612's resume takes as before. One that ends on a 429 is never taken as a dropped connection (each CLI's recorded words checked): it isn't resumed, which would only add to the throttle.
  - The pane's tooltip adds "Retrying since {time}" once there was more than one try.
  - **Afterwards** (HI-1996): each wait, as it is cleared (a hook, its turn's end, its retry time passed: at that time,
    not when Combwork noticed), is added to the launch's tally (`LiveSessionState.retryWaited`: how many, their time
    together, the latest), so a slow round can be told from a throttled one once it is over. `cw_agent_activity` gives
    it as `retryWaits` (the one under way counted to now, `ongoing`), beside the `model` and `effort` the agent runs
    with (its CLI's report, else what the launch gave it, `LiveSessionState.launchedWith`, else its CLI's default). A
    running session's pane footer resolves its model and effort the same way (`footerChoices`: the launch's, with
    whether it was given a model, never the settings changed since; a stopped agent's, its connection's values, never a
    project's or Settings' old ones, which no launch uses since HI-2106). A model its connection chose shows plainly,
    before and after it starts; only a model its CLI picks itself (none given) is marked "(default)" (HI-2398). The pane footer's model hover adds the total ("This session has waited 7 minutes in all … (2 waits, the latest from
    15:05)"). A new launch starts a new tally.

**Status as fields** (`LiveSessionState.runtime`, `.turn` and `.backgroundTasks`, gathered by `shared/runtime.ts` `agentRuntime()`): separate facts, each stored where Combwork learns it, never read back from the status word. **Lifecycle** (starting, running once the CLI reports anything or shows its prompt, needs sign-in from a refused sign-in until a request of its own works, stopped). **Turn** (running, over, unknown, none; with the CLI's id: the ledger). **Maintenance**: compacting from `PreCompact`, mid-turn too, or Combwork's Compact, until `PostCompact`, the turn's end, a prompt starting a new turn or Combwork's Compact ending. **Attention**: waiting when the status rules make the agent wait for a person, until they move it on; a question while one waits beside its work. **Composer**: held while Combwork types into its input, confirms a wake or waits for a typed line to be taken (or one wasn't), else free. **Background tasks**. The labels (the pane, the dot's tooltip, `statusText`) are projected from these facts (`runtimeLabel()`: stopped, asking, starting, needs sign-in, compacting, silent with its state unknown, working); when no turn runs, Combwork's policy words apply: watching, finished or ready, background tasks. The status word stays as the coarse gate today's producers use (Messaging 3 moves them onto deliveries). `GET /v1/projects/{name}/agents/{agent}/activity?detail=true` (`cw_agent_activity` with detail) gives them as `runtime`; the short form's `statusMessage` says when the state is unknown.

**Hook journal** (`logs/hooks.log`, beside `combwork.log`, kept to 5 MB and one older copy): each hook a CLI sent, with its launch (`run=`), its receive order (`seq=`), event, turn and call ids, sub-agent, `continued`, the status before and after, and what the ledger made of it (stale and why, carried on by Combwork), so the next stuck status can be traced (#642's couldn't). Ids and statuses only, never the user's text; reconciliations and Mark idle are journaled too.

**Hooks health** (#1336; there is no hooks-free mode, §16.15 row 10): hooks that stop arriving while Combwork thinks all is well (a CLI update changed them, a policy turned them off, Combwork refused their token) are said, never left as a wrong status. Read from what Combwork already has, no status engine of its own (`main/hooksHealth.ts`), each sign needing time and evidence, never time alone, within **Hooks missing: wait** (Settings → Advanced, `cw.hooks.missingSeconds`, 60 s):
- **its start**: a CLI that sends a hook as it starts (`capabilities.startHook`: Claude Code's SessionStart; Codex's and Copilot's come with the first prompt) sent none within the wait, the time a question at its start (folder trust) is on its screen not counted;
- **a prompt**: one sent while it was idle (the user's Enter in its pane, a line Combwork typed, a task on its command line) had no hook of a current turn after it for the wait (the turn ledger's verdict: a late hook of a turn that is over answers nothing; while the user's own Enter waits, for a CLI with `typedTurnsWithoutPrompt`, a hook of a turn the launch has never seen answers it, HI-2673, since it can't be late news: not an earlier turn's, a sub-agent's, or one past the bound on the ids kept; the ledger remembers the turn it answered for, so the same turn's hook again answers no later prompt), while its screen reading said working (it was idle when the prompt went, so that work is this prompt's), seen at least 15 s before (at most the wait). The check runs in the launch's hook order, so a hook that came first is taken first. A long silent think never counts (its prompt's hook came), nor a prompt sent while it works; an Enter that started nothing (a menu, a local command) is dropped once its screen shows it idle.
- **a turn its transcript shows** (#1371): a turn the CLI's own records identify, begun by a prompt written since this launch started and taken up by the model, with no hook naming it for the wait since Combwork found it. Identity, not position: Claude Code's turn is its prompt's `promptId` (every user entry carries it; an assistant entry belongs to the turn its `parentUuid` chain leads to), which its hooks carry as `prompt_id`; Codex's is its `turn_id` (its prompt's `item_completed` UserMessage, or before 0.159 its `user_message` inside the task; its model's items and reply), carried by its hooks; Copilot's is an `interactionId` (`user.message`, then `assistant.turn_start`/`assistant.message`), and its hooks carry none, so its prompt hook answers it by the prompt's text (Copilot records the prompt once that hook has returned) and any hook received after the prompt was recorded answers it too. A hook naming the turn answers it whenever it comes, before or after the transcript is written (a Stop that comes first, a response flushed late after a local command: both are their own turn's). Not turns: a local command (no model work), a compaction, a sub-agent's or side conversation's (`isSidechain`, Codex's sub-turns), Claude Code's task-notification wakes (whether their hooks come isn't certain). The reading (`turnsReader.ts`, each adapter's `transcriptTurns`) is one per conversation and file, done in the 5 s transcript look: this launch's new conversation from its start, any other (resumed, switched to by `/clear` or `/resume`, found later) from its end then, so history never counts (nor a prompt older than the launch); another path or conversation, a shrink or other first bytes (a file replaced under its name) start it again and drop what it found; whole lines only, a line begun before the reading dropped; more than 4 MB since the last look forgets what it knew, so a turn whose prompt it didn't read is unknown; what a read found is kept only if the launch, conversation and reading are still the ones it read for. The check only reads what was stored: no hook waits on a read. A quick turn over before Combwork's first look at its screen is caught this way, and Copilot too.
- **Not covered**: a new Codex session's turns while its hooks are missing (with no hook it reports no session id, so there is no rollout to read; a turn long enough to be seen on its screen is caught, and its start with a task); a Copilot turn whose turn before's late hook arrives after its prompt was recorded (taken as its hook: it errs toward saying nothing); Claude Code's task-notification wakes.

Then, for that launch (`LiveSessionState.hooksMissing`: since, after start, prompt or transcript (with the turn's id), and why when Combwork can tell: it refused their token, the CLI's settings turn them off (Claude Code: the first scope setting `disableAllHooks`, or managed settings with `allowManagedHooksOnly`), or the CLI is newer than Combwork was tested with, said as just that: Combwork knows the version only at launch, so it never guesses at an update during the session, HI-2673): its status reads **"Status unknown: no hooks from Claude Code"** (pane, sidebar row, board, the Agent API's `statusMessage`), its mark is stalled, nothing is typed into it (`readyFor`: no wakes, messages or tasks), its lanes pause (`hooks`: "paused: B6's hooks aren't arriving"), the project's banner over its pane says why and what to do with **Restart session**, and a toast says it once a conversation (kept in Notifications). A current turn's hook of that launch clears it (a late hook of a turn that is over doesn't); one a transcript turn raised clears only on that turn's hook or a newer turn's, by identity. The invariant (#1371): a transcript turn T stops being waited on, alarm or not, only on a hook naming T or a turn the transcript places after T, whichever comes first, the hook or the record; nothing else but dropping the reading ends it. One transition does it (`answeredUpTo`, from `hookTurn` as each hook is taken, or from `transcriptTurns` when a hook came before its record), whether or not an alarm has fired: a newer turn's hook before the deadline means the older turn is never flagged. An id the transcript hasn't placed is unknown, never newer, whatever the ledger makes of it (the ledger's current turn may be older than the flagged one) (Copilot: any hook answers a standing flag, and only the turns read so far). Places are bounded (the latest 500): a turn still waited on or flagged keeps its own place when they let go of it, and one let go that wasn't (answered, or never worked) is remembered as forgotten, so a late record of it is unknown, never placed anew as newer. What is answered stays answered for that reading: a record of an answered turn appended later (Claude Code chains one to it) isn't waited on again, while a turn read after the answer still is. The transcript reading starting again (another file, a shrink, other first bytes, another conversation) drops that alarm with the evidence it came from; a start or prompt alarm stays. A read whose file changed while it waited (a hook naming another transcript) is dropped. A restart starts a new launch.

**Background tasks.** An agent can leave work running when its turn ends: a test run, a server, a watch. Each adapter reads them from the transcript as it grows (`backgroundTasks()`), and Combwork counts the ones started since the agent launched (`backgroundTasks` in its live state; shown as "· 2 background tasks running").
- **Claude Code**: a background Bash call's result has `backgroundTaskId` (also a command moved to the background after running too long), a Monitor's has `taskId` and an expiry. A **subagent** the Agent tool runs in the background (#1584) has an `async_launched` result with its `agentId` (a background workflow the same with a `taskId`); a message to one that has finished resumes it (`resumedAgentId`), which counts it again until it notifies again, and a message queued to one still running changes nothing. A task ends with a `<task-notification>` naming it (any status but a Monitor's events) or a `TaskStop`. Claude Code is told when a task ends and starts a new turn by itself, so the provider has the `backgroundWakes` capability: a turn that ends with tasks open leaves the agent **background** ("Waiting on 2 background tasks"), not finished. Each end it is told of begins a turn, also while other tasks run on (that wake may open a turn, as the turn ledger's rule 1 has it); when the last one ends, the agent is **working** again (the notification's turn), then finished at its Stop. No "finished" notification or chime until then. A task the agent stopped itself (`TaskStop`) gets no notification and starts no turn: the last one ending that way leaves it **finished** (#640). Combwork keeps what each task is (a command, a Monitor, a subagent, a workflow) and a subagent's description with its count, for the activity graph (#1254).
- **Codex**: a command still running when `exec_command` returns gives a `session_id` instead of an `exit_code`; Codex records its end as an `item_completed` CommandExecution with that `process_id`. In code mode (0.160) the command runs inside an `exec` script that prints what the model chooses, and Codex records no start (only each command's end, and no record of which `exec_command` calls a script ran), so a start needs evidence: an id the output shows (the result's whole-number `session_id`, or a script that reads `session_id`, printed only numbers, such as `text(r.session_id)`, and had none of its commands end within it), ended by its `process_id`; or else a script that runs its one `exec_command` once (a real call, not one in a string or a comment, as a statement of its own at the top level, with no loop, condition, function or `try` in the script) and completed with none of its commands ended, since Codex writes the end of every command that ends within a script before the script's output (counted under a stand-in id, ended by the CommandExecution of the same command text). Anything less clear (a loop that printed no ids, a condition, a failed or aborted script, an end that could be the script's own) counts nothing: a command missed rather than one counted that isn't running (`providers/codex/background.ts`, which keeps what it needs between reads of the rollout). Codex isn't told when one ends (checked with 0.159), so its agents stay **finished** and the count is only shown. Its **subagents** (`spawn_agent`, 0.164) can outlive the turn that spawned them (#1584: a real run's parent turn ended 78 s before its subagent, and Codex started no turn for its end); the parent's rollout records each as a `SubAgentActivity` item, `started` and then `completed` (any other kind ends it too), by its thread id and named by its task (`agent_path`), and they count the same way. The CLIs' subagent records (Claude Code's launch status, id, description and resume fields; Codex's activity item, its started kind and its thread and task fields) are advanced settings (`claude-code.subagent.*`, `codex.subagent.*`). Guardian reviews (subagents too) run within the turn and write no such item.
- **Time limit.** Combwork can't tell a test run from something that never ends (a dev server), so a task stops counting after **Settings → Agents → Count background tasks for up to** (60 minutes; 10–480), and a Monitor at its own expiry if sooner. Combwork logs it, and an agent left background then shows finished ("Stopped counting its background tasks after 60 minutes"), with the notification.
- A **background** agent counts as busy: `cw_wait_for_agents` waits through it (unless `ignoreBackground`), `cw_prompt_agent`, Hand Over, Compact and Merge refuse it, *Confirm before quitting* asks (its tasks would stop), and *Quit when agents finish* waits for it. The sidebar dot is a slow, faint pulse.
- **Needs sign-in** (`signin`, #309) is the status of an agent whose CLI refused its turn because the sign-in has expired or was refused. Each adapter says so (no provider ids elsewhere): Claude Code by `StopFailure` with `authentication_failed`; Codex, which sends no hook then, by its rollout: a `task_complete` whose `error.codex_error_info` is `unauthorized` or carries HTTP 401 (0.160.0, an invalid API key: `http_connection_failed: { http_status_code: 401 }`), else only Codex's own sign-in messages (a 401 status line, a refresh token that expired, was used or was revoked) — `LiveDetails.signIn`, applied in order with the launch's hooks (not when a hook came while it was being read: the next prompt is newer than the refusal, #480). Before this, both CLIs' agents stayed **working** for ever. The turn ends (locks released, not told as finished) and the agent keeps the CLI's message (`LiveSessionState.signIn`, shown in its tooltips; the status line says **Needs sign-in**). It needs the user (the inbox, the taskbar count, `cw_wait_for_agents` stops for it, `cw_prompt_agent` refuses it; its `statusMessage` there says why). One notice per CLI and expiry, a few seconds after the first agent so agents refused together are counted together ("3 agents need you to sign in to Claude Code", with the descriptor's `signInHelp`); a later agent in the same expiry is shown, not told. Combwork checks the CLI's sign-in at once (Provider Setup shows it signed out) and every minute while agents wait. It is **signed in again** when a request of an agent of that CLI works (a tool call, or a turn that ends well: Claude Code carries the turn on after `/login` in its terminal; not a prompt merely sent, an interrupt, or a turn that failed on something else, such as a rate limit — Claude Code's other `StopFailure` errors are `stop` events marked `failed`), when its check goes from signed out to signed in, or when Provider Setup's Sign in task ends well (`providerService.onSignedIn`). Until then the expiry lasts: an agent it stopped keeps `signIn` through a retry that doesn't get through (its own prompt or Resume's shows **working** meanwhile; interrupted, or failed on something else, it is **signin** again, not told as finished), and the minute's recheck ends the expiry quietly only once no agent it stopped is running. Then the agents still stopped are **ready** with "Stopped while signed out" and a toast; until a request of their own works they keep `signIn`, and **Resume All Agents (n)** counts them (`stalledOnSignIn()` in `shared/resumeAll.ts`): it gives each a short "carry on" (`session:carryOn`; a control delivery for that launch, given now, #649), never one that has carried on by itself, and never unasked. Codex's behaviour after signing in again mid-session wasn't observed.
- **Waiting for the connection** (HI-1612, `outageResume.ts`, `outageCore.ts`; Darren's decision, 28 Oct: **off by default**, for everyone, solo users too) is what an agent stopped by a dropped connection shows while Combwork waits to resume it, with **Settings → Advanced → Resume agents after a connection drops** (`cw.outage.resume`) on. It starts from a failed turn (`LiveSessionState.failedTurn`, above) whose words its CLI's pattern finds (`<provider>.outage.connectionError`: Claude Code's StopFailure message after its retries, `server_error` with *Connection refused … (ECONNREFUSED)* or *Can't reach the API server … (ENOTFOUND)*, 2.1.312; Codex's task_complete error, *stream disconnected … Transport error*, 0.164.0, which only a stream dropped mid-turn gives: a provider refusing connections doesn't fail Codex's turn, it waits for the network; Copilot's `session.error`, *error sending request … [ENOTFOUND]* or *Could not connect to*, 1.0.105, the same words as its hooks') and Combwork's pattern for what is never a dropped connection doesn't (`cw.outage.notConnection`: a usage or rate limit, a sign-in, an overloaded server, 401/403/429/529), so none of those is ever resumed or looped on; a refused sign-in is `signin` anyway. The agent's status says *Waiting for the connection…* (its failed-turn mark stays, so it still needs you), and a Progress run of the agent's, *<agent>: waiting for the connection*, waits for *the connection to come back*. Combwork checks its CLI's API host (`cw.outage.checkUrl.<provider>`: api.anthropic.com, chatgpt.com, api.githubcopilot.com; a server connection's base URL instead, HI-1772) with a HEAD request by IPv4 and by IPv6 at once, any answer counting (an error status too), asynchronous throughout so main's thread is never held; first after `cw.outage.checkFirstSeconds` (30 s), the wait doubling up to `cw.outage.checkMostSeconds` (300 s). Once it answers, the agent's own conversation gets one `control` delivery for that launch, given now or not at all (only while the agent is still stopped on that failed turn): *The connection dropped at 11:47 (UTC+01:00) and came back at 11:57 (UTC+01:00): check what was cut off, rerun it, and carry on.* (no lane context: the conversation has it); the run ends passed, *Resumed: the connection dropped at … and came back at ….* It gives up, with a warning notice naming the likely fixes (renew the adapter's addresses, `ipconfig /renew`; flush DNS, `ipconfig /flushdns`; restart the PC: the PC's own network may not have recovered, as on 25 Oct) and its status *Stopped: its connection didn't come back* or *Stopped: its connection keeps dropping*: once the wait passes `cw.outage.waitMinutes` (120 min), or when its turn ends on a connection error again after `cw.outage.resumesPerHour` (3) resumes in the past hour. Anything else that ends the failed turn (a new turn: the user's prompt, a wake) or the launch ends the wait quietly (the run ends stopped), as does turning the switch off. The workspace's Assistant gets a `control` delivery of what was resumed or given up, agents resumed within 5 s of each other in one; never of itself.
- **Watching** is the status of an agent whose turn has ended with a card watch running (§6.6, *Waiting on cards*): its `ready`/`finished` shows as `watching` (`SessionManager.emitState`), and when the watch ends it is `finished` again. It counts as busy like `background`: *Confirm before quitting* asks, for quitting and for closing a window or workspace or switching it (the dialog says what it waits for: stopping pauses its card loop until it is resumed, the watch kept); the Assistant's stop asks the user first; Merge is refused until it has finished or its watch is cancelled (merging commits unfinished work); `cw_prompt_agent` and Start Task refuse it. *Quit when agents finish* waits for it only while a card it watches is in Doing or Review with another agent (`watchKeepsQuitWaiting`, the same rule for the dialog's offer and the wait); once the watches have seen a watched card move or change hands (`onWatchedCardsMoved`), a pending quit checks again, so it goes ahead when no such card is left even though no wake comes. But `cw_wait_for_agents` doesn't wait for it (it reports `watching`, with the watch's label as `statusMessage`), and Compact is allowed from the header, the agent menu and the dialog (the watch is kept; a wake waits until the compaction has ended). No "finished" notification or chime while it watches. The sidebar dot is a hollow ring in the info colour. The window words the watch itself (`watchText`, HI-1679): its cards by key and in the user's language, never the watch's English `label`, which is what agents and the Agent API read (it may carry a card's workspace-wide number). In the Overviews' **Running now** and the focus view's strip, a watch on one card reads *Waiting → Review* beside that card's chip (the chip a working agent's card has, a click opening it), the whole status on hover; in Running now a watch on several cards reads the same with a chip each (keys only), or how many (*2 cards*) when they don't all fit, never a key cut. As a Running now row narrows, its card's title gives way first (down to the key), then the status, then the project before the agent's name; the agent's name and the card's key stay whole, and the chip stays one line.
- Combwork looks at a running transcript every 5 seconds and reads it again when its size or modified time changes: Windows can report an old modified time for a file Codex keeps appending to.

**Safeguard stops** (#606, Darren's decisions of 11 and 12 Oct). A CLI's safety classifier can stop an agent's response (Opus 5.5's safeguards stopped one of HB3's on 11 Oct), ask what to do about it, or switch the agent to another model by itself (Claude Code's fallback when `/config` says to switch models when a message is flagged). Combwork shows when, on which model, and the **names** of the agent's last few tool calls before it (5), never the stopped content (the CLI withholds it anyway) nor a call's input.
- **What it is told by**, as named defaults in one place (`SAFEGUARD_DEFAULTS` in `shared/safeguards.ts`: data, not code), the note and the question Advanced settings (§9.3, #685: `claude-code.safeguard.note`, `.prompt`) that the detection reads through `advanced`, so an override changes them; the record subtypes and Codex's codes join them once a real session of one is recorded (#697): **Claude Code**'s transcript (`claudeSafeguards()`, its 2.1.296 records): a stop it retries once is its system note ("Opus 5.5's safeguards stopped the response above · continuing once with that noted", subtype `informational`, matched by the `claudeNote` pattern) and, as the next entry in its chain, the notice it adds for the model (a user entry with `refusedMessageId`, the stopped response); a flagged request another model answered, or none did, is its record of it (`claudeRecords`: subtypes `model_refusal_fallback`, with `originalModel`, `fallbackModel` and `scope`, and `model_refusal_no_fallback`), which for the session (`scope: session`) is also a switch the safeguard made; a fallback for another reason (its `trigger` not `refusal`) isn't one. Its own messages (`/feedback`'s `local_command`) and side chains don't count. A model change in its assistant messages after a stop is a switch, except the one response another model answered alone (`scope: local`). **Codex** (`codexSafeguards()`, from its 0.160 binary: no rollout of one seen yet): a `model_reroute` event whose reason is in `codexReroute` (`high_risk_cyber_activity`) is a stop and a switch from `from_model` to `to_model`; an `error` or `task_complete` with a `codex_error_info` in `codexStop` (`cyber_policy`, `bio_policy`) a stop.
- **One stop, counted once, by its identity, never by time** (`SafeguardEvent.id`, kept in the detector's memo: `newStop()`): Claude Code's note and its notice are one stop (adjacent, or the notice's `parentUuid` the note's `uuid`); a notice alone is a stop by its `refusedMessageId`, a record by its `requestId`; Codex's a stop per turn (its `turn_id`, or the count of turns started) and kind. A record read again is no other stop, and two stops seconds apart are two. **Copilot**'s session events have no equivalent: **not detected** (`safeguardHelp: null` in its descriptor), and Combwork says so where it would show one.
- **The agent's note** (`LiveSessionState.safeguard`, `noteSafeguard()`): the last stop's time, model and tool names, the stops this launch, the switch (from, to, since) until the model changes back, and whether it waits on the CLI's prompt about it or is idle after one. Each stop a detector or the screen check gives it counts. Its pane shows a shield beside the status (amber while it waits, is idle after one, or runs on another model, with that model's name), its tooltip saying what happened and the provider's pointers (Claude Code: `/feedback` for a false positive, `/model` to switch back, `/config` for the switch setting); the agent's tab tooltip says it too.
- **A switch** is told: Combwork's notice ("HB3 now runs on Opus 4.8"), a comment by Combwork on the agent's Doing cards (`commentOnDoingCards()`), and the attention inbox (**After a safeguard stop**) until the agent's pane has been on screen (`safeguard.unseen`, cleared by `markSeen`).
- **The prompt about a stop.** Claude Code asks whether to switch models (a question it puts through its permission check, header "Model switch": "…'s safeguards flagged this message. … Switch to Opus 4.8 and keep going whenever this happens?", choices **Switch automatically** and **Stay on** its model) with a `Notification` (`permission_prompt`) naming no tool ("Claude needs your permission"), after its turn's `Stop` (so the turn ledger finds it stale), and the stop that asked HB3 left no record in its transcript. So a blocking ask naming no tool, from a CLI whose adapter tells a safeguard prompt by its screen (`safeguardAsk()`: the `claudePrompt` pattern, the open dialog's two numbered choices, in the last 24 lines it wrote; never the words "safeguards" or "safety classifier" in task text or an earlier stop's note, nor an answered prompt, which shows only its answer), is checked against the screen when it arrives and as the screen draws, for 10 seconds; once it is one, the agent **waits** (even after its turn's Stop) and the status and notification say why, with the last tool calls ("A safety classifier stopped a response: Claude Code asks what to do (its last tool calls: Bash, Edit)"). The prompt is a stop (once, however often it is told while it waits), kept on the session's record (`SessionRecord.screenStops`) for Performance with its **turn** (`SafeguardEvent.turn`: the uuid of the prompt that started it, in the transcript's order; a prompt is any user entry with text, markup and all, or images alone, that isn't Claude Code's own: meta entries, a compaction's summary, tool results). Claude Code's record of a stop it asked about (`model_refusal_fallback` after **Switch automatically**: `SafeguardEvent.asked`) carries its turn the same way, so in a turn one prompt and one record are the same stop, whichever Combwork reads first, however late (after the next prompt) and across a restart: the agent's note counts it once (`seenInTurn()`), and so does Performance, which matches them from what is kept (`SessionUsage.safeguardsAsked` per turn, `withScreenStops()`). A second prompt in a turn, a record in a turn with no prompt, and a prompt with no turn known are each a stop of their own. The CLI sends no hook for the answer, so HB3 showed "Claude needs your permission" for half an hour: the wait ends (`safeguardAnswered()` in `hookStatus.ts`) when its `idle_prompt` comes, or the prompt is gone from its screen, once the user has typed in its terminal since it asked (or the prompt is no longer on screen at all). It is then **ready** with "Idle after a safeguard stop: give it a nudge" (or **background** on its tasks) until it is given something to do.
- **The Assistant** sees it in `cw_agent_activity`: `safeguard` with when, the stops, the model, the tool names before it, the model switched to and from and since when, and whether it waits on the prompt or is idle after one; `"not detected"` for a CLI Combwork can't tell. **Performance** counts the stops (below).

**A CLI's question by itself while idle** (HI-1959). Claude Code 2.1.312 offers, after a turn in auto mode, to teach auto mode about the environment ("Teach auto mode about your environment?": Yes / Not now / Don't show again, then a wizard whose Continue reads the project, recent sessions and optionally shell history and other repositories). It sends no hook. Its own code shows it once per home after 5 starts and 5 auto mode denials, again a week after Not now, never after Don't show again, unless the settings turn the `auto-mode-setup` skill off (`skillOverrides`). HB4's wake was typed into it and Combwork's Enter again answered it (Yes); the line it took left the agent held behind an empty input.
- **Told by its screen**: the adapter's `idleQuestion` (Claude Code: the Advanced pattern `claude-code.screen.idleQuestion`, its title as a line of its own in the screen's last lines, with no input box drawn (2.1.312's dialogs replace the box) or under the last box drawn (2.1.314 draws the offer under its empty input box and footer, recorded on 31 Oct, HI-2191): the same words above the box, in a prompt being written or in a reply, are never it), looked at as the screen is drawn while the agent is between turns (ready, finished, background, watching), waits on it, or holds a line, and once as a hook makes it idle (the CLI draws the offer right after its Stop, before Combwork has carried it out, and may draw nothing after it: HI-2191), one look at a time in hook order. Showing, the agent waits for the user with it as with any question (`{ kind: 'question', blocking: true }`, status "Claude Code asks: …": Needs input, For you, the notification, the Assistant's wake); gone, it is idle again (`idleQuestionGone`).
- **Never answered by Combwork**: while it shows, `sendPrompt` refuses before clearing, before each part and before Enter ("Its CLI shows a question for you…"), `submitAgain` presses no Enter, and `whyNoLine` says why to an agent's call. The choice reads the user's data, so it is theirs.
- **A held line it took** (#430's mark): let go only on positive evidence, twice. A look counts it lost when no question shows, the agent is between turns, its CLI has taken no prompt since the mark, and its ordinary input is drawn and empty (the adapter's `promptText`: the Advanced pattern `claude-code.screen.input`, the last box between two rules, read from the screen with dim cells blanked, since Claude Code's empty input holds a dim hint). The first look is taken as the line is marked (in hook order, for that launch), not only at the next draw, which may never come once a dialog that took the line has closed. A second look after `cw.lostLine.steadySeconds` (2 s) must say the same for the same launch and line, and any draw between that says otherwise (no box, text in it, the question, a turn) calls it off. Then the mark goes: the deliveries it rang for are offered again (one read meanwhile was taken, and clears the mark as before), and a line that rang for none is told to the user with its words. Text in the input (the line, wrapped or whole, or the user's own) is never cleared or typed over.
- **Turned off per launch** with **Offer auto mode's environment setup** (`claude-code.autoModeSetup.offer`, on by default): off, Combwork's `--settings` file sets `skillOverrides["auto-mode-setup"]` to `off` (never where the user's own `--settings` name that skill), so the offer isn't shown in Combwork's sessions; auto mode's decisions don't change (unlike an `autoMode.environment` entry, which also stops it), and `/auto-mode-setup` still runs it. Its effect is read from Claude Code's code (`tests/fixtures/advanced/envsetup-code-claude-2.1.312.txt`), not yet seen on a screen: the test home's probe didn't get the offer.

**Codex's offer of a cheaper model** (HI-2609). Near an account's usage limit, Codex 0.166.0 offers a cheaper model between turns ("Approaching rate limits / Switch to gpt-6-luna for lower credit usage?": 1. Switch to … (selected), 2. Keep current model, 3. Keep current model (never show again)). It sends no hook, and Enter takes the selected choice. On 5 Nov a card-event wake's Enter took it: CB1, launched on its connection's `gpt-6-astra`, ran `gpt-6-luna` from then on (its rollout's `thread_settings_applied`), and other Codex agents on the same account did the same. The connection's model stays the model:
- **Turned off per launch** with **Don't offer a cheaper model near the limit** (`codex.rateLimitNudge.hide`, on by default): each Codex launch gets `-c notice.hide_rate_limit_model_nudge=true` (Codex's own `[notice]` key, typed: a wrong value is refused, `tests/fixtures/advanced/ratelimit-nudge-hide-codex-0.166.0.txt`), before the user's own arguments, which win. Nothing is written to Codex's files. Combwork doesn't answer the offer itself: which choice Enter takes depends on its selection and order, which the CLI owns.
- **Told by its screen**, with the switch off or where Codex shows it anyway: the Codex adapter's `idleQuestion`, as above. It is read by the view's own layout (HR2's round 1). The view replaces the input while it shows, so it is the last thing drawn. The last line Codex marks with `›` in its first column must be its **selected row** (`› 1. Switch to …`, whichever choice is selected). The choices above it (not selected, indented and numbered, or a choice's text wrapped onto a line indented further) lead up to its first choice (HR2's round 2). Its title (`codex.screen.idleQuestion`) must start a paragraph of its own in the few lines just above that first choice, with only the view's indented lines between (no `•` conversation item, no `›` line). One of its choices (`codex.screen.idleQuestionChoice`, "2. Keep current model") must be in the view. So its words are never it in a reply or a prompt above the input, in what is left of a view answered, or typed into the input however the draft wraps or is numbered: a draft's first line `› 1. …` has nothing of the view above it, and its other lines follow its `›`. The agent waits for the user with it ("Codex asks: Approaching rate limits"), and nothing is typed or pressed, as for Claude Code's question. A question read on the screen is put to the user at once, though Codex's terminal title otherwise decides when Codex asks (`Ask.onScreen`): nothing says this view titles the terminal. The screen is composed from Darren's screen and the binary's strings (`ratelimit-nudge-codex-0.166.0.txt`); recording one needs an account near its real limit.

**Codex's prompts at a workspace's limit** (HI-2619). When a workspace member's turn fails at the workspace's credit or usage limit, Codex 0.166.0 shows a choice view of the same kind in place of its input (`workspace-usage-nudge`): "You've reached your workspace credit limit / Your workspace is out of credits. Ask your workspace owner to add more. Notify owner?" or "Usage limit reached / Request a limit increase from your owner to continue using codex. Request increase?", then `1. Yes (y)` and `› 2. No (default) (n)`. Yes emails the workspace's owner, so a key typed into it reaches outside the PC: Enter or `n` answers No, and a wake's `y` (in "your") would answer Yes. Each is a question by itself, read as the offer above is: their titles are in `codex.screen.idleQuestion` and their `No (default)` in `codex.screen.idleQuestionChoice` (patterns that list each view's). Codex word-wraps the view's header (its title and its question) to the pane, at most 8 lines, and leaves two blank lines before the choices: the header is read as that paragraph, up to 10 lines above the first choice, its lines joined again, and the title must begin on its first line (HR1's round 1: a 30-column pane draws the credit title on two lines). Nothing hides them per launch: Codex's `features.workspace_owner_usage_nudge` is listed as removed, and the view is opened on the failed turn with no `[notice]` key. Not recorded on a screen (that needs a workspace at its limit): the fixtures (`credit-limit-nudge-codex-0.166.0.txt`, `usage-limit-nudge-codex-0.166.0.txt`) are Codex's own snapshots of these views at its `rust-v0.166.0` tag, with the error line it prints above them.

**A model other than the launch gave it** (HI-2609). Whatever changed it (the offer above taken, `/model`, a CLI's own fallback), a session that reports a model its launch didn't give it is marked while that lasts (`LiveSessionState.modelSwitch`: the launched and the running model's IDs, and since when):
- **Compared by ID** (`modelSwitched`, shared): the launch's own model (`launchedWith.own`; the CLI's default decides nothing), an alias resolved through the CLI's catalogue (`dialectModelId`: one it can't resolve decides nothing), against the model ID the CLI reports, both by `modelIdentity` (case aside, and only the suffixes `MODEL_ID_EQUIVALENT_SUFFIXES` lists, now Claude Code's `[1m]`; any other suffix such as `[preview]`, a snapshot date or another name is another model). Never by display name: two IDs can share one, and a renamed label is the same model. A server connection's session decides nothing (its CLI names the Claude model the server's stands in for, HI-1772). A record from before the launch (a resumed rollout's earlier turns: `LiveDetails.modelAt`) decides nothing.
- **Shown**: the footer's model (the running one, as before) gets the warning mark, its hover saying "Launched with …; Codex now runs …. Restart the agent to go back to …"; Activity shows *Model changed: … → …* under Now; `cw_agent_activity` adds `launchedModel`. The user is told once a launch, in a notice kept in Notifications that opens the agent, and the log says each change. Back on its own model, the mark goes. A restart launches on the connection's model again.

**An input that takes no keys** (HI-2191). On 31 Oct, Claude Code 2.1.314 drew its offer under the empty input box, which `idleQuestion` then didn't count. Its dialog took Combwork's keys: HB5's card was typed into it 105 times in 5 minutes, and HB3's wake about 1,000 times in 53 minutes, while nothing showed the user, so any dialog Combwork doesn't know is caught by what its keys do:
- **Blocked**: before typing, Combwork clears the input (Claude Code: a letter that must show alone in the box, then the Backspace that takes it back). A clear refused because a key went unanswered while the box read empty counts. Any clear that empties the box resets the count, a key answered late but within **Clearing the input: wait for each key** too. At 3 in a row (one delivery's tries) the input is blocked for that run. At its prompt, the agent waits for the user with *Something on its screen is taking its keys: answer it there, then Try again* (a blocking question: Needs input, the notification, a lane watch's `waiting`); already waiting on another question, that one's reason stays.
- **Nothing typed meanwhile**: `sendPrompt` refuses before any key, `submitAgain` presses no Enter, and `whyNoLine` says why ("something on its screen is taking its keys…"). So wakes and messages wait queued, unpressed, and a slot's placement makes no delivery (below). No timer types into it again: time passing is no evidence the dialog is gone.
- **Free again only on evidence, in the same run**: a hook that shows its CLI moved (a prompt taken, a tool, a turn's end, a question of its own, which then keeps its own reason; not its idle notice); its input box drawn differently from when it was blocked after the user typed there (their key reached it; keys that only move about a dialog leave the box as it was); or **Try again** beside its status (and in its pane's ⋯ menu, where a narrow pane's header has no room for it), the user's: one clear, one at a time, for that block only (a click for an earlier block, or after it ended, types nothing), which frees it if answered and otherwise says *Its input still takes no keys*. A box showing the user's text is never cleared: it took their key, so it is free. Their typing during the try stops it. The pause after they type doesn't hold Try again (their Esc that put the dialog off counts as typing). A new run is never blocked by the last.
- **A slot's placement waits** (HI-2191, HB3's re-give every second): before making the card's delivery, a pass whose builder can't take a line now (`whyNoLine` with `free`: blocked, a line of Combwork's being typed, watching, working, the user typing…) waits (`place`'s `nextLook`). It makes no delivery, says why once, and looks again by what ends each reason: the builder's status (watching, working, blocked, a question), Combwork done with its line there (the writer's lock released, or its check that the CLI took it: `onLineFreed`, no status change), the pause after the user typed there (one timer, at its end), its folder steady again, its Combwork tools connected; and `nextLook`'s own look after 30 s. Never a delivery made on a timer. One made and cancelled each pass wrote the lane each time, which triggered the next pass.
- Codex and Copilot: their input isn't read (no `promptBox`), so Combwork's one Ctrl+U is never checked and no input is blocked this way. A line they don't take is held as not taken (#430).

**File locks.** Hooks are matched to sessions by `session_id`, so every agent reports its own status. For file edits, `PreToolUse` asks Combwork first: the first agent to edit a file claims it (by its real path, so a junction or link to the same file is the same file; the file is named to agents, in the agent's locked files and in Agent API activity relative to that agent's folder, by real paths when the folder and the file are written two ways: `placeRelative`, #494); while the claim holds, another agent's edit of the same file gets, depending on the lock mode, `permissionDecision: "deny"` with a reason naming the holder (**Block**, default), `"ask"` (**Ask me**: Claude Code's permission prompt), or `additionalContext` warning it (**Warn**); **Off** skips the check. For CLIs whose hooks can't hand an edit to their own approval prompt (Codex rejects `"ask"` and then runs the tool; descriptor capability `lockAsk`), **Ask me** denies the edit, telling the agent to stop and wait, and Combwork shows a notification with **Allow**; Allow lets that agent edit that file until its claims are released and tells it to go ahead: at once if the agent is idle, else when its turn ends (Allow is often clicked while the blocked agent is still replying; the edit is then allowed again for the turn the go-ahead starts, and several files allowed in one turn get one go-ahead). The notification's **Allow** stays open after the blocked turn ends (the agent ends it within seconds to wait for the answer): until the user answers, the agent's edit of the file goes ahead anyway, the holder's claim ends, or the session ends or moves (HI-2386); an older notification's Allow answers no newer ask of the same file (HI-2320). An ask and an Allow are about the holder's claim they named (each claim has an id, the same while one holder keeps the file; every claim and release goes through one place): when that claim ends unanswered (released, or taken over by an allowed agent's edit or once it expired), the waiting agent is told, once its turn has ended (a go-ahead like Allow's, allowing nothing), that the other agent has finished with the file and to try again, and an Allow not yet acted on goes the same way; the retry claims the file, or asks again about whoever has claimed it since. An Allow pressed for a claim that is no longer the file's answers nothing, and its notification says it no longer applies. The go-ahead is a delivery (#649: a control notice for that launch), offered as every line of Combwork's is: only while the user isn't writing in that terminal (**Pause after you type**), checked again until Enter, so it is never added to or sends their input; put off, it goes when the pause ends, or at the end of the turn the user's own prompt started (the file stays allowed for it). An edit of the file that goes ahead meanwhile (in the same turn, or after the holder finished) needs no go-ahead, and an interrupt drops it, even one that comes while the go-ahead is being typed (it stops before Enter). A claim is released when the holder's turn ends (`Stop`), when its session ends, or 15 minutes after its last edit. Claims, approvals and questions are numbered as they happen, and a turn's end releases only those from before it arrived, so a late `Stop` never clears what the next turn has claimed (an agent's hooks are handled in order, but `PreToolUse` is answered at once). Denials return at once, so agents can't deadlock; if Combwork doesn't answer, the edit goes ahead. Only these tools are covered (and Codex's `apply_patch` run as a shell command, which Codex applies as an edit: its files are read from the patch's own headers, HI-2408): other shell commands (`Set-Content`, `sed`, redirection…), formatters and Claude Code's own config writes (`~/.claude.json`) are not — concurrency there is the developer's responsibility. Agents in different worktrees never collide (different paths). Claimed files are shown on the agent's tab and pane header (lock icon with a count; the list on hover).

**Status line** (Claude Code): `launch/settings.json` also sets Claude Code's `statusLine` to the same `curl.exe` command, posting to `/hook?statusline`. The hook server answers 204 with no body, so Claude Code shows no status line in the terminal. From the JSON Combwork takes the session's effort (`effort.level`), model name and cost (`cost.total_cost_usd`) into the live state, and the plan limits (`rate_limits.five_hour` / `seven_day`: `used_percentage`, `resets_at`) into `config.json` (`planUsage`, account-wide, last report wins). Claude Code reports with every status-line update, many times a minute while agents work, so the latest report is kept in memory and written only when a shown value changes (a whole percentage or a reset time), at most once a minute, and on quit. Warnings at 80% and 95% are shown once per limit per reset period (`planWarnings`; a reset time within 30 minutes of the stored one counts as the same period). Combwork never calls Anthropic's usage API or reads credentials itself.

### 6.4 Codex

Tested with Codex 0.159 and 0.160. Combwork never edits Codex's own `config.toml`; everything is passed as `-c key=value` overrides (TOML values):

```
codex [resume <id>] --no-daemon          # options must follow "resume <id>"
      -c hooks.<Event>=[…] -c hooks.state={…trusted hashes…}
      -c tui.terminal_title=["activity","project-name"]   # keeps "Action Required" in the title (Status)
      [-m <model>] [-c model_reasoning_effort=<e>] <preset flags (§5)>
      -c developer_instructions="<the combwork MCP server's instructions>"
      -c mcp_servers.<name>={…}          # each enabled workspace server
      -c mcp_servers.<other>.enabled=false   # the user's and the project's own servers
      [extra args]
```

- **Hooks**: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, Stop, Interrupt, PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionEnd, each a command hook. Codex runs hook commands through PowerShell on Windows, so the command is `curl.exe -s -m 5 -X POST -H "@<auth file>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary "@-" "<url>"` (the launch's auth file, #345, so the `-c` arguments, which process listings show, carry no token). Codex only runs hooks it trusts: Combwork passes the trust records in one `hooks.state` table, keyed by `<session-flags config path>:<event label>:0:0` with `sha256:` of the hook's canonical JSON. For each new Codex version Combwork checks its hashes against Codex's own (the app server's `hooks/list`) once, and uses Codex's if they differ.
- **Ready**: Codex fires SessionStart only with the first prompt, so Combwork marks the agent ready when Codex's prompt appears in the terminal, and records the session (its ID and rollout path) at the first hook.
- **Status**: who is asked comes from Codex's terminal title, not its hooks. Codex sends PermissionRequest before anyone answers it, in every preset with the same payload: in **Approve for me** its auto-reviewer (a Guardian sub-session that sends no hooks) answers it, allowing it (PostToolUse follows) or denying it (nothing follows). It titles its terminal `[ ! ] Action Required | <project>` (blinking with `[ . ]`) exactly while a person must act: an approval prompt, or a question. So from Codex 0.160.0 (`titleAttention()`; Combwork pins the title's items so a user's `[tui].terminal_title` can't hide it) the title saying so makes the agent **waiting** (a permission request or `request_user_input`, which stops Codex), or gives it a **pending question** (`request_user_input_async`, which returns at once: Codex works on, and the answer comes later as a prompt). The hooks only say what is asked: PermissionRequest is the status message ("Codex asks to run …"), or, in **Approve for me**, an action under automatic review (`LiveSessionState.review`) while the reviewer considers it: the status stays **Working…** with a small shield beside it in the agent's and the Assistant's headers (`ReviewMark`), whose tooltip names the reviewer and what is asked; the request is never the status, a label elsewhere or a notification, and the Agent API reports it as `reviewing`. It goes when the next tool starts or ends, a prompt comes, the turn ends or is interrupted, the session ends, or a person is asked after all (no review is shown over a wait). The command in a request is its first line, cut at 120 characters with an ellipsis. The title is one for everything asked, so Combwork keeps what is open: each ask from its hook until it is resolved (its own tool call ends, the turn ends or is interrupted, or the title goes back). The title coming on is about what is open (the latest prompt is waited on, the latest question shows beside it), else about something the hooks didn't say (waiting, with no message). A permission request in Approve for me is never open: the reviewer decides it (one it can't decide fails; one it handed to you would still be told, unnamed), so a finished review can't be taken for a later title. While the title is already on, an ask is judged by what it is: a reviewed request stays the reviewer's (the agent works on, a question stays pending, no alert); anything else is put to you at once, as a new need. A wait ends when the tool call it is about ends (its PostToolUse names the same tool and command as the request); another call ending beside it doesn't, and with two prompts up the wait moves on to the other. The title going back ends the wait and the question. A title change is applied in order with the hooks: Combwork answers hooks at once and handles them one at a time, so a change waits for the hooks that came before it (a slow first hook, recording the session, could otherwise let the title land before that turn's prompt and its request, and the prompt be told twice). Older versions go by the hooks: PermissionRequest is **waiting** except in Approve for me (the preset's `reviewed`), a question waits or is pending, and the next prompt answers a pending one. Interrupt (Esc) means **ready** and releases the agent's file locks. File locks use PreToolUse with `apply_patch` (paths from the patch; in code mode too), and with a shell command that runs it (HI-2408: Codex 0.166 sends that as `Bash`, the command in `tool_input.command`, and no PostToolUse): only the form Codex applies as an edit itself, the whole command one `apply_patch` or `applypatch` with the patch as a heredoc (`<<'EOF'`, the delimiter quoted or not), after an optional `cd <dir> &&` that the paths are then relative to (`shellPatchPaths`). With a command before or after it, or the patch as an argument, Codex runs it in the shell like any other command (a PostToolUse follows), so it claims nothing; recorded in `tests/fixtures/pretooluse-codex-0.166.0-shell-patch.json`.
- **Live preset changes** go through Codex's `/permissions` menu: Combwork clears the input, types `/permissions`, then the number its menu shows beside the preset's **label** (Read Only, Ask for approval, Approve for me, Full Access), read from Codex's screen as rendered (#396: Codex 0.161 reordered the menu from 0.160's Read Only, Ask, Approve, Full Access to Ask, Approve, Full Access, Read Only, so a fixed number picked the wrong preset; the arrow keys wrap around, so counting presses did too). A key step can be such a pick (`KeyStep` `pick`, `main/keySteps.ts`; the label match in `providers/codex/permissionsMenu.ts`): it waits up to 4 seconds for the menu, and a label that never shows fails clearly (the menu closed with Escape, nothing chosen: "Combwork couldn't find …") rather than choosing another preset. Codex sessions keep a rendered screen for it. Each key goes in only while the session is still the one being switched, isn't asking the user anything and isn't busy (working, or Codex's screen showing it holding what was typed: "tab to queue message" under its input, `adapter.busyScreen`); busy, it waits, at most 30 seconds. Otherwise typing stops there (`KeysStopped`): nothing more goes in, the badge goes back, the mode stays as it was, and Combwork says why ("…, as its session ended"). The Enter after `/permissions` goes in again while Codex's input still holds the command once it is free (#363, as for the sandbox setup below). The badge shows "Switching to X…" until Codex confirms, from its "Permission selection requested: X" line or the rollout's `thread_settings_applied`, within 12 seconds; otherwise it reverts and says so.
- **Models** come from Codex itself (`codex debug models`: the listed models, in Codex's order, with each one's reasoning levels and default) when the CLI is found, so new models appear without a Combwork update (§10, models and capabilities); `model_reasoning_effort` in its config.toml is the default effort for every model when set.
- **Live details** (model, effort, context, plan limits, preset, Plan mode) come from the tail of the rollout file (`token_count` events and `thread_settings_applied`), read as it grows.
- **Sandbox**: on Windows Codex needs its sandbox set up once (`windows.sandbox` in its config); without it every command asks for approval. Provider Setup runs Codex read-only in a scratch folder and brings up Codex's own setup prompt (default or non-admin sandbox): with no sandbox yet, by choosing "Ask for approval" in `/permissions` (by its label, as live changes do; if Codex doesn't show it, a warning says so and the terminal stays open for the user); with the non-admin sandbox on (`unelevated`), by typing `/setup-default-sandbox`, which only exists then. The keys go in once Codex has loaded (`CommandSpec.readyPattern`, read from the screen its output draws, `KeyGate`: its session header names the folder where it said "loading", which Codex writes over in place; its prompt is drawn while it is still loading) and it has shown no sign of being busy for a second: no spinner in its window title (`CommandSpec.busyTitle`), and no "tab to queue message" on the last line it draws, under its input (`CommandSpec.busyScreen`, `codexHoldsInput()`; the same words in the conversation don't count), which can show before the title's spinner on a loaded machine (#363). Codex is briefly busy once it has loaded. Each key waits again until it has been free for half a second, asked just before it goes in; still busy after 30 seconds (the 30-second start too, for a Codex never seen loaded), or closed, typing stops there with a warning to finish in the terminal. The Enter that runs a command is then checked against Codex's screen (`KeyStep.heldOn`, `inputHolds()`): if, once Codex is free, has had a second to draw what it did, and is still free, its input (the last line it marks with "›") still holds just the command, unrun, Enter goes in again, at most twice more. A command Codex took (run, or queued by Codex to run when it is free) leaves its input, so it is never sent twice, and nothing is sent again on a guess (an Enter in an open menu would choose from it). Provider Setup explains the two choices in Combwork's terms (`ReadinessIssue.detail`), and with the non-admin sandbox shows an info item with **Upgrade** (the same task). Codex stays open after its setup, so the task ends itself once Codex's config names a new sandbox (`CommandSpec.done`); Provider Setup then shows that the task succeeded (the issue it was started for is gone) instead of the terminal.
- **The Microsoft Store's PowerShell 7** (#585, Darren's decision: options 1 and 3; evidence on #499 with Codex 0.162.1): Codex's Windows sandbox can't start the Store's `pwsh` while any other process of that package runs on the machine (`CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 5`), so a Codex agent's commands fail whenever a PowerShell 7 is open anywhere. With the sandbox set up and the Store's `pwsh` the first on PATH (its app execution alias in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps`, a reparse point only `lstat` sees, or the package's folder; `providers/codex/storePwsh.ts`), Codex's readiness has a **warning** (`store-pwsh`), its label short (*PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store is installed*: Provider Setup's badge and the window's banner, #1404) with what goes wrong under it, that names the symptom and suggests the installer's PowerShell 7, in the order that works (#1512): uninstall the Store one first (`Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell | Remove-AppxPackage`, or Settings → Apps), since winget takes it for the same app and installs nothing while it is there; then `winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget --installer-type wix`; then restart Combwork and its Codex agents (their PATH is read at start). Combwork never changes the shell agents get (no PATH without the alias: option 2 was declined). The `codex-storepwsh` e2e suite keeps checking the refusal itself, and the upstream report is a comment on openai/codex#35871 (the Store pwsh with the elevated sandbox), adding the unelevated one's trigger: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35871#issuecomment-6277580003.
- **Resume**: `codex resume <id>` restores a rollout only at its original path, so Combwork keeps that path in `sessions.json` and restores a backup there when Codex's copy is gone.
- `.git` is read-only in Codex's workspace-write sandbox (committing asks for approval).
- **A stray `.codex` folder** (#509): Codex treats a project's `.codex` as its own and protects it before every sandboxed command; one an agent wrote scratch into (made by the sandbox's own user) made that protection fail ("deny ACE failed on …\.codex"), so every Codex agent's commands in the project failed ("setup refresh had errors") until it was deleted. With Codex turned on, Combwork warns (a toast, once while the folder stays so) when a folder an agent works in has a `.codex` holding anything that isn't Codex's configuration: `config.toml`, custom agents (`agents/*.toml`), `rules`, `prompts`, `skills`, and what those TOML files name in a path field (a key ending in `file`, `path` or `dir`, such as `model_instructions_file` or a skill's `path`: the file and the folders holding it; other text, such as a profile's name, names nothing) (`strayCodexEntries`); checked as each agent starts (any provider) and at each turn's end (`folderWarning` in the adapter). Combwork's session contract tells agents to keep scratch, probes and logs in a temp folder, never in or beside a project or worktree, nor in its `.codex`, `.claude` or `.agents`.

---

### 6.5 Assistant

- **What it is.** Each open workspace has one Assistant, its overseer, shown in a panel on the right of the window (Ctrl+Alt+I, the command palette, or clicking the strip it folds into when hidden: a narrow bar down the right edge with a chevron, "Assistant" written downwards and a status dot while it runs; each workspace remembers whether its panel is open and how wide it is, 430 px by default). It answers questions about any project, reports what the agents are doing, plans and reviews, and (as far as **Control** allows, below) runs the agents for the user: adds them, changes their settings, starts, stops and briefs them, and creates projects. It never edits project files itself.
- **How it runs.** It is a session like an agent's (terminal, hooks, status, usage, transcript backups, quit/close/switch handling, notifications), hosted by `<Workspace>/.combwork/assistant`, a home Combwork never lists as a project, with one agent (`assistant`). It **works in the workspace folder**, so it can read every project, and gets the combwork MCP server scoped to the workspace (no project of its own) and the workspace's skills meant for it (`metadata.audience` `assistant` or `all`, §7.1: `coordinate-agents`, `run-lanes`, `split-work`, `handover`, `pick-up`, `workspace-note` as Combwork ships them), not the project agents' skills, nor the workspace's other MCP servers but those it has on (HI-1472, §7.2). Reading a skill grants nothing: its tools and Control decide what it can do. Quit and close dialogs call it "Assistant".
- **What it is told.** Combwork's session contract for the Assistant (`combworkInstructions(…, 'assistant')`, the combwork MCP server's instructions: use the Combwork tools for Combwork's things, and which skills cover its workflows), then at launch its role (`assistantInstructions`): the workspace and its projects at launch, what Control lets it do and the boundaries it keeps whatever else it reads (`controlRules`), that nothing wakes it but the user and its own tool calls, that its mode never changes what it may do and that it may suggest another mode, and its mode: Claude Code through `--append-system-prompt-file` (a file in its launch folder), Codex through `developer_instructions`. How to run agents and cards well (briefs, starting cards, waiting, handing over, stalled cards) is the `coordinate-agents` skill's, not its prompt's; how to run a team's lanes (planned by files, complete builder and reviewer briefs, a confirmed watch on each lane's last card, a board sweep on each wake, changing a running lane, checking agents' claims against git and the board) is the `run-lanes` skill's (#402, from the coordinator playbook). Its habits fit the setup (Darren's decision on #402): `coordinate-agents` brings in `run-lanes` for three or more agents in a project, builder and reviewer pairs or agents in worktrees, and with one or two agents in the project folder stays light, suggesting more structure in one line at most; the setup changes how it works, never what the user can do. The Coordinator mode puts first a watch on running work (never "they'll tell you") and checking what agents report. The rules on what it may do come from Combwork and replace anything a mode says; Combwork's four modes carry no procedure or permissions. Its Combwork tools (below) are pre-approved where the provider allows it, only those its Control allows (Claude Code `--allowedTools`, Copilot `--allow-tool=combwork(<tool>)`, Codex a per-tool `tools.<tool>.approval_mode="approve"` on the combwork server, #1174, Codex 0.163.0), so writing shared notes still asks: in Codex's Approve for me (the Assistant's default there), its reviewer decides instead, as Claude Code's Auto does.
- **Control** (Settings → Assistant → Control, for every workspace; default **Control agents and create projects**): **Look and advise** (it reads and suggests; you act; it lists lanes too, #500: `cw_lane` is trusted at every level, its description says that only `list` works there, and the Agent API refuses starting, joining and ending one below Control agents), **Control agents** (also adds agents, changes their settings, starts and stops them, gives idle ones tasks, turns projects on, and releases a slot once the user agrees: #1561's `cw_release_slot`, whose `list` works at every level), **Control agents and create projects**. It never removes agents, discards worktrees or deletes projects. Changing it marks a running Assistant for restart.
- **Combwork's settings** (#186). Every setting is described once, in the **settings catalog** (`src/shared/settingsCatalog.ts`): its id (`<section>.<key>`, `<provider>.<key>`, `project.<key>`), scope (app, provider, workspace, project), control and values, default, description, tip, "when it helps", place in Settings, user guide heading, whether a change waits for a restart (agents' sessions, or the Assistant), and whether it is **sensitive**. Settings and Project Settings draw their rows from it (the views add only the custom controls, by id), and the Assistant's tools read it, so the two never drift; a unit test fails when Combwork's settings or a project's config gain a field it doesn't describe. The Assistant reads and explains settings at every Control level (`cw_list_settings`, `cw_read_setting`; `GET /v1/settings`). It changes one (`cw_update_setting`; `PATCH /v1/settings/{id}`) only with **Settings → Assistant → Control → Change settings** on (`assistant.changeSettings`, off by default, independent of the level; the tool is offered only then, and turning it on marks a running Assistant for restart, while turning it off refuses at once), when the user asked or agreed (its rules and the `tune-settings` skill: suggest first, one line). The value is checked as Settings checks it and set as Settings sets it (`config.updateSettings`, or the project's config under its lock). **Sensitive settings are read-only to it**, enforced in the API: permission modes and the dangerous-mode switch, the Agent API, what Combwork runs (CLI paths, extra arguments, a project's setup command, background sessions, pre-release updates), where agents and it may attach card files from (Card attachments: more folders, Combwork's and a workspace's, HI-2480), where agents and it write their temporary files (Agents' temp folder, Combwork's and a workspace's, HI-2496) and its own Settings → Assistant (Control, Change settings, the typing pause, its provider, working mode and launch settings); the Assistant's own provider settings are an entry each (`assistant.<provider>.model`, `.effort`, `.permissionMode`, `.extraArgs`, `.use200kContext`, drawn together as "With <provider>"), readable like the rest. Tables are set whole as JSON: the board's column colours (an object of column → colour, merged), a provider's prices and its fallback model and effort lists (replaced through the same setters as Settings; null puts back Combwork's, for prices the shipped models removed from the table too, as Reset to defaults does). An effort level must be one the effort picker offers for the model that would run (or the default). Keybindings are read-only for now; agent settings stay with `cw_update_agent`. The permission and the value it replaces are checked again at the moment of the change, under the project's lock for a project's setting: a change waiting behind the user's own write is refused if Change settings was turned off meanwhile, or if the Assistant session that asked for it has ended (its launch's token isn't the current one: a restart doesn't carry out the old session's changes). A table's change is listed and answered by the entries that changed ("doing: #3b82f6 → doing: #ff0000"). Each change is listed with old → new and an **Undo** button (§16.14), through `assistant:undo`. Undo checks the value again at the write, under the project's lock for a project's setting; it skips a value changed since and preserves the newer edit. A price table's removed models are checked separately: those changed since are kept while unchanged price overrides can still go back.
- **Messages for a busy agent** (#530). `cw_prompt_agent` refuses an agent that is working, starting, waiting on background tasks or for the user, or watching, which in a running card loop is nearly always: on 10 Oct the user pasted about ten of the Assistant's messages into agents' panes, and cards waited hours for them (#521). `cw_message_agent` (`POST …/agents/{agent}/message`, Control agents) leaves the agent a message instead (`main/agentMessages.ts`), a **delivery** (#647, below) of kind `rebrief`, which the agent reads with `cw_inbox` (#650: never typed in). Its **doorbell** is typed at once when the agent is idle or **watching** (a watching agent is idle, so it is woken by it; its watch carries on, since typing never ends one, and the line says so: `[CW] New in your inbox: 1 message (m4). Call cw_inbox to read it, act on it, then ack it. (Your watch is still on, waiting for #506 → Review: do what this asks, then end your turn, and Combwork wakes you when it changes.)`). A busy agent is told at its next tool call or before its turn ends (Notices and the doorbell, below); else it waits for its next line, whichever comes first: **a line with a wake** (#649: a watch's or a loop's wake is a delivery too, and the delivery service names whatever waits for the agent in one doorbell, `[CW] New in your inbox: 1 message and 1 card event (#2) (m5, m6). …`, whose inbox lists the message first, so the agent has it before it acts on the wake; a delivery cancelled, refused or added while that line is typed stops it, and it is offered again with what waits then), or a line of its own, as a wake is: only while it is idle, nobody types there (Pause after you type) and no earlier line waits to be taken. Tried on its status changes and every 5 s. Several waiting go in one line (`[CW] New in your inbox: 2 messages (m4, m5). …`). One the agent reads first (`cw_inbox`, mid-turn) is received and never offered after. **Each keeps its sender's permission**: the Assistant's `assistantChange` guard (its Control level, its session) is asked before its doorbell is typed, before each piece and Enter, and again as the agent reads its inbox: one whose sender may no longer send it (Control turned down, its session ended) is refused, never given, however long it waited. **A doorbell is never taken back** (#652): once typed it names ids, never what they say, so #376's Enter again (`confirmTaken`) submits it even when what it names has ended meanwhile, and the agent's `cw_inbox` gives nothing of that. (Before #650 a line carried the message's text, and Combwork cleared such a line with Ctrl+U, `clearTyped`, and typed nothing more until a draft typed over it was submitted; #652 retired that.) **Tied to a card round** (#652, from #699's history: the Assistant's re-brief for a round's finding reached its builder a second after the card passed, and the builder reopened the passed card to apply it). `card` ties a message to that card's round under way (its failed reviews plus one: the fix after a failed review is the next round; refused unless the card is in Doing or Review). Once the card has moved on (passed, done or archived, out of Doing and Review, or another review failed) the message is **stale**: ended with why (`#699 passed review`, `#699 is in round 7 now`), never offered, and not given by `cw_inbox` even when its doorbell has already rung, checked under the delivery lock as it is offered or read (judged against the board right before the plan, and read again if the board changed meanwhile; if it keeps changing, the message is held back unread, never judged on an outdated read), and as the board changes; the Assistant's activity list records it. The reply names the round (`Gave HB6 a message (m12) for #699 round 6`).
