At most 5 waiting per agent (`MAX_QUEUED`, counted as one is made) of at most 4000 characters (`MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS`); saved, so they survive the agent's stops and Combwork's restarts (the Assistant's are then refused, since the launch that left them has ended). The call's reply says what became of that message by the time it returns, with its id: told (its doorbell typed), queued, or (a `409`) cancelled meanwhile, refused, expired or stale, never told when it wasn't. The agent shows them (`inbox`): its pane header has **✉ n unread** (each one's id, who from, its state and the start of it in the tooltip; a click offers **Cancel the Message(s)** for those not read yet (#650: until the agent reads one, it can still be taken back), `session:cancelMessages`), and `cw_agent_activity` has `inbox` (unread, overdue, and the latest deliveries with their states and times), so the Assistant sees whether it was received and acked. `cancel: true` cancels them. `cw_prompt_agent`'s refusals name the tool. A message is for what the agent already works on (a re-brief, the user's answer, a lane addition); a new task is still `cw_prompt_agent` or `cw_start_task`.
- **Deliveries and the inbox** (#647, the messaging redesign's first card: `plans/2026-10-12-messaging-redesign.md` §3.1, decisions on #645 and #649). Everything Combwork has for an agent to read is a **delivery**: a record (`shared/deliveries.ts`) with a short id unique in its project (`m12`), its target (agent and conversation), kind (task, re-brief, card event, the user's answer, handover, control), sender, card, created and expiry times, body and state, saved in the workspace's database (`.combwork/combwork.db`, #1018: a row each, under its project's id, or `assistant` for the Assistant's; a project's `.combwork/deliveries.json` from before is moved in the first time and kept as `deliveries.json.imported-<time>`), each change one transaction, and restored when Combwork starts (`main/deliveries.ts`). **States**: queued → offered → received → acked, or cancelled (by whom), refused (its sender may no longer send it), expired (not received within 24 hours, `DELIVERY_EXPIRY_HOURS`, or its agent is in another conversation now, or the launch it was for has ended), stale (#652: tied to a card round, and that card has moved on) and uncertain. **Received is automatic, acked is explicit** (#645): received means **read through `cw_inbox`**, the only receipt (#650: the line typed is the doorbell, which names it by id, never its text, so its CLI taking that line is no receipt; #649's `receivedVia: 'typed'`, when the line carried the whole text, is still read back from saved records). A card event or a control notice is done once received; a message, a task, a handover or the user's answer waits for the agent's ack (`cw_inbox` with `ack`), once it has read it: an id alone, as a doorbell names it, acks nothing (it is `unread` in the ack's reply, unchanged, and its source isn't told it was received). One of those not acked 30 minutes after it was made (`OVERDUE_MINUTES`) is **overdue**: shown in the agent's pane (**✉ 1 overdue**, in the warning colour) and in its activity, so a message that went nowhere is a named state, not a mystery. **One scheduler offers them**: the delivery service alone, which types the doorbell for an idle agent (#650, Notices and the doorbell, below), saved as offered before the first key. A doorbell its CLI took whose agent is idle again without having read it (the Stop drain asked it first) **rings once more**, never a third time; it then stays offered, unread in the pane. **Uncertain** (#649): one offered when Combwork stopped, or when its agent's launch ended (or another began) before it was read, may not have reached the agent: it is offered once more, its doorbell saying so (`[CW] New in your inbox: 1 card event (#7) (m2). Call cw_inbox to read it. (m2 again: Combwork restarted while offering it, so it may repeat.)`), and stays uncertain (shown, cancellable, fetchable) if that one isn't received either; agents tell a repeat by its ids. **One transaction at a time, saved before anyone sees it**: each host's changes are checked and planned on a copy, saved by one atomic write (a temp file, then a rename), and only then published (`transact`, under the host's lock), so a read or the pane never sees a change that isn't on disk, and a save that fails changes nothing, on disk or in memory, and fails the call (`NotSaved`); a delivery made, offered, fetched or acked is on disk before the call says so or the line's first key is typed. **An operation takes effect at its save**: its checks (its sender's permission, its expiry, the agent's conversation) are made inside the lock as it is planned, with no check after the save: a permission change that lands while it is saved applies to the next operation, not this one (the fetch was decided before it). **A typed line is checked at each write**: the writer checks its offer (`offerHolds`: still offered by it, its sender's permission, its expiry, the agent's launch and conversation, and whether its producer still wants it) before each piece and Enter; one that no longer holds gets no Enter, and each delivery in it is recorded as what is true (refused, expired, cancelled, stale, or put back to wait and offered again). Once typed, the doorbell isn't checked again before its Enter again (#652): what it names is checked as the agent reads it, and one that ended meanwhile is recorded so when Combwork next looks (its status, the 5 s tick, the read). One can be **cancelled** until the agent reads it (#650): while it waits, while its doorbell is typed (which then gets no Enter), and after; read, it is the agent's. Taken is counted from the CLI's prompts just before the line's own Enter (the writer's last check, after its offer was saved), so a prompt of the user's submitted while that save was slow is never taken for the line. **Permission is worked out again at every step** from the sender saved with it and the settings now (never a token or a closure): the Assistant's needs Control agents and the launch that sent it still running, so **a waiting message (or task) from an Assistant launch that has ended is refused, and shown** (#645) in the agent's activity and the Assistant's activity list (`A message for B1 (m3) was refused`). A delivery for a known conversation goes to that conversation only. Waiting ones survive the agent's stops and Combwork's restarts; a card's events coalesce into one inbox item (`#607: 3 changes, read the card`). **`cw_inbox`** (agents and the Assistant; `POST /v1/inbox`): lists the caller's unread deliveries, oldest first, each with its ids, sender and card, marking them received, and the ids received before and not acked; `ack` takes ids, and one that isn't the caller's is unknown, like one that doesn't exist; `ack` with `read: true` (#1531, opt-in, for an agent with more in its inbox as it acks) acks, then reads, in one call, what it reads received, never acked: nothing is acked by being read. Both check what is unread as an offer would, as they plan (its sender's permission, its expiry, the agent's conversation, and its source's say, #649: made again from things as they are now; an offered one keeps the version it was offered as while that still holds, and one that no longer does is made again rather than never given, since its doorbell carried no text (#650; a receipt covers exactly the version read), so a wake telling a reply the user no longer lets be told, a watch that has ended, a loop wake or a decision line that is no longer that agent's is cancelled, and a delivery its producer no longer holds is neither listed nor acked): one that may no longer be delivered is refused, expired or cancelled, never listed or acked; one already received can still be acked. The Agent API gives each delivery's state and times (`GET …/agents/{agent}/deliveries`, and the activity's `inbox`). Bounded: 500 live per project, ended ones (and card events and control notices once received) kept 50 per agent for a week, received ones never acked expire after a week; the file within a 4 MB budget (counted as written, UTF-8, with room for each live one to reach its end), while Combwork reads back up to 8 MB, so a file it wrote is never set aside as too big: a delivery that doesn't fit after the oldest ended ones make room is refused when made. A damaged file is set aside, never overwritten; saved entries that aren't deliveries are kept aside in the file (or moved to a file of their own when they don't fit).
- **Every way into an agent is a delivery** (#649, Messaging 3). Each producer makes a delivery and neither types nor keeps a cursor of its own; the delivery service alone offers them, in one doorbell per offer (#650: the counts by kind, cards and ids; the agent reads each in its inbox, a message first, then each other as its producer made it, a wake's words as they were); a task or a handover in a line of its own. A producer registers itself as the delivery's **source**: it makes the line again just before each offer from things as they are then (none left to tell: cancelled), says whether it still holds before each key (a board or lane change since: made again at the next try), and is told when the delivery is received, which is when its cursor moves on, never on "typed". What an agent must be doing to be offered each is one check (`readiness.ts`), read from the turn ledger's facts (#648): its CLI running (or, for the carry-on after a sign-in, stopped by the refused sign-in), no turn running and none whose state is unknown (unknown is never idle), no compaction, nobody asked, and, for new work, no background tasks that will start it again (#726: an agent whose turn has ended while its own background tasks run, a sleep or a timer, takes a message or a card event as an idle one does: HB6 slept 40 minutes to renew a merge slot and heard of neither #720's comment nor a message until it woke; its CLI takes the line as a new turn, Claude Code's; Codex and Copilot, whose tasks start no turn, were idle then already; card-loop, work-on-card and merge-ready have agents wait with a watch's `limitMinutes`, never a timer); a watch is Combwork's policy on top: a watching agent takes a message or a wake (its watch carries on), not new work (a task, a handover, the user's answer, a lock's go-ahead). A line put off part-way (the user began typing, what it was made from changed), or held back by the typing pause, is tried again in a moment, and on every status change and a 5 s tick. **The producers**: `cw_message_agent` (re-briefs, above); **`cw_prompt_agent`** and **Start** on a running agent (`cw_start_task`, the board): a task, given now or not at all (refused as before for an agent that is busy, waiting or watching; never queued; a Start whose task isn't given puts the card back), its doorbell typed and the task read from the inbox; **an agent started with a task** (`cw_start_agent` or Add Agent with a prompt, Start on a stopped agent, `cw_prompt_agent` with `newConversation`): a task its launch carries, its doorbell as the launch's prompt, offered into that launch and received once the agent reads it (`cw_agent_activity` shows that task as the agent's current one, not the doorbell); **card, lane and agent watches**: a fired watch's line is handed over as a card event once its agent can take a line (made from the cards as they are then), and the watch stays (the agent shows watching) until that delivery is received, then ends, and what its line told is where the agent's next watch starts (`watches.json` keeps the delivery's id: read back, a watch follows it, ending if it was received, firing again if it ended without that); **loop wakes** (card events, the latest per agent and card, noted on the card once received); **decision wakes** (the user's answer, acked; told once received); **Assistant mode notices** (control, for that launch; the conversation records its mode once received); **a lock's go-ahead** (control, for that launch, once its turn has ended); **the carry-on after a sign-in** (control, given now); **handovers and Continue with** (the source's request to write one and the target's to read it, handover deliveries given now). **Outside the service**: the user's own typing and attachments, and the Agent API's explicit raw session input (privileged, as before); the CLI controls (Compact, the mode menu and Shift+Tab, the Plan toggle, exit keys) stay separate but take the same composer reservation as Combwork's lines: none goes in while a line is typed, nor a line while one runs.
- **Notices and the doorbell** (#650, the messaging redesign's channels: `plans/2026-10-12-messaging-redesign.md` §3.2, §3.4, §3.5; the spikes in `notes/2026-10-12-messaging-spike-*.md`). Combwork tells an agent it has something to read without typing into a busy one. **A checkpoint**: when one of the agent's own tool calls ends (PostToolUse, never a sub-agent's), the hook's reply carries a notice of what arrived since it was last told in that launch (`[CW] New in your inbox: 1 message and 1 card event (#607) (m4, m7). Call cw_inbox now to read them; act on them and ack them, then carry on.`). **The drain**: when its turn would end with something unread, the Stop hook's reply carries the turn on with a notice of everything unread that `cw_inbox` would give then (HI-1687: a notice, at a checkpoint or the drain, names only what passes the read's own gate as it stands, made again of nothing, so it creates or replaces no delivery; a loop wake nothing has made yet, or whose own card, lanes or project settings changed since it was made, isn't named, and the doorbell offers it once the agent is idle. A read hands a loop wake out unless its own card, lanes or project settings changed between its making and the hand-out, then makes it again, a few times at most; another card's change doesn't hold it back. A builder's step for a card that is Done with no lane running it any more is no longer due, and dropped) (`[CW] Before you finish: your inbox has 1 message (m4) you haven't read. Call cw_inbox, act on it and ack it before you end your turn.`), at most once a turn: not at a Stop after a continuation (`stop_hook_active`), nor in a turn Combwork carried on already. **Lanes unwatched (HI-2069)**: the Assistant's drain, with lanes running in the workspace that no watch of its covers (a lane watch on `all`, or on each by id), also carries the turn on with one line naming those lanes' builders (`[CW] Lanes are running (HB1, HB2) and nothing will wake you about them: watch the lanes (cw_wait_for_tasks with lanes ["all"], wake) before you finish.`), after its inbox's notice when it has one: the same drain, so once a turn and for every CLI the Assistant runs on. Only when its control level lets it control agents (HI-2187): at **Look and advise** the lanes are the user's to run, so no line is sent (a watch the Assistant starts on its own is still its choice). None with no lane running, for a project agent, with the stop continuation off, or with Settings → Advanced → *Lanes: remind the Assistant to watch them* (`cw.lanes.unwatchedNotice`) off. Builders' names are kept to letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 10; a name with nothing left (an emoji's) is counted among the rest (`HB2 and 2 more`, or `1 lane`), so no lane goes unsaid for its name. Whose turn a hook is, and whether it is stale, is the turn ledger's word: a hook that may carry a notice is answered in the launch's hook order, after the hooks before it, so a late hook of an earlier turn gets nothing and a prompt sent meanwhile waits behind it; the turn ledger counts that Stop as a continuation (#648), so the turn ends at the next one. **The doorbell**: for an idle agent, one short line of the same kind typed into it (`[CW] New in your inbox: 1 task (#12) (m9). Call cw_inbox to read it, act on it, then ack it.`): every line Combwork types for a delivery is one (a task, a handover, a wake, the user's decisions, a notice), with Enter again once if its CLI doesn't take it, never a third; taken but not read by the time the agent is idle again, it rings once more. **Not before its Combwork tools are there** (#865): a resumed Claude Code is ready at its SessionStart before its combwork server has connected, and a doorbell then was a turn that couldn't call `cw_inbox` (and said so in the conversation). A launch given Combwork's tools takes no line of Combwork's until its combwork server says the CLI has connected it (on `notifications/initialized`, or its first `tools/list`: `POST /v1/launch/connected` with the launch's own token), at most Settings → Advanced → *Combwork tools: wait to connect* (30 s) from when it first became ready, for a CLI whose server never starts; a message waits, and a task given meanwhile (given now or not at all) is held until then too (`deliverNow`'s `heldByTools`, `sessions.combworkToolsSettled`), not refused (round 3: refusing it failed the Assistant's task to an agent in the second after it became ready). Codex (0.163.0) and Copilot (1.0.98) connect their MCP servers as they start, before any prompt (Copilot even before its folder-trust question is answered; checked with a probe server whose initialize was held 8 s), and send `notifications/initialized`, so the same gate holds for them. **`cw_inbox` is the only receipt** (Deliveries, above). **No inbox** (Darren's decision on #650): an agent that can't read an inbox (a project agent while the Agent API or the built-in combwork server is off: `agentReadsInbox`; the Assistant always has its own) is given no delivery, and its bodies are never typed instead. Every automated or Assistant-originated delivery (messages, wakes, the user's decisions relayed, notices, a handover's steps, the carry-on) is refused with the reason its sender sees ("B1 has no inbox: turn on the Agent API"): when it is made, or, one already waiting when the Agent API was turned off, when it is next looked at. Only the user's own action from Combwork, a task they Start, is typed as their input, as their typing in its pane is: no delivery and no receipt. No new typed receipts; historical ones (`receivedVia: 'typed'`) still read back. It gets no notices. Each is **Combwork's own fixed wording** with counts by kind, card numbers and delivery ids (`shared/doorbell.ts`), **never a delivery's body, a sender's name or anything a person or an agent wrote**: bodies come only from `cw_inbox`, labelled with their sender, so a "the user says" quoted in a card or a message is data (#643). **Per CLI** (the adapter's `noticeReply`, beside `lockReply`; PreToolUse stays for locks, since its context reaches the model only after the tool ran, as PostToolUse's does): Claude Code (2.1.296) gets context at PostToolUse and Stop (a user-role reminder; Stop with context, not a block, which the user would see as "Stop hook error"); Codex (0.162.1) context at PostToolUse (a developer message, which is why the text is fixed) and a block at Stop (the reason goes on in the same turn as a user-role hook prompt); Copilot (1.0.95, checked offline against a stand-in model) top-level `additionalContext` at PostToolUse (added to the tool's result; the `hookSpecificOutput` form doesn't reach its model) and a block at Stop, whose reason comes back as a new prompt hook: Combwork takes that prompt as its own in the running turn (`drainIsPrompt`, the turn ledger's injected prompts), never a new prompt or turn. A notice is answered in the hook's reply, so a working agent is never typed into; a CLI that can't carry one on an event is never asked about it.
- **How it acts.** Through the Agent API with **its own token**: a new one each time it starts, in a per-workspace file under the profile (`assistant-api/`) that its combwork MCP server reads, so its launch settings don't change. When it stops, its token stops working and any question it was asking is answered no. Its session doesn't get the Agent API's token, and its Combwork tools ignore one inherited from the CLI. Asking to stop a busy agent stops only the run it asked about, and only if Control still allows it when the user answers. Busy is starting, working, waiting for the user or on background tasks; one only watching cards or agents is idle and stopped without asking (HI-1994). The question is closed whatever ends the wait: the user's answer, 270 s without one (`STOP_ASK_MS`, under the Combwork tools' 300 s reply limit; the reply says it timed out and was withdrawn, `408`), or the call going away (withdrawn); an answer after that is nothing. The API applies Control (not Settings → Agent API) to its calls and confines them to its workspace; with the Agent API off, the server still runs for it alone, and its combwork MCP server is always there. Its tools: `cw_list_providers`, `cw_agent_activity` (status, the task it was last given, its latest reply, this turn's tool calls, locked files, when the user last typed there), `cw_wait_for_agents` (which project agents have too: #416), and as Control allows `cw_activate_project`, `cw_add_agent`, `cw_update_agent`, `cw_start_agent`, `cw_stop_agent`, `cw_prompt_agent` (with `newConversation`, #437: the agent's conversation ends, kept in the Sessions tab, and it starts in a new one on the task, as Hand Over to… itself does but with no handover, through `sessions.newConversation` and the provider's adapter; the same refusals, and also while Combwork is typing into it; the Assistant's Control and session are checked again after the stop and just before the new launch spawns, so a request whose permission ended meanwhile starts nothing), `cw_hand_over` (Hand Over to…: the first agent writes a handover, Combwork waits until it exists, then starts the second on it; refused at once when project agents lack Combwork's tools or the user just typed in either), `cw_create_project`. Project agents don't get these (AGENT_API.md lists them). Adding an agent, changing its settings, starting and stopping it run `assistantChange`'s guard (Control and the Assistant's launch) at their boundary, not only on arrival (HI-2328): `addAgent`'s and `updateAgent`'s `check` with the write under project.json's lock, `sessions.start`'s `allowed` just before the spawn, and just before `sessions.stop`; turned down or ended meanwhile, nothing changes.
- **Its rules** (enforced by Combwork, and in its instructions): a first task goes on the CLI's command line, last and behind `--` (`claude … -- "<task>"`, `codex … -- "<task>"`, so extra arguments ending in a list option such as `--allowedTools a b` or Codex's `--image a.png` can't take it as one of their values, #523, Darren's decision; extra arguments never hold a bare `--` of their own, which would end the options early or be read as the task (Claude Code 2.1.296 runs on a second `--`): the connection dialog and the Agent API refuse one when saved ("Combwork passes the task after `--`; remove it from extra arguments"), a launch with one saved before refuses to start, before anything changes, naming its connection to fix in Settings → Accounts & Connections (HI-2140), and an option whose value is `--` is written `--option=--`; Combwork doesn't guess what a bare `--` meant; Copilot's `-i "<task>"` is an option, which ends a list already; through cmd.exe, below, it becomes one plain line); a task is typed into an agent only when it is idle (ready or finished), never while it works, starts or waits for the user, and never while the user may still be writing there: within **Pause after you type** (Settings → Assistant, default 15 seconds; **No pause** turns it off) of their last keystroke in its terminal, unless that keystroke was Enter and **Enter ends the pause** is on (the default). Combwork records the user's keystrokes per terminal, ignoring the terminal's own replies (focus, cursor and device reports, colour queries such as Codex's at start, ended by BEL or ST); stopping a working, waiting, starting or `background` agent (not one only watching, HI-1994) asks the user on a card at the top of the panel (or a notification with the panel hidden), and the call waits up to 270 s for the answer (`STOP_ASK_MS`), then withdraws the question, leaves the agent running and says it timed out (`408`), as it withdraws it at once when the call goes away; a worktree only if the user asked or agreed. There is no count of its changes per message (#1170, which removed the 30-change cap: undo, §16.14, protects the board, and Control limits what it may do at all); a new turn starts with each prompt it receives and groups its changes for undo. A batch of cards (`cw_update_tasks`) changes up to 100 cards in one call. Every change and refusal is listed in the panel (**Done by the Assistant**: the last three, or all) and in `combwork.log`.
- **The user's view never moves.** Its actions don't change the selected project, the page or the focus. Pages that weren't given a layout by hand follow their agents as usual. A new agent on the project on screen marks its page's button with a dot until that page is shown; on another project, that project opens on the new agent's page next time.
- **Trusting a folder.** When a CLI asks whether to trust a folder before it starts (Claude Code and Codex: "trust this folder"), the agent shows as **waiting** ("Asks whether to trust this folder") and notifies, instead of looking stuck in Starting, for any agent; the Assistant tells the user.
- **Journal** (#1031, design on #989; Darren's decisions there). The Assistant's memory across sessions: its own SQLite file `<Workspace>/.combwork/assistant/journal.db` (`main/journal.ts`, on `db.ts`, its own migrations, WAL, `auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL`; the home's `.gitignore` keeps it out of git), separate from the board. **Entries** (`entries`): time, kind (decision, plan, event, incident, insight, preference, moment, digest), project (none: the workspace), a one-line summary (at most 300 characters), optional detail (over 1 KB kept Brotli-compressed) and why, source (`assistant` or `combwork`), importance 0–3 (1 by default), `superseded_by` (cleared when the newer one is deleted), `digest_of` (a digest's period); **links** (card, commit, note, artifact, session, agent, project, entry) and **tags** in tables of their own, deleted with the entry. **Full-text search**: an FTS5 table, contentless (the text is only in `entries`; not `detail=column`, which leaves a contentless table's bm25 at nought), kept by triggers that read a compressed detail through `journal_text()`, a function each connection registers. **Recall**: newest first, or for words (each a prefix, any of them) best first by bm25 (summary weighted 3, why 1.5, detail 1) × (1 + importance/2) ÷ (1 + ln(1 + age in days/90)), ties by importance then newest; filters by time range, kinds, project, link, tag; superseded entries left out unless asked; at most 10 rows by default (50 at most), a line each; an entry's detail one at a time. **Settings** (workspace.json `journal`, Settings → Assistant → Journal, `JournalSettings.tsx`): on/off (off keeps the data: nothing is written and a call is refused at once with `409`; the tools leave the Assistant's list at its next session start, and come back the same way: Darren's decision on #1031), the scope (default decision, plan, event, incident, insight; a digest is always allowed; a kind outside it is refused saying which are allowed), retention of everyday entries (importance under 2, not digests; 90 days, 7 to 3650), and a size cap (50 MB, 5 to 10,000, or no limit: past it the oldest everyday entries go first, 200 at a time; important entries and digests are never pruned; freed pages go back to the file). The two numbers are `NumberField`s (HI-2345): a blank box keeps the saved number, and one out of range says so under it and saves nothing; `journal:set` refuses a number out of range or not whole ("Nothing was changed"), rather than raising it to the minimum and pruning to that, while reading workspace.json still makes what is there safe. Pruning runs after a write once an hour or when over the cap, after every change of an entry, and at once when a setting is tightened; past the cap it deletes the oldest everyday entry, one at a time, each in its own transaction, and measures the space used after each (pages in use, not a prediction: what an entry frees depends on its links, tags and index, which share pages), stopping as soon as it fits. A settings change is worked out in workspace.json's save from the settings as they are then, so two at once keep each other's fields. While a journal is being deleted nothing opens it (calls get `409`, facts and its size are skipped). A change of on/off or the scope tells the Assistant (an inbox notice). **Delete Journal…** (confirmed) closes it and moves its files to the Recycle Bin, and tells the Assistant. **Tools** (Assistant only, offered while it is on: `CW_JOURNAL` at its start, trusted like its read tools): `cw_journal_write`, `cw_journal_recall`, `cw_journal_entry`, `cw_journal_update` (correct, importance, supersede, add links and tags, or `delete`), through `/v1/journal` (other callers `403`). **Combwork's facts** (events by Combwork, tagged `combwork`, written only while it is on and events are in its scope): a lane started, ended (with its merge commit, importance 2) or abandoned; a card moved into Done (merged); Combwork closing unexpectedly (importance 2). **Builds** (#1534, #1062; deferred from #1031): each successful build of Combwork itself, by `npm run dist` or `npm run release` (`scripts/buildFact.mjs`; a failed build exits first, and dist's counts only with its `build-info.json`, written once its code is certain), is a fact: its kind (beta, baseline, rc, release: `--kind`, else from the version, a dist build of a release version being its candidate), version, commit (linked), branch, installer and time; importance 2 for a baseline or a release. Sent through the Agent API (`POST /v1/builds`, the session's `CW_API_URL` and token) while Combwork answers; otherwise left as a marker, `<workspace>/.combwork/builds/<time>.json` (written whole, a temp file renamed), the workspace being `CW_WORKSPACE` or the nearest above the main checkout, which Combwork records once as the workspace opens and removes whatever became of it. Off with Settings → Advanced → `cw.journal.builds` (on): nothing is written, and markers are dropped, so switching it on never brings back old builds. Local only, never sent anywhere. How the Assistant uses it (its guidance, the start-of-session recall, digests) is #1032. **The journal browser** (#1033; Darren's decision on #989: Combwork's own, under the Assistant view, no external SQLite tool; `JournalView.tsx`): the Assistant view's **Journal** section, **Timeline** (every entry) and **Weekly Digests** (kind digest only), and the command **Show Assistant Journal** (`view.assistantJournal`). The timeline is newest first (by time, never ranked), grouped by day (Today, Yesterday, then the day's name), a row each: time, the kind's codicon (shape, not colour alone), the one-line summary, a star for importance 2 or more, Superseded (struck through), a digest's period, the project, who wrote it (the Assistant's mark, or Combwork's), and its card links as the board's chips (`TaskChip`: the card's column colour, a click opens it; three, then +n). 100 rows at a time with **Show More**, and how many match. **Search** (FTS5) needs every word, each a prefix (unlike recall's any word, so Forget deletes only what plainly matches); **filters**: kind, project (or the workspace's own entries, no project), source (Combwork or the Assistant), From and To days (local days). An entry opens beside the timeline (under it in a narrow window): its summary, when (and when edited), project, writer, importance, a digest's period, what it supersedes or is superseded by (links that open them), detail (Markdown, sanitised), why, links (cards as chips, entries as links, the rest as their type and ref) and tags. **Edit**: summary, kind (the scope's kinds, digest, and its own: `updateEntry` refuses a kind outside the scope, as a write does), importance, detail, why; only what changed is sent. **Delete…** asks, naming it. **Forget These…** (only with a search or filter set; the whole journal is Settings' Delete Journal…) asks main what the search matches now (`journal:forgetPreview`: a count and a token, a hash of exactly that set's ids), asks with that count ("Forget everything about “X”?" for a search), then `journal:forget` deletes in one transaction only while the filter still matches exactly that set; an entry written, edited into or out of the match, or deleted meanwhile, and nothing goes and a notice says how many match now, to check and ask again (#1033 round 2). Forget is off while a new search or filter's rows are still being read (the previous rows dimmed, `aria-busy`), and **Show More** adds rows only to the search they were asked for. Deleted entries are gone for good (not the Recycle Bin), their links, tags and index rows with them, the space given back. The **footer** says the size, entries, the retention and the cap, with **Journal Settings** (Settings → Assistant). **Off**, a note says so with **Turn On**; reading, editing and deleting still work (the user's data; only the Assistant's and Combwork's writes stop). Reading never makes a journal that isn't there. Every write, change, delete, prune and Forget is told to the window showing that workspace (`journal-changed`), whose browser reads again, keeping as many rows as it showed. Keyboard: Up, Down, Home and End along the rows (buttons named "kind, when: summary"; the open one `aria-current`), Enter opens, Escape closes the entry, Ctrl+F the search, Down from the search to the first row. Escape on the open row also closes it. The sidebar's section rows (Conversations, Timeline, Weekly Digests, Attachments) are tab stops (Enter or Space), the one shown `aria-current`. IPC: `journal:browse`, `journal:projects`, `journal:entry`, `journal:edit`, `journal:deleteEntry`, `journal:forgetPreview`, `journal:forget`, on the window's workspace.
- **How the Assistant uses its journal** (#1032, #989's "How the Assistant knows"). While the journal is on:
  - **The state view** (`main/startView.ts` gathers, `shared/startView.ts` writes): Combwork answers the Assistant's SessionStart, which comes at a start, a resume, a `/clear` and after every compaction (source `compact`), with a short generated view as context (`adapter.startContextReply()`: Claude Code's `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, printed by the forwarding curl; never a sub-agent's start). Codex takes it the same way (`hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`; it sends SessionStart with the first prompt, on resuming and after each compaction, source `compact`; 0.163.0). Copilot takes a top-level `additionalContext` from SessionStart (source `new` or `resume`), but starts no session after a compaction, only PreCompact: Combwork then gives the view once with the next prompt hook's reply (`startContextAfterCompaction: 'prompt'`; 1.0.98). Checked with each real CLI, Copilot offline (#1065: `tests/fixtures/sessionstart-codex-0.163.0.json`, `tests/fixtures/copilot/sessionstart-1.0.98.json`). The view: what waits on the user (blocked cards, agents waiting or needing a sign-in, with what they ask; past its cap of 10 lines, #1078, the agents asking come first, then blocked cards: those in hand, then On Hold cards waiting on a decision, a reason or label naming design, discuss, decide or choose, or asking a question, then the rest of On Hold, each group most recently changed first), cards in Doing and Review (number, column, project, agent and reviewer, title), running lanes, running agents by project, each project's open cards per column, and from the journal recent decisions and plans (14 days, up to 6), entries linked to the cards in Doing and Review (up to 2 a card, 6 in all), recent incidents (7 days, up to 3), and, when last ISO week had entries but no digest of it, a line asking for one. Kinds the scope leaves out aren't shown. **Hard budget: 9,000 UTF-8 bytes** (about 2,200 tokens; Darren's ~2–3k): every section first gets its first two lines (a line is at most 300 characters and 400 UTF-8 bytes, cut between whole characters, so these floors fit together whatever the script, and a crowded section can't leave the journal or the board out: #1069), then the rest goes in order of importance (waiting on the user, decisions and plans, the cards in hand, the digest, entries on cards, incidents, lanes, agents, the board), a line whole or not at all, long titles and summaries clipped, and "(N more: <tool>)" where lines were left out ("(N more On Hold: cw_list_tasks column hold)" when those are all On Hold cards). **No section grows with the board** (#1078: 60 On Hold cards were ~4K tokens in every new conversation): however much room is left, a section shows at most 10 lines for what waits on the user, the cards in hand and the board, 8 for lanes and agents (the journal's are capped where they are picked, above), so a big board's view stays near 1.5K tokens; it is shown in reading order, headed as a snapshot to check against the live state. Its size is in the performance metrics as a reply of its own, `session start view` (with the Combwork tools' replies); a unit test fails if any input takes it past the budget. Off, Combwork gives no view.
  - **Guidance**: one rule after the Assistant's session contract (`journalRule()`, `withJournal()` in `shared/combworkGuidance.ts`; the combwork MCP server gets the scope as `CW_JOURNAL_SCOPE`): keep a journal (the journal skill), recall before deciding from memory, write decisions in the user's words, plans and why; it replaces handovers (one the user still wants is the handover skill's; HI-2048: the contract's skills line then leaves out handover). Then the scope. Absent while off; like the tools, it follows the setting at the Assistant's next start.
  - **The `journal` skill** (bundled, audience assistant): when and what to write (each kind, open threads and hunches, preferences and moments only in scope), how (a one-line summary, why, links, importance), recalling small first, correcting and superseding, the weekly digest (`kind: digest`, `digestOf` the ISO week, "2026-W42"), the scope, saving before a fresh start (open plans, half-formed ideas and what waits on the user, so nothing exists only in the old conversation; #1082), and handovers. Once a week has a digest, recall by words ranks that week's originals at half (`journal_week()`, a function each connection registers), so the digest's gist comes first; they are kept, and newest-first recall is by time alone.
  - **Handovers** (Darren's decision on #989): journal on, asked for a handover the Assistant says it isn't needed and why, and writes one only if the user still wants it (for another agent or a person). Journal off, it writes the handover, and the first one the Assistant writes in a workspace with the journal off says in its reply to suggest the journal once (workspace.json `journalSuggested`, so never again).
  - **Fresh starts** (#1082; HI-2226, Darren 31 Oct): Combwork's own nudge (§16.10.4, #1437) owns the suggestion that a project's agents start fresh at a natural break, whatever the model; the Assistant's skills no longer suggest it too (weaker models never read the rule on those wakes). The Assistant keeps only its own advice: before suggesting or starting a fresh conversation of its own, its journal holds what is open (journal skill). It never restarts or stops agents for a fresh start itself; the user decides.
- **Settings.** **Settings → Assistant** holds what applies to every workspace's Assistant: the default mode (how it works, below), **Control** and **Change settings** (above), **Pause after you type** and **Enter ends the pause**, **Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent**, the panel's side, **Highlight Compact over** (500,000 tokens; see Compact, §6.2) and the journal, and the workspace's MCP servers for it (a link to the Assistant's view). It has no provider, model, effort, permission mode, context or extra arguments since HI-2108 (decisions A and B): like an agent's, those are its **connection's** (Settings → Accounts & Connections), chosen per workspace in **Assistant Settings**; a workspace's Assistant with none chosen yet runs on the first usable account's CLI and connection (decision A). `settings.assistant.provider` and `.providers` stay in `config.json`, read-only, as the migration's input. Its permission mode is its connection's, except a connection on *The CLI's own setting*, which Assistant Settings greys out and its launch never runs in: the CLI's `assistantMode` instead, the one where the CLI approves safe actions itself and only asks about risky ones, as agents default to: **Auto** for Claude Code, **Approve for me** for Codex (never a plan mode, which blocks MCP tools). Its model and effort are best the agents' (until 0.3 they were lighter, Sonnet with low effort, which made the Assistant careless). That it only looks and advises comes from its instructions, not its mode. A provider can warn about a mode it may not run with a model (`modeCaveat` in its descriptor): the connection dialog says so under its mode when the model that would run doesn't take it (HI-2145: since HI-2108 the agent and Assistant dialogs and Settings → Assistant have no mode or model of their own). For Claude Code's Auto, whether a model takes it depends on the CLI's version and the account (#129), and is what Claude Code reports (`supportsAutoMode` in its initialize reply: absent for Haiku 4.5 with 2.1.289, §10); such a session runs in Manual instead (2.1.286 and 2.1.289), which the warning says. Without the reply's word, the shipped guess ("may not offer Auto with Haiku"). The real-CLI suite (`claude-real`) launches the Assistant with Haiku in Auto and checks that the mode Claude Code itself shows (`LiveSessionState.modeObserved`: from its footer, a hook or its transcript, never the mode asked for at launch, which `permissionMode` starts as) is the one it said, that Combwork shows that mode, and that it warns exactly when Auto isn't offered; `automode` runs the same checks with the fake Claude Code acting out each answer (Haiku takes Auto, doesn't, or the CLI doesn't say) (#234). It is a warning, not a rule: Combwork shows the mode the CLI really runs in. **Assistant Settings** in the panel (⋯, or clicking the footer's model) chooses its **Connection** and **Mode** for the workspace, stored on the home's agent. Another connection while it runs asks first, then restarts it: the same CLI resumes its conversation, another CLI starts a new one (HI-2108). Its CLI is for new conversations: any of its past conversations resumes in the provider it ran in (#506, §13 Providers), so the Sessions tab never refuses one for running in another provider.
- **Modes** (#259; called *personas* in files and code until 0.9.3, #1084). Files in `.combwork/modes` with a header (`name`, `description`, `icon`, and `summary`: the mode's habits in a few lines, on one line or a `summary: |` block) and the instructions. A mode changes what the Assistant puts first, its defaults and its output shape, never its tools or permissions. Combwork ships four: **Coordinator** (the default, `DEFAULT_PERSONA`), **Planner**, **QA triager** and **Release manager**, in a neutral tone, with no procedure or permissions of their own, each pointing at the skill that owns a workflow. **P8 (#1528, #1346's fixes 1 and 5):** Coordinator looks at the state before every request, not only the first, and looks a fact up (the card, the project's docs, then the card's builder) before asking the user, taking the user's request as the OK; Release manager follows the project's release path a stage at a time (for Combwork, RELEASING.md's integration branch, baseline install, RC and release), each step that builds, versions, merges, tags or publishes asked for on its own. They are kept up to date in each workspace like the bundled skills (§7.1): added when the workspace has never had them, an untouched copy of an older version updated, an edited one kept (with **Update available** when it came from an older version, and **Revert to Default**), a deleted one left deleted (with **Restore**). **Switching** (the header's mode menu, **Use in This Workspace**, or Assistant Settings) never restarts it: the workspace keeps the choice, and a running Assistant is told in its conversation, which keeps its context: Combwork types `[CW] Mode: <name> (chosen by the user). <summary> Your tools and permissions are unchanged.` (the last sentence always Combwork's, never the file's; a file without a summary gives its first lines). It is a delivery (#649: a control notice for that launch), offered only while the Assistant is idle and the user isn't typing there, else at its next idle (only the latest switch; a stop drops it: `assistantMode.ts`). Each conversation records the mode it was last given once its message is received (`SessionRecord.mode`: the one it started in, or the last one it was told), and **a resumed conversation** in another mode, or with none recorded (one from before this), is told its mode the same way, once (#334): a switch while it was stopped, or a message a stop dropped, reaches it on resume. It is checked as taken as every line of Combwork's is (#376): Enter again once if its CLI doesn't report it submitted, since a CLI still drawing a resumed conversation can lose the Enter (never over the user's typing; still not taken, the agent's pane says so). A switch made while a resume's check or an older message is under way wins: each home counts its switches, and older work is dropped. Resumes also get the mode's full instructions: Claude Code (2.1.267 on) records a conversation's system prompt on its first request and sends that record on every resume until it compacts, so the adapter resumes the Assistant with `--system-prompt-snapshot off` (unless the user's own arguments set it); agents have no launch instructions and are unaffected. **Restart in This Mode…** (in the same menu, while it runs) asks, then stops and resumes the same conversation with the mode's full instructions, which re-caches it. Its launch instructions say the user picks the mode and that it may suggest another in one line when a request clearly fits it, never switch or insist. **Retired personas:** Overseer, Orchestrator and Reviewer (`RETIRED_PERSONAS`: Coordinator, Coordinator, QA triager) are no longer shipped; the sync removes a workspace copy that is a version Combwork shipped (nothing of the user's), keeps an edited one, moves a workspace's Assistant that chose a removed one to its mode, and says so once in a notice. Config version 7 does the same for Settings → Assistant's default. The **Modes** section of the Assistant view (below) lists, creates, edits (with the unsaved-edits protection of the other editors), deletes and restores them.
- **Assistant view** (the Assistant's mark in the activity bar, "Assistant"; the robot until #979): the sidebar has a **summary** of what the Assistant has used, with the Overview's periods (conversations, prompts, tokens, API-equivalent cost; not counted in any project's Overview), then the sections **Modes**, **Conversations**, **Journal** (#1033, the journal browser: § Journal above) and **Attachments** (#243, #387), each folding. **All Conversations** shows its conversations in the main area with the same tree as a project's Sessions tab (§ Sessions tab: by provider, with the conversations' sub-sessions; search, counts, Archive All / Delete All with the in-use checks, can't-resume markers, reading in full, export, rename, resume), in its own words and with Combwork's conversations only; **Show** on the running one opens the panel. **All Attachments** shows the files pasted or dropped into its conversations (kept like agents' in its home's `.combwork/attachments/<conversation>`) with the project Attachments tab's grid, filters, viewer and actions, grouped by conversation (name, count, span of days and day dividers; newest first; archived conversations last, marked): a group's name opens that conversation in the tree, and its bin moves all its attachments to the Recycle Bin after asking (`attachments:trashGroup`: all or none, none if another program has one open; deleting attachments follows the Attachments tab's rules below). Main reads them through the session-host path (`assertSessionHost`), and watches the home for new ones. A mode opens in the editor. The panel's ⋯ has **All Conversations…** and **Manage Modes…**, which open this view; the commands **Show Assistant Conversations**, **Show Assistant Modes** and **Show Assistant Attachments** do too (its id, `view.assistantImages`, and the section's, `images`, are from before #387, kept). **Memory** (HI-2666, its section `memory`): the Assistant's own memory, what its coding agent saved by itself for the folder its sessions run in (the workspace's, `sessions.ts`'s place for the Assistant): `AssistantMemoryView`, a project's Memory tab's list and `DocEditor`, its files read and saved through the same guard (`file:read`/`file:write`, `fileAllowed`; Claude Code's auto memory is already among what it allows, no new powers). IPC `assistant:memory(provider)` asks the provider's adapter for its optional `autoMemory(folder)` (Claude Code: `memory/` in the folder its transcripts are under, through a connection's junction, else where it would be made; its `.md` files, MEMORY.md first; the project Memory tab's auto memory is the same method); a provider without it gets `folder: null`, and the view says it shows saved memory for Claude Code only (never that the CLI keeps none). The provider is the one the Assistant runs on now (its live session's), else its next launch's (`assistantMemoryProvider`); the load is scoped to the workspace and provider (`useScopedLoad`), so a reply for another, or a file chosen in another, is never shown, and the editor is keyed to scope and file. The folder's path shows over the list with **Copy Path** and **Open Folder**; no file is created here. Its tip says whose memory it is and where, not who else reads it: a project whose folder is the workspace's own reads the same. Repair copies it with the Assistant's conversations when the workspace moves (`workspaceMove.ts`).
- **The panel.** **Header** (#979, after an agent pane's, #977; `AssistantHeader`, 26 px): the Assistant's state mark (#973, `StateMark` from `agentState(live)`: idle, working, waiting for you, stalled), "Assistant" (its provider in the name's tooltip, "Assistant · Claude Code"), the mode as a pill (`assistant-mode`, the mode menu; it gives way first, with an ellipsis), then Stop's place: Stop while it runs; when it doesn't, **Resume** (|▷, its last conversation, when there is one it can resume with its provider) or **Start**; then ⋯ and **Fold** (#1330: the Progress panel's chevron button, pointing to the edge the panel folds to, right or left as the panel sits; its tooltip "Fold the Assistant panel (Ctrl+Alt+I)" names `assistant.toggle`'s shortcut, rebound too; it folds the panel and the Assistant keeps running); those three never shrink, so a 300 px panel keeps them all. ⋯ (opened with the keyboard too) has the rest: **Compact…** while it runs (disabled until it has finished or while the conversation is empty, its detail saying why; "Recommended: the context is over your threshold." past **Highlight Compact over**, as an agent's ⋯), **New Conversation** (Start with nothing to resume), Resume (while it isn't running), Resume a Conversation…, All Conversations…, Assistant Settings…, Manage Modes…, Move Panel to the Left/Right, **Fold the Assistant panel** (with its shortcut; "Hide the Assistant" until #1330, which made Fold the window's one word for both side panels; the header had a hide button and Compact and New buttons before #979). Under it, the **watch line** (#312, `AssistantStatus`, wording in `assistantStatusLine` in `shared/assistant.ts`): "Status: " and Not running, Starting…, Working (or its status message), Idle (· n background tasks running), Waiting on n background tasks, Waiting for you (waiting, sign-in, error and a question it works on through are the attention tone: the warning colour's AA shade, `--attention-fg` (#399: 4.5:1 or more on the line's tint in both themes), a faint tint), "Waiting for your approval: <title>" (n questions) while Combwork's own questions its actions wait on are pending (`assistantQuestions`, the cards under the line: first, over working, idle, a watch and the CLI's waiting; sign-in and an error keep their words with " · waiting for your approval"; answered, the line is as before), or a card watch's "Waiting for HI-12 HI-13 → Review (watch until 22:22)" (an eye before it while watching), each card the app's card chip (#399, `TaskChip` in `CardChip.tsx`: icon and `#n` tinted with the card's column colour from Settings → Board, the eye in Review; a click or Enter opens it, `taskOpen`), side by side without commas (the tooltip's whole line keeps them); one line cut with an ellipsis, the whole line in its tooltip. At its end, once the Assistant has changed something, **Done by the Assistant (n)** (#979: a link-styled button with the Assistant's mark, `aria-expanded`) opens and closes **the list** under the line (#312, `AssistantActions`; closed until opened, remembered per workspace: `ui.panes`, `assistant-done:<workspace>`, 1 while open; the old fold key `assistant-actions:` is no longer read): its changes by the user's message (#1283, §16.14: `AssistantChanges`), each message's last 3 changes newest first (rows of one height, 24 px, each with its Undo button; ✓ or ⊘, text, Undo, time ago; tooltip: date and time, "Not done:" reason) in the shared `ShowAllList` (#352): Show all scrolls every change inside the same height, Show fewer goes back to the top. It sits above the workspace and the terminal, so the terminal refits as it opens or closes (its `ResizeObserver`). **Panel side** (`settings.assistant.panelSide`, `right` by default; one app-wide setting, not per workspace): Settings → Assistant → Panel side, the command `assistant.moveSide` (View menu and palette, its label saying where it goes: "Move Assistant Panel to the Left"), and ⋯. On the left the panel (or its folded strip, arrow pointing right) sits between the sidebar and the main area, with its border and resizer on its right edge (`PaneResizer edge="right"`, the same `assistant` width); the Progress panel stays on the right. The pop-ups (bottom right) only move aside for the panel when it is on the right (`.assistant-panel:not(.on-left)` in `CornerPlacement`). At the top, as tall as it needs up to a third (drag the line under it to set its share; double-click to go back): **the workspace section** (#979; it replaced #240/#311/#399's agent tree), with the agents that need you first (the attention inbox, §14: each row a button that goes to the agent, its tooltip on hover and keyboard focus and its `aria-description` "Click to open HR3 and dismiss" ("Click to open HR3" while it waits for you, which going there doesn't end); a finished row, or a model switch after a safeguard stop, has a quiet × on its right (#1047: `IconButton`, shown on hover and focus-within, transparent but in the tab order otherwise, named "Dismiss: HR3 has finished") that marks it seen (`session:markSeen`) without going there, so it stays gone until the agent finishes again; no Clear all), then **one line per project** (active, or with an agent running): its name (a button that opens the project; cut with an ellipsis, between 4 and 12 em), its agents' **state marks** (`StateMark`, `agentState` with the board's `boardExtras`) for each agent running and each not running whose board state is waiting or stalled (a card in Doing with no one on it, or one blocked on the user), in the project's order so they stay put as states change (wrapping in a narrow panel), "no agents running" or "no agents" otherwise, and "n running". Each mark is a button that goes to the agent (`revealAgent`, switching project), with a tooltip shown on hover and on keyboard focus: first "<name>: <state>" and, after a dot, what it is doing when that says more (`activityOf`: its status when it needs the user, else its open progress run in a few words, `agentOpenRun`/`runWords` in `shared/progress.ts`, else its status) or "not running", so the state the mark draws, the board's included (stalled, waiting for you), is always in words ("Parked: Stalled · not running", "Coder: Idle · e2e: 12 suites 4/12"); then "Coding agent: <provider>", every Doing and Reviewing card with its title, progress (with its step) and the worktree's branch. The first line is its `aria-label`, the rest its `aria-description` (#979 round 2: a screen reader gets all of it). **Names** are on hover by default; the section title's tag toggle (`aria-pressed`, remembered per workspace: `ui.panes`, `assistant-names:<workspace>`) shows each name beside its mark. The other inactive projects fold into one "N inactive projects" row (a button, `aria-expanded`) that expands them, remembered per workspace. It scrolls under its title, which stays put with the counts. (The per-project fold of #399, `ui.assistantFold`, is no longer shown; its stored preference is kept.) Then its terminal, and a footer like an agent pane's (#978, `PaneFooter`: model and effort, mode; the transcript's size, context and cost on the right, #1013). When it isn't running: **Start Assistant**, Resume, and its past conversations. Hiding the panel doesn't stop it; the strip's status icon (the mark with its dot, #399) shows what it's doing. **The Assistant's mark** (`AssistantMark`, Darren's pick of three on #399: a honeycomb cell with a crown in it, for the queen) is used wherever the Assistant is listed: **the activity bar** (#979, in place of the robot: 24 px, the bar's colour, its line about a codicon's weight), a skill's "Assistant" audience badge, the strip (with its status), Done by the Assistant, its runs in the Progress panel (in place of the provider's icon), its row in the attention inbox (the item's dot on it) and in the Workspace Overview (its group, its table row, and its running row, with its status). Its colours are tokens (`--mark-accent`, `--mark-off`) that keep 3:1 on the sidebar in both themes.
- **Room for the work** (HI-1737: Darren's decision, 26 Oct, then the Assistant's rule for the rest; `layoutRoom.ts`): at 900 px and 150% (600 CSS px) the sidebar and the panel had left the main pane 0 px. The work never goes below 280 px while anything beside it can still give way, and what is beside it gives way in order, covering nothing: the Assistant's panel narrows to 240 px, then the Progress panel to its 240 (flex-shrinks 1000 and 10, the sidebar's 1); the sidebar to 160 px; the Projects list folds to its rail (48 px, `sidebarFolded`); the Progress panel folds to its strip (`progressFolded`); last, the Assistant's panel narrows below 240, to 190 px (`--assistant-min`; its mode pill is then cut inside its border). Each fold holds only while the window is that narrow, is never saved (the saved sidebar width, Compact and the Progress panel open stay as they are), comes back on its own once there is room, and is decided from the room without itself, so it never flickers at the edge. Opening a folded one by hand (**›** on the rail, the Progress strip, their shortcuts) shows it anyway until there's room again; the Progress panel folded by hand stays folded. With less room than all that the work takes what is left (`--main-min`), never pushing a panel past the window: a panel opened anyway, or **a sidebar view with no rail** (Notes, Skills, Templates, MCP: the bounded exception the Assistant approved on HI-1737, as the user opened that sidebar and a panel narrower than 190 px overlaps itself), where the work keeps at least about 170 px at 900 px and 150%. The Projects view keeps 280. A panel's drag keeps its own minimum (the Assistant's 300 px).

### 6.6 Task board

- **What it is.** One board per workspace, in `<Workspace>/.combwork/combwork.db` (a row per card, its lists in tables of their own; §4.4, and **Where the board is kept** below). Cards have a number (#12, unique in the workspace and never reused, including past cards whose files were lost or damaged), a title, a Markdown description, a project (or none: about the workspace), an agent of that project (optional; its name is kept for when the agent is removed), labels (up to 12; a change's `labels` replaces them, and `addLabels` and `removeLabels` add or take off only those named, keeping the others, with a history line of what was added or removed, #1131: for tagging cards in bulk, with `cw_update_tasks`; both kinds in one change are refused), a **blocked** reason, the cards it **depends on** and **related** cards, comments and a history of who changed what (**You**, **Assistant**, or the agent, "Agent 2 (web)"). A card saved with fields missing or of the wrong type (by an older Combwork, a script, an export copied back) is read safely (each gets a default).
- **Where the board is kept** (#990, #1017). In SQLite, `.combwork/combwork.db`, with Node's built-in `node:sqlite` (`db.ts`; nothing native to build). Since 1.0 (#1209, the cards step of the 1.0 upgrade, §16.17) a card is a row of typed columns in `cards` (title, project and its id, agent, reviewer, column, order, blocked, archived, dates…) with its labels, links, context, comments, history, decisions and holds in child tables, and every reader is given the card's JSON document composed from them, byte for byte the document it was saved as (`schema/cardRows.ts`, the card JSON contract: a field Combwork doesn't know, or one of another type, is kept as it was, and so is a card's own key order), so the Agent API's JSON and Export Board are unchanged. In 0.9 (and for a 0.9 board waiting for its upgrade, read-only) a row held the card's JSON document as its file did, with columns made from it for queries. WAL, `synchronous=NORMAL` (a crash of Combwork loses nothing committed; a power cut may lose the last commit or two, never the file). Cards don't need editing by hand any more: Combwork manages them, for the user and agents. **Every change is one transaction** under the board's lock (one change at a time for every window): all of it is saved or none (also when SQLite itself undoes the transaction part way, a full disk or an I/O error: nothing more of the change is written and it fails whole, whatever it made of the error), and the board is told once (`tasks-changed`) as it commits; a batch (Archive All, a batch move, a project's cards) is one transaction too. No folder is watched: Combwork's own writes tell the board, and a change committed by another process (another copy of Combwork, a script) is noticed within about a second (each open board polls SQLite's `data_version`, 3.5 µs a look). **Moving in**: the first time a workspace opens in 0.9, every `<n>.json` card file of `.combwork/tasks` (never `.bak`, `.tmp` or anything else) goes into the database as its text was, with `board.json`'s next number and the archive batches, in one transaction checked before it commits (as many rows as card files read, each with its file's number, column and archived); a card file that isn't valid JSON stays out and is named in a notice. The folder then becomes `.combwork/tasks.imported-<time>`, kept as a backup (a rename Windows refuses is done at the next open; the cards are in the database meanwhile, imported once), and, until 1.1, a stub `.combwork/tasks` was left with `board.json` (the next number) and a README for older versions (none is written since: the names upgrade retires it, §4.1.1, HI-2594). A board that can't be opened or moved in says why on every use and leaves the files as they were. **Export Board to JSON…** (the board's **⋯**, the command palette) writes every card, archived ones too, to a new folder inside one the user picks: `<n>.json` each, exactly as the cards' files were before 0.9, with `board.json` and `archive-batches.json`. **Older versions** (a downgrade): an older Combwork doesn't know the database and shows an empty board, with nothing lost; a card it makes gets a number past the board's (the stub's `board.json`, moved on as each number is taken until 1.1, so also after Combwork was ended without closing), and when 0.9 opens the workspace again (since 1.1, the names upgrade as it retires the stub), nothing in `.combwork/tasks` is taken back on its own (Darren, 17 Oct): every `<n>.json` found there is set aside, intact, in `.combwork/tasks.set-aside`, free number or not, the board is unchanged, and one notice says "n cards made by an older Combwork were found: review them", with **Review…** (#1044, Darren's decision on #1017: the only way they reach the board). Its dialog (`SetAside.tsx`; also the board's **⋯** → **Set-Aside Cards (n)…** while any remain, and the command `task.reviewSetAside`) lists each file, oldest number first: the number its name gives, whether that number is free on the board, title, who made it and when, project, column, comment count and the description's first 600 characters; a file that isn't a card is listed as unreadable and can only be discarded. **Add to Board** (`tasks:addSetAside`, in one board change, the file read again there) adds the card with every field the older Combwork stored (its own fields too, and past holds for its cost), Combwork's own fields as any read shows them (one of the wrong type gets its safe default, so it never stops the card coming back), but its number, place, history and date (a review under way there ends, its hold closed), last in its column, under its old number when no card has it, else the next free one, with a history line by `Repair` ("Added from an older Combwork, where it was made as #n"); its content's hash is recorded as added (`board_meta` `setAsideAdded`) in the same transaction and the file moved to the Recycle Bin after the commit (recoverable), so a file Windows holds, or the same file set aside again, is never listed or added twice. **Discard…** asks, then moves the file to the Recycle Bin (`trash()`). Only a name of the folder's own form is accepted, never a path out of it. Nothing is rewritten: links to an old number stay as they are. Each file is set aside once: one whose very content is there already isn't kept twice, and another file of the same name is kept beside it under a name of its own; it is copied before it leaves the stub, so one Windows won't let go of is removed at a later open. Their numbers are never given to new cards. Export Board to JSON is the way back. No card number is ever given twice: past every card file's number, a damaged file's too. To use the board in an older Combwork, export it and copy the files into `.combwork/tasks` with Combwork closed. A board saved by a newer Combwork (a schema version this one doesn't know) is shown read-only, every change refused saying so. Schema changes are steps in `db.ts` (`schema_version` records each, with the Combwork that ran it), and a copy of the file is kept in `.combwork/backups` (the last 3) before a step runs on one with data. **The window's board** has the cards on it in full and archived cards in short (`summary`: title, place, agent, labels, dates), so a change doesn't send every archived card's comments and history again; the Archived view and an archived card's dialog read them in full while open (`tasks:list` with `fullArchive`). **Reads that run often ask the query for the cards they need** (#1107, `CardQuery` in `boardStore.ts`: archived or not, numbers, agents, reviewers), never parsing archived cards for nothing (on a busy board 945 of 1058 cards, 13 MB, most of it comments; a whole read took 64 ms and about 22 MB of short-lived strings): decision notices (before and after each project agent's API call), the Assistant's start view, the hourly archiving and reordering read the live cards; lane watches read their lanes' cards by number (a card archived mid-lane is still the lane's) and the live cards only once an agent waits for the user; ending an agent's reviews asks for the cards it reviews; costs (a card's panel, a lane's hover, Performance's Cards) read every card's holds only (`holdDocs`: its project, agent, reviewer and holds, its history only when it keeps no holds), then the cards wanted in full. Measured on a copy of the live board: decision notices 64 → 7 ms, the hourly archiving 70 → 5 ms, ending reviews 65 → 11 ms, a lane round 66 → 11 ms, costs 70 → 41 ms (SQLite parsing every document is most of what is left). With the cards in tables (#1209, the same copy of 1186 cards, median of runs): the window's board 30 → 16 ms, costs' holds 28 → 17 ms, places 7 → 6 ms, decision notices 8 → 6 ms, a lane round (four changes and a read) 22 → 19 ms, a card in full unchanged (0.09 ms); the whole board, archived cards in full, 44 → 65 ms (each card composed from its rows; the reads that run often ask for the cards they need, above). Deleting a card puts it in the Recycle Bin as `<n>.json`, as exported.
- **Columns, fixed** (#170): **On Hold**, **Todo**, **Doing**, **Review**, **Passed**, **Done** (`hold`, `todo`, `doing`, `review`, `passed`, `done`), so the Assistant, agents and the API all speak the same six; not configurable. **On Hold** is parked work nobody picks up: only the user and the Assistant put cards there (a project agent's move there, or a card it creates there, is refused, 403, its error sending a parking the user decided to the Assistant, `cw_ask_assistant`, and any other to the user, HI-2227; it may take one out when the user asks it to work on it). **Passed** is work whose review passed, waiting to be merged: the reviewer moves the card there with its verdict. **Done means merged**: the builder moves its cards there after merging its branch (the merge-ready skill), or the user does. **Blocked** (a reason, or cards it depends on) stays a property of a card in any column: a blocked card doesn't move to On Hold by itself. Cards in On Hold and Passed are never stalled (only Doing cards are, and cards in Doing or Review that an agent in a card loop left with no watch, #376). Nothing moves on upgrade: cards already in Done stay there. Agent states aren't columns (they change by the second): a Doing card shows its agent's live status (working, waiting on background tasks, needs your input, finished, not running), and a Doing card whose agent has finished gets a green edge. **Blocked** is a red flag on a card in any column. **Archive** hides a card from the board but keeps it searchable (the **Archived** view), and **Bring Back** returns it to the end of its column. **Archived (n)** in the board's toolbar shows the archived cards as a data table (#249; `DataTable`, below): number, title, project (the whole board only), labels, agent (the last it had), **From** (the column it was archived from), **Archived** (its latest "Archived…" in its history, `archivedAt()`) and **Created**, the dates in the shared date format; newest archived first; filters: text for number, title and agent, a choice of project, label (a card with several shows for each) and From; pages with rows per page (`table-rows:archived-cards`). The board's search narrows the rows too (both apply). A row (click or Enter) opens the card, read-only as an archived card is. **Unarchive** on a row, or **Unarchive Selected** for the rows ticked (the header's box ticks every row the filters let through, on every page), brings each back to the end of the column it was archived from, as Bring Back does; nothing else changes an archived card. Cards in Done are **archived automatically** after **Settings → Board → Archive Done cards after** days (14, or **Never**; the same for every workspace), counted from when the card last went into Done or was brought back, not its last change; Combwork checks when a workspace opens, every hour and when the setting changes, and the card's history says so (`archivedFor: 'done'`).
- **Column colours.** Each column has a colour on its top edge and heading, and a subtle tint of it on its cards (mixed with the theme's background, so it reads in light and dark): On Hold grey, Todo slate blue, Doing blue, Review purple, Passed teal, Done green. A card's tint follows its column (a colour saved before a column existed falls back to its default). The state edges (blocked red, stalled amber, finished green) stay solid over the tint, with their text. **Settings → Board → Colour columns** turns it off; **Column colours** has a picker per column (stored as `#rrggbb` in `board.colors`; anything else falls back to the default) with a reset for a changed one.
- **Long text on a card** (#372). Text the user or an agent wrote stays inside the card however long its words (hashes, paths): the title and the blocked, stalled and reviewing notes wrap anywhere (`overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the note's text, `.task-note-text`, its icon at the top); the blocked reason is clamped to 3 lines with the whole in its tooltip ("Blocked: …") and in the card dialog, whose Blocked field wraps to show it all (up to six lines, then it scrolls; one line of text: Enter and pasted line breaks become spaces). A long label ends in "…" (whole on hover); the agent line's status stays on one line while the name gives way. Elsewhere: tooltips break long words (`overflow-wrap: break-word`) and are never taller than the window: one that would be is measured again as wide as the window allows (`.tip.wide`), and only if it still doesn't fit is it cut at the window's height with its end faded (`.tip.clipped`); and a sidebar row with a tooltip (the Board's Stalled list) ends its title in "…".
- **Short titles** (HI-1872, Darren's decision of 27 Oct 2026: "cleaner to write short messages anyway for the board", and "we have the card itself to carry proper information"). A card's title is about 70 characters and names the outcome or the problem; evidence, numbers, file names, paths and people's names go in its description. The title is the merge commit's subject in Combwork's default commit message (HI-1697), where git's convention is about 72 characters. The rule is agents' and the Assistant's, said once, in `cw_create_task`'s `title` and use-cw-api's tools.md (`cw_update_task`'s: short, the detail in the description). Combwork never refuses a long title (titles stay at most 200 characters, as before): when an agent, the Assistant or a script sets one longer than Settings → Advanced → **Suggest a shorter title past** (`cw.cards.titleNudgeChars`, 80 characters by default, 0 off), the change is made and its reply adds a line suggesting a shorter one (`main/titleNudge.ts`). A title of any length that names what belongs in the description gets a line too (HI-2061, so the rule is Combwork's, not only the tool's text): a path, a file name, a card's number or a key of one of the workspace's projects (current or old, so `UTF-8` isn't one), or a measurement (a number with a unit), at most three of them quoted, with the step to take: retitle it without them (`cw_update_task` with `title`), keeping them in the description (HI-2260: told only to put them in a description that already had them, agents kept the title); the length's setting at 0 turns off only the length's line. People's names aren't detected and stay the tool's rule. The user's own titles, typed in the window, are never questioned; existing titles stay as they are.
- **An agent's card.** An agent with cards given to it in **Doing** shows the first (in board order) as a chip with the board icon, in the Doing column's colour (plain with Colour columns off): only `#4` (and `+1` with more) in its pane header at every width (the name's tooltip lists them, #975) (#311; the chip's tooltip lists Doing and Reviewing with titles) and on its row in the Assistant's workspace overview (whose row tooltip lists them); `#4 title` on its row in the Overviews' running lists. The short chip keeps its size: the agent's status gives way first. Clicking it opens the card's dialog in place. The project's tooltips (the compact rail tile's, the sidebar's agent count and status, the project header's status) show its agents as a table (#529, `AgentsTable`): **Agent** (with its status dot) · **State** (working, waiting on n background tasks, watching, ready, not running…) · **Card** (the card in Doing, else "reviewing #n …", cut to one line) · **Waiting for** (a watch's cards and column, "#506, #509 → Review"; the column only when one waits). Rows are in lane order (`laneOrder`, `shared/agentTable.ts`): each running or paused lane's builder then its reviewer, the lanes in the Progress panel's order (#568: the user's own once they move one), then the other agents in the project's order. **The same table elsewhere** (#572; `AgentRowsTable`, each place choosing its columns after Agent, five columns taking smaller shares of the room, `cols-5`): **Stop All**'s confirm (the running agents: Agent · State · Card · Waiting for), **Start New (All)**, **Archive and Start New (All)** and **Remove All**'s (`BatchAgentsTable`: Agent · State · Card · Worktree (its branch; Remove All's "merged and clean" or "always kept (reason)", `removeWorktreeText`) · What happens (`batchOutcome`: "Stopped (will be interrupted), then a new session", "Removed"…, in the warning colour when stopping interrupts something)), in a wide confirm with the note under it (`AgentsDetail`; in a dialog the table takes its width and a long cell wraps rather than being cut, so a kept worktree's reason reads in full); **Every table has a plain-text form** made from the same rows (`tableText`, `agentRowsText` in `shared/agentTable.ts`): a line an agent with every cell the table shows, in its order, the card too ("• Worker — Working… · card #12 Lanes · worktree cw/w · Stopped (will be interrupted), then a new session"; "card reviewing #9 …" for a reviewer; an empty cell left out), a heading's line ("workspace-a:") over its agents. In a dialog (`AgentsDetail`) the table is `aria-hidden` and the plain text, visually hidden, is what screen readers get, so nothing is said twice; it is also the confirm's `detail`. **The quit dialog** (quit, close window, close or switch workspace) lists its agents as the table, wide: Agent · Project · State (a watcher's watch) · Card · Stopping it (only when one is busy: will be interrupted, background tasks will stop, waiting for you, its card loop pauses, in the warning colour), under a heading row per workspace when several windows are open, with its plain text grouped the same way; main adds each agent's name, id and card (`withCards`: each workspace's board read once, as the question is held, then shown). **The status bar's running sessions** (`RunningAgentsTip`): the counts, then the workspace's running agents as the table (Agent · Project · State · Card · Waiting for), at most 24 rows ("and n more"), with the table's plain text (every running agent) as the item's `aria-description`. It shows whenever the project has agents (one idle agent too). The tooltip is wider than a plain one but never scrolls: each column takes at most its share of the room the window leaves, so all four fit at any width and zoom, and a longer cell (a card title, an agent's name) is cut with an ellipsis. Keyboard: the rail tile is a button (Tab reaches it, Enter or Space opens the project), and it, the sidebar's status and the header's badge show the table on keyboard focus; each has the same rows as text in its accessible description. The row itself is unchanged. Todo, Review and Done cards aren't shown; it follows the board live.
