The Assistant has no cards. **Each session records its cards**: whenever an agent has cards in Doing (the board changed, or its session was recorded), main adds those not already there to the running session's record in `sessions.json` (`cards: [{ number, title }]`, in order, the title as it was then; only for a session Combwork has recorded). The Sessions tab shows **Worked on #5 Prompt snippets, #7 …** under the transcript's toolbar; each card links to its dialog, and a deleted card shows its number and recorded title without a link.
- **Reviews.** An agent asked to review a card (check its work, often another agent's) marks it rather than taking it: `review: "start"` on `cw_update_task` / `PATCH /v1/tasks/{n}` (a card in Review, on its own, by an agent of the card's project through its own token; the user, the Assistant and scripts don't) sets `TaskCard.review` (the reviewer's id and name, and since when). The card stays in Review with the agent that did the work. `passed` or `failed`, with the verdict as the comment, ends it ("Review passed" / "Review failed" in the history); with `passed`, a `column: "passed"` in the same change moves it to Passed, which the review-agent-work and card-loop skills tell reviewers to do (#170; `"done"` still works, for a user's explicit say-so). A `failed` verdict sends the card back to Doing for its fixes, its agent kept (its builder holds it again), as the verdict intent does, on every path (HI-1946: P3's kept 0.9's rule, a failed card staying in Review, so in a project whose rules have no Review stage, with the rules off or on a card from before 1.0 the PATCH and the intent ended differently, and round 2's work had no hold for cost per card); its history says "Review failed", then "Moved to Doing", and the recorder writes the Verdict before the Moved, as the runtime does; a wake about it names the verdict ("is in Doing: R1 failed it"). With any column other than `doing` it is refused (400) before anything is saved. One reviewer at a time: another agent's start is refused, naming the reviewer; the same agent's start renews its mark (saved, without another history line); only the reviewer gives the verdict, and only while its review is going: once the card has moved on (out of Review for fixes, or the review ended with the reviewer's session), an old verdict is refused, so it can't settle newer work; a new review starts again. **Returning a failed card for review** (#214): a failed verdict left the card in Review before HI-1946, and a card failed then may still be there, so a move to Review by the card's own agent (its Combwork tools, or the Agent API with its own token) or the user (the board's **Move to → Review (next round)**), on a card in Review whose latest verdict failed with nothing since that starts another round (a move, a review started, another agent, an earlier return), records "Returned for review, round N" (N: one more than the reviews failed since it last passed one). That is a move into Review for waits (`movedIntoSince`), so it wakes a reviewer waiting for the card's return, whose line says so (`#159 (Claudette's card) was returned for review (round 2)`), and it starts a new round (the failed verdict is no longer named). Any other move to the column a card is already in (by another agent, the Assistant, a script; a card not failed, or already returned) is no change. The review also stops (with a line in the history) when the card leaves Review or its project, when the reviewer's session ends (`session-exit`) and when the reviewer is removed (`endReviews`). An end that came as a window closed the workspace doesn't reach its board, which is fenced then (#1379), so as the workspace opens again the reviews whose reviewer has no session running end too, with the same history line (`endReviewsWithoutSession`, #1392); a reviewer running then keeps its review. The board shows "Reviewing: <name> · <how long>" on the card (eye icon; click shows the reviewer), in amber with the reason when the reviewer has gone or isn't running (`reviewStalled`); the reviewer's chip (strip tab, pane header, the Overviews' running list) shows the card with an eye in the Review column's colour when it has none in Doing, and tooltips say "reviewing #n". Its session records the card as reviewed (`cards[].review`), shown as **Reviewed #n** beside **Worked on** in the Sessions tab. Agents' session contract, the tool's description and the bundled review-agent-work skill (which also covers finding the exact state reviewed, findings with repro and impact, and reviewing again after fixes) say that reviewing isn't working on a card: only fixes they're asked to make move it to Doing. Cards and records without these fields read as before.
- **Waiting on cards** (#128). An agent that has to wait for another agent's work on a card (a builder for its review, a reviewer for the fixes) waits without spending tokens: `cw_wait_for_tasks` / `POST /v1/tasks/wait`, on up to 20 of the caller's cards (a project agent: its project's; others are unknown to it, 404). What counts as a change: a column move, a new comment, a review verdict, a new agent (`changes`, default all). A project agent's own comments never count for its watch (`watcherName`) (#1074: a builder watching for its verdict or a reviewer's request for a commit isn't woken by the summary it posts as it moves the card to Review), nor its own moves (HI-2015: a builder watching its card's column moves was woken by its own submission's move into Review, a wasted turn on every submission; a column changed only by the watcher's moves since doesn't count, nor a move of its own into the column it waits for, while another's move, such as the reviewer's verdict sending it on, does). Every route into Review is the submitter's own step, recorded as it. `column` alone waits until a card is in that column (at once if it already is), and nothing else counts: a comment on a card still in Doing doesn't end a wait for it to reach Review. `column` with `changes` naming `column` waits until one *moves into* it, or for another change listed (the builder's "a verdict, or into Passed"). Either way a card already in that column answers at once (#434: a builder watching for "→ Passed" on a card already passed must not wait for a move that has happened), whoever waits and whatever its history. **`fresh`** (with `column`) asks for the next move into it instead: a card already there waits until it leaves and comes back (the card's history is checked, so a quick out and back between checks still counts) or, in Review, is **returned for review** (the reviewer's wait for a failed card's next round); `fresh` without `column`, or `column` with `changes` that don't name it, is refused. A watch keeps the agent's view of the board: a project agent's own project's cards (worked out from the agent, never from what is saved), the Assistant's whole board. A card moved to another project, archived or deleted counts as **gone** ("#12 is gone from your board (archived, deleted or moved to another project)") and nothing about its new state is told; a line that fired is checked again just before it is typed.
  - **`wake: true`** (an agent or the Assistant; not scripts) starts a **card watch** and answers at once: the agent ends its turn, and **A wake is confirmed taken** (#376: on 7 Oct a Codex reviewer's wake was typed and its Enter dropped, so the line sat unsent in its prompt for hours while its watch had ended). **How the line goes in** (#597; since #650 the only line Combwork types is the doorbell, or the user's own task for an agent with no inbox): `sendPrompt` clears the prompt (Ctrl+U), puts the line in and presses Enter. Any line it types, and Compact's focus, goes without invisible characters (#1547, `withoutInvisible`: Unicode's format characters and variation selectors, but for those an emoji is made of): Claude Code 2.1.309 takes such a character out of a prompt and leaves it unsent ("Removed 1 invisible character · review and press Enter to send"), which a user's task pasted from a web page could carry; Combwork's doorbell has none, and Ctrl+U before the line isn't one (tried alone, 150 ms before, and read with the line, pasted or typed). A CLI busy for a moment (a CPU-pinned machine, its own work after a turn) reads all of that in one go, and Claude Code (2.1.296) takes a read of several characters as a paste in which Combwork's Ctrl+U and Enter are text: the line isn't sent by Enter, nor by Enter again, and only a third Enter (the user's) sends it. On 8–11 Oct about 2% of wakes went so, the Assistant's and agents' alike (9 of 492 and 8 of 531 in Combwork's log: not long lines, a narrow pane or the end of a turn, which a narrow 45-column pane with Assistant-sized lines, idle and straight after long turns, took every time). So a CLI that reads a bracketed paste as text however it arrives (`capabilities.bracketedPaste`: Claude Code) gets the line as one (`ESC[200~…ESC[201~`, control characters left out) while its terminal has bracketed paste on (Combwork's screen of it, `TerminalScreen.bracketedPaste()`); a line starting with `/` is still typed, since a pasted slash command is sent as a message. Copilot gets it as a bracketed paste too (#600: typed in pieces, a line that Copilot 1.0.98 read with its Enter while paused wasn't sent by that Enter, 3 of 3; pasted, 7 of 7 were, as text). Codex 0.163 drops an Enter that it reads with the line, typed or pasted alike (its paste-burst handling: 6 of 6 paused 0.5–3 s needed Enter again), so its line is typed in pieces and Combwork presses Enter only once Codex has drawn the line on its screen (`capabilities.enterOnceDrawn`: the line's end shows once more than before it was typed), at most 5 s (Settings → Advanced, Codex → *Typed line: wait to be drawn*, `codex.prompt.drawnSeconds`, 1–60 s; Combwork logs that it waits), then Enter anyway: 12 of 12 were then taken at the first Enter. Codex's own `disable_paste_burst` setting would also do, but it splits a user's multi-line paste into Codex at its first line, so Combwork doesn't set it. Claude Code shows a pasted line of more than about 800 characters as `[Pasted text #1]` in its prompt until it is sent; the conversation shows it whole. After typing it, Combwork waits up to 10 s (`TAKE_MS`) for the CLI to take a prompt (UserPromptSubmit: `promptsTaken`). **What the line rang for being read counts as taken too** (#1514, `LineFollow.read`): on 23 Oct five Codex 0.164.0 reviewers read the wake Combwork typed 4 to 8 s after it was typed, with no prompt Combwork saw (Codex takes a line typed while a turn runs, its compaction at a turn's start, as queued input with no UserPromptSubmit, and their hooks weren't reaching Combwork after a PowerShell move), and Combwork still pressed Enter again, marked the line not taken and refused every prompt until someone pressed Enter on an empty composer. A delivery offered by the line and read (`received` or `acked`) ends the confirmation as taken (`… was taken after N ms: what it rang for was read, with no prompt seen`); read after the line was marked, the mark goes, in the launch it was offered into (`sessions.lineTaken`), and only when the delivery read is one that very line rang for (the mark keeps their ids, `untakenFor`): an older line's delivery read late says nothing of a newer line still in the composer (HR4's round 1 finding). The e2e suite `codexqueued` acts it out with the fake Codex (`compacting N`, `fake-queue-<agent>`). If it doesn't, Combwork presses Enter once more (`submitAgain`: the same launch, idle, nobody typing, Combwork not typing, and no input of the user's since the line began: #652, a line the user typed into is their draft, whatever the typing pause, so Combwork never sends or clears it; what it named waits again, and nothing more is typed there until a prompt is sent, `leaveToUser`), as soon as that is safe within six times that wait (#430: not given up at once), waits again, and if it still isn't taken, logs it; the loop check above then flags the card. **Still not taken** (#430: in 0.4.0 the Assistant's and project agents' Claude Code sessions sometimes weren't reading their input at all, and took the line by themselves 1 to 19 minutes later; not the window's focus, which quiet test copies ruled out), the agent is marked (`untakenLine`: "A line Combwork typed wasn't taken" in its pane header, and in the Assistant's status line), the user is told once, and Combwork types nothing more into it until its CLI takes a prompt (the user's Enter alone isn't proof). The same holds, centrally in `sendPrompt` (checked before the input is cleared, before each piece and before Enter) and in a wake's delivery, while a wake is being confirmed (held from its typing until it is taken, marked not taken or the launch ends, however long the wait for a safe Enter again: `holdForConfirm`), and while any other line Combwork typed in the last 30 s isn't taken yet (`lineWaiting`), so nothing is typed over a line being confirmed; `cw_prompt_agent` is 409 meanwhile. The notice says whether Enter was pressed again. Enter stays at most twice a wake. The log has each wake's typed (`Woke …`), taken (`… was taken after N ms`), Enter again and not taken. When a watched card changes, Combwork gives the agent its **wake**: a card event delivery (#649) that it reads with `cw_inbox`, rung by the doorbell while it is idle (#650; told at its next tool call if it works), whose text is `[CW] #12 is in Review; latest comment by Codex (web): "first line…". Your card watch has ended: carry on (…)`. **The Assistant's card wake while lanes run** (#402) ends with `Lanes are still running (cw_lane list): before you end your turn, watch them all again in one watch, each lane by its last card (run-lanes).` whenever a lane of the workspace is active or paused (`withLanesTail`, kept whole: the rest of the line is cut to make room): a model that reads no skill on a wake otherwise ended its turn watching nothing. **Changes landing together are told together** (#224): a watch fired by a change waits 1.5 s (`SETTLE_MS`) before its line is made, and it is made then (as it is handed to the delivery service) from every watched card's changes since the watch began (`wakeLines`): one card as below; several, each with where it is and its verdict, `[CW] #217 is in Review: Codex (web) passed it (latest comment …); #119 is in Review: Codex (web) failed it (…). …`, comments cut first; when even that is too long, every card is still named, in a few words without names or comments (`#217 in Review, passed; #119 in Review, failed`, a gone card as `#12 gone`) or by number alone, and the line says details were left out and to read each card (#226). **No gap between watches:** a watch keeps, per card, where its view ended (`seen`: the last history entry and comment it counted), and counts comments, verdicts and moves into a column by the entries after it, never by time, so an entry sharing a millisecond with one already seen, even one alike in author and words, still counts, and the one seen is never counted again. Every history entry and comment gets an id when written (`id`, unique on the card; the Agent API's card views and latest comment leave it out); entries from before ids are found by time, a hash of who and what, and their place. History and comments only grow at the end and are capped at the start, so when the entry seen is no longer kept, everything kept came after it. Combwork remembers, per agent and card, what its wakes told (in memory, the latest 100 cards an agent): the card's mark and `seen` as the line was made from it, or for a limit line the watch's own starting point. The agent's next watch starts each such card from there (`carriedOver`), moved on only past what the agent did itself since (by its board name), kind by kind, unless someone else made that kind of change too; column, agent and archived compare with the told state. So a verdict, comment, move, reassignment or archiving by others between a wake and the next watch fires it at once; the agent's own work in between doesn't. **A watch also starts from the agent's own last change to a card** (HI-2302, `ownCut`): when the agent commented on the card or changed it in its current launch after what its last wake told it, or no wake told it of the card, the watch starts from just after that change, so what others did after it counts (its column and latest verdict and comment as they were then, from the card's history; a reassignment by someone else since makes its agent then unknown, so the reassignment counts too: HR1's round 1 finding). On PE-39 a reviewer asked the builder for logs, the builder answered a minute later, and the reviewer's watch began after that, from the card with the answer already in it, so it never fired. A change from an earlier launch doesn't reach back (a card touched days ago would fire a new watch with old news); an intent's card (#1639) still starts from that intent. **A move into the watched column counts for every watch with a column** (#521), not only one asked for as a move: a watch that waits for a card to be in Review, started after a wake that told the card in Review (since gone back to Doing), compared the card with that told column and never fired when it came back (on 10 Oct three Codex reviewers sat "watching" cards already in Review for five hours). So it can't be misread (#143): when the change is a review verdict, the line names the reviewer (`#12 is in Review: Codex (web) failed it; …`); on another agent's card (a dependency, or the builder's card a reviewer waits for) it says whose (`#12 (Claude's card) is in Review`), and in Passed that Passed isn't merged (`#12 (Claude's card) is in Passed: Codex (web) passed it (Passed isn't merged); …`; #170: before it, Done said so). In Done, which means merged, it names the verdict that passed it and nothing more. The watcher's own card and a card without an agent get no owner. A verdict is named only for the current round: once the card has gone back to On Hold, Todo, Doing or Review, a new review has started, or it has gone to another agent, an earlier one isn't (a card moved to Passed or Done by hand names none). Names in the line are cut to 40 characters and the comment's first line gives way, so the card, its state and what to do always fit the line's 1000 bytes. A condition already met answers with the change instead of watching (and ends the agent's earlier watch). One watch per agent; a new one replaces it. The line is handed over only when the agent is idle and the user isn't typing in its terminal (the same guard as the Assistant's prompts); otherwise Combwork tries again on the agent's next status change and every 5 seconds. The watch stays until the agent has read its wake with `cw_inbox` (it still shows watching and takes no other work meanwhile), not when the doorbell is typed; cancelled or replaced meanwhile, its delivery is cancelled (a doorbell being typed stops before Enter, and `cw_inbox` no longer gives it), and a cancelled watch never comes back. Typing in its terminal doesn't cancel the watch. A workspace's watches change one at a time, so a board change made while a watch is being set up is checked once it is in place (and the board is checked again right after every new watch).
  - **Wait limit.** `limitMinutes` (1–1440, default 120): with no change by then, Combwork wakes the agent with `[CW] No change on #12 in 2 h: your card watch has ended. Tell the user (cw_notify) and ask what to do.` A watched card in Review as the limit passes (HI-2295; seen 1 Nov, CB1's watch on CL-5 timed out 6 s after its own submission and it told the user and the Assistant a review was late, 10 s before the pool gave the card to CR1) is said to be there instead, read from the board as the line is handed over (a line held while the agent was busy is made again then, so a card it submitted meanwhile is told in Review, and one sent back isn't; the watch's `fired.limit` marks it): being reviewed (`#12 is in Review, being reviewed by R1`), given by the reviewer pool to a reviewer that hasn't started, waiting for the pool to give it to one, or waiting for its reviewer; and the agent is told to watch it again for its verdict, not to tell the user. Likewise a card waiting on another agent's card in Doing or Review (`#10 waits on #8`), and another agent's card in Doing that a watched card waits on or, in a project agent's watch, that it isn't the loop reviewer of (`#8 is in Doing with CB1`) (HI-2381): another's work going on is nothing to ask the user about, so the agent is told to watch them again, not to tell the user; the lane shows what its next card waits on (its start wait). Only the watch's other cards ask for that (`… for the rest, tell the user …`). Not a card the watcher reviews itself.
  - **Kept.** Watches are kept in the workspace's database, `<Workspace>/.combwork/combwork.db` (a row each, #1018; with each card's state when the watch began, so a change while Combwork or the agent was closed still counts: they are checked as soon as they are loaded), and a stopped agent with a watch is woken when it is resumed. They belong to their workspace: its folder is taken when they load, and once it closes or its window opens another workspace they are dropped from memory and nothing more is read or written for them (a registration under way then fails). Saves are one transaction in the workspace's database (#1018), checked against the workspace's lifetime just before it with nothing awaited between: a save can't land after the workspace closed (one under way then fails, and nothing is written). A copy is removed only once another is confirmed, so whatever fails, the earlier watches are left in some file. Each saved watch is checked in full when read; one that isn't valid (or is another workspace's agent's, or over the limit) is kept aside in the file as it was, under `invalid`, and never acted on, and one bad entry doesn't stop the others. At most 500 watches and a 1 MB file, for what Combwork writes as for what it reads, with room for each watch to grow to its longest (fired, with its line cut to 1,000 bytes, and being typed; the cards as last seen aren't saved), so a watch Combwork took can always fire, be typed and end. A new watch that wouldn't fit first moves the entries kept aside to a file of their own (`watches.json.kept-aside-<time>`, created new); if it still wouldn't fit it is refused (409; replacing an agent's watch is always allowed). A file read back too big for that moves its entries kept aside, then its last watches, to such a file, so nothing is lost. The watches were kept in `watches.json` before #1018: it is moved into the database the first time the workspace opens (and kept as `watches.json.imported-<time>`). Only a missing file means no watches then: one that can't be read is an error. A file too big or not JSON is renamed (`watches.json.too-big-<time>`, `.damaged-<time>`) and none are moved in; if it can't be renamed, that is an error and the file is left as it is. A watch or a cancel that can't be saved is reported as failed, and nothing changes. **Followed to its receipt** (#649): a fired watch's line is handed over as a delivery, and the watch saves its id before the delivery service can type it (nothing is handed over if that can't be saved); the watch ends once that delivery is received (fetched with `cw_inbox`, #650: the only receipt), not when its doorbell is typed. A watch read back with a delivery follows it: received while Combwork was closed, it has ended; ended without that, it fires again; offered when Combwork stopped, the delivery is uncertain and offered once more, saying it may repeat. A watch read back from before #649 marked as being typed is handed over once more, saying it may repeat. A save that fails in the background is tried again by the 5-second tick. Keeping within the file's limit is measured watch by watch, each once (#321: making the whole file's text for each watch set aside, and every watch reading its 20 cards from disk at each check, took seconds at 400 watches); one check of the watches reads each card once, whatever the number of watches on it.
  - **While watching** the agent shows **watching** (§6.3) and its pane header says what for ("Waiting for HI-12 → Review", eye icon; short of room it shortens, with the whole in its tooltip); **Cancel Card Watch** in the agent's ⋯ ends it (#977: an inline Cancel before); the agent can cancel its own watch (`cancel: true`). It takes no other work meanwhile: `cw_prompt_agent` is 409 and Start… can't choose it. *Quit when agents finish* waits for it while a card it watches is in Doing or Review with another agent (the work it waits for is going on), and not otherwise. Every status reply says what it waits for: `statusMessage` is the watch's label, and agents have `watching { cards, column, changes, label, limitAt }` in project status, the project list, activity and `/v1/agents/wait` (the short rows: `watching`, the label).
  - **A watch belongs to the conversation that set it** (HI-2197; HB3's stall of 31 Oct: its previous conversation's watch on its merged card fired after its lane ended, its wake couldn't be typed, and it showed as waiting on cards, so Combwork's placement of its next card was refused for 50 minutes). Watches outlive a launch, so a resumed agent is woken. A start that resumes nothing (a lane's or a slot placement's new conversation, `newConversation`, Start Fresh, a handover from another agent, a restart that couldn't resume) ends the agent's earlier watch first, whatever its kind, its wake cancelled by that watch's own id, before anything is launched (`sessions.conversationEnds`, `watches.endConversationWatch`); only the agent's handover to itself keeps it (`keepWatch`). Two guards for an agent's own watch (`watchGuards.ts`): while Combwork is giving the agent a card in a slot (its start, the placement not made yet) a new watch, of any kind, is refused (409: *Combwork is giving you HI-2189 in slot-b: end your turn with no watch…*; `cancel` still works), checked as the watch is written, under the watches' lock (`onWatchPlacing`), so a watch and the start racing can't leave one behind, and a start that leaves its own placement due ends the watch it had, its reply saying so. And an agent's plain number in a watch's cards (`2189`, `"2189"`) that reads as another card's key of its project (2189 is HI-2182's number while HI-2189 is another card) is refused (400), naming both, never remapped; `#2189`, keys, a number no key reads as and scripts' numbers go on, and only cards in the agent's view are named.
  - **A card leaves the watch of an agent whose part in it ended** (#420). A project agent's watch records its part in each card as it begins (`on`): the card's agent, its reviewer, or a reviewer waiting for it to arrive in Review (`awaiting`, a `column: review` watch on another agent's card, and since HI-2487 any watch of a reviewer agent (its workflow role) on another's card but one for its Done: HR1's watch on HI-2444 from its design check, set again after HR2 had started reviewing it, woke it with "in Review" and it started a review of its own; now the card leaves that watch at once, saying who reviews it). A card it has no part in (another agent's card its own depends on) and the Assistant's watches are never released. The card leaves the watch (`releaseOf`) when it is given to another agent (or none) while the watcher had it; another agent reviews it while the watcher reviewed it or awaited it; or the agent an awaiting reviewer waited on is replaced by another. **A blocked card is never released** (#481, Darren's decision: it stays in its lane, paused; the reviewer never drops it): #420 released it too, so a loop moved on while the user decided, but on #468 (9 Oct) the reviewer dropped the card its builder had blocked to ask a question, and when the builder unblocked it and returned it to Review nobody reviewed it (builder waiting for a verdict, reviewer for the next card). The watch now carries on over the block; the card-loop skill says a blocked card is paused, not gone, and the loop doesn't take the next card meanwhile. Watches saved before (with `on[n].blocked`, or a `released` entry `why: 'blocked'`) still load. The watch's only card: the watcher is woken once (`[CW] #354 was reassigned to B4 (your watch on it ended). Your card watch has ended: drop it from your list and carry on with your next card.`). With other cards, it is dropped and told first in the watch's next line (`released`), including the limit's (`… (your watch on it ended). No change on #2 in 2 h: … Drop the first from your list; for the rest, tell the user …`). A watch that had fired but whose line wasn't typed yet (the watcher was busy) checks its cards again as it is delivered, through the same release step (`applyRelease`, under the lock): a card released meanwhile is told as released, not as the change that fired it, and when that change was all it had to tell, the line isn't typed: the watch keeps its other cards and tells the release with its next line. An awaiting reviewer is also released when the card's agent is taken off it (no agent now), and a reviewing watcher when its review is taken from it (stopped, or cleared by someone else; not its own verdict). Each is noted in the card's history as Combwork (`Ended R6 (web)'s watch on it: reassigned to B4`). The card-loop skill: such a wake means drop that card and carry on, without asking. Prompted by #354/#359 moved to another lane while R6 waited on #354 (7 Oct), and #356 blocked mid-lane while R3 waited on it and lane 3 stalled (8 Oct). **Watches that can never fire end** (#1475, seen twice on 22 Oct: HR5 still "waiting for #1422 → Review" hours after its merge, and for #1322 after lane "Override trial" ended merged, so the next lane's `cw_prompt_agent` was refused). Two more reasons in `releaseOf`, for a card the watcher has a part in: `done`, the card reached Done since the watch began and the watch doesn't count that move (`countsDone`: it waits for another column, or for no plain column change); and `laneEnded`, a lane listing the card with the watcher as its builder (for its own card) or reviewer (reviewing or awaiting it) ended or was abandoned since the watch began, with no running lane of its project listing the card with the watcher in that part. The lanes are read once a round, only while some card watch has a part in a card, and a `lanes-changed` event runs the card watches' check too (abandoning a lane writes no card). A watch that fired but whose line isn't handed over yet is checked again with them as it is delivered (HR4's round 1): an arrival in Review of a card whose lane was abandoned meanwhile is told as the lane's end, never as the arrival, and with other cards left it is withdrawn and told with the next line, as #420's releases are. A watch that waits for the card's Done (`countsDone`) and sees it there is told that change, never its lane's end. Its line says there is nothing more to wait for (`[CW] #1322 is in Done (your watch on it ended). Your card watch has ended: there is nothing more to wait for on it. Don't watch it again; end your turn unless you have other work.`; "#1322's lane ended" / "was abandoned"), so the agent goes idle and takes the next lane's prompt with `newConversation`; the history notes it (`the card is in Done`, `its lane ended`, `its lane was abandoned`). Off with the project's **Wake reviewers and builders** (`loopWakes`), as the loop's other wakes, except `done`: **a card in Done ends every card watch on it** (HI-2153, seen 30 Oct: HR2 watched HI-2148 "for completion" after its merge, for a column change that never came, and Archive All skipped the card for that watch until the watch's limit). Whoever watches it (a dependency, the Assistant) and for what, with loop wakes on or off: a watch that counts the move into Done (`countsDone`) is told it as that change; any other is released (`done`), as is one that sees nothing new on a card in Done (a watch saved on it there, or the watcher's own move). **A watch set on a card already in Done or archived answers at once** (`already`, `cardOver`), whatever it waits for, unless it starts from before the card got there (a wake that told it elsewhere, #224; an intent's card, #1639), whose move then fires it; the bounded wait (`/v1/tasks/wait` without `since`) answers at once too. A lane watch's cards beside its lanes (#726, HR1's round 1 and 2 findings; the Assistant's design call): one in Done that the watch doesn't count, or archived, leaves the watch at once **with no notice of its own** (the lanes' own events tell the watcher), the lanes still watched; also after the watch fired and before its line is handed over (its line never names it, and the cards it hands on to the next lane watch are without it); the history still notes a Done one. A move into Done the watch counts is told as that change, as before. One named that is already in Done or archived never joins (the reply's `dropped`). The "(your watch on it ended)" notice is for plain card watches only. An archived card already ended the watch, told as gone.
  - **A builder's own card in Review with unsubmitted commits** (HI-2245; card-loop-follow-up on Haiku, 2/5 after HI-2228: builders saw the card in Review, took the asked change as handed over and ended their turn without `cw_submit` with `followUp: true`). A card watch's reply (`wake: true`, its "Waiting for…" and "Already: …") and `cw_lane next`'s "Carry on with…" say, for each of the caller's cards in Review that it builds, how many commits its line has past the submitted revision (`Workflow.unsubmitted`, the Git platform's `unsubmitted`): "First hand HI-12 over: HI-12's line has 2 commits since its submission (ab30f52); cw_submit with followUp: true, then end your turn: …", in place of "End your turn now" (the watch is registered as ever). Only what is proven: the card's folder (its slot or worktree, or the project folder) there, on the card's line (not another branch, not detached), its HEAD the line's head, the submission strictly an ancestor of it, the committed history only (a dirty tree never counts); in the shared project folder, only the commits on the line now that are attributed to the card (the folder's attribution brought up to date first). Counted up to 100 (past it, "at least 100"). The folder is read again after the history, and the card's cycle, stage, submission, builder and folder after it all: a checkout, reset, submission or return meanwhile drops it. An amend or reset of the submission (not a descendant), another agent, the reviewer or the Assistant: nothing said. Up to 10 cards a reply; nothing kept between replies.
  - **A lane's builder watching its own card while nothing waits on it** (HI-2285; on 1 Nov CB1 committed CL-5's plan, watched CL-5 for a comment and ended its turn: no question to the user, no design step for the reviewer, the card in Doing; watching counted as waiting, and the user found it idle). A card watch (`wake: true`) by an agent on one card alone, that card its own in its **active** lane, where nothing on the card waits on anyone (in Doing, so not submitted; not blocked; no design or follow-up posted for the reviewer's check still open; no For you request open, any asker's): its reply says so in place of "End your turn now" (nothing waits on the card; carry on with its work, or ask: `cw_ask_user`, a design step with `cw_loop_step`, `cw_submit` once ready), and that only watching shows it as stalled. A warning, not a refusal: card-loop lets a builder watch its card for a comment it asked for, which Combwork doesn't track; the watch is registered as ever. A watch with usage beside it says nothing. If the builder keeps only watching (its status `watching`, the watch on that card alone, with no usage, lanes or agents beside it: a watch's info says `usage` when it has some) for 5 minutes since the watch began or the card came into Doing, whichever is later (HI-2445: a watch kept through Review for the verdict isn't idle time in Doing, so a failed verdict doesn't stall the card the moment it sends it back), with the same nothing waiting, the card is **stalled** (the Agent API's `stalled`, a lane watch's `stalled` event): "HB3 only watches HI-12 (6 min), and nothing waits on it: no question for the user, no design step, not submitted.". Main's check only (as a returned or stale card's), not the board's mark. A paused lane's or team's isn't.
  - **A lane card waiting on its dependencies is a state, never a stall** (HI-2618; on 5 Nov HB6's HI-2616 was next in its lane while the three cards it depends on were still being built in other lanes, and the lane-next stall reported it 29 times in 50 minutes). The cause was a race: each lane-start look (`checkLaneStarts`) cleared its workspace's start waits and set them again only after its awaits, so a lane watch or a card read in between saw the card waiting on nothing (its stall mark flipping, a notice and a lane watch `stalled` each time). Now:
    - **A look's waits are published whole**: built aside and put in place in one synchronous step, only by a complete look still current. Current means the same open of its workspace (`WorkspaceService.openGeneration`, which changes as it closes and as it opens, so a close and reopen by the same service is another open), the same folder, and no later look begun. A failed or overtaken look leaves the last complete look's waits in place.
    - **From the board**: a running lane's due card (its first card not Done, in Todo, with `blockedBy`) has `LaneInfo.dueDeps` where Combwork waits for its dependencies (the rules off, where a lane is bookkeeping; on, only under its start rule `start.dependenciesIntegrated`, else Combwork starts it anyway). It gives the ones not Done by key (`open`, in `blockedBy` order) and, once none is, when the last went Done (`readyAt`, from its history). The lane's status says it as `startWait`/`dependencies` with `waitingOn` (every key; *HI-2616 waits to start: it waits for HI-2610, HI-2611 and HI-2612 to merge*), before the lane-start look's own wait, so it doesn't depend on that look having run. The lane-next stall (`laneNextWaitReason`) is null while one is open, whatever the status says, and once none is it counts from `max(previous card's Done, readyAt)`: *the last of the cards it depends on went Done 16 min ago*.
    - **An episode kept with the lane** (`LaneRecord.depEpisode`, in its row's `extra`, changed only under the lanes' lock with the look's fence checked inside): `waiting` once Combwork sees the card due with one open (a new id each time, so a reopened dependency begins another), then `pending` once none is (the claim), then `sent`. With the rules on there is no readiness wake: Combwork's own start of the card (HI-2129) is the one task, so the claim goes straight to `sent`. With the rules off nothing starts it, so its builder is owed one readiness wake (*HI-2616's dependencies are Done (HI-2610, HI-2611, HI-2612): it is your lane's next card. Start it now*, a card event). It is made with `createDeliveryOnce`, whose receipt (`store_meta` `once:lane-deps:<lane>#<card>#<episode>`) is checked and written in the deliveries' own save transaction. So a retry after any crash (claimed and nothing enqueued; enqueued and not checkpointed; received, acked and pruned since) makes no second, and two makings at once make one. The checkpoint `sent` is recoverable; the delivery's `received`/`ended` callbacks also set it, and nothing depends on them. Its source (`lane-deps`) refresh cancels a queued wake once it isn't due: the lane not running, another builder, the episode changed or a dependency open again, the rules on, the card started or moved. Receipts are never dropped as an episode ends (a late producer from another process would make it again); the deliveries prune them after 30 days, and an obligation older than 29 days is given up, never retried.
  - **A card waiting on purpose** (HI-2618; on 5 Nov HB3 held HI-2590 for a quiet window, waiting for the Assistant's go, and was reported stalled four times). A card in Doing can be marked waiting with a reason: `TaskCard.waitingFor` (`{ reason, by, at }`, in the card's row `extra`), set by `cw_update_task` / `PATCH /v1/tasks/{n}` `waitingFor` (1–500 characters; `''` or `null` clears it), the card dialog's **Waiting** box and its menu's **Mark as Waiting…** / **Clear Waiting**. Only the card's own agent, the user and the Assistant (and a script with the workspace token) may set or clear it: another project agent is refused (`403`), so it can't silence someone else's card. Setting it on a card not in Doing is `409`. While it is set, `cardStall` is null for the card (every reason: the board's Stalled mark, lane watches' `stalled`, the Agent API's `stalled`, the Assistant's reading). Nothing is stopped: its agent keeps running and the card its slot. It is cleared, with a history line (*No longer waiting*), by any move out of Doing, in the same locked write as the move (`updateTaskAs`: submit, put back, a verdict, the user's move). `cw_list_tasks` rows say *waiting: …*. The Assistant's marks are undone as any card field (§16.14, `CARD_FIELDS`): recorded whole (`reason`, `by`, `at`) and put back whole, a move out of Doing that cleared one recording it too, so undoing that move puts back the card in Doing and the mark as it was; one changed since is kept. With the rules off, a builder owed its readiness wake that is refused for now (its inbox full, say) is retried by the lane-start looks its status and deliveries changes and the retry tick bring (`setDepWakeOwed`), until it is made.
  - **Without `wake`**, the call waits in place (event-driven) up to `timeoutSeconds` (default 300, at most 840, under the CLIs' tool timeouts) and replies with each change (the card, its column, who changed it last, its latest comment's author and first line) or no change, with a `since` token to pass to the next wait so nothing between them is missed. It reads the cards as the caller sees them (a card that leaves its view is gone), listens for board changes before its first check (so none falls between), checks again after a change that came during a check, and ends (409) if its workspace closes. At most two such waits per caller at once (429).
  - **The `card-loop` skill** (agents) runs a builder and a reviewer through a list of cards in turn with these watches: the builder sends a card to Review and watches for a verdict or a move into Passed; the reviewer watches for a card arriving in Review and, after failing it, for its return, and moves a card that passes to Passed with its verdict (#170; once the builder has merged its work, it moves its Passed cards to Done); the builder moves a failed card to Doing while it fixes it, then back to Review (a move to Review without leaving it returns it too, #214). Each starts its watch *before* the step that lets the other act, so a fast reply isn't missed. It counts rounds, a round being one build and its review (round 1 is the first build and review), and asks the user when the last round's review fails (5 rounds by default), and tells the user when a wait limit passes. A finding that comes back is marked recurring in the failed verdict and is another round, not a reason to stop early; one the builder disputes is a design question and stops the loop to ask (#163). **Asking the user** is the same for either side, and for any agent with a question only the user can answer (card-loop, review-agent-work, work-on-card; #840): it sets the card's `blocked` to the question and tells the user (`cw_notify`), never only a comment, since a lane watch wakes on a card becoming blocked and never on a comment (a reviewer's question left as a comment on #805 sat unseen for over an hour); once Combwork tells it of the user's decision, it clears `blocked` and carries on. A builder's merge step at the lane's end that needs the user (a commit or merge its CLI or a permission check refuses, a conflict it can't settle) is asked the same way, on the last card (#869): with every card passed nothing else shows the lane waiting.
  - **Card-loop defaults** (#412, Darren's decision: Rounds 10 and Wait 6h, set per workspace, a project can override, a prompt's own values win). Since HI-1766 they are workflow options, resolved Combwork → workspace → project (§16.6.7); what follows is the 0.9 to pre-1.0 design they replaced. **Settings → Workspace → Card loop rounds** and **Card loop wait** (`workspace.loopRounds`, `workspace.loopWaitHours`: whole numbers, 1–50 and 1–24 hours) are the workspace's own, kept in its `workspace.json` (`loops: { rounds, waitHours }`, absent: 10 and 6). They are the first settings with a value per workspace: the catalog's `settingValue`/`settingDefault`/`settingPatch` take the workspace's config for scope `workspace` (`{ workspace: { … } }`, saved by `WorkspaceService.setLoops`, which checks the range; the window through `workspace:setLoops`, the settings tools through `applySetting`, so the Assistant reads and, with Change settings, changes them). **Project Settings → Card loops → Rounds** and **Wait (hours)** (`project.loopRounds`, `project.loopWaitHours`, null inherits) override them for a project. `loopDefaults(ws, project)` (`shared/lanes.ts`) resolves them; a lane started without rounds or a wait (`startLane`) takes them, so the card-loop skill gives `cw_lane start` only the values its request named and uses the lane's from the reply (10 and 6 hours with no lane); the reviewer's `join` reply has the lane's too. coordinate-agents briefs a lane with rounds and a wait only when the user gave them. A prompt's values always win; a change applies to lanes started afterwards.
  - **Loop wakes** (#405, Darren's decision: on by default for cards with a reviewer, with a per-project opt-out). The loop only worked if every agent remembered its card watch; Combwork knows each card's agent and reviewer, so it delivers the two routine handoffs itself (`main/loopWakes.ts`). Each **handoff** is a durable `wake` action (§16.4.5) written with the fact that causes it, in the change's transaction (#1266: the recorder for the board's changes, the runtime for its own), and run by the actions worker once the change commits; there is no other path, so nothing wakes twice: the card moved or returned into Review (`review`, the reviewer's), a review's verdict (`verdict`), the card moved into Passed or Done not by a verdict (`approved`, `done`), a reviewer's request mid-review (`request`, #912: at once, its text in the line, which no card watch stands in for; a plain comment, no move or verdict, by a running lane's reviewer on its card in Review that it hasn't started reviewing counts as one too, #1410: "waiting for #12 first", with the same history line, and a comment once its review has started stays a comment), and the runtime's own notes (`note`: a pass gone stale, the user's answer), the builder's. **The builder's reply** (`reply`, HI-2302) is its reviewer's: a plain comment (no move or verdict) by the card's agent on its card in Review, after the card's loop reviewer commented on it in that round (since its latest arrival in Review, return for review or follow-up), writes the history line *Replied to the reviewer: "…"* and wakes that reviewer with its text, the mirror of #1410; a watch that counts loop steps tells it instead, it is due until the reviewer acts on the card or the card leaves Review, and it is off with the project's loop wakes. Before, a builder's answer to its reviewer's question reached nobody (PE-39). Both the request and the reply are read from a comment however it is written (HI-2428): a change with a comment, or a comment alone (`cw_update_task` with only a comment, the window's comment box), so a builder's later plain comment wakes its pool or lane reviewer too, watch or not; on HI-2410 a comment alone was written past both and a pool reviewer slept for seven hours after its builder's two answers. Only a card in a loop (a running lane with a reviewer, or an agent has reviewed it) gets the actions at all. A **decision** recorded on a card in a loop wakes its builder, and its reviewer while it is in Review or Passed (`wakeOnDecision`, one action per agent; S5, closing #587's manual step): the decision line (below), now also to an agent that is watching rather than waiting for the user. Each wake's delivery carries its action's id, so an action run again (a restart, another Combwork) makes none. A card's **reviewer** is the reviewer of a running lane (active or paused) with the card, else the project agent that last started reviewing it (its board name in the history); a card with neither has no wakes, so a solo user never sees one. A `review` handoff wakes the reviewer, a `verdict` the card's agent (its builder); never the agent that made the change, nor a builder reviewing its own card; never an agent whose own card watch tells it of that change (`watchCovers`, with the card's column: a watch on the card counting a move into Review; one counting a verdict, or a move into the column the verdict left the card in, so a watch for Passed alone stands in for a passing verdict that moved the card there but not for a failed one, which leaves it in Review; or one that has fired with it), checked when queued, again before typing and before each piece. **Whose wake it is is worked out again as it is delivered** (`targetOf`, from the lane and the card then): a lane whose reviewer changed while the wake waited gives it to the new reviewer, and one left with no reviewer drops it; a change to its own card, the lanes holding it or its project's settings while it is checked or typed stops it, and it is worked out again on the next try. Unrelated board traffic does not interrupt its doorbell (HI-2486): offers and inbox hand-outs use the same per-card state key; only when that key cannot be read does the strict board-change counter stand in. Off when the project's workflow option **Wake reviewers and builders** (Card loops, `loopWakes`) is off: inherited Combwork → workspace → project since HI-1766 (§16.6.7; before it, `project.json`'s own `loopWakes: false`, not inherited). The line is a card watch's, with its own tail (`loopWakeLine`: `[CW] #12 (B1's card) is in Review. You review this card in its loop: carry on with it (cw_read_task with latestComment for the comment in full).`; the builder's: `… is in Review: R1 (web) failed it; latest comment by …. This is your card in its loop: carry on (…)`), made from the card as it is when it is offered or read. It is a delivery (#649: a card event), made at once (#652: no settle of its own; what lands with the handoff is in it, since it is made again from the card just before it is offered or read) and given as a wake is (its doorbell only while the agent is idle, the user not typing, no line of Combwork's waiting there, no fired watch of the agent's going first, one line at a time per agent, checked as taken, #376; a busy agent told at its next tool call, #650); until then it waits, saved, the latest per agent and card (made again from a newer handoff; a day each), tried on the agent's next idle status and every 5 s, and made again from the card just before each offer. It is dropped once it has nothing to tell, judged by what the card's history has since the handoff's entry (`historySince`): a reviewer's when the card has left Review or that round has been reviewed (a review started or a verdict given since, also one that has ended: a round reviewed and failed while the reviewer was busy is the builder's now); a builder's when the card is another agent's, the builder has acted on it since the verdict, or another round has started; the user's answer only once it is read, or its card is Done with no lane running (HI-1721: HB2 submitted its next round on HI-1694 before reading Darren's answer, which was dropped as acted on). A later arrival queues a wake of its own. A watch's line telling the handoff's own entry stands in for its wake (#578), never for a `note` or the user's answer (HI-1721): no watch's line says what they say, and their anchor is only the card's latest entry when they were made (the merge queue's return writes none of its own), which a watch begun after them has read; on 26 Oct HB2's return from the queue on HI-1694 was dropped as "told", and HB2 watched for Done for three hours while the card waited for it in Doing. **A watch for another column on one's own returned card** (HI-1721, `tellReturned`): when a builder begins a card watch on its own card in Doing that the merge queue returned to it (`queueReturnOf`: the last entry failed and nothing submitted since), for any column but Doing, it is told of the return at once, from the card's state as it is (the return's own text, a `note` loop wake, the latest per card), its watch carrying on. Each received (read with `cw_inbox`) is noted in the card's history as Combwork (`Woke R1 (web) to review it (a loop wake)`, `Woke B1 (web) with its verdict (a loop wake)`). The card-loop skill says Combwork may wake the agent itself, and that watches stay how it waits.
  - **Lanes** (#483). A loop is registered as a **lane**, so Combwork knows the loops it runs: `cw_lane` / `/v1/lanes` (Agent API §12), kept in the workspace's database (`.combwork/combwork.db`, a row each, #1018; moved in from `lanes.json` the first time) (`main/lanes.ts`, logic in `shared/lanes.ts`; read and written whole under the lanes' lock). The builder's card-loop starts it (`start`: the cards in order, the reviewer, rounds, wait in minutes, an optional name), the reviewer's joins it by the builder's name (`join`: with its cards, only a running lane sharing one; with none such it starts one from its cards as the builder's start would, which that start then updates), and the Assistant (Control agents, through `assistantChange`) or a script can start one for any builder. **One running lane per builder:** a start sharing a card with its running lane updates it in place (resumed, a card added, the order changed; a reviewer given replaces the old one), one sharing none ends it (ended when it has no card left to do, every one Passed, Done or gone, since it only waits for its merge; else abandoned). **Lifecycle:** `active`; `paused` while it waits for the user, read from the board, not kept: its first card not in Passed or Done is blocked and no other is in Doing or Review (#512: a builder that moved on to the next card while one waits for the user is working). Its current card is the one being worked: the first in Doing that isn't blocked, else the first in Review, else the first unfinished (`currentCard` in `shared/laneBar.ts`); `ended` once every card is Done (Combwork notices on the board's next change) or when ended after the merge (with its merge commit); `abandoned` when its builder or reviewer is removed from the project (`removeAgent`, and found on the next look if removed while Combwork was closed), or when ended unmerged. An ended or abandoned lane keeps its cards as they were when it ended (`frozen` in the file, #512) and reads them from there, never from the board: a card another lane has taken on shows only in that one. Without that record (a lane ended before #512, or one that doesn't read back) its cards are `unrecorded`: not known, with no current card, and never read from the board. A stopped agent doesn't abandon its lane: quitting, restarts and setting changes stop agents too. Ended lanes are listed until their builder starts another or for an hour, and kept a day (at most 200). **Lean replies:** a line per lane (`B1 / R1 (web) lanes and loops: active, on #405; #483 Passed, #405 Review r2, #412 Todo; rounds 10, wait 6 h. lane-3fa2c1`). **Scale-down:** a lane is bookkeeping, never a gate. Nothing refuses or waits on one; a solo agent on a card (work-on-card) makes none; the skill carries on if the tool is missing or a call fails; an unknown reviewer leaves the lane without one rather than refusing. The window gets `lanes:list` and `lanes-changed` (the listed lanes with each card's column, blocked reason, round and review, sent when a lane or one of its cards changes); the Agent API's stream sends `lanes-changed` with the workspace only.
- **Waiting on lanes** (#531). A coordinator follows card loops, not cards: on 10 Oct the Assistant, with seven lanes and about 25 open cards, swapped cards in and out of its 20-card watch on every wake, missed one (#390 sat in Review unreviewed), and was woken by every column move, most of which needed nothing. `cw_wait_for_tasks` / `POST /v1/tasks/wait` with `lanes` (lane ids, or `["all"]`) and `wake: true` (an agent or the Assistant) starts a **lane watch** instead of a card watch (`shared/laneWatch.ts`, `registerLaneWatch` and `evaluateLanes` in `main/watches.ts`): the agent's one watch, kept in `watches.json` like the others (`lanes`, and `laneMarks`: each lane as last measured, its state, whether its merge is due, and each card's column, blocked, stalled, and latest failed and passed verdict times), with no cards and no card limit. `"all"` follows every running lane in the watcher's view (a project agent: its project's; the Assistant: all), lanes started later too, and each lane's cards as the lane goes on (cards added included). It counts only **events**, `events` narrowing or widening them: `failed` (a review failed), `blocked` (a card became blocked: a question for the user), `stalled` (a card became stalled, by the board's own reasons, `cardStall` in `main/cardStall.ts`, shared with the Agent API's `stalled`: nobody on a Doing card (its agent removed or not running; one whose start is under way, HI-1976, a Start giving it the card, its slot being prepared and its builder placed there or its session spawning, is starting, not stalled, for at most 10 minutes (`agentStarts.ts`); one whose start failed is stalled with why, "HB5's start failed: Combwork couldn't get slot-g ready: …", from a slot not prepared, a placement that failed three tries or the CLI exiting before its session started; the window's board reads the same start state, HI-1977: each agent of a ProjectInfo carries `start`, `{ starting: true }` or `{ failed }` (`withAgentStarts`), told to the window at once with each change (`agent-start`) and read again, a change counted (`startSeq`) so a read made before it and arriving after doesn't undo it, and its Stalled mark says the failure in the window's language, *HB5's start failed: …*, the reason as given), a loop agent with no watch, #376, a reviewer watching but not reviewing, #521; a card the merge queue returned, in Doing and unchanged for 15 minutes since, its builder idle or only watching it, HI-1721, `returnedWaitReason`: "HI-1694 came back from the merge queue 16 min ago; HB2 is only watching it, not fixing it."; a running lane's next card not started, HI-1741, `laneNextWaitReason`: in Todo, not blocked, every card before it in the lane Done, the last of them for 15 minutes, its builder idle, only watching or not running (one queued to resume isn't), never in a paused lane: "HI-1735 is the lane's next card: HI-1727 went Done 23 min ago, and HB3 is idle without starting it." (HB3 read HI-1727's Done and ended its turn, and its lane sat for two hours); or a lane's merge, #869: every card passed and none blocked, its builder not running or idle with no background task and no place at the merge slot for 10 minutes since the later of its cards' last change and its own, `mergeStallReason`, told once as "its merge is stalled" with why: on 14 Oct lane G's builder had its commit refused, told the user and stopped, and nothing woke the Assistant for two hours), `merge-due` (every card passed or done, one not yet merged), `unblocked` (a card's block lifted, #922, #1272: the user OK'd what it waited for in the agent's pane), `reblocked` (#1475, default: a card blocked when last measured and still blocked, whose blocked reason changed (a new "Blocked:" history entry) or whose agent commented since, `blockNewsAt` as the card mark's `r`, told as "#1432 is still blocked, with news" with its reason: on 22 and 23 Oct a builder re-shot for the Assistant's OK, commented and changed the reason, and the Assistant's lane watch stayed asleep for up to 2 h; a mark saved before has no `r` and never fires it, and a fresh block is told as `blocked`), `ended` (with the lane's merge commit when its end names one, #1270), `abandoned` (the default), `paused-user` (HI-1991: always counted, whatever `events` says, `readLaneCondition` and `registerLaneWatch` adding it: a new request for the user on a running lane's card, an agent's `cw_ask_user` question or Combwork's own, the card mark's `q` the newest open request's time from For you's items (`forYouOfCards`), told as "HI-12 waits for the user (HB6 asks): …" with its first line, and the tail saying to tell the user; twice a builder's question sat under For you about 20 minutes, its builder not waiting at a prompt so `waiting` never fired, and the Assistant having dropped `paused`, which also fired on every merge; a mark saved before has no `q` and never fires it), and `passed`, `moved` (any column change), `paused-merge` (a lane paused for a card passed but not merged, or merging; `paused`, its name before HI-1991, is read as it) when asked. The user's prompt to a lane's agent from its pane (with Settings → Assistant → Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent on) reaches the Assistant as a line of its own with its first line, the lane watch going on (#1099, #922). Plain moves stay quiet. While nothing that counts happens each lane's mark moves on to now, so a card blocked again after an unblock counts; a lane that starts after an `"all"` watch began, and a card added to a lane it follows, start from an empty mark (a block or stall they come with is told once, and verdicts since the watch began). A watch on `"all"` keeps a lane it follows in view until that lane's end has been told, also across a wake: a lane that ends or is abandoned between a wake and the watch after it is told by that watch. Once a watch fires, its marks stay where they were until its line is handed over, and the line is worked out again then (`laneRound`), so events that land meanwhile are told in the same line; the marks become what that line told once the agent has read it (#649). One line tells every lane's events (`laneWakeLine`, within the wake size: `[CW] Lane B1 / R1 (greetings): #12 failed review (R1 (alpha)) | Lane B2 / R2: #15 is blocked: "Which icon?". Your lane watch has ended: …`; reasons, then labels, then all but each lane's events give way). A watch after a wake starts each lane from what that wake told (`wokeLanes`: its marks, and when its line was made), so an event in between fires it at once; and what is new is measured from when that line was made (`laneSince`), not from the new watch: a card added to a lane or a lane started in between (also one already ended or abandoned) starts from an empty mark, so its verdicts, block, stall or end are told once. Checked on board changes, `lanes-changed`, agents' status changes (debounced) and every 30 s (a stall that comes with time). Its label is "Waiting on all running lanes" / "Waiting on 3 lanes" / one lane by its **name** (HI-2522: Darren read WR1's "Waiting on lane lane-1d1c05" as a commit id): "Waiting on lane combwork screenshots", with its builder when another lane in the watcher's view has the same name ("Waiting on WB1's lane combwork screenshots"), and as "Waiting on WB1's lane" when it has none; the watch keeps each named lane's name and builder as they were when it began (`laneTitles`); one saved before HI-2522 takes them from the lanes as they are when it is read back (and keeps them), and a lane no longer listed is "a lane": never its id. A wake line too long to tell in full shortens each lane to its name ("B1 / R1" for one with none), never its id; its limit line says to check them (`cw_lane list`). `cw_lane start` from the Assistant nudges it to watch the lanes unless a lane watch on `"all"` (or that lane) runs, and its card wakes while lanes run end with the lanes-running tail, now pointing at a lane watch; run-lanes and coordinate-agents use one. **An ended lane is the answer at once** (HI-2521: WR1 watched its lane 2 s after it ended, merged, and sat watching it for its 6 h limit): a watch naming a lane that has ended or been abandoned starts none, ends the caller's watch before it, and replies with each such lane's end (`lanesAlready`: "Lane WB1 / WR1 (screenshots): ended: merged at 47a3d54c0ffe"). A watch naming lanes always counts their end, whatever its `events`, and one ending while the watch is being set up is told by the check the watch makes once in place.
- **Lanes, the cards beside them and agents waiting, in one watch** (#726). On 13 Oct the release card #720 was in no lane, so HB6 waited about 45 minutes for Darren's push before the Assistant noticed, and only because another lane's merge came due: a session has one watch, and a lane watch saw only lane cards. A lane watch now takes `cards` too (up to 20, each in the caller's view, else `404`): cards beside its lanes, kept in the same record's `cond` with their `marks` and `seen` and checked as a card watch checks its cards (`check`, from what a wake told about them, `changes` defaulting to comment, column and verdict), a card becoming blocked counting too (`blocked` on the condition: a `Blocked:` entry in its history since, and still blocked). One line tells each lane's events, then each card that changed (as a card wake tells it, with why it is blocked) and each agent waiting (`laneWakeLine`). A later lane watch keeps the last lane watch's cards (the one it replaces, or the one whose wake was read: `wokeLanes`), less those since done or gone, unless it names its own (`[]` for none); its reply says which (`cards`: `now`, `kept`, `replaced`, `dropped`), and its label names them ("Waiting on all running lanes and #720"). A new default event, `waiting`: an agent of the projects it follows (the watcher's view; named lanes: their projects; never itself) starting to wait for the user, the status Combwork shows as waiting (a permission prompt or a question in its pane). Each start is recorded as it happens (`waitStarts`, numbered on the events' clock, in memory); a watch counts those after its `waitSeq` whose agent still waits in the same launch (a wait answered at once has nothing to tell), so a wait is told once, not on every refresh. The line names the agent, its card (its Doing card, else the one it reviews) and what it asks when Combwork knows (the status message), and its tail says to tell the user and never answer for them. Like the lanes' marks, `waitSeq` moves on while nothing counts, stays put once the watch fires, and becomes what the line told once it is read; a watch after a wake starts from there. A fired lane watch whose line has nothing left to tell when it is handed over (the wait answered, the block lifted) isn't given, and waits on. Opt out with `events`. coordinate-agents and run-lanes put a release or one-off card in the lane watch as `cards`, and say the `waiting` event means telling the user; the lanes-running tail on the Assistant's card wakes says so too.
- **Agents beside the lanes, and what a swapped watch drops** (HI-1987). On 28 Oct the Tools Assistant, following LB2's build (on no card), replaced its lane watch with an agent watch (taking it that it could have one watch at a time), and nothing would have told it of LB1's lane meanwhile. A lane watch now takes `agents` too (`{ project, agent }`, as `cw_wait_for_agents` names them; never itself), followed as an agent watch follows them, in the same record (`agents`, `agentMarks`): a wake when one finishes its turn (through its background tasks), waits for the user or stops, told in the lane watch's line after its lanes, cards and waits (`[CW] Lane B1 / R1: #12 failed review (R1 (alpha)) | LB2 (tools) finished: "…". Your lane watch has ended: …`). The user's replies to them reach the Assistant on their own (#1099), as for a lane's agents. One not working when the watch starts isn't followed: the reply gives its state (`agents.already`). Each is one-off work, followed until a wake tells it: a later lane watch keeps the last one's agents (the one it replaces, or those its wake didn't tell: `wokeLanes`) unless it names its own (`[]` for none), the reply saying so (`agents`: `now`, `kept`, `already`), and the label names them ("Waiting on all running lanes and #720, LB2"). `agents` without `lanes` is `400` (an agent watch is `cw_wait_for_agents`). And a card or agent watch that replaces a lane watch, or follows a lane wake with no lane watch since, while lanes it followed still run, says so in its reply (`lanesLeft`, the lanes' builders: "This replaces your lane watch: 2 running lanes (LB1, LB2) are no longer followed. To follow them as well, watch them with this instead: cw_wait_for_tasks with lanes, and agents or cards."); with no such lane running, nothing is added. The descriptions and skills add no rule for it: the watch takes the work, and the reply is where the mistake is made.
- **Waiting on agents** (#416). Work without a card (a release step, an installer build, a push and its CI, a one-off prompt) is waited on with an **agent watch**: `cw_wait_for_agents` / `POST /v1/agents/wait` with `wake: true` (an agent or the Assistant; not scripts) answers at once and Combwork gives the caller a wake (a delivery it reads with `cw_inbox`, rung by the doorbell, #650) when a watched agent **finishes its turn** (through its background tasks unless `ignoreBackground`), **waits for the user** (a question, a permission prompt, a sign-in) or **stops** (or is in error), naming every agent that did, with the start of its latest reply as its turn's end reported it: `[CW] B6 (web) finished: "The installer for Reinstall 12 is built…". Your agent watch has ended: carry on (cw_agent_activity for more).` Before this, the Assistant polled `cw_wait_for_agents` in calls under 300 s (Claude Code moves longer tool calls to the background): a dozen wake-ups for one 0.4.0 test run.
  - **The same watches.** An agent watch is a watch record in `watches.json` that follows agents (`agents`, each one's launch, prompts taken and whether a typed prompt was pending when it began) instead of cards; it is the agent's one watch (a card watch replaces it and it replaces one, the reply naming the card watch it replaced), checked on every status change and on the watches' tick, settled, handed over as a delivery (only while the watcher is idle and the user isn't typing there; its doorbell gets #376's Enter again once if not taken) and ended once the watcher has read it, limited (`limitMinutes`, default 120: `[CW] B6 is still working after 2 h: your agent watch has ended. Check on it (cw_agent_activity) and watch again, or tell the user (cw_notify) if it seems stuck.`), kept across restarts and cancelled (`cancel: true`, the pane's **Cancel**) as card watches are. The watcher shows **watching** with the label "Waiting for B6 to finish" (`watching.agents` in status replies). What it tells comes from each agent's **events**: Combwork records every agent's events: waiting for the user, a stop or an error, and the end of a turn under way, one seen working (or on its background tasks) in that launch since the last turn ended (finished, interrupted, or into background tasks; a launch becoming ready, also after a startup question such as folder trust or a refused sign-in, ran no turn and isn't one) (the last 8 each, numbered from the clock, whether or not anyone watches it yet: `noteAgentStatus`), and a line is made, again just before it is handed over, from each watched agent's latest event since the watch began, so one that finished and was given work again meanwhile is still told ("… finished: \"…\" (working again now)"), with any that finished since. A watch started after a wake starts each agent from the event that wake told (`wokeAgents`, as `woke` for cards), so an event in between (an agent that finished and took new work while the watcher read its wake) fires it at once; one already told isn't told again. Agents still not working when it is asked for are the answer at once (below). Events aren't kept across a restart: a watch read back is checked against the agents as they are.
  - **What counts as working**: `working`, `starting`, `background` (unless `ignoreBackground`), or a prompt Combwork typed in the last 30 s that its CLI hasn't taken yet (`SessionManager.agentNow`: the agent was just given a task), also for the bounded wait, so a wait right after `cw_prompt_agent` waits for that task. A launch given its task on its command line (`cw_start_agent` or `cw_add_agent` with a prompt, `cw_prompt_agent` with `newConversation`, a card's Start) counts the same until its CLI takes that task (#712): the CLI is ready at its SessionStart and submits the task only after, and a wait in between was answered "ready" before the task began; at most 30 s after it became ready. Nor does Combwork type a line of its own (a doorbell, a wake) into it in that gap (#721): typed there, the line went first and the task's prompt was taken for the line's (the fake Claude Code merged them into one prompt), so the message waits until the task is taken. That gap is timed from when the launch first became ready (`launchReadyAt`), and also counts while a watch that outlived the agent's last launch shows that ready as watching, or as finished once the watch ends. An agent not working when the watch is asked for is the answer at once (`Already: B6 (web) is idle: "…"`) and no watch starts, as for a card already in the column; a prompt that was pending and is never taken is told as such ("its CLI hasn't taken the prompt it was given"). Without `agents`, every agent working now (the caller excepted); never the caller itself (400), at most 32 (a project's most, 24, and more, #562).
  - **The user's replies** (#418). The Assistant's watches (never an agent's) are also told when the user sends an agent a prompt from its pane: an agent watch on that agent, a card watch on a card that agent has or reviews (`card.agent`, `card.review.agent`), in the same line as other changes (`User replied to B1 on #399: "C, the honeycomb cell"`, `… to B1 (web): …`; the user is named by **Settings → General → Your name** (#426: `general.userName`, "User" by default and when empty, made one line of at most 40 characters by `userNameOf`), which goes into the Assistant's context, so it is the user's to set). It is the user's when the CLI reports the prompt taken (UserPromptSubmit, with its text: `HookEvent` prompt `text`; Codex's answers to its questions without their tag) within 15 s of the user's own Enter in that pane, and later than any line Combwork typed there (`SessionManager.noteUserReply`); slash commands and the Assistant's own pane aren't, nor is a turn the CLI starts by itself (HI-2410: Claude Code's wake when a background task ends sends a prompt hook with the same fields as the user's, only its text, `<task-notification>…`, tells it apart, so the adapter marks a prompt whose text matches the advanced pattern `claude-code.prompt.cliTurn` as the CLI's own, `HookEvent` prompt `cli`: still a turn, never a reply, whatever Enter the user pressed before it, such as one answering a permission dialog; Codex and Copilot start no turn by themselves). Kept on the events' clock (`noteUserReply` in watches.ts, the last 200, first line to 120 characters), and counted from what the watcher's last wake told (`replySeq`, `wokeReplies`), so one is told once. **When no watch of its own tells it now** (#1099: a reply waited for the Assistant's next watch, often turns later, since its watch ends at each wake and an agent watch on an idle agent is answered at once with none started; a lane watch tells no replies): a reply to an agent the Assistant follows is given to it at once, as a wake of its own (`[CW] Darren replied to HB2 (web): "go ahead.".`, a `card-event` delivery from Combwork, source `reply`), and no watch tells it again. It follows an agent that a watch of its own covers now, or its last wakes told it about: an agent watch on it (`wokeAgents`, also an answer at once), a card watch on a card it has or reviews (`woke`), a lane watch with a running lane it builds or reviews. The watches are checked first: one that tells it picks it for its line, as before; what none picked (none covers it, or the one that does had made its line already) is given on its own. Each reply has one owner, claimed at once by whichever picks it first (`Reply.owner`: a watch's `replyTo`, or the direct path after its lookup; rolled back if its delivery can't be saved, and left to the watches then), so it is told once. Turned off, such a wake not read yet is cancelled too. In a card watch's line each reply is told once (with the watched cards its agent has or reviews), first, and fitted with the card changes within the line's size (`cardWakeLine`: what was said gives way first, then whose and the verdicts; the end always stays), and only a reply the line names counts as told. An agent watch's line too long for each in full says whom the user replied to and which agents changed, by name, else by count (`Darren replied to 12 watched agents; 3 watched agents changed`): the user's replies are always told as theirs (`agentWakeLine`). **Settings → Assistant → Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent** (`assistant.tellReplies`, default on) off: none is kept or told, also a reply already waiting to be typed in a wake (`revokeReplies`, and the setting is checked again whenever a reply is picked, and before every piece of a wake that tells one is typed and before its Enter: also when it was turned off and on again in between (each revocation raises a generation the wake was made under: `replyGeneration`), what was typed is cleared, the wake is dropped without counting anything as told, and the watch fires again on whatever else changed, without the reply, or waits on); turned on again, none comes back. The Assistant may read it, not change it (its own permissions). The coordinate-agents skill: a reply that decides something is recorded on the card as a decision, not asked again.
  - **Who may watch whom.** Any agent of the workspace's projects (never the Assistant), as the bounded wait has always allowed: agents' status is open to every caller. Project agents now have `cw_wait_for_agents` too (it left the Assistant-only tools), but a project agent's line leaves out the reply of another project's agent (`shownTo`), whose conversation holds that project's cards, as its activity is closed to it. The `coordinate-agents` skill prefers an agent watch to polling for card-less waits.
- **Who may do what.** The user does everything from Combwork.
