## 7. Skills and MCP

### 7.1 Skill levels

Skills have no on/off switches: every skill an agent can see is always available. Combwork lists them by where they come from.

| Level (label) | Location | Loaded by | In Combwork |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Combwork** | `<Workspace>/.combwork/skills/`, copied into `<Project>/.combwork/launch-<agent>/plugin/skills/` (Claude Code) or `<agent folder>/.agents/skills/cw-<name>` (Codex) | Its audience (`metadata.audience`): project agents (every agent, every provider; the default), the Assistant, or both | Skills view: add, add from file, edit, delete; bundled ones restore/revert |
| **Local (User Managed)** | `<Project>/.claude/skills/` (Claude Code), `<Project>/.agents/skills/` (Codex), project root only | That provider's agents in the project | Project Skills tab: add, add from file, edit, delete |
| **User** (`machine`) | `~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.codex/skills/` | That provider's agents everywhere | Project Skills tab: view only |
| **Plugin** | Installed Claude Code plugins | Claude Code agents | Project Skills tab: view only |

- **Deleting from lists** (skills, MCP servers, shared notes, modes, sessions): a bin on the item's row that shows on hover, and another in the top bar of the open item. Rename uses a tag icon everywhere (sessions, notes, files).
- **Skills view** (activity bar): the workspace's Combwork skills only, under a warning, "Warning: Editing these skills may change agent behaviour in Combwork" (`CombworkSkillsWarning`), shown again above the editor while a Combwork skill is edited there (not in preview, nor in a project's tab, where Combwork skills are view only). **Project → Skills**: what the project's agents get: Combwork skills first, in a group that starts open (its count beside it; a note under them counts those for the Assistant alone, which aren't listed, and links to the Skills view) (view, and **Edit in workspace**, which opens the Skills view with the skill in edit mode; if it no longer exists, the view says so), then one turned-on provider's skills, picked from a dropdown (each with its count), in a group that starts folded: Local, User, Plugins (#118; Combwork open and the provider folded by Darren's decision of 5 Oct). The dropdown starts on the project's default provider; the last choice, and whether each group was left open, are remembered per project (`config.json` `ui.skillsProvider` and `ui.skillsFold`, by project path; the newest 200 projects). Each change is saved as that one project's (`ui:setProjectPref`, merged into the saved map in main, every window's copy following by `ui-pref-changed`), so windows showing different projects keep each other's choices (#245); `ui:set` doesn't write these maps. **Copy to workspace** on local, user and plugin skills; its tooltip and notification say who gets the copy, from its own audience.
- **Audience in the UI**: a Combwork skill's page shows its audience as a badge (**Project agents**, **Assistant**, **Agents + Assistant**; a tooltip says what it means and how to change it), also for a deleted bundled skill. A row shows it only when it isn't the default. The Skills view's footer and empty page, the Combwork tooltip and the delete confirmation say the same: deleting says who stops getting it, that a running Claude Code session keeps its own copy until it restarts, and that running Codex sessions share their folder's copy, which goes when another Codex session in that folder starts.
- **Adding** (both places): **+** creates `<name>/SKILL.md` from a starter; **Add from file** takes a `.md` (becomes `SKILL.md`, with the frontmatter `name` set and a frontmatter added if missing) or a `.zip` (unpacked as the skill folder: `SKILL.md` at its top or inside one top folder; at most 500 files and 50 MB; unsafe paths refused). Names: letters, numbers, `-`, `_`, max 64. A local skill can be added for both providers at once (tick box, shown when both are on). **Deleting** moves the folder to the Recycle Bin; only Combwork and local skills can be deleted, never Combwork's marked Codex copies.
- **A skill's reference files** (HI-2011, Anthropic's skills guidance: a CLI loads a skill's name and description always, its `SKILL.md` when the skill is used, other files only when needed, and skims deeper links). Every bundled skill keeps `SKILL.md` to **4,000 characters** (one rule for every skill, replacing card-loop's 11,000 cap): when it applies and the steps used every time, then a **Reference files** list linking each `.md` beside it with when to read it. Reference files are Markdown at the top of the skill's folder, linked from `SKILL.md` only (never file to file: one level deep), each starting with a heading of its own; `tests/guidance.test.ts` checks this, and reads `SKILL.md` and its reference files together for every rule it checks. Split: card-loop (`builder.md`, `reviewer.md`, `waiting.md`, `rounds.md`: a builder never reads the reviewer's half), coordinate-agents, run-lanes, work-on-card, review-agent-work, merge-ready and journal; the smaller skills stay one file. Delivery needed nothing new: the launch plugin's copies (Claude Code) and the `.agents/skills/cw-<name>` copies (Codex, Copilot) copy the whole tree, revisions hash it (`contentHash`), and `bundled.ts` updates untouched copies, Restore and Revert by tree. **The skill page** (`SkillDetail`) shows a skill's files as tabs (`role="tablist"`) when it has more than `SKILL.md`: `skills:files` lists them (`listedSkillFiles`: only for a skill the Skills view or the project's tab lists, else refused; `skillFiles`' bounds, a note when it stopped short), each opened in the same `DocEditor` with its save-conflict check (editable where `SKILL.md` is). A link in the preview opens a tab only when it names one of the listed files exactly (`skillLinkTarget`: no scheme, absolute or drive path, backslash, `.`/`..` segment or undecodable escape; a link inside the folder is never followed by `skillFiles`); any other link behaves as before. The scenarios count a reference file read (`skillRefsRead`, beside `skillsRead`, which stays `SKILL.md` only) only from a successful single-file read whose result holds that file's own first line.
- **Who gets a Combwork skill** is its `SKILL.md`'s `metadata.audience` (the Agent Skills format's place for a tool's own keys, so the CLIs read the file as usual): `agents` (the default, also for a skill without it) for project agents, `assistant` for the Assistant, `all` for both. It is not a switch: it says which kind of session a skill is written for, so a user's skills don't reach the Assistant and the Assistant's don't reach agents. Reading a skill grants no tools or permissions. The header is read as YAML (js-yaml, core schema; from the first 64 KB of the file), so comments, flow mappings (`metadata: { audience: assistant }`), quotes and block scalars mean what YAML says, and only `name`, `description` and `metadata.audience` of the right types are used. **A Combwork skill whose header can't be read** (not closed, not valid YAML, including a key given twice, not a mapping) **or whose audience is anything else** (a misspelling, a list, or written but empty: `audience:`, `null`, `~`; only an audience left out is the default) **is given to nobody until it is fixed**, never to a guessed recipient: the Skills view marks it **Not given** with the reason, the API's listings and status carry `problem` (`audience: "none"` in the status), tool listings say "given to nobody: …", and each launch lists it in its problems.
- **Bundled skills** ship in the installation (`resources/skills`): for agents `work-on-card` (carry a card from Doing to Review; tests it writes wait for conditions, not for time, #524), `review-agent-work` (review another's work, with the board's review marks; a new or changed test that sleeps and then checks, reads state once after an action, depends on another test's leftovers or raises a timeout with no reason is a blocking finding; it checks the builder's run record instead of repeating it, running the quick checks, the tests the change affects and its own probes, and a whole suite again only when the record is missing, for other code or doubtful, or the change is to shared test code, saying why, #533), `merge-ready`, `licence-audit` (what ships, read from its own files: dependencies, bundled libraries, vendored material, assets, installer parts and runtimes; anything not plainly permissive flagged for the user; general, not Combwork-only, #410) and `use-cw-api` (scripts against the Agent API); for the Assistant `coordinate-agents` (plan as cards, brief and start agents, follow them, stalled cards) `run-lanes` (a team's card loops: lanes by files, briefs, watches to the end) and `triage-report` (a problem report to a card: the cause found in the code first, a duplicate check including Passed and unmerged work, then the card with its evidence and place; the QA triager mode uses it, #408), `board-hygiene` (tidying the board: duplicates linked for the user to archive, the user's answers recorded as decisions, out-of-date blocked reasons rewritten or raised; columns, stalled cards and lanes' lists are left to Combwork, #409); for both `handover`, `pick-up`, `split-work` (plans only) and `workspace-note`. **They're kept up to date in each workspace** (`bundled.ts`, each time it opens, once the window has it, in the background: an agent's launch waits for it, HI-1705; the bundled modes the same way): a bundled skill the workspace was never given is added; an untouched copy of an older version (its content, line endings ignored, matches a version Combwork shipped before this one; a link (symlink or junction) in it is never followed and counts as a change, since Combwork ships none: `src/main/bundledHistory.json`, which `npm run bundled-history` appends to and a unit test keeps current) is replaced whole (a copy beside it renamed into place, so nothing reads it half-copied; a copy whose files are open stays until next time). **An automatic update or add never overwrites the user**: the swap (`swapIn`, also used for modes) is told what the copy was when the update was decided (its content hash, or nothing there for an add) and checks it again once the new version is copied (holding Combwork's own editors' file locks), on the old copy once it has been moved aside, and once more before the old copy is removed (a write through a file left open); a copy edited, deleted or replaced meanwhile is put back as the user has it, the update is abandoned until the next scan (which sees its real state), and the manifest isn't changed. When both the old copy and the new one were edited, the old goes back in place and the new is kept beside it as a conflict copy; what a putting-back sets aside is removed only if it is still exactly the new version, and if a rename for it is refused, nothing is deleted (what can't go back is kept as a conflict copy). What a crash in a swap left behind (an old copy, a rollback's backup) is removed only when it is a version Combwork shipped; anything else is kept beside the item as `<name>-conflict-<time>` (listed like any skill or mode), after the user's original is put back in an empty place. Another program writing through a file it held open in the instant between the last check and the removal is the one case this can't see; on Windows an open file usually stops the swap altogether. Restore and Revert, which the user asks for, replace whatever is there (sending it to the Recycle Bin first); an edited copy is kept, and offers **Revert to default** (with **Update available** only when it was made from a version this Combwork knows to be older than its own: not from a newer Combwork's, where Revert would go back); a deleted one stays deleted, listed greyed with **Restore**. `.combwork/bundled.json` records which were given and the version each copy came from. A workspace from before it has none: a bundled skill missing there was deleted by the user (a new bundled skill is added), and a modes folder that doesn't exist means it never had them. A copy of a version this Combwork doesn't know (a newer Combwork's, sharing the workspace) is left alone. Revert and Restore send the workspace copy to the Recycle Bin.

For Codex, Combwork skills are copied into `<agent folder>/.agents/skills/cw-<name>` on each launch (removing Combwork copies of skills it no longer gets), since Codex reads skills only from there; the Assistant's go into the workspace folder, where it works. Those copies carry a `.combwork-copy` marker and are never listed as local skills; a changed skill is swapped in whole, and what a crash during a swap left behind (Combwork's dot-folders named for it) is tidied at the next launch, under the same lock. Each launch records what it delivered of each skill (`launched` in `GET /v1/projects/{name}`): the revision of the copy the CLI reads, and `problems` for a skill not delivered as asked (a folder of the user's has its name; its old copy was in use, so it kept that one; its folder in the workspace is gone or couldn't be read). A kept old copy leaves the agent needing a restart; a user's folder doesn't, since a restart can't change it. **A skill is copied within the hashing limits as it is read** (`copySkillTree`: entries listed a batch at a time, depth, bytes actually read; the entry limit counts the skill's own entries, with Combwork's `.combwork-copy` marker allowed on top, one a folder, so a skill at the limit is still within it once its copy is marked), since its source can change while it is copied, and the copy is hashed before it is published: what is recorded as delivered (and in a Codex copy's marker) is that copy's revision, not the source's from before. A source grown past the limits, or with a file gone or unreadable, mid-copy publishes nothing: Codex keeps its old copy (reported with its revision and why), a Claude Code launch leaves the skill out (revision null, and why); nothing is left half-copied. One skill's failure is its own: the launch delivers the others, and the failed one's record is Combwork's copy from an earlier launch (its revision, the problem saying it kept it) or nothing, never a folder of the user's. A source that couldn't be read may work at the next launch; one over the hashing limits, or with a link that can't be made, is a lasting problem. If the skills folder itself can't be set up, each record is what is already there, the same way, and a failure to keep the copies out of git changes no record.

A link in a skill (symlink, or junction for a folder) is copied as a link to the same place, never as what it points to, and counts as content by where it points (`contentHash`, also for the markers and when telling the user's same-name folder from a copy of Combwork's); a link Windows won't let Combwork make (a link to a file needs a privilege) is a lasting delivery problem, naming the links: a Claude Code agent gets the rest of the skill without them; a Codex copy is swapped all or nothing, so it keeps its old copy whole (or, the first time, has none).

The workspace folder is a store only; no agent loads from it directly. Copies are used (not links): a Claude Code agent's are its own (`launch-<agent>`), so a running one keeps the version it started with. Codex agents sharing a folder share its copies, so when one launches with a changed skill, the others read the new version the next time they use it (Codex reads a skill's files when it uses them). Edits reach a session at its next launch either way.

### 7.2 MCP servers

One file per server: `<Workspace>/.combwork/mcp/<name>.json`, in Claude Code's format plus an optional `description`:

```json
{ "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"],
  "env": { "GITHUB_TOKEN": "${GITHUB_TOKEN}" }, "description": "GitHub issues and PRs" }
```

Enabled servers are merged into `launch/mcp.json` for Claude Code, and passed to Codex as `-c mcp_servers.<name>={…}`. Only Combwork's own `combwork` server is pre-approved, in every CLI (Codex: `default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"` on it alone, #1166; Copilot: `--allow-tool=combwork`): every other server's tools follow the CLI's approval policy for the agent's mode, as its other tools do. `combwork` is reserved, so a hand-made `.combwork/mcp/combwork.json` is never passed to a session (the old name is an ordinary server name since HI-2594). The user's own servers and a project's own (`.mcp.json` for Claude Code, `.codex/config.toml` for Codex) are not loaded, by the same rule as §5. Secrets are passed as environment references only; a definition whose values can't be passed safely to Codex is skipped with a log warning. Server code in `<Workspace>/.combwork/mcp/<name>/` is referenced in place, not duplicated. Combwork warns when a definition looks like it contains a literal secret.

**Add MCP Server from File** (#550, aligned with Add Skill from File, Darren: "in 0.6.0 we should have the skills and MCP aligned"). The MCP view adds a server from a `.json` definition (it becomes `<name>.json`) or a `.zip` of a server folder (unpacked to `.combwork/mcp/<name>/`, its definition from `combwork-mcp.json`, else `combwork-mcp.example.json` as the mcp repo ships it (the names before the rename aren't read since 1.1: HI-2594), at the zip's top or inside its one top folder, which is dropped; `__MACOSX` and `.DS_Store` are skipped; no definition file, under either name, is copied into the folder). The definition is checked as launches need it (an object; a `command` or an http(s) `url`; `args` strings; `env` and `headers` objects of strings) before anything is written. The suggested name is the file's (a `.json`), the folder's, or the zip's own name (a flat zip), made a valid server name (never `combwork`); `${CW_MCP_DIR}/<folder>` references move to the name it is added as. A definition points at the MCP folder with `${CW_MCP_DIR}`, the only variable read (the names upgrade converted the definitions stored with the old variable; HI-2594). A name in use (its `.json`, or for a zip its folder) is refused unless the user chooses **Replace** (the old definition, and for a zip the old folder, go to the Recycle Bin; a `.json` replacing a server keeps a folder there, which its definition may run). It is added to the workspace added nowhere, with no question where to add it (HI-2059), even if the name was added before (a definition deleted by hand), and **what it runs** (`mcpRuns`: the command and arguments, or the URL and type, the folder, and environment variables and headers by name, a whole `${VAR}` reference shown as itself, never a literal value) is shown before it is added, in the server's view, and each time a server is added somewhere (the Add Server picker, Add to…); an Add carries the server it showed (its definition, and its revision: the definition file's identity, modified time and size, which a replace changes even when the text is the same, as in an upgrade of only the code beside it), and is refused if either has changed since (replaced or edited meanwhile: "Check what it runs and add it again"). Adding, replacing, deleting servers and adding them to places take turns, so an Add can't land in the middle of a replace. Safe unpacking: entries with `..`, an absolute or drive path, characters or names Windows can't hold (`:`, reserved names such as `con`), or a Unix symbolic link (read from the zip's central directory) refuse the whole zip; at most 5,000 files and 200 MB unpacked (a `.json` at most 1 MB); the folder is claimed (`mkdir`, never reused) and written in place, removed again if a write fails. Nothing runs during the add. Deleting a server also moves its `<name>/` folder to the Recycle Bin when its definition runs what is in it; a definition that can't be read (broken JSON, not an object) is deleted and removed where it was added, with no folder guessed. The workspace's watcher ignores everything in `.combwork/mcp` but the definitions: a watched folder inside a server's folder would stop Windows moving that folder (Replace, Delete).

**The Assistant's servers** (HI-1472, Darren 28 Oct: "the Assistant works as if it were a project"; HI-2059). workspace.json's `mcp.assistant` is the servers added for the Assistant, as a project's `mcp.enabled` (`assistantMcpAdded`): a server runs for it only while in that list (before its conversion, #1093's meaning: on in the workspace too). Its launch gets exactly those, and Combwork's `combwork`; no project's choice reaches it nor its a project.
- **Where it's set** (HI-2059, Darren: "Settings should be a place to design the shape, Assistant on activity bar is where you work"): the Assistant's view on the activity bar has **MCP Servers**, its added servers with a remove button each and **+** (the same picker as a project's Add Server…, `addMcpTo('assistant')`); the MCP view's **Add to…** ends with **Assistant** (`setMcpPlaces`' `assistant`). It is one value: both read and change workspace.json's `mcp.assistant`. Settings → Assistant → **MCP servers (this workspace)** only links to the Assistant's view. Adding carries the definition shown (refused if replaced or edited, as a project's Add is); removing is at once. Deleting a server (or adding one under a name used before) removes it from the list, as from the projects'.
- **Shown:** the MCP view's "where" line ("Added in Ambrosia and for the Assistant", "Added for the Assistant only"); `GET /v1/mcp`'s `added.assistant`, left out for a project agent's call.
- **Moving the old switch:** once per workspace, before its open ends (so before the Assistant can start), `migrateAssistantMcp`: a new workspace gets `[]`; one from before gets the servers on in its workspace when `cw.assistant.otherMcpServers` was on in advanced.json (kept there for this, `advanced.legacy`), else `[]`. A list already there, an empty one too, stays; the save is worked out as it is written, so a choice saved meanwhile wins.
- A change marks a running Assistant's launch stale (restart needed), as a project's choice does.

### 7.3 Built-in Combwork MCP server

If "Provide Combwork tools to sessions" is on (default), every session, of every provider, also gets a `combwork` MCP server (bundled script run via Combwork's own executable) exposing the Agent API as tools: list projects, project status, read/write shared notes (a read gives the note's revision, a short hash of its text; a write naming it as `expectedRevision` is refused, with the current revision, if the note changed since: checked and written under the note's lock, the one Combwork's editors save under, so two agents rewriting one note can't drop each other's change; appends always keep every entry; #349), read the latest handover, create handovers, notify the user, session usage. Its MCP instructions (sent on `initialize`) are Combwork's **session contract** (`combworkInstructions` in `shared/combworkGuidance.ts`), kept to what must hold whatever else is loaded: which project and workspace, that handovers, shared notes, other projects and the board are Combwork's (use the tools, not the file system), the board's scope, which skill covers which workflow (`work-on-card` for a card given to it, `review-agent-work` to review one), and the board's boundaries in a line (Doing first, Review with a summary when done, reviewing isn't working on a card, Done only when the user asks, follow-up work as new cards, column order is priority), so a session without the skills keeps them, and that Combwork sets its folder (#476, #482: no git worktree of its own to work in unless the user asks, else it asks for an agent with its own; a subagent's worktree merged or removed before it finishes: Combwork's locks, Changes, merging and card tools follow the folder it gave, not one made there). Procedures live in the skills, arguments and side effects in the tools' descriptions, and enforcement in the Agent API. If the project has a handover, the instructions name the latest one. `GUIDANCE_REVISION` (a hash of this text, the control rules and a card's prompt) is in `GET /v1/status`, Help → Copy Diagnostics, and each running agent's `launched` in `GET /v1/projects/{name}` with its skills' revisions, so an older build's or launch's guidance can be told apart. Skill revisions are kept per open workspace (and once for Combwork's shipped copies) and hashed again only when a skill's files change (their sizes, times and file ids, checked on each call without reading them), so status polls don't re-read every skill; callers asking at once share one scan, a closed workspace's revisions are dropped and hashing for it stops, and a skill over the hashing limits (64 MB read, 2000 entries, 12 folders deep) has no revision and says why. Too big by its files' sizes is found without reading them and kept like a revision while nothing changes, so polling an unchanged too-big skill reads no content (over the entry or depth limit, each check is a walk stopped at the limit); a file that grows while it is read is still stopped by the cap on bytes read. Listing skills reads only the first 64 KB of each `SKILL.md` (its header), again only once it changes, and at most 1000 entries of a skills folder. A launch checks each skill against the limits before copying it: one over them isn't delivered (Claude Code) or keeps the copy it had (Codex, which reports that copy's revision), with the reason in `launched.problems`. A handover belongs to a project when its file name is `<date>-<project slug>-<title slug>.md` (as `cw_create_handover` writes it). When project names overlap (`web`, `web-admin`), a file that could belong to either is decided by its `- **Project:** <name>` header line. Codex doesn't show MCP server instructions to the model, so Combwork passes the same text to Codex as `developer_instructions`. **Deferred tools** (HI-2229, `shared/combworkToolLoad.ts`): a CLI that defers MCP tools behind a tool search (Claude Code: the model sees their names and loads a schema before a call) gets each role's most used Combwork tools in full, marked in `tools/list` with `_meta` `anthropic/alwaysLoad` (Claude Code 2.1.316): agents `cw_inbox`, `cw_read_task` and `cw_list_tasks`, the Assistant those and `cw_project_status` and `cw_agent_activity`. The rest stay deferred; a CLI that doesn't defer ignores the mark, and no CLI config is changed. A refused call that gave arguments its tool doesn't take, or left out one it requires, gets a line after the refusal naming what the tool takes, the missing and the unknown (names only, never the values given, at most six of each).


### 7.4 Dialects

Agent text (HI-2065; `shared:plans/2026-11-03-dialects-design.md`, Darren's decisions of 3 Nov on HI-2065): everything Combwork tells agents is declared beside its code as a catalogue entry (`agentMsg`, its English the **Default**), and a **dialect file** overrides some of it, sparsely. Files are per workspace in `.combwork/dialects/`: `workspace.json`, `<CLI>/cli.json`, `<CLI>/<label>.json` (a model file, with `model`, or a test copy, without), `api/cli.json`; JSON `name`, `model`, `texts` (id → `{ text, why }`).

- **The chain**, each text the first layer's that has it: model file (Auto: by the real model ID, exact, then its base ID; never the friendly name; or the agent's **Dialect** pick) → CLI file → Workspace → Default. No family layer. Callers with no session: API → Workspace → Default. An unknown model leaves the model slot empty, and the launch record says "model unknown".
- **Pinned at launch** (HI-2443): a session speaks the chain resolved when it launched (its text, its hook replies, cw-mcp.js and cw-progress through `CW_DIALECT_FILE`); an edit applies at its next launch, and "restart to apply" shows on the agents whose chain it changes. The API chain follows the files, for the workspace a request names.
- **The only check is the schema** (decision 11): each id exists and its text has exactly its placeholders. A save that fails is refused, saying why; nothing checks what a text says. After an update, an override that no longer matches is **outdated**: flagged, kept as written, and skipped for its id.
- **One file per model** in a CLI folder; a test copy has none. Set Model ("Use for a Model" before HI-2523; `promoteDialect`) moves the claim onto one of the user's own files; the old owner becomes a test copy, all or nothing.
- **The Dialects view** (HI-2444, activity bar): the list with each file's state (Shipped, Edited, Yours, outdated count), its on/off switch (kept in `.state.json`, not the file), and the running agents using it; a file shows every text, even when empty, inherited text dimmed with its layer and each layer's value on expand; Save (schema-checked, refused with reasons, never over a change made on disk meanwhile), a JSON tab over the same draft; Duplicate, Import, Export, Revert to shipped, Set Model, Delete (the user's own files only). Agent Settings → Dialect: Auto or a file of the agent's CLI folder.
- **New Model File, Duplicate, Set Model** (HI-2523; Darren 4 Nov: the model is typed, free text first): one dialog (`DialectFileDialog`), New Model File on each CLI group (an empty file, `{ name, texts: {} }`), Duplicate on a model file or test copy (its texts, the name "*name* copy"), each with an optional model ID (none: a test copy), and Set Model on the user's own model files and test copies (never a shipped, CLI, API or Workspace file; a blank ID refused). The model ID: suggestions only (`dialects:models`: the running sessions' launch model IDs and the CLI's connections' models; nothing curated); normalised only where the CLI recognises it (`dialectModelOf`: an alias its catalogue resolves → that ID; an ID its catalogue or descriptor lists → without a `[…]` suffix or snapshot date), anything else kept exactly, trimmed; refused only empty or with a control character. Notes, never blocking: the ID it saves as, the file that has the model (it becomes a test copy), no agent has run it, an alias Combwork can't resolve. Names: `dialectLabelProblem` (Windows-safe, no device names, no trailing dot or space, not `cli`, at most 100 characters) and new in the folder (any case). Main (`createDialect`) checks all of it again under the folder's lock, and moves a claim all or nothing.
- **Aliases and model unknown** (HI-2523): a launch's model is unknown for dialects only when it is one of the CLI's aliases (`capabilities.modelAliases`: Claude Code's fable, opus, sonnet, haiku, default, best, opusplan; Copilot's auto; or an alias the catalogue lists) that the catalogue doesn't resolve. Any other word ("gemma") is a model ID like any other, so a file claiming it matches.
- **Shipped files** (decision 8) are empty until a change is measured; untouched copies follow updates, edited ones are kept with Revert. Skills and the Assistant's modes stay out of dialects (decision 9).

## 8. Git

**1.0 (on the `1.0.0` branch):** the workflow layer (§16) retires "Git only": Git becomes the first platform under a capability model, beside None (no version control), with Jujutsu and Mercurial to follow. What follows describes 0.9.x until each 1.0 phase updates it.

**Platforms (1.0, P3, #1213):** Git is no longer the only version control Combwork knows: it is the first **platform** (§16.3), beside **None** (no version control). Each project has one (`ProjectInfo.platform`: its id, its descriptor's capabilities, what detection finds and an offer when they differ; `src/main/platform/registry.ts`). It is recorded in the project's `project.json` (`platform`) when Combwork sets the project up (makes its `project.json`), from detection (§16.3.5: a Git repository, its own or one above, is Git; no version control, Mercurial, Jujutsu or a colocated jj+git repository is None), and detected again at every refresh (the one ensuring `.combwork`'s exclude). A project from before has none recorded until the 1.0 upgrade records it (§16.17); meanwhile it follows detection and nothing is offered. A recorded value that names no platform (`platform: "mercurial"`, a number) leaves the project readable: it uses what detection finds, offers nothing, and a warning notice says what the file holds (`platform.invalid`). Notices are the open workspace's: a read begun before a close or a switch says nothing. A different detection (a None project gets `git init`, a Git project's repository is gone, another system appears) is **never switched to silently**: the project keeps its platform, the refresh says it once in a notice and logs it, and `platform.offer` names the switch (the Version Control tab offers it in a later phase). The window formats revisions through the descriptor (`revisionShort`), never by switching on the id. Every git call goes through `git()` (`git.ts`), `checkGit`'s `git --version` and `excludeCopies`' `rev-parse --git-common-dir` included.

- Project: `.combwork/` is kept out of version control (#345, `combworkVcs.ts`): Combwork adds `/<path>/.combwork/` to the `.git/info/exclude` of the nearest git repository holding the project (its own: `/.combwork/`; or one in a folder above, such as a workspace kept in git; a worktree's common git dir), the path's pattern characters escaped (`/project\[1\]/.combwork/`), idempotent, never a tracked `.gitignore`. Whether it is excluded is **git's own answer** (`git check-ignore -q --no-index -- .combwork/` in the project, kept until the exclude file changes or for a minute), not the line Combwork wrote: a `.gitignore` rule (`!/.combwork/`) can bring it back, and then it is `not-excluded`; only when git can't be asked (not installed), the line. It is ensured when the project is set up, at every refresh (`projectInfo`) and before every launch, so a repository made later (`git init`) is covered. `ProjectInfo.combworkVcs` says how it stands: `excluded`; `not-excluded` (a git repository whose exclude file Combwork couldn't write); `other-vcs` (the nearest is Mercurial, Subversion, Jujutsu, Bazaar or Fossil, which Combwork doesn't configure); `none`; and `sync` when the folder is in OneDrive (Windows' `OneDrive*` variables) or Dropbox (its `info.json`), which copies `.combwork` whatever version control does. Unless excluded and unsynced, the project's Overview and Project Settings show a notice saying why it matters, with **Exclude** for `not-excluded` (`project:excludeCombwork`) and Learn more; the Overview's can be dismissed for that situation (`ui.combworkVcsNotice`, a project preference), and shows again when it changes.
- **A project set up isn't set up again by a refresh** (HI-2564): a refresh makes a project of a folder found since the workspace opened (#1423: its `.combwork`, a default project.json, the exclude line), but not of one already set up in this lifetime whose project.json has gone: a folder half way through a delete in place (Shift+Delete, `rmdir /s`: its `.combwork` goes first, and making it again ended the delete in ENOTEMPTY) or a project reset by deleting its `.combwork`. Its refresh writes nothing for it (its exclude line neither: `combworkVcs` asks only) and reads it with the defaults; the workspace's next open, or a change to the project (`mutateProjectConfig`, a session started, Activate), sets it up again. "Set up in this lifetime" is its own record (`setUpAt`: each project seen with its project.json, or set up by `ensureProject`), not the id index, which drops a project once its config is missing. It is fenced as `registerRoots` is: a read from before a close, or from before a listing that found the folder gone, records nothing. It is forgotten when the workspace closes and when a refresh finds the folder gone, so a folder made again by that name is new.
- **Committed before it was excluded** (#364): an exclude rule keeps only untracked files out, so files under the project's `.combwork` committed earlier (a `git add -A` before Combwork set it up) stay tracked. `trackedCombworkFiles()` asks `git ls-files -z -- .combwork` in the project (its own `.combwork` only, also in a repository above it), again only when the repository's index changes (its index file's time and size: a commit, a `git rm --cached`), not at every refresh; only git's answer is kept, so a failed read says nothing (no `tracked`) and is asked again at the next refresh, never remembered as none. `CombworkVcs.tracked` is how many. The notice (Overview and Project Settings, its own dismissal key) says how many files are committed, why excluding doesn't untrack them, and the command (`git rm -r --cached .combwork`, then commit; the files stay on disk), and offers **Untrack…**: a confirmation listing the files git tracks there now (`project:combworkTracked`, read afresh; at most 50 shown), then `project:untrackCombwork` with exactly those files: main asks git again and, unless it tracks exactly those, untracks nothing (a file staged or untracked meanwhile: "changed since you were shown them"); otherwise `git --literal-pathspecs rm --cached --quiet -- <each file>` (never the folder, so nothing added in the last moment is touched), which stages their removal and leaves the commit to the user. Combwork never changes the user's index unasked.
- Workspace: `.combwork/` is **not** excluded; it is meant to be committed.
- The Git tab's Changes section (the Changes tab before #607) shows `git status` and a Monaco diff (HEAD vs working tree) per file.
- **Comparing two branches** (HI-1824; `src/main/gitCompare.ts`, `src/renderer/src/components/ChangesCompare.tsx`). Since slots, no agent keeps a worktree on a long-lived branch, so the Changes picker's first group, **Branches**, compares any two local branches with no folder of their own: the project's integration line (its workflow target, G7, when that is a local branch other than the default branch) against main first, then each local branch no slot has checked out against the integration line (it against main); a **Slots** group lists each slot whose folder has a branch (free ones and those lent to blocked cards included, HI-1823's slot-c), with its open lease's card, opening its branch against the slot's target. Slots come from the board's records (`boardSlots`, a plain read: never `poolFor`/`slots:list`, which would make the pool as the project opens). The Changes tab opens on integration ↔ main when the project has one and the user hasn't picked another page. The page picks either side and swaps them; it shows ahead/behind (`rev-list --left-right --count`), where they parted, each side's commits (50 a page), and the files head changes since the merge base (three dots, as a card's changes; names only, up to 5,000, listed 200 at a time). A comparison reads each branch once as a commit and returns both (`baseCommit`, `headCommit`); a file's diff, and every page after the first until Refresh, is asked for those pinned commits, so it belongs to the counts and files shown though a branch moves (a refresh takes the new tips, keeping the file only if still listed). A file's diff (merge base against head's blob, `cat-file`, the same 2 MB cap and binary rule as Changes) is read only when it is opened. Read-only by construction: only for-each-ref, rev-list, merge-base, log, diff of two commits and cat-file, through git's worker (HI-1783) with `GIT_PREFIX`; no checkout, worktree, index refresh or write. Both names must be listed local branches (`refs/heads/<name>`, so never an option or another revision); one deleted since the list is refused.
- **Leftover branches** (HI-1823; `ChangesLeftovers.tsx`, `branchCleanup.ts`'s `leftoverBranches`, `gitRepo.ts`'s `leftoverInfo`). The picker's Branches group ends with **Leftover branches (N)** when the project has a target: every local branch `localUse()` finds free (not the target, the default or the folder's branch, none checked out in a worktree or slot, no open card's), merged into the target or not. `git:leftovers` reads every local branch, never cut at BRANCHES_SHOWN as `git:info` is: 0 commits only when git's `--merged` says so, a count for the first 60 unmerged, null (not counted, never taken for merged) for the rest or a read that failed. Each row: its card, Compare (the comparison against the target) and Delete… (#1642's flow, shared as `deleteBranch()`: one confirm when merged, the commits it drops listed when not, `-D`). Main checks each deletion again as before (`branchUseNow`, at the commit shown). Names are read from whole refs (`refs/heads/…`), never `refname:short`, which says `heads/x` where a tag is also x. **An open card's lines** are every line it has started on, not only this cycle's: a card's fold keeps `lines` (its Started and Adopted lines, across cycles, renames followed; on its work view and badge), so a card back from Done that started again elsewhere (the project folder, say) keeps its earlier line out of the leftovers, and main refuses to delete it while the card is open.
- **The Git view** (#607; `src/main/gitRepo.ts`, `src/shared/gitRepo.ts`, `src/renderer/src/views/GitTab.tsx`). A Git project's view (a project without git, a None project, keeps working in its folder, with no worktrees, merges or Git view). The project's Changes tab became **Git** (its id stays `changes`, so saved tabs and `project.tab.changes` are unchanged; its key is Alt+8 since #1043), with three sections (`GIT_SECTIONS`, `gitSection` per project in the window, Changes when none): **Changes** (as before: whose changes, from the picker), **History** (a branch's commits, `git log`, with their decorations, 20 a page with the shared pager (`Pager`, as the archived cards' table; #1643); by default the project's target when it is a branch here (its options' `target`, where its work goes, such as `1.1.0`), else the folder's branch, and any local or remote branch from the picker in its heading (each named whole, `refs/heads/x` or `refs/remotes/x`, and checked against the repository's own list, so a local branch named like a remote's never hides it), and its tags newest first, at most 50 listed, with how many more; **Create tag…**: lightweight, or annotated with a message, optionally pushed to a chosen remote) and **Branches & remotes** (`git:info`: the branch or detached HEAD, a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert or bisect in progress (from the git dir's files), the upstream with ahead/behind (`%(upstream:track)`), when the folder last fetched (FETCH_HEAD's time), local branches (each one's upstream, ahead/behind, last commit and the worktree it is checked out in), remote branches with no local one, the remotes with their URLs (a password or token never shown or logged, `redactRemoteUrl`, erring towards hiding: the sign-in is everything before the last @ ahead of the query, all of it for http(s) and ftp(s), the password for other schemes, and the whole query and fragment, as •••; git's own failure messages pass through `redactUrlsIn`, each URL taken to the next whitespace, since a password or query can hold an apostrophe or quote; an action's failure is also cleaned of the exact secret parts of every configured remote URL and of a URL being added, as written and decoded (`urlSecrets`, `scrubSecrets`); an edit that keeps a ••• is refused), the repository's other worktrees, read-only, each with its agent and **Changes**, and the commit identity: this repository's (`--local`), the global one and the one git uses, with warnings (`identityWarnings`): no name or email (commits fail), and a personal address on a repository with a GitHub remote (GitHub's no-reply address keeps it private). A **status bar item** for the selected project (`GitStatusBarItem`, `gitStatusText`: "main · origin · ↑2 ↓0", "main · no upstream", "detached at abc1234 · rebasing"; none for a folder that isn't a repository) opens Branches & remotes; its tooltip says when the counts are from. Reads are cheap (no working-tree scan) and happen when the project's branch or agents change, after a Git action, on window focus and every minute. **No automatic fetch**: ahead/behind is as of the user's last **Fetch** (`git fetch --all`), with its time. **The user's actions only**, never an agent tool or Agent API route, and only in the project folder (`assertProject`: an agent's worktree is refused; its work comes in through Merge): switch branch (`git checkout <branch> --`, or `--track <remote>/<branch>` for a remote branch with no local one; not to a branch checked out in another worktree), create a branch (switching to it, or not), add a remote, change a remote's URL (an unchanged redacted URL saves nothing), fetch, pull, push, create a tag, set this repository's identity (`git config --local`; empty unsets it). **Pull** fetches the upstream's remote, then `git merge --ff-only @{upstream}`; a branch that has diverged is refused with the counts and left as it is. **Push** pushes to the upstream (`refs/heads/<branch>:<its merge ref>`), or with `--set-upstream` to a chosen remote when there is none; never forced (a rejection says to pull first). **Push to…** (#1385, `git:pushTo`, `pushToRemote`): any remote, the branch the form named when it opened, sent by name (never whichever is checked out when it runs: `push --porcelain -- <remote> refs/heads/<b>:refs/heads/<b>`) or every branch and then every tag (`push --porcelain --all`, then `--tags`), **never `--set-upstream`**, never forced; each ref's outcome from git's porcelain lines (`parsePushPorcelain`: `=` up to date, `!` refused, else pushed); with all of them, the reply lists each branch by its outcome, a line each (pushed, already up to date, refused (branches and tags), tags pushed; every one by name, sorted; a long notice or dialog error scrolls in its own box), a failure when any was refused, the rest pushed. The form offers a remote other than the branch's own first. **Remotes' Rename and Remove** (#1385): `git remote rename -- <old> <new>` (refused for an invalid name, or one another remote has, case-insensitively: remote-tracking refs are files), the branches tracking it following (git's own); `git remote remove -- <name>` after a confirm listing every local branch whose upstream is on it (`git:remoteTracking`, read in full, never the view's list capped at 200), whose upstream git clears; that set goes back with the removal, which is refused if the branches tracking it differ by then; nothing on the remote changes. **A branch's Track… and Stop tracking** (#1385, `git:setUpstream`): `git branch --set-upstream-to=<remote>/<branch> -- <local>`, or `--unset-upstream`. A remote branch Combwork doesn't know (no `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`, as of the last fetch) is refused unless the user agreed to push it there first (the form says so when it isn't in the view's remote branches, re-read as they change): then the local branch is pushed there (never forced), a fetch of that remote if its tracking ref still isn't there, and tracked. None of these needs the folder steady (they don't touch the working tree), so they aren't refused while agents work. Fetch, pull and push run with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (a credential helper's own window still opens) and a 5-minute limit. **Safety**: switching branch, creating one to switch to and pulling are refused (`folderBusy`), in the window (the buttons disabled with the reason as their tooltip) and again in main, while an agent working in the project folder (no worktree) is starting, working, waiting for an answer, waiting on background tasks or cards, or stopped mid-task at a sign-in, or while the project's merge slot is held (an agent's, or the user's own merge) or waited for, saying who and why; the change itself runs holding the merge slot of the branch it leaves (`mergeSlots.asUser`) and the project's merge lock, so a merge can't start in its middle; the agents (and, with a detached HEAD, the slots) are checked again once those are held, right before git runs, so an agent that started working while the action waited stops it. **The folder is fenced** from that last check to git's end (#646, `changingFolder` in `src/main/folderFence.ts`, a general per-folder fence any operation that rewrites a folder can take, e.g. 1.0's merges): no line of Combwork's is typed into an agent working in that folder or inside it (the line writer's `whyNoLine`: "its folder is being changed (a Git switch)", checked again before each piece and Enter, so every delivery waits: messages, wakes, loop wakes, tasks), and no agent starts or resumes there (`launch` awaits `folderSteady` just before spawning). A delivery wanted now (a card's Start on a running agent, the Assistant's prompt, the user's own task to an agent with no inbox: `deliverNow`) is held, not cancelled: it waits for the fence, then is given once, and a wait isn't one of its tries (#646 round 1). So is Enter again for a line not taken yet (`submitAgain` refuses inside a fence; the confirmation waits for it, and the wait doesn't count against its window). The Git action's fenced check counts an agent with input of Combwork's on its way as working (a prompt or launch task given and not taken, `agentNow().pending`, or a line typed and not taken, `lineWaiting`): its CLI may start that turn while git runs, and a fence can't take back what is in its input. When the fence comes down (git done, failed or refused: never longer than the check and git), what waited is offered at once (`onFolderSteady`). What the user types into a terminal can't be held. An idle agent's session in the folder doesn't block: the confirm says it finds the new branch on its next turn. One Git action at a time per project folder. After a switch or pull, the workspace refreshes (the project's branch) and worktree agents' unmerged counts are checked again. A project folder inside another repository (a workspace kept in git: `rev-parse --show-toplevel` is a folder above it, `parentRepo`) shows that repository read-only, with a note: every action is refused (`parentRepoText`), as Combwork changes only a project's own repository. A project that isn't a repository shows "<name> isn't a git repository" with the setup notes and **Initialise repository…** in every section; git that can't run shows the problem with Provider Setup and Retry.
- **Initialise repository** (#701; `src/main/gitInit.ts`, `src/shared/gitInit.ts`, `src/renderer/src/components/InitRepo.tsx`). The user's, from the window only (no agent tool or Agent API route), for a project folder (`assertProject`). Its button is on Git's page of a None project whose folder has no repository of its own (HI-1905, §16.6), on the Git tab of a Git project that isn't a repository (and the Changes section's hint), and, as **Initialise its own repository…**, on Branches & remotes of a project inside another repository. `git:initCheck` says whether it can be done (refused, with why: git can't run, another version control system keeps the folder or one above it (`otherVcsOf`: its markers looked for at every level whatever git is there, so a colocated Jujutsu repository, .jj beside .git, is refused, never offered as a git one to nest in), or the folder is a repository's top already), the repository around it (`parentRepo`), the identity from the system and global config with their includes (`--includes`), read with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` above the folder so an outer repository's own config, or a conditional include that matches only it, never counts, and whether they have conditional includes (`includeIf`, `conditionalIdentity`: only the new repository can resolve those, so the fields are optional), whether the folder has a .gitignore, and whether it is empty but for .combwork. The dialog offers a starter .gitignore (`GITIGNORE_CHOICES`: none, minimal (OS and editor files, logs), Node, Python, .NET, Godot (4 and 3), each with the minimal lines; never listing .combwork), none when the folder has one (kept, never overwritten: written with `wx`); asks for the name and email git lacks (`initProblem`), used only for what git still lacks once the repository exists (read there, conditional includes resolved) and saved with `git config --local`, never global (nothing entered and still none: it stops right after `git init` and the exclude, before the .gitignore or anything is staged, saying so); **a repository with no commit yet** (`resume`: one that stopped there, or made by hand; `HEAD` unborn) is taken on from there: everything but `git init`, its identity read from the repository itself; the dialog belongs to the Git tab (`gitInitFor`, `InitRepoHost`), so it stays open as the page under it changes, asks again after a failure, and goes on as **Make the first commit** with the fields the repository lacks; Branches & remotes of such a repository says it has no commits, with **Make first commit…**; and, inside another repository, a checkbox naming it, without which Initialise stays off. `git:init` checks it all again in main, then in order: `git init -b main`; `ensureCombworkExcluded` (#345) and Combwork's skill copies' exclude lines, refusing to go on, with nothing staged, unless git confirms it ignores .combwork (a .gitignore rule bringing it back); the .gitignore; the identity; `git add -A`, then a check that nothing under .combwork is staged (unstaging all and stopping if so); `git commit --allow-empty -m "Initial commit"` (hooks run); and a workspace refresh, so `isGitRepo`, the Git tab and worktrees work at once. One at a time per project (the Git view's queue). No undo: its reply says what it did ("Initialised a git repository on main, added a Node .gitignore and committed 42 files."), and a failure says which steps were done and where it stopped.
- **Combwork's git commands never write the index as a side effect** (#212): they run beside the user's and agents' own git commands, and `git status` (and `git diff` against the working tree) otherwise refresh the index, taking `index.lock` for a moment, so a `git add` or `commit` at that moment failed with "index.lock: File exists". Every git command Combwork runs (`git()`, `GIT_PREFIX` in `src/main/git.ts`) passes `--no-optional-locks` and `-c diff.autoRefreshIndex=false`; locks a command needs (commit, merge, reset, worktree add) are still taken. Status compares content in memory, so a file touched but unchanged still isn't listed; a worktree branch's changes since it left base (`diff --name-status <merge-base>`, which without a refresh lists stat-only files as modified) drop such a file only when git says exactly that it isn't changed: its working copy matches the index (status) and the index matches the merge base (`diff --cached`, mode included). A working copy that differs from an index that differs from base is kept (shown even if it was changed back by hand), never hidden.
- **Git itself** (#346, `gitTool.ts` in main and shared): whether git runs is kept apart from whether a folder is a repository. `git --version` on Combwork's own PATH (a Start-menu launch can have another PATH than a terminal), with a 10 s timeout, at start and with Provider Setup's **Check again**, cached: `ok`, `missing`, `old` (older than **2.38**, `GIT_MIN`: `merge-tree --write-tree`, which checks a merge for conflicts first, recognises squash-merged branches and is what the merge-ready skill runs) or `unknown`, with the version and the executable (git.com or git.exe on PATH, as Windows starts it). **The git Combwork starts** (HI-2137, `gitExe()`): where that executable is exactly Git for Windows' launcher (`<root>\cmd\git.exe`), which starts the real git as a second process, the check also finds the real one (`git --exec-path` is `<root>/mingw64/libexec/git-core`, or `clangarm64`, `mingw32`, under the same root; its `git.exe` is there and gives the same `--version`), and every git Combwork starts (git's worker, the merge queue's git host and launcher) starts it directly, in the environment the launcher gives it (`withLauncherEnv`, as Git for Windows' `git-wrapper.c` sets it up: its own `MSYSTEM` whatever was set, `PLINK_PROTOCOL=ssh` unless set, `HOME` unless set from `%HOMEDRIVE%%HOMEPATH%` when that is a folder other than System32, else `%USERPROFILE%`, then `<root>\<mingw>\bin`, `<root>\usr\bin` and `%HOME%\bin` before PATH), so hooks and aliases see what they see through the launcher. Anything else (another git, a wrapper, git.com, a different version) is started from PATH as before. The check itself always runs PATH's git, and finds the git to start again each time; a command that can't start the real git (uninstalled, moved) runs once more with PATH's git, whichever command found it gone first, and git is checked again. Below **2.17** (`GIT_REQUIRED`: `--no-optional-locks` needs 2.15, `git worktree remove` 2.17) nothing of Combwork's git runs, which counts as missing. `git()` reports a call that couldn't start git (ENOENT and the like, when its working folder exists: Node says ENOENT for a missing folder too) as `missing` with exit code -1, never 1, so no caller takes it for git's "no" (`check-ignore`'s "not ignored"); such a call marks git missing at once, and a call that runs while it is marked missing clears it and checks again (`git-tool` event, every window's store). **Provider Setup** shows a Git row under every provider's tab: the version and path; or **Git not found** / **Git x is older than 2.38**, what doesn't work and the fix (install or update Git for Windows, or add git.exe's folder to PATH, then Check again: no restart, as Check again reads the fresh PATH, #472), with **Git for Windows** (git-scm.com). No setting for git's path. The status bar shows **Git** (warning) when git is missing or unusable, **Git x** (caution) when old; either opens Provider Setup. Copy Diagnostics lists it. **Every git-dependent screen says "git missing" instead of "not a repository"** (`gitProblem`): Add Agent's New worktree ("Git isn't installed (or isn't on Combwork's PATH)", `ProjectGitInfo.gitProblem`), the Board's Start in a worktree, adding a worktree agent (Agent API and cards too), the Changes tab (`GitStatus.gitProblem`: the problem, the fix, Provider Setup and Retry), the Merge dialog (the error in place of the merge, which can't be started), Remove All and template loads (the reason a worktree is kept, or the load refused), Remove Project. **Fail safe**: a git call that can't run, or fails, never counts as merged, clean or nothing to lose. `branchStatus` throws whenever git can't read the project folder's branch (`checkedOutBranch`: a failed read is not a detached HEAD, which counts against the base), count the branch or read the worktree's status (no more "nothing to merge" on a failure: the unmerged badges show nothing, the Merge dialog the error; merging refuses too), `worktreeCheck` is never removable then, and `removeCheckedWorktree` deletes nothing git can't run for. The Changes tab's status is "not a git repository" only when git says so: any other failed `git status` (a damaged index, a dubious owner), merge base or diff against an agent's base is an error the tab shows with Retry, never an empty list. A read that fails only because another git command is rewriting the index (`INDEX_BUSY`, "index file open failed" on Windows while a user's `git add` runs) is tried again briefly first (`gitReading`: 4 tries, 50 ms apart; the Changes tab's status and diff, worktrees' uncommitted counts, the Files tab's ignored entries). `.combwork`'s exclude line is still written without git (file work), reported `unconfirmed` and logged, and stays excluded. Bundled skills keep to git that Provider Setup's row covers: merge-ready's `merge-tree --write-tree` needs 2.38, which the row names.
- **Ignored entries in the Files tab** (#222): `git check-ignore` exits 0 or 1; any other exit (128, "index file open failed" while another git command rewrites the index on Windows) is a failure, not "nothing ignored". A busy index is tried again (4 tries, 50 ms apart); outside a repository nothing is ignored. If git still can't say, the folder keeps its last known ignored entries (a memory of the 500 folders listed last) and is listed again 500 ms later (`files-changed`; at most 3 times in a row while it keeps failing). The failure is logged once per project.

---

## 9. Usage, compaction and memory

Each provider's adapter reads its own transcripts into one usage shape. Codex: rollout files under `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-…-<id>.jsonl` (`token_count` events for tokens, context window and plan limits; `session_index.jsonl` for titles). Claude Code: `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-path>/<session-id>.jsonl`, where the encoded path replaces every non-alphanumeric character of the project path with `-` (matched case-insensitively). A folder's sessions are found by place, whatever the folder is called (#493; a tool's path in a transcript shows relative to the project when it is inside it under another name, `shortPath`, #494): Claude Code names its transcripts' folder by Node's realpath of its cwd (a junction or symlink followed, an 8.3 short name kept), so Combwork looks under that name, its own spelling and the real, long path, and last under folders named by an 8.3 spelling of the folder, which none of those gives: only names that may hold one (on its drive, with an encoded `~n`), each read once for the cwd its transcripts record (in their first 64 KB) while it is unchanged, and compared by place. It lists the sessions of all of them, restores a transcript under the first (where Claude Code looks on resume), and Repair copies a moved folder's data from each of them in that order (`copyPathData`, a copy per folder: the first one's file wins, a later one's that differs is kept and listed, in the preview too); Codex (`session_meta.cwd`) and Copilot (`workspace.yaml`'s `cwd`) record the cwd as given, and Combwork compares it by real path (`placeMatcher`). Claude Code's transcripts don't carry the context window; for a running session it comes from the status line (`context_window.context_window_size`) and is added to the session's usage.

**Model choice** (global default, per project, per agent and for the Assistant): the models Claude Code reports (§10, models and capabilities), else the fallback list in Settings → Claude Code (as shipped: Latest aliases, pinned versions and older versions, hidden until requested); and a custom model ID. There is no 1M-context choice: current models (Fable, Opus 4.7+, Sonnet 5+) have the 1M window without asking, and Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 reach it only through a `[1m]` model ID, typed as a custom model (the placeholder says so). Saved `[1m]` choices from 0.2 still work and show as custom models. Availability for the account is only known when a session starts.

**Use 200K context (instead of 1M)** (providers with `capabilities.contextLimit`: Claude Code): global (Settings → Claude Code, off by default), per project (Inherit / On / Off), per agent (Add Agent and Agent Settings: the project's / On / Off, stored as `use200kContext` on the agent and cleared when its provider changes) and for the Assistant (Settings → Assistant and Assistant Settings). Resolved like the model: the agent's, else the project's, else the global setting. A session launched with it gets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1`, and a `[1m]` suffix is dropped from its model, since Claude Code rejects such a model as unrecognised when 1M is off (2.1.287). A change applies on the next start or restart (it's part of the launch signature, so running agents show Restart session).

**Metrics per session**
- Input, output, cache-write, cache-read tokens (assistant `message.usage`, de-duplicated by request id).
- Current context size: the last assistant entry's `input + cache_read + cache_creation`.
- Compactions from `system/compact_boundary` entries: trigger, `preTokens`, `postTokens`.
- Copilot (#454, 1.0.98): `session.compaction_start` and `session.compaction_complete` (the whole context before and after: system + conversation + tool-definition tokens, each a field name in Settings → Advanced, `copilot.compaction.*`, as is the summary for the Sessions tab; the `trigger`; one with `success: false` or never completed counts nothing). Copilot sends PreCompact but no hook at the end, so the completion read from `events.jsonl` ends Combwork's compacting status (`LiveDetails.compactedAt`, once per completion of the launch, only while Combwork shows it compacting, and never one read before a newer hook came or older than the compaction under way). The sample is a `/compact`: no automatic compaction could be made offline (the stand-in model, even with `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS` near the base context), so its `trigger` value is passed through as Copilot writes it.
- Cache TTL detected from `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` vs `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` (overridable in settings).
- Model, Claude Code version, session title (`ai-title` / `custom-title`), last activity.
- API-equivalent cost from `cost-state` entries (`totalCostUSD`), shown on the Overview as "API-equivalent cost". Claude Code writes them only at some turns' ends (hours can pass without one), so the requests after the last one get Combwork's estimate on top, and the cost shows as partly estimated ("≈"). A provider that reports its cost (`capabilities.reportsCost`: Claude Code, Copilot) has **Settings → <provider> → Session costs** (#436, Darren's decisions): its reported cost, the default and the truth (it follows the CLI's own price table, even when that lags a price change, #442: Combwork never recomputes it), or **My prices**, Combwork's estimate from the table for every session it has a price for (the footer's live cost too, re-priced at once when the choice or a price changes, idle sessions included; the CLI's last report is kept, so going back shows it, as reported; days estimated, not shared out from the reports), the CLI's newest report (its status line's, else its transcript's, never recomputed) for a model without one, and with neither a price nor a report the cost is unknown (`costSource`, `usesOwnPrices`). No price page is fetched or scraped. For providers that don't report cost (Codex), Combwork **estimates** it from a price table (per million tokens: input, cached input, cache write, output), shown with "≈". Combwork ships the published API prices as editable defaults (checked 30 Sep 2026, GPT-6.1 Sol 5 Oct 2026, Haiku 5.5 8 Oct 2026; Claude's cache writes are 1.25× input and cache reads 0.1× unless listed; never fetched or scraped). Haiku 5.5's row is the prompts-up-to-100,000-tokens rate with five-minute cache writes: longer prompts (5× the price) and one-hour cache writes are not modelled, so its estimate is low for those sessions, and a cost Claude Code reports is kept and each provider's settings page has the table, labelled with the date they were checked: the user can change any price, add models, remove them (a removed shipped price is no longer used) and **Reset to defaults**. Only the user's changes are stored (`prices`, `pricesRemoved`), so Combwork's later prices still reach models they never edited. A session whose model has no price has an **unknown** cost, never $0: the agent's footer shows **$?**, the Overview's running agents **Unknown**, and its cost totals (the summary, each provider's, the Workspace Overview's and the Assistant's, by agent and by day) and session details **Unknown** when no session in them has a price, or the known subtotal with **+ ?** ("≈ $1.20 + ?") when some haven't; the agent's footer and the running agents say (on hover) that Combwork has no price for the model and to add one in Settings → <provider> → API prices. It is the API-equivalent value, not what a subscription charges.

**Keeping up with the CLIs**: a transcript of over 200 KB in which Combwork finds no requests at all is taken as a format change it doesn't understand, and the user is told once per provider version. Sample transcripts per supported CLI version are unit-test fixtures (`tests/fixtures`).

**Overview tab**: first the project's cards at a glance (`TaskStrip` in `Board.tsx`, shared with the Workspace Overview, counts from `taskOverview()` in `shared/tasks.ts` for the project's cards only): On Hold, Todo, Doing, Waiting for review, Passed, Done, Stalled and Blocked (blocked not counting Done), from the store's board, so they follow every card change without a reload; each number opens the project's Tasks tab, and a project without cards shows "No cards for this project" with **Open Tasks** (the Workspace Overview's strip hides when the board is empty, and its numbers open the whole board). Then a period (Today, 7 days, 30 days, All time; All time by default) and a project summary across every provider (tokens, API-equivalent cost, sessions, prompts). Periods are **local calendar days** (Today since midnight; 7 and 30 days include today) and count only what happened in them: each session's usage is kept **by day** (`SessionUsage.days`, `shared/usageDays.ts`): requests, tokens, prompts and compactions on the day they happened; Codex's running totals by what they grew by each day. A day's cost is its share of the reported cost (each Claude Code cost report's increase is split between the days of the requests it covered, in proportion to Combwork's estimate for them, so the days add up to the reported total) plus Combwork's estimate for requests after the last report; for providers that don't report cost, Combwork's estimate. A session counts in a period's sessions when it had activity in it. For 7 and 30 days a chart shows tokens per day (cost and prompts on hover). The day charts (both Overviews' and Performance's) share their look: each day or hour is a tile with a soft background (`.daily-col`, `--daily-slot`), 3 px apart, so a day without tokens still reads as its own column; Performance adds its hatching (not recorded) and fade (partly recorded) on top. Usage is read incrementally: each transcript keeps its parser and offset, and only lines added since are read (a long session's transcript can be over 100 MB). Then the agents running now (context against the model's window, cost), then one section per provider used (its totals and its plan limits: Claude Code's 5-hour and weekly, Codex's primary and secondary windows, Antigravity's weekly quotas by group of models, Copilot's quotas by kind of request), a table by agent, and one agent's session details (its running session, else its most recent; the focused agent's until another is picked in the agent picker shown with more than one agent; compaction history as a data table, below). Its **compaction history** is a `DataTable` (`components/DataTable.tsx`, rules in `shared/tableView.ts`; #124): When (newest first by default; a text filter on the formatted date), Trigger (a choice), Before, After, Freed (sortable, biggest first); ten rows a page. A row (click, or Enter when focused) opens the Sessions tab on that session at that compaction's divider, its summary open (`openInSessionsTab(path, id, n)` → `transcript:compactions` gives the nth compaction's item id), when its transcript or Combwork's backup is there; otherwise rows aren't clickable. The footer's context (`showInOverview`) scrolls to it (`#compaction-history`), else to the session details.
- **The board's search through an index** (#1237): `combwork.db` keeps an FTS5 index of each card's title, description, project, agent's name and labels (`card_search`, the 1.0 group's step 11; contentless, the trigram tokenizer, kept by triggers on the card tables, so every write path keeps it). A words search of three characters or more (`searchedWords`: not a number, `#12`, or a project's key form) asks it for the cards that contain the words, any case (`searchCards`), and confirms each with `cardMatches`, so it finds exactly what the in-memory search finds (checked over 400 pieces of a live board's text); shorter words, numbers and keys are matched in memory, and so are words with a letter FTS5 folds apart from what `toLowerCase` makes of its capital (`FOLD_APART`: İ's `i̇`, Georgian Mkhedruli, Cherokee small letters and a few dozen more, worked out again from SQLite by a unit test) or ending in `i`, and so is everything on a 0.9 board waiting for its upgrade. `GET /v1/tasks?q=` uses it, reading only the cards found. The window filters the cards it already holds in memory, which is faster than asking main (0.1–0.7 ms on a live board's 254 live cards). Comments aren't indexed: the board's search doesn't read them, and they would make the index nearly five times as large.
- **Search and filter boxes** (#433): every one is `SearchInput` (`components/ui.tsx`): the board's search, Settings' and Project Settings' search, the Files tab's Find, the Sessions tab's search, the sidebar's Filter projects and Filter skills, a data table's text filters, Tips, Keyboard Shortcuts and the command palette (`tests/searchBoxes.test.ts` fails for a plain `<input>` named for searching, filtering or finding). While it has text, a × (`IconButton` "Clear") sits inside it on the right (`.search-box`, which takes the box's place in the layout; the box keeps its size): clicking it clears the text as typing would and keeps the focus in the box. **Escape** with text clears it too; with the box empty, Escape does what it did before. In a dialog (`Modal` leaves an Escape to a clearable box with text, `escapeClearsSearch`) and in the palette, the first Escape clears the box and the next closes it. The Files and Sessions searches already cleared on Escape; the palette used to close at once.
- **Data tables** (`DataTable`): one component for tables that grow, with the look of Combwork's other tables (`.table` in `.table-wrap`, Performance's too): a header click sorts (ascending, or descending first for dates and numbers; then the other way; then the default order; `aria-sort`, a chevron, the header a button), quick filters in a row under the headers (text contains, any case; a choice of the rows' values), and paging under it (rows per page 10/20/50/100, remembered per table in `ui.panes` as `table-rows:<id>`; "21–40 of 133"; first, previous, "Page n of m", next, last), hidden when one page of the fewest rows holds them all (so a bigger size can always be made smaller again). Rows can be selectable (`selection`, #249): a checkbox before each row, and one in the header for every row the filters let through, on every page. A choice filter can match rows with several values (`values`: a card's labels). Filters and sorting apply before paging; a filter or rows per page change goes back to page 1, and a page past the end shows the last. Only the page is rendered. No rows: a message instead of the table; no matches: a row saying so, with Clear filters. It scrolls sideways inside its pane at narrow widths. A clickable row (`onRowClick`) is a button: Enter or Space on the row opens it, but not on a control inside it, which does its own action (an archived card's **Unarchive**, #267). **Its sort is remembered** per table too (#250), in `ui.panes` as `table-sort:<id>:<column>` (1 ascending, 2 descending; one a table; the default order keeps none, and a column that no longer sorts is ignored; `rememberedSort()`/`sortPanes()` in `shared/tableView.ts`). A table can also have totals under its rows (`foot`, a tfoot: Storage's), a row's detail opened under it (`detail`, with `aria-expanded` on a clickable row: Compare's scenarios), a row's own class (`rowClassName`), a header's (i) (`headerTip`), a column's class (`className`), and filters shown only past a number of rows (`filterFrom`: small tables show none, or while one is set). **Where** (#250): the compaction history and archived cards; Settings and Project Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts (every command on one page, its edit controls kept); Performance's Combwork tools (by characters), Agent API (by requests), Guidance at launch and Provider usage (unknown totals sort last; a latency past the histogram's last bound, shown "> 10 s", sorts as the slowest, `latencyOrder()`, #305); Compare's scenarios (worst first; a row opens its measures), an export comparison's measures (sortable by change) and the kept list; Storage (a project's, with its total under it; Clean Up…'s preview, a table per kind; Settings → Workspace's projects); the Workspace Overview's table by project (by tokens; a row opens the project's Overview); a project Overview's table by agent. **Left as they are**: About, the shortcut cheat sheet overlay, the Files tab's file details and a session's details (label and value lists), the editable price and model-fallback tables, hidden projects, a template's agents (a form), Markdown and CSV previews, and Compare's per-scenario measures inside an opened row, and the Assistant panel's **Done by the Assistant** (#301): its last 3 changes at a fixed height under its status line (#312, #399), in a side panel, where a table's headers, filter row and paging would take more room than its rows; and it lists only this run's changes (up to 200, in memory), so there is little to sort or page. It (and the session lists) update per **Settings → Sessions → Overview updates**: **Live** (default: as sessions change, at most every 15 seconds, only while shown), **Every minute**, or **Only on Refresh**; the Overview has a Refresh button. A session list reads each project and session file once, and nothing of a transcript but its size and, for a record not yet known to be a sub-session, its first line (#1649): it finds each transcript once (Claude Code's projects folder read again only when it changed), Combwork's backups from their two folders' names, a few sessions at a time; a transcript is read when its session is opened. **The other sessions** (HI-1681: those the CLIs keep for the folders the host's sessions ran in, not started by Combwork) are read beside Combwork's: each CLI leaves Combwork's own sessions out by id before looking at their files, reads a transcript folder's names again only when the folder changed, opens only a transcript it hasn't seen (Codex's session_meta, Claude Code's first line, kept by time) and stats only the rest. **Combwork's first**: the Sessions tab's first load shows Combwork's sessions from their records (`session:list` with `own`), with *Looking for sessions started outside Combwork…* above them, and the whole list when it comes: they show only while the whole list's load runs, which alone says how it ended (its 60 s limit included), and without deleted sessions' usage, which only adds to totals. **One at a time** (#1646): a view starts no update while its last one is under way (asked meanwhile, one more once it ends), and main runs one listing per host at a time, callers asking meanwhile sharing one more of Combwork's sessions after it and joining the other sessions' listing under way (HI-1681: nothing tells Combwork when those change, and one more after it doubled the wait); a load with no answer after 60 s shows as failed ("no answer after 60 s"), with Retry, never a spinner without end. A listing over a second is logged with where its time went.

**Workspace Overview** (activity bar, Ctrl+Shift+O): the same summary for the window's workspace.
