A period (Today, 7 days, 30 days, All time; **7 days** by default, kept while Combwork runs), then a strip with the board's cards per column, stalled and blocked (each opens the board); the summary (tokens, API-equivalent cost, sessions, prompts) across every project **and the Assistant**; for 7 and 30 days a chart of tokens per day **stacked by project** (the six that used the most in the period, in name order so each keeps its colour while the set stays the same, the rest as "Other (n)"; a legend, and each day's numbers by project on hover; colours from a validated categorical order stepped for each theme); every running agent (the project's name and the agent's, click opens it; the Assistant's opens its panel); a sortable table **by project** (sessions, tokens, cost, share of the tokens, last active; the Assistant is its own row; click opens that project's Overview, or the Assistant view); and a section per provider with its totals and plan limits. Hidden and removed projects aren't counted (a note says how many). The sidebar lists each project with its cost for the period. It uses the project Overview's counting (`shared/usageTotals.ts`) and its update setting, and only while shown; main sends only what totals need (`workspace:usage`: each project's and the Assistant's Combwork sessions, with deleted sessions', no sessions started outside Combwork), from the usage history (no transcript is read, nor looked up). While the history imports the workspace's sessions the first time, a note under the summary says how far it is ("Importing the usage history: 120 of 283 sessions") and that the figures are partial; they fill in as it goes, and are read again when it ends, whatever the update setting. In a narrow window its period buttons go under the title and wrap, the summary cards stack, and only the table by project scrolls sideways (#252). Down to a few dozen pixels of page (the sidebar and the Assistant open in a small or zoomed window), both Overviews keep everything with less padding: words break rather than push the page sideways, and the board strip, the period buttons and the cards take a row each (#269). The project Overview's session details (model, CLI version, started, last activity) keep their labels whole and their values a readable width, and scroll in their own box (#307). Budgets, alerts, export and comparing periods are not in it.

**Re-cache estimate on resume**: if time since last activity exceeds the TTL, "Resume will re-cache ≈ N tokens" (N = current context size); otherwise "cache likely warm (≈ M min left)". Always labelled as an estimate. Resuming a session whose cache has expired with more than 20k tokens asks first: **Archive and Start Fresh** (archives it and starts a new session in the same agent) or **Resume**.

**Transcript backups**: while a session is live Combwork brings its copy in `<Project>/.combwork/sessions/` up to date at most once a minute while it changes, at the end of every turn (`Stop`) and when the session exits, so sessions survive Claude Code's own cleanup. Transcripts only grow, so while the copy is still the start of the transcript (same first and last 4 KB at its length) only the new bytes are appended; otherwise (the first copy, a rewritten transcript) the whole file is copied to a temp file and renamed into place (`syncCopy` in `fsutil.ts`, one at a time per copy). A failed backup is retried at the next look. Archiving moves the backup to `.combwork/archive` and brings it up to date the same way.

**Compressed backups** (#1110): once a session ends (its CLI exits) or is archived, its backups are gzipped, `<id>.jsonl` to `<id>.jsonl.gz` (2,465 MB of real backups became 723 MB, 3.4×, in 23 s on one core; text alone shrinks about tenfold, pasted images little), written beside it and renamed into place, the plain file removed only after (`transcriptFiles.ts`); never while it runs or is starting, nor while its files move (archive, delete, Clean Up), and with its backups locked. Backups of sessions that ended before this, or whose compression was missed, are compressed in the background once the usage history's import is done and at each ten-minute sweep, one at a time, the oldest first, skipping sessions active in the last ten minutes. Everything that reads a backup reads either kind through `transcriptFiles.ts`: the transcript viewer, its search, images and export, usage (the usage worker too), a sub-session's first line. A resume that needs the backup (the CLI deleted its transcript) decompresses it where the CLI looks, the only time it is decompressed; while the resumed session runs its backup is plain `.jsonl` again, copied from the CLI's transcript, and compressed at its end (where both exist, the plain one is the newer). Archiving and unarchiving decompress first (a plain copy beside a compressed one wins), move as before, and compress after. A temp file a crash left behind is swept with the other stores' after a day (`leftovers.ts`, `sessions` and `archive`).

**Keep transcript backups** (#1110, Settings → Sessions, `sessions.backupRetention`: **Always** (the default), 30, 90 or 180 days, or 1 year): Combwork's copies (active and archived) of a session last active longer ago than that go to the Recycle Bin (`trash()`), checked after the usage history's import and at each ten-minute sweep (`applyRetention`). **Only where the CLI still has the session's transcript**, so it can still be opened and resumed from there, and only once the usage history has recorded what it used; a session whose only copy is Combwork's backup is never touched (Darren's decision via the Assistant, 20 Oct: deleting those stays the user's, with Delete Session, Clean Up or the purge). Running sessions and those whose files are moving are skipped; each is checked again with its backups locked, just before they go. The session's record stays.

**Memory tab**: grouped by provider. Claude Code: `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, the user `CLAUDE.md` and its auto-memory folder for the project. Codex: `AGENTS.md` and the user `AGENTS.md`. A file not there yet opens with a starter naming whom it applies to (HI-2667, the row's `scope`; English, for its agents): a project's file `# <project>` and "Instructions for {provider} in this project.", a connection's `# <connection>` and "Instructions for {provider} agents on this connection, in every project.", the user's `# All projects` and "Instructions for {provider} in every project." When a project's agents use more than one provider and they don't read the same instructions, **Share one AGENTS.md…** makes AGENTS.md the shared file: CLAUDE.md gets an `@AGENTS.md` import line (anything else in it stays, for Claude Code only); with no AGENTS.md yet, CLAUDE.md's content moves into it first, so nothing is lost. Providers declare the import line in their descriptor (`instructionsImport`); those that read AGENTS.md themselves need none.

**Usage history** (#1106, Darren's decisions of 19 Oct): what sessions used is historical and only ever added to, so it is recorded once, as it happens, and every usage view reads the record rather than the CLIs' transcripts. Kept in the workspace's `.combwork/usage.db` (§4.1), beside `combwork.db` and its session records, under each host's scope (a project's id; `assistant` for the Assistant). A file of its own (Darren, 20 Oct, replacing "inside `combwork.db`"), so its writes never wait on a board change (those hold their transaction across awaits), never look like another process's change to the board's poll, and an older Combwork still opens `combwork.db` for writing. Real tables, every value a typed column (Darren, 20 Oct: no JSON in the database); the parser's saved state is the one blob: `usage_sessions` (a row a session: who, where it was read, its state, and what isn't a sum of its rows: title, model, CLI version, context, activity), `usage_rows` (keyed by scope, session, day, model, card and role; indexed by scope and day for the Overviews, and by card), `usage_compactions`, `usage_safeguards` (stops by model, those it may have asked about by turn), `usage_timeline` and `usage_charges` (its use over time and the provider's charges), `usage_baseline` (what was counted for it before, by day: below), `usage_meta` (the import's record).
- **What is recorded**: a row per session, local day, model and card it worked on (and its role on it): tokens by kind, requests, prompts, compactions, the part of the cost known as an amount (the provider's charges, each split between the requests it covers by Combwork's estimate, else tokens, requests or equally) with the tokens it covers; beside them, the session's summary (title, model, CLI version, context, compactions, safeguards, first and last activity, who it was) and its timeline (a lane's cost, and the cards shared out again when their holds change). Costs are worked out when shown, with the prices of the time, so a price change or **Use my prices** needs nothing more; a kept usage imported from before keeps the cost it was priced with. A card's rows are its share of the session's use while the session's agent held it (`TaskCard.held`, by the agent's id; by name for a hold from history), shared equally while it held several (≈); the rest of each day is card 0, so a day's rows add up to the day, in whole tokens and requests (shared out by largest remainder: a request shared by two cards is still one). Keyed by card and session, never by an agent's folder. When a session's cards' holds change (a card moved while it runs, or after it stopped: a hold that ended within its last request's second), its rows are shared out again from its stored timeline, its file not read again; the key it was shared by (`holds_key`, open holds as open) says when. A job of its own does it for every recorded session of the workspace, running, stopped or deleted, after each board change (a second apart at most), after the import, and before cost per card or per lane is read; holds are worked out once per agent.
- **How it is recorded**: a worker thread (`main/usageWorker.ts`, its own `node:sqlite` connection; WAL, so main and other readers never wait for it, and another Combwork's worker waits up to the busy timeout) reads only what a transcript added since it was last read, taking up the parser's saved state (its fields, kept for the file and the bytes it was made from: the same path, at least as long, the 4 KB before its offset unchanged, and the Combwork version and parser shape that saved it; anything else, or a read from the start or of another file, lets it go and reads from the start), and writes the session's rows in one short transaction. Main keeps the queue (`main/usageHistory.ts`), one job in the worker at a time, most urgent first: a session about to be deleted, then running sessions (at each turn's end, a tick about every minute, as each ends, and when the board changes for its cards' holds: the views lag by up to a tick), then the import and the sweeps. The parser's state is kept as a session ends and at most every ten minutes while it runs (states of sessions unused for two weeks let go). A **sweep** (every ten minutes, and after a workspace's import) reads what changed while Combwork wasn't reading: a record the history doesn't have yet (an adopted session), a file that grew (a session continued outside Combwork). Usage history is only added to: each session has a **baseline**, what was counted for it before, by day (a kept usage imported from before the history; or what its rows had when a later read counted less of something, a backup that lags the transcript it replaced, a file cut short or rewritten), and its rows never go below it, each day, in any count (tokens by kind, requests, prompts, compactions) nor in the charges the provider reported (a kept usage: the cost it was kept with; Combwork's estimates aren't kept, they are priced again when shown): what a read lacks is a `kept` row of that day on card 0. A read replaces the rows only when it counts at least as much in every one of those, reported charges included (a rewrite that lost a cost report never erases the charge; a charge is kept with the tokens it paid for, as one record, and restoring it marks those tokens covered on the day's rows, so the same use is never estimated again on top of it, with the amount shared between those rows as any charge is, so a card has the charge for its tokens, never them for free; only an amount no row's tokens took stays on card 0). Every write makes a session's rows the same way (`sessionRows`: its base rows, read from its file or shared out again from its stored timeline, with its baseline applied), so reading its file again, importing a kept usage or sharing its cards out again never changes what it counted or cost, only which card each part is on; otherwise what the rows had joins the baseline first. No snapshot wins over another by a sum, so nothing either counted is lost. A file that is there but can't be read (held, no permission, a disk error) is `failed`, never taken as unchanged: a delete then keeps the session. A session another Combwork recorded meanwhile is left as it wrote it.
- **The import** (once per workspace, recorded in the history): each record's transcript (or Combwork's backup), newest first, so recent periods fill first; each record's kept usage (`keptUsage`, into its baseline: a stale backup never loses what was kept); each deleted session's kept usage (`deletedUsage`). Nothing already counted is lost, and those lists stay where they were (no longer written or read once the import is done). It is recorded as done only when every session was imported: one that failed (the worker ended, a write another Combwork held) leaves it not done, nothing retired, and it runs again at the next open or ten-minute tick; so does an interruption (Combwork quit, the workspace closed). Either way what was imported is skipped. Delete and Clean Up record a session first, its kept usage too, even before the import reaches it, and keep it when that can't be done. Its progress shows in the Workspace Overview, whose figures are partial meanwhile. Done, `usage-cache.json` (§4.3) is removed.
- **Who reads it**: the Workspace and project Overviews, deleted sessions' totals, the Sessions list and a session's usage (`session:usage`, `GET …/usage`) for a session that isn't running, Performance's provider usage, cost per card and per lane. The Workspace Overview and Performance read running sessions from the history too (their last turn's end or tick: no transcript is read for them); the Sessions list and the project Overview take a running session's as its pane does (#1157: from the history, a CLI's `/rename` showed there only at the next turn's end or tick), the usage worker's read of its transcript (below), asked only when the file changed, so main reads no transcript for them either; cost per card and per lane first record the running sessions' latest use and share cards out again (and wait for sessions that just ended), as they are read when asked. A running session's own footer and gauge, and its usage asked for alone (`session:usage`), follow each turn from its transcript as it grows, read by the usage worker, never in main (#1147), from where its last read stopped; after a restart (a session resumed) from the session's parser state saved in the history, so only what was added since is read. The worker's jobs for that session go on from the same parser, so a running transcript is parsed once. **Settings → Sessions → Usage cache size** (5,000 transcripts; 100–50,000) bounds the worker's in-memory reads, least recently used first, with the parsers themselves limited to 200; **Clear the usage cache** forgets them (the history and its saved states stay). Lists and views only ever read the history: a session it doesn't have yet (its import under way, one just started, a session started outside Combwork whose file changed) is queued for the worker and shows its kept usage, or none, until the worker has it and tells the window (`usage-changed`; such a list item is `pending`, and the project's lists read again 1.5 s after each such word while any is, whatever the update setting), so no transcript is parsed in main for them. A session's usage asked for alone that the history doesn't have yet is read from its transcript, by the worker too.
- **Old sessions' timelines in 1-hour steps** (HI-1648, Darren's decisions of 27 Oct): a session last active longer ago than **Settings → Advanced → Usage history: keep full detail for** (`cw.usage.timelineDetailDays`, 14 days by default, 1 to 3,650) has its timeline merged into 1-hour steps per model and flags, as `boundTimeline` merges a long one (`coarsenTimeline`, `shared/usageTimeline.ts`): tokens, requests and charges stay exact (charges sharing an hour become one, their sum), and only where a share of it began or ended inside an hour blurs (a lane's span, or its cards shared out again after their holds change). Its rows (`usage_rows`, what every usage view, card cost, Performance and the Overviews add up) aren't touched. Done in the usage worker, never on main: at a workspace's opening (after the import) and about daily, in batches of about 50 ms queued behind other work, each session in its own transaction (checked again inside it: still that fine and that old), never a running session's; Combwork's log says how many sessions and rows it merged. Then the space goes back to the disk: a file from before this (`auto_vacuum` off) is vacuumed whole once, which makes it incremental; after that `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum` gives back the free pages, and a WAL checkpoint (TRUNCATE) shrinks the file at once. Measured on a copy of a busy workspace's history: 91 sessions' 7,609 old rows became 222, in 57 ms; the one vacuum took 0.44 s and the file went from 63.3 MB to 44.9 MB (most of it 3,636 pages already free), its totals identical. Most of what was left was the parsers' saved states of recent sessions (28 MB in `usage_sessions`), not the timeline: since HI-1912 a state keeps only what the parser reads of each request (Claude Code's four token counts, not its whole usage block) and is saved brotli-compressed (quality 4), its format part of its shape so one saved another way is read afresh. On the same copy the 277 states went from 28.3 MB to 1.9 MB (the largest from 3.4 MB to 0.19 MB, saved in about 6 ms and taken up in about 5 ms rather than 10) and the file, vacuumed, from 44.9 MB to 18.4 MB.
- Sessions started outside Combwork are kept in it too (source `external`), for the Sessions list, which reads one again only when its file changed; they never count in totals, and one adopted is Combwork's from its next record. Purging what Combwork keeps is its own card (#1138); it never clears the usage history, which always stays (Darren, 20 Oct).

**Busy actions** (a shared pattern: `useBusy()`, `BusyButton` and `Modal`'s `busy`/`error`; `confirm({ run })`; `runOnce()` for buttons without a dialog): while an action runs its button shows a spinner and an "…ing" label, the dialog's other controls are disabled, Escape, × and clicks outside don't close it, and repeat clicks do nothing; a failure keeps the dialog open with the error (the button offers **Try Again** where it helps). Used by Start, Remove Project (its label says what it does: Hiding…, Removing from Combwork…, Moving to the Recycle Bin…; no stages reported), the card's Save, Delete, Archive and Comment, Compact, Agent Settings, Stop All Agents, Delete note and Delete MCP server; Resume All and Remove Agent show a spinner on their button or tab. **Starting and resuming an agent** (#1177): from the click until `session:start` answers (the session runs, or the start failed) the agent is marked starting in the window (`whileStarting`, `starting` keyed by project and agent, with the session resumed); the button clicked shows a spinner and "Resuming…" or "Starting…" (Retry Setup and Start Without Setup each their own) and is `aria-busy`, and every other way to start that agent (its pane's buttons, its menus, the Assistant's panel and header, the project's menu, the project header's Resume and Agents ▾ starts, the Sessions tab's Resume of a session it would run) is disabled meanwhile; a second start of an agent already starting is ignored. Asking first (a running session to stop, an expired cache) counts as part of it, and so does adding an agent for it (a project without agents, a session no agent can run: held under the project, `ADDING_AGENT`, then under the agent added). In main, a start that takes over a second logs which steps took over a second (`StepTimes`: `[sessions] Resume of <agent> in <project> took 43.1 s: usage 42.0 s`), and the usage worker logs a query (one it answers at once, not after its jobs) that took over a second to answer, so a slow start can be traced to its step. A start never waits for the usage history's import: nothing in it waits for the worker's job queue, and the one read it makes of the session's transcript (for a name given in the CLI) is `noWait`, so the worker answers it with nothing rather than queue it behind the import's turn on that file (the name is then adopted at a later resume) (`tests/startDuringImport.test.ts`, which holds the import inside that turn). Questions (confirm, choose, prompt) render above every other dialog, and Escape closes only the topmost dialog.
**Dialogs dim the window buttons.** A backdrop (`.overlay`: a dialog, nested or not, or the command palette) dims the whole page, but Windows paints the native minimise, maximise/restore and close buttons over it (`titleBarOverlay`). So the page tells main how many backdrops are up (`useBackdrop()` keeps them per window, in order; `window:setBackdrops`), and main dims the buttons' background and symbols the same way: black at the backdrop's 45% once for each, as the page's layers stack (`shared/titleBar.ts`; a question over a card is two), back to the theme's colours when the last one goes. The same stack decides which backdrop Escape is for: the top one only, so Escape with the palette over a card closes the palette. Main keeps each window's theme colours and dimmed state (`main/titleBar.ts`), so a theme change while a dialog is up stays dimmed in the new theme's colours, each window is on its own, and a page that reloads starts undimmed. The buttons keep working, and Windows still highlights them on hover. The overlay exists on Windows and Linux only; elsewhere there is nothing to dim.

**Footer usage belongs to its conversation**: the usage an agent's footer shows (context, cost) is held with the project and session it was read for (`src/shared/liveUsage.ts`); after a switch it shows `– ctx` until the new conversation's own usage is read, never the previous one's, and a refresh that fails keeps the same conversation's numbers, faded, with a note in the tooltip.

**Transcript size**: a running agent's live state carries its transcript's size (`transcriptBytes`, from the 5-second look). The pane footer shows it next to the context count ("6.1 MB"), orange from **Settings → Sessions → Warn when a transcript is over** (20 MB; per-project override; **Never** turns it off; a 50 MB saved by 0.3.x or earlier, the old default, is moved to 20 MB once, config version 5). A long transcript slows the CLI and Combwork (each turn, resume and transcript view reads more), and compacting doesn't shrink it, since the file keeps the whole history. Crossing the limit notifies once per conversation (a toast, and a desktop notification under the usual settings, no chime); **an agent in a turn is told at its turn's end** (HI-1695, Darren's option 1, 26 Oct: a transcript grows only in a turn, so it is nearly always crossed in one, and a notice made then had no Hand Over to…, never offered again): the look at the turn's end, or the next 5-second one, makes it, with the button when the agent may hand over then. **It informs, and offers Hand Over only when that can't disrupt the agent** (#1057, Darren, 18 Oct; a queued "hand over after this card" is #1067, after 0.9.0): "Its transcript is 24 MB (over 20 MB): it may slow down", then **Hand Over to…** only while the agent **may hand over now** (`handOverNow` in `shared/handOver.ts`, with the lanes in `src/main/handOverCheck.ts`: ready or finished, no background tasks that will wake it, no merge slot held or waited for, and not the builder or reviewer of a running lane); otherwise no button, only "It can hand over to a new conversation when it has finished". The footer's size says the same in its hover, and a click on it does the same as the button. **Checked when clicked** (`session:mayHandOverNow`; a notice can be old by then): still allowed, Hand Over to… opens with the agent itself chosen (its transcript over the limit); no longer, a notice says the agent is busy and nothing opens. **The hand-over itself checks too:** to the agent itself it is refused (`session.handOver.notNow`; 409 from the Agent API) unless it may hand over now, Hand Over to… doesn't offer the agent itself then (the choice disabled, its note saying why), and **just before the conversation ends** it checks again, since writing the handover takes minutes: the same launch, no merge slot, no running lane, and no other work (no turn begun after the handover file was written, no more than the one turn the request began since it was asked, no background tasks that will wake it, nobody asked; with no new handover, no turn running). If anything changed, its conversation isn't ended (`session.handOver.momentLost`, the handover kept). The Assistant sees `transcriptMB` and `transcriptWarnMB` in `cw_agent_activity`. For the Assistant itself the notice says it can start a new conversation (⋯ → New Conversation) once idle, with no button, and the click does nothing. The Sessions tab (a project's, and the Assistant's) shows every session's transcript size beside its context (`transcriptBytes` in `session:list`, #671): a stat of the CLI's own transcript (Claude Code's, Codex's rollout, Copilot's events) each time the list loads (it opens, or a session changes), never a read; amber past the same limit, with a tooltip suggesting a handover (the Assistant: a new conversation); **—** when the file is missing or can't be read.

All parsing lives in the adapter, tolerates unknown fields, and degrades to "unavailable".

---

### 9.1 Performance metrics

Combwork counts what its own parts cost, locally, per workspace (`metrics.ts`; the contract and units are in `shared/metrics.ts`), so a change to its guidance or API can be judged by what it does to real use. **On by default** (Settings → Sessions → **Record performance metrics**); turned off, nothing new is recorded and what was recorded stays until **Reset performance metrics**. Kept **30 days**: hourly buckets for 7 days, folded into daily ones after, in the workspace's database, `.combwork/combwork.db` (#1019: a row a bucket, so a save writes the hour under way and any bucket folded or new, never the whole history; git-ignored, this machine's; at most 32 MB measured as the buckets' JSON, what their rows hold (HI-2628: 2 MB, the old `metrics.json`'s cap, kept a busy workspace to about 5 days): past it the oldest buckets go, each trim logged with what it dropped and the time it covered, and the page says history was removed), saved 30 seconds after a change, when the workspace closes and when Combwork quits. A `.combwork/metrics/metrics.json` from before is read at the first open and moved in by the first save, with the same numbers, then kept as `metrics.json.imported-<time>`; one found after that (an older Combwork's) is kept the same way, unread. Retention is applied whenever the data is loaded or read, however long Combwork was idle, and what expires is removed from the file too (a read that changes nothing writes nothing); a store holds at most 201 buckets whichever way the clock moves, and buckets dated more than a day ahead (a clock that was ahead) are dropped. A workspace's metrics file has one writer at a time across openings: a workspace reopened (by any window, its path in any case) while its last save is still going continues with that same store, so a Reset or new records can't be overwritten by the older save. The size cap is in UTF-8 bytes, even if only one bucket is left. The saved data is untrusted input: a `metrics.json` from before over 2 MB isn't read (the read itself stops at the cap), and every bucket, series, counter and label in it is checked as it is loaded (what isn't valid is skipped).

- **What is measured, in exact units**: UTF-8 bytes; characters as UTF-16 code units (JavaScript string length); milliseconds on a monotonic clock (the wall clock only picks the bucket, so a clock set back lands in an earlier hour). **No token estimates**: provider token usage is only ever what the provider reported.
- **Agent API**: requests by route template (never the path asked for), method, caller role (agent, Assistant, script) and outcome (ok; refused, a 409: a workflow rule or a guard said no and what to do instead; invalid, a wrong call: any other 4xx but 401 and 403; denied, 401 or 403; server error, a real error; client error, a 4xx recorded before HI-2553 sorted them, its kind not known; cancelled: a client that went away before the reply; waiting: a reply that says to ask again, as an isolated check's resolve does while no check copy is free, HI-1831, never counted as a failure, and before HI-1831 recorded as a client error, so older history still shows those waits as client errors); count, a latency histogram, request body bytes as received (a partial or refused body as far as it came) and response body bytes as serialized (an aborted reply may not all have been sent; headers and transport not included). A refused or invalid series also counts its requests by **reason** (HI-2553, `reasonOf()` in `metrics.ts`): the workflow rule's id (`rule:<id>`) or the error's message id (`msg:<id>`; an agent message's, `agent:<id>`, HI-2681: the Agent API's own errors keep their message's id, `HttpError`'s `saidId` from `apiSaid()`, as a text's `said` part does; HI-2691: so do the services' agent messages thrown behind it, a `SaidError` from `saidError()` in `combworkError.ts`, its message exactly `say()`'s, its id kept when `httpFrom()` wraps it; HI-2704: so do the shared checks' refusals, a `Said` from `sayWithId()`, and every error of Combwork's gives its status as a `kind` where it is thrown, the same whatever its values, `statusFor()` reading only errors that aren't Combwork's own), never its text, `other` without either; at most 12 a series, the rest `other`. They are a field of the series, not a family of their own, so an older Combwork reading the same database ignores them. Requests refused before Combwork knew whose they were, event streams (connections, events, bytes, time open) and requests in flight are process-wide, not any workspace's. The health check and the bridge's own reports aren't counted.
- **Combwork tools (MCP)**: the bridge reports each call's final text, the one the model got (characters and UTF-8 bytes), its time, outcome and mode (compact, or detail when the call asked for it). A failed call's outcome is its **kind** (HI-2553, `failureOf()` in `cw-mcp.ts`): `refused` (the Agent API's 409, 401 or 403), `invalid` (another 4xx, or the bridge's own check of the arguments), `failed` (a real error: a 5xx, no reply, a timeout, a fault in the bridge); `error` is a failed call recorded before HI-2553, its kind not known. Once a session start it reports the tool list as its CLI got it (its JSON's UTF-8 bytes and characters, and `upfrontBytes`, Combwork's estimate of what a CLI that defers MCP tools gets at the start if it does: the tools Combwork marks to be sent in full and the others' names as a JSON list, HI-2553, never an observation: whether a launch's CLI deferred (Claude Code's tool search can be off by a setting, a model or a gateway) and how it worded the list aren't observable; counted by the **provider** of the launch its token is for, or the Assistant's session, `unknown` before HI-2553 or once that launch has ended; providers say whether their CLI defers, `capabilities.defersMcpTools`: Claude Code does, Codex and Copilot get the whole list; and of those characters the tools' descriptions and their parameters' descriptions, every `description` string in an inputSchema, each as the JSON has it, escapes included: HI-2063, `shared/toolListSize.ts`; the rest is the schemas and the list's structure), counted on the workflow role of the launch its token is for (HI-2049: `unknown` once that launch has ended or another has replaced it, so a late report never takes the next launch's role; an older bridge's, with no characters, counts its start in `starts`, not `charStarts`, so the characters' average is over the starts that had them; one from before HI-2063 has no parts, so they average over `partStarts`, with those starts' own characters, `partToolsChars`. Parts come both or neither, with the characters, and add up to no more than them, else the report is refused). The Performance view's **Combwork tool list** table shows it a start per provider, role and workflow role (tools, characters, descriptions, parameters, schemas, bytes, and **If deferred**: `deferredEstimate()`, the estimate with ≈, for a CLI whose descriptor can defer, `capabilities.defersMcpTools`, only, a dash for one that gets the whole list or a provider not known; a dash where it wasn't measured), with a tip on deferral and caching (the list sits at the start of the prompt, where a provider's prompt cache can keep it; whether it did isn't measured). A budget keeps it lean: `tests/e2e/replysize.cjs` fails when an agent's or the Assistant's list grows past it, raised only on purpose, and Copy Diagnostics each open workspace's last 24 hours of it, counts only. Reported with the session's own token (an agent's or the Assistant's), checked and bounded (at most 50 calls a report; a malformed one is refused, not stored), and never counted again as API traffic. Reports never hold the bridge up: one at a time, each with its own 3-second deadline, at most 500 calls waiting; a report that fails or times out drops what is still waiting, so a bridge whose CLI has gone exits within one deadline.
- **Guidance**: each launch's Combwork-supplied parts, exact sizes, by provider, role and **workflow role** (HI-2049, `launchWorkflow()` in `shared/workflow/roles.ts`, taken once as it launches: its part in its project's running lanes, which wins over its own role, builder of one lane and reviewer of another being `either`; else its own role, builder, reviewer or either; `none` for a generalist and the Assistant; series recorded before it are `unknown`), each part apart (`launchParts()` in `guidance.ts`): **core** (the session contract, once, whichever way the provider gets it), **custom** (what Combwork adds for the project: the latest handover's pointer), the Assistant's **role** (who it is, the workspace, Control's rules) and its **mode** (text that isn't as expected is counted whole, never split by guesswork), the skills that reached the session, measured on the copies its CLI reads, not their sources (how many, their catalog entries' bytes, their bytes on disk; a model reads a skill's body only when it uses it, which isn't observable), how many skills asked for didn't reach it (too big, a link that can't be made, a failed copy, a broken header), and how many it got whose copy couldn't be measured (`skillsUnmeasured`: gone, unreadable, or a header that isn't a valid skill header; left out of the sizes, unknown rather than zero).
- **Skill service**: scans (timed), shared scans, hits, misses, invalidations, skills too big to check, and the files, bytes, header bytes and directory entries it read: the workspace's, not any project's.
- **Provider usage**: what the providers reported for sessions active in the range (as the Overview has it), summed per provider and whose sessions they were (project agents' or the Assistant's; scripts have none, and the report says so): each session's total, labelled as such, how many are running now, requests, compactions, and context as a snapshot (each session's last request: how many reported one, average, largest, the largest window), never summed. Its cells are one or two deliberate lines (#241, `CellLines` in `components/DataTable.tsx`): Sessions the count over "n running · n unknown", Context the average over "max of window", Cost "≈ $…" over "+ n unknown"; a table's numbers never wrap (`.table td.num`), and a table too wide for its section scrolls in its `.table-wrap`. A session with none reported is unknown, not zero: left out of the totals and counted as unknown cost too (a row whose sessions are all unknown shows unknown, not $0). The workspace's own work and the Assistant filter keep the Assistant's sessions only; a project scope never has them. Session history that can't be read (a project's or the Assistant's) is counted, never named (`providersUnreadable` of `providersHosts`): the totals are partial, or unknown if none could be read, and the page says so even when there is nothing else to show; the next read that works reports in full again.
- **Coverage**: when Combwork observed the workspace (open in Combwork, recording on, since the last reset), kept with the metrics as up to 500 `[start, end]` stretches, extended by each record and query and every 5 minutes while the workspace is open (an unref'd tick; saved with the next save, never a write of its own), so it is right to within about 5 minutes; a longer gap starts a new stretch. Known boundaries are never joined over, however short the gap: recording turned off ends the stretch at that moment (the setting's change, or a touch that finds it off), the last window holding the workspace closing ends it (another window reopening it while it saves starts a new one), and a store loaded from disk starts a new one at its first use. History evicted to keep under the size cap or the bucket count (not by age) is unavailable, not idle: the store keeps `evictedThrough` (saved), observation before it is removed, and every report whose range reaches it says so (`coverage.evictedThrough`, the storage's own fact, no loss count). Expired with the buckets, cleared by Reset. A report has `coverage` (the range, the time observed in it, since when, how many stretches) and each trend point `observedMs`, so an unobserved slot reads as no data, not zero; rates are per hour observed.
- **Scope and attribution**: work is recorded in the workspace it started in (a workspace that is closing admits nothing new: its lifetime stays ended until it has fully closed): a request, launch, scan or read that is still going when its workspace closes (or its window opens another) is dropped, never recorded in the next one, and a metrics read that the workspace switches under is refused. An agent's work is its project's; the Assistant's, scripts' and the shared skill service's are the workspace's own, never spread over projects. A workspace query has each project's part and the workspace's own, which add up to its totals without counting anything twice; a project query has that project's part only (matched case-insensitively, as the API matches project names), and its `dropped` counts only that project's dropped measurements. Who lost measurements is itself bounded (as many owners as projects); past that a loss is untracked: a workspace report has that total (`droppedUntracked`), and a project report only says some losses couldn't be attributed (`lossesUnattributed`), with no count from other projects or the workspace, never a known zero. A project's own known losses are summed bucket by bucket. Project names are plain keys: a project called `constructor` or `__proto__` is like any other, and a name longer than 128 characters is kept under a bounded label of its own (its start, `|` and a hash of the whole name), matched the same way. `|` can't be in a project's name, so such a label never equals another project's name. A measurement that is only dropped (a cap was full) is still saved as a loss. An agent may read its own project's.
- **Bounds**: every label comes from a fixed set: the Agent API's route templates, the combwork MCP server's own tools (a list a test keeps equal to the server's), the provider ids; anything else is "(other)". Per hourly bucket at most 100 projects and 2000 series, what doesn't fit dropped and counted (`dropped`); catalog series and those whose labels are all "(other)" don't count against it (bounded by their keys). Folding a week-old day's hours into it keeps every total (HI-2628): a series the day has no room for goes into its family's "(other)" overflow series, keeping its role, outcome, mode or workflow side. Nothing stores a prompt, a body, a token, a URL or a path. Recording a request costs about 0.3 µs; a bucket at its series cap is about 430 KB; the collector has no timers while idle.
- **Performance view** (activity bar, after Workspace Overview; `views/Performance.tsx`, selection and totals in `shared/metricsView.ts`): the workspace's metrics, with a scope filter (sidebar or **Scope**: the whole workspace, the workspace's own work, or one project, queried as that project's scope), and a **Performance** tab in each project (after Overview) fixed to its project (no workspace or other-project data reaches it: its query is the project scope). Ranges **24 hours, 7 days, 30 days**; filters by role (agents, Assistant, scripts; the tab has agents only) and provider (launches and provider usage; the rest isn't per provider), kept per view and project while Combwork runs. Each filter sits with the sections it changes, never above ones it doesn't (#270): **Who** heads a framed group (`.perf-group`) of the cards, trend, tool, route, guidance and provider usage tables and the tool list; the skill service and Combwork-wide numbers are below it, outside. **Provider** heads a group inside it holding only the guidance table, the Combwork tool list (per provider from HI-2553) and provider usage, the parts recorded per provider (a provider still chosen keeps the group, saying "Nothing from it", even when the scope or range has nothing at all, so it can be seen and changed, #294) (the guidance per launch card and the trend's launches are every provider's). Role and own work go to Combwork with the query (`queryFor()`: `role`, `own` for the workspace's own work), which narrows the parts, the trend and the provider usage alike; the page's query has no provider (its key neither), and `select()` applies the provider to those two sections, so the filter's choices (`providersIn(report, chosen)`) are every provider with data in the scope, range and role, plus the current one, and switching provider needs no query. The load, **Export** and **Keep current view** all use that query (`pageQuery()`), so what is saved is what the page loaded, every provider's (each per-provider row names its provider), and its launches, trend and totals agree with the cards whatever provider is picked; a kept view says "every provider". What a filter can't narrow is said (`filters.notFiltered`: the skill service, Combwork-wide numbers and dropped measurements aren't per role). Cards (requests per hour observed, failure and cancelled shares apart, **Failures** by kind (HI-2553: real errors as its value, in red when there are any; refused by a rule, wrong calls and, when there are any, not sorted under it: refusals are the workflow working, not faults), p50/p95 from the histogram, bytes sent and received, tool characters and bytes, guidance per launch with the tool list a start and, ≈, what a CLI that defers tools gets at the start if it does), a trend (`trend` in the query: every hour of a range up to 2 days, else every day, at most 200 points, empty slots zero) of requests with real errors in red (a point's `errors`) and refusals, wrong calls and cancelled ones in a neutral colour, tables by tool (by characters) and route, each with **Refused**, **Wrong calls** and **Errors** (real ones, in red) and **Not sorted** when a row has failures from before HI-2553 (route: cancelled apart), the most common **refusals and wrong calls by reason** (route, kind, the reason as a general sentence, count; top 20: `views/perfReasons.ts` says a rule's refusal sentence or the message of a `msg:` id, found in the English catalogue loaded only then and said in the window's language, with its values left out, `trTemplate()`: placeholders “…”, a plural's general form; an `agent:` id's agent message from the agent-text catalogue, in English (agent text is never a window message), its values left out the same way (`englishTemplate()`), marked `lang="en"` with “· in English” beside its id; the id under it; `other`, no reason recorded), guidance (provider and role: per launch core, project, role, mode, skills, catalog, bytes on disk, not delivered or unmeasured) and provider usage (by provider and whose: sessions and running, tokens, reasoning shown as part of output, requests, context average and largest of the window, compactions, cost with ≈ when estimated and unknown sessions counted). Unobserved trend slots are hatched, partly observed ones shaded. The workspace scope adds the skill service and Combwork-wide streams. Coverage (range, retention, how long Combwork was recording in it and the gaps, dropped measurements, losses not attributed: shown for any project scope, from either entry) and what isn't measured are always shown, and a banner when recording is off. Refreshes every minute while shown and the window is visible, one request at a time, and a late reply for another scope or range is never shown; it reads through IPC (`metrics:query`), so looking at it records nothing. **Export** (`metrics:export`) saves the page's own query (scope, range, filters) as JSON (`schema: "combwork-metrics/1"`, Combwork's version, units, export time, range, filters, coverage, and the report with its trend) through a save dialog; Shift+click sanitizes it (project names become `project-N`, the same name the same number; no workspace path).
- **Compare** (#117; the Performance page's Now/Compare switch, `views/PerformanceCompare.tsx`, rules in `shared/benchmark.ts`, storage in `main/benchmarks.ts`): a baseline against a run, each a kept artifact of the page's scope. Sources: **Keep current view** (the page's own query as an export summary), **Import…** of a Performance export (`combwork-metrics/1`, kept as its summary) or a scenario benchmark (`combwork-benchmark/1`, written by `npm run scenarios`; 1.0's format is refused, HI-2611). Files are untrusted input, imported or kept alike (the same normalisers, a fresh bounded object, never the one read): read with a cap (at most 2 MB in UTF-8 bytes, however the file changes meanwhile), known measures only, bounded scenarios (100), samples (20), checks (60), skill revisions (60) and text; a series that isn't what it should be counts as none. Scopes: the whole workspace, **its own work** (the view with "Workspace's own work" chosen: its own list, never the whole workspace's) and each project (its tab, or the view with it chosen). A scenario benchmark is the whole workspace's only. A project's export must hold only that project's data (one also holding other projects' or the workspace's is refused, never summed); a workspace export's project part only after the page asks (sanitized ones, own-work ones and ones without that project are refused, and why); an own-work export must hold no project's. Up to 20 kept per workspace in `.combwork/metrics/benchmarks` (an index and one file each); each scope remembers its baseline and run (selections of scopes with nothing kept are dropped). Every operation is bound to the workspace it started in: its folder and lifetime are taken before any await (a dialog, a read, the queue), and one whose workspace closed or switched meanwhile is refused, never written into the next; a project-part answer is bound to that workspace, scope and lifetime, used once, within 10 minutes. The index is the only authority and records every change in progress: an entry being added (`adding`) or removed (`removing`), with its change's id. Keeping is (1) the index records the new entry as adding and the evicted ones (the oldest unpinned, when full; refused if all are pinned) as removing, (2) the file is written, (3) the new entry becomes kept; then each evicted file is removed and its entry dropped only once the file is gone. Remove is the same: recorded as removing (off the list), the file removed, then the entry dropped; a removal whose file can't be removed stays recorded, is retried on every read (also after a restart), is said, and never comes back to the list. The index holds at most 40 entries in all (kept, being added, being removed): the reader's bound, which every index Combwork writes is checked against first, and a keep that would pass it (removals piling up while their files stay in use) is refused, saying why, until they finish. Renames are retried while Windows holds a file for a moment, the workspace checked before every attempt, so a retry after it closed or switched commits, moves or sets aside nothing. Every write is staged and renamed into place only after the workspace is checked again, so a workspace that closes or switches during a write commits nothing. Every read first validates the whole index, then reconciles it with the folder, deleting only what that validated index proves: an add whose change never finished is rolled back (its file goes, what it evicted is kept again), and recorded removals are retried. A file the index doesn't account for (unreadable, or valid but unlisted) is never deleted: it is moved once to `quarantine/`, named by when it came there (time, then a sequence for the same moment), and the newest 100 so named are kept (the oldest by that time go, whatever their ids; other files there are left alone) and said, and an entry whose file is gone is dropped. A damaged index (not JSON, not an index, over 512 KB, an entry invalid or repeated, too many entries) is never acted on: it is set aside as `index.damaged-<time>.json` (the newest 10 kept) and rebuilt by adopting every valid kept file with what the old index still said about it (pin, when kept); invalid files and valid ones past the limit go to quarantine, so the rebuilt index accounts for every file and is stable afterwards; the page says it was recovered. An index that can't be read for another reason (permissions, I/O) is an error and nothing is written. A kept file whose scope doesn't match its index entry is refused. Comparable only when they measured the same thing: the same kind and scope; for benchmarks the same fixtures version, provider, fake or model, and for model trials the same model, effort and mode (CLI versions differ: a note); for exports the same filters and some recorded time on both. Otherwise **Not comparable**, with why, numbers shown. Benchmarks compare scenario by scenario on usable samples: completed, correctness known (a sample whose checks all skipped is unknown, never passed) and not stale (left-out ones said). Each measure has mean, min, max and n, the change and whether it is within the spread; a measure some sample didn't measure is **unknown** (no zero-filled totals: context and guidance exist only when every part is known) and isn't compared. Correctness first, check by check, the check list being authoritative (its counts are used; summary counts that disagree with it, a check listed twice, an entry that isn't a check, or more checks than can be read leave the sample's correctness unknown, and any failed check in it fails the sample): a check that passed or ran less often, or failed more often (one the baseline never had included), in the run is a regression (a fake's declared skips are skipped on both sides, so they aren't), shown with its counts and the run's failed checks; a regression is *smaller but failing* (less context) or *worse*. Otherwise more failed calls, tool errors, API failures or cancellations, more calls or retries, or more than 1% more context is *worse*; less context is *better*, else *same*; a scenario with a partial measurement (recording off or unknown, measurements dropped or missing) or an unknown failure measure is *incomplete*, not judged on size. Comparable also needs both runs' sources unchanged while they ran. Provider usage only between model trials (a fake's is simulated: said), only when every usable sample on both sides reported that field (unknown stays unknown, a resumed session's is the conversation's), cost only when both have one (≈ said when Combwork estimated it), reasoning its own row. The skill revisions each session was given are compared, and a difference (an edited skill) said. The page shows each side's provenance; while comparing it hides the live range and filters, which only shape **Keep current view**. Exports compare per hour recorded (guidance and the tool list's characters per launch as they are, each with each workflow role's launches, guidance and tool list a launch for the roles either side has: HI-2049), noting partial data and that real use isn't a controlled workload. A total that any damaged piece of the export adds to (a series that is missing, isn't a list, is too long to read, or has an invalid number) is unknown, said, and not compared; never zero. A late answer for another pair or scope is never shown. A scenario's measures are also split by agent (HI-2186): the subject (the Assistant, or the agent under test) and the other agents, each measured on its own, never one as the total less the other. The Assistant's from Combwork's metrics by caller role (every measure, only with whole coverage); an agent's tool calls and tool lists from the combwork servers' test log by agent, its API and launch measures unknown (the metrics don't say which agent). The log is used only when every served call and tool list in it is placed against the two snapshots by its own report (each line has an id; the server logs which ids each metrics report carried, and when it was sent and taken), so the window holds the very calls the metrics counted between them; a report that overlapped a snapshot, one not on record, or a line without an id leaves nothing from the log (unknown, never guessed). Each agent's Combwork calls in the window, by its fixture name (the subject first, at most 10 rows with an overflow row). Compare shows the parts in a scenario's details (the subject, the other agents, all agents: what the result judges) only when every usable sample on both sides has them, else the totals with a note; the result and the table's columns stay on the totals.
- **Scenario benchmarks** (`tests/scenarios`, developer tooling): each run writes `benchmark.json` with every scenario's samples: each check (passed, failed, skipped), failed checks, incomplete with a path-free reason, stale guidance, resumed, the guidance and skill revisions the session was given, the measurement's coverage (recording, dropped, what made it partial), and measures: Combwork's metrics before the launch and after the turn, the harness's own requests left out (context in parts with bytes and characters, tool replies, calls and repeated calls, failures, API traffic, delivered and undelivered skills, skill service work, time, and the session's provider usage as reported: a field it didn't report is left out). Fixtures v5 adds controlled pairs: **list-compact** / **list-detail** (the same cards, the compact list against the explicit detail form, the same required correctness) and **skill-unchanged** / **skill-changed** (a skill edited inside the measured window, `beforeLaunch`). Both fake providers act the scenarios out (`fake`, `fake-codex`); model trials are opt-in and record their model, setup and authorization. Model trials keep to `--budget` (a finite amount above 0): a trial that reports no cost makes the spend unknown, so no further trial starts unless `--allow-unknown-cost` is given, and the spend is the reported subtotal plus the unpriced trials, unknown in all (never $0). `--repeat N` (default 1), `--save-baseline NAME` (the new one read first and swapped in atomically; the older one archived under a name of its own, never overwritten, also when saved twice in a second; 5 kept), each run in a results folder of its own, the newest 30 fake runs and, counted apart, the newest 30 model trials kept (HI-2236: fake runs never push a paid trial's results out; besides those a card cites, and one a run still writes into, which no other run's start prunes: HI-2234; a run whose folder goes all the same makes it again with what it had written).
- **Cost per card and per lane** (#602, Darren's decision of 11 Oct; `shared/cardCosts.ts`, `main/cardCosts.ts`, `components/CardCost.tsx`, `views/PerformanceCards.tsx`). Usage is the card's while an agent **held** it: its builder (`TaskCard.agent`) while it is in Doing, its reviewer (`TaskCard.review`) from `review: "start"` to the verdict. Cards keep their holds (`TaskCard.held`: agent id, name, role, from, to; the newest 100), updated whenever a card is saved (`trackHolds` in `saveCard`), whoever changed it; a card from before #602 gets them from its history the first time (`holdsFromHistory`: "Given to", "Taken from", column moves, "Started reviewing" and verdicts; agents by name, the card's own agent and reviewer by id). The holds are left out of the Agent API's card views (lean replies). Each provider's parser also gives the session's usage **over time** (`SessionUsage.timeline`, `shared/usageTimeline.ts`): rows of a second (about one a request: Claude Code's requests, Codex's `token_count` increases, Copilot's requests), merged into 10, 100… second steps past 20,000 rows (`boundTimeline`: each step's charges merged into one, their sum, so a session with a charge per request is bounded too and no charge is lost; a hold taking part of a merged charge gets ≈; charges no request refers to are left out), with the **charges** the provider reported and which requests each covers (`reports`; a row's report index, or none): Claude Code's running total, each increase covering the requests since the last; Copilot's credits at each checkpoint, covering the requests since the one before (a checkpoint that charged nothing more covers its requests at $0). Copilot gives tokens only when a launch exits: until then its requests' tokens are **unknown** (`TOKENS_UNKNOWN`), and then the launch's total is spread over its requests (`TOKENS_SPREAD`, ≈). The timeline is kept in the usage history with the session's rows (#1106), and never travels with a session's usage. A hold's usage is its agent's sessions' timeline rows inside it (a row partly inside counts in part), worked out as each session is recorded: a card's cost is its rows in the usage history (each session's a part), and a lane's is sliced from the timelines there. Its cost: a charge is split only between the requests it covers (by Combwork's estimate for their tokens, else their tokens, their requests, or equally), so a later card never changes an earlier one's; exact where all of a charge's requests are in the hold, ≈ where the hold takes only some; requests no charge covers are Combwork's estimate (≈), and with the user's own prices (#436) everything is; no price, or no tokens to price yet, is unknown. Tokens are tracked apart from cost: unknown tokens are never shown as 0 ("tokens unknown", "+ unknown"), and shares Combwork worked out are ≈. While the agent held several cards at once, what it used then is shared between them equally (`sharedSpans`, ≈), so nothing counts twice. A hold's sessions are its agent's (by id; by name for one from history, also matching sessions whose record kept that name); a kept usage imported from before the history (a deleted session's, or one whose transcript went) has no timeline and is **unknown** where it was active in a hold, as is a hold whose agent has no session in the history. Estimates are marked ≈ and unknown parts shown as such (`costText`: "Unknown", "+ ?"), never $0. **Where it shows**: the card's panel ("cost: ≈ $1.84 · 2 rounds", rounds as `cardRounds`: none before it first went to Review, then each failed review and the round under way or passed; the builder's and reviewer's parts and tokens on hover); its **cost by round** (HI-1906, from HI-820's item 2; Darren kept it 27 Oct), the last part of the card dialog's Work section: a row per review round (#1226's `roundSpans` from the card's facts) and a Total row, each with the builder's and reviewer's parts and their sum. It **adds up to the card's cost**: each agent's part of the card's ledger rows (as cost per card counts them; unknown for an agent with no session) is shared out over the rounds it held the card in, by what its sessions' timelines give each (cost, else tokens, else time held, else equally: `shareRole`), and rows no hold's agent has go over the role's rounds, so a share is ≈. Use outside every round (a card adopted at the upgrade, held before its cycle began) is a **Before its rounds** row. What is shown is allocated once (`costCells`): the total rounded as the cost line rounds it (cents; whole dollars from $100), its units shared over every round's builder and reviewer parts by largest remainder, so each row, column and the Total add up as shown; a part with use but no unit shows "< $0.01" (or "< $1"). The exact amounts stay in the data (`costs:rounds`: `rounds`, `outside`, `total`), and `costOf` is unchanged. Only the card's own sessions' timelines are read (by its ledger rows' scope and session; on a busy workspace's copy, the busiest card's 49 sessions took 46 ms and 0.55 MB, against 429 ms and 6.35 MB for the project's 1,177). A card from before 1.0 has no rounds and shows its cost line only. A note says rounds older than the usage history's days of full detail may be split to the hour (HI-1648). The Overview and Performance's Cards table don't show it; the **lane's hover** (its top line in the Progress panel: the builder's and reviewer's usage from the lane's start to its end or now, split into on cards (holding any card) and **overhead** (holding none: merges, watching, compactions), and the cost per finished card); and Performance's sortable **Cards** table (cards held in the range, each card's whole cost as Provider usage counts whole sessions; a project's scope only its cards; none for the workspace's own work; outside Who's box, since it is agents' work of every provider). Read on request (`costs:cards`, `costs:lanes`), from the usage history: no transcript is read. Money by default (#436's prices), tokens on hover.
- **Safeguard stops** (#606): each session's stops by model, read from its transcript with its usage (`SessionUsage.safeguards`), summed per provider (Providers' **Safeguard stops** column, "not detected" for Copilot) and per project, agent and model (`MetricsReport.safeguards`, the **Safeguard stops** table below Providers; the Assistant as itself). A sanitized export names agents agent-1, agent-2… as it does projects. A stop seen only on screen (the prompt about one that left no transcript record) is counted from the session's record (`screenStops`, added by `usage()` unless the transcript recorded it in the same turn), so it counts during the launch and after a restart. Each row is the agent's name now (its name then once it is gone: `SessionRecord.agentName`, `KeptUsage.agentName`).
- **Not measured**, and said in every report (`notMeasured`): provider tokens per tool or guidance part, provider network traffic (Combwork isn't a proxy), context a CLI adds itself, whether a model read a skill, and HTTP headers.

### 9.2 Developer console

What each CLI actually sends Combwork, next to what Combwork made of it (#366: the CLIs are the most likely thing to break Combwork, and this shows what happens instead of ad-hoc probes). For power users and Combwork's developers. Built in three parts: the capture layer and the agents' read-only tool (#636), the console window (#637: Help → Developer Console and a shortcut, its own window, hidden until "Show developer features"), and recording to a file, Copy Diagnostics and contract tests (#638).

- **Sources** (`devConsoleSources.ts`): each agent's session (a project's agents and the Assistant), whether it runs or not (capture can start before it launches), and **Combwork itself** in a workspace. A session's events: its hooks (with the reply a PreToolUse got), status lines, transcript reads (the newest records and the details read from them, plan limits included), the terminal markers Combwork reacts to (the title asking for attention, the startup question, the prompt showing, the footer's mode), the lines Combwork types into it, its launch (the CLI, its version, the option names it was given from a fixed list of the CLIs' own, and how many other arguments: an option's value, inline or not, can be a prompt, so none is kept) and exit, and its own Agent API calls. Combwork's: Agent API calls (route template, caller, status, time, sizes; never a body), refused hooks, merge slot claims, releases and changes, watches waking agents, and Progress runs as they start, step on and end.
- **Each event is paired** with what Combwork made of it: a hook with the event Combwork took it for, the status that followed and the actions it ran; a status line or transcript read with the details read from it; a terminal marker with the status it set. A one-line summary in Combwork's own words goes with it.
- **Off unless the console is open** (`devConsole.ts`, #366 decision 4): a source is captured from the first console window watching it to the last; before and after, a capture point returns at once without building its event, and nothing is kept. The one exception is the flight recorder (below), and only while one of its triggers is on. Readers (agents' and the Assistant's Combwork tools) start nothing: they read what an open console has, and are told when it captures nothing. Each source keeps its newest **500 events or 1 MB**, in memory only; at most 40 sources a window and 50 windows; an event is never over 32 KB (its payloads cut to their outline, then to `<cut>`; names and summaries cut too); what waits to be sent to a window is bounded (500 events or 1 MB, the oldest dropped and counted in `dropped`).
- **Redacted at capture** (`shared/devConsole.ts`): payloads are copied field by field, and a field's context follows everything under it. A secret or sign-in field (tokens, authorization, cookies, logins, device and user codes) is `<redacted>` whole; under a text field (prompts, messages, replies, commands, titles, questions) no string is kept; elsewhere a string is kept only at a path listed for that kind of payload (`HOOK_FIELDS`, `STATUSLINE_FIELDS`, `TRANSCRIPT_FIELDS`, `DETAILS_FIELDS` and each capture point's own: a hook's envelope and its tool input's file path, a status line's model, a transcript record's type, model and tool names, Combwork's own fields) and only when it looks like an identifier, a path or a time: any other string, one word or many, is `<text: N chars>`, so a tool's arguments (a search query, a URL), an unknown record and an unlisted id, name or model stay hidden. Field names are matched by their words, however spelt (`idToken`, `api-key`, `Prompt`); a text field named as an envelope (a transcript record's `message`) keeps only the listed fields under it. Anything kept that looks like a token or key is masked too (`redact.ts`). Summaries and names are built from such safe values only (a Progress run's title, someone's text, stays hidden in its payload). Bounded: 40 items a list, 60 fields an object (names cut to 64 characters), 6 levels. A subscription may include text, the user's recordings (#638) and the console's windows while **Developer console: show text** is on (#699, below): it alone is sent a copy with text kept, secrets still masked; agents never.
- **Showing text** (#699): **Settings → Advanced → Developer console: show prompt, reply and command text** (`cw.console.showText`, off by default, a value of the advanced registry, §9.3) makes main subscribe the console's windows with text (`console:subscribe` takes no opt-in from the page: main decides from the setting), and a change applies to open windows at once (`DevConsole.setIncludeText`; turned off, what waits to be sent is dropped and the window reads its events again, redacted, so no text stays on screen). Only what is captured from then on has text: while a source has a subscriber with text, its events with text are kept in a second ring (same bounds, dropped with the last such subscriber), which only those subscribers read (`eventsFor`: a window's resume after a pause); the redacted ring stays the only one readers see. While it is on the window shows an **Unredacted** banner and its status bar says so, and the recording box starts ticked. **Never configurable:** secret and sign-in fields are masked whole as always, and the text kept goes through `maskText` (`redact.ts`). Its main rule (the Assistant's, after #699 round 3, replacing three rounds of a value scanner that let fragments through): **from a credential's name to the end of the string, everything is masked**, with no parsing of quotes, escapes, continuations or options: after a command-line option naming a credential and its separator (`--api-key k`, `--token=t`), a key naming one and its `:` or `=` (`token=t`, `password: p`, `Authorization: Bearer t`, `$env:API_KEY = k`, a key whose quotes are escaped as in a JSON string inside another), `-u user:…`, or `Bearer ` (`credentialStart`, the Assistant's rule after round 5: no regex, a single pass of direct character checks: each run of name characters, letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, is read once and holds a credential's word once its spaces, dots, underscores and dashes are taken out (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `csrftoken`, `x-api-key`), then the characters after it are checked for a key's closing quote and `:` or `=`, or an option's whitespace; a quoted name, whatever is in it (`'api key':`, `"token[0]":`, `"password/value":`), is read up to 100 characters ahead to the next quote of either kind and tested whole, `-u`'s user:password up to 256 after its quote; one that reaches its limit without a clear end (no closing quote, `:` or space) is masked from there whatever it holds, a quoted name once what was read names a credential (#705 round 3: no exact budget decides whether a password shows)). Losing what follows a secret (the flags after it, a URL's other parameters) is the accepted cost. A quoted name counts the same (the Assistant's rule after round 4): a JSON or Python key naming a credential at any depth, in a list, in malformed or embedded JSON, spelt with spaces or dots too (`"password":`, `'api key':`, `"api.key":`), masks everything after it to the end of the string, the JSON's other fields too, so no container can hide one (round 4 found a field-by-field JSON masking that an ordinary object or list swallowed). A payload Combwork holds as an object is masked by its keys instead (`redactPayload`'s field rules), not by this. Then: known token and key formats, JWTs, OAuth and signed-URL codes in a URL (`code=`, `state=`, `otc=`, `sig=`, `ticket=`, `nonce=`), long hex and base64 runs, email addresses, and sign-in codes no name announces: a device code standing alone (`ABCD-EFGH`) and a code after the words a sign-in uses (`enter QX7PL29KD`, `code: …`). Every pattern left starts only where its match can start (a word's or a run's start: a JWT only where its run starts, a base64 run not after a `+` or `=`), has no two quantifiers next to each other that can read the same characters, so a failed match never reads the same run again and masking is linear; the log's user-text marks stop at the next opening mark too. Unit tests bound it on every whitespace class, on long input shaped to make a backtracking pattern slow, and on a sweep of every pair of the characters the patterns care about and every credential prefix followed by long runs (200,000 characters each, where a quadratic pattern takes minutes; #699 round 5 found the credential-name regex's quoted-name escapes and `-u` lookahead, JWT, base64 and user-text marks quadratic, round 4 the email and sign-in-code patterns; since round 6 credential names use no regex at all), and on backslashes and quotes at 10k, 100k and 1M characters. A report goes through it line by line (Copy Diagnostics' log: a credential masks the rest of its line, and of the lines a backtick or backslash continuation carries it onto). It errs towards masking. In the console the text is cut to its cap (2,000 characters) first and then masked (the Assistant's rule after round 5: masking never reads more than is kept, and nothing past the cap is kept); a word the cut goes through is dropped whole, so no part of a secret too short to be recognised is kept. And it is the **last step over the whole event**, text kept or not (`makeEvent`: the event's name and summary, every payload string and every field name; the size bound after it only cuts), so a secret is masked wherever it sits, not only in the fields known to hold one; a source's label is masked too. Cookie headers (every cookie), and a device login's or signed URL's `otc=`, `sig=`, `ticket=`, `nonce=` are masked as well. A pattern it lacks goes into `redact.ts`, so the log and Copy Diagnostics get it too. **Agents' `cw_console` stays redacted** whatever it says (#366 decision 1: agents' access is read-only, redacted and bounded; the Assistant reads every agent of its workspace, so following the setting would hand it their prompts); a recording with text is still never attached to Copy Diagnostics, and Copy Diagnostics lists the setting among the advanced overrides by its id.
- **Agents and the Assistant** read it through `cw_console` (Agent API `/v1/console/…`), only while **Settings → Agent API → Let agents read the developer console** is on (off by default; read-only to the Assistant; the tool is offered from a session's next start). A project agent reads its own session; the Assistant its workspace's agents, its own session and Combwork's events there; a source a caller may not read is refused as if it didn't exist. Replies are a line per event (the newest 30 the first time, then oldest first after `since`), with up to 3 events in full on request; sources come 50 a page, each with `select`, the exact arguments that read it (the agent's id and its project's name), apart from its display label. The console's own reads aren't events.
- **The window** (`consoleWindow.ts`, `ConsoleApp.tsx`, #637; #366 decisions 1–3): hidden until **Settings → Advanced → Show developer features** is on (off by default; drawn first in Settings → Advanced's list since #367, under the same key): until then **Help → Developer Console** (Ctrl+Alt+J) is in no menu, the palette or Tips, the shortcut does nothing and `console:open` is refused; turning it off closes open consoles. Its own window like Chrome DevTools, one per Combwork window on the workspace that window shows (opening it again brings it forward; with no workspace it is refused), remembering its size and position (`consoleWindow` in `config.json`), fitted to the display it opens on as Combwork's windows are (`placeOnDisplay` in `windowBounds.ts`, #862; minimum 560 × 320). It closes with that window, and when that window leaves its workspace (another workspace opened in it, or the workspace closed): its capture ends with it, and opened again it shows the new workspace. Any window's subscription ends when it leaves the workspace it subscribed in, and `console:snapshot` reads only sources the window's current workspace may read. It may call only the console's channels, `settings:get` (for its theme) and `app:info` (for its language: #1104, without it the console was English in every language). A **source picker** (Combwork and the Assistant, then each project's agents) watches one source at a time, which starts its capture; picking none or closing the window ends it. The list shows each event's time, type, name and summary; picking one shows its **raw payload beside what Combwork made of it**, as trees whose nodes over 1.5 KB start collapsed. **Filters**: event type (the types present, each on or off), provider and **search** (name, summary or payload, Ctrl+F); **pause** holds the list (capture goes on; the indicator counts what came) and resume fills it in from the ring; **clear** empties the list through the newest event received, including any held while paused, which never come back (a resume's snapshot starts after it); a **Live / Paused / Not watching** indicator; events not delivered (a burst over the window's queue) are counted in its status bar. The window keeps its source's newest 2,000 events. No recording yet (#638).
- **Recording** (`consoleRecorder.ts`, #638; #366 decision 4): **Record** in the console writes the watched source's events from then on to `console-recordings\console-<date>-<time>-<ms>[-<n>]-<kind>.jsonl` in Combwork's profile folder (reserved with an exclusive open; the newest is the one that started last, by its name's time and number): a header line (format, Combwork's version, the source's kind, label and provider, whether text is kept, and each CLI's installed version beside the version this release was tested with), one line per event as the console captured it, and an end line (events, lost, why it ended). **Redacted by default**, as capture is; ticking **Include prompt and reply text** keeps text in that recording only (a subscription of its own with `includeText`; tokens and sign-ins stay masked), and the box starts unticked each time (ticked while the console shows text, #699). One recording per window, of a source it watches and only while it does: a window's starts and stops run one at a time, and a stop, a close, another source or another workspace cancels a start still on its way (checked again after each of its awaits; Combwork logs a start that doesn't happen). It stops when the user stops it, the window watches another source, closes or leaves its workspace, or at 50 MB or 100,000 events; what was captured until that moment, even still queued, is written before the end line, and nothing after. Every write is written whole (however many writes it takes) and counted only once it is in the file; a header, event, end line or close that fails ends the recording as **failed**, with the reason, the file kept as written. The bar shows its progress, then the file's name and **Show in folder** (only Combwork's own recordings, by name), or **Recording failed** and why.
- **Copy Diagnostics** (#638) offers the newest recording, unticked: attached, it adds a line about it (source kind, provider, Combwork and CLI versions, events, how it ended) and its newest 200 events (at most 64 KB of UTF-8), every string redacted again as the log is (folders, names, secrets), and **every path `<path>` whole** (HI-2332, the Assistant's rule after two rounds of finding where a path ends in a string that redaction had changed): the value of a path field at any depth (`PATH_FIELDS` in `consoleFixtures.mts`: `file_path`, `notebook_path`, `path`, `transcript_path`, `transcriptPath`, `cwd`, `current_dir`, `project_dir`, `file`, the safe fields that hold one), and any string that starts as an absolute path does (a drive's, a share's, `~\`), in whatever field the capture kept it. Even a workspace's path goes; the console and the log keep theirs. A recording with text is never attached; the dialog says so.
