- **The flight recorder** (`flightRecorder.ts`, #698; Darren, 13 Oct: opt-in per trigger, local, redacted, bounded and pruned, one capture per trigger per agent per few minutes, attached to Copy Diagnostics, its always-on cost measured): when something rare happens to an agent, its newest console events are saved as a **capture**. **Triggers** are advanced values of Combwork's own (§9.3), each off by default and applying at once: `cw.recorder.safeguard` (a safeguard stop or model switch, `noteSafeguard`), `cw.recorder.unknown` (a hook named outside the events the CLI is known to send, or a hook or Claude Code's status line with a top-level field outside the fields it is known to send: each CLI's advanced values `<cli>.hooks.knownEvents`, `<cli>.hooks.knownFields` and `claude-code.statusLine.knownFields`, CLI-facing with recorded samples (a `list` value's `fields` sample reads when every field the CLI sent is in it; a list may take more than 10 names, `max`), built from the recorded fixtures, which a unit test keeps all known, and the events and fields the adapters read, so a harmless newcomer is added in Settings without a release; a CLI without them is never judged, `shared/flightRecorder.ts unknownIn`), `cw.recorder.version` (an agent launched on a CLI version other than the previous launch of that provider's, kept in the profile's `flight-recorder.json` whether the trigger is on or not), `cw.recorder.stalled` (the turn ledger's unknown state, #648's `checkSilence`) and `cw.recorder.pattern` (a regular expression, case-insensitive, matched against each kept event's name and summary; its default `(?!)` never matches, which is off, as the registry refuses an empty pattern). A contract test's mismatch has no runtime trigger of its own: at runtime its signs are the version and unknown triggers. **Always on, while a trigger is**: the console keeps every agent session's events (not Combwork's own source) in a ring of its own, redacted, never text, 200 events or 256 KB a session, at most 100 sessions (the least recently written go), which only the recorder reads; capture points then build their events with no console open, and readers and the console's rings are unchanged. With every trigger off nothing is kept and a capture point returns at once, as before. Measured (#698, a typical PreToolUse with a file edit, 12 sessions): about 55 µs a kept event, the same as a source a console watches (the redaction), against 0.07 µs with every trigger off; 113 KB a busy session's ring. **A capture**: the trigger is first an event of the agent's own (kind `trigger`, its summary what it saw), then `cw.recorder.afterSeconds` later (10; what follows it) the session's ring is written as a recording (§ above: header, events, end line `captured`), named `…-capture.jsonl`, with `capture: { trigger, what }` in its header, `text: false`. What a capture says it saw is a message with its names and numbers as values (`FLIGHT_WHAT`, `shared/flightRecorder.ts`), kept in the capture's header as `whatText` beside its English `what` (recorded data, #1104: maintainers, older versions and Copy Diagnostics read the English), so the notice and the console's list say it in Combwork's language (Darren, 19 Oct: every translation in); built from safe values (names a name's characters only, models cut short) and masked as an event's summary is (`maskText`), in its file, its notice and the console's list. **Bounded beyond the rings**: it remembers no agents (the pattern trigger asks sessions which running agent an event's source is when it matches, so an agent started before the pattern was set is caught too); cooldowns only while they run, at most 1,000; captures at most 20 from their trigger until their file is written, a slow disk's writes included (a slot is free only once its write settles). **Off is off**: a trigger turned off drops its captures still waiting at once (another trigger still on keeps its own), and a capture checks its trigger again as its write begins; with every trigger off the recorder holds nothing. The versions file is read as untrusted input: missing, damaged or not as written, it counts as none. A trigger captures an agent at most once every `cw.recorder.minutes` (10); the newest `cw.recorder.keep` (20) captures are kept and older ones removed (the user's own recordings never). A notice (a toast to the agent's window) says "Captured <trigger> on <agent>", how many events and what it saw, with **Show in Folder** (`console.showCapture`); the console's **Captures** button lists them (`console:captures`: trigger, agent, age, events, Show in folder), and Copy Diagnostics offers the newest recording whichever it is, a capture saying its trigger in its line. Captures are local and never sent anywhere.
- **Fixtures and contract tests** (`shared/consoleFixtures.mts`, #366 decision 5): `npm run console-fixture` turns a redacted recording into a fixture in `tests/fixtures/console/` (the CLI's events and Combwork's reading of them, in order, absolute paths as `<path>`; a recording with text is refused). Real-tier **contract suites** record a scripted turn through the console and compare it with the fixture (`compareContract`): a hook, status line, launch or exit no longer arriving, or a **recognition marker** (`prompt shown`, `footer seen`: noted once a launch the first time Combwork recognises the CLI's prompt or footer, whatever the agent's status, `screenRecognition.ts`; the suite waits for each the fixture has before its turn) no longer arriving, which means the CLI's screen changed, a hook's, status line's, launch's or exit's field gone or retyped, or a reading of the fixture's Combwork no longer makes (a hook's event kind, status and actions; a marker's, launch's or exit's status, mode and flags, where both runs have it; text and what varies between runs left out) fails; Combwork's status markers (`ready`, `footer mode`) come and go with timing (a transcript can make an agent ready before its prompt draws), so they are never required; new events, fields and readings are flagged. Transcript reads hold whichever records were newest, so only a new one is flagged. The first is `contract-copilot` (the real Copilot CLI offline against the stand-in model); tests/e2e/README.md and tests/fixtures/console/README.md say how they run and how a fixture is made.
- **The window's IPC** (`api.ts`): `console:open` (from a Combwork window), `console:sources` (the window's workspace), `console:options` (`showText`; changes come as `console-options` to the console windows), `console:subscribe` (replaces the window's list and returns what each source has so far), `console:snapshot`, and `console:record`, `console:stopRecording`, `console:recordings`, `console:showRecording` and `console:captures` (the flight recorder's, #698); live events come as `console-events` and a recording's progress as `console-recording`, to that window only. `app:diagnostics` takes `{ recording }`.

### 9.3 Advanced settings

An asynchronous read of advanced.json applies only while no newer read, load or saved setting has superseded it (HI-2454). Stopping the store also invalidates pending reads, so an old watcher callback cannot restore values afterward.

What Combwork relies on that a CLI update can break, and timeouts and limits for power users, as named, documented defaults that can be overridden without a Combwork release (#367; import and export are #683). The CLIs are what most often breaks Combwork; the developer console (§9.2) shows what changed, and an override fixes it the same day. Remote updates of the defaults are not fetched (revisit after 0.7.0).

- **The defaults** (`shared/advanced.ts`, `ADVANCED_DEFS`): each has an id (`<cw|provider>.<what>.<which>`, as advanced.json names it; Combwork's own are group `cw`, shown as **Combwork**, HI-2517), a title, what it is for and what goes wrong when it's wrong, its kind and default, and who takes a change (at once, or sessions started afterwards). **Data only, never code**: a regular expression's source (its flags are part of the default), text found as it is, a field name, a list of names, or a whole number in a range. From the adapter audit:
  - **Sign-in and trust**: each CLI's folder trust question (`claude-code.trust.prompt`, `codex.trust.prompt`, `copilot.trust.prompt`); the refused sign-in: Claude Code's StopFailure error (`claude-code.signIn.stopError`), Codex's error message in its session file (`codex.signIn.expired`), Copilot's session error type and message and its ErrorOccurred hook's message (`copilot.signIn.*`).

- **Settings → Advanced** lists them about:config style: grouped (Combwork, then each CLI), on tabs since HI-1839 (the shared `Tabs`: Combwork with its mark, then each CLI with advanced values in `PROVIDERS` order with its `ProviderIcon`; a CLI turned off keeps its tab, dimmed, marked *off* and still chosen, its tooltip and accessible name saying so, and a line atop its values (*Codex is turned off: these settings apply once you turn it on*); the tab remembered in `ui.tabs['settings.advanced']`; every group's rows stay mounted, the tab shown alone visible), filtered by its own search and **Modified only** and by Settings' search and Modified only (while any filters, each tab counts its matches; the tab shown is the remembered one if it has any, else the first that has, and a value's own id searched for opens its group; a tab clicked meanwhile isn't remembered, and clearing the filters brings back the remembered tab; a tab with none says so); each shows its id, what it is for, the value, a modified mark with the default beside it, and **Reset**. A value that doesn't check out is refused there; one in the file that doesn't is listed as not valid, and Combwork uses the default (logged once).
- **advanced.json** (Combwork's profile folder) holds the same values: `{ "format": 1, "values": { id: value }, "madeFor": { id: { "version", "value" } } }`, written in order. **Open advanced.json** opens it in the user's editor (creating it); Combwork follows the file and reads it again when it changes (an editor's save that replaces it too). A file it can't read (not JSON, not an object, a newer format) keeps the values read before, says why in the list, and changes from Settings are refused until it's fixed (they would overwrite it). A change from Settings while the file was edited since Combwork read it is refused, and the edit read. Combwork's own changes to the file go one at a time, each from the state the last one left, so two CLI versions learnt at once both reach it. Ids this Combwork doesn't know are kept and listed, not used.
- **The `cw.` ids** (HI-2518, Darren's decisions of 4 Nov: one way, no aliases): Combwork's own settings had the old name as their prefix and group until 1.1.0; each is now `cw.<what>.<which>`. Saved values move to the new id once, by the names upgrade (§4.1.2; `upgradedAdvancedIds` in `storedNames.ts`): its profile step rewrites advanced.json's values and version records before the store reads them (with the two `LEGACY_ADVANCED` settings, now `cw.assistant.otherMcpServers` and `cw.agents.perProject`, and the retired preview switch dropped), and a workspace's open rewrites `workspace.json`'s own `advanced`. Where a file has both, the `cw.` value is kept (by presence: `false`, `0` and `[]` count) and the old one dropped. Nothing reads the old ids while the app runs: a 1.0 opened afterwards shows its defaults for them, and the settings tools and the Agent API answer an old id as any id that isn't a setting (404, *No setting "…"*). The translations' message ids are `settings.advanced.cw.…` since HI-2589.
- **App-wide**, with a **workspace's own** value only where one makes sense (`workspace: true`: the lanes shown; agents per project, #562, until HI-2001 made it a workflow option), in `workspace.json` (`advanced`), set in the list's **This workspace** box; empty uses Settings'. A workspace's switch (or choice) is a select whose first option inherits, labelled with Settings' value ("on (Settings')", sending null), then each value (HI-2344).
- **Validation**: a pattern must compile (with its flags), be one line of at most 500 characters and not match empty text (it would match any screen); text one line of at most 200; a field name `[A-Za-z_]\w*`; names `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*` (1 to 10, a list or comma-separated); numbers whole and in range.
- **CLI versions** (#367 decision 4): every value of a CLI's is CLI-facing, what Combwork reads from it and what it gives it (hook timeouts, title items, tool timeout, Copilot's exit grace). Its override records the CLI version installed when it was set (or when Combwork first learns it). A value edited by hand is made for the version installed when Combwork reads it, and Combwork writes that record back to the file (unless the file changed again meanwhile), so a restart after the CLI updates still flags it. Once another version is installed, the list flags it (**Made for Claude Code 2.1.296; 2.1.300 is installed now**) with **Keep for 2.1.300**.
- **Tested against recordings** (#367 decision 6): each CLI-facing default carries samples from recordings (`tests/fixtures/advanced`, recorded with test homes, no sign-in; and the earlier recordings): for a value Combwork reads, the text or fields the CLI sent; for one Combwork gives it, the CLI taking it (its hooks arriving, Codex listing the tool timeout it read, its title spinner, Copilot writing its totals and exiting by itself when Combwork stopped it). The unit tests check each sample is in its fixture (named with, or saying, the CLI version), that the default reads it, that the adapters do with the defaults, and that an override takes effect (Codex's plan limits read under renamed fields once the overrides name them). The developer console's own recordings redact screen text, so the screens are recorded apart. An override is tried on the same samples: one that no longer finds them is kept (the CLI may have changed) and says what it misses.
- **Reset all settings** (Settings → Advanced) clears advanced.json's overrides too (ids this Combwork doesn't know are kept), before Combwork's settings; it is refused while advanced.json can't be read. A workspace's own values are kept.
- **Copy Diagnostics** lists the overrides by id (never their values), the workspaces' own values as a count, which aren't valid, which were made for another CLI version, and unknown ids.
- **The Assistant's settings catalogue** has each as `advanced.<id>` (and `workspace.advanced.<id>` for a workspace's own), read, explained and (with Change settings) changed like any other setting, null putting the default back.
- **IPC**: `advanced:state`, `advanced:set` (scope app or workspace; null removes), `advanced:keep`, `advanced:open`; the `advanced-changed` event to every window.

## 10. Provider framework

A provider is two pieces:

- **Descriptor** (`src/shared/providers.ts`, static data both processes use): id, product and company names, icon, permission modes (with danger flags and labels), effort levels, model groups, capabilities (fixed session IDs, live mode switch by cycle or menu, Plan toggle, prompt-cache TTL, reports cost, compact focus, 200K context limit, image paste, the attachment kinds it reads itself), terminal keys the CLI reserves, instructions file and import line, setup notes.
- **Adapter** (`src/main/providers/<id>/`, `ProviderAdapter`): locate the CLI and check readiness (login and which one with its account, `AgentInstallInfo.authMethod`/`account`; sandbox; short `notes` Provider Setup shows), setup tasks, launch (`prepareLaunch`, `buildCommand`), hook normalisation and file-lock replies, live details (status line or transcript tail), mode-switch keys, transcripts (path, restore, list, usage, conversation parser, images, export), memory sources, allowed files and skill folders, the project's own MCP servers.

**Models and capabilities from the CLIs** (#125). The CLI is the source of truth wherever it can say; where it can't, the lists are manual (never scraped or fetched) and every one is editable in Settings, so nobody waits for a Combwork release.
- **Where they come from.** An adapter's `listModels` asks the installed CLI for its models and what each can do, at start and on every refresh (Check now, a changed CLI path), with a timeout, never blocking start. Claude Code: the Agent SDK's `initialize` control request (`claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config` in a folder of Combwork's own, in the sessions' environment), which sends no prompt and uses no tokens; the CLI is closed as soon as it answers. Only `models` (and `unavailable_models`) is read: `account` and the reply's other personal fields are never read, logged or stored. Each model gives its value, resolved id, name, `supportedEffortLevels` and `supportsAutoMode`; the pickers (and the Agent API's model list) show an alias with the model it stands for, "Opus (Opus 5.5)" (#248), a pinned version as the CLI names it; the `default` entry isn't offered (it is "Claude Code default") and its resolved model is the CLI's default model. Codex: `codex debug models` (hidden models left out; `supported_reasoning_levels`, `default_reasoning_level`). The replies are the CLIs' protocols, not documented commands, so they are read defensively: unknown fields ignored, a missing or odd field falls back for that field, a reply without models is a failure (logged without personal data). Per-model flags are trusted only when the reply uses them at all: then a Claude model without effort levels has none (Haiku), and one without `supportsAutoMode` no Auto. Contract tests run against recorded replies in `tests/fixtures` (personal fields removed), which the fake CLIs answer with too.
- **Cache.** The last good catalog per provider is kept in config.json (`modelCatalogs`), keyed by the CLI version, so pickers fill at once on start while the fresh read runs ("as it last said; asking again"); a different version's is not used. Only the latest refresh's answer is kept.
- **Pickers.** Models: the CLI's (unavailable ones shown, not offered), else the fallback. Effort pickers (global, project, agent, Assistant) offer the levels of the model that would run (`models.ts` `modelCaps`); without the CLI's word, the effort fallback. A saved effort the model doesn't take stays chosen and is shown as such ("Extra high (not offered with Opus 4.6)", with a warning), never changed behind the user's back. A model without effort (Haiku) says so.
- **Default effort.** The footer and the pickers' Inherit option show the model's own default when nothing is set or reported: "Medium (default)". It is the CLI's config (Codex's `model_reasoning_effort`), else its catalog (Codex's `default_reasoning_level`), else the effort a session started without one reported for that model (Claude Code's status line; `observedDefaultEffort`, the newest 50 models per provider). Unknown: nothing shown, as before.
- **Fallbacks in Settings → each provider:** **Models (fallback)**, used only when the CLI can't be asked (not installed, too old, an unexpected reply), with where the models come from now ("From Claude Code 2.1.289", "Fallback (Claude Code couldn't be asked)"); **Effort levels (fallback)**, used when the CLI doesn't report a model's own (its names also name the CLI's levels, in the pickers and the agent's footer alike); and the prices (§9), which list the CLI's models too (#436: a listed model without a price is a row marked "No price: enter one"; a priced one the CLI no longer lists stays, greyed, "not in <provider>'s list"; a provider whose cost is only estimated (no `reportsCost`) says so, with a link to its `pricingUrl`). Each can be edited (add, remove, rename; models marked Older) and has **Reset to defaults**. The lists are folded while the CLI's answer is in use and they are Combwork's own. Defaults stay in code (the descriptor's `modelGroups` and `effortLevels`, `SHIPPED_PRICES`); only an edited list is stored (`modelFallback`, `effortFallback`), so improved shipped defaults reach users who never edited them.

The registry (`src/main/providers/index.ts`) lists the adapters; the rest of Combwork (sessions, Overview, settings pages, status bar, Provider Setup, Sessions tab) works from descriptors and adapters without naming a provider. Adding a provider means a descriptor, an adapter, an icon and a price table. Skills and MCP are stored in a Combwork-neutral form; adapters translate them at launch. A readiness note's or install note's `code` spans (commands and paths) each get a copy button (#1204, `CopyableCode`/`CodeText` in `components/ui.tsx`) that copies exactly the span, never the text around it, and says Copied for a moment; Performance → Compare's hint (`npm run scenarios`) uses the same.

---

## 11. Provider installation and updates

The same rules apply to every provider's CLI; the details below are Claude Code's. Codex: installed with OpenAI's installer (`irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex`) into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenAI\Codex`, signed in with a ChatGPT plan or an API key, plus the one-time sandbox setup (§6.4). **Provider Setup** (Help menu) has a tab per provider with its install, sign-in, sandbox and update steps, and the readiness banner links to it for enabled providers that need something.

**A fresh PATH** (#472, `freshPath.ts`): installers add their folder to the user's or the machine's PATH in the registry, which running processes don't see. Before Combwork looks for the CLIs (`providerService.refresh`: at start, after an install, update, sign-in or setup task, Check again, a failed launch) and before Check again's git check, it reads the machine's then the user's PATH from the registry (PowerShell's `[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable`, expanded; `reg query` where PowerShell can't run) and appends the folders its own PATH lacks, in that order: its own keep their order and come first, nothing is removed, one read at a time. `where.exe`, the CLIs' checks and every session started from then on (`childEnv` copies Combwork's environment) get it; running sessions keep theirs. **Before Combwork starts a process of its own** (#821) it reads it again (`refreshPathBeforeStart`): an agent's launch (`sessions.start`, before a worktree's setup command too), a provider task's terminal (install, update, sign-in, setup) and **Open External Terminal Here** (`wt.exe`, else `cmd`), so what was installed outside Combwork since it started reaches them with no Check again. That wait is bounded (2 s, `FRESH_WAIT_MS`): a slower read lets the start go on with Combwork's PATH as it is and counts for the next one; launches at the same time share one read. A Windows Terminal already running opens the new window in its own process, with the environment it has (or reloads from Windows, its *reloadEnvironmentVariables* setting): Combwork can't give that one its PATH. No provider is named: every adapter's `PATH` candidate gains it. After an install task, Provider Setup says the CLI was found and needs no restart (agents already running get the new PATH when they restart), or, when it still isn't found, that the install ended without Combwork finding it (Check again, or set its path in Settings). Test copies (unpackaged, with a test profile) never read the registry: `CW_TEST_REGISTRY_PATH` stands in for it (none by default; the `freshpath` suite changes it while Combwork runs, as an installer would). **A CLI found off PATH** (#1103): a standalone CLI can be found where its installer puts it without being on any PATH (Claude Code's native install in `~\.local\bin`, whose installer can leave the folder off the user's PATH: seen on Darren's PC in the 0.9.2 release, where Provider Setup found Claude Code while a shell Combwork started couldn't run `claude`). When `providerService` finds a provider's CLI it notes its folder (`noteCliFolder`, one per provider, dropped when it isn't found), and `childEnv` adds the folders the PATH lacks at its end (`withCliFolders`), as does **Open External Terminal Here** (`externalTerminal.ts`: Windows Terminal, its cmd fallback, the system terminal elsewhere), so every session and terminal Combwork starts runs by name the CLI Provider Setup found. Combwork's own PATH, which it finds the CLIs on, isn't changed: a folder found by a fixed place (Codex's own) mustn't come before one an installer adds later (the `freshpath` suite). The user's PATH in the registry is never changed either, and folders already on a child's PATH keep their order.

**GitHub Copilot** (`copilot`, #403 spike on CLI 1.0.93; readiness #452, `providers/copilot/install.ts`, which the adapter delegates `locate`, `readiness` and the install, update and sign-in tasks to):
- **Installed** with WinGet (`winget install --id GitHub.Copilot --exact --source winget`, the **Install** task; WinGet links `copilot.exe` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Links`) or npm (`@github/copilot`, a `.cmd` launcher). Discovery: settings path → `PATH` → WinGet's Links → npm global. The version is `copilot --version` (its "GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.93." without the full stop), read with `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false` as its agents run. **Update** goes through the installer it came from to keep its package record consistent (`winget upgrade …`, `npm install -g @github/copilot@latest`); any other install gets no Update button, only a note to update it the way it was installed. The latest version is what that installer can deliver (HI-2729): a WinGet install's is the WinGet source's (`winget show --id GitHub.Copilot --exact --source winget`, run as a child process within `cw.winget.showSeconds` (30 s), read by the pattern `cw.winget.version`: the first `<field>: <version>` line, since WinGet words field names in Windows' language), which follows npm days later, so Update is offered only once WinGet has the newer version; none when WinGet can't say. Any other install's is npm's. An upgrade that WinGet answers with *no newer version* (`0x8A15002B`, signed `-1978335189`) ended well, not a failure. Copilot’s self-update can replace a WinGet-installed executable without updating WinGet’s record (#1101). After a WinGet portable uninstall failure (`0x8A150057`, signed `-1978335145`), Provider Setup shows a tentative explanation with the failed terminal and an explicit **Update anyway** button, retrying the same upgrade command with `--force` only when clicked. The retry is bound to the executable and version that failed, cleared on a new update or when either changes, and still refused while Copilot agents run. Check again refreshes the installed version as usual.
- **Signed in, and how**, in the CLI's own order (`copilot login --help`), for the environment its agents get (Combwork's, without `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which other tools set and Copilot launches leave out, `COPILOT_ENV_STRIP`; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, set for Copilot alone, is kept, #450): a token variable (`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`; the other two only outside Combwork), else a **stored login** (`copilot login`: the token is in Windows Credential Manager, keyed by account, and `loggedInUsers`/`lastLoggedInUser` in the CLI's `config.json`, under `COPILOT_HOME` else `~/.copilot`, name it), else the **GitHub CLI's** login (`gh auth status --active --hostname github.com --json hosts`: its account and `state`). Combwork only checks that a token variable is set, reads only the login names from `config.json` (a JSON file after a `//` comment line), and never asks gh for the token. `authMethod` is the variable's name, "Copilot login" or "GitHub CLI", and `account` the login (a token's isn't known; an Enterprise host follows it in brackets). Provider Setup's chip: **Signed in as octocat (Copilot login)**. Signed out: **Sign in** runs `copilot login` in a visible terminal that the user signs in with (Combwork types nothing; tests never run it), and the detail names `copilot login --device-code`, the gh fallback (`gh auth login`), and any token variable set in Combwork's environment that agents don't get.
- **Plan note** (`notes`): "Copilot Free uses Auto only; choosing a model needs a paid plan." (the CLI can't say an account's plan). Usage is in AI credits (1 AIC = $0.01). Copilot Pro's "third-party agents (Claude Code and Codex)" are GitHub's cloud agents (Agent HQ), not the local CLIs: a Copilot plan doesn't sign in Combwork's Claude Code or Codex.
- **Tested with** (#365) works as for the others: Copilot is in `REAL_CLIS` with its real suite (`copilot`, the installed CLI offline against a stand-in model, #453), and its `tested-clis.json` entry comes from the release's real-tier run (`npm run tested-clis`), first in 0.4.2. Until a release names it, Provider Setup shows no Tested line for Copilot.
- **Agents** (#450; how in ARCHITECTURE, GitHub Copilot): turned on in Settings → Providers like the others. Launched with a session id Combwork picks (`--session-id`, `--resume`), a launch plugin of HTTP hooks (statuses, the file-lock reply), the workspace's MCP servers and the combwork server with its instructions (the user's and the project's own servers and Copilot's built-in ones turned off), and Combwork's skills as the `.agents/skills` copies it shares with Codex; Combwork never writes Copilot's config. Modes: **Accept edits** (the default, #468: Ask with writes under the agent's folder approved, `--allow-tool=write(<folder>/**)`; where the folder's path has `(` or `)` it approves no edits, since Copilot refuses parentheses in its rules and any stand-in would also match a look-alike folder, and Combwork says so once when such an agent starts), **Ask**, **Plan**, **Allow all** (`--allow-all`; no opt-in since #490, Darren's decision: Copilot needs one low-interaction mode, and its description says plainly that it approves every tool, path and web request, in its folder and outside it), and the danger mode **Autopilot**, unlocked by the opt-in, which names the danger modes it unlocks (**Enable the Autopilot option**, from the descriptor's list, #461; turning it off reverts projects and agents using it to Inherit). Autopilot is Allow all and more: on its first turn Copilot 1.0.93 sets *Permission policy: Allow All for this session* (the footer turns to Autopilot · Allow All), whether launched with `--autopilot` or switched to live, and leaving it keeps Allow All (Interactive · Allow All, read as Allow all), so after it Ask and Accept edits need a restart (#490's probes, offline in a test home); the footer says which (Accept edits and Ask look the same there, so the launch decides), Shift+Tab cycles to Plan and Autopilot and back live, switching between Accept edits, Ask and Allow all needs a restart. The combwork server's tools never ask, in any mode (`--allow-tool=combwork`; the Assistant's only those its Control settings trust), as for the other CLIs: the Agent API enforces what an agent may do. Its folder-trust dialog is the startup question. It reads the project's `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and runs a project's `.claude/settings.json` hooks. Sessions, the conversation and usage come from `COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<id>` (#451); cost is Copilot's own figure in AI credits. **Plan limits** (HI-2734): a model call's `model.model_call_success` carries `quotaSnapshots`, one per quota (`chat`, `completions`, `premium_interactions`), as the CLI's SDK documents them (`entitlementRequests`, -1 or `isUnlimitedEntitlement` for unlimited; `usedRequests`; `remainingPercentage`; `resetDate`); its other quota readings (`session.quota_observation`, `assistant.usage`) are ephemeral, never written to `events.jsonl`. Each quota with an entitlement above 0 and a percent left from 0 to 100 is a limit (used = 100 − the percent, its counts in the (i), no window: only the reset date); an unlimited one says *Unlimited*, with no meter, and is never warned of; one whose entitlement is 0 (Copilot Free's premium requests: 0, 0% left) is known, and says *Not in your plan* (an allowance of 0; in the status bar's tooltip, not its item), never a share, so it never reads as all used; `{}` (a custom provider's model) is no report. An unlimited or not-included limit keeps `usedPercent` 0 as a placeholder, never a measured 0: every reader (cards, status bar, warnings, accounts' bars, usage moves, the Agent API's connection usage) checks `hasShare()` first. Merging (`mergeLimit`): what the plan allows changing (unlimited, not included, another entitlement) takes the reading reported later than the allowance was last seen (`allowanceAt`, which a reading of the same allowance moves on even when an older, higher share is kept), whole; otherwise the higher share in a period, as before; what the limit is (label, window, models) is the latest report's to say it, by `describedAt`, so a delayed report never rolls it back. With nothing known of a provider's limits, the Overview says it hasn't reported them in its sessions so far. Combwork calls no GitHub API and reads no token for them. Copilot writes a session's token totals (`session.shutdown`) only as it exits by itself, so Combwork ends it as a person would (#465): Stop, closing its workspace, quitting Combwork and a restart type Ctrl+C on conditions (HI-2272, `main/exitKeys.ts`): in a turn or a dialog (Combwork's turn ledger or its status), one Ctrl+C cancels it and its end is waited for; at its prompt one arms the exit, and the next goes once its screen shows *ctrl+c again to exit* (Settings → Advanced's `copilot.exit.armed`); a key lost (no hint within 400 ms, or the hint gone with Copilot still running) is typed again. [Three keys 400 ms apart lost the exit under load: a cancel took ~380 ms, the second key came 18 ms after the turn ended and was lost as it wound down, the third only armed it, and Copilot was killed without its totals.] A lane's end (`quit`, its turn over) still types the three keys. Combwork kills it only if it is still running 10 s later (#716: under load it took up to 2.4 s to exit by itself, and 2.5 s killed it, losing its totals; the grace is Settings → Advanced's `copilot.exit.graceSeconds`, #727). Quitting, closing a workspace and removing a project wait past that grace for it to end. Models: Copilot's ACP session (`listModels`, only while Copilot is on); Free has Auto only.

**Antigravity CLI** (`agy`, HI-2543's probe of 1.5.0; HI-2544, `providers/antigravity/`):
- **Installed** with Google's installer (`irm https://antigravity.google/cli/install.ps1 | iex`, the **Install** task) into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\agy\bin`. Discovery: settings path → `where agy` → `%LOCALAPPDATA%\agy\bin\agy.exe`; an editor's copy is rejected. The version is `agy --version`. **Update** is `agy update`. Every child Combwork starts (sessions, the version, sign-in and model checks) gets `AGY_CLI_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true` (an advanced override, `antigravity.override.noAutoUpdate`). Those checks (`--version`, `agy models`, and the catalog's read) run in a **check profile** under Combwork's own data (`<local data>\antigravity\check` as USERPROFILE, HOME kept; HI-2698), never the user's own: agy writes its home on every run (logs, its conversation index, its onboarding state), and Combwork never writes the user's `~\.gemini`. The sign-in is Credential Manager's, so a check there sees the agents' account. A run that would be in the user's profile is refused (`runAgy`), and so is an agent's launch (`inUserProfile`). A test copy's check profile is under its test data; the e2e harness fails a suite that changes the user's own `~\.gemini\antigravity-cli`. The install, update and sign-in tasks are the user's own, in a visible terminal, on their own agy.
- **Signed in**: one PC-wide sign-in, like Copilot's (§11.2, account id `antigravity`, "This PC's, every workspace"); Combwork never signs in. Readiness runs `agy models`: its `id<TAB>label` lines are the model catalog (`antigravity.models.line`, unknown ids kept), and only its signed-out error (`antigravity.signIn.needed`, recorded in a Sandbox) means signed out; any other failure is shown as it is. `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `AGY_ADC_AUTH` and `AGY_ACCOUNT` are left out of every child (`antigravity.override.stripAccountVars`).
- **A private profile per agent** (Darren, HI-2544): agy reads its home from `USERPROFILE` only, so each agent runs with `USERPROFILE` set to its own profile under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Combwork\antigravity\profiles\<agent>` (the Assistant's keyed by the workspace), `HOME` left the user's. The user's global agy customizations aren't seen by agents. Per launch Combwork writes the profile's `.gemini\config\mcp_config.json` (Combwork's servers, with the launch's token) and `hooks.json` (Combwork's hooks), and a `--settings` file (the status line, `stack_with_default` so agy's own line stays, and `permissions.allow` for Combwork's tools in agy's rule form, `mcp(combwork/*)` or `mcp(combwork/<tool>)`, `antigravity.override.preApproveCombworkTools`, and `trustedWorkspaces`: the launch's folder and its added folders, so agy asks no trust question), never the user's config. A launch without Combwork's server (its connection's tools off, or an Independent agent) also removes agy's own cache of that server in the profile (`.gemini\antigravity-cli\mcp\combwork`: its `instructions.md` and tool schemas, which agy reads lazily), so nothing of an earlier launch's is left for the agent to find (HI-2731). **A removed agent's profile** goes to the Recycle Bin with it (Remove Agent, `agentRemoved`; Darren's 7 Nov decision, HI-2731): its rules, servers and conversations are its alone, and a new agent never has its id. An agent a template load replaced keeps its profile, since the load's undo gives it back with its id and conversations. The other CLIs' homes are a connection's, not an agent's, so they have nothing to remove.
- **Guidance** (HI-2547, agy 1.5.0's `/context`): agy auto-loads only `~\.gemini\GEMINI.md` as a system file, so each launch writes the profile's `.gemini\GEMINI.md`: Combwork's guidance (when the agent has Combwork's tools), the agent's instructions and its notes, in that order. The project's `AGENTS.md`/`GEMINI.md` are agy's own, read lazily; Combwork writes nothing in the project. Skills are Combwork's marked copies in the working folder's `.agents\skills`, as for Codex and Copilot (agy's `/skills` also reads the profile's `config\skills`, `antigravity-cli\skills` and `skills`, which Combwork leaves empty).
- **First-run setup** (HI-2547, Darren's choice (a)): agy shows onboarding screens (a theme, the terms, a data-use choice) until its home's `cache\onboarding.json` says `onboardingComplete`. Readiness warns while the check profile isn't onboarded, with Provider Setup's **Set up** task: `agy` in the check profile (its own folder trusted by a `--settings` file), the user's own answers in Combwork's terminal, Combwork typing nothing; the task ends when the file says complete. Each launch copies the check profile's `onboarding.json`, and its `jetski_state.pbtxt`'s `post_onboarding` block only into a profile without that file (never its installation id), so the agent starts past the screens. Not onboarded, the launch goes ahead, its start notice saying the screens will show in the pane.
- **What agy can't take** (HI-2547): a legacy HTTP+SSE MCP server (`type: 'sse'`) isn't supported by agy 1.5.0, so it's left out of the profile's `mcp_config.json`; Auto needs Windows 11 24H2 or later with the August 2026 update (Google's sandbox docs, the CLI tab): build 26100 or 26200 (24H2 and 25H2 share their updates) at revision 9168 (KB5121003) or later, or any later build, read once from the registry (`CurrentBuildNumber` and `UBR`, asynchronously) for a launch in Auto. The launch's start notice names each: the SSE servers, Auto on a Windows below that (its build and revision), Auto where the version couldn't be read (said as unknown, never assumed), and the setup not done. **The rules file's size:** agy truncates a rules file over 24,000 UTF-8 bytes (Google's rules docs), so a launch whose GEMINI.md (guidance, instructions and notes together) would be larger is refused before anything is written, its pane giving both sizes and saying to shorten the agent's instructions or the Workspace notes (HR1, HI-2547).
- **The project's own MCP servers refuse the launch** (fail closed, HR1 on HI-2544). agy loads servers from each workspace folder's `.agents` (and `.agent`, `_agents`, `_agent`) `mcp_config.json`, in the folder it runs in and each `--add-dir`, and each parent up to the repository root. Combwork reads them first: if one is a server the agent wasn't given (every definition of that name, in any of those files, must be the same server as the agent's under that name: equal in every field, command, arguments, environment, URL, headers and anything else, an unknown field counting as a difference; names compared as own keys only, so `__proto__` or `constructor` is a server like any other), or a file can't be read or isn't valid, the launch is refused before agy starts, naming the servers and files. **Upstream limitation (agy 1.5.0, HI-2544's sentinel runs):** nothing keeps agy from starting such a server. `--settings` takes no MCP setting, `disabled: true` still starts it, and a same-name definition in the private profile replaces it only while that one runs: once it ends, agy starts the project's. A stand-in that could die mid-session would fail open, so none is used. Project hooks run as they do under the other CLIs (statuses from hooks are HI-2545's).
- **Conversations**: agy picks the id. Combwork adopts it from the status line (`conversation_id`), for the current run only, never replacing a known id; a resume is `--conversation <id>`, only of a conversation in the agent's own profile.
- **Transcripts and usage** (HI-2546, from 1.5.0's recorded runs; `transcript.ts`, `conversations.ts`): `<profile>\.gemini\antigravity-cli\brain\<id>\.system_generated\logs\transcript_full.jsonl`, its arguments as agy gave them (`transcript.jsonl` beside it, each argument JSON-encoded again, isn't read), one step a line: `USER_INPUT` (`source: USER_EXPLICIT`, the prompt inside agy's `<USER_REQUEST>` among what it adds, `antigravity.transcript.userRequest`), `PLANNER_RESPONSE` (the model's text, its `tool_calls` and its `input_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `output_tokens`) and each call's result step after it, in order (its `step_index` is the call's id, as agy's hooks name it; agy's times before the output left out, `antigravity.transcript.stepHeader`; an image a tool read is a file in `logs\media` that its `media` names, shown only from there, in one of Combwork's profiles), `SYSTEM_MESSAGE` (agy's own notes, and a subagent's task and answer, `antigravity.transcript.systemMessage`) and `CHECKPOINT` (a compaction: its summary and its own request's tokens). A prompt that is a slash command (`/compact`) shows as a command and isn't counted as a prompt. A **subagent** is a conversation of its own, whose first step is its parent's task: it is listed under its parent (`subSessionOf`), its tokens its own, never added to its parent's. Not recorded with 1.5.0 headless, so not read: an image the user attaches (`@file` attached none) and a rewind. The format isn't documented as stable: anything else is left out (only a result step takes a call's result), as is a line whose `step_index` isn't a whole number from 0 or was read already. **agy may write a transcript again in place** (the parsers' `rewritten`): the viewer keeps a hash of what it read and reads the file again from the start when a change of size or time leaves those bytes different (an equal-length overwrite, a rewritten start that grew), or when another file is in its place (its identity, volume and file id, differs: a rename over it keeping size and time); the usage worker reads it whole whenever its size, time or identity changes (`rereadsWhole`), never taking up a saved state or the history's unchanged shortcut. A step is read only in a shape agy 1.5.0 wrote (a known type in another shape is left out whole, its index still free for a valid one). Append-only providers are read as before. **Every file read is checked by its real path** (links and junctions followed): the transcript, as agy reported it or as derived, only when it is that conversation's in one of Combwork's profiles; an image only from that same conversation's `logs\media`, at most 20 MB, read off main's thread; the title and `last_conversations.json` likewise, bounded. **Usage**: each `PLANNER_RESPONSE` and `CHECKPOINT` is a request; its input is without its cache read (HI-2546's runs: a subagent's first request, the usual ~7,100-token prompt, recorded 2198 input and 5058 cache read; `antigravity.usage.inputIncludesCache` off), so the cache is counted once; the context is the last request's input, cache read and output, and after a compaction what it left (manual after `/compact`, else auto); the model is the one the first prompt names (`antigravity.transcript.modelChange`), the status line giving the live model, effort and context window. No cost: agy publishes no per-token prices, and its status line reports none Combwork has seen. **Plan limits** (HI-2734): the status line's `quota` has one bucket per group of models (1.5.0: `gemini-weekly`, `3p-weekly` for the other providers' models), each `remaining_fraction` (0 to 1) and `reset_time`, and `plan_tier` names the plan. Each valid bucket is a limit by its key (used = 1 − the fraction; a `-weekly` one's window a week, any other's none), named in the window by the models it covers (`PlanLimit.models`: *Gemini models, weekly*, *Other models, weekly*); a bucket without a share from 0 to 1 is left out. The plan's name alone (no valid bucket) is reported as the plan, with no limit made up: the Overview says the plan's limits aren't reported yet. A line with neither reports nothing, so the figures kept stay as of when they were reported. The title is agy's (`annotations\<id>.pbtxt`), read asynchronously when the transcript is found or listed and kept, so a usage asked for without waiting never reads a file. **Sessions**: the Sessions list also has the conversations in the profiles of agents that ran in the folder (`cache\last_conversations.json`), which Combwork has no record of (one started by agy's `/new` inside a launch); never the user's own `~\.gemini`. **Resume** reopens agy's own store of the conversation (`conversations\<id>.db`), not the transcript: a transcript put back from Combwork's backup can't bring a deleted conversation back (`restorePath` none, so with no transcript the session starts afresh), and with the transcript kept but the store gone the resume is refused before agy starts, saying agy no longer has that conversation. HI-2540's rules apply as to any session: every Antigravity session was launched under the current names, so only a moved folder starts one afresh.
- **Modes**: Accept edits (the default, `--mode accept-edits`), Ask (none), Plan, Auto (agy's sandbox, Windows 11 24H2 with the August 2026 update), Skip all permissions (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, danger); no live switch. Efforts low to max (`--effort`). Unpriced (`SHIPPED_PRICES` empty).
- **Hooks** (HI-2545, design s56, `providers/antigravity/hooks.ts`; agy 1.5.0's hooks.md and the recorded runs: `hooks-run-antigravity-1.5.0.jsonl`, `statusline-run-…`, `tests/fixtures/antigravity/run-*`): one named hook, `combwork`, in the profile's `hooks.json`, a handler per event agy has (SessionStart, PreInvocation, PostInvocation, Stop, and PreToolUse and PostToolUse while **Hooks: before and after each tool** is on, `antigravity.hooks.toolHooks`, on by default). Each is `agyForwardCommand` (curl with the launch's auth file) to the hook URL with `&event=<Event>`: agy's payloads don't name their event, so the hook server fills in `hook_event_name` from that query. **agy 1.5.0 runs a hook's and the status line's command as `cmd /c "<command>"` with each `"` in it escaped as `\"`** (HI-2548's run of the real CLI: every hook failed with curl's exit 3, and a no-prompt probe recorded the command line), which cmd doesn't undo, so the command holds no quote: what needs one comes from the launch's environment (`agyHookEnv`: `CW_AGY_HOOK_AUTH`, the auth file's `"@<path>"`, which may have spaces; `CW_AGY_HOOK_ALLOW`), which cmd expands before it reads quotes, and the URL's `&` is `^&`. The fake agy runs commands the same way. PreToolUse's command answers `{"decision":"allow"}` when Combwork can't be reached (`|| echo %CW_AGY_HOOK_ALLOW%`), as 1.5.0 takes no answer as a denial. **Each hook is prepared once** (`prepareHook`, in the launch's hook order, before it is normalized, admitted and given its notice): what it is, decided from its raw fields and this agent's own transcript (`trustedTranscript`), kept on the hook (`combworkPrepared`) so every reader normalizes it the same. A hook not prepared (the lock check and the reply, which come first, or one whose preparation failed or whose launch ended meanwhile) is only what its raw fields say for sure: a tool's start with the files it edits, a tool's end. No SessionEnd: the end is the process's. A resume sends no SessionStart.
- **Turns** (HI-2410's lesson; recorded with 1.5.0): agy sends no prompt hook. `invocationNum` counts a turn's model calls (a Stop's continuation doesn't start it again), and at `invocationNum` 0 the step `initialNumSteps - 1` is on disk and is what began the turn. So each invocation zero is the turn `<conversation>:i<initialNumSteps>`, admitted once per launch: a duplicate or an older one (at or below the conversation's highest start) is left out, whether its first read found the step or not. Its prompt is the user's words (a `USER_INPUT` from `USER_EXPLICIT`, `antigravity.transcript.userRequest`), else a turn agy began itself (`cli`), never the user's. The step is read from the transcript's last 1 MB, again every 100 ms while it isn't written, for up to `antigravity.hooks.userStepWaitSeconds`; a line being written isn't read; a step in another shape, or a window without it, is `cli`. `invocationNum` and `initialNumSteps` must be whole numbers. Every later event of the conversation belongs to the latest start at or before its position (PreInvocation's and PostInvocation's `initialNumSteps`, a tool hook's `stepIdx`), so a late event of an earlier turn is that turn's (stale). A Stop, with no position, belongs to the conversation's latest start: **this relies on agy 1.5.0 waiting for each hook's reply before going on and never sending one again** (recorded: each reply's effect was seen); a Stop of `executionNum` above 0 is after a continuation. The launch's memo (bounded: 256 starts a conversation, 64 conversations' roles, 4096 conversations' highest start) is dropped with it.
- **Conversations in a launch**: the launch's own; another whose step 0 is the user's prompt (agy's `/new`; `/rewind`, which 1.5.0 makes a new conversation, the old transcript left as it was; `/resume`): its invocation zero carries that conversation, so the launch follows it (`switchSession`), as for Claude Code's `/clear`; one whose step 0 is a SYSTEM_MESSAGE from another conversation is a subagent's: a child (`ids.sub`), never a prompt, a session, a transcript or a notice. One that can't be read is neither: left out. **File locks never depend on whose conversation an edit is**: a subagent's edit of a file another agent holds is refused as the agent's own would be.
- **Replies** (recorded with 1.5.0: `{}` denies a tool, `allow` leaves it to agy's own permission check, `deny` with a reason blocks it and tells the model why, `ask` and `force_ask` let it run): every PreToolUse is answered. A locked file's is `{decision:'deny', reason}`, and a lock that would ask is a deny too, its reason saying to ask first; anything else (a warning included) is `{decision:'allow'}` (`preToolUseDefault`). The files an edit names: `antigravity.hooks.editTools` (`edit_file`) and their `antigravity.hooks.editPathField` (`Path`). Notices (`noticeEvents`: PreInvocation and Stop, decided in the launch's order after preparation, every reply settled): a checkpoint at a PreInvocation between a running turn's model calls, that very turn's, once per position and counted as given only once a reply carries it (`injectSteps: [{ephemeralMessage}]`); the drain at the Stop of the running turn, `executionNum` 0 (`{decision:'continue', reason}`); none at a turn's start, a child's, or after the hook's timeout (`noticeDeadlineMs`: agy no longer waits for it). Start context: a SessionStart `systemMessage`, decided in the launch's hook order once the hook is prepared (an unprepared SessionStart says nothing of what it is: HI-2548, the Assistant's state view), the launch's own start only.
- **The status line**: `antigravity.statusLine.confirmField` (`tool_confirmation_pending`, recorded with `agent_state` tool_use) is the only sign of agy's permission prompt: a blocking ask once as it begins, while the turn runs, in hook order (waiting for you; Combwork never answers it); gone with no tool's start or end, it is no longer asked. Cancelling the prompt sends **no hook at all** (recorded): a status line saying idle with none pending, while the turn runs, starts a grace (`antigravity.statusLine.idleGraceSeconds`, 3 s) bound to the launch's run, session and turn. Any hook of the launch, any other status, a new turn or session, or the launch's end cancels it; at its end, in hook order, if all is still so, the turn is interrupted. The status line also gives the model's display name, effort and context window (`statusLine`), and never opens a turn. **Started with no prompt** (HI-2548): agy sends SessionStart only with its first prompt, and its status line says `authenticating`, `initializing`, then `idle` before any (recorded), so the current launch's idle status line while it is still starting, and asked nothing at its start, makes it ready, in hook order.
- **Tested with** (HI-2548): Antigravity is in `REAL_CLIS` (`agy`), its real suite `antigravityreal` (Darren's (b): one agent, its launch and one tiny prompt on the cheapest model at low effort, in a test copy's own profiles on the PC's sign-in, never the user's `~\.gemini`, its updates off; the user's agy folders and the PC's agy and Google credential names the same afterwards), so its `tested-clis.json` entry comes from the release's real tier like the others'. The fake agy's suites (`antigravity`, `antigravity-windows`: a path with spaces and non-ASCII letters, two agents on the one sign-in at once on two connections with different models) and the scenarios' `fake-antigravity` stop before any session unless Combwork selected the fake, never another copy it found. A CLI's checks run through its `.cmd` with the path and any argument with a space quoted (`run`: such a path was read as its first word, the copy not found, and another taken); a launch through cmd.exe of a `.cmd` that isn't a Node launcher, at such a path, is HI-2722.

**OpenCode** (`opencode`, Anomaly's anomalyco/opencode **V2**, `@opencode/cli`; HI-2756's research, HI-2758's probe of 2.2.6, HI-2759, `providers/opencode/`). Darren's decisions (8 Nov): per-account credential stores; local models neither blocked nor promoted; updates held as for Antigravity; the project's own config off by default. OpenCode's nested **Claude Agent** provider is out of scope, and no Claude subscription credential is ever routed through OpenCode.
- **Installed** from the official standalone Windows asset (the **Install** task, PowerShell in a terminal the user watches): the newest non-prerelease **v2** tag from GitHub's releases list (GitHub labels V1 "Latest", so never `/latest`), `opencode-windows-x64.zip` (or `-arm64`), checked against the release's `SHA256SUMS`, unpacked into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenCode`. Discovery: settings path → `where opencode` → that folder → `~\.opencode\bin`. The version is `opencode --version` (`opencode.version`: `opencode v2.2.6`); anything below 2 (V1 `opencode-ai`, the archived opencode-ai/opencode), V1's npm package and an editor's copy are rejected, and readiness says why. **Update** (Provider Setup) runs the same verified download into the copy's own folder (`npm install -g @opencode/cli@latest` for an npm copy). OpenCode never updates itself under Combwork: `update: "disable"` in every private config and `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1` (**Don't let OpenCode update itself**, on by default). Checks run `--standalone` on Combwork's own roots, never the user's `~\.local\share\opencode` or the machine-wide service.
- **Accounts** (decision 1, `capabilities.connections`, `homeEnv: XDG_DATA_HOME`): each OpenCode account is a private data root, its folder OpenCode's data root (its database: its saved credentials and its sessions) with its config, state and cache roots beside it. **Sign in** runs `opencode auth login --standalone` on the account's roots in a terminal (Combwork types nothing; a login config with Claude Agent denied); the account's **Set Up** runs the same, prepared the same (`accountSetUpCommand`), never the raw CLI on its data root alone. Its status is `opencode auth list --format json`: never signed out (OpenCode runs local and built-in models with no sign-in, decision 2), its providers with saved credentials named. A saved credential beats an environment key for the same provider (HI-2758 Q4). The catalog is `opencode models` on each account's roots together (`opencode.models.line`: `provider/model` ids, unknown-safe; Claude Agent's never listed).
- **A launch** (HI-2758's recipe, design s7 to s16): the pane runs Combwork's launcher (`launcher.ts`: a hidden PowerShell compiling a small C# program). It holds a handle to the Combwork instance that launched it (by pid and exact creation time, `ownerToken`), makes a **job object that ends its processes when its only handle closes** and puts itself in it, starts `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port <free>` hidden with a per-launch `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` (up to 3 ports), waits for `/api/info` (**Server: time to start**, 30 s), creates or checks the session, records the server's address, port and pid (never the password) in the launch's private folder (`opencode-server.json`), and runs the TUI on the pane's console: `opencode --server <url> --session <id> [--auto] [--prompt <task>] <folder>`, `--prompt` being the launch's first task where it has one (a Combwork start's, the Assistant's), which 2.2.6's TUI submits as it opens. That Combwork's end is watched throughout, the server's start and the session's creation included: the launcher stops where it is and does nothing more. A Node CLI launcher (`.cmd`) runs as its node and script; any other `.cmd`/`.bat` through cmd.exe with each argument quoted as `cmdArg` quotes it (`&`, `|`, `%`… kept literal). When the TUI, the server or that Combwork ends, the launcher exits and Windows ends everything left in the job (the server and its MCP servers): a forced kill of the launcher or of Combwork included, with no reliance on Combwork's process tracking. Without PowerShell the launch is refused.
- **Isolation**: a private config folder per launch (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` in the launch's private folder, removed when it ends): `service.json {"disabled":true}` (the machine-wide service off), `opencode.json` (the model, the mode's agent, the MCP servers given with an `mcp.use` deny-all and an allow per server, the provider policies, and the project's `AGENTS.md` as an explicit `instructions` entry: decision 4) and an `AGENTS.md` with Combwork's guidance, the agent's instructions and the notes. `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1` and `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1` (**Keep the project's OpenCode config out**, on by default) keep a project's own `opencode.json`, `.opencode`, plugins, a config above it and Claude Code's folders out (HI-2758: with policies alone a project's same-name server replaced Combwork's and its plugins ran). The system's `%ProgramData%\opencode` (an administrator's managed policy) is left in force: it outranks Combwork's on purpose.
- **Credentials** (design s10 to s16): the environment is built in a fixed order: the inherited variables OpenCode reads as a provider's key or token (`opencode.env.credentials`, from 2.2.6's integration listing) left out; the ambient credential files pointed at empty ones (`AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE`, `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`, `CLOUDSDK_CONFIG`, `AZURE_CONFIG_DIR`…, defence in depth); then Combwork's protected values last (the account's roots, the config folder, the password, the switches), which nothing inherited or chosen repoints. The providers whose sign-in uses what the PC already has (`opencode.ambient.integrations`: Amazon Bedrock's AWS profile, Google Vertex's gcloud credentials, Azure's `az`) are denied by policy unless the account saved a credential for them (read from `auth list` at each launch; denied when it can't be read); their files stay blocked unless that credential is the ambient method itself. **Claude Agent** (`claude-agent`) is denied in every config, under every switch, and its models refused at launch. **Keep other credentials from OpenCode** (on by default) turns the stripping and the ambient denials off; it also takes `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `HF_TOKEN` and the like from the agent's shell. An agent's extra arguments may not set `--server`, `--standalone`, `--session`, `--continue`, `--prompt` or `--auto`.
- **Only the connection's own provider** (HI-2769, Darren's option (a) after HI-2768's source research on 2.2.6): by default (`opencode.override.ownProviderOnly`, on) a launch's private config denies every provider and allows only the provider part of the connection's model (`provider.use * deny`, then `<own> allow`), placed **before** Claude Agent's deny and the ambient denies so those still win (2.2.6: the last matching statement wins; the config folder's policies outrank a project's). Why: 2.2.6's default side jobs stay on the chosen provider (titles pick a small model of the same provider, compaction the session's), but an `agents.title.model`/`agents.compaction.model` override can name another provider's model, and image generation falls back to any provider with an image model; signed-out free cloud models (`opencode/*-free`) are available with no account. With the switch on, a launch whose connection names no model, or no `provider/model` id, is refused (`providers.opencode.noModel`), new or resumed: with none, 2.2.6 chooses from its catalogue, free cloud models included. An unknown but valid id is taken. A real-tier test provider is its model. Account checks and sign-ins are unrestricted (they make no model calls; the model list shows every provider). Off (and in the Independent terminal preset, every override off): no allowlist and no model needed. Not added: pinning the title and compaction models (a same-provider small model is within the promise) and `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS` (it would break a connection whose own provider is `opencode`). It enforces provider identity, not the network: a provider's configured endpoint, web search and fetch, MCP servers, plugins and shell commands are outside it (HI-2768 §4).
- **Sessions**: Combwork picks the id (`ses_` and 26 base62 characters; 2.2.6's API takes any `ses…` id). A new session: `GET /api/session/<id>` 404, then `POST {id, location}`; a 200 there is an id clash and fails. The launcher records it in the account (`combwork-sessions\<id>.json`), which stands in for a transcript until HI-2762. A resume only looks: 200 must be that id in the launch's folder or the project's, a 404 fails ("session missing") and never creates one; a session another account made isn't resumed (its record isn't in this account's data). Modes: **Build** (the default, OpenCode's own permission rules), **Plan** (its plan agent, `default_agent`), **Approve all** (`--auto`, danger); no live switch; no efforts yet. Unpriced. History and usage (HI-2762) and the dialect (HI-2764) are their cards'.
- **Status from the server's events** (HI-2760, design s7 to s22; 2.2.6's recordings in `tests/fixtures/opencode/real-2.2.6`): OpenCode sends no hooks, so the launcher carries its server's event stream to Combwork's hook server (`providers/opencode/launcher.ts`'s `CwStream`, off main's thread), deciding nothing: it subscribes to `/api/event?types=…` (the types the tracker follows), projects its session's events (only the fields status needs, text cut: `events.ts`'s `projectEvent`) and posts them in order, each with its generation, with the launch's hook token. **Before the TUI starts** it subscribes and posts a **settled baseline snapshot**; failing that (a read, the post, the stream), the launch fails (`LAUNCHER_EXIT.baseline`) and its job ends the server, so a retry starts clean. A snapshot is **settled** when the session's durable watermark (`/api/experimental/session/<id>/log?after=0`'s `log.synced` seq) is the same before and after its reads (the session, its pending permissions `GET /api/session/<id>/permission`, its messages paged back with `limit` ≤ 200, `order`, `cursor` to a submission Combwork has taken, a resumed session's baseline marker or the start, within 10 pages and 1 MB a page); an unsettled one is never posted. A **baseline** must establish where Combwork's knowledge starts: a new session's is its start; a resumed session's stops at its newest idle marker (only an execution running after it matters, and the history before it isn't read); one whose messages were bounded out (a message over the size bound, the page limit, the body's) fails the launch, nothing posted. A reconnect, an overflow (512 items or 1 MB), a refused post, an over-long frame (256 KB) or a failed read holds what comes and takes a settled snapshot again, then posts what it held beyond its watermark, **all or nothing**: what doesn't fit the queue beside the snapshot is dropped and held anew, and the next snapshot covers it; a failed repair is asked for again, never ending the launcher. Combwork's side is the tracker (`events.ts`, per launch in its hook memo; `prepareHook` expands each body into the hooks it stands for, each handled in the launch's order through the turn ledger and the status rules): a turn is one **execution**, named by its first submission (its inbox id, the user message's id); a submission while one runs (a steer) is a prompt in it; `session.tool.*` are its tool calls; `permission.asked` (attributed by its assistant message) is **needs you**, `permission.replied` (by its request id) answers that call's wait, and another still pending is asked again; `session.retry.scheduled` is a retry; `execution.succeeded`/`failed`/`interrupted` end it (failed on `provider.auth` is a refused sign-in). A **compaction** (`/compact`, HI-2762's recording) is an execution of its own under its inbox item of type `compaction`, counting no prompt: `session.compaction.started` makes the agent compacting (the turn ledger's compaction the CLI began, under that id) and its execution's end ends it, however it ended; one inside a user's turn (none recorded) is that turn's, ended by `session.compaction.ended`. A snapshot's `compaction` message stands for that execution's submission. `session.usage.updated` (cost and tokens; no durable seq, so never replayed) is forwarded for HI-2762's live usage and gives no hook. A settled snapshot replays what Combwork hasn't had, once each, oldest first; a resumed session's closed history (at its baseline) counts nothing; a stale generation's body is ignored; history beyond the bounds is never invented (Combwork's own silence path says unknown). A test seam (`CW_TEST_OPENCODE_PROVIDER`, unpackaged builds only: HI-2763's real tier) puts a local test provider in every config Combwork writes, with every other provider denied, so a real run makes no cloud call; without it, nothing changes.
- **Combwork's tools, skills and guidance** (HI-2761): the combwork MCP server with its per-run token and the workspace servers the agent was given, in the launch's `mcp.servers`, every other server denied (`mcp.use`); each OpenCode server is the agent's own, so no token is shared. 2.2.6 offers MCP tools to the model only inside its Code Mode `execute` tool (`tools.combwork.cw_inbox(…)`, HI-2763's R0). Combwork's skills are copied into the private config folder's `skills` (the one skill folder 2.2.6 reads with both discovery switches on, listed to the model by id and loaded with its `skill` tool: HI-2761's R0b), each copy's revision what the agent gets; Combwork's guidance is in that folder's `AGENTS.md`, only with Combwork's tools. An **Independent** agent (HI-2731: the whole "as from a terminal" preset, read from its launch policy) gets no combwork server, skills or guidance, and all three switches off; with no server given and the project's config let in, its config has no `mcp.use` rules, so the project's own servers start as in a terminal. A managed launch with no servers still denies every one, and Claude Agent stays denied in every case. With **Keep the project's OpenCode config out** off, a project's server named as one Combwork gave replaces it, Combwork's own included (HI-2763's R0), as the setting says. Its reviewers review read-only (`extraDirs` not verified). A test seam (`CW_TEST_OPENCODE_PROVIDER`, unpackaged builds only: HI-2763's real tier) puts a local test provider in every config Combwork writes, with every other provider denied, so a real run makes no cloud call; without it, nothing changes.

**Tested CLI versions** (#365): each release ships `resources/tested-clis.json`, the version of each provider's CLI its real e2e tier ran against: `{ "<provider id>": { "version", "testedAt", "record" } }`, `record` being the run record's code. It is never typed by hand, and the versions are what Combwork itself selected: each suite's test copies of Combwork note the CLI their detection chose (the standalone one, never an editor extension's copy), its path and version, in a log the runner gives the suite (`CW_TEST_CLI_LOG`, carried into the test Combwork; `noteSelectedCli` in `testedClis.ts`, unpackaged test copies only), in the CLI homes the suite gave it. The runner starts no CLI of its own; it keeps each suite's CLIs in the run record (a "Real CLIs (as Combwork selected them)" line, and per suite in `run-record.json` beside `run-record.md`), and `npm run tested-clis` (`scripts/testedClis.mjs`) replaces a provider's entry only from a valid record in which every real suite of that CLI ran, passed and says which version its Combwork used, all the same one. Between releases it may lack Claude Code's entry (its real suites run in the default home until #368, so only the release's run writes it); `npm run release` refuses a manifest with an entry missing, from uncommitted changes, or from a commit that differs from HEAD in anything but the manifest (RELEASING.md). Main reads it on each provider check (`testedClis.ts`; `CW_TEST_TESTED_CLIS` replaces it in unpackaged builds, for tests) and compares the installed version by the adapter's `isNewer`: `AgentInstallInfo.tested` (`same`, `newer`, `older`, `unknown` when the CLI gave no version), null when the release names none. **Provider Setup** shows, under the CLI found, "Tested with X · installed Y": a tick when the same; newer: "This version came out after this Combwork release was tested. Most updates work; if something behaves oddly, report it (Copy Diagnostics)."; older: "Older than tested; consider updating."; unknown: that Combwork couldn't tell (`shared/testedClis.ts`). Nothing is blocked. **Copy Diagnostics** lists both versions per CLI, and the Agent API's `/v1/providers` (`cw_list_providers`, the Assistant's) gives `tested: { version, installed }`.

- Not bundled (proprietary; redistribution would need Anthropic's permission).
- **The standalone CLI is required** (Claude Code and Codex alike). Copies bundled with editor extensions (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf) are never used, even if set manually: they move on every extension update and can't be updated with `claude update`. If only an extension is present, the setup dialog explains that the CLI is still needed.
- Discovery: settings path → `PATH` → `~/.local/bin/claude.exe` → npm global.
- **`.cmd` launchers** (npm's `codex.cmd`, say) aren't run through cmd.exe when Combwork can tell what they run: a Node CLI's launcher that does nothing else, matched whole (npm's cmd-shim template, with its `node.exe` beside it or `node` on PATH, or the bare one-line `@node "%~dp0cli.js" %*`), is started as that node and script directly; one that sets anything, adds its own arguments or Node flags, or runs another interpreter is not, since a direct start would leave that out (`shimTarget` in `providers/common.ts`), so its command line can be as long as an .exe's (32,767 characters) and the first task and session name are passed as they are. cmd.exe takes at most 8,191 characters, less than the Assistant's Codex launch (its hooks, instructions and combwork server, about 9.5K). Any other `.cmd`/`.bat` still goes through cmd.exe, with its first task and name flattened to one plain line, and a launch too long for it is refused before it starts, saying to point Settings at the CLI's `.exe`.
- Not found → first-run dialog offers a one-click install using Anthropic's official installer, run in a visible terminal.
- On launch (if enabled): read `claude --version`, compare with the latest version its installer delivers, offer **Update** in a visible terminal. Never updates while sessions are live. **What its installer delivers** (HI-2729), for Claude Code and Codex alike: a copy WinGet installed (in WinGet's default portable roots or their Links folders: per user `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\{Packages,Links}`, per machine `%PROGRAMFILES%\WinGet\{Packages,Links}` and Program Files (x86)'s; a custom root in WinGet's own settings isn't known) is compared with the WinGet source's version (`winget show`, as for Copilot below) and updated with `winget upgrade --id Anthropic.ClaudeCode` / `OpenAI.Codex` `--exact --source winget`, since `claude update` leaves a WinGet install as it is ("Claude is up to date!") and WinGet gets each release days after npm and GitHub; WinGet's *no newer version* (`0x8A15002B`) ends such an update well. Codex otherwise: GitHub's latest release, `codex update`. Claude Code otherwise (native or npm): npm's dist-tag of the channel `claude update` follows, `claude update`. The channel is read, never changed, as Claude Code resolves it: managed settings first (the HKLM policy `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode` `Settings`, then `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json` merged with `managed-settings.d\*.json` in name order, then the HKCU policy only when neither is present; the first with a policy key used whole unless it sets `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"`), then the user's `settings.json`, else `latest`. Where it can't be told (an admin source that can't be read, a registry policy among them: one is absent only when `reg query` of its parent key lists no `ClaudeCode` subkey, and a lookup that is refused, times out or can't start is unreadable; a value that isn't `stable` or `latest`, a user `settings.json` that isn't JSON, npm with no tag for it) there is no latest version, so no Update and no *Up to date*. Server-managed settings (claude.ai) aren't on the PC to read. The setting's name, WinGet's version pattern and its time are advanced settings (`claude-code.update.channelSetting`, `cw.winget.version`, `cw.winget.showSeconds`).
- Auth is handled by each CLI itself. Combwork never touches credentials, and never edits a CLI's own config files.

### 11.1 Combwork's own updates

- **electron-updater** against GitHub Releases of `Suremise/combwork` (`publish:` in `electron-builder.yml`). It reads `latest.yml`, downloads the NSIS installer (differentially when a `.blockmap` is available) and checks its SHA-512 before installing. Only published releases of a public repository are seen (drafts are not); no token ships with the app. With no published release, checks report "No release of Combwork has been published yet". 0.1.0 (29 Sep 2026) was the first published release.
- **Settings → Updates**: *Check for updates automatically* (on: 30 s after start, then every 6 hours), *Download updates automatically* (on), *Install updates* — **Automatically, when Combwork quits** (default) or **Manually, with Restart and Update** — and *Include pre-releases* (off). With it on, a pre-release install (`-beta.n`, `-rc.n`) is offered the newest published version newer by semver, whichever of beta, RC or release it is (HI-2311: Combwork's own GitHub provider picks the tag from the releases feed, `src/main/updateFeed.ts`; electron-updater alone offers a running RC only a later RC, and a running beta no RC); a release install takes electron-updater's choice, the feed's newest entry. Combwork never installs while it is running: sessions are never cut off by an update.
- **Restart and Update** goes through the normal quit flow (the quit dialog when agents are working, including *wait for them*), then installs silently and reopens Combwork. Cancelling the quit cancels the update. The install (and Restart Combwork's restart) belongs to its own quit request (HI-2427): chosen while a quit or close question is already open, it only brings that question forward and is dropped, so cancelling it leaves nothing for a later quit; a quit already going ahead, or waiting for agents, takes it. Only over an older installed copy (#1647, below).
- **Where it shows**: the status bar's version item becomes *Combwork X available*, *Downloading Combwork X… N%* or *Restart to update to X* (click: update dialog); a notification when a download is ready; the update dialog (version, date, size, progress, release notes from the GitHub release, **Download**, **Skip This Version**, **Later**, **Restart and Update**, **On GitHub**); **Help → Check for Updates…** (always shows the result: up to date, available, or the error); the About panel and Settings → Updates (status and **Check Now**); the tray menu (*Restart to Update*). After an update, a notification links to the release notes.
- **Skip This Version** stops automatic checks offering that version; a manual check still shows it.
- **Local builds and what an install replaces** (#1647). On 23 Oct a running 0.9.2, which had downloaded the published 0.9.3, ran its installer when it quit (electron-updater's install on quit), and the user's local build of 0.9.3, with fixes the release lacked, didn't end up installed: most likely its installer, started after that quit, found the release's installer running and quit (the log shows the old version and the install on quit; which installer quit is inferred). So:
  - **A build says what it is**: `resources/build-identity.json` (`{ version, commit, local }`, `scripts/appIdentity.mjs`), `local: true` from `npm run dist`, `false` from `npm run release`; none (a build from before) is a release. Settings → Updates and About say **Local build X (abc1234)** for a local one.
  - **Versions compare by semver**, prereleases included (1.0.0-rc.2 < 1.0.0, `shared/updates.ts`). A newer release updates as before, a local build too. A published release of a running local build's own version is **offered, never downloaded**: a notice and the update dialog say so, with **Open Release Page** (its GitHub page; nothing is installed in the app). electron-updater never takes a release of the running version itself.
  - **An install is decided when it happens**, on the copy installed on disk as read then (`main/buildIdentity.ts`: its identity file, the version in its `app.asar`'s package.json, the identity file again), never the running Combwork's version: only a newer download is installed.
