A copy that can't be read (malformed, its identity and app disagreeing, changing under the read) is never replaced. Combwork's own quit installs (`installsOnQuit`, at the end of its quit flow, so a cancelled quit installs nothing; electron-updater's `autoInstallOnAppQuit` is off), and Restart and Update checks first, then again at the end of the quit; refused, it says why (*Combwork X wasn't installed*) and Settings → Updates shows it. A download is checked as it completes too: one Combwork won't install gets no *ready* notice and the status bar doesn't offer it. A refusal isn't kept once it no longer holds: **Check Now** reads the copy again, and so does **Restart and Update** (still offered), which go on once it reads older (HR3's round 1).
  - **A local build's installer installs last** (`build/installer.nsh`, `preInit`, compiled in only when `CW_LOCAL_BUILD=1`): every installer of this app holds the mutex `${APP_GUID}` while it runs and one finding it held quits (electron-builder's `ALLOW_ONLY_ONE_INSTALLER_INSTANCE`, the published releases' installers included). A local one first waits for it (at most 10 minutes; `SYNCHRONIZE | MUTEX_MODIFY_STATE`), lets it go and waits until it is gone, then carries on to take it; a timeout, or any call failing, installs nothing, with a message and exit code 3. Not the uninstaller's build, nor the elevated inner instance. A release installer finding a local one running quits, as before. A local build's install also deletes the updater's pending download (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\combwork-updater\pending`). `tests/installer` checks the handoff with stand-in installers in Windows Sandbox (both orders, an abandoned mutex, the timeout); with real installers it is unverified until checked so.
- Development builds never check (the status bar says so); tests point `CW_UPDATE_FEED` at a local feed, with their own download cache, and never run what they download.
- **A packaged Combwork a test started never checks** (#1332: each check fetches `latest.yml`, which GitHub counts as a download, and test launches were most of its count): with `CW_TEST_QUIET=1` (`testQuiet`, which the e2e suites set) it checks nothing, automatic or manual, and Settings → Updates says it is a test copy. A released 0.9, which can't be changed, is held off by the suites (tests/e2e/README.md, No update checks). The installed app is never started with it.
- **Install folder permissions** (#431): Electron refuses to start (a deliberate crash, nothing on screen) when its sandbox can't read its folder: a DACL with an entry for an AppContainer package SID but none for ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES (`S-1-15-2-1`). The installer (`build/installer.nsh`, `customInstall`, run by updates too) grants `*S-1-15-2-1:(OI)(CI)(RX)` on `$INSTDIR`, inherited by what it holds. At start, before Electron's check (which runs after the main script's first synchronous pass), `installDir.ts` reads the SDDL (`icacls /save`, ~20 ms) of the file Electron checks (`icudtl.dat`; the folder's if it isn't there) and, in that condition, grants the entry the same way, then reads it again; if that file doesn't inherit it from the folder, it also gets `*S-1-15-2-1:(RX)` of its own (that one file, read only). If it still lacks it, or can't be read again, Combwork tells the user and quits: a PowerShell Windows Forms window (Electron's other dialogs need `ready`) naming the folder, or the checked file when that is what still lacks the entry, with the PowerShell command (each argument a single-quoted literal: the folder grant, then the file's), **Copy Command** and **Close**; if PowerShell can't show it, Electron's `dialog.showErrorBox` (which works before `ready`) with the same text. Permissions it can't read at all leave the start as it was. Only the installed (packaged) app changes its folder: a development or test copy runs from `node_modules`' Electron, which it never changes (it tells the user instead), and tests point it at a test folder of their own (`CW_TEST_INSTALL_DIR`). The sandbox is never turned off.
- **The name** (#443, HI-2458): the app is displayed as **Combwork** (`productName`; `shared/appName.ts`), the window title and title bar ("Combwork Dev" for dev builds, also their Windows app ID's name), About, the status bar's version and the update items and notifications that name a version, the tray tooltip, native dialog titles, the installer, the Start menu and desktop shortcuts (`shortcutName`), Installed apps (`Combwork <version>`), the installer's file name `Combwork-Setup-<version>.exe` and the GitHub release title. Sentences and labels in the window say **Combwork** too ("Combwork couldn't…", Quit Combwork, Combwork skills), in every language, and the Assistant is just **the Assistant**, with no longer name. What agents see says Combwork too since HI-2463: the `combwork` MCP server and its `cw_*` tools, the `[CW]` doorbell and prefix (`NOTICE_PREFIX`; a stored line with the old prefix is made `[CW]` once, by the names upgrade, §4.1.2; Combwork's text keeps every word, since it may quote a person's or an agent's, and one naming an old tool or command outside its quotes, `<<< >>>` or `"…"`, gets a note on how the names map: `withCurrentNames`, HR1's round 1), `cw-progress` and its `##cw-progress` step lines (the only ones read since HI-2594: no old-name command, and an old-name step line is the command's own output), the `combwork:` plugin and `cw-` skill copies (the old-prefix copies retired by the names upgrade when provably Combwork's own, §4.1.2), guidance and tool descriptions, the session's `CW_*` variables (inherited `CW_*` ones stripped), the Agent API's `app`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, card history's author and Combwork's runs' names (stored ones from before still read). A conversation launched before it (SessionRecord without `names: 2`) is never resumed: its next resume starts a new one through Start Fresh, with that start's first prompt, the old one kept in Sessions, and one notice counts those that started. It carries on the agent's own work, as a handover to itself does: its watch stays, and its deliveries still due for the old conversation are for the new one (`carryConversation`), so none expires as another conversation's; what the old one read and never acked is shown again, in full, on the new one's next inbox read (`carriedFrom`; shown once to each conversation that reads it since, `replayedTo`, so a later fresh one, the old conversation resumed again, is shown it too; still received, never acked for it), and a notice rings for it. The `Combwork-Card` trailers stay (history reads them; an old-name trailer from before 1.1 is history, never read: HI-2594), and the profile is `%APPDATA%\Combwork` since HI-2461 (1.0's had the old name; set by main, since Electron would take `productName`), and the app ID, the install folder and the exe are Combwork's since HI-2460 (the install identity, below; 1.0's had the old name). Not moved: the workspace `.combwork` folders (HI-2462) and the update feed. An update renames the old shortcuts (electron-builder's installer keeps them under the new name). Releases before the rename, and their installers, had the old name. `tests/appName.test.ts` pins the names and the folders.
- **The install identity** (HI-2460, 1.1): the Windows app ID is `it.surmise.combwork` (`it.surmise.combwork.dev` for dev and test builds), installed as `Combwork.exe` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Combwork` (`executableName`), the Start menu and desktop shortcuts named Combwork (`shortcutName`). A new app ID is a new app to Windows (a new uninstall entry, installer mutex and shortcut AUMID), so the Combwork installer upgrades the 1.0 install itself, in its `customInit` (`build/installer.nsh`, the outer instance), before anything is installed, on a manual install and on 1.0's updater path (`--updated /S --force-run`) alike: (1) it takes 1.0's installer mutex too (its APP_GUID), held until it exits, so a 1.0 installer or updater can't run meanwhile (one running is waited for, at most 10 minutes; else exit 4, nothing changed); electron-builder's uninstaller never takes it, so no deadlock. (2) `build/legacyUpgrade.ps1`: the apps of both exact installations (Combwork's `$INSTDIR`, an RC's perhaps, and 1.0's recorded `InstallLocation`) are asked to close (`askToClose.ps1`, HI-1707) and checked by exact executable path to have exited (a list that can't be read counts as running: exit 5, nothing changed); 1.0's own uninstaller, in its install folder as its records say, runs as electron-builder's `uninstallOldVersion` does (a copy, `/S /KEEP_APP_DATA --updated _?=<its folder>`), then its uninstall entry and its exe must be gone (else exit 6: the profile folders untouched, the partial state said), and the Run values whose executable is exactly its exe are removed (Launch at login; others are left); then the profile folders move (§4.3): for each, one rename only when 1.0's is a folder and Combwork's is confirmed absent; before the local one, the installer's record `profile-move.json` (`{ v: 1, from, movedAt, by: "installer" }`) is put inside 1.0's folder, so it arrives with the folder or waits there for the next install (a record there that isn't the installer's is kept, and the folder moved without one; one that can't be written: not moved). Nothing is ever deleted or copied. The installer stops with a message (in its eight languages) on exits 4 to 6, and installs nothing. At each start the installed app writes Launch at login for its own exe while the setting is on (`loginItem.ts`). The MCP servers' paths are written at each launch, so they follow the new exe.
- Releasing: `npm run release` uploads a draft release (installer, `latest.yml`, blockmap) with the `gh` login; it is published by hand on GitHub. See `RELEASING.md`.

### 11.2 Connections (HI-980)

**A connection** is a configured CLI plus where it gets its model (Darren, 26 Oct ~22:20). For example "Anthropic · Max 1" is Claude Code, signed in; "DeepSeek" is Claude Code with a base URL and key; "ChatGPT · Work" is Codex, signed in; "Ollama (local)" is a local model.
- An agent runs on a connection, and switching accounts means picking another connection.
- Profiles (Work, Personal; HI-1202) sit above, per workspace: which connections are available, plus the Git identity, GitHub host and MCP credentials.
- "Provider" keeps meaning the CLI.
- Each connection has a `kind`, where it gets its model (Darren, 27 Oct ~08:55): `signIn`, its CLI's own sign-in; `server`, a server by its base URL, with a key or none (S6, below). DeepSeek, Ollama and other compatible services are presets of `server`, not kinds of their own.

Below, an **account** is a **sign-in connection**: a login folder of Combwork's, signed in through the CLI's own sign-in. Settings shows it as Settings → **Connections**. The code's names follow: the types (`Connection`, `ConnectionIdentity`, `ConnectionObserved`, `WorkspaceConnections`, `ConnectionsView`, `ConnectionStatus`), `config.json`'s `connections` and `lastUsedConnection`, `workspace.json`'s `connections`, the descriptor's `capabilities.connections`, the IPC (`connections:*`) and the event (`connections-changed`). Only private and on-disk names keep `account` (nothing has shipped, so nothing stored is renamed): the modules (`main/accounts.ts`, `shared/accounts.ts`, `AccountsSettings.tsx`) and their function names, the message and advanced-setting ids (`settings.accounts.*`, `claude-code.accounts.*`), Settings' section id, and the folder `<profile>\accounts`.

**Built in slices** (Darren, 26 Oct ~23:25), each merged behind a preview switch (Settings → Advanced → Connections (preview)) until S8 removed it: connections are on for everyone.
- **S1 (HI-1755):** launching on a connection.
- **S2 (HI-1769):** agent rows, and the template load dialog.
- **S3 (HI-1770):** model, effort and context belong to the connection, with the migration.
- **S4 (HI-1771):** the Agent API.
- **S5 (HI-1756):** usage per connection.
- **S6 (HI-1772):** base URL + key connections.
- **S7 (HI-1757, HI-1758, HI-1773):** Codex, Copilot and Ollama.
- **S8 (HI-1774):** removed the switch and the old plumbing. Combwork runs nothing from `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`, which stay the user's own for their terminal (Darren, 26 Oct). Below, **On for everyone**.

The design across every surface is HI-1755's design note and addendum. The decisions are on HI-980 and HI-1755.

**Launching on a connection** (S1):
- **Since HI-2106** an agent's `connection` is a connection's id and the account it launches on is that connection's (**Accounts and connections**, below, for which one and decision H's fallback); the launch itself (the claim, the check, the last look) is as here.
- **Which connection** (`resolveConnection`):
  - an agent's own choice (`AgentDef.connection`, Agent Settings, Add Agent, templates) when it is on in its workspace;
  - **off there:** the same CLI's workspace default, noted on the agent ("off here: the default runs it");
  - with no default, or a choice removed or for another CLI: **refused**, saying why.
  - No choice: the workspace's default for the CLI.
  - The Assistant: its own choice per workspace (`workspace.json` `assistantConnection`, Settings → Assistant), else the default.
  - **None on:** refused ("No Claude Code connection is on in this workspace"), with a banner in the project offering **Add a Connection**. Never the CLI's own home.
  - Each window's workspace resolves its own, so two run on different connections at once.
- **The launch** (`connectionForLaunch`):
  - **The claim:** a claim under the connection's lock, with its folder checked (removal is refused while it's held, and it's released however the launch ends).
  - **The check:** a fresh identity check.
    - **Refused:** signed out, its login changing throughout the check (`fresh: false`), or its folder missing or replaced.
    - **Goes ahead, noted:** a check that couldn't tell, or a changed login.
  - **Its home:** the connection's folder, set in the launch's environment under the descriptor's `homeEnv`.
  - **Just before spawning** (`launchOnChosen`, the launch's last await): the agent's own choice as saved then, read under the lock its saves take (the Assistant's: its workspace setting), is resolved again and must still be this connection, and it must still exist. Nothing awaits from there to the spawn, so no save lands between. Changed meanwhile: the claim is released and it starts once more on the choice saved now; changed again during that: refused ("changed again while it was starting"). Each launch looks at its own choice and the defaults it follows only: another agent's or the Assistant's save never ends it.
  - **On the run:** `launchedConnection` (id, name, note), fixed until the run ends. Its `id` and `name` are the account's (its home, login and usage: the session record keeps those); its `connection` (HI-2397) is the named connection on it whose values the run launched with, which the footer and the agent rows name (`launchedName`). A run on another connection than the one chosen now, the same account's too, shows ⟳ in its rows until it restarts; a run from before HI-2397 names its account.
  - **The choice** is part of the launch signature ("restart needed").
- **The CLI's own home, never read for a connection's agents:** its default model (`configuredDefaultModel(home)`), user memory (`memorySources(project, homes)`), skills and plugins (`skillRoots(home)`), file access (`fileAllowed(path, write, homes)`, the same narrow policy).
  - Provider Setup runs no `auth status` or sign-in on `~/.claude` for a CLI with connections (`connectionsManaged`).
  - Transcripts stay shared through the junction.
  - **Auto memory by its real path** (HI-1899, Advanced `claude-code.memory.realPath`, on). Claude Code writes a project's auto memory without asking only when every form of the path, the resolved one included, is inside the memory folder it computed (`<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/<key>/memory/`); the protected-path check on `.claude` comes first, so allow rules can't help (read in 2.1.312). Through the junction, every memory write asked.
    - **The fix:** each Claude Code launch on a connection (agents and the Assistant) gets `autoMemoryDirectory` (the setting's name is Advanced `claude-code.memory.setting`) in its `--settings`: the same folder by its resolved path, through any link in it too (`memoryDir.ts`); a part not made yet is named as Claude Code would make it. Nothing moves, nothing more is allowed, and no CLI file is written.
    - **The key:** Claude Code's own. The base is the repository's main working tree (every worktree shares it), else the folder. Every character but letters and digits becomes `-`. Past 200 characters, the first 200, `-` and its 32-bit hash in base 36.
    - **None set** (fail closed): a home whose `projects` is its own folder or doesn't resolve, a link on the way to the memory folder that doesn't lead to a folder (a dangling junction) or a file where a folder goes, git unable to tell the base, a settings scope that names `autoMemoryDirectory` (the user's `--settings`, managed, project, local or user) or that Combwork can't read, `CLAUDE_COWORK_MEMORY_PATH_OVERRIDE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_MEMORY_DIR` or `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` in the launch's effective environment (its own, or a settings scope's `env`, as Claude Code applies them: `effectiveEnv`), a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` there other than the connection's home, or the switch off.
- **Sign-out recovery** is per auth scope (`authScope`: the CLI, or the CLI and the connection), rechecked through the connection's own check. One connection signing out never stops, relabels or clears another's agents, in any workspace.
- **Switching at a safe point** (`connectionSwitch.ts`, `sessions.switchAtSafePoint`): offered on the restart banner and in Settings → Connections ("N running agents run on another connection than the one chosen now"). Which agents those are is judged by connection, as the ⟳ mark judges it (HI-2413, `connectionSwitchDue`): another connection on the same account counts, its own chosen again doesn't, and a run from before HI-2397 is compared by account; the banner counts the same agents the switch takes, not every restart an agent's settings ask for.
  - **One per agent:** asked again while one waits, nothing changes.
  - **The exit:** once its turn is over (HI-1706's predicate), its CLI's exit is typed once (a quit `held` typed nothing, so it's asked again at the next change).
  - **The resume:** only after that run has exited, its last session is resumed once, on the connection chosen then.
  - **Cancelled by:** a manual stop or start, its workspace closing, or Combwork quitting (no resume). It's never kept across a restart.
- **The test seam** (`CW_TEST_CLI_HOME_CONNECTION=1`, DEV_SEAMS; `lib.combworkEnv` sets it):
  - **When it applies:** only an unpackaged build with a test profile and an explicit CLI test home, never the user's own (compared by real path, so a junction or 8.3 alias is the user's too).
  - **What it does:** launches as before connections where the workspace has none on, with the CLI's own sign-in handling.
  - **Where it's off:** the `connections` suite sets it to `0`.

**Model, effort and context belong to the connection** (S3, HI-1770; Darren, 26 Oct ~23:10 and ~23:25 (2)):
- **Since HI-2106** a connection is a setup on an account and holds the mode and extra arguments too (**Accounts and connections**, below): the layers here are the accounts migration's reading of the data from before; its move and notice are kept.
- **Each connection's defaults** (`Connection.defaults`: model, effort, context; Settings → Connections → Defaults for agents on it). The CLI's first sign-in connection gets its old per-CLI defaults copied (`defaultsFrom: 'cli'`; since S8 only the first, below), as do connections from before, once, only where `defaults` is absent; edited, they are the user's. The pickers use the connection's own models (`connectionModels`, by its kind: a sign-in connection's are its CLI's catalogue).
- **Resolution** (`agentLaunchSettings` with a `connection` layer, for every CLI with connections): the agent's own, else its connection's default, else the CLI decides in the connection's home. Never the per-CLI defaults or the project's model, effort and context. With no connection usable, the agent's own alone. An explicit context off is kept. Permission mode and extra arguments stay the CLI's and the project's. The Assistant's own are its agent's, else Settings → Assistant's, then its connection's defaults.
- **An effort the model that runs doesn't take** (the agent's or the connection's default model, else the connection home's configured default, else the catalogue's) is kept but not passed at launch.
- **Screens:** the CLI page's default model, effort and context rows and Project Settings' model, effort and context rows are hidden (a note points to Settings → Connections). Agent Settings and Add Agent name **Connection default (…)**, and the Agents list says "Its connection's defaults (…)".
- **The move** (once per project and CLI): each of the CLI's agents without its own model, effort or context gets the project's (an explicit value is never overwritten, and nothing is given where the project set nothing).
  - It runs in one write under the project's lock, with its record `project.json migrations.connections1[cli] = { at, moved }`, so an interrupted run repeats and a second changes nothing; a CLI given connections later moves its own.
  - **A launch awaits it** before reading the project, so none starts with the project's values unread and not yet its agents'. A failure refuses the launch, saying so, and the next start retries. It also runs at a workspace's open and when Connections are turned on.
  - The project's own values stay in project.json, read only by the move (for a later upgrade from 0.9 or an RC). The Assistant's home is never moved.
- **The notice** of moved values the agent's connection can't use is worked out from the moves' records when shown (`connections:notice`, the asking window's workspace only), so a stop between the move and anything else loses nothing. Dismissed entries are kept app-wide (`ui.connectionsNoticeDismissed`, by project and entry id), so they stay dismissed; a later CLI's entries are new.

**The Agent API and Combwork tools take a connection** (S4, HI-1771; api.version 10; AGENT_API.md "Connections"):
- **`connection`** on adding and changing agents (the Assistant's `POST`/`PATCH /v1/projects/{name}/agents…`, cw_add_agent and cw_update_agent): an id, or a name unique among those on in the workspace (`connectionRef`; two sharing it: 409, use its id; none: 404). Saving checks it with the write (on here for the agent's CLI).
  - **With `provider`:** they must agree (409). **Alone:** its CLI is the agent's, and on another CLI it is that change of CLI (refused while running; model, effort, mode, context, last session and the old connection cleared). Whether the CLI changes is decided again against the agent as saved under the lock (changed meanwhile: refused whole).
  - **Left out:** kept. **`null` or `""`:** cleared (the CLI's default). **`provider` alone:** no connection of its own (the CLI's default; starts refused while none is on).
- **Status:** each agent row has `connection` (the one chosen, `{ id, name, problem? }`, or null), `launchedConnection` (the account its run is on, with `connection`, the connection on it the run launched with: HI-2406) and `switchPending`. A project agent isn't told the name of one not on in its workspace.
- **`GET /v1/connections`, `GET /v1/connections/{ref}`** (`connectionsFor`, `connectionShown`): a project agent sees only those on in its workspace (`id`, `name`, `cli`, `kind`, `signedIn`; another one is 404 by id or name); the workspace token and the Assistant see every one, with `on`, `default`, `email` and `plan`. Nobody sees a token, a key, where a login is kept, its settings or defaults; `details=true` widens nothing. cw_list_providers lists each CLI's connections on here.

**The rows and templates name connections** (S2, HI-1769):
- **One rule for every row** (`connectionOf`, `src/shared/connectionLabel.ts`), the launch's own (`resolveConnection`), so the window and a start never disagree:
  - its own choice on here: its name;
  - its own off here, same CLI, with a default: the default's name, its hover saying so;
  - removed, another CLI's, off with no default, or none on: shown as unusable, saying why. No connection is made up for it;
  - none of its own: the workspace's default for its CLI, which it follows (the hover says so).
  - **While it runs,** a row names the connection its run is on, until it restarts, marked ⟳ when that isn't the one it would start on now (or that one is now unusable).
- **Where:** Project Settings → Agents (the connection's name in place of the CLI's, the CLI's icon kept), the Overview's running agents, the sidebar's agents hover table (a Connection column), and the Assistant panel's agent hover.
- **Templates:**
  - **Saving:** an agent's connection is kept by id, with its name beside it (`connectionName`), which is for display only.
  - **The load dialog** has a Connection column, and asks only about an agent whose **own** connection can't be used here: removed or never on this machine, another CLI's, or off. An agent with none of its own follows the default and isn't asked about.
    - For each one asked about, the box's first choice, preselected, is **the workspace's default** (it then follows it). The CLI's connections on here follow, each pinning that one.
    - Never matched by name, never another CLI's.
  - **Loading:** the answers go by the plan's indexes and must be for exactly the agents asked about now, else the load is refused ("connections changed since you looked"). Each connection is checked again as the agent is prepared and with the write. One turned off or removed meanwhile refuses the whole load, nothing changed (the load is all or nothing).
  - **Add Agent from Template:** its own connection where it can be used; else the default, and a notice says why.
  - Combwork's own templates' agents moved to another CLI drop their connection.
- **An agent's own connection is checked with the write that saves it** (Add Agent, Agent Settings, the template load): on here for its CLI, else refused, saying why; never dropped quietly. Agent Settings may keep the one already saved when it's off here (the default runs it).
- **Another CLI's connection:** Add Agent's and Agent Settings' choice of connection also lists the other CLIs' connections on here. Picking one changes the agent's CLI, which Agent Settings asks about first, as a change of CLI does (its model and the rest start again, and its conversations stay with the old CLI). Never while it runs.

**Plan usage per connection** (S5, HI-1756; `planUsage.ts`, the status bar's `PlanUsageStatus`, the Overview's and Project tabs' `PlanLimits`):
- **Kept per connection:** a session launched on a connection reports that login's own limits (`reportPlanUsage(provider, report, agent, launchedConnection)`), kept by the connection's id in `config.json` `connectionPlanUsage`, never mixed into its CLI's `planUsage` (two logins are two sets of figures). A session not on a connection (Copilot, or a test copy on its CLI's test home) reports its CLI's, as before. The windows are told which connection a report is for (`plan-usage` with `connection`).
- **Warned of per connection:** the 80% and 95% warnings are kept as `connection:<id>:<limit>` in `planWarnings`, once per reset period each, the notice naming the connection ("96% of the 5-hour limit used on Max 1").
- **Removing a connection** takes its usage and warnings with it.
- **A login's figures** (HR2's round 1): kept with the login they came from (`login`, a hash of its email and organisation, `usageLogin`), and taken only from a session launched as the login the connection is signed in as now (its latest check's, else the accepted one: `connectionLoginNow`). The run records who it launched as (`launchedConnection.login`, from the launch's fresh check). A session still running as another login (one kept since, or changed in a pane), or whose launch couldn't tell who, reports nothing. When the connection is signed in as another login than its figures are from, they and its warnings are cleared, here and in the windows (`plan-usage-cleared`), so none shows under the new email; signed in again as the same login, they stay.
- **The status bar:** for a CLI that has connections, one item per connection a session of this window's workspace (its projects' agents and its Assistant) runs on, named before its limits ("Max 1 · 5h 62% · Week 10%"), its hover the connection, its CLI and plan, then each limit. It is what each session launched on, not what is chosen for it, until it restarts. That CLI's own item (its sessions' reports from before connections) isn't shown.
- **The Overview and Project tabs:** under each such CLI, each of its connections on in this workspace or in use by its sessions, named with the login it is signed in as, then its limits (or "Its limits appear after the next message in a session on Max 1"). None on: a line saying so, pointing to Settings → Connections.
- **The pane footer's connection** (S1) also says who it is signed in as, in its hover.
- A CLI without connections (Copilot) keeps one item and one set of limits, as before.

**Usage moves** (HI-2195; the design is HI-2195's s7 as revised by s9, s11 and s13, checked by HR1; Darren's request of 31 Oct: "move them to Anthropic-2 when the usage gets to 98%"; `main/usageMoves.ts`, `shared/usageMoves.ts`, `components/UsageMoveRule.tsx`):
- **The rule, one per account, the user's:** `Account.usageMove` `{ percent, limit: weekly | fiveHour | any, to }` in `config.json`, set in a sign-in account's Account Settings… dialog, from its ⋯ in Settings → Accounts & Connections (HI-2528, Darren 4 Nov ~21:40: off the card; "When it reaches [98]% of [its weekly limit], move its agents to [account]", off by default; `connections:setUsageMove`), to another account of the same CLI. The Assistant reads it (`cw_connection list`) but can't set it. Removing the target account turns the rule off.
- **When it fires:** a limit of the rule's kind (`any`: the weekly and the 5-hour limit, each on its own) reaching the share in its current period (its reset ahead; an expired reading, or one with no reset time, never fires), as `connectionPlanUsage` keeps it for the login the account is signed in as now. Looked at on each usage report, accounts or connections changed, a sign-in, a workspace opening and the Advanced switch; never on a timer.
- **Once per limit and period:** `config.json` `usageMoves[account][limit]` records the period (`resetsAt`, the same period as `samePeriod` tells it), the rule it fired with and each agent it handled (`<project id>/<agent id>`: `moved`, `kept` on the user's own choice, or `failed`), kept until the reset passes. A handled agent isn't looked at again in that period, so a manual return holds; a reset moves nothing back. A rule changed within the period is a new firing. A workspace opened later in the period catches up.
- **Who moves:** every project agent of the open workspaces, and each workspace's Assistant (HI-2530, Darren 4 Nov: "Assistant -> Assistant"; before, never), whose connection as it would launch (`resolveAgentConnection`: its own, or its CLI's first usable here) is on the account. The Assistant moves as an agent of its home does: only between its turns, once per period, never back, and kept where the user puts it (Settings → Assistant's choice counts as a manual one); Settings → Assistant then shows its new connection.
- **Where to** (`matchConnection`, HI-2530): the target's connection with the same **tag** as the agent's connection (`Connection.tag`: free text, optional, trimmed, at most 40 characters, compared ignoring case and runs of spaces; the first in order if several have it; an untagged connection skips this), else the same name (any case), else the target's first. Combwork reads no meaning into a tag (it isn't a workflow role). Set in the connection dialog (**Tag**), on `POST`/`PATCH /v1/connections` (`tag`, api.version 13) and `cw_connection`, shown beside the connection's name on its row and in `cw_connection list`.
- **When:** a stopped agent's connection is written at once. A running one's is written at its safe point (HI-1755's switch, `switchAtSafePoint` with a usage intent: once its turn is over, never mid-turn), then it is resumed on it, the same conversation. At that moment, under the agent's lock, the move is checked again: the Advanced switch on, the same rule and firing, the target usable, and the agent's choice unchanged since it was queued (`agentChoice.ts`: every save of an agent's connection through `projectAgents.updateAgent` counts, the same connection chosen again too). A manual choice in between keeps the agent where the user put it for the rest of the period (`kept`, through later reports and a restart); a stop or start, the workspace closing or Combwork quitting cancel it and leave the agent to be tried again.
- **Sharing a switch** (`SwitchIntents`, `connectionSwitch.ts`): one switch per agent can be for HI-1755's own reason (`base`) and a usage move. A usage move rejected or dropped (the rule changed, the switch turned off) leaves a base switch to go on without its write; one alone is cancelled with nothing typed.
- **A target that can't take them** (gone or another CLI's, signed out, no connections, already at the rule's share of a limit it watches, off in a workspace, or a write failing three times for an agent): nothing is marked handled except the given-up agent, and a notice says why, once per reason and period. Since a full target takes no one, two rules pointing at each other never bounce agents; nor does a rule move an agent back onto an account a rule moved it off in a period not reset yet.
- **The notice** (Notifications, and told as plan-usage notices are): "3 agents move from Anthropic-1 to Anthropic-2", naming them (the Assistant among them when it moves), each with the rule that matched it ("Builder (by tag Builders)", "(by name)", "(to its first connection)"), saying a working one moves when its turn ends and that moving back is by hand.
- **Off switch:** Settings → Advanced → **Move agents at a usage threshold** (`cw.accounts.usageMoves`, on by default). Off, no rule fires and waiting moves are dropped; the rules stay, and their rows say so.
- **For agents:** `cw_connection list` ends with a line per account with figures or a rule ("Usage of Anthropic-1: weekly 95% (resets 2026-11-02T09:00Z); moves its agents to Anthropic-2 at 98% of the weekly limit"; `GET /v1/connections` `usage`). `cw_wait_for_tasks` takes `usage: [{ account, percent, limit? }]` with wake, alone or beside cards or lanes (`POST /v1/tasks/wait`): it wakes once an account's limit reaches the share ("Already: …" when it has), kept in watches.json with the watch.

**Launch settings: as from a terminal** (HI-2670; Darren, 6 Nov: "turn off including guidance, tools, mcp and anything else that Combwork launches the agent with… as if it was launched from a terminal"; the design is the card's s9, s13 and s16, OK'd by HR3; `shared/launchPolicy.ts`, `main/connectionLaunch.ts`, `components/LaunchSettings.tsx`). **Built.**
- **Connection level only** (decision 2): `Connection.launch` holds `guidance`, `tools`, `typing` (each stored only as `false`) and `overrides`, each of its CLI's override switches by its key (`statusLine`, `mcpIsolation`…; only those not at their default). Absent: everything, as before. An agent is made plain by choosing a plain connection; there is no per-agent setting. `launchPolicy(conn, cli, { assistant })` is the one owner: the launch, its hooks and deliveries, the Agent API, project status and Settings read it.
- **The switches moved** from app scope: `cw.guidance` and every `<cli>.override.*` are a connection's now (`onConnection` in `advanced.ts`): Settings → Advanced and the settings catalogue no longer list them, `advanced.set` refuses them, and everywhere they read as their default. Migration `launch1` (config.json's `migrations`, once, at start, not while advanced.json can't be read): each that advanced.json had set is copied onto every connection of its CLI (`cw.guidance` onto all), key by key, so a mix survives (`copyAppSwitches`). Combwork's own runs of a CLI that read an override (Copilot's sign-in check and model catalogue: `noAutoUpdate`, `stripGitHubTokens`) leave it off only when every connection of that CLI has it off (`ownRunOverride`), so just after the copy they do as before; a change of a connection checks the CLI again.
- **The preset** "Launch as from a terminal" (decision 1) sets everything off (`terminalPreset`); any switch on again makes it partly plain (`plainness`). Settings: a connection's **⋯ → Launch Settings…**, and an **As from a terminal** / **Partly plain** badge on its row. Agent API: `PATCH /v1/connections/:ref` takes `launch` (`{"preset": "terminal"}`, `{}` for all on) and `confirm`; connection and agent rows give `launch` in short when not everything (`policySummary`); `cw_connection` takes both.
- **What each switch takes off a launch** (`effectiveHere` and `startReserved` in `sessions.ts`, frozen on the run as `policy`):
  - **guidance:** the guidance and its latest handover, the Workspace notes note, `CW_GUIDANCE=0` for the combwork server.
  - **tools:** the combwork server, every skill delivered (Combwork's and the workspace's; copies already in the folder go by the copy book, kept while another session there may read them), the agent's API token and `CW_API_URL`/`CW_API_TOKEN_FILE`, the dialect file, `cw-progress` on `PATH`, the review copies' grant, `CW_PROJECT`, `CW_PROJECT_PATH`, `CW_WORKSPACE`, `CW_AGENT` and `CW_PROVIDER`; with `mcpIsolation` off as well, the workspace's MCP servers too.
  - **typing:** the launch's first task (refused when asked for, never dropped), and every line of Combwork's.
  - **overrides:** each `<cli>.override.<key>` as the connection says (`LaunchContext.overrides`); with every one off, Agents' temp folder goes back to the system Temp.
  - **Kept:** the connection's model, effort, context, permission mode and own `extraArgs` (the user's), its home and server variables, `CW_HOOK_TOKEN`, `CW_RUN_ID`, `CW_SESSION_ID`, the slot's variables, and the status-only parts each CLI needs for them: its hooks (Claude Code's `--settings` with its hooks and status line forwarder, `--plugin-dir` and an empty `--mcp-config`; Codex's `-c hooks.*`, its per-launch trust and rate-limit nudge; Copilot's hooks plugin and an empty `--additional-mcp-config`). `tests/plainLaunch.test.ts` holds each CLI to that list.
  - Changing a switch never erases context a conversation already has: a resume keeps what earlier launches gave it.
- **Hooks:** status observations always stay. What injects context follows its owning switch and the agent's role **now**: SessionStart context the guidance switch, PreToolUse lock replies the tools switch (the edit is still claimed), UserPromptSubmit/Stop inbox notices the typing switch (`noticeIn`, `startContextFor`, `preToolUse`).
- **Typing and deliveries:** `sessions.keepsOut(project, agent)` (`independent`: its role now; `plain`: its launch without tools or typing) gates `whyNoLine` (no line of Combwork's), `createDelivery` and every recheck (refused, its sender told why), `newConversation` and a start with a task.
- **Independent** (§16.10.6) is the role a tools-off connection gives (`readToolsOffWith`: main reads the agent's connection, the window `AgentInfo.toolsOff`), whatever is saved. Turning a connection's tools off, moving an agent onto such a connection, or choosing Independent, where that takes an agent in an open workspace off a running lane or from a card in Doing or Review, is refused unless it carries `confirm`: the fingerprint of that exact set (`launchImpact`, `agents:impact`), worked out again as it is saved, so a stale confirmation never approves newly affected work. Such a lane pauses (`independent` status) until it gets another agent or ends, here and in a workspace opened later; its cards stay. A usage move never moves an agent onto a connection whose tools differ.
- **The Assistant** (`assistant`) always gets guidance, tools and typing, whatever its connection says (its role, instructions and wakes); its connection's overrides apply. Launch Settings say so on a connection it uses.

**On for everyone** (S8, HI-1774; Darren, 26 Oct ~23:20, with the Assistant's list on HI-1755; HR3's design check):
- **No switch.** The preview switch is gone, dropped from advanced.json by the names upgrade's profile step (HI-2598; never listed as unknown). `connectionsManaged(cli)` is a CLI with connections and not the test seam (unchanged, for test copies only).
- **Removed for a CLI with connections** (Claude Code, Codex): the per-CLI default model, effort and context rows (Settings → Claude Code, → Codex) with the greyed "moved to Connections" row, Project Settings' model, effort and context rows, their entries in the settings catalogue (so the Assistant's settings tool can't set them), every launch path reading the CLI's own home or the per-CLI and project values, and Provider Setup's sign-in (refused, `signInConnections`). Their stored values stay: the per-CLI ones are **migration input only**, given once to the CLI's first sign-in connection (or to connections from before defaults, `seedConnectionDefaults`), recorded in `config.json` `connectionDefaultsTaken` in the same write; every CLI with a connection from before the record (a preview's, whatever its defaults) is recorded as having taken them at start (`seedConnectionDefaults`) or at the next add, so removing those connections never brings them back; a later new connection starts with none, the CLI deciding. The project's are read only by the S3 move, which is kept, awaited before a launch reads the project.
- **Copilot** (HI-1758, held): no connections, its own machine-wide login, model, effort, context, setup and plan usage, all by its capabilities (no provider id in the UI). Settings → Connections says so in a line ("GitHub Copilot has no connections: it signs in once for the whole PC, in Help → Provider Setup…").
- **Where nothing is on** (decision 1a for everyone): a start is refused (`main.connections.launch.none`), never on `~/.claude`. The project's banner offers **Add a Connection**; the **Assistant panel** shows the same banner while neither its own choice nor the workspace's default is on (`useLaunchConnection` null); **Provider Setup**'s tab for such a CLI says how many of its connections are on in the workspace ("signs in per connection: 2 are on…", or none yet) with **Open Connections**, in place of a sign-in of its own. A test copy on its CLI test home (the seam) shows none of them.
- **The one-time notice** ("Agents now run on connections: add one for Claude Code and Codex in Settings → Connections…", **Add a Connection**, **Dismiss**): main decides (`ConnectionsView.intro`: the CLIs with connections that are on and not on a test home, while no connection was ever added and it wasn't dismissed), so every window shows and hides it together; adding a connection or Dismiss sets `ui.connectionsIntroShown` for good. It is separate from S3's notice of moved settings, which stays.
- **The Agent API:** no refusal for connections being off; `provider` stays the CLI's alias (deprecating it is a 1.x decision). No api.version change.

**Accounts and connections** (HI-2106, card 1 of HI-2056; the design is HI-2105's s11 as revised by s13, with decisions A–H, OK'd by Darren on 30 Oct ~10:45). It replaces S3's layers above: where they differ, this holds. Cards HI-2107 to HI-2109 build the screens, the Agent API and templates on it; until then today's screens and API work on it through a thin adapter (below).
- **An account** (`Account`, `config.json` `accounts`) is a sign-in or a server: what S1–S8 called a connection, without its defaults, keeping its id, so its folder (`<accounts>\<id>`), its key-store entry and its `connectionPlanUsage` key don't move. Accounts are on or off per workspace, as before (`workspace.json` `connections[cli].on`, whose ids are accounts'; the stored `default` is gone). **One order for all CLIs** (decision A): `accounts`' order. It replaces the provider order, each CLI's connection order and Default/Make Default; a CLI's first account on in a workspace is the one its agents fall back to there.
  - **The CLI's own home as an account** (`home: 'cli'`, made by Combwork, never removed): the one PC-wide sign-in of each provider without connections (`pcWideSignIn`: Copilot's, decision C, id `copilot`, and Antigravity's, HI-2544, id `antigravity`), its home the CLI's own; and a test copy's CLI test home (the seam, `cli-<provider>`), made the first time the seam needs it. Both are on in every workspace and aren't Combwork folders (no checks, watches, keys or trust). Settings lists Copilot's (HI-2107), not a test home's.
- **A connection** (`Connection`, `config.json` `connections`): `{ id, account, name, model?, effort?, use200kContext?, permissionMode?, extraArgs? }`, each value absent meaning the CLI decides. Ordered within its account by their order in the list; an account's first is its **base connection**, made with it (named after it). Connections have no on or off of their own: one is usable where its account is on. A server account's take no effort or context.
- **Agents and the Assistant hold only `connection`** (a connection's id) for how they launch, with `provider`, its account's CLI, kept beside it. No agent, project or provider layer is read to launch.
- **The launch** (`agentLaunchSettings(cli, connection, settings, server)`): the connection's values, else the CLI's: its default model and effort, its default mode (also for a mode it won't take now, a no-guardrails one switched off), a 1M context, no extra arguments. Which connection (`resolveAgentConnection`, decision H): its own, on an account of its CLI that's on here; its account off here, the connection removed (or another CLI's), or none: its CLI's first usable connection here (the base connection of the first account in the order that's on), noted on the run as before (`offFallback`); none usable: refused, saying so. An effort the model that runs doesn't take, left by a later catalogue change, is kept but not passed (as before).
- **An effort a model doesn't take is refused when it is saved** (decision E): every save the user makes refuses a change of model or effort that leaves one, nothing changed (`assertEffortTaken`: Agent Settings, Add Agent, the Agent API, the connection dialog (HI-2107); Settings → Assistant before the change of settings is saved, `checkLaunchSettings` through `config.onSettingsCheck`, the pair made with what the connection keeps, so `settings:update` and the settings tool refuse it whole and nothing changes).
- **The migration, one rule:** for each agent and the Assistant, take exactly what `SessionManager.effective()` launched it with at 16e8d6129, through whichever layer applied (`connection`, or `legacy`: Copilot), kept verbatim as the migration's reading of the old data (`legacyEffective`, `legacyLaunchSettings` in `shared/connectionDefaults.ts`): its model, effort, context, permission mode and extra arguments (the CLI's and the project's joined, `joinArgs`, so they split into exactly the same). Point it at the connection on the account it ran on with those five values, made if none is (`connectionFor`), named after what differs from the account's base connection ("Personal · High · Plan"; the Assistant's "Personal · Assistant"; a number added to a name taken). Matching setups share one connection everywhere.
  - **Each account's base connection** is made the same way: what an agent on it with nothing of its own launched with (its old defaults, the CLI's mode and extra arguments, no project's; `baseValues`). Global settings are never copied in bulk: the global 200K context isn't carried onto connections (the connection layer ignored it); for the legacy layer (Copilot) it is carried where it applies (Copilot has no context choice).
  - **Agents with no connection** are pinned to the one they resolved to; **an agent whose connection was off here** to the workspace's first on, as it ran; one removed since, to its CLI's first on here, else its first account. **An agent whose CLI has no account at all** (an upgrade from 0.9 before one is added) keeps no connection, and its own model, effort and context, with the mode and extra arguments it would have launched with, are kept in the project's record (`migrations.accounts1.unplaced`); once its CLI has an account here it gets the connection with them over that account's base (`placeUnplaced`), at the workspace's next look (an open, an account added or turned on) or before it launches. An agent given a model, effort, mode or context while its CLI has no account keeps them on itself the same way, until it gets one.
  - **HI-1770's move** of a project's own model, effort and context onto its agents is made first where a launch would have made it, and its record (`connections1`) is kept: its notice of values a connection can't use is kept (it reads the agent's connection now).
  - **The Assistant** gets a connection for each CLI it has a setup for in the workspace (`assistantConnection[cli]` set, or `settings.assistant.providers[cli]` with any value), its launch on that CLI as it would run it now; only the active one (the one it runs) is its agent's. The others are kept in its home's record (`migrations.accounts1.assistant`), which a change of its CLI picks.
  - **Copilot's** Settings → GitHub Copilot values become its account's base connection; its agents follow the rule.
  - **Templates'** `connection` and `connectionName` are dropped as a template is read, and never written; HI-2109 drops their model, effort, mode and context too, and chooses connections when one is loaded (§16.10.6).
  - **The default provider goes** (decision A): the project's is removed; Settings' stays read-only. A new agent naming nothing goes on the first account in the order that's usable here (its CLI on and installed).
- **How it runs:** `config.json` once at start, before anything reads it (`config.ts`, `migrations.accounts1`, with the old connections kept read-only in it as `legacy`, the input for workspaces not opened yet; the order's one-time move, HI-1875, moves them too). Each project's and the Assistant's home's files when the workspace opens, and before anything launches there (`ensureMigrated`, `connectionMoves.ts`), under their locks: `config.json` is saved first, and a write that needs a connection not made yet writes nothing; the connection is made, saved, and the write runs again (`withConnections`), so a project never names a connection `config.json` lost (a save that fails publishes nothing and is tried again). Then the file's own old fields (`providers`, `defaultProvider`, 0.1's flat fields, agents' model, effort, mode and context) are removed in the same write that records `migrations.accounts1`, so an interrupted run repeats and a second changes nothing. `workspace.json`'s own (`assistantConnection`, each CLI's stored `default`) go in one write recording its `migrations.accounts1`, after its Assistant's home. A failure is said once (the project's move notice) and tried again at the next open or launch; a launch it fails is refused, saying so. Global sources (`settings.assistant.provider` and `.providers`, `settings.providers[cli]`'s default model, effort, mode, extra arguments and 200K, `settings.defaultProvider`, `settings.providerOrder`) stay in `config.json`, read-only, for workspaces not yet opened: 1.0 never deletes them. One-way, as §16.17 allows: an older Combwork can't read `accounts` and `connections`.
- **Today's screens and the Agent API** (the adapter, until HI-2107 and HI-2108):
  - Since HI-2108 an agent sent to the window (`AgentInfo`) has its connection's id as `connection`, as saved, and its connection's model, effort, context and mode as its own (the footer before it starts, the stopped agent's mode menu), never sent back; the Agent API names connections (below).
  - A change of an agent's model, effort, mode, context, connection or CLI (Agent Settings, Add Agent, quick add, templates, the Agent API) becomes the connection on its account (or the account named) with its current values and the change over them (a value emptied: the base connection's), made if none is (`connectionFrom`, `projectAgents.ts`); another CLI's agent gets only what the change gives. Cleared (`connection: null`): its CLI's first usable connection here.
  - Settings → Assistant's CLI, values and connection per CLI are gone since HI-2108 (its dialog chooses its connection); `pointAssistant` with them. Project Settings' provider pages write each agent's connection the same way.
  - A new account's base connection takes the per-CLI defaults (mode, extra arguments) as it is made (with the old per-CLI model, effort and context for a CLI's first sign-in account, once, as before); since HI-2107 no screen shows or changes them.
- **Agents, the Assistant and the Agent API choose a connection** (HI-2108; HI-2105's wireframes, decisions A, B, D and H):
  - **Add Agent** (`AddAgentDialog`): Name, **Connection**, Note, Role in the workflow, MCP servers. The connection picker (`ConnectionChoice`, `ConnectionChoice.tsx`, shared with HI-2109's template dialogs) groups connections by account (`<optgroup>` per account: "Personal (Claude Code)"), offers only those usable here (`offeredConnections`, `shared/connectionLabel.ts`: on accounts on in the workspace or the CLI's own home, of CLIs turned on, in the one order) and preselects the first (decision A, `firstUsableConnection`); a saved one off here or removed stays listed, saying so. **New Connection…** opens HI-2107's connection dialog on the chosen connection's account and chooses what it makes. Under it, its values in a line (`connectionLine`, HI-2107's `connectionSummary`). No provider, model, effort, mode or context: the CLI follows from the connection. **Quick add** (`actions.quickAddAgent`) sends the first usable connection (a resumed session's CLI's, when it names one); with none usable (no account on, a test copy on its CLI test home) it sends a provider, as before.
  - **Agent Settings** (`AgentSettingsDialog`): the same picker with its summary, and name, note, role and MCP servers as before. A running agent's picker offers its own CLI's connections only, saying another CLI's can be chosen once it is stopped (its conversations stay with their CLI); choosing another CLI's asks first (*Switch to Codex?*). `agents:update` with a connection sets its CLI from it (`updateAgent`: a change of CLI refused while it runs, its last session cleared).
  - **No account on here** (HI-2127, not for a test copy on its CLI test home): the picker's line ends with **Open Accounts & Connections**, and Add Agent's **Start a session now** is unticked and disabled with *No account is on here yet* beside it; the agent can still be added, and no session is started.
  - **Off here is not missing** (HI-2650). Where nothing can start for want of a connection, what exists but is off here is named, never "add one". `offHereChoice` (shared/connectionLabel.ts) picks it, and nothing is turned on until the user clicks.
    - **Eligible:** Combwork's accounts (not a CLI's own home) whose CLI is on in Settings, not a test copy's CLI on its test home, and off in this workspace. For a project's agents, only their CLI's. With no agents, those of an installed CLI first.
    - **The banner** (`NoConnectionBanner`, `data-off-here`: `one`, `several` or `none`) shows in a project whose agents' CLI has none on, in the Assistant panel, and on **the empty project's card** (no agents, no connection usable here, not a test copy on a CLI test home: `where="empty"`).
      - Exactly one eligible: *{name}, your {cli} account, is off in this workspace, so … can't start*, with **Turn On Here**. That is `connections:setOn` for this window's workspace only; another workspace's choice and the order are untouched.
      - Several: they are named, with **Choose in Settings** (Accounts & Connections).
      - None at all: as before, with **Add an Account**.
    - **The other texts:**
      - An agent's refused start (`main.connections.launch.offHere`, the Agent API's too) says the CLI's accounts are off here and to turn one on with On here.
      - The choice of connection's line (`connections.choice.offHereAll`, also Add Agent's Start-a-session-now reason) names those off here.
      - Provider Setup's line (`shell.setup.connectionsOff`) does too.
  - **Assistant Settings** (the dialog, per workspace): **Connection** and **Mode** only. Its picker greys out connections whose permission mode is *The CLI's own setting*, saying why (Control relies on knowing the mode); its launch never runs in it anyway (`effective()`: the CLI's `assistantMode` instead). Another connection restarts a running Assistant after asking: the same CLI resumes its conversation, another CLI starts a new one. A workspace's Assistant with no connection yet runs on the first usable account's CLI (decision A), not Settings' old provider. **Settings → Assistant** keeps the default mode, Control, Change settings, the typing pause, tell replies, panel side, Highlight Compact over and the journal: its provider, connection and per-provider values are gone from the window and the settings catalogue (`settings.assistant.provider` and `.providers` stay read-only, the migration's input), with `connections:setAssistant`, `pointAssistant`, `followAssistantSettings` and the Assistant's half of `checkLaunchSettings` (Copilot's went with HI-2107).
  - **Decision H, said:** an agent whose connection is removed or on an account off here launches on its CLI's first usable connection (`resolveAgentConnection`), its launch noted `offFallback` (off here) or `missing` (removed, or another CLI's); its pane's footer marks its connection ⚠ with why on hover, its row's mark says it, and a notice at the launch names the connection it started on (*HB4 runs on another connection*).
  - **The Agent API** (api.version 12; AGENT_API.md "Connections"): `cw_add_agent` / `POST …/agents` and `cw_update_agent` / `PATCH …/agents/{agent}` take `connection` (id, or a name unique among those usable in the workspace; default: the first usable, or on update `null`/`""` its CLI's first usable), `name`, `workflowRole` and `mcpServers`. **`provider`, `model`, `effort`, `mode` and `context200k` are refused** (decision D: removed, not aliased; `400`, naming the connections on the account concerned: the agent's, or the one a new agent would go on); the combwork server passes them on when a caller still sends them, so they fail loudly once. Agent rows' `connection` is `{ id, name, problem? }` (`problem` `missing` or `off`); `launchedConnection` names the account its run is on. `GET /v1/connections` lists `connections` (id, name, account, CLI, values; `usable: false` for the Assistant and the user's token on one whose account is off here; extra arguments to them only) and `accounts` (as before); `GET /v1/providers` lists each CLI's usable connections and has no `isDefault`.
  - **Starting a card on a new agent** (HI-2121, decisions A and D): the board's **Start…** and **Move to Active → Assign and start** ask a new agent's **Connection** with the same picker, the first usable preselected and Start held while that is still being found (as Add Agent); `TaskStartTarget`'s `connection` (its id) replaces `provider`. `cw_start_task` / `POST /v1/tasks/{n}/start` takes `connection` for a new agent (as `cw_add_agent`: id or name, default the first usable; with `agent`, `400`) and refuses `provider`, `model`, `effort`, `mode` and `context200k` the same way. **The Skills tab's provider** starts on the CLI of the first usable connection (the one a new agent gets) when none was picked for the project. None of these reads a default provider.
  - **`cw_connection`** (`list`, `add`, `update`; `POST /v1/connections`, `PATCH /v1/connections/{ref}`): the Assistant's, offered to every Assistant (`ASSISTANT_CONNECTION_TOOLS`: listing is a read); `add` (on an account that exists, by id or name) and `update` need Settings → Assistant → Control → Change settings, checked before and again at the change, through `assistantChange()` (actions `add-connection` and `update-connection`, with the connection's id; undo can't take them back: `UNDO_FINAL.connectionMade`, `connectionChanged`). They save through HI-2107's `addConnection`/`updateConnection` (decision E, a mode the CLI has, a server's connections without effort or context). Accounts (sign-ins, servers, keys) stay the user's alone.
  - **Undo** of an agent's settings records `connection` (with its CLI as before): `AGENT_FIELDS` is name, provider, connection, MCP servers and workflow role; a change of CLI puts back its connection and last session with it. A change recorded before (model, effort, mode, context) still goes back through the adapter (the connection on its account with them).
- **Settings → Accounts & Connections** (HI-2107; HI-2105's wireframe), replacing Settings → Connections (`AccountsSettings.tsx`; Settings' section id stays `accounts`):
  - **Accounts** in the one order (`ConnectionsView.order`: every account, the CLI's own homes too; `connections:move` moves one in it, `movedInGroup`): Combwork's of the CLIs turned on, and Copilot's sign-in while Copilot is on. Each is a **card with the same fields in the same place** (HI-2528, Darren's approved mockup v2, 4 Nov ~22:00): its drag handle (Alt+Up and Alt+Down), CLI icon, name and CLI, **Off here** when it's off in this workspace; then **Signed in as** (its email), **Plan** (as the CLI names it, title-cased, never mapped: "max" → "Max") and **State** (signed in, set up, and **Sign-in expires {date}** from the CLI's `loginExpiresAt`, Claude Code's `auth status`, advanced field `claude-code.accounts.loginExpiresField`, sample 2.1.318; kept on `ConnectionObserved.loginExpiresAt`); then a **bar per plan limit** not reset yet (`connectionPlanUsage`; amber from 80%, red from 95%) with its share and "resets at 23:00" today or "resets Thu 09:00" within the week, else a date, as plan notices word it (`accountCard.ts`), or "Usage: not reported yet"; a server's card shows its address and key instead. On the right **On here**, Set Up, Sign In or Keep the New Login when it needs them, and **⋯** (**Account Settings…**, the usage move's dialog since Darren's 21:40 decision moved it off the card; Rename, Sign In again, Set Up, Remove). **Copilot's** (decision C) shows who Copilot is signed in as (Provider Setup's reading) and its **⋯** only opens Provider Setup; it has no On here, Rename or Remove.
  - **Connections** inside their account's card, as a small table (HI-2528; Darren 21:40: "keep connections where they are but break up the space a bit with a table"; `ConnectionsView.connectionRows`, in their account's order then their own): ↑/↓ (`connection:move` within the account), **Connection** (**First** on the base when there are others), **Tag** (HI-2530), **Model**, **Effort**, **Context**, **Mode**, **Extra args** (`connectionCells`: "CLI's own" for a value left to the CLI, "none" for no arguments, "—" where it doesn't apply: a server's effort and context, a CLI without a context limit), **Used by**, then Edit, Remove and ⋯. Below 660 px of card (a container query) each row takes two lines, its values summed up on the second (`connectionSummary`); the heading row is hidden then. Who uses it (`ConnectionRow.users`: the agents and Assistants of the open workspaces whose `project.json` names it, `connectionUsers`; a count, the names on hover), decision E's mark when its effort is one its model no longer takes (`effortUnusable`), and **⋯** (Edit, Duplicate, Remove). **Add Connection** under each account.
  - **The connection dialog** (`ConnectionDialog`, `ConnectionDefaults.tsx`; also Add Agent's new connection, HI-2108): Name, Model, Effort (the model's levels), Context (a CLI with a context limit), Permission mode (the CLI's, its no-guardrails ones only while enabled; one it has kept), Extra arguments; a server account's has no Effort or Context. It saves through `connection:add` and `connection:update` (`main/accounts.ts`): a name is needed and unique on its account, a mode must be the CLI's, a model and effort that don't go together are refused (decision E), extra arguments with a bare `--` are refused (#523, `extraArgsProblem`, as a launch would), a server's effort and context dropped; a refusal changes nothing. A saved change refreshes the open workspaces, so running agents on it show Restart, or **Switch Now** for a mode (`noticeModeSetting`).
  - **Duplicate** (`connection:duplicate`) adds "<name> (2)" after it; **Remove** (`connection:remove`) is refused while an agent or Assistant of an open workspace uses it, naming them. It reads each project's agents as saved, under the lock their writes take (`savedUsers`), never a window's snapshot; it marks the connection first, and while it is marked (or once it is gone) a write giving it to an agent is refused under that same lock (`mutateProjectConfig` asks `connectionAssignable`, set by `initConnections`), so an assignment either lands before its project is read or is refused (HR1, round 1). An agent of a workspace not open whose connection was removed falls back (decision H). `connection:move` orders connections within their account.
  - **Add Account…** is S1's Add a Connection (CLI, name, sign-in or server): the account comes with its base connection, named after it.
- **Settings → Providers keeps only the CLI** (decision F): its list (on or off, installed, in Combwork's order: `settings:moveProvider` and the order's revision went with HI-2113, and every reader of `providerOrder` but the migration's with HI-2139), and each CLI's page: on or off, installation and path, update checks, Allow background sessions, the no-guardrails opt-in (which modes a connection may choose), the fallback lists, cost source and prices. Its installation's **Check now** re-checks that CLI alone (HI-2550: install, version, problems, the latest version; `provider:refresh` with its id), leaving the others' results as they are and showing *Checking…* on that page only, as Provider Setup's **Check again** and an install's end already re-check their own provider alone; start-up and Help → Check Coding Agents for Updates check them all. Gone: Default provider, and the CLI's default model, effort, mode, extra arguments and 200K context (`settingsCatalog.ts`; still in `AppSettings` as migration input). The Copilot half of the adapter (`followCopilotSettings`) went with them.
- **Project Settings** loses its Claude Code, Codex and Copilot pages and Default provider (decision A); it keeps the key, sessions, chime, MCP, skills, workflow and shortcuts. Its Reset no longer writes `defaultProvider` or `providers`.
- **The status bar's plan usage** is one item per account a session of the window's workspace runs on, by its name now, all in the one order of accounts across every CLI (HI-2119, `planUsageItems`), then the CLI-wide item of each CLI whose accounts don't apply here.

**Server connections** (S6, HI-1772; Darren, 27 Oct ~08:55; the design is the card's s10, s17 and s21, OK'd by HR3):
- **What it is:** a connection whose model comes from a server: a name, its CLI (one whose descriptor has `capabilities.connections.server`: Claude Code), a base URL, a key or none, and its models, each with the Claude names it stands in for (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku: each name on one model at most, a model on several). Add Connection asks for the name, then **Gets its model from: its sign-in / a server**; a preset fills the rest (DeepSeek, per its Claude Code guide; Ollama on this PC, per its Claude Code guide, checked with Ollama 0.33.1 for HI-1773, its recommended context length of 64,000 tokens or more shown under the preset as advice, never enforced, since Combwork passes no context and doesn't change Ollama's settings), all of it editable. It has its own folder like a sign-in connection (`<profile>\accounts\<id>`, the `projects\` junction), with nothing to sign in, check or watch.
- **The base URL:** `https:`, or `http:` only to this PC (`localhost`, 127.0.0.0/8 as the URL parser writes it, `[::1]`; `localhost.example.com` and the like aren't). No user name, password, query or fragment, so a key can't be kept in it. Changing it to another origin removes the key in the same locked step ("its key was removed"); a path on the same server keeps it.
- **The key** (`keyStore.ts`):
  - **Stored** encrypted with Electron's `safeStorage` (DPAPI) in `<profile>connection-keys.json`, the only record of a key: `{ v, origin, last4, at, blob }` per connection, bound to its base URL's origin; `v` is the save's own random id, never reused (a key removed and saved again, or saved after the store was emptied, is a new one). `config.json` names no key, so restoring config from its `.bak` can't bring one back. Refused, nothing written, where safeStorage can't encrypt (never plain text).
  - **Written** once per change (Save, Replace, Remove Key, removing the connection), atomically, with no `.bak`, under one lock for the whole file (`serial`); lock order: the connection's own lock, then the store's, then config. Damaged: read as empty (keys entered again). At start, keys of connections no longer there (or no longer server connections) are dropped, the keep-list read under the lock.
  - **Removing the connection** deletes its key first: if that fails, nothing is removed, the row still shows its key, and Remove tries again.
  - **Entered** in a password box in Add Connection or Add/Replace Key, sent once over its own IPC (`connections:setKey`, `connections:addServer`), whose reply has its last 4 characters only; refused (by kind, never echoing it) when it isn't 16–512 printable ASCII characters without spaces, or appears in the connection's name, base URL or a model id. Never sent back to a window: the row says "Key …a1f3", with Replace Key… and Remove Key. IPC logging and tracing carry channel names only.
  - **Decrypted** only for a launch's environment, a Set Up terminal's, a model listing's request (`withKey`, checked against the current origin), or Reset Masking Data (the user confirmed it). Never for masking, an export or at start-up.
  - **Masked by fingerprints** (`keyMatcher.ts`, `keyCoverage.ts`): when a key is saved (the one moment Combwork has it), its fingerprint is kept, before the key itself: a keyed hash (HMAC, truncated, with a secret salt) of every run of 8 characters of it, as it is, JSON-escaped once and twice and URL-encoded, behind a rolling prefilter with a secret base. All of it, salt included, is one safeStorage-encrypted blob in `<profile>key-fingerprints.json`, read at start-up (matching data, not a credential), and kept after Replace, Remove Key and the connection's removal, so a key printed in any session, old or new, is masked for good. Any 8 characters or more of a key are masked wherever they are, whole or cut anywhere. `maskSecrets` (the developer console, recordings and flight captures, Copy Diagnostics, transcript views), `combwork.log`'s line (`logLine`: its message and data, after serialising) and the exports (a transcript's Markdown, Export Board, a template, the Performance report: JSON by value, `maskDeep`) use it.
  - **Never pruned:** at most 100,000 windows in all (about 500 typical keys); past that a further Save is refused ("can't keep masking for another key").
  - **Evidence and states:** `key-coverage.json` and config.json's `keyMasking` (their union; a backup never lowers them) say `ever` (a key was saved, written before its first fingerprint) and `gap`. **None:** no evidence, no key store entry and no fingerprint file (a profile that never saved a key; keyless servers don't count): nothing masked, safeStorage not needed. **Ready:** fingerprints read. **Unavailable:** evidence or keys but the fingerprints missing, damaged or not decryptable: strict masking (every run of 8 or more characters without whitespace, in every sink above), and exports, Copy Diagnostics, console recordings and flight captures refused before anything is written, and a new key refused, until **Reset Masking Data…** (Settings → Connections). Electron's main process is strict from its start until its state is known.
  - **Reset Masking Data** (confirmed): fingerprints made again from the keys that can still be read, and a sticky `gap`: strict masking for **all** later output, for good, since a lost key's fingerprint can't be told any more (the dialog says so; nothing in the app clears it).
  - What the user's own commands print, and the CLI's own transcript files, are outside Combwork (the key box says the agent's commands can read it).
- **The launch** (`connectionForLaunch`, `serverEnv`): the descriptor's variables, set after those left out (`claude-code.accounts.dropEnv`, a pattern: every `ANTHROPIC_*` (keys, tokens, `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, base URLs, models), the provider switches and their auth skips, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_*`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `CLOUD_ML_REGION`; Claude Code probes showed it reads them as a login, sends custom headers to its server, or routes by them), for a launch and Set Up alike: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, the key as `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (a bearer token; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` would ask to be approved in the pane), each alias's model, `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` (Haiku's) and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` (Opus's, else Sonnet's, else the first). No key: refused ("has no key") unless the server is on this PC, which gets the descriptor's placeholder `none` (not secret; with no variable at all, Claude Code shows its login screen). The last look before the spawn also checks the connection is still a server connection on the same origin with the same key version. No effort or context is passed.
- **First run:** a folder that never ran Claude Code shows its own first-run screens (its look, its notes, the folder's trust), answered by the user, in the agent's pane or once in **Set Up** (a terminal of Combwork's running the CLI on the connection, with its server's variables). Combwork types nothing into it and writes none of the CLI's files.
- **A refused key:** after its own retries (10, about 3 minutes, recorded), Claude Code's StopFailure says `authentication_failed`, the same as a refused sign-in, so the agent stops as signed out; on a server connection its status says **Key refused**, and its hover "Replace it in Settings → Connections, then Resume".
- **Models:** typed, or read from the server when the user asks (Read Models, or after Add), never at a launch: one request from main, to the preset's listing (DeepSeek's `/models`, Ollama's `/api/tags`, else `<base>/v1/models`), the key as a bearer token (none for a keyless one), redirects refused, 10 s, 1 MB, at most 500 ids. A newer reading, a closed dialog, or any change of its base URL (its path too), preset or key meanwhile makes the reply stale (dropped), whatever it said; an edit or a key change also ends a reading under way. Failures by kind only (key refused, access refused, unreachable, server error, not a list, a redirect, too large), never the server's text. Read again, a model's names are kept while it is still listed; those no longer listed are dropped and said.
- **Shown:** the pickers list its models (`connectionModels`: "deepseek-flash (as Opus, Sonnet)", no effort), its default the one Opus runs; the pane footer shows the server's model and the names it stands in for (`serverModelOf`, a reported Claude name mapped back); the CLI's own cost reports (which price the server's model as a Claude model) are never counted for a session that ran on one (`SessionRecord.serverRan`, kept once set; `withoutCostReports` in the usage worker's reads and the history's ingest; the history's own `reports_ignored`, set once and never cleared whatever a later job says, a change re-reading the session and stripping its stored rows and baseline; main's and the worker's cached reads valid only for the policy they were read with; while it runs, its live run's own markers, each conversation it moved through, which go with the run, and after, its record (HI-1829): one whose `serverRan` write failed, and failed again at the exit, is kept in memory and retried after its host's next record write, dropped when it is deleted, never evicted to Claude pricing. At most 32 are kept: past that its host is read without cost reports for the rest of Combwork's run, as are the hosts of a workspace closing with one kept, and past 16 such hosts every read is, until Combwork restarts, each said once in `combwork.log`): its live cost, Performance, the history and card costs are Combwork's estimate by the real model id, unpriced unless the user priced it. The Agent API shows `kind: "server"` and, to the workspace token and the Assistant, its host, never its key or whether it has one.
- **Diagnostics** (HI-2683, design s7 and s11 OK'd by HR3; `main/serverDiagnostics.ts`, judgements in `shared/serverDiagnostics.ts`, the dialog `components/ServerDiagnostics.tsx`). **Check Server…**, on a server connection in Settings, beside its line in the connection editor, and on Provider Setup for one on this PC, opens **Server diagnostics** for one of its models. Read-only, asked for by the user, never at a launch, never changing the server.
  - **Context** comes from the server's own root paths, never from a base URL with a path (a gateway): there it is "not reported", and nothing is asked.
    - **llama.cpp:** `/props` (`default_generation_settings.n_ctx`, allocated) and `/v1/models` (`meta.n_ctx_train`, trained).
    - **Ollama:** `/api/ps` (`context_length` while loaded, else "not loaded") and `POST /api/show` (`model_info.<arch>.context_length`, trained; a Modelfile's `num_ctx`, configured). It says that `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` isn't readable over its API.
    - Which server it is comes from what answers (the Ollama preset asks Ollama first), never from its name. Each value has its source and when it was read; one not sent is "not reported", never 0.
  - **The user's own context**, `ServerModel.context` (tokens), is set only by the user (shared with HI-2682, which launches with it). It is kept through a model listing, and never written from a server's figures.
  - **The advice** (a preset's `contextAdvice`: Ollama's 64K) is compared with the allocated value, else the configured one, else the user's. Beside it, a measurement from HI-2552 as a fact, not a rule: Claude Code's first request with Combwork's tools was about 14K–28K tokens on the test server.
  - **llama.cpp's template:** `chat_template_caps` (`supports_tools` and `supports_tool_calls`) is read as supported, unsupported, not reported or inconsistent. `--jinja` is only ever offered as a possible remedy, never asserted, since the flag's state isn't observable.
  - **The tool-call test** goes through the Messages API Claude Code calls, `<base URL>/v1/messages` with the base path kept, the key as a bearer token, thinking off and 1,024 output tokens.
    - **Step 1** offers one tool (`get_weather`) and asks for Reykjavik's weather. It passes only on exactly one call of that tool, its arguments valid and naming that city.
