Ticked, the load removes them with their branches only once it is published (a refused load removes nothing), and only a removed agent's worktree, listed in the dialog, that no agent works in by then, checked again at that moment (`worktreeCheck`: still merged into the main branch the user was shown, and clean; a main branch that moved on while the dialog was open doesn't keep a worktree that is still merged) and removed through `removeCheckedWorktree` with that branch: if either branch moved after that check, or the worktree has files written since it, it is kept. Each is reserved before it is checked (`reserveForRemoval` in `projectAgents.ts`, which records when each removal started and ended on one counter), and whether an agent works in it is read under the project file's lock after that. Whatever gives an agent a worktree (adding an agent, a load) takes a mark (`claimMark`) before it looks at the project's worktrees and, under the same lock, refuses one whose removal went on at any time since (`removedSince`) or whose folder is gone. So an agent given it first keeps it, and one that saw it before or while it was removed is refused ("That worktree is being removed, or was just removed"), however long it took: no agent is ever left in a removed worktree. A notice says what went with its branch, what went while its branch stayed (a ref moved in the last step: `branchKept`, #313), and what was kept, why (`oldWorktreesNotice` in `templateLoad.ts`); it is refused while an agent runs or is starting, a removed worktree agent has uncommitted work (or git can't say whether it has: then it isn't known to be safe), a provider the template needs is off or not installed (Provider Setup or Settings offered), or the template has worktree agents and the project isn't on a git branch (#702 found this was why templates were unavailable in a project without git; the reason now names the agents and the case: git can't run, the folder isn't a repository, or no branch to start from (detached, or no commit yet), with the way out: make it a repository with a first commit, or edit the template to put them in the project folder; a template of project-folder agents loads anywhere); and if the agents changed since they were shown (the confirmation carries their ids). One load per project at a time, and **all or nothing**: the project's agents can't start for the whole load (a fence on its starts, `sessions.fenceStarts`, lifted however it ends); the new agents and their worktrees are staged first without touching `project.json`, then published in one write under the project file's lock, only if the agents are still those shown and none runs or is starting. If an agent can't be created, or the agents changed meanwhile (one added by the Assistant, say), the staged worktrees go and the project stays as it is now: nothing half loaded is ever seen, and no change made meanwhile is lost. Removed agents keep their worktrees and branches (to merge or reuse), their conversations stay in Sessions, and their open cards go back as Remove Agent's **Move them back** does. Since 1.0 (HI-1502, §16.10.6), the Assistant lists, plans and loads templates through the Agent API (`cw_template`); project agents have no template tools. **Templates view and tab (#127):** the **Templates** view (activity bar, next to Skills; `components/Templates.tsx`) lists the workspace's templates, then each project's under its name, with a filter (All, Workspace, a project; kept while Combwork runs); a project's **Templates** tab (after Skills) lists its own and the workspace's, each with its scope. Selecting one shows its description (optional, #271, at most 500 characters; one that isn't text or is too long is left out when read), its agents (name, role, coding agent, model and 200K context, effort, mode, worktree or the project folder) and layout. Actions: **Edit…** (#271: in its place, `TemplateEditor` in `Templates.tsx`: its name, description and layout (automatic or a chosen one); its agents added (**Add Agent…**), copied, moved up or down (their order is a project's: pages hold them in turn) and removed, at most 12; each edited in the **Agent Settings dialog** itself (`AgentSettingsModal` in `AgentDialogs.tsx`, shared with a project's agents, in its template mode, `TemplateAgentDialog`: a choice of its own worktree or the project folder in place of the worktree's details, no running session, role suggestions from the template's agents, names unique within the template; an empty choice stays empty, following the project it is loaded into, shown with the tab's project's or Combwork's defaults); an agent whose coding agent this Combwork doesn't know can be moved or removed, not edited. **Save Template** sends the draft to `templates:update` (`updateTemplate`), which reads it as untrusted (`readTemplate`, as an import) and writes it in its file under the place's lock (`changing`), refused if another template there has its name or the template's `savedAt` isn't the one the editor opened (a save meanwhile, from a project or another window, is never overwritten). The editor keeps the template as it opened it, whatever the list shows later: the draft is compared with that, and that revision is the one a save expects; when the list shows a newer one, the editor says the template was saved again and offers **Discard and Reload**, keeping the draft until then; its place stays (Duplicate… moves it). Cancel asks before throwing changes away. **An agent's Save saves the template** (#510: Save means save): when the agent's dialog saves, the editor saves the whole draft at once (its other changes too), unless the draft can't be saved yet (no name, or the template was saved again meanwhile: then it stays in the draft, as before), and stays open, comparing with what it saved; the list showing the revision it replaced until it reads it again isn't a save meanwhile. The draft is kept in the window (`templateEdits` in the store, by workspace and template) until it is saved or discarded: leaving the editor another way (another template, another view, the project's tab) keeps it, the list marks that template **Not saved** and the editor says **Changes not saved**, and the template opens in the editor again with them; an editor left with nothing changed keeps nothing. A draft with changes is one of the window's unsaved edits too (`editorDrafts`, listed by its file, `.combwork/templates/<file>`): quitting, closing the window or the workspace, switching workspace and Reload Window ask about it as they do for files, even with quit confirmation off; Save there saves it as Save Template does (refused, as that is, when the template changed meanwhile: then Combwork stays open with the draft), and Discard drops it. While a save runs (Save Template's or an agent's), every field and button of the editor is disabled, so no change is made that the save didn't take, and no agent's Save is accepted that isn't saved; Save Template closes the editor only when nothing changed since it began. The editor's Cancel reads Close when nothing is changed. A template's agents table (in the editor and a project's Templates tab) keeps each agent's name, role and coding agent on one line and wraps its settings between words, so it fits its pane rather than scroll (#890); in a pane under 560 px the cells are tighter and the coding agent wraps too, and under 380 px the editor puts its fields' labels above their boxes. A language whose words are longer still than the pane can hold scrolls the table in its own box. A project's Templates tab lays its list and the template out as the Changes tab does (#906): the list gives way first (down to 200 px, leaving the template at least 320 when it can), and in a tab under 400 px it sits above the template, so the template has the tab's width. Projects loaded from it earlier are never touched);  **Load into Project…** (the view asks which; the tab loads into its project; a project's template can load into any project, `from`), **Rename…** (in its place; a name taken there is refused), **Duplicate…** (into the workspace or any project, " (2)" for a taken name), **Delete** (file and `.bak` to the Recycle Bin), **Export…** (a save dialog, `<name>.combwork-template.json`; the file is `exportable()`: version, name, savedAt, layout and agents only, so no paths, ids, sessions or names of people) and **Import…** (an open dialog; the file, at most 256 KB, is read as untrusted and refused with `readTemplate`'s reason before anything is asked or written; then where to keep it, the workspace or a project; a name already there asks **Replace** or **Keep Both**, " (2)"; one write, so nothing is half imported). Every change to a place's templates (save, import, duplicate, rename, delete) runs locked against the others for that folder (`changing()`), from any project or window, with its clash check and the choice of name and file inside: two at once never take the same file or replace each other unasked. The dialog for a place is a choice with a drop-down (`ChoiceRequest.select`). The lists refresh when this window changes a template (`templatesVersion`). Agent Settings has **Role** (free text, suggesting builder, reviewer and the project's roles), shown in the agent's tab tooltip.
- **Agents** (Session tab): the **session toolbar** above the panes (#975, which replaced the agent strip: below); a project without agents shows "No agents yet" with Add Agent, New Session (adds one and starts it) and All Sessions (its single empty pane draws nothing over it), and — once there is more than one agent — the layout: **one at a time** (the summary chip's list switches agents), **two columns**, **three columns**, a **2×2 grid** or a **3×2 grid**. **Pages** (#134): up to twelve agents (24 with Agents per project, #562), and **one layout for the project**: automatic (the one that shows its agents, up to the 3×2 grid) until one is chosen, which then stays as agents are added; choosing the one that shows the agents makes it automatic again. A page holds as many agents as the layout has panes, so every agent on a page has a pane: **pages = agents ÷ panes** (6 agents in a grid of four: 4 + 2; 4 in three columns: 3 + 1; 12 in the grid of six: 6 + 6), the last page's spare panes empty (Add Agent). One at a time (Single) is one page of every agent, the summary chip's list choosing who is shown, so it has no page buttons. The toolbar's right-hand group is, left to right, the page buttons and the layouts (#292: the pages beside the layouts they follow from; Panes only), then + Add ▾. With more than one page, numbered buttons in the toolbar switch pages (Ctrl+Alt+PageDown / PageUp), each with a dot for that page's most urgent agent and its agents in the tooltip; more than six pages (more than 12 agents in two columns, #562) show a compact pager instead, **‹ 3 / 12 ▾ ›**: ‹ and › go to the previous and next page (round from the last to the first; each a page button, with that page's dot, its tooltip and its drop target, held over while dragging to step through the pages), and the middle opens a menu of every page with its agents' names, a dot on it when another page has an urgent agent. **Panes too narrow for a terminal** (#1037): a layout whose columns would each be narrower than a terminal can be fitted to (`terminalMinWidth()`: `MIN_COLS` and two over in the terminal font, with its padding and scroll bar) is shown with fewer (`layoutFitting`: three columns → two → one at a time, the 3×2 grid → the 2×2 grid → one at a time), the Session tab's width measured as it changes (`paneColumns` in the window's store: the window, the sidebar, the Progress panel, the Assistant's panel); its pages are the shown layout's (`shownLayout`, `shownPerPage`: panes, pages, page keys and what is on screen), and the layout chosen is never changed or saved by it: its button stays the one chosen, with a tooltip naming the layout shown. Once there is room, the chosen layout is shown again, a little past the point (`paneColumnsFor`: 24 px, `FIT_MARGIN`), so a pixel either way at it doesn't flip the layout. The focus view (#976) keeps its pane a terminal wide, the terminal first (#1050): its strip shows narrower than its chosen width (#1021, kept and shown again with room), at most 40% of the Session tab (`TILE_STRIP_SHARE`) and at most half the room above both least widths past 24 px, so it is at its least (170 px) while the terminal still has 24 px over its own, whatever the terminal font (a 24 px font makes a terminal's least 342 px), then is hidden (`tileStripRoom`, with the same margin; Esc, Ctrl+Alt+Esc and the Tiles toggle still go back). Short of room, the toolbar's controls fold (`useFolds`, measured as the project header's are; `TOOLBAR_FOLDS`): first the layout buttons become one button showing the current layout, whose menu lists them all; then the page buttons become the compact pager (‹ 3 / 6 ▾ ›) even with six pages or fewer; then the pager is only its menu (3 / 6) and the summary chip, the layouts, the pages and + Add drop their ▾; then + Add is only its + (#1046: its name on hover and for screen readers); then Panes | Tiles are their icons (a terminal, a grid; their names in tooltips and accessible names); the summary chip's counts are cut with … only after that, down to its mark (its tooltip's wrapper may narrow), so nothing of the toolbar is cut at the narrowest window with the sidebar and the Progress panel open (about 265 px). Widened, it unfolds again. Changing the layout re-pages at once. A page's panes show its agents in their order; choosing an agent on another page in the summary chip's list goes to that page. Going to a page focuses the agent last focused there. Stored per project as `layout` (§4); the per-page `layouts` of earlier versions are read as page 1's (else automatic). Every agent pane, with one agent or several, has a **header** (#977, quiet: the state mark, the name (its provider in the name's tooltip), the status, the card; then **Stop** (red) while it runs, or **Resume** (amber; **New Session**, green, when there is nothing to resume) when it doesn't, and **⋯**; details below) and a **footer** (#978: one quiet line, `·` between its items; since #1013, Darren's call reviewing 0.9.0-beta.1, model · effort · mode on the left and the transcript's size · ctx · cost right-aligned, balancing the header, after a flexible space (`.grow`); warnings only when they matter, just left of the right side; the same `PaneFooter` in agent panes, the focus view and the Assistant's panel). Its items: model · effort (click: Agent Settings), the permission mode badge (click: switch), the transcript's size (`foot-size`, "2.4 MB", its hover the transcript tip; not shown before the session reports it), the context as "ctx 42%" of the context window ("ctx 84k", its tokens, while the window isn't known; "ctx –" before it is read; its hover has the tokens with the last turn's breakdown, where the CLI compacts, the compactions, the transcript's size (also there for a narrow pane, where the line's size has gone) and the click line; a click opens the Overview at its compaction history), and the session's cost ("≈$3.70"; "$?" unpriced); a click on the cost opens the Overview on that agent's session, scrolled to its details, as an anchor: `showInOverview(path, agentId, 'session')`; its tooltip ends, after an empty line, with "Click to see this session's details in the Overview" (#122; not on the Assistant's footer, whose clicks open nothing). **Warnings, in the warning colour, only when they matter:** the context gets a ⚠ past the Compact threshold (`compactThreshold()`); the transcript's size becomes a warning in its place (`foot-transcript`, "⚠ 34 MB", its hover the transcript tip, a click Hand Over to… while the agent may hand over now, #1057) past *Warn when a transcript is over*; "⚠ n background tasks" while `backgroundTasks` > 0, the first item of the right side. What the footer had before #978 and where it went: the session's icon → the agent's ⋯ (Open in Sessions Tab with the session's name and start as its detail, Rename Session…); the transcript's size → the context's hover, and the line only as a warning (back in the line, on the right, since #1013); the context's tokens → its hover (the line shows the percentage). Short of room (`useFooterFit` in `AgentPanes.tsx`: worked out from what every item takes in full, and back to more text only with 2 px to spare, so a footer on the edge never flips), first the transcript's size while it isn't a warning goes, with its dot (`data-give` 1: the context's hover has it), then the warnings give up their text for their icon in turn (`data-give` 2, 3): the background tasks', then the transcript's; their tooltips keep the figures. The right side never overlaps the left: the space between them goes first. Then the permission mode's label shortens with an ellipsis (its icon and caret always show), then the model's, and only then is the line cut off at the right; the context never shortens before that (`tests/e2e/footerfit.cjs`). **The pane header** (#977; 0.9.0's calmer session page, #971: the user rarely touches a terminal beyond typing, so only Stop stays visible) is 26 px: the state mark, the name (bold; its tooltip what the agent strip's tab said, #975: "<name> (<provider>): <state>", the sign-in note, the safeguard, its role, its MCP servers when it chose them, the cards it works on and reviews, its session or what Resume opens, its worktree and branch, what is left to merge), the status (the same texts as before: a question, a watch with its eye, Silent · state unknown with **Mark idle** beside it, which stays since the agent is stuck until someone looks), the review and safeguard shields (which give way with the status; Mark idle from 300 px of header, `MARKS_FROM`; narrower, Mark idle is only in ⋯, which then also has the safeguard's note, and ⋯'s dot shows), the card chip, then Stop's place (Stop / Resume / New Session, quiet icon buttons in their action colours) and **⋯**. **⋯** (also a right-click on the header, and **Agent Menu…**, `agent.menu`, in the Session menu and the palette, which opens the focused agent's under its ⋯ on its first entry: `requestStripMenu(project, 'agentMenu', agent)`) has, first, what needs a look: processes its launches left running (#507: how many, the first three; its menu lists them with End and Keep Running), messages not received or not acked in time (#530, #647: how many; its menu lists each and cancels the waiting ones), the files it is editing this turn (its menu lists them) and Mark idle; then the agent's menu (`agentMenu()`): Stop or Resume, Resume a Session…, New Session, Compact…, Archive and Start New…, Cancel Card Watch, Hand Over to…, Move Left/Right, Agent Settings…, for a worktree **Review Changes** (its branch as the detail) and **Merge…** (what is left to merge as the detail, or why it is disabled), Remove Agent… and Discard. A dot on ⋯ says something in it needs a look: amber for left-running processes or overdue messages, the accent for unread ones; its tooltip and accessible description list them. What the header showed before #977 and where it went: the provider icon → the name's tooltip; the worktree icon → the tab (#287; since #975 the name's tooltip) and Review Changes' detail; Compact → ⋯ (the footer's context turns amber past the threshold); Resume a Session…, New Session (with something to resume) and Merge… with its count → ⋯ (and the name's tooltip, #975); locks, left running and unread messages → ⋯ with its dot; the watch's Cancel → ⋯'s Cancel Card Watch. Short of room, the status gives way entirely first (its shrink far outweighs the name's), then where it works ("in slot-b", "0.9 worktree: hb1": #1568), then the name (all three with an ellipsis and the full text on hover); below 200 px the card goes; Stop's place and ⋯ never shrink (`tests/e2e/paneheader.cjs` measures 900 to 150 px at 100% and 125%). **A worktree's branch, folder, base and what is left to merge** are in the name's tooltip (#287; the agent strip's tab had them on its worktree icon until #975); agents in the project folder have none. While Remove or Remove All removes the agent, a spinner takes its state mark's place (#975: its tab had it). While a compaction runs, the status says so until it ends, fails or the agent stops, and Compact… is disabled in ⋯. The **project header** is the project's only: name and combined status; Active, Explorer, Terminal, **Resume All Agents** (while any stopped agent has a session to resume; resumes those one after another, never restarts a running agent, asks first only when some prompt caches have expired, and reports each agent that couldn't resume with the reason while the rest still resume; also in the project's right-click menu when it has several agents), **Stop All Agents** (while any runs; always confirms, listing each agent and its state) and ⋯ (Changes, Project Settings, Remove Project…; agents are added from the agent strip); below 860 px Explorer and Terminal show icons only. The rule for new controls: a button when it is used often, the ⋯ menu otherwise. A pane whose session has ended shows a bar with **Resume** (and its ▾) and **New Session**; with several panes it is short ("Session ended.", on one line), the two buttons wrap together under it when the pane is narrow, and in a bar under 180 px they are only their icons, their names in tooltips and for screen readers (#890). **Resume** is a split button in pane placeholders and the empty-session card (in the agent header it is Resume plus Resume a Session…): the main part resumes the agent's own session — its last one, else the latest it ran in its folder, skipping archived ones and any open in another agent (worked out in main as `AgentInfo.resume`) — and is disabled with an explanation when there is none; **▾** opens a picker of the 10 most recent sessions from the agent's folder with when each was last active, which agent last ran it and an expired-cache warning; sessions open in another agent are greyed and clicking one shows that agent. **The session** shows in the agent's footer as just its icon, right-aligned before the context, at every width and whatever its name: hover for its name, when it started and its ID (its accessible name is "Session: <name>"), click to read it in the Sessions tab, right-click to **Rename…** it (as the Sessions tab's Rename). The name is the **latest rename**, in Combwork or in the CLI (Claude Code's `/rename`, Codex's thread name): Combwork passes its name to the CLI at launch (`--name`), so it records the CLI's name each time the session is renamed in Combwork (`titleAtRename` in `sessions.json`), and once the CLI's name differs from that, the CLI's is the newer one. Resuming such a session makes the CLI's name Combwork's, so the launch passes it back rather than the old one. Without a rename the CLI's own title shows; Combwork's automatic name ("<project> · <agent> · <date>", which Claude Code keeps as its title) counts as no name, and then the time the session started shows ("2026-10-04 14:05", in the user's date and time format; names the user typed are never changed): its record's `createdAt`, which a new session's record takes from its launch's start (`LiveSessionState.sessionCreatedAt`), so the footer and the Sessions tab show the same minute, and a resumed session keeps its time rather than the resume's (#630; "Running since" in the tooltip is the launch's). The same name is used in the Sessions tab, the session pickers and the agent strip's tooltips (`sessionLabel()` in `shared/defaults.ts`). The Assistant's footer leaves the name out. The agent strip's tooltips say what each agent is running or what Resume would open. Clicking a pane or its terminal focuses that agent; keyboard shortcuts, the Session menu, Ctrl+V images and Insert into Session act on the focused agent. Clicking an agent that isn't on screen puts it in the focused pane, or goes to its page. Empty panes offer Add Agent. Ctrl+Alt+] / Ctrl+Alt+[ cycle agents (across pages). The sidebar keeps **one dot per project** (the most urgent agent's state: needs input, then working…), with a count when several agents run; the project header badge does the same, with each agent's status on hover. Notifications, the quit dialog and the tray name the agent when a project has several. There is no limit on running sessions across projects. Only visible terminals use WebGL, within a budget of 8 contexts per window (Chromium drops the oldest context beyond about 16, which could be a terminal on screen): hidden terminals keep theirs for 30 seconds so switching back is instant, or give it up at once when a visible terminal needs one; the rest draw with xterm's DOM renderer. A terminal giving WebGL up (hidden too long, or ended: each new session re-creates its agent's terminal) also loses its context at once (`WEBGL_lose_context`): disposing the renderer alone left it alive until garbage collection, so Start New (All) on many agents pushed the window past Chromium's limit and the oldest context, the Assistant's, was dropped (#293). A terminal whose context is lost anyway draws with the DOM and is fitted again, the DOM's cells being wider.
- **The session toolbar** (#975, 0.9.0's calmer session page, #971; `SessionToolbar` in `AgentPanes.tsx`, replacing the agent strip): what is about all of the project's agents, each agent's own controls being on its pane. Left to right: **Panes | Tiles** (a radio group; `SessionView`), the **summary chip**, then the page buttons (Panes: the panes' pages and the layouts; Tiles: the tile pages, `TilePager`), and **+ Add ▾**. **Panes | Tiles**: Panes is the panes and terminals as before; Tiles hides them (the terminals keep running; `TerminalLayer` shows none) for the Tiles view (`AgentTiles`, below). The view is remembered per project as `sessionView` in its `project.json` (`setSessionView`); a project that never chose takes **Settings → Sessions → Default session view** (`sessions.defaultView`, Panes by default; Darren's decision of 17 Oct: Panes stays the default, the setting lets users move to Tiles at their own pace, and a project's own choice wins once used; `projectSessionView()`). The palette's **Switch Between Panes and Tiles** (`session.toggleView`, no default shortcut: Ctrl+Alt+letters are AltGr's) switches the selected project's. **The summary chip** counts the agents in each state (#973's, with the board's: `projectAgentStates`), most urgent first, idle ones too, and an idle agent with no session running as stopped, the same count as the header's state line ("1 waiting · 2 working · 3 idle · 1 stopped", `projectStateSummary`, HI-1908), after the most urgent state's mark (grey, as a stopped agent's, when every agent is stopped: `allStopped`, the header's too); the chip's border takes the waiting colour while one waits. Its **▾** is a menu (`ContextMenu`: it takes the focus, its chosen entry is its `aria-activedescendant`, and it gives the focus back on closing; the chip says `aria-expanded`) of every agent, most urgent first and in the project's order within a state, each with its state's mark (`MenuEntry.state`), its name, and its state in words · its status · its card as the detail (a spinner and "Removing…" while it is being removed); choosing one focuses it and shows its page (`showAgent`). It replaces the strip's tabs as the way to go to an agent; the commands and shortcuts (Next/Previous Agent, Agent n, Next/Previous Page, Agent Menu…) are unchanged. **+ Add ▾**: **Configure Agent and Add…** (the Add Agent dialog), **Add Agent** (the quick add, with its shortcut), **Add Agent from Template ▸** and **Templates ▸** (Save Template…, then the templates to load); no builder–reviewer pair entry, as Combwork has no such flow. Its entries are greyed out at the agent limit. Where each of the strip's other functions went (#975's audit, on the card): double-click → ⋯ Agent Settings…; right-click → the pane header's right-click and ⋯; drag → a pane's header and the page buttons; dot and removing spinner → the pane header's state mark; provider icon, worktree mark, role, cards, session and what is left to merge → the name's tooltip; locks and the unmerged count → ⋯; the "second agent" tip → the toolbar.
- **The Tiles view** (#976, 0.9.0's headline, #971; `AgentTiles.tsx`, `shared/tiles.ts`): a tile per agent in a responsive grid (columns of at least 230 px), **as many to a page as fit the Tiles area** (HI-1951, Darren's call: "only when it fills up the space"; #976's 12 a page, at least 12 agents on one page, before it): the grid's columns times the whole rows its height holds at the tile's one height (`tilesThatFit`), measured by a ResizeObserver on the area and the grid (no polling) and kept per project in the window's store (`tilesFit`, `tilesPageSize`), never fewer than 6 (`TILES_PER_PAGE_MIN`, Darren's decision: as Panes' largest page, the 3×2 grid; a window too small for 6 shows them in fewer columns, down to one, and scrolls), 12 (`TILES_PER_PAGE`) only until it is measured. All agents on one page when they fit, so no pager; pages only when they don't (a small window). A resize that changes it shows the page of the tile the keyboard is on, else of the first one shown (`setTilesFit`). The helpers take the page size (`tilePageCount`, `tilesOnPage`, `tilePageOf`, `tilePageShown`, `urgentByPage`). A tile is a button showing what Combwork already has, no CLI call and no terminal drawn for it: the state's mark (#973), the name and the provider; the status line (as the summary chip's list words it: the session's status, why a launch failed, or Not running); the card it works on, else the one it reviews; its progress run (Combwork's progress reports: the newest still running or stale, its title, status line and a bar); **two lines** of the start of its latest reply (`LiveSessionState.replyStart`, set at its turn's end from the CLI's last message: `replyStart()` takes Markdown's heading, bold and code marks out, runs whitespace together and cuts it at 300 characters); and badges for background tasks and the footer's warnings (its context past the Compact threshold, a transcript past its flagged size). **One fixed height** (#1145, Darren's request: tiles resizing as runs started and ended was jarring and made them hard to read): every row keeps its place whether or not it shows (status, card, progress line and bar, two lines of the reply, one line of badges: the warnings first, each giving way with an ellipsis, the background tasks' first, down to its icon, and all of them in full on hover), so every tile is the larger size and a page never reflows when one tile's content changes; a row's text cut short (an ellipsis, the reply's second line) is in full on hover (`useClipped(lines)`), the row's own width holding the line whether or not its tooltip's wrapper is there (one that changed it made the measuring loop, React #185: round 1 of #1145). Waiting for you stands out most (the border in the waiting colour, doubled, and the diamond); stalled has its colour's border. **Tile order** is **Settings → Sessions → Tile order** (`sessions.tileOrder`; Darren's decision): **Same as panes** (the default: the panes' order, so lanes stay lined up and reordering one reorders the other; urgent tiles, waiting or stalled, stay in place, highlighted, and a page button counts the urgent tiles on its page while another is shown, `urgentByPage`) or **By urgency** (waiting, stalled, working, idle; the panes' order within a state, `tileOrder`). **Reordering tiles** (#993, Same as panes only: By urgency the order is computed, so tiles aren't draggable and have no menu): a tile drags like a pane header (`agentDragProps`): dropped on another tile the two swap (`swapDrop`; the tile shows "Swap with …" while the drag is over it), dropped on a tile page button it goes to that page's last place (`pageEndIndex` with the page size; not a target where it already is) and that page shows; held over another page's button for 600 ms, that page shows, to drop on one of its tiles. From the keyboard, **Move Agent Left/Right** (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+←/→, or whatever keys the user gave them) on a tile moves that tile's agent, not the focused one (the command, resolved once by the window, asks the grid first: `onTileNudge`); a key bound to any command is the command's, not the grid's arrows, and the tile's menu (right-click, the menu key or Shift+F10) has **Move Left** / **Move Right**; the grid then shows the page it lands on, the keyboard staying on it until the user presses something else (`refocusTile`: a workspace refresh can redraw it, #999). It is the project's agent order (project.json), so the panes follow. Paging is like Panes': the page buttons in the toolbar, and Next/Previous Agent Page (Ctrl+Alt+PageDown/PageUp) page the tiles while Tiles shows. A page past the end (agents removed) shows the last (`tilePageShown`). The keyboard: the grid has one tab stop (the tile last focused on the page), the arrows move between tiles (↑ ↓ by the grid's columns), Home and End to the first and last, Enter or a click opens the tile's **focus view**. The grid is a group named with its page ("The project's agents, page 1 of 2"); a tile's name for a screen reader is its text, the mark named by its state. Tiles shown count as on screen (`agentsOnScreen`: what they show is seen); in the focus view, its agent.
- **The focus view** (#976): the agent's live pane (the same header and footer as in Panes, #977, #978, fully interactive: type, scroll, select) fills the agents' area beside a strip: **← Tiles**, then every agent in tile order (its mark, name and status; the one shown marked, `aria-current`; ↑ ↓ move between them); choosing one shows it. **The strip's card chip** (#1021, `RowCardChip`, `agentRowCards`): right-aligned on each agent's name line, the card it works on (Doing), else the one it reviews, else one it holds in Review, then Passed; none, no chip. Darren's words: it must look part of the current design, not added on, so it is the card chip's style (#311, #977) made quiet: `#n` with its icon (the eye in Review), a light tint and edge of the board's column colour (Settings → Board, the column the card is in; blocked, the board's red), no new colours; an unseen copy holds its room on the name line, so the chips line up down the strip and a long name ends in an ellipsis before its chip (the full name on hover when it is cut). Its hover lists the agent's cards with their columns; a click (or Enter, it is its own tab stop) opens the card; its accessible name says the card and column ("Card #1016, Passed"). Waiting on that card only, the status drops the number the chip shows: *Waiting → Passed* (*Waiting for its card* with no column); other statuses are unchanged. The pane header keeps its own rule (#399: only what the agent works on or reviews); a tile shows its card's title as before. **Resizable** (#1021): the strip's right edge drags like Combwork's other splitters (`PaneResizer`, `tileStrip` in the saved pane sizes: kept across restarts and shared by projects), 170 to 420 px, 200 by default, and double-click resets it; at the narrowest the name keeps room beside the chip, so the chip never moves or overlaps. **Reordering the strip** (#1053): in the panes' order (Tile order *Same as panes*; By urgency the order is computed, so no row moves), the strip changes the same saved order as the tiles (#993: project.json's agents, `agents:move`), which the tiles and the panes follow. A row is dragged by its button (with its chip) up or down the list; a 3 px line in the accent, in the gap between rows, shows where it goes (before the row whose middle is below the pointer, or after the last; none where it would stay), and dropped it goes there (the strip's own drag, so the pane's and page buttons' drop targets don't appear). From the keyboard: **Alt+Up** / **Alt+Down** on a row (as the Progress panel's lanes), its menu (right-click or Shift+F10: **Move Up**, **Move Down**, unavailable at the ends) and Move Agent Left/Right move that row's agent a place, the keyboard staying on it, a screen reader told where it went ("B: 2 of 6") or that it can't go further. The agent shown stays shown, and stays the one session commands act on (`moveAgent(…, focus = false)`). Esc closing a menu leaves the focus view as it is (the menu takes its Escape). Per project and not saved (`tileFocus` in the store, `openTile`/`closeTile`); `ProjectView` gives the pane layout just that agent (`TerminalLayer` and `PaneChrome`), the agents' area moved right of the strip (`.tile-focus`). **Back to the grid**: **Esc** outside the terminal (the strip, the pane's header; in the terminal, a field or an open menu, Esc stays theirs: in the terminal it interrupts or answers the CLI), **Back to Tiles** (`session.backToTiles`, **Ctrl+Alt+Esc**, which works in the terminal too). Darren's decision of 17 Oct: Esc stays with the CLI while its terminal has the keyboard (it interrupts the agent or declines a prompt); the shortcut and the visible ← Tiles work from anywhere, the strip's **← Tiles**, the **Tiles** toggle again, a page button or Next/Previous Agent Page. Back on the grid, the page is the agent's and the keyboard is on its tile (`focusTileAfter`, unless the user chose another place meanwhile). Switching to Panes leaves it (Tiles shows the grid again). Showing an agent from anywhere else (the summary chip's list, Agent n, Next/Previous Agent, a notification, the board, the Progress panel, the attention inbox: `showAgent`) opens its focus view while the project shows Tiles; adding an agent only chooses it (`showAgent(…, 'select')`): its tile appears on the grid.
- **A stopped pane** (HI-1881): a stopped agent's terminal is dimmed (`.terminal-host.dimmed`, visual only: selection, scrolling and copy unchanged), its ended bar says *Stopped · {time} · {why}* with Resume and New Session, and its header's status and its tile say *Stopped · {time}*. One source drives all three: `session-exit`'s `ended` (`{ runId, startedAt, at, why, code? }`, `shared/sessionEnd.ts`), why worked out as its CLI exits by `endReason`: a failed launch none (its failed bar), Combwork shutting down `quit`, else the cause its stopper gave (`you` from the window's `session:stop`, `assistant` or `agent` from the Agent API by the caller's token, `lane` from a lane end's quit, `closed` from its workspace closing; `stopped` with no cause), else `exited` (code 0) or `crashed` (its code). The renderer keeps the last end per agent (`sessionEnds`, by host and agent, the Assistant's too), only for the run it last saw start (an older run's exit is dropped), pruned as agents, projects or workspaces go; it shows only while the agent neither runs, nor starts (from the accepted click), nor failed to start (`useStoppedEnd`). Presentation only: not an agent state.
- **Session terminal**: Ctrl+V pastes text; if the clipboard holds only an image, Combwork saves it to `.combwork/attachments/<session id>/` (`session:pasteImage`) and pastes the path, which Claude Code attaches. Files dropped on the terminal (or inserted from the Files or Attachments tab) are **attachments** (§ Attachments). Right-click is Combwork's in every pane (#737): it copies xterm's selection, else pastes text (only); the button never reaches the program. **The mouse in Copilot's pane** (#737): Copilot 1.0.95 turns on any-motion mouse tracking (`?1003h ?1006h`) and selects with the mouse itself, so a plain drag is Copilot's selection and Shift+drag xterm's (the user guide says so). xterm reports each mouse move to a program tracking any motion as the user's input, and clears its selection on input, so while xterm has a selection there Combwork doesn't pass on moves without a button: the selection stays until a click or a key, and the right-click that copies it finds it. Combwork never passes `--no-mouse` or `--mouse`: Copilot saves either into the user's own settings (`~/.copilot/settings.json`, "Using either flag persists the preference to config"), changing their Copilot outside Combwork. Claude Code 2.1.301 and Codex 0.162.1 track no mouse. Every Combwork override of a CLI's own behaviour has an Advanced setting that turns it off: here **Pass right-click to Copilot** (`copilot.mouse.rightClickToCli`, off; at once) gives the button to Copilot, which copies its own selection with it, rather than Combwork's copy/paste. A provider whose CLI handles the mouse has a `<provider>.mouse.rightClickToCli` value; one without keeps Combwork's right-click. **A program's own copy** (#736): a CLI that selects text with the mouse itself copies it by writing an OSC 52 sequence to the terminal (Copilot: a drag over its screen, then Ctrl+C; Claude Code sends one beside its own copy; Codex copies without one). Combwork puts the text on the clipboard when the terminal has the focus in the focused window and had the user's key or mouse button in the last 10 s (leaving the window forgets that input, so coming back alone allows nothing), up to 1 MB, and never answers an OSC 52 read: a program can't read the clipboard. Refusals are logged (each kind at most once a minute a terminal). Shift+drag still makes Combwork's own selection, which Ctrl+C and right-click copy. (Claude Code's own Alt+V image paste still works, but its image is not kept by Combwork.) **File links**: file paths in an agent's or the Assistant's terminal (`src/a.ts`, `src\a.ts`, absolute, `./` and `../`, with `:line`, `:line:col`, `(line,col)` or Python's `", line N`) are links when they lead to a file that exists in a workspace project or agent worktree; **Ctrl+click** opens the file in that project's Files tab (the worktree's folder for a worktree) with the cursor on the line, a Markdown or other previewed file switching to Split or Edit. A plain click stays a click (select, focus), and web links still open on a plain click. Relative paths are from the agent's folder (its worktree or project); the Assistant's are from the workspace folder. Names may have brackets and braces (`app/[slug]/page.tsx`); a path wrapped in brackets (`[src/a.ts]`) links without them. A quoted path (`"…"`, `'…'`, `` `…` ``) may have spaces, and a location inside the quotes (`"src/a.ts:12"`); quoted text that looks like a path is one path, so when it isn't a file no piece of it is linked (not `file.ts` in `"missing file.ts"`, nor `src/a.ts` in `"Fix src/a.ts"`). Unquoted, a path with spaces is tried as a run of words (from a word with a folder in it, or one plain word just before one) and its longest beginning that is a file is linked; a run that starts with an absolute path and isn't a file as a whole links none of its pieces. Paths outside the workspace's projects and worktrees, folders, `.git` and missing files aren't linked. Existence is checked in main (`files:linkFiles`, within a project or worktree root) only for the lines being hovered, remembered for 5 s; it returns each file's path as spelled on disk, which the link opens (Windows ignores case, the Files tree doesn't). A path wrapped across two lines or redrawn mid-word isn't matched (`shared/fileLinks.ts`). **Card links** (#440): a card number (`#12`) in any Combwork terminal is a link when it is a card on the window's board (archived too); hovering shows its title and column as they are now, and **Ctrl+click** opens the card dialog in that window, like a file link. Not linked: inside a longer word, path or HTML entity (`abc#12`, `a/#12`, `&#12;`), hex or a version (`#fff`, `#12ab`, `#12.5`), a leading zero, more than seven digits, or a URL's fragment (`shared/cardLinks.ts`).
- **Terminal size and scroll** (#247, `TerminalView.tsx`): `fitTerminal()` is the only place a terminal is fitted to its pane and its size sent to the CLI (`pty:resize`). Never while it is hidden (its own view, or an ancestor not displayed: Settings open, another tab, project or page) nor while it measures under 20 × 5, so a hidden terminal keeps its last size and the CLI isn't told it is a few characters wide; it is fitted once its layout settles (100 ms after the last change: a resize, the terminal appearance settings, being shown again), and main passes on only a size that changed. A terminal following its output (at the bottom; only the user's own wheel, keys or scroll bar change that) is held at the bottom for a second after each fit and after being shown again, since xterm syncs its scroll position a frame or more late; one the user scrolled up in keeps its line.
  **From the process's start** (#486): until it is fitted, a terminal is its process's size (`pty:size`), not xterm's 80 × 24, so what a CLI draws before the fit (its first screens, or everything while its pane is hidden) lands where it drew it; output drawn into a smaller grid had left Copilot's screen with stacked frames and rules cut short until the window was resized. Main keeps the size the window last gave each terminal (`startSize` in `ptyHost.ts`, also one given before its process exists), and a process started in it (a restart, a mode switch that restarts) starts at that size rather than 120 × 32. These kept sizes (and a quiet exit's output, kept for the process that continues in the terminal) are bounded (#489): at most 200 sizes and 20 outputs of stopped terminals, the least recently set dropped first (a running terminal's are always kept on top of these, and trimmed once it stops); a removed agent's are forgotten at once, and all of a removed or deleted project's (`forgetPtys`), a hidden project's kept. A provider whose full-screen interface a resize while it starts can leave at the wrong width (`capabilities.startupSizeRefresh`: Copilot) gets a **size refresh** (`refreshPty`: one row shorter for 80 ms, then its size, or the size the window gave meanwhile), as resizing the window by hand would, half a second after its first status, again once it is ready, and after Combwork switches its mode live (Shift+Tab or a menu; a switch that restarts it is a new start). Claude Code and Codex redraw their own way at a resize and don't get it. A mode whose CLI names it differently on its own screen says why in the mode badge's tooltip while a session runs in it (`ModeOption.cliNote`: Copilot's Accept edits, whose own footer still says Manual Approval, as Accept edits is its Ask with Combwork's allow rule for edits in the agent's folder).
- **Progress panel** (`components/Progress.tsx`, `main/progress.ts`, `main/progressService.ts`, `shared/progress.ts`): long runs agents report through the Agent API (`/v1/progress`; a run is the calling agent's by its token, the Assistant's or a script's; only its owner, or a workspace-token script, updates or finishes it). A panel on the right, left of the Assistant's when both are open, shown and folded with **Ctrl+Alt+P** (`progress.toggle`), open state per workspace (`ui.panes`, `progress-open:<path>`), width draggable. Folded it is a 28 px strip with a small vertical bar per shown run (the newest six) and **+N** for the rest (#142: red if one of them failed, else amber if one is stale; hover lists them, up to 12); the strip's accessible name counts every run by state ("8 runs: 6 running, 1 failed, 1 stopped reporting"); it never opens by itself. Each run: agent and provider icon (the Assistant's mark for its runs, #399), project, title (command on hover), a bar (moving when it has no steps), "n of m: step", elapsed and time left (`estimateMs` is the time left as of the last report). Every line of a run stays inside its box: one line with an ellipsis (title, step, status, agent and project), the failure's summary wrapping; the panel never scrolls sideways (#220). Passed runs show for 10 s, then move to **Recent**. Failed and stale ones stay until the user has **seen** them (`progress:seen`: the panel open, the window focused, a failed or stale run with `seenAt` null; main sets each one's `seenAt` and clears the taskbar's red), then 10 s more, then move to Recent too (`isListed`, `isRecent` in `shared/progress.ts`), marked red; the folded strip drops a seen one at once (`inStrip`), so its red clears with the taskbar's. A new report (back to running) or a failure makes it unseen again. Dismiss moves one to Recent at once. **Honest states** (#549, `runStatusLine`, `barLook`): a run reported `waiting` (`waiting`, `waitingSince`) shows what it waits for as its step and "waiting n min" (after how long it ran first, when it ran over 5 s), never a time left, with a still, hatched bar (`aria-valuetext` "waiting"; the strip's bar the same); while it waits it has no `estimateMs` (the time that was left is held, `heldEstimateMs`, and given back from when it stops waiting, so the wait isn't counted; an estimate sent while waiting is held too) and never goes stale (`isOverdue`). A command `cw-progress` runs that keeps writing output keeps its run reporting (HI-1993): at most once a minute (`KEEPALIVE_MS`) its output sends an empty update, which counts as a report (the run stays running, its deadline unchanged: a stress loop with no step lines isn't "stopped reporting"); one silent for longer than expected still goes stale. A running run past its estimate says "finishing" for a minute (`FINISHING_MS`), then "longer than expected", never "0 s left" (less than a second left counts as reached). A **stopped** run (`state: 'stopped'`) is neither passed nor failed, muted (⊘), listed for 10 s like a passed run, then under Recent: `stopReason` `interrupted` (a finish with `stopped: true`: "Stopped after n min") or `gone` (its reporter's `pid`, sent at the start, is no longer a process while the run is open, running or stale, checked with the stale sweep every 15 s: "Ended without a report after n min"); neither marks a failure unseen. A reused pid reads as alive: such a run goes stale as before, never ends wrongly. **Recent** (#352) shows the newest 10 ended runs (`RECENT_RUNS`), then **Show all n**: unfolded, every kept run in a box of the same height (the 10 rows'), scrolling inside, so the panel around it doesn't move; **Show fewer** folds it back to the top. The fold is kept per workspace (`ui.panes`, `progress-recent-all:<path>`). The **Recent** heading folds the whole section to that line (#1228, Darren 20 Oct): a button with `aria-expanded`, a chevron (right folded, down open) and the count of its runs as the Lanes bar has its own, Enter or Space from the keyboard; kept per workspace as the lanes' and merges' folds are (`usePanelFold`, `ui.panes`, `progress-recent-fold:<path>`), across restarts. The list is `ShowAllList` (`components/ShowAllList.tsx`), the shared "last few, Show all n, fixed-height scroll" pattern (#312's Done by the Assistant uses it too): a real button with `aria-expanded`, the unfolded box a named, focusable region. The agent's name on a run is a button that shows its agent (the Assistant's panel for the Assistant's), and says so: the pane (or panel) flashes for 1.2 s and its terminal takes the keyboard (`flashPane`; retried for up to a second while a switched-to project's terminals appear; this focus, and a terminal's own focus a frame after it is shown, apply only while nothing newer chose where the keyboard goes: no key or pointer press, no other agent shown, and no other control that took it meanwhile, `deferredFocus.ts`, #327), so showing an agent already on screen visibly does something (#220: the reported "does nothing"). A click elsewhere on a run, or on a Recent row, or the chevron right-aligned at the end of every run and Recent row (after a Recent row's time; down while closed, up while open; a button, "Show/Hide details for <run>", `aria-expanded`; #251), opens its **details** inline (one at a time; Escape closes), as `runDetails()` in `shared/progress.ts` lists them: title, command (Copy command), the card and its revision (`revision`, the card's, #1233) with **Tested on** (`testedCheckout`, what was checked out where it ran) only when that differs from it (#1273: a folder agents share, a reviewer's checkout; for no platform both are the content hash), the check it counts as, agent and project, provider, started and ended (`formatDateTime`), how long against `expectedMs` (the first estimate's total), steps (done of total, last step), state and why, `exitCode`, `logPath`, then the summary, and **Show the agent**, or why not (a script's run; an agent removed; a project gone). **Copy details** copies them all as plain text, a `Label: value` line each and the summary last (`runDetailsText`). **Open log** and **Show in folder** (`progress:openLog`, `progress:showLog`) take the run's id, not a path: main opens only the `logPath` that run reported with its finish, a full path to an existing file, wherever it is (an e2e record is under `%LOCALAPPDATA%`), without widening `guardFile` for the window's own file calls. Open log opens only text logs and reports (`.md`, `.txt`, `.log`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.xml`, `.html`…) in their default app, never a program; anything fails with a toast saying why (no log, not a full path, gone, not a text log). A **filter** at the top of the panel (#251; `activeFilter`, `filterRuns`, `filterChoices`, `agentChoices` in `shared/progress.ts`): **All projects**, each project with runs (by name), **Assistant and scripts** (runs with no project); a project with runs from more than one agent adds an agent filter. It applies to the listed runs and Recent alike, and to the merge cards and lanes (`filterMergeSlots`, #810: the project's slots, and with an agent chosen those it holds or waits for, as a lane shows for its builder or reviewer; none under Assistant and scripts) (Recent is the filtered runs' last 10, and Show all n counts and lists every kept run the filter shows), is kept per workspace (`ui.progressFilter`, by workspace path in lower case, the newest 100), and the folded strip shows and counts only those runs, with a filter mark and "<project> only: …; n in all" in its name. Hidden while every run is in one project; a choice whose project (or agent) has no runs left falls back to all (or the whole project). The taskbar and seeing failures still cover every run. Stale: running with no report for longer than expected (a step's share of the time left + 2 min; the estimate + 2 min; 10 min with no estimate), or its agent's session stopped (checked every 15 s); a new report revives it. Open runs live in memory per workspace and go when it closes or its window opens another (`WorkspaceService.closingListeners`; a report whose caller lookup outlived the workspace is refused): at most 30 open per workspace whoever reported them (`429` beyond). Ended runs (#352): the newest 200 per workspace (`RECENT_KEPT`; the oldest ended go first, open ones never), also kept in `<userData>/progress-history/<hash of the workspace path>.json` (saved 2 s after a run ends, at once when the workspace closes, and when Combwork quits; loaded the first time its window asks, merged with runs reported meanwhile; read as untrusted input, `keptRuns()`: malformed entries dropped, text capped, each counted as seen so it is under Recent); runs open at a restart aren't kept. A save before the file has loaded merges the file in first, and reads and writes go one at a time. Turning the panel off forgets the kept files too; 5 open per owner, field lengths capped, every field checked before anything changes, updates merged to at most four window events a second. An update without `estimateMs` keeps the deadline. `total` is set at the start or, on a run started without one, once by an update (#145; again is `409`; a step past it is lowered to it). A dismissed stale run has ended (out of status, taskbar and limits; `409` to reports). The window showing the workspace gets `progress-runs` events (#1108: the runs that changed, put in place by id in the renderer, the others kept as they were so their rows aren't drawn again; the whole list when it changes, a run ending, dismissed or forgotten, the history loaded; numbered per workspace (`seq`); the window reads its runs with `progress:snapshot`, the list with the number of the last telling sent before it, at first, when its workspace changes and when it missed a telling (`ProgressSync` in `shared/progress.ts`): tellings that arrive during a read wait and those numbered after it are applied on top, in order, and a read answered for another workspace, or replaced by a newer one, is dropped; the rows are memoised and each follows the language itself; with 150 ended runs and 5 live ones updated 4 times a second, the window got 255 KB in 20 s instead of 8.4 MB and its script time fell from about 300 to 65 ms; the Agent API's stream and the developer console still get the whole list, `progress-changed`, in process) and a **taskbar progress bar** (`setProgressBar`): the combined steps of running runs, indeterminate when none has steps, error mode (red) after a failure until the panel is looked at (open, window focused). An agent's open run is in its API status as `progress`, and in the short project listing (`cw_list_projects`) as a few words. **Settings → General → Progress panel** (on by default) turns off the panel, strip and taskbar; reports are then accepted and ignored (`ignored: true`), also one whose caller was still being looked up when the setting changed (`admitReport`: the setting and its generation are checked again after the lookup, with no wait before the change).
- **Merge card and lanes** (#484, Darren's revision 1 of the panel; `components/ProgressMerge.tsx`, `components/ProgressLanes.tsx`, `shared/laneBar.ts`). Top to bottom the panel is: a **merge card** per merge going on: a slot whose holder has taken it (`holder.taken`; the user's own merge counts), not a turn given but not claimed yet nor a line alone (every project's; the project's name when the workspace has more than one), a divider (with a card only), the runs and Recent as before, and the **lanes**, pinned to the bottom. Neither shows without a merge or lanes, so a solo user's panel is as before. **The merge card** is in its own colour, teal (`--merge`, `--merge-ink`; no status uses it; dark `#2aa9bb`, light `#0e7f8e`): the holder (`holderText`: "B1 is merging #484", "You are merging"), the holder's branch from its worktree and the slot's (`cw/b1 → main`; "into main" for an agent in the project folder or the user), the holder's current step (its newest open Progress run in that project: "Full test set · 113 of 146: mergeslot"), "n min so far · n min left" (the warning colour once over its time), "Waiting: …", and **Release** (the Overview's confirm, `releaseSlot`). Its chevron folds it to its first line with the minutes so far, remembered per workspace (`ui.panes`, `progress-merge-fold:<path>`). On a short panel the merge cards take at most a third of it and the lanes give way (their bar always shown; at most half before #569, 40% before #512), each scrolling inside, and the runs keep at least 72 px. **Lanes** are #483's (`LaneInfo`, `lanes:list` and `lanes-changed`, the store's `lanes`) through one adapter (`renderer/src/laneSource.ts`), which maps them to what the panel reads (`Lane`: id, the project's path from its folder name, builder and reviewer, name, card numbers in order, state active/paused/ended/abandoned; a lane of a project not in the workspace is left out). Each card's segment is read from the board as it is now, not from the lane, except in an ended or abandoned lane: its segments are its cards as it left them (`Lane.frozen`, `frozenSegment`, #512), muted and never animated, with "…, when the lane ended" in the tooltip, no failed mark (the lane keeps no verdicts) and no current card; an `unrecorded` card is a dashed outline, "not recorded: the lane ended before Combwork kept where its cards were", and the lane's count reads "–/n". The panel's filter applies (a project's lanes; an agent's: builder or reviewer). A header bar, **Lanes** with the count (a button, `aria-expanded`), folds the section to itself at the bottom (`progress-lanes-fold:<path>`); open, the list shows **up to four lanes**, then scrolls (#569, Darren: six (#512) was too many), and with fewer it is only as tall as they are. **Its top edge is a handle** (`.progress-lanes-edge`, a WAI-ARIA window splitter: `role=separator`, focusable, `aria-valuenow` the lanes shown now, `aria-valuemax` the most that fit, `aria-valuetext` "5 of 7 lanes shown"): dragging it up shows more lanes and down fewer, snapping to whole lanes (the list's `max-height` is the lanes shown times a lane's measured height with its margin, so the next lane starts at the edge), **within a range** (HI-1673, Darren 26 Oct: as before #1309): its floor is every lane up to the lanes shown setting (six), so a drag never hides a lane while they fit and, with more, never shows fewer than six (folding the section makes it smaller); its most is four more (ten), no more than there are, and no further up than leaves the runs above 120 px (`RUNS_KEEP_PX`) (`laneRowsRange`, `aria-valuemin` the floor); double-click goes back to six; focused, Up and Down change it by a lane, Home and End to the floor and to the most. **The lanes take priority** over the runs: they sit at the bottom of the Pulse tab, and on a panel too short for the floor the runs give way, down to nothing, behind them; only a panel too short even then shows fewer, the whole lanes that fit, the rest scrolling. **A panel too short for more than the floor** (a smaller window, zoom, a merge card) shows the whole lanes that fit while the runs keep 120 px, and the splitter says that number and that maximum; the choice is kept for when there is room again (the room, the list's height plus the runs', and a lane's height are measured with a `ResizeObserver`; `laneRowsNow`). A drag or key sets the choice to what it then shows. The choice is a number of lanes (`chosenLaneRows`, `lanesShown`, `maxLaneRows`, `laneRowsNow`, `draggedLaneRows`, `keyedLaneRows` in `shared/laneBar.ts`), kept per workspace (`ui.panes`, `progress-lanes-rows:<path>`; none is the default), and folding keeps it; the handle isn't there while folded. **Order** (`panelOrder`, #512, #568, Darren's decisions of 11 Oct): running lanes (active and paused) first, then ended and abandoned ones in the order they finished (`endedAt`), the latest last, so the finished ones read oldest first and a lane that finishes always drops to the very bottom. Without a move the running lanes are as #512 had them: active ones, then paused ones, newest first in each. **The user can put the running lanes in their own order** (only running lanes move): dragging a row (HTML5 drag, `application/x-combwork-lane`; the top half of another running lane drops before it, the bottom half before the next running one, or after the last; an accent line, `drop-before`/`drop-after`, shows where, none where it would stay; held near the list's top or bottom edge, the list scrolls every frame, as the board's columns do (`shared/edgeScroll.ts`), and the line follows what scrolls under the pointer), focused (a running lane is a focusable `role=group` named by its pair and name) **Alt+Up** and **Alt+Down** a place (not past either end, said as such), or the row's context menu: **Move Up**, **Move Down** and **Usual Order** (forgets the order). Each move is said to screen readers in a status region ("B8 / R1 (one more) moved: 3 of 5 running lanes"), and the moved lane keeps the focus. The order is the running lanes' ids as they then show (`droppedLaneOrder`, `nudgedLaneOrder`), kept per workspace in Combwork's settings (`ui.laneOrder`, by workspace path in lower case; `ui:setLaneOrder` changes this window's workspace's only, on what is saved now, at most 100 ids, `keptLaneOrder`), and survives restarts. Lanes it doesn't name (started since) go on top, newest first whether active or paused (a new lane paused at once on a blocked card is still on top), and the others keep its order below them; a lane that pauses or runs again keeps its place; a finished lane leaves it (its id is dropped at the next move). The same order is every lane list's (`useLanes`): the agents tables (#529) follow it too. A lane is a header (builder / reviewer, its name, the state word for paused, ended "merged" and abandoned, the current card: the one being worked (`currentCard`, #512), and finished/total, finished being Passed or Done; ended and abandoned lanes dimmed) and a **segmented bar**: one equal-width segment per card in the lane's order (`laneCards`), each a button (click: `taskOpen`; tooltip and accessible name: "#405 Built-in loop wakes · Review, round 2", `cardSegment`). **Its marks explain themselves** (#706, Darren had to ask what the red line meant): under that line the tooltip has a line per mark (`CardSegment.notes`), and the accessible name ends with them (`segmentName`): a failed round's underline "#650: review failed (round 4): waiting for round 5", then "Reviewer: " and the first line of the comment its reviewer gave with that verdict (`failedVerdictGist`: by the verdict's author, within 10 s of it, Markdown bold and heading marks dropped), and the hatching's "#7: blocked: <reason>" or "#7: On Hold: <reason>" (an On Hold card with none: "waiting for you to move it on"), the reason's first line, both cut at 160 characters. A card failed and blocked has both; a finished card with a stale reason has none. An ended lane's segment keeps its blocked or On Hold reason as a note (no verdicts, so no underline note). Segment states, colour and pattern both (colour-blind safe, both themes): todo an empty track with an edge, doing `--info` diagonal stripes moving (still with reduced motion on), review an amber (`--warning`) outline on its tint, passed `--success` with a light inner edge, done `--success` dimmed and flat, blocked (a blocked reason, or On Hold: waiting for the user) `--error` cross-hatch; a failed round (`reviewRounds`: the latest verdict in its history "Review failed" with no "Returned for review", "Moved to Review" or "Started reviewing" after it, in Doing or Review) underlines the segment in `--error`. Rounds count the card's failed reviews: in Doing or Review it is in round failures + 1 (the failed one while failed), a finished one "Passed in round n" past round 1. Segments are at least 12 px with 2 px gaps (`segmentsThatFit` on the panel's width); a lane with more cards than fit folds its finished cards into one "✓ n" segment at the left, and if that isn't enough, its last cards into "+n" (`fitSegments`; their tooltips list the cards). Cards not on the board (deleted) read as todo, "not on the board".
- **Progress reporters** (#137; `main/progressReporters/`, `tests/progressReport.mts`): **`cw-progress [--title T] -- <command>`** reports any command as the calling agent's run. Combwork writes a `.cmd` and an sh script into `<profile>/bin`, first on every session's `PATH`, which start the unpacked `cw-progress.js` with Combwork's executable as Node. Output and exit code pass through, and the command gets the caller's environment (the shims' `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`, which runs the wrapper, is swapped back for the caller's own, kept in `CW_PROGRESS_RUN_AS_NODE`, so an Electron app it runs starts as an app); finish is ok on exit code 0 (else `exit code N`), and **stopped** (`stopped: true`, summary `interrupted`) when the command ended by an interrupt (`STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT` 0xC000013A, or 130) or `cw-progress` was sent a stop signal (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Break, the console closing, SIGTERM: the command has 5 s to end by itself, a second signal ends it at once). Told to stop, the run is stopped however the command then ends (a server shutting down cleanly exits 0; its exit code is passed on), and a stopped run is never timed. Ending it ends what it started too (`endTree`: on Windows, where a `.cmd` or npm command is cmd with the server under it, the tree is listed with start times and each process ended through a handle checked against its start time, never one that started before the parent its id names, which `taskkill /T` would end (#655); the command alone if that fails), and the run ends 2 s after the command exits even if something still holds its output. Run by the shims it is Electron as Node, with no console, and its command has a hidden console of its own, so a Ctrl+C typed in the agent's terminal reaches neither, and an agent stopping it ends the process tree, which nothing can see: that run is ended by Combwork when its pid is gone (#549). The entry ignores SIGINT itself. A `##cw-progress wait=<what>` line reports `waiting` (the run starts at once, without waiting for a total), `wait=` (empty) its end; the time waited is left out of the command's timing. The estimate is the median of the last five passing runs of that command line in that folder (timings under a hash in `<profile>/progress/timings.json`, never the project; a timings file keeps 1,000 keys, giving up those run only once first and then those with a history, each oldest first, never the one just recorded, so a busy machine's one-off commands don't push out a suite's or a daily command's estimate: #1549, `evictionOrder`). Step lines `##cw-progress step=N total=M name=…` (N the step starting, from 1) are taken out of the output and reported (`step` N−1 finished, `stepName`); the run starts at the first step line with a total, or after 2 s; a run started without one sends the first total printed later once (`PATCH`, #145), and later totals are ignored. Silent and harmless outside Combwork, unreachable, refused, or `CW_PROGRESS=0`. **Agents use it unasked** for commands and background tasks likely to take over 30 s: the session contract (`progressRule` in `shared/combworkGuidance.ts`) says so while **Settings → General → Agents show long commands in the Progress panel** (`general.progressCommands`, on by default) and the Progress panel are both on, and otherwise to use it only when the user asks; the setting is greyed out while the panel is off (#167). The combwork MCP server gets the choice as `CW_PROGRESS_COMMANDS`, Codex the same text in its developer instructions; it applies to sessions started afterwards. The command gets `CW_PROGRESS_WRAPPED=1`: a reporter inside it (another `cw-progress`, Combwork's own runners) then reports no run of its own (`progressTarget` is null) and Combwork's runners print step lines for the wrapper's run instead, so a wrapped `npm test` is one row (its total, printed once Vitest has found the files, comes late if that takes over 2 s). Combwork's own runners report through `tests/progressReport.mts`: a heavy run waiting for a test slot (or the Codex test home) reports `waiting` (its own row, or wait lines under `cw-progress`, and a `wait=` line when it gets the slot); `npm run e2e` a step per suite with per-suite estimates (`%LOCALAPPDATA%/combwork-test/progress-timings.json`; `--no-progress`), `npm test` a Vitest reporter added to Vitest's own reporters, a step per file; output unchanged; the e2e runner and the scenario harness give the suites, their test copies of Combwork and the wrappers they start only an allowlisted environment (`tests/e2e/runContext.cjs`), so no session or wrapper variable (`CW_*`, `CW_PROGRESS_WRAPPED`) reaches them (#202, #203).
- **Project view tabs**: Session (terminal), Overview (usage, compaction, re-cache), Performance (its metrics), Tasks (its board cards, §6.6), Sessions (list and transcript viewer), Files (file browser), Attachments (what was pasted or dropped into sessions; its id `images`, and its command `project.tab.images`, are from before #387, kept so tab settings and shortcuts carry over), Git (its id `changes`), then **More ▾** with Memory, Skills, Templates (#127) and MCP (#1043: `more` in `PROJECT_TABS`, `MAIN_TABS` and `MORE_TABS`). More ▾ is the strip's last item, a quiet button in the tabs' style (a chevron after its label) that opens a menu of its four tabs (their icons, and a key a user gave one), then a separator and **Project Settings…** (HI-1840: the `project.tab.settings` command, its icon `settings` and its key as `commandKeybinding` gives it; an action, never More ▾'s label or a selected tab, and not in its tooltip's list); while one of them is open it is the active item, underlined, with that tab's icon and name (*Skills ▾*), else the ellipsis icon and **More**. It is a button, so Tab reaches it and Enter opens its menu on the first entry. **Shortcuts** (#1043): the strip's tabs are Alt+1…8 in the order they show (Session, Overview, Performance, Tasks, Sessions, Files, Attachments, Git), More ▾'s have none (the Project menu, the palette and Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts reach them, and a user can bind them), Project Settings Alt+0; no other command takes Alt and a digit. Users' own bindings are kept (overrides are by command id). The title bar's **Project** menu lists the main tabs with their keys, a separator, More ▾'s four, a separator and Go to Project Settings (`PROJECT_MENU`). **Project Settings** (project overrides) isn't in the strip (#974): it opens from the header's ⋯, the title bar's Project menu and its command (`project.tab.settings`, Alt+0), shows with no tab of the strip chosen, and any tab leaves it; Ctrl+Tab cycles the strip's tabs, More ▾'s included (from Project Settings, to the first or the last). The strip is compact (#974): 30 px high, 12 px labels, no dividers, the chosen tab underlined in the accent (`STRIP_TABS` in `shared/projectTabs.ts`). When their labels don't fit the strip (More ▾ is measured and fitted as one more tab, its chevron kept), every tab shows its icon only except the active one, which keeps its label if that fits (otherwise it is an icon too, and the strip scrolls sideways with the active tab kept in view when even the icons don't fit). The strip measures each tab with and without its label (`ProjectTabStrip`), so the fit follows its width (window, sidebar, panels) both ways; it goes back to a roomier fit only with 12 px to spare, so it doesn't flicker at the switching point. Icon-only tabs are narrower, keep their order, height and tooltip (name and shortcut), and their label for screen readers. At the window's minimum width (900 px) with the sidebar shown, all of them fit with no scrolling (`tests/e2e/tabstrip.cjs`).
- **Files tab**: tree of the project folder with create (file/folder, inline name, `a/b/c` creates intermediate folders), rename (F2), delete to the Recycle Bin (Del, confirmed), cut/copy/paste and duplicate, multi-select, drag to move (Ctrl copies), drop from Explorer to copy in, drag onto the Session tab to paste paths, open in the default app, reveal, copy path. Git status colours; git-ignored entries and `.combwork` dimmed; `.git` hidden. Folders load on expand; a recursive `fs.watch` keeps the tree live while the tab is open (changes inside `node_modules` aren't followed; while files keep changing, the tree still updates at least once a second). Moving several entries checks every destination first, so a name already taken moves none. A paste, duplicate, drop, rename or new file selects what it made when it ends, only if the selection hasn't changed since it started (counted per change, `selectionSeq`): a row clicked meanwhile keeps the selection, so the next key acts on it, not on what was pasted (#641). Find searches the project (`git ls-files`, so ignored files are excluded). Selecting a file opens it in the right pane as an **editor** (Monaco, Ctrl+S saves, UTF-8 with BOM preserved, 5 MB limit, binary files refused; text that isn't valid UTF-8 is refused too, kind `not-utf8` with Open in Default App, never decoded with U+FFFD, which a save would write over its bytes, HI-2331; converting or keeping other encodings is not done). Its toolbar drops its labels when the labelled toolbar doesn't fit (measured, so it follows the language; back with 12 px to spare): the mode buttons and Save become icons named in tooltips and `aria-label`, the size and time go, and narrower still it wraps onto a second row, so Save is never out of view (#814). Previews come from a registry in `FileView.tsx`: Markdown (Preview/Split/Edit, front matter hidden, Monaco-coloured code blocks, relative images and links), CSV/TSV table, HTML in a no-permission sandboxed iframe, SVG as an image, images and PDF (Chromium viewer) through `combwork-img:`. Unsaved edits are kept as in-memory drafts across file and tab switches (marked ● in the tree). The other editors (shared notes, skills, instruction and memory files, MCP server definitions) keep theirs the same way across view and file changes, are included wherever unsaved files are asked about (quit, reload, closing or switching the workspace), and saving one whose file changed on disk since it was loaded asks before overwriting it. Deleting a shared note, skill, mode or MCP server (all to the Recycle Bin) drops its unsaved edits, so saving them can't bring it back; a note with unsaved edits can't be renamed until they are saved or discarded. Typing while a save is in progress keeps the newer text as a draft. Renaming or moving a file or folder in the tab carries its drafts along; deleting warns that unsaved changes will be lost; quitting always asks while any file has unsaved edits (listed, with **Save them** or **Discard the changes**; a file that changed on disk is never overwritten, and Combwork stays open), and **Reload Window** and switching or closing the workspace offer **Save All** first. Drafts are not kept across a crash (hot exit is a possible later addition). Saves carry the file's modified time and are refused if it changed on disk; the user chooses Reload or Overwrite. Clean files follow changes on disk. Third-party preview plugins are deferred.
- **Dates and times** (`shared/dates.ts`): every date and time Combwork shows goes through one formatter (`formatDate`, `formatTime`, `formatDateTime`, `formatWhen` for "14:05 today, else the date too", `formatWeekdayTime`), following **Settings → General → Date format** (`general.dateFormat`: `ymd` 2026-10-04, the default; `dmy`; `mdy`; `system`, Windows' regional format's short date: `app.getSystemLocale()`, given to the window with the language, never the language Combwork shows, #767) and **Time format** (`general.timeFormat`: `24h`, the default, or `12h` "2:05 PM"). The numeric forms are the user's choice in any language; words (a weekday, a month, AM and PM: "午後2:05") are in the language Combwork shows (#851), through `shared/i18n/locale.ts`, which imports nothing (agent scripts reach `dates.ts`) and which `setLanguage` keeps current. Each process holds the current choice (`setDateStyle`: main from its settings, the renderer from a store subscription made before any component), and components that show dates re-render when it changes (`useDateStyle()`). It applies to every date and time a person reads: sessions named by when they started (`sessionLabel`) and Combwork's automatic session names (`autoName`, which still count as no name), the session lists and transcripts, Markdown exports (the title, "exported from Combwork" and each message), the Overview's session details (Started, Last activity) and compaction history, "Running since" and a watch's deadline in the footer, "last updated" notes, a card's history, the Assistant's activity list, the Files tab's Modified and image times, the Performance views, an update's release date and plan-usage resets. File names, keys and what agents are told keep a fixed yyyy-mm-dd. Names users typed are never changed. Relative times ("2 hours ago") stay, with the full date and time on hover in the Sessions tab; the charts' day axes keep their short "Mon 5 Oct" labels.
