- **Language** (#767; `shared/i18n/`, `main/i18n.ts`, `renderer/i18n.ts`): user-visible text is a message, `msg({ id, defaultMessage, description })` (`shared/i18n/msg.ts`, which imports nothing, so data modules agent scripts reach can hold messages), shown with `tr()` (or `tRich()` for markup) in the current language by FormatJS (`@formatjs/intl`, ICU MessageFormat, pinned exact); numbers, money, percentages, relative times, dates and lists go through `fmt`, in the language's locale, and sizes and token counts through `shared/units.ts` (the number from `fmt`, its unit a message: "1,5 KB", "12,3k"; #851). A unit test (`tests/i18nFormatting.test.ts`) fails on a `toLocaleString()`, `toLocaleDateString()`, `toLocaleTimeString()` or `Intl` call outside `shared/i18n/` unless it names English (what agents and the English developer views read) or its line says why (`// i18n-ignore:`). Text is translated when shown, never at module load. **Translations** are `locales/<code>/<area>.json` (id → ICU message), found by the loader (`shared/i18n/catalogues.ts`, which only main imports); `locales/en/<area>.json` is the English extracted from the code, with each message's note for translators, and `shared/i18n/values/<area>.d.ts` types each message's placeholders for `tr()`. A message a language lacks, or whose translation can't be formatted (a renamed placeholder, broken ICU), shows its English, and the problem is logged once. **Languages** (`LANGUAGES`, `shared/i18n/languages.ts`): English and seven drafted by AI (de Deutsch, es Español, fr Français, ja 日本語, pl Polski, pt-BR Português (Brasil), zh-CN 简体中文), all at 100% for 0.8.0, each with its own name, its AI mark and note in its own words, and its `dir`. Every language can be chosen (its untranslated text shows in English), but Automatic picks one only once it has a translations folder, so Windows alone never gives a language that is still all English. **Choosing** (before ready, since Chromium takes its language only at start): a forced language (the `--lang` start option, or `CW_LANG` in unpackaged builds; it may be the pseudo-locale or a language without translations, and wins over the setting for that run), else **Settings → General → Language** (`general.language`: `auto`, the default, or a language's code; read from config.json directly, `config.savedLanguage()`), else the first of Windows' display languages (`app.getPreferredSystemLanguages()`) that Combwork has translations for, matched exactly, then by language (de-AT → de, pt-PT → pt-BR; Chinese only Simplified: zh, zh-CN, zh-SG, zh-Hans, never zh-TW, zh-HK, zh-MO or zh-Hant), else English. The locale for formatting is the Windows tag that matched (en-GB, pl-PL), else the code; Chromium starts with it as `--lang` (the pseudo-locale as en-US). Main loads the chosen translations once and gives them to each window with `app:info` (`AppInfo.language`: the code, the locale, the language Chromium started in, what Automatic picks, the languages with translations, Windows' regional format, the forced language and the messages); the window applies them before its first render (`initLanguage`, awaited in `main.tsx`) and sets `<html lang dir>`. **Switching** is live for Combwork's own text: a changed setting switches main (the latest request wins: a load still running when another request comes, even one back to the language shown, is dropped) and sends `language-changed` to every window and developer console, and `App` renders again on `useLanguage()`. Chromium's own parts (the PDF viewer, date pickers) follow at the next start, and the picker says so; it also says when a forced language wins. **The picker**: *Automatic (Windows: <language>)*, then each of Combwork's languages by its own name, an AI-drafted one marked short ("Polski (AI)"), with the chosen one's AI note in its own words under the list; in any language but English the row's title adds its English ("Język (Language)", the catalogue row's `text.englishTitle`). **Agent-facing text stays English**: cw-mcp.js and cw-progress.js never import `shared/i18n` beyond `msg.ts` (a unit test walks their imports); the settings catalogue keeps its English for the Assistant's tools, while a row's `text` messages are what Settings shows (and searches, with the English); the Assistant sets `general.language` as a select (Automatic, or a language's English name or code). **Text read by both** (#845): a service's refusal is a `CombworkError` (`main/combworkError.ts`: its text as a message and values, its English as its `message`), which IPC formats in the window's language and the Agent API answers in English; text a service stores or returns keeps its English field (agents, old records and code that compares it read it) and adds its text as data beside it (`…Text`: a `Text`, or a `StoredText` id and values in a file, where a value can be a message of its own: the CLI's help in the safeguard comment Combwork writes on cards, #866), which the window shows and the Agent API never sends (`WindowTextField`). **Key names** in shortcuts and menus are written as keyboards in the language print them where they differ (`formatKeybinding`: Ctrl, Shift and Del are messages, so German shows Strg and Entf, Spanish Ctrl, Mayús and Supr; #885); every key a menu shows goes through it. **Japanese and Chinese** (#893): a language's descriptor says where its formatting differs (`unitList: 'narrow'`: unit lists joined with 、, where CLDR's unit list uses spaces or nothing; `uiFont`: Windows' UI font for the windows Combwork draws without Chromium); a weekday and time are one formatter; two sentences in a row go through a message (`sentences()`, no space in Japanese or Chinese); app.css scopes CJK line breaking by `:lang(ja)`/`:lang(zh)` (strict line breaking, phrase breaks in titles and buttons, no italics or upper case), and monospace text uses `--font-mono` (Cascadia Mono, Consolas), never a bare `monospace` that falls back to a CJK font. **The pseudo-locale** `en-XA` (start option or `CW_LANG` only): each message accented, about 30% longer and in brackets, its placeholders, plurals and tags kept, so text not converted yet shows plain. **Tests pin English**: `combworkEnv()` sets `CW_LANG=en`, so suites find the window by its English text and dates and numbers format alike on any Windows. **The installer** speaks Combwork's eight languages (`installerLanguages` in `electron-builder.yml`), following Windows' display language without asking. **Help → Improve This Translation** (`help.improveTranslation`, #795) opens CONTRIBUTING's *Fix a translation* on GitHub; each language's glossary and style notes are `docs/translating/<code>.md`. **The user guide stays English** for 0.8.0 (Darren, 15 Oct 2026, on #860: the Assistant already knows the app): the Docs view's own heading, page list and actions are translated, but its documents (the user guide, the Agent API reference, the release notes) are English in every language, and the release notes and the guide say so; loading a translated guide by language is #860, later. **Developer views are translated too** (Darren, 19 Oct 2026, #1104, replacing the 14 Oct exclusion of #808): the Performance view and the developer console's own text (headings, buttons, filters, explanations, notices and errors) are messages like the rest. What the console **records** stays English: event names and summaries, the turn ledger's reasons, payloads and redaction placeholders are the data its recordings save and attach to Copy Diagnostics for maintainers, so they are kept like log lines (`// i18n-ignore`); benchmark text the scenarios harness prints is CLI-facing and English. The built-in skills' descriptions are shown translated while a workspace's copy has Combwork's words (`shared/skillDescriptions.ts`, kept equal to the SKILL.md files by a unit test), as the Assistant modes' names and descriptions are (#885; `shared/modeDescriptions.ts`, kept equal to the mode files by `tests/modeDescriptions.test.ts`, #1593); the SKILL.md files agents read stay English.
- **Sessions tab** (a tree since #239, like the Files tree): the project's sessions (Combwork's, external, optionally archived) on the left as **provider → agent → session → its sub-sessions** (`shared/sessionTree.ts`), newest first; selecting one shows its transcript read-only on the right, under a **Ran in …** line. A session sits under the agent whose id it recorded, under that agent's current name; never an agent added later with the same name or worktree folder. Sessions record their agent's name too (`agentName`; older records don't have it), so a removed agent's branch is "Coder (removed)", and older ones' "Removed agent". Sessions without a recorded agent (adopted, external, or from 0.1) go under **Not from an agent**. Each session row has a badge saying where it ran (`sessionOrigin`): "Project folder" or "Worktree · cw/reviewer", with the full folder and the agent's id on hover (the **Ran in** line names the agent too); external sessions keep their *external* badge and the Assistant's conversations have neither a location nor an agent level (provider → conversation).
  - **Sub-sessions**: sessions a CLI started for another one, not conversations of their own: Codex's **guardian reviews** (in Approve for me it starts one to judge each action, saved as its own rollout) and other sub-agent sessions. The provider's adapter reads it from the transcript's first line, cached by file and mtime (Codex: `source.subagent`, `thread_source` other than `user`, `parent_thread_id`; Claude Code: `isSidechain` with the starting `sessionId`), as `SessionListItem.sub` (`{ parentId, kind }`, kept on the record when adopted; records adopted before this are checked from their transcript, or Combwork's copy of it, and the result kept on them: when listed, and once per run when their project's agents are read, so resume targets never pick one). Besides the project folder, sub-sessions are looked for in the other folders its sessions ran in (agents' worktrees, folders sessions recorded, the Assistant's workspace folder), where only sub-sessions of listed sessions are taken; a session's transcript is looked for in the same folders when it is read, searched, exported, checked or adopted (`providerTranscript`). A Claude Code sub-agent's own transcript (its first message `isSidechain`) is read in full: only within a conversation are sidechain entries left out (`SidechainFilter`). They are shown, not hidden: each nests under the session that started it, which says how many ("3 guardian reviews"); one whose session isn't listed stays under its own agent, marked. Archived sessions take their sub-sessions with them. A sub-session is never an agent's resume target or last session, and never in a Resume picker (`resumeRecord` and the pickers skip `sub`).
  - **Counts and folding**: every branch shows its count (sessions, then "+ n" sub-sessions; the tooltip spells it out). Branches start folded except the focused agent's (the Assistant's: its provider's) and the branches down to the session shown; what the user opens or folds is remembered per project (`ui.sessionsTree`, by project path in lower case: up to 300 branches per project and 200 projects; saved one project at a time like the Skills tab's, #245). **Expand All** / **Collapse All** in the header and on every branch.
  - **Keyboard like Files**: ↑/↓, Home/End move (moving onto a session shows its transcript, onto a match opens it there), → opens a branch or goes into it, ← folds it or goes to the branch above, Enter folds or opens a branch, F2 renames, Delete deletes (a branch: Delete All).
  - **A Codex script's calls** (HI-2240, Darren's decision: the full version). In code mode (Codex 0.166) every tool runs from a script (its `exec` tool), shown as one tool, **Script** (one that only applies a patch, as the **Edit** of it). Codex's rollout records each call the script made as it ends, an `item_completed` event (McpToolCall, CommandExecution, FileChange, ImageView, WebSearch, other kinds by name), inside the script's run or later from a command it left running; `CodexConversationParser` adds each to the `calls` of the script it started in (`providers/codex/scriptCalls.ts`): the last script started by the call's `started_at_ms` that hadn't ended by then (its output's time), or, with no start recorded, the script running now [HR1's round 1: a command left running ends in a later script, even a later turn]; a call whose script isn't known is in none, never guessed, named as the same call made directly is (`combwork · cw_read_task`, Shell, Edit, view_image), leaving out a direct call also recorded as an item (its id the call's own) and the conversation's own items (messages, reasoning). A script shown as the Edit of its patch that did more becomes the Script it is. The transcript shows a script folded with how many calls of each kind it made, in the order they first came, and how many failed (*Script · 3 Combwork calls, 1 command, 2 edits, 1 failed*: an MCP server's calls by server, commands, edits, image views, other calls); open, each call folded with its own icon, input and result (a command's exit code as a badge, `exitCode`, red when not 0, also on its folded line; none while it runs), then the script's code and what it printed. `transcript:read` shortens each call as any tool (`transcript:tool` on the script gives them whole). `cw_agent_activity`'s `recentTools` and `toolCalls` count a script as the calls it made (`callsMade`); a script whose Codex recorded none is itself. A script's `calls` is empty when it made none and its Codex records calls (an `item_completed` seen in the rollout), and absent when they aren't known (HI-2246); every script is marked `script`, whatever it is shown as (an Edit of a patch it may never have applied too, HR1's round 1): the scenario harness reads them from the transcript in the script's place and credits an unknown script nothing (`tests/scenarios/codexScripts.cjs`, HI-2235, HI-2246). Fixture: `tests/fixtures/codex-0.166.0-code-mode.jsonl`, recorded in the Codex test home.
  - **Branch actions** (right-click, or a row's ⋯): **Expand All**, **Collapse All**, **Archive All… (n)**, **Unarchive All (n)** (when archived ones show), **Delete All… (n)**, on every level (provider, agent, a session with its sub-sessions). One confirmation names the count and branch ("Delete 4 sessions under Claude (Claude Code)?"); `session:bulk` then does each session as one at a time would (all or nothing per session) and skips those in use, and the result says how many were done and which were skipped and why ("Deleted 2 sessions; 2 skipped: 1 running, 1 in use"). Archive All includes only Combwork's sessions (an external one has nothing of Combwork's to keep; an external sub-session goes with its archived session). Usage totals stay as they are.
  - **Clean Up Old Sessions…** (#895; the header's clean-up button, beside Refresh; *Conversations* in the Assistant's view): one dialog picks an age, last active more than **24 hours**, **7 days** (the default) or **30 days** ago, and **Archive** (the default) or **Delete**, says what goes ("2 sessions older than 7 days.", "3 of them are archived." for Delete, "Nothing older than 30 days to delete." with its button off) and what it leaves alone ("Left alone: 1 running."), then sends the ids through `session:bulk`, the branch actions' path, which checks each again. *Last active* is the session's last transcript entry (`lastActivity`), else its record's `lastActiveAt`, else `createdAt`; a session with none, or last active exactly at the cut-off, stays (`shared/sessionCleanup.ts`). Its scope is the sessions the tab lists for the project, whether or not Archived is ticked or a search narrows the tree; each session is judged by its own activity, sub-sessions too. Archive takes Combwork's own sessions not yet archived; Delete takes all, archived and external ones too. Always left alone: running sessions, the one whose transcript the tab shows (not closed first, unlike a branch action), the Assistant's current conversation (the one it resumes) and, in main, anything else in use. The result is the branch actions' toast, with the dialog's own skips ("open here", "the Assistant's current conversation") alongside main's. **Progress** (#1659): `session:bulk` reads the host's records once, works on 4 sessions at a time (each still all or nothing, under its own reservation and locks), and sends `session-bulk` events to the window showing the host (at the start, at most every 250 ms, and once it ends), each listing every run on the host with its own id, so one ending leaves another shown (a branch's action started while Clean Up runs); the tab, and the dialog while it waits, show a line for each, "Archiving 120 of 300 sessions…" (Unarchiving, Deleting; *conversations* for the Assistant). Not in the Agent API's event stream.
  - **Can't resume**: a session that can't be resumed has a muted **can't resume** marker (a sub-session: its kind's badge) in the tree and over its transcript, and its Resume buttons and menu item are disabled with the reason as their tooltip (`shared/sessionResume.ts`): a sub-session; its provider turned off or not installed; no transcript left anywhere (neither the CLI's nor Combwork's backup); for the Assistant, a conversation from another provider than it runs now; no agent can run it (a worktree no agent of its provider uses, or no room for another agent). A running one shows **Show** instead. A removed agent's session that another agent can resume says so ("Its agent Coder was removed: it resumes in Helper."). Where a session ran is separate from who resumes it now: **Resume in …** names that agent, and its menu gives each agent's location (project folder, or worktree and branch), with "running, its current session stops first" where it applies. The transcript is read from Claude Code's file or Combwork's backup. Your messages and Claude's replies (Markdown) are shown in full; thinking and each tool call (one-line summary: the command's description, the file, the pattern…) collapse, with input and result on expand. Tool input/output over 4,000 characters is shortened, with **Show all**. Subagent work appears as its Agent tool call with the final report. Each compaction is an inline divider with trigger, size before and after, the first request's real size after it (including instructions and tools) and the collapsible summary. Slash commands and `!` commands show with their output. Pasted images show as thumbnails (the base64 stored in the transcript, loaded lazily) and open in a viewer that also shows where the image came from. The view opens at the latest message and loads the latest 200 items; earlier ones load as you scroll up (or click), keeping your place, and a search hit further back loads from just before it. A running session is followed (2-second poll of the appended bytes, while you are at the bottom) only with **Follow** switched on (off by default: Settings → Sessions → Follow running sessions); otherwise **Refresh** loads what is new. Search (Ctrl+F) looks through every session: names, dates, providers, agents and transcript text. It filters the tree to the sessions that match (and the sessions of matching sub-sessions), opens their branches, and lists each session's transcript matches under it; the line under the box counts sessions and matches. Clicking a match opens that transcript, expands the item and highlights the matches. Per-message Copy, **Export as Markdown** (tool calls, thinking and summaries as `<details>`), **Resume** for sessions that are not running — **Resume in ▾** to choose the agent when several work in the session's folder (by default the agent that last ran it, or another one that isn't running) — and **Show** for a running one, which opens that agent's terminal; plus Rename (a tag icon: the pencil means editing contents), Archive, Delete and Adopt. Each session row shows Rename, Delete and ⋯ on hover. Parsing is incremental and cached per transcript in main (`transcripts.ts`, `agents/conversation.ts`); blocks off screen use `content-visibility: auto`.
- **Activity tab** (#1254; HI-1743, Darren's decisions of 26 Oct 2026 and the Assistant's round 1 notes; `shared/activity.ts`, `views/ActivityTab.tsx`): **what runs now**, nothing else ("the card is the history": past work is read from the card, its comments, history and rounds, never here). Last of the strip's main tabs (Alt+9). **A tab per agent** across the top, in pane order, scrolling sideways when they don't fit (no "All" tab), each with its state mark (a pulsing dot working, a diamond waiting for you, a square stalled, a ring idle) and the key of its current card. **Hide finished** (on by default) leaves out the agents with nothing running: not running, or idle with no process of its own besides its plumbing and no background task (`activityTabs()`); the tab shown keeps its tab. **Agents ▾** and **Cards ▾** narrow the tabs (several can be ticked; an agent by its current card, the cards offered those in progress). **Each tab is a list** read top to bottom (`buildActivityView()`), nothing off to the side: a **header line**, its current card (`currentCard()`: one it builds in Doing, else one it reviews in Review, else one of its in Review) as its key (a link to the card), title and column on one line (HI-1884: the key and the column never wrap or shrink; the title is cut with "…", whole in its tooltip), else its session's name; then the agent's work in groups: **Now**, its running session's latest turn (the prompt and how long ago it came) and what it does in it, the tool call under way with how long it has run, else **Thinking…** (nothing yet since the prompt or the last tool call) or **Writing…** (after a reply), from what came last in the transcript (`ActivityTurn.lastKind`), else its state (*Not running*); **Subagents and background tasks**, its sub-sessions active since that prompt (each with its tool call under way, else thinking or writing, while it can run: while the agent works or a background subagent of its runs, when its transcript is read again with the agent's; else *Done*) and its background tasks (a plain icon with the task's name); **Processes**, those of its launch (Stop's tracking), each by what it runs (`commandText()`: a `cmd /d /s /c "<x>"` wrapper as `<x>`, anything else by its label, whose switches keep their slash) and how long it has run. The agent's **own plumbing** (its CLI and the terminal hosting it, Combwork's tool server `cw-mcp.js`: `ownProcess()`) is left out unless **Show the agent's own processes (n)** beside the heading is ticked (kept with the view). A card's builder and reviewer work as a pair: on a card both are on, the other's work follows under its name and role, only while it runs on this card (a builder gone on to its next card while this one is reviewed isn't). Groups with nothing are left out (Now always shows). Nothing from earlier sessions or cards, no time ranges, no diagram (HI-1678's zoom, levels and jump went with it). **Frozen when opened**: each opening of the tab (shown again after another view or the window restored, or opened from an agent or a card) takes a snapshot once what runs is read, and the tab is drawn from it; each newer read counts in the pill, **12 updates · Refresh**; **Refresh** (or the pill) takes a new snapshot; **Play** goes live, **Pause** freezes again. Live mode is a choice, never the default, and never kept. Live, nothing shown moves: what is shown stays where it is and new rows come at the end of their group, and what ended (a process, a subagent) fades out where it was over 1.5 s, then leaves (`keepGoneList()`); another tab, a filter or a new snapshot draws it afresh. **No spinners**: working is the state mark's pulse, nothing that looks like loading. **Entries**: **Activity** in an agent's ⋯ menu opens its tab, filtered to it, frozen; a card's **Activity** opens the workspace level (below). The filters, Hide finished, the tab and the own processes are kept per project in the window's storage (`activityView.ts`). **Where each part comes from**, nothing collected anew: the board (cards, builder, reviewer), the session records (`activity:sessions`, for a running session's name and its subagents), the agents' live state, a session's transcript parse (`activity:turns`: masked like the log, cut short; read for each session shown, and again while it runs, or a subagent can, only when its transcript changed, a few at a time) and Stop's process tracking (`activity:now`: each running launch's job and its background tasks, masked). **Details** (click a row): its status, its input exactly as written (a prompt or a tool call's whole input and result, a process's whole command line), masked like the log, its last action, and **Open in Sessions Tab** for a subagent's session. **End Process…**: one process at a time, after a confirmation, only the agent's own: main ends it only while it is in that agent's running launch's job as the process listed (pid and start time), never the agent's CLI or its terminal (Stop does), never by name (`endAgentProcess`; `notOwn`, `cli` or `failed` are said). **Cost**: nothing read or drawn while the tab or the window is hidden; what runs now read once a second, the session list every 5 s and when an agent starts or stops, the tab drawn again only when something changed (the renders' times stay readable for a test copy). **The workspace level** (HI-1664, Darren's rescope of 26 Oct 2026: added on top of the project's tab, which stays as it is; `views/WorkspaceActivity.tsx`): the activity bar's **Activity** (`view.activity`), the same view across every session host of the window's workspace with an agent running, the Assistant's home among them; its tabs **grouped by project** (each group after its name, the Assistant's last), every agent named by its host and id together (`activityAgentKey`: two projects' agents or sessions with one id are never one). Its sidebar: **Whole workspace**, then a row per project with its running agents' count, opening that project's own tab. Its view (filters, tab, own processes) is the workspace's own, kept per workspace (`workspaceActivityKey`), never a project's or another workspace's. Frozen when opened, Play, Refresh, Hide finished, Agents ▾ (each agent with its project) and Cards ▾ as in a project's tab; nothing past. **Entries**: a card in progress (Doing or Review), a project's or the workspace's own, has **Activity** in its dialog and its right-click menu, opening the workspace level on **the agents working on it now** (`cardActivityAgents()`: its builder and its reviewer while each runs with this card as its current one, `currentCard()`, and every agent whose *running* session's record has it, found by main through the cards' index, `sessionsOfCard()`, one query per host with an agent running, only as it opens and again as an agent starts, stops or begins another session, never for a status change; a session the agent ran before doesn't count, nor, for a project card, an agent whose current card is another, though its session's record keeps this one, as a card loop's does). Found before it opens: if the window went elsewhere meanwhile (another view, another workspace, another opening), it doesn't open, with **Card HI-12** above, naming the filter (its × shows every agent), else *Nobody is working on HI-12 now. The card has its history.* (a workspace card has no builder or reviewer: its agents are the running sessions whose records have it). The Progress panel: a run's details have **Show in Activity** (its agent, the Assistant's for its runs), and a lane's menu **Show in Activity** (its builder and reviewer). **Cost** (HI-1887, HI-1909: no per-agent reads on main): nothing read or drawn while the view or the window is hidden, late results dropped; a tick reads what runs now in every host shown in **one call** (`activity:nowAll`: each a host of the calling window's workspace, any other refusing the whole call, each once), never overlapping the last; the session lists (`activity:sessions`) only of the hosts shown, every 5 s and when an agent starts, stops or begins another session (never for a status change: what is drawn follows the agents' status once a tick, what is read their sessions), two at a time; turns only for the tab shown, as a project's tab reads them. `activity:now`, `activity:sessions` and **End Process…** take the Assistant's home as a host too. **Lock blocks** (HI-982): under Now, an agent's edit Combwork's file lock blocked (or asked the user about) while that decision stands (`activity:now`'s `blocks`, `sessions.hookBlocks()`): the latest per launch, by its launch, tool call, file and the holder's launch, so a restarted agent or a lock passed on inherits none; gone once the holder no longer holds the file in that launch (its turn's end, the lock's TTL), the blocked launch makes another tool call, the blocked call ends, its turn ends (a new prompt, a stop, an interrupt, the session's end), or the user allows it; scoped like the rest of `activity:now` (the project's agents), the holder named only when it is in the same project. Live only: no history here.
- **Processes left running while the agent runs** (HI-2111, the Assistant's card after HB2's stray `grep -rh … /` ran orphaned for five hours; `main/orphanProcesses.ts`): one rule, nothing classified (HI-2081 dropped classifying the CLI's children). An **orphan** is a process in a running launch's job whose parent has exited, by the parent's id and start time: the job host's `lineage` gives each member's parent id (a snapshot), and the start time of the process running by that id now (`0`: none; a later start than the child's: the id was given again; `?`, access denied: not counted), with its CPU time. The CLI and what it runs directly (its MCP servers, a command under way) have a live parent, so never count; a server started with `&` from a shell that has ended does. Running launches are looked at every 30 s (never starting the host); an orphan seen at two looks that has run **ten minutes** (from its start) is **shown**: Activity marks its row *Left running · process 4120 · running 12 min · CPU 3 min* (a warning mark), its details say why and its CPU time, with **End It…** behind End Process's question (`endAgentProcess`, pid and start time); **one notice** per process (*HB2 left grep -rh … running for 12 min*, clicking to the agent: a toast's agent target); and the **agent is told once** in a hook notice at its next tool call or turn's end (`inboxNotices.ts`, English, its pid and command: *End it if not needed; Combwork won't*). Combwork never ends it. **Pause the Team** names every orphan at once (not only shown ones) as a busy process, with End It. **Settings → Advanced → Processes left running: tell me and the agent** (`cw.processes.orphanNotice`, on) turns off the notice and the agent's line; Activity still marks it. Test copies shorten the bound and the look (`CW_TEST_ORPHAN_MS`, `CW_TEST_ORPHAN_POLL_MS`).
- **An agent's Hooks dialog** (HI-982, Darren's decision of 28 Oct 2026; `shared/hooks.ts`, `main/hookListing.ts`, `components/HooksDialog.tsx`): **⋯ → Hooks…** and the command **Agent Hooks…**, while the agent runs; read-only, never a hook or a CLI's config changed. **What's loaded**: from each provider's adapter (`launchHooks`, never a switch on the provider), each row with how sure Combwork is: Combwork's own as passed for the launch (**Passed by Combwork**); Codex's others from its own hooks/list, asked when the dialog opens in the launch's environment and folder with the launch's config overrides only (`hookQueryArgs`: never -s, -a or resume), through Combwork's owned app-server request (its request and timeout the advanced settings codex.hooks.listMethod and codex.hooks.listSeconds, which the launch's hook-hash check uses too), with Codex's trust (Combwork's are those of the session flags running exactly Combwork's command; Codex unable to answer: Combwork's as passed, a note, the rest unknown); Claude Code's from its settings scopes as read at launch (**Configured · loading unverified**; **Turned off** where the deciding `disableAllHooks` is on; **Not loaded** outside managed settings with `allowManagedHooksOnly`; a form Combwork doesn't know listed as such), and a file whose hooks changed since then noted as changed (the list stays the launch's); Copilot's Combwork's alone, with a note that it may load others. A file Combwork couldn't read or that isn't JSON is a note, never "no hooks". Bounded: a settings file read only within its size limit (a bounded read, as for auto-compaction), at most 100 hooks a source (the rest counted), a command 4 KB and a reason or event 300 characters, marked when cut; Combwork's authentication (the token, the run id in its URL, the auth file's path) left out of what is shown. Every hook not Combwork's is **not observed by Combwork**. **What fired**: the launch's last 50 hooks Combwork received on its authenticated route (`observeHook` in the hook server, recorded once handled, `hookHandled`; apart from `recentHooks`, whose log lines are unchanged), each with the event as sent, Combwork's hook it came through, **Combwork's reply** (`none`, `context`, `allowed` (Combwork didn't deny: no claim about other hooks), `warned`, `asked`, `blocked` with the reason, `error` with its step: reading the body, the reply, handling) apart from **the turn ledger's verdict** (applied, carried on, ignored with why, not reached), and Combwork's handling time (not any hook's runtime); in memory only, grouped when alike, never logged. A hook of no running launch is recorded nowhere. **Refresh** reads again; an answer for a launch that has since restarted says so (`runId`) rather than showing it as current. IPC `session:hooks` returns the rows and history only, never the launch's arguments, environment or token.
- **Attachments** (#387, Darren's decisions of 7 Oct 2026): any file can be attached to an agent's or the Assistant's prompt, by a paste (a clipboard image), a drop on its terminal, or Insert into Session. Every attachment reaches the CLI the same way, **as its path in the prompt** (a type the CLI doesn't read itself is not refused). Main decides per file (`session:planAttach`, then `session:attach`, `shared/attachments.ts`): a file from **outside the session's folder** (`state.cwd`: the project or worktree; the Assistant's is the workspace) is copied into the host's `.combwork/attachments/<session id>/` (`run-<runId>` until the provider names the session, moved when it does), named `<time>_<its name>`, and the copy's path pasted; so is every **image**, from anywhere, so the Attachments tab keeps what was shown; a file **inside** the session's folder, one already in the attachments folder, and a folder are pasted as they are. Files over **20 MB** (`LARGE_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`) are confirmed first (one dialog for all of a drop's large files; cancelled, nothing is pasted or copied). Nothing attached is ever run: Combwork copies it and pastes its path, and the Attachments tab opens in its program only images and PDFs. **Kinds** by extension: image, PDF, text (text, logs, data, code) and file (anything else). Each provider's descriptor lists the kinds its CLI reads **itself** (`capabilities.attachments`), checked against the installed CLIs in test homes (`tests/fixtures/attachments/matrix.json`, a unit test holds the descriptors to it): Claude Code images, PDFs and text (2.1.296: its Read tool returns a PDF as a document); Codex images and text (0.162.1: a PDF only as raw bytes through a shell); Copilot images and text (1.0.95: its view tool returns a PDF's raw bytes). **Chips** (`AttachmentChips`): while the prompt is written, a chip per attachment over the terminal's top right, its kind's icon, name and label ("PDF", or "PDF · by path" where the CLI doesn't read that kind itself; the tooltip says which and the path); × dismisses one (the path stays), and Enter in that terminal clears them. **Old folder** (`attachmentsFolder.ts`): a host's `.combwork/images` is moved to `.combwork/attachments` the first time anything uses the folder in a run (renamed whole, else file by file into the same session folders, a taken name getting " (moved)", recorded in `.combwork/attachments/.moved.json` before the file moves (if the record can't be written, or is there but can't be read, which is never overwritten, the file stays at its old path, where old links find it first); only real files move, between real folders of the host's own; what can't move stays for the next run), and paths into the old folder still lead to the moved files in Combwork: the `combwork-img:` protocol and file links (`files:linkFiles`) resolve a gone old path through `movedAttachment()` (the renamed file when the move renamed it, else the same name under `attachments`). **Containment** (decision 4): every write and move into the attachments folder goes through `ownAttachmentsFolder()`, which checks that `.combwork`, `attachments` and the session folder are real folders of the host's own (no junction or symbolic link, really inside the host) and refuses otherwise; new files are created exclusively (never over a file, or a link left in its place).
- **Attachments tab**: since HI-1841 two tabs (the shared `Tabs`), each with its count: **Pane attachments** and **Card attachments** (by card, below); each its own kind filters counting only its own files; the tab remembered (`ui.tabs.attachments`), or Pane attachments when the remembered one is Card attachments and the project's cards keep none, decided once their files are read (never while they load or failed; a click stays). **One viewer for both** (HI-1958; rc.9 had a card file's tile open nothing on a click, only a double-click outside Combwork): a click on a tile of either tab opens the same viewer, its arrows going through that tab's files as shown (its kind filter applies); a card file's text is read by its card and id (`cards:readAttachment`), never a path from the window, through `cw_read_attachment`'s own read (`readCardAttachment`: one opened file, its folder chain and identity checked again after the open and its row before the reply; HR2's round 1: a path checked and then read later could follow a folder swapped for a junction meanwhile), whole up to 2 MB. Its footer: **Delete** for a pane file (the rules below), **Remove from Card** for a card's (asked first, as the card's own Remove); **Open in Its App** for an image or a PDF only, so Windows' own viewer gives zoom, printing and the rest, and **Show in Folder** for any other kind instead (Darren's decision on HI-1958: #387, nothing attached is ever run); Copy Path, Copy Image (images) and Insert into Session (while an agent runs). A card file gone from disk says so in place ("Its file is gone"), with Remove from Card and nothing to open. Neither kind's tile does anything on a double-click. Links: the card dialog's **Show in Attachments** opens Card attachments at its card, an agent's ⋯ **Show Session's Attachments** opens Pane attachments at its running session (`attachmentsJump`, for its project only, consumed once its target is drawn or, absent, once the files are read; its tab kept, not remembered, and that tab's kind filter back to All). The Assistant's view has no tabs: its pane attachments alone. Pane attachments: what was pasted or dropped into sessions (`.combwork/attachments`), grouped by session, archived sessions last, each group headed by its name, count and the span of days its attachments were added ("71 attachments · Oct 9 – today"; one day shows one date; "today" and "yesterday" in words, other days in the language's day and month, with the year when it isn't this year's; #900), and a group that spans days has a thin divider labelled with the day ("Wednesday, Oct 14") where each day's attachments start, under a one-line description of what it holds ("Files pasted or dropped into this project's agents' sessions, by session."; the Assistant's: "…into the Assistant, by conversation.", #255). Images as thumbnails, other files as their type's icon (the Files tree's, by extension: Markdown, JSON, PDF, zip, code, text for `.txt` and `.log`, else a plain file) and name; every tile shows its size bottom-left and its time bottom-right; with more than one kind, filter buttons (All, Images, PDFs, Text, Other, each with its count; a filter whose kind is gone shows all again). Viewer with keyboard navigation: an image, else the file previewed read-only with the Files tab's previewers (`ReadOnlyPreview`: PDF, Markdown, CSV, and text otherwise, from `attachments:read`, up to 2 MB; a file of kind file, a binary or a larger one says there's no preview); insert into session, copy path, copy image (images), open in its app (images and PDFs) or show in folder (any other kind), delete to the Recycle Bin, and a group's name opens its session's transcript. Deleting (one attachment, or a session's group at once: `attachments:trashGroup`, all or none, whatever the filter shows) has the checks of deleting sessions (§ lifecycle, In use): the session is reserved and must not be running (`sessions.whileStopped`: it can't resume and paste meanwhile; Delete is greyed out for a running session's attachments, in the menu, the group's bin and the viewer, whose Delete says why and follows the one shown and its session starting or stopping, #258), none goes if another program has one open, and only what Combwork keeps there: a `.combwork/attachments` folder, group folder or file that is a link (junction or symbolic link) elsewhere is neither listed nor deleted through. Images and PDFs are served to the renderer through the `combwork-img:` protocol, restricted to image and PDF files inside the workspace.
- **Card attachments** (HI-1700, design on the card: s8, s11, s13). A card keeps files of its own, whatever sessions it has had: in its host's `.combwork/attachments/cards/<card number>` (its project's folder, the workspace's for a card with no project), named by its number, which never changes (its key does), one row each in the board's `card_attachments` (`card`, `id`, `file`, `name`, `size`, `sha256`, `by`, `at`, `comment`: where it first came, a comment's id, `description`, `pane` or none). The same bytes are kept once per card. Each file is at most Settings → Advanced → Card attachments: largest file (25 MB), one change at most 10 files and 100 MB, checked before anything is copied and again while each file streams in (one that grew fails). **Adding:** the card dialog's paste or drop into its description or comment box makes a draft (a chip, a `attachment:draft-<k>` link), stored only by Save or Post, the drafts of both boxes in one change with the comment; a pane's attachment chip and the Attachments tab's session files copy one to a card (Attach to HI-n, the project's other open cards); agents and the Assistant pass `attachments` (paths) to `cw_create_task`, `cw_update_task` and the Agent API's `POST /v1/tasks`, `PATCH /v1/tasks/{n}` and comments. Where a path may come from: a project agent only its project's folder, slots, review copies and 0.9 worktrees, and the system temp folder, never another project's folders or any `.combwork` but its own `attachments` (protected hosts are checked first, on real paths, a junction anywhere included); the Assistant and scripts the workspace, every project's folders, the Assistant's home and the temp folder; both also the folders the user lists in Settings → Advanced → Card attachments: more folders (HI-2480: Combwork's list, or the workspace's own over it, a workspace's empty list being Combwork's; sensitive, so only the user sets it; full paths separated by semicolons, a `%VARIABLE%` at the start filled in from the environment, empty by default; HI-2538: Settings' box and the tools show the list `;` apart with no space, spaces around each folder are trimmed; only `;` separates them, as a comma or a `%NAME%` after one can be in a folder's name), still after the protected hosts; the window the user's own pick or drop. A refusal to an agent, the Assistant or a script names the folders it accepts (the temp folder by its path, the listed ones) and that the user adds another there, so an agent doesn't copy the file into the temp folder. **Showing:** a card's text links an attachment as `attachment:<id>`, resolved against that card only: inline for an image, a link for any other file, a grey "removed" chip once it is gone; agents read the links as the files' paths (`cw_read_task`'s `attachments` lists them all, the start prompt names up to ten). **Lifecycle:** every attach, remove, move and delete takes the board's write lock and rechecks the card there; files are copied, never moved, until the change that makes their place true commits (staged in `cards/.staging`, renamed in with their rows); a removal or deletion renames into `cards/.trash/<op>` with its record (`op.json`) first and goes to the Recycle Bin once committed, back if undone. At each workspace open the records are read against the committed board: an uncommitted removal or deletion is put back, a committed one finished; staging goes; a folder of a deleted card goes to the Recycle Bin; one left by a move goes once the card's own folder holds every file; a file with no row goes to the Recycle Bin; a record that can't be read, or isn't one Combwork writes (a path in a file's name, an id or card number it never makes), is left and logged, nothing it names touched, and every folder from `.combwork` down to the operation's must be a real folder of the host's own (never a junction); staging an operation of this Combwork's still uses (registered from before it is made until it is disposed of), or another running Combwork's, is left too. The Agent API copies nothing before the destination is known to be allowed: the card's project a project of the workspace (a project agent's own), inside the operation that makes the change (the Assistant's: once admitted), its staging removed whatever happens. The card dialog's drafts go when it closes or opens another card. Archiving keeps them, until the project's clean-up (below); deleting the card sends them to the Recycle Bin, a move to another project copies them across. **Clean-up of archived cards** (HI-1842, Darren's decisions of 27 Oct 2026: only archived cards, archiving being the user's signal; a 3-day choice for a busy project): Project Settings → Storage → **Remove archived cards' attachments**, per project in project.json (`cardAttachmentCleanup`): **Never**, or **3**, **7**, **30** (the default) or **90 days after archiving**, counted from the card's latest archive line in its history (`shared/cardCleanup.ts`). Never an open or Done card's, nor a card archived because its project was hidden or removed (restoring it brings them back); bringing a card back from the archive first keeps them. **A plan, then an apply that checks it again** (round 2, HR5's review). The plan and the apply both run on main (Darren's decision after round 2, "Simplify: no worker", replacing "off main's thread"), in short steps while the PC is idle. The plan changes nothing: from a cursor, it examines at most 100 of a project's cards that can be due (archived, not with a hidden or removed project, with attachments, by the board's index: the rest never use up a batch) and plans at most 20 due ones, a card at a time with a yield between, each with its files as they are on disk then (device, file id, size and last write); a card whose folder isn't the project's own (a link or junction at any step from the project's folder, or a real path elsewhere) or holds a link where a file was is left out. The apply goes a card at a time, each one change of the board (`tasks.cleanUpAttachments`) refused once the run's workspace lifetime has ended (`boardWrite`'s `alive`, checked again once the lock is held); in it, the card must still be on the board, archived and in the planned project, that project still shown (not hidden or removed since), and due under the project's setting read now; its folder is checked again, and only planned files still the same on disk (or still missing) go, through the cards' trash (one record for them, so a crash is settled at the next open as a removal is) to the Recycle Bin once it commits, their rows deleted. A file attached or changed since the plan stays with its row. A comment of Combwork's on the card says how many and which went, and why (it keeps its own time); its links to them then show the removed chip, and `cw_read_task` no longer lists them. Each run belongs to its workspace's lifetime: it stops when that workspace closes or the window opens another, and a new lifetime never joins or waits for an old one's run; one listener per lifetime clears what it kept (its plans, its queued run). **When:** a workspace's opening queues a run (after old Done cards are archived), and so does each day while it is open; a queued run starts only while the PC is idle (no input for 2 minutes, checked every minute), at most 200 due cards a project a run, a card at a time with a pause between, and input pauses it, while it plans as while it applies, after the card it is on, until the next idle moment (it stays queued, and carries on from that card). Each project's cursor carries on from where the last run stopped, round the board once a run, so cards that keep failing can't hold later ones back. **Clean Up Now…** beside the choice (disabled at Never) lists the cards due now (key, title, when archived, files and size), at most 200, saying when more are due; the list is a plan main keeps (an id for that workspace lifetime and project, 10 minutes, at most 8 kept, gone when the workspace closes), and its Move applies that plan once, checked as above: an expired, used or other workspace's plan is refused (*This list is out of date*), and the notice says what went and how many files were left because they changed. Unpackaged test builds can shorten a day (`CW_TEST_DAY_MS`) and say the PC is idle or not (`CW_TEST_IDLE`). Pane attachments are outside it (Settings → Storage's Clean Up has its own). Undoing the Assistant's change doesn't take back what it attached with a comment, as the comment stays. The Attachments tab shows them on its **Card attachments** tab, by card (HI-1841); Storage counts them on a row of their own. **Agents read them through Combwork** (HI-1751: the document tools refuse `.combwork`, and a Codex reviewer rightly didn't go round Combwork to read the builder's evidence): `cw_read_attachment` (`GET /v1/tasks/{n}/attachments/{name}`, by its name or its file's name), for a card the caller may read (its scope, as `cw_read_task`), from that card's own folder only. Its whole chain (`.combwork`, `attachments`, `cards`, the card's folder) and the file are checked to be no link, its stored name plain, before the file is opened and again after, with the opened file's identity, and the card's row again before the reply: a card moved or deleted, or its file swapped, meanwhile is refused ("read the card again"), never read from elsewhere. Text (UTF-8, no NUL in its first 8 KB) comes in pages of up to 64 KB by byte offset, each ending on a whole character (a first page leaving out a byte-order mark), so the pages joined are its text, the reply naming the offset its next page starts at; an image, a PDF or a file that isn't UTF-8 gives its kind and path, for the CLI's own file reading. The document tools keep their boundaries.
- **Resizable panes**: the sidebar, the list beside the Sessions, Files, Changes and Memory tabs and the Docs view, and the Markdown/HTML split view have a drag handle (orange on hover). Double-click resets to the default. Sizes are kept per pane, not per project, in the app config (`ui.panes`); list widths are limited so the main area keeps at least 320 px, and the split stays between 20% and 80%. However little room the side panels leave the main area, nothing in it paints over them (#227: `.main-area` clips, and so does each agent pane, so a narrow pane's buttons stay off its neighbour): the empty project page and the pane placeholders start at their edge and scroll in their own area when they don't fit (`safe center`), and under 280 px the project page keeps only its title, warnings and buttons. The Changes split (#906, `ChangesSplit`, `.changes-split`) also gives way as the room for it shrinks, whatever width its list was dragged to: the list narrows first, to 200 px, so the detail keeps 320 px; under 520 px for both, the list sits above the detail (at most 40% of the height, its files scrolling; no drag handle) and the unused worktrees' heading and rows wrap, so the detail never goes to nothing behind the panels beside it. Wider, it is as before.
- **One-line descriptions in side-panel lists** (HI-2527, Darren: "They look good on one row", "tooltips would cover it"): a list row's description stays on one line, cut with "…", and hovering it shows the full text in the app's tooltip, only while it is cut (`OneLineDesc`, `useClipped`, as `OneLineTitle` does for headings). Rows keep their height. The lists: Modes and MCP servers in the Assistant view, Skills, Dialects' files, Templates, MCP Servers (description and where it is used) and the MCP catalogue. The keyboard too (HR1, round 1): list rows aren't Tab stops, so while a description is cut its text is one (`tabIndex=0`, only then), ringed round its line (`.one-line-desc:has(:focus-visible)`); keyboard focus shows the same tooltip, and Tab on or Escape hides it.
- **Settings page**: JetBrains/VS Code style — searchable, category tree, every setting has a tooltip. **Project Settings** uses the same layout with its own categories (General, Agents with each CLI under it, Sessions, Advanced…) and search; overridden values are marked.
  - **Section names cut short** (HI-2531): both lists' rows stay compact (30 px), a name that doesn't fit is cut with "…", and the app's tooltip gives it in full on hover, only while it is cut (`SectionNavRow` in `ui.tsx`, `useClipped`, the pattern of HI-2527's `OneLineDesc`). The tooltip wraps the whole row with `focus` on, so keyboard focus on a row shows it too.
  - **Section lists by keyboard** (HI-2532, from the HI-2529 audit): both lists are one `SectionNav` (`ui.tsx`), a vertical `tablist` named "Settings sections" whose rows are `tab`s with `aria-selected`, on Tabs' roving focus (`tabAfterKey`): one row in the Tab order, the selected section, or the first while a search or Modified only shows every section. Up and Down (and Left and Right, for the narrow pane's row layout) choose the next section and move the focus with it, wrapping; Home and End the ends; Enter and Space choose the focused row (ending a search, as a click does). The focus ring is the app's `:focus-visible`.
  - **Settings steps aside for the work** (HI-2525, Darren: "Settings designs the shape, the activity bar is where you work"). Settings (the gear) fills the main area while the side panel keeps the last view beside it. Any activity bar item, its shortcut or menu command, and **a click anywhere in that side panel** (a row, a switch, its filter; not its resizing edge: `leaveSettingsForSidePanel`, a capture-phase click on `.sidebar`) leave Settings for that view, the clicked row's own click still doing its work. The gear brings Settings back on the section it was on (`settingsSection`, with its search). Nothing typed is lost: a field that saves as it loses the keyboard is saved as the click takes it, and before a shortcut or menu command leaves Settings (`setActivity`/`showView` blur the focused element inside `.settings` first, as a shortcut doesn't move the keyboard and the unmount runs no blur); a box that saves only on its button (a model's price or a fallback row to add, a catalogue's address, a viewer token's name) keeps its text while Combwork runs (`useSettingsDraft`); a column colour picked under the 300 ms settle is saved as Settings closes.
- **Files and Changes tabs** get a selector (Project folder / each worktree agent) when agents work in worktrees. For a worktree, Changes lists everything that differs from where its branch left the base branch (its commits and uncommitted edits, `git diff <merge-base>` plus untracked files), diffs against that point, and offers Merge.
- **Command palette** (Ctrl+Shift+P; **Go to Project**, Ctrl+P, lists projects only), toasts and notification centre.
- **Tips** (`shared/tips.ts`, `components/Tips.tsx`, `renderer/tips.ts`): about 25 one- or two-sentence tips, each with a group (Sessions, Agents, Board, Assistant, Files, Shortcuts), an optional command (**Try it**, shown when it can run now) and a user guide heading, by its id (**Learn more** opens the Docs view there). Shortcuts in a tip's text are `{key:<command>}`, shown with `commandKeybinding()`. A **pop-up** of the quietest style in the notifications' stack (§14 Notifications, HI-2320), never modal, hidden while a focused terminal lies under it, never kept in the bell. The card: the tip, Try it, Learn more, **Next tip**, ✕ and **Don't show tips** (turns *Settings → General → Show a tip when Combwork starts* off, with a toast pointing at Help → Tips…). **When**: on start, 4 s after the window loads, at most once a day (any window); and at four **moments**, each once; either way only when nothing else goes on (§14 Notifications: queued until then, dropped at the day's end) (the first transcript over the size warning, the context over the Compact threshold, a project with a second agent, the first pasted or dropped image). **Which**: in list order, skipping those seen in the current round and those about something the user already does (they have run the tip's command, or its `knownBy` commands: every command run is noted), then a new round. The profile keeps it (`ui.tips`: seen, the day one last showed, moments used, commands run). Each change goes to main as that one change (a tip seen, the day, a moment, a command: `ui:changeTips`), applied to what is saved, every window's copy following by `tips-changed`, so one window's older copy can't undo another's (#266). A window starting up listens before it loads its snapshot (`ui:get`): the `tips-changed` and `ui-pref-changed` events that arrive before the snapshot is applied are handled again after it (`renderer/startupReplay.ts`, #295), so a change another window makes while it loads isn't undone by the older snapshot; `ui:set` doesn't write `tips`. **Help → Tips…**: a dialog with all tips by group, a search box, Try it and Learn more on each, and the setting. New user-visible features add a tip.
- **Failed loads** are never shown as empty results. A list, search or page whose load fails says so in its place, with the error and **Retry** (`LoadFailed`); one whose refresh fails keeps the last results under a note, "Could not refresh …; last updated 14:05", with the error on hover and **Retry** (`StaleNote`). Loading, empty, failed and stale look different. What a view loaded belongs to the scope it was loaded for (the project, the workspace, the search and its query: `useScopedLoad`): after a switch the new scope shows loading, then its own results or its own error, never the last scope's results (as stale or otherwise), and a load that finishes after the view moved on, or after a newer load started, is dropped. This covers the Sessions tab (list and search), the Overviews, the Skills, Attachments, Memory and MCP tabs, the Files tab's filter, the workspace's Skills view and Settings → Workspace's hidden projects; Add Agent says when git couldn't be read rather than that the project isn't a repository. Calls that only add to a view (git colours in the Files tree, live file watching, transcript images, modes) stay quiet when they fail.
- **Settings in a narrow pane** (#887): Settings and Project Settings follow their own width, not the window's (container queries on `.settings`). A row whose description and control don't fit side by side (the text needs about 240 px) puts the control under the description, on the right; a switch alone takes only its own width. Under 560 px the categories list is 132 px wide (220 otherwise) and the padding less; under 420 px the categories are a row above the settings that scrolls sideways, the selected one underlined. Settings → Advanced's ids break after a dot, the shortcuts table keeps its row buttons in view at its right edge while it scrolls sideways, and the price table's boxes narrow (90 px down to 60) before it scrolls in its own box.
- **Keyboard shortcuts** are configurable. Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts lists every command with its shortcut, its category, where it comes from (default, changed, removed), as a data table on one page (#250: sort by a header; filter by where it is set, in a strip above the table that wraps and never scrolls sideways with it, DataTable's opt-in `filtersAbove`, HI-1878, whose review dropped the Category filter as the tabs already choose the category; the search box narrows it too), on tabs since HI-1838 (the shared `Tabs`): **All**, then one per category in the commands' order, each with its count; a category's tab has no Category column; the tab is remembered (`ui.tabs`: `shortcuts`, Project Settings' `shortcuts.project`, which offers All, Project and Session); a search shows All with each tab's count its matches, a tab clicked meanwhile narrows that query only (kept with the trimmed, lower-cased query it was clicked for; a changed query shows All again, and going back to the first doesn't bring the click back, HI-1885, as Advanced's HI-1839) without being remembered, and clearing it brings back the tab remembered before. Conflicts are found across every category (a warning naming the other commands with their categories, *Session: Compact Conversation*, and a question before saving one) and keys that go to Claude Code while the terminal has focus. A shortcut is recorded by pressing it; a second combination within 1.2 s makes a chord. Refused: keys without Ctrl or Alt (except F-keys), Ctrl+C/V/X/A/Z/Y and Shift+Tab. Overrides are stored in `settings.keybindings` (`null` removes a default). **Project Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts** overrides the Project and Session commands for that project only, in `.combwork/project.json` (`keybindings`), over the global ones. Keys are matched by physical key (`KeyboardEvent.code`), so Shift and AltGr don't change a combination's name. Defaults besides the existing ones: Ctrl+P Go to Project, Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab next/previous project tab, Ctrl+1…9 focus agent N, Ctrl+Alt+1…5 layouts (of the page on screen), Ctrl+Alt+PageDown / PageUp next/previous agent page, Ctrl+Alt+M permission mode, Ctrl+Alt+C Compact, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N Add Agent, Ctrl+` focus the session terminal, Ctrl+Shift+` external terminal, Ctrl+Alt+U notifications, Ctrl+Alt+P Progress panel, Ctrl+Shift+J Task Board, Ctrl+Shift+O Workspace Overview, Ctrl+Alt+T New Card; the project tabs Alt+1…9 in the strip's order (Activity, #1254, the 9th) and Alt+0 Project Settings (#1043). Help → Keyboard Shortcuts shows the current ones and links to the editor.
- **Providers**: Settings → Providers enables and disables each provider (disabling one with running agents asks whether to stop them now or let them run). **There is no default provider** (decision A, HI-2106; its last readers went with HI-2132): a new agent's CLI is its connection's, the first usable connection in the one order of accounts (on here, its CLI on and installed: main's `firstUsableAccount`, the window's `firstReadyConnection`), for Add Agent, the quick add, New Session, the Agent API, a new template agent's suggested CLI, the Board's Start, the Skills tab and a new workspace's Assistant alike. A 0.9 `settings.defaultProvider` (or a project's own, or `settings.assistant.provider`) is read only by the migration (`connectionDefaults.ts`), which keeps each agent on the CLI it ran. **Automatic** (`autoProvider`) survives only as the last resort: an agent with no CLI of its own and no usable account (a test copy on its CLI test home) gets the first provider in the order that is turned on and installed, else the first turned on, else Claude Code (each process tells `shared/providers.ts` what it found, `setInstalledCheck`: main's providerService, the window's store). **The order** is Combwork's (`PROVIDERS`: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot), with no order of the user's: 0.9's `settings.providerOrder` (HI-1965) went with decision A (its reorder with HI-2107, `settings:moveProvider` and its revision with HI-2113, the setting itself with HI-2139: nothing in the window or at launch reads it, and a `settings:update` sending it changes nothing). A 0.9 user who reordered sees Combwork's order again. One saved by 0.9 stays in `config.json`, read-only, as the migration's input: what 0.9's Automatic picked followed it, so the migration reads an agent or Assistant that followed Automatic with its own resolver in that order (`legacyAutoProvider`), never today's `autoProvider`. Everything in the window that lists providers is in it: Add Agent's provider choice, Provider Setup's tabs, Settings' and Project Settings' provider pages, Settings → Advanced's CLI tabs (Combwork's first), the project's provider lists, the workspace overview, the Sessions tab's provider groups and Keyboard Shortcuts' reserved keys, as are Automatic's fallback (`enabledProviders`) and a Combwork template's stand-in provider (`templates.ts`). The one order the user sets is the accounts' (decision A). Config version 8 turned a saved Claude Code default into Automatic: it was the default saved into every config up to 0.4.x, so it can't be told from a choice, and Automatic still picks Claude Code wherever it is turned on and installed; Codex and Copilot defaults stayed. A project with no agents names the CLI a new agent gets (its first usable connection's) and warns only when no account is on here (*No account is on in this workspace*), or when accounts are on but none of their CLIs is installed (*No account on here has its coding agent CLI installed*); a CLI no connection leads to is never named, and nothing is said while Combwork is still looking. The same rule holds for the providers banner, the status bar and Provider Setup opening by itself (`providerWarnings` with `providersInUse`): they are about providers turned on **and in use** (the first usable connection's CLI, what a new agent gets, and any agent's own provider in the window's workspace, the Assistant's included). When none of those turned on is installed, one banner says so instead (Provider Setup at the first one). A provider only turned on that isn't installed shows plainly in the status bar ("not installed", no warning). Nothing is decided while Combwork is still looking for a provider it hasn't found (at start), since Automatic's pick isn't known yet. **Automatic never resolves from partial detection** (#506): detection answers per CLI and in any order, so Automatic is only decided once **every turned-on provider has answered**, found or missing (`autoProviderPending`). Until then `autoProvider` is a guess for display only (the first turned-on provider not known to be missing: never a later one because it answered first). A CLI counts as found as soon as it is located, before its version, models and sign-in are read. What commits to a pick waits for it: main's `providerService.settle()` (at most 20 s) before a new conversation of an agent with no CLI of its own, an agent added without a provider or connection (the first usable account may be on a CLI not answered yet) (Add Agent, the Agent API) and any launch whose CLI hasn't answered (a launch of a known provider waits only for that CLI, never for another); if Combwork is still looking after that, it is **refused** ("Combwork is still looking for … Try again in a moment."), never decided from the guess, and nothing is saved or started. In the window, the quick add, New Session and Resume wait the same way before deciding (rather than opening Provider Setup for a CLI not answered yet) and, still looking, say so and do nothing; Add Agent shows *Checking which coding agents are installed…* and holds Add until it is known, unless the user picks a provider. Tests only (unpackaged builds): `CW_TEST_SLOW_DETECT="<provider>=<ms>"` holds one provider's detection and `CW_TEST_DETECT_WAIT_MS` shortens the wait (`providerdetect`).
- **A resume runs its conversation's own provider** (#506, Darren's decision). Resuming a conversation reopens it in the provider that recorded it (one Combwork has no record of, started outside Combwork: the provider whose CLI has its transcript), in whichever agent works in the folder it ran in, even if that agent's provider (its own, or a default it follows: the Assistant's, from Settings → Assistant or Assistant Settings) has changed since; new conversations use the agent's provider now. A conversation of another provider than the agent's runs with the project's settings for its provider (the agent's own model, effort, mode and context are its current provider's). If that CLI is turned off or not installed, the refusal names it. While it runs, a change of the agent's provider or a default asks for no restart: it is for the next new conversation. Resume (the agent's last conversation) is still its current provider's last: changing an agent's provider clears it. A conversation still never changes provider (§15, 22): Hand Over to… moves work between providers. `cw_list_providers`' `isDefault` is what new agents use now. Each provider has its own settings page (path, default model, effort and permission mode, dangerous-mode option, extra arguments, update checks, price table). **Allow background sessions** (providers with `capabilities.backgroundSessions`: Claude Code) is off by default: Combwork starts Claude Code with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW=1`, because ← on an empty prompt opens its agent view and moves the session into Claude Code's background service, where Combwork can't see or stop it (Stop only closes the terminal, and resuming fails until `claude stop`). The user's own Claude Code settings are not changed. If a resume exits because the CLI holds the conversation in a background job (it names the job: `claude attach <id>`), Combwork shows a notification with **Stop It and Resume**, which runs `claude stop <id>` and resumes the conversation in the agent (`backgroundJobIn()`/`stopBackgroundJob()` on the adapter; nothing else is listed or stopped). Provider icons show on agent tabs, pane headers, the Sessions list, pickers, settings, Provider Setup, About and the status bar. They are **Combwork's own badges, never a provider's logo** (#470: the logo owners' terms need their permission): an outline, a glyph and a colour per provider (Claude Code a coral circle with a tilde, Codex a teal rounded square with braces, GitHub Copilot a violet diamond with a double chevron), always with the provider's name or as its tooltip. The status bar draws them in its text colour with the glyph cut out, so the outline tells them apart (`ProviderIcon.tsx`). A banner shows while no provider is enabled, none enabled is installed, or one in use needs setup (#474, above).
- **Status bar**: workspace, branch, session counts, the attention inbox's **n need you** (§14), plan usage per provider (one item each: Claude Code's 5-hour and weekly %, Codex's windows; reset times and the agent that reported each on hover; darker at 80%, red at 95%; a limit whose reset has passed with no new report is left out). **Which reading is kept** (#383, from what the CLIs were recorded sending through the developer console, `tests/fixtures/planusage-2026-10-19.json`): each session relays the reading of its own latest API call (Claude Code 2.1.303 only with its turns, none while idle, none before its first call when resumed), and a resumed Codex session reports the last reading in its rollout, however old. So per provider and limit (`mergePlanUsage`, `main/planUsage.ts`), compared as reported: a reading of a period already over is ignored; the later period wins; within a period (resets under 30 min apart) the **higher** reading is kept, with the later reset time; with no reset time, the latest report. A limit is its window: Codex's `limit_id` was only ever `codex` (Darren's decision on #383: limits per `limit_id` wait for a recorded second id). The windows are told of any change to a kept value as reported, unrounded. Warnings run on what is kept. The status bar also shows each enabled provider's CLI version. Only app-wide items: an agent's model, effort, permission mode and context are in its pane footer (effort as the running session reports it, else the configured one; model shown as what actually runs (#248): the running session's reported model (Claude Code's status line, else its transcript; Codex's rollout), else what the choice resolves to (an alias by the model the CLI says it stands for: "Opus" shows as "Opus 5.5", the choice in the tooltip, "Opus 5.5 · chosen as Opus"), named as the CLI lists that id, else as the provider formats it; never guessed: an alias the CLI doesn't list shows as named. A project or agent choice shows plainly, an inherited one with "(default)"; Claude Code's own default is named from its settings' `model` (an alias there resolved the same way) or the model last seen in a session started without `--model`, else "Claude Code default"), Agent API state, Combwork's own version (opens About; dev builds show "Combwork Dev"), notifications.
- **About** dialog (versions, data folder, update status with Check Now, licence links: Combwork's MIT License and the third-party notices open in the Docs view, the Chromium licences file opens from the install folder), **Docs** view (user guide, Agent API reference, release notes, licence, third-party notices, shortcuts), first-run Claude Code setup. **The user guide's headings have stable ids** (#1535): each ends with an empty anchor, `## Card loops <a id="card-loops"></a>` (hidden on GitHub, which still scrolls to `#card-loops`; `{#id}` would show there as text), its slug when the ids were added, kept when the heading is renamed. The Docs view gives the heading that id and drops the anchor; `cw_doc_outline` lists it as the heading's slug. Every link into the guide goes by id: tips' Learn more, the window's other Learn more links (`openGuideAt(id)`), the settings catalogue's `docs`, the guide's own `#links` and the README's; the Assistant's settings tools give that heading's text as it is now. `tests/userGuide.test.ts` fails on a heading without an id and on a link to an id the guide lacks. A new heading gets its slug as its id; a renamed one keeps its id.

### 13.1 Colour scheme

VS Code's dark neutrals with **honey orange** replacing VS Code blue as the accent.

| Token | Dark | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Accent | `#F59E0B` | focus, selection, primary buttons, active indicators |
| Accent strong | `#D97706` | status bar, pressed states |
| Background | `#1E1E1E` / `#252526` / `#2D2D30` | editor / sidebar / panels |
| Info | `#3B9EFF` | links, informational badges |
| Success / Warning / Error | `#4EC96B` / `#F5C451` / `#F2555A` | status dots, bypass warning |
| Sign-in | `#B48CFF` (light `#8250DF`) | the needs sign-in dot and badge |

A light theme uses the same accent with VS Code Light neutrals.
