## 14. Tray, notifications and sound

- Close and minimise go to the tray (each configurable). Quit via tray or File → Exit.
- **Quitting** stops all sessions (they stay resumable). Setting *Confirm before quitting*: **When an agent is working** (default; working, waiting on a prompt, or waiting on background tasks), **Whenever sessions are running**, or **Never** (the earlier on/off setting migrates to working/never). The confirmation is an in-app dialog (the window is shown first) listing each session with its status, marking the ones that would be interrupted, with *Don't ask again* (about sessions), *Cancel*, *Quit when agents finish* (only when an agent is working) and *Quit now*. Files with unsaved edits in the Files tab are listed at the top and always make Combwork ask, whatever the setting, with the choice to save or discard them (the buttons read *Save and quit…* when saving). No native message boxes.
- **Quit when agents finish**: Combwork hides, the tray tooltip and menu show the pending quit (*Quit Now*, *Cancel Pending Quit*), a banner shows it if the window is opened, and Combwork quits as soon as no agent is working or waiting on background tasks. Before it does (the last agent finished, or Quit Now from the tray or the menus), each window with unsaved files, edited after it was reopened during the wait, asks about them as the quit dialog does (save or discard; `finishPendingQuit`, once however many session events come, HI-2336); *Cancel* there cancels the pending quit.
- Quitting without a dialog (or after waiting) shows a notification that the stopped sessions can be resumed. Shutdown waits up to 3 s for each session's final transcript backup.
- **Close commands** (HI-1368; Darren's decisions of 28 Oct: option C, waited on with a panel, a spinner): **Settings → Workspace → When this workspace closes, run** (`workspace.json` `onClose: { command, onUpdate }`, an object so it can later be one of a workspace's named commands) and **Settings → General → When Combwork quits, run** (`config.json` `settings.general.onQuit`, the same shape). Both are `SENSITIVE` (`PATCH /v1/settings` refuses them at any Control level; only the user sets them, in Settings; `closeCommand:setWorkspace` saves the workspace's). **When:** a workspace's runs as it closes (`closeWithCommand`, `closeCommand/closeCommands.ts`): its window closes (not the last, `requestCloseWindow`), the window switches workspace (`openHere`), **Close Workspace**, or Combwork quits; the last window closed to the tray is a hide, not a close; never after a crash. One close per open: a second close of the same open (a switch, the window's close and a quit at once) joins the first, whose reason wins. `{workspace}` (path), `{name}` (folder name) and `{reason}` (`window`, `switch`, `quit`, `update`) are filled as written (`shared/closeCommand.ts`); a restart to install an update runs neither command unless *Also when Combwork restarts to install an update* is ticked. Never from a test copy of Combwork, quiet or shown (`CW_USER_DATA`, or `CW_TEST_QUIET=1` packaged), but for an unpackaged build's `CW_TEST_RUN_ON_CLOSE=1` (the `onclose` suite). With no command set anywhere, closing and quitting are as before. **The drain:** the command starts only after the workspace has closed (`WorkspaceService.close`) and Combwork has finished writing it (`closeCommand/drain.ts`): no write under way to its databases (`dbWrites.ts`: every board change, store save, lease and the stores' moves counted from the moment it is asked for, its wait for the board's lock included; `tests/dbWrites.test.ts` lists each such place and how it is counted), its board and journal closed, and no WAL checkpoint holding either file; woken as writes end, with no timer (Darren's decisions of 28 Oct ~14:15 and ~15:30): the close and drain are the panel's first step, *Waiting for <workspace> to finish saving…* with the spinner and **Skip the command**, which cancels the command, never the close: that workspace's command won't run, nor When Combwork quits, the drain's wait ends, and the panel (*Skipped: the command won't run…*) stays until Combwork's own close has finished. Combwork always finishes closing the workspace as before close commands: never cancelled, never begun again, one close per open (`CloseOp`). A close joined by another (a window's close, then a quit) has one saving step, brought up by the quit if the window's close had none. **Don't wait** is for a command once it runs. There is no seal: once the command starts, what the user does (reopening the workspace included) is theirs; the user guide says so. **Waited on:** Combwork starts `cw-close-runner.js` (Combwork's own executable as Node, detached and hidden, with no pipe to Combwork), which starts `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<command>"` in the workspace's folder (the user's home for When Combwork quits) with a session command's environment, reads its output as it comes (it never blocks on a full pipe), keeps only its last 64 KB, and writes `tail.txt` and `status.json` whole (temp and rename) at most every 250 ms in its run's own folder (`<userData>/close-commands/ws-<name>-<hash of its real place>-<time>-<random>` or `quit-…`, made exclusively, so neither same-named workspaces nor runs started in the same millisecond share one; the newest 5 of each workspace and of quit kept, never one still running or still starting: `runner.pid` keeps it until its first status). Combwork reads `status.json` and the last 16 KB of the tail about 4 times a second for the panel: the window dims with a spinner, *Running your close command…*, the command, the time so far, its last 8 lines (each at most 400 characters) and **Don't wait** (Combwork goes on; the command carries on, outliving Combwork if need be). Success closes the panel at once; a failure (an exit code, a command or runner that couldn't start, a runner gone before the command ended, the drain's bound) stays until **Close**. No timeout on the command. The switch opens the next workspace after it, the window closes after it, and a quit closes every window's workspace at once, each with its saving step (no timer; the user's Skip the command), runs each command in its window, then When Combwork quits in the last window used, then exits. When Combwork quits runs only once every workspace has closed and drained, whether it had a command of its own or not (one skipped for an update too): a close that failed means it doesn't run, its panel saying so; the user's Skip the command at a saving step means it doesn't run, quietly. A hidden window that runs one is shown, without the focus (never a quiet test copy's). The panel is keyboard-modal: Tab stays on its button, focus that leaves it comes back, no shortcut reaches the window behind, and Escape does nothing (never an implicit Don't wait). The settings rows save the command and the tick as one value, in order, never letting an older save's reply undo a newer edit. `combwork.log` notes each start, end (exit code, time, bytes of output) and a Don't wait.
- **Custom commands** (HI-1954, like JetBrains' External Tools; Darren's decisions of 28 and 29 Oct; design HI-1954/s15, s19, s21). HI-1368's single close and quit commands above became points' lists.
  - **Data** (`shared/commands.ts`, `shared/types.ts`): a `CustomCommand { id: 'c-<8 hex>', name, command, folder?, needed? }`. Combwork's commands and its point `onQuit` are `settings.commands` (`CommandsCombwork`); a workspace's commands and its points `onOpen` and `onClose` are `workspace.json` `commands` (`CommandsWorkspace`), in `.combwork`, which Combwork keeps out of version control, so a cloned repository brings none that run by themselves. A point is `{ run: CommandRef[], onUpdate? }`, a ref `{ scope: 'combwork' | 'workspace', id }`: a workspace's points may pick Combwork's commands, When Combwork quits only Combwork's. Saved cleaned (`cleanCombwork`, `cleanWorkspace`) through `commands:setCombwork` and `commands:setWorkspace`, the user's window only.
  - **Migration** (one way, at load, written with the next save): HI-1368's `general.onQuit` and `workspace.json` `onClose` become a command named "Quit command" or "Close command" and a point running it, their `onUpdate` kept. The id is `migratedId` (a hash of the text), so a load repeated before a save, or a file with both, adds nothing twice.
  - **Placeholders** (`fillCommand`): `{workspace}`, `{name}`, `{reason}` (`open | window | switch | quit | update | manual`) and `{project:<name>}`, filled as written (the user quotes, as HI-1368's contract). One that can't be filled, or a folder that isn't there, fails its step before anything runs; Settings warns beside a point's command that can't be filled there.
  - **One runner owns a list** (`main/closeCommand/listRunner.ts`, started by `cw-close-runner.js` as HI-1368's): `job.json` is a snapshot (the steps' templates and the placeholders' values as the run began), each attempt of a step run by `runJob` in a folder of its own. Its `status.json` keeps `state` and `runnerPid` as before, so pruning and HI-2007's carry read old and new runs alike, under HI-1368's prefixes; `KEEP_RUNS` is 10 per workspace (all points and by-hand runs) and for When Combwork quits.
  - **Choices on a failure:** while Combwork watches (it touches the run's `observer` every 5 s), a failed step waits for the dialog's Rerun, Skip it and continue or Stop here, written as `control-<step>-<attempt>.json` and taken once (renamed), so a stale or repeated choice does nothing; Combwork's IPC (`closeCommand:control`) checks the run, step and attempt too. Don't wait writes `control-detach.json`: the step under way isn't run again, and from then, or once the observer is 30 s stale (Combwork gone), a failed step that is `needed` ("The commands after this need it") stops the list, any other goes on. A launch that fails is the first step's failure with the same choices, Skip launching the rest.
  - **The dialog** (`CloseCommandPanel`): the point's commands in order, each waiting, running (time, command, last 8 lines; the command cut to two lines, whole in its tooltip: HI-2031), done, failed or skipped; Don't wait while one runs; Rerun, Skip it and continue and Stop here on a failure, Stop here leading (and Skip warned) when the step is `needed`; Close on a failure Combwork can't go past (its runner gone). Tab moves among its buttons; Escape does nothing.
  - **Open** (`openGate.ts`): the gate is reserved in `WorkspaceService.open` as `workspace.json` is read, before anything hears of the open, when `onOpen` has commands and this Combwork runs them; while it is held every start is refused at `sessions.assertStartsAllowed` ("This workspace's open commands are still running…", a conflict), and restart-resume treats the workspace as not ready. `runOpenCommands` (from `onOpened`) runs the list in the window; the gate settles once (`done | detached | stopped | closed`): the list ended, Don't wait, Stop here, or the open's lifetime ended (closed or switched: nothing it held starts).
  - **Close and quit** as HI-1368's (the saving step, then the list); **by hand** from the palette's **Run Command: <name>** and Settings' Run it now (`commands:run`), one step in the same dialog.
  - **Settings:** General → Commands and When Combwork quits, run; Workspace → Commands, When this workspace opens, run and When this workspace closes, run (`CommandsSettings.tsx`), each saved whole and in order. The settings tools read their names (`commandsSettingValue`) and never set them (sensitive).
  - **The Assistant** (decision 4, design s21): it may list and explain its workspace's and Combwork's commands and run one by hand when the user asks; every change it proposes (a new draft, an edit, a delete, a point's refs) is a proposal the user confirms, applied only if the scope's `commandsVersion` hasn't changed, whatever its Control level. Split to HI-2028 (Darren's r16, 29 Oct): until it lands, the Assistant has no access to them; the settings tools read their names only.
  - **Not mixed in** (decision 2): the workflow's check commands and the slot setup command stay Version Control → Workflow's.
- **Sleep** (`main/power.ts`, `shared/keepAwake.ts`): while any agent in any window (the Assistant too) is **working** or **waiting on background tasks**, Combwork holds `powerSaveBlocker.start('prevent-app-suspension')` (the screen may still turn off and lock) and releases it as soon as none is. **Settings → General → Keep the PC awake while agents work**: *When plugged in* (default; not on battery, `powerMonitor.isOnBatteryPower()`, re-checked on `on-ac` / `on-battery`), *Always, on battery too*, or *Never*. While it's held the status bar shows **Keeping the PC awake: n agents working** (click: Settings → General).
- **Windows shutting down** (shutdown, restart or sign-out): Windows' callbacks (a window's `query-session-end`, then `session-end`; `powerMonitor` `shutdown` elsewhere) don't wait for anything asynchronous, so Combwork backs up every running session's transcript before the callback returns: the transcript's bytes only (appended to the backup, or copied whole), no reading of usage or cost. It has 2 s at `query-session-end` and 1 s at `session-end` (which catches up with what was written since), well inside the ~5 s after which Windows offers to end an app, and never cancels the shutdown. It copies 1 MB at a time and starts nothing once its time is up; a step under way can't be cut short, so it can run over by about one disk write. Out of time, a whole copy is dropped (the backup stays as it was) and an append stops where it got to (a shorter backup that is still the transcript's start); sessions after it aren't tried. Every window gets these notices: one save covers them all. A shutdown another app cancels leaves nothing to undo. Best effort: a session whose transcript Combwork hasn't found yet keeps its last ordinary backup, and the log counts what was saved, incomplete, not tried or failed. An ordinary backup under way at the time doesn't undo it: appends write each byte at its own offset, and a whole copy is put in place only if the backup hasn't changed since it began, checked and renamed in one synchronous step (retries too), so no rename is left pending across the shutdown copy.
- **Waking up** (`powerMonitor` `resume`): each running session's transcript is read again (usage, background tasks and their time limit, plan usage from it) and its state reported; the workspaces refresh. Logged.
- **Attention inbox**: one list of the window's agents that need you, across its projects and the Assistant: agents **waiting** for input (a permission prompt), **needing sign-in**, with a **pending question** they work on beside (Codex's async question; *Asks: …*), all until answered, looked at or not (`asksYou()`), and agents **stopped by an error** until their next turn starts: a turn that ended on one (`LiveSessionState.failedTurn`, with what the CLI said, from a failed stop: Claude Code's `StopFailure` other than a refused sign-in, Copilot's unrecoverable `ErrorOccurred`, and its `session.error` of a query (`copilot.turnFailed.errorType`, HI-1960: a model call it gave up on after its retries, 1.0.105, whose `ErrorOccurred` hooks all say `recoverable: true`, the last too, and which sends no Stop; read from its `events.jsonl` as `LiveDetails.turnFailed`, and, as the descriptor's `failureEndsTurn` says, ending the running turn failed with Copilot's words, in order with the hooks; its next prompt clears it). Codex's Stop says nothing of a failure, so its rollout's `task_complete` with an error that is neither a refused sign-in nor a usage policy's stop (a safeguard's, #606) is read as one (#1658, `LiveDetails.turnFailed*`), and settled by the turn it names (`turn_id`, `failureTurn` against the turn ledger) and that turn's current run (one recorded before Combwork continued its Stop, or a new tool call reopened it, ended the work it went on from: it neither marks nor, by its record of the end, ends the continued work), never whichever turn is current, in order with the hooks: that turn over, marked; running, ended failed by its Stop or by the transcript's record of its end; a newer turn begun, dropped; not heard of yet, kept; consumed only once applied or dropped, never one from before the launch; and a turn marked failed keeps it through its own late Stop (only its next start clears it: a new turn, or Combwork continuing it); with no words from the CLI the window says *The turn ended on an error* in its own language, agents read it in English), the agent's status staying the turn's end (`finished`) so it is prompted and woken as any idle agent. Apart from them and never counted as a need (#1632: a count that includes finished agents trains you to ignore it), agents **finished, unseen** (`finishedUnseen()`). An agent is seen once its pane is on screen in a focused window: the selected project's panes on its Session tab (the page shown), or the Assistant's open panel. A finish on screen is seen as it happens; one in another project, on another page or tab, or while the window is unfocused or minimised stays unseen until its pane is shown. Main marks every finish and wait unseen and the window marks what it shows seen (`session:markSeen` with the agents' ids, from `agentsOnScreen()`), so main never needs to know what is on screen. Each agent's state records when it last changed (`statusSince`), and the list is oldest first, saying how long ago. Below it, **To review** (not counted): worktree agents that are stopped, ready or finished and have unmerged commits or uncommitted files, with a summary (*3 files, +120 −40 · 2 commits, 1 uncommitted file*; the diff from where the branch left the project folder's branch, tracked files only) and **Changes** and **Merge…**; one leaves once nothing is left to merge or when it starts working again. The list is worked out from each agent's live state and branch status (`shared/inbox.ts`), not tracked separately.
  - **Status bar** (#1632): **n need you** (with a bell, darker) counts things (HI-1931, Darren: "how many things wait for me"; `shared/needYou.ts`): each card with open requests (§16.8.5, `tasks:forYou`) once, however many it has, and each agent that needs you once; an agent stopped on a counted card (the asker of one of its requests, or working on or reviewing it) goes under that card, not counted again. Its tooltip says them, "2 cards and 1 agent need you". It opens the popover above the status bar: **Need you (n)**, the cards first, by their oldest request (a card with one request: the card and what it asks; with several, or an agent stopped on it: the card's row with "3 questions", then each request and agent under it, each opened on its own; a click opens the card) then the other agents, then **Finished (n)**, then **To review (n)**. Beside it, quieter, **✓ n finished** (the agents finished unseen; it opens the same popover); with nothing that needs you but work to review, **n to review**; hidden when all are empty. Each says what it counts on hover. An agent's row goes to its agent (the Assistant's opens its panel). Escape or a click outside closes it.
  - **Projects** in the activity bar shows the agents' count as a badge, and each project in the sidebar shows how many of its agents need you (a bell and the number; a badge on the compact rail's tile).
  - The **Notifications** bell (bottom of the activity bar; every notification its window showed, below, not the inbox) shows its dot and the accent (`--accent-on-activity`: the accent in dark, the stronger accent in light, at least 3:1 against the bar, kept on hover and focus) while any are unread, and tells assistive technology how many ("3 unread"); opening the panel (or Show Notifications) reads them, and only new ones light it again. The status bar is unaffected.
  - The Assistant's panel lists the same agents at its top (without itself).
- **Taskbar button** (per window, its own workspace's count: the status bar's *need you*, its cards and agents counted once each, #1632, HI-1931): a badge over Combwork's icon (`setOverlayIcon`, a red disc with the number, 9+ above 9, drawn by the window at its scale, with an accessible description) and the count before the window title, "(2) alpha — work — Combwork" (Alt+Tab, hover); none at 0. When an agent comes to ask you something (`asksYou()`: it starts **waiting for input**, or a question appears) while its window isn't focused, the button flashes (`flashFrame`) until the window is focused or closed, or the flash setting is turned off (which stops one under way); finishes never flash it. **Settings → Notifications → Show a count on the taskbar button** and **Flash the taskbar button when an agent needs input**, both on (`shared/taskbar.ts`, `main/taskbar.ts`).
- **Tray**: the icon shows an attention badge while any window's inbox has agents that need you. The menu lists them under **Need you (n)**, then **Finished (n)** (#1632: not counted with them), then **To review (n)**, across every window, oldest first, up to 10 each (then *and n more*); an item opens its agent in the window showing its workspace (`agent.show`). Below them, active projects with their status.
- **Notifications** (HI-2320, Darren's decisions of 2 Nov: "each event once in one place, the bell keeps everything, one pop-up system, Windows notifications only when unfocused; tips only when nothing else is going on"). Combwork tells the user something in exactly one way.
  - **One entry, one route** (`shared/notify.ts`, unit-tested in `tests/notify.test.ts`): every message is one entry (`ToastMessage`) of one **kind**: `needsYou` (an agent waiting for input, a question, a sign-in, a trust prompt, an untaken line, a card loop not watching, a card that needs you, the Assistant's question with its panel hidden, told by main), `finished` (bursts, below), `work` (a lane's events, safeguards and model switches, a missed line, nobody has your answer, the Assistant missed a request, a good moment to start fresh), `usage` (plan usage and usage moves), `warning` and `result` (Combwork's own messages by level: warning and error, info and success; the window's `notify()` and `cw_notify` too), `transcript` (a long conversation), `update`, `quit` (Combwork has closed) and `tip`. `notifyRoute()` gives `popup` (a pop-up in its window, kept in that window's bell), `windows` (a Windows notification, its bell row kept quietly), `bell` (the bell only) or `none`; first match wins: (1) `desktopNotifications` off: none for `needsYou`, `finished`, `work`, `usage` and `quit` (Combwork's own messages still pop up); (2) that kind off (`notifyOnFinished`, `notifyOnWaiting`): none; (3) no Combwork window focused (visible, not minimised): `windows` for those five kinds, else `popup`, which waits in its window (its clock paused, below); (4) a window focused: `quit` none (its windows are closing), `bell` for `needsYou`, `finished` and `work` left out by **Show pop-ups about agents for** (`bannerScope`: `all`, `workspace`, `project`, or `none`, only in the bell; an entry about no project passes every scope), else `popup`. "Off" means absent: no pop-up, no Windows notification, no bell row; the attention inbox, taskbar and tray still count the agent. The chime is not routed (it follows the chime settings, before routing). There is no *While Combwork is focused* any more: a Windows notification only ever comes with no Combwork window focused.
  - **One way in, one owner** (`main/notify.ts` `tell()`; main's `toast()` goes through it): routed once, logged with why (`Notice <kind> told: <route> (<why>)`, so a late or missing one can be traced from Copy Diagnostics), and sent with `emitTo` to its one **owner window**: for Combwork's own result or warning made while serving a window's IPC request, that window, even if another has the focus by then (HI-2355: `ipc.ts` `requestingWindow`, from the request's `senderStore`; agents' kinds never follow a request, whose context can carry into later callbacks); otherwise the window in use, whatever workspace it shows (a click opens the target where it is, `notice:target`/`notice:action`); with none focused, the window showing the entry's workspace (or a `source` path's), else the last focused. Its pop-up and its bell row live there only. A Windows notification is one exclusive branch (`showOsNotification`, so quiet test copies only log it to `CW_TEST_NOTIFY_LOG`, which records each entry too: `{ kind: 'entry', id, notifyKind, route, owner }`); its click shows the owner window and opens the target. The entry id is the dedup boundary (`pushToast` replaces by id); window-made entries (`notify()`, `pushToast()`) are owned by the window that made them and always pop up. The Agent API's `notice` event keeps its shape, sent from `tell()` for the five kinds above (`windows: true` when it went to Windows); `notice-resolved` as before. Each event is told once: a long conversation is one `transcript` entry (it was a toast and a routed copy), plan usage and usage moves one `usage` entry (a bell-only toast and a routed copy), and the four tip moments wait behind the quiet rule (below), so a tip never comes beside the notice it is about.
  - **One pop-up system** (`components/Popups.tsx`): notifications and the tip in one stack, one look (icon, title, message, buttons, ×, the target's chevron; kind and level by colour: `needsYou` the accent, warning amber, error red, a tip the quietest), at **Pop-up position** (`bannerPosition`, six places, **bottom right** by default: `CornerPlacement` keeps it left of the Assistant's panel and above a pane's ended bar). The newest nearest the edge, four shown, then **+N more** (`keepPopups`: one that stays is never pushed out). A pop-up closes after **`bannerSeconds`** (6), one with live buttons or an error after at least 15 s, its own `timeoutMs` first (an Undo's, an offer's) until it is resolved, then `bannerSeconds` again from then to read what happened (HI-2370); the clock pauses while hovered, while it holds the keyboard focus, while its button runs, and while its window isn't focused. One that needs you stays until clicked, dismissed or answered (`waitingBannerStays`). Keyboard: its text is the target's button, then its buttons, then ×; Escape with the focus in it closes it. `alert` for `needsYou` and errors, `status` otherwise.
  - **The bell keeps everything** (the Notifications panel, `NotificationCenter`): every entry its window showed or told quietly, every kind but tips (Help → Tips… lists them), newest first, 100, in memory; *Clear all* empties it and the window's pop-ups with it (HI-2354: the tip is left as it is). **Closing it** (HI-2376, the Assistant's call of 2 Nov): its ×, a link in it, Show Notifications again (Ctrl+Alt+U toggles it, as the bell does), or Escape, unless a handler took the key (a shortcut being recorded, a pop-up with the focus), a dialog is open, or the focus is in a field, a terminal or an editor, which use Escape themselves. Pop-ups give way to it while it is open (each still goes into its list, newest at the top); the result of the user's own action gets no exception (HI-2373). Each links to its subject (`target`: an agent opens its pane, a card its dialog, a project (new) shows it; Combwork-wide ones have none) and shows its buttons while unresolved. The attention inbox stays the live list of who needs you now.
  - **Buttons, live while they apply** (Darren's decision of 2 Nov ~08:25). An entry's buttons act on an **offer**: main registers the entry under the offer's own identity (`offer`, e.g. `ask:<project>#<agent>#<n>` per ask, `leftovers:<agent>#<runs>`, `bg:`, `lock:<key>#<seq>`, `transcript:<agent>#<session>`, `update:<version>`, `slot:<run>`, `platform:<path>`, `names:<workspace>`, `lastrun:`, `restart:`, `modes:<n>`), and `resolveOffer()` emits `toast-resolved { ids, outcome }` for exactly that offer's entries, so an older offer's completion never touches a newer one; the windows drop the buttons and show the outcome in their place (`main/outcomes.ts`). An offer resolves when its action is done (*Ended 3 processes*, *Answered*, *Released*, *Stopped and resumed here*, Resume's report, Switch Now's result, the Undo's *Brought back n cards*) or when its condition ends without a click (the agent no longer asks, the leftovers ended or changed, the conversation ended or moved, the ask let go, the slot released another way, the update no longer the one ready, the names no longer shared, the platform settled). Each button carries its offer through its command and IPC, and its handler acts for that offer only (a stale click resolves its own entry and changes nothing). A click runs the command awaited, its button's spinner until it has finished (`runEntryAction`; an entry about a project runs in the window that has it, `notice:action`, which waits for that window's own `notice:actionDone`, at most 30 s and cancelled if that window reloads, its renderer goes or it closes: then the entry says *Didn't finish: try again* and keeps its buttons, never passing for done), and main checks again before acting: **End Them / Keep Running** (`settleOffer`) read each listed launch again from the job itself (never the kept list) and act only when it still has exactly the processes shown, by **id and start time**, and none beyond them; End Them then ends exactly the processes the notice showed, frozen as it showed them (pid and start time, never read back from the kept list, which a poll may change during the click), each only while it is that process, never the whole job, so one started since is never touched, and what is left stays listed; a notice that couldn't list them all, or a changed list, ends nothing and says so, pointing to the pane's ⋯; the reconciler leaves an offer alone while its own action runs, so the entry says what was really done. Stop It and Resume acts only while its offer is open and the agent isn't running, checked again after each wait before it stops or starts anything, and its entry resolves once the agent runs again (its conversation here, or another); Allow answers only its own ask (its sequence); Restart and Update checks the downloaded version is still the one offered, and its entry says *Installing* only once the quit goes ahead (`markInstalling()` from `quitNow`; HI-2425: a quit cancelled in its dialog, or a Quit when agents finish cancelled, leaves the button); Release Slot… re-reads the holders; Switch Now carries the mode it offered each agent: a newer offer for one of them supersedes it (*Settings changed since: nothing switched*), and a click does nothing and says so if the settings no longer name that mode, checked again at the switch; Hand Over to… only for its own conversation (`session:handOverOffer`), then `mayHandOverNow`. An entry with independent buttons (the unexpected close's Resume All and Stop Them) drops each as it is done (`toast-update`: the button goes, a note says what it did), and is resolved once none is left. Other conditions are checked when clicked rather than watched (the Assistant's scope for round 3; whether more go live is Darren's call). Window-made entries with a condition of the window's (`EntryCondition`: an MCP offer) are re-checked by `renderer/entryConditions.ts`, the Antivirus suggestion settles once a status read shows no folder scanned, and an archive's Undo says what its own action did (*Brought back n cards*), main checking each card, refused in a window showing another workspace; a button that only goes somewhere (Show, Open, Review…, Start Fresh (Idle Agents)…) stays, and an entry whose agent, project or card has since gone says so. The Assistant's question with its panel hidden is told by main (`assistant:tellQuestion`, once per question, `aq:<id>`), so it is routed like any agent that needs you and resolved once the question no longer waits. A failure keeps the buttons and is its own notice. `forgetOwner` lets a closed window's offers go; the registry keeps at most 300.
  - **Bursts** (`shared/bursts.ts`): finishes are collected and told together once none has come for 3 s (at most 10 s after the first): one alone reads as before ("web · Claude finished" and its last message); several in one project "3 agents finished in web" naming them ("Claude, Codex, Agent 3"); across projects "3 agents finished" with "web (2), api (1)". When the group is shown, each finish is checked again (`noticeRoute()`, the same check as when it came): one turned off meanwhile is left out, nothing is shown if none is left (a finish whose agent starts its next turn before it is told, HI-2312, is taken out of the group then: its status going from its turn's end to working, starting or waiting, as when Combwork's delivery typed at its turn's end starts one. Told later, the notice would arrive as the agent works again, with the last turn's message; it isn't told whatever that next turn ends as, which is told as any turn's end is); the rest go as one entry, a pop-up in the window then in use or one Windows notification, as things are then; those the scope leaves out go to the bell as a group of their own. Clicking it shows the (first remaining) project. Each notice told, or not told, is logged with its route and why (`noticeRouteWhy()`), so a late or missing one can be traced in Help → Copy Diagnostics. **Waiting for input** is never grouped or delayed: it is told at once, on its own, with its chime, once per need: when the agent starts waiting, or a pending question appears while it isn't (*<agent> has a question for you*). A wait that turns out to be a question already told, or the same prompt reported again, isn't told twice. The rules are in `main/hookStatus.ts` (pure, unit-tested per provider), which learns who is asked from the CLI's hooks or, for Codex, its title (§6.4); each change of whether an agent needs you is logged at debug level with its cause (a hook's name or the title), never what was asked.
  - **Waiting for input** is never grouped or delayed: it is told at once, on its own, with its chime, once per need: when the agent starts waiting, or a pending question appears while it isn't (*<agent> has a question for you*). A wait that turns out to be a question already told, or the same prompt reported again, isn't told twice. The rules are in `main/hookStatus.ts` (pure, unit-tested per provider), which learns who is asked from the CLI's hooks or, for Codex, its title (§6.4); each change of whether an agent needs you is logged at debug level with its cause (a hook's name or the title), never what was asked.
  - **Tips** use the same stack, as its quietest style, and only when nothing else goes on (`quietNow`, `shared/tips.ts`): the window focused, no pop-up showing or queued in it (those behind +N more and those paused included), no finishes waiting to be told together (`notify-pending`), no agent of the window waiting for the user, and no key pressed in it for 10 s (`TYPING_QUIET_MS`, a capture-phase `keydown` listener). The day's tip and a moment's tip are queued (a moment's takes the day's place) and tried again on each of those changes, on focus, and every 5 s while queued; one still queued when its local day ends is dropped (the day's tip records its day only once shown, so it is tried at the next start; a moment only once its tip shows). Any notification arriving closes a tip showing.
  - **Settings → Notifications** (config version 9 migrates): `whileFocused` is gone (Show nothing becomes **Show pop-ups about agents for: None (only in the bell)**, which keeps the Windows notifications in the background; a Windows notification while focused becomes a pop-up); **Pop-up position** (top centre, the banners' old default, moves to bottom right; any other place is kept), **Pop-ups close after (seconds)**, **Pop-ups for an agent waiting for you stay until handled**; the master switch, the per-kind switches, the chime, the taskbar count and flash and Suggest a fresh start are unchanged.
- Chime synthesised in-app (several styles, volume), global on/off with per-project override. A window plays at most one chime every 2 seconds, so agents finishing together chime once.
- **A notice's target** (HI-1961): `cw_notify` (`POST /v1/notify`) takes an optional `target`, an agent (`{ agent, project }`, its name or id; project defaults to the calling agent's, and the Assistant and scripts name it) or a card (`{ card }`, its key), at most one; one that isn't there is refused (404), both at once 400. Main resolves it when the notice is made (`ToastMessage.target`: the agent's project folder, id and names, or the card's number, key, project and workspace: a card's number is its workspace's alone, so a notice kept from one workspace, clicked after its window moved to another, never opens that board's card of the same number) and the reply says what a click opens (`opens`). The toast's text and its row in the Notifications panel are then a button (`ToastText`: the text as written, a trailing chevron, the pointer and a hover background, its tooltip "Open HB4's pane" or "Open HI-12"; the Assistant's change on its screenshots, so a plain notice, which has none of these, doesn't look the same): a click opens the agent's pane (`agent.show`'s steps) or the card's dialog in this window when it has the agent's project or the card's workspace, else in the window that has it (`notice:target`, which runs the internal command `notice.openTarget` there), else back in this one; an agent removed, a card deleted, or a card whose workspace no window has gives a short notice instead ("WB4 isn't in web any more", "HI-12 isn't on the board any more", "HI-12 is on work's board, which isn't open"). A notice is not a change: Settings → Assistant → Control leaves `cw_notify` to every level. The coordinate-agents skill has the Assistant give the target in a notice about a waiting agent.

## 15. Resolved decisions

1. `<Workspace>/.combwork/` is committed.
2. Archived transcripts are preserved until the user deletes the session. Non-archived sessions are backed up too.
3. Skills/MCP must be deployed to the workspace before a project can use them. Project-only MCP servers are disabled until copied.
4. Permission mode: global default Auto (Manual until 0.1.0 development), per-project and per-agent override, bypass behind an opt-in setting.
5. Machine and Local skills are always on and read-only in Combwork.
6. The standalone Claude Code CLI is mandatory; editor-extension copies are not supported.
7. Pasted and dropped files are attachments: passed to the agent as paths, images and files from outside the agent's folder copied into the project's `.combwork/attachments` (by session) first, so each is kept and tied to the point in the transcript where it was sent (§ Attachments).
8. Deleting from the Files and Attachments tabs moves items to the Recycle Bin; Combwork never deletes project files permanently. Attachments are never removed automatically; Clean Up and Purge never remove a card's (HI-1700). A test copy of Combwork moves them into its own trash folder instead (`CW_TEST_TRASH_DIR`, `trash.ts`) and starts with tips off (`CW_TEST_TIPS=off`): every unpackaged build with them, and a packaged one only when a test started it quiet (`CW_TEST_QUIET=1`, `takesTestSeams`, #1599), as it already writes `CW_TEST_NOTIFY_LOG` (#1253). The installed app is never started quiet, so it always uses the Recycle Bin and the user's tip setting.
9. Transcripts are read-only in Combwork: the Sessions tab shows and exports them but never edits them. Claude Code owns the file and only ever appends to it.
10. Up to twelve agents per project, up to 24 with its Maximum agents raised (#562, HI-2001, HI-2058) (a page holding as many as the layout has panes), each in the project folder or its own Combwork-managed git worktree (Combwork creates, merges and removes worktrees itself rather than using Claude Code's `--worktree`, because the worktree must outlive sessions).
11. Agents sharing a folder are protected by Combwork-enforced per-file locks (Block by default). Concurrent changes to shared config and memory are a documented risk, not prevented.
12. Worktrees live next to the workspace (`<Workspace>.worktrees/<Project>/<agent>`). New worktrees get `.env*` copied by default and an optional per-project setup command. Merging defaults to a merge commit (`--no-ff`), and the worktree, branch and agent are kept unless **Remove** is ticked, so one agent can merge task after task; a squash that keeps the worktree moves the branch to the merged branch afterwards (ticked by default).
13. Combwork is open source under the **MIT License** (`LICENSE`, © 2026 Darren Marshall). Everything it ships is under permissive licences (mostly MIT and ISC; DOMPurify MPL-2.0 or Apache-2.0; codicons CC-BY-4.0; sax BlueOak-1.0.0; argparse Python-2.0); `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists them with full texts and is regenerated by `scripts/licenses.mjs` on every build. Each package links to its repository as an `https://` page, whatever form its `repository` takes (owner/repo, `github:`/`gitlab:`/`bitbucket:`/`gist:`, `git@host:…`, `ssh://`, `git+…`; `repoWebUrl`, #788), else to its homepage when that is a web page, else to nothing. Electron's and Chromium's licences ship in the install folder (electron-builder adds `LICENSE.electron.txt` and `LICENSES.chromium.html`). The installer's NSIS plug-ins are listed there too; WinShell (freeware, by an NSIS maintainer, with no licence text) is kept with attribution, and electron-builder's `elevate.exe` isn't shipped (`packElevateHelper: false`: a per-user install's updates never need administrator rights) (#385).
14. Combwork updates itself from GitHub Releases with electron-updater: checked and downloaded automatically by default, installed only when Combwork quits or with Restart and Update (or only manually, by setting), never while it runs.
15. The permission mode of a running session is switched live (Shift+Tab driven by Combwork, confirmed from the footer), not by restarting; settings changes are offered to running agents, never forced.
16. Every command's shortcut is configurable globally, and project and session commands per project.
17. Providers: Claude Code and Codex, chosen per agent, so a project can mix them; each CLI's own terminal UI is shown (Combwork doesn't draw conversations). The framework is built for more providers.
18. Workspace skills and MCP servers are shared by every provider; user-level MCP servers load for none, and a project's own servers follow the same rule for each CLI.
19. Fresh installs start with every provider disabled; upgrades from 0.1 keep Claude Code enabled. No enabled provider is a valid state.
20. Codex defaults to Approve for me; Full access is opt-in like Bypass. Combwork drives Codex's `/permissions` menu for live changes.
21. Cost for providers that don't report it is estimated from a shipped, user-editable price table and always marked as an estimate. Each provider's table carries the date it was last checked against the published prices (`PRICES_CHECKED`), and a model with no published price (Codex's `codex-auto-review`) has no row. Tokens with no price are never $0: a session or day with none priced is **Unknown**, and one priced only in part (a model with no price beside priced ones, HI-2675: `costUnpriced`) shows its known part with **+ ?**, and counts as without a price in totals too. So does a row whose known charge leaves tokens with no price, and a running session's cost (its footer, Running now, its session card): a session on more than one model is priced a model at a time from its rows, as the history prices it, and its live state carries `costUnpriced`.
22. Conversations never move between providers: a resume reopens one in the provider that recorded it, whatever its agent runs now (#506); **Hand Over to…** moves work through a handover. Projects that mix providers can share one `AGENTS.md`, imported by `CLAUDE.md`.
23. Agents are all equal and a project starts with none; the provider is stored on each agent. Upgrading from 0.1 clears existing agents (their sessions stay).
24. Combwork keeps a last good copy of its own JSON files and never silently replaces a damaged one.

**Status:** the 1.0 design, written in P1 (#1117, 20 Oct 2026) for the builders of P2–P8. It describes what 1.0
builds on the `1.0.0` branch; the rest of this spec describes 0.9.x as built, and each phase updates the sections it
changes (§8, §6.6, §12, §13) as it merges. Where this section and an older one disagree about 1.0, this one wins.

then the shared note's decisions; then the phase cards' comments (the Assistant's carry-overs); then this spec's own

**Reading order for a phase's builder:** §16.1 (principles), §16.2 (the model), then your phase's sections (the table
in §16.19), §16.18 (the scenarios your phase must pass) and §16.20 (open points that touch you).

### 16.1 Principles

1. **Facts, not claims** [note §3, #1112 E]. A card's stage comes from facts Combwork recorded or observed: revisions,
   check runs, verdicts, approvals and merges. An agent asks for a move with an intent; Combwork's rules decide and move
   the card. A lane's merge commit, a verdict's revision and a Done are never an agent's say-so.
2. **The work owns the branch** [note §3, #1123]. A card (or a lane) owns its branch and borrows a slot; agents are
   sessions attached to the work, never owners of a folder.
3. **A verdict is tied to a revision** [#1112 B]. A review covers the whole change (from the card's base to its
   revision). Combwork always stores the exact revision; by default an approval carries over to a later revision that is
   the same change.
4. **Options, not a workflow editor** [#1112 UI, D]. The user picks the version control and sets outcome-worded
   options (or a preset). The options compile into stages and rules from a fixed library of pieces written and tested
   in code. Users never see or edit a template.
5. **Every refusal is an instruction** [note §3]: it names the rule, the next step and where the rule is changed.
6. **Overrides are explicit and recorded** [note §3, #1120]: the user always, the Assistant within Control, agents
   never; the reason goes on the card, and the card and lane show it.
7. **Work done outside Combwork counts** [#1112 C]. A commit or merge made in a terminal or another tool is observed and
   reconciled; the rules never fight it.
8. **It scales fully down** [#1112 down]. With Git, every check and balance can be off; several agents can build in
   the project folder with no worktrees. *Off is really off*: only data-safety protections stay (§16.6.4).
9. **Without the Assistant** [#1117 solo]. Everything here works with the Assistant turned off: gates, the merge
   queue, lanes (started from the window), slots, overrides and questions to the user. The Assistant is a convenience
   on top.
10. **Every gate and override has an off switch** [#966, #737's principle, note §3]. For the workflow, the off switch
    of a rule is its option; a few rules can't be switched off on their own because others depend on them (no
    self-review while a reviewer is required, a verdict naming its submission, a duplicate submission),
    and for those **the user's override is the switch** (§16.8.4) [HB3's round 1 finding 18]. For Combwork's overrides of
    the CLIs, a setting in Advanced (§16.15).
11. **Clean cut-over** [#1112 plan]. No warn-mode period: on upgrade every project moves to the layer, with options
    that match how it works today (§16.17).
12. **The skills describe, Combwork enforces** [note §3, #1124]. Once a rule is a gate, guidance only explains it (P8).

### 16.2 The model in one page

Five layers [note "Core model v2"], from the bottom:

1. **Platform** (§16.3): where the content lives (None or Git now; Jujutsu and Mercurial later). It declares
   **capabilities** and answers facts about the content.
2. **Facts** (§16.4): a typed, append-only log per card, recorded by Combwork or observed from the platform.
3. **Workflow** (§16.5, §16.6): the project's options, compiled into a **ruleset**: stages (in six fixed
   categories), and for every move the guards that must hold and the actions Combwork then takes.
4. **Roles** (§16.10.6): builder, reviewer, either, generalist (HI-686) and independent (HI-2670) for agents; approver (the user); integrator (Combwork).
5. **Runtime** (§16.7, §16.8): intents from agents and moves from the user pass through one place
   (`tasks.ts` → `boardWrite`); guards are evaluated there; the card's stage is derived from its facts; observed
   facts that contradict recorded ones are reconciled.

```
 agent ──intent──▶ Agent API ──▶ workflow runtime ──guards──▶ boardWrite (one transaction:
 user  ──move────▶ IPC        ─┘        ▲   │                   fact rows + card stage cache)
                                        │   └─actions──▶ platform adapter (git / none)
 platform watcher ──observed facts──────┘                merge queue, slots, wakes
```

### 16.3 Platform layer

#### 16.3.1 Capabilities

A platform is a descriptor (shared, pure) and an adapter (main), in a registry, mirroring providers (§10) [note §4].
The descriptor lists the platform's **capabilities**; an option that needs a capability the platform lacks isn't
offered, and its row says why [#1112 plan, note "Core model v2"].

| Capability | Question it answers / operation | Git | None |
|---|---|---|---|
| **revisions** | Name an exact state of the work; read the current one; say whether it is **ready** (no unresolved conflicts stored in it, nothing pending to snapshot). | A commit id (`rev-parse HEAD` in the card's folder); always ready (git can't commit unresolved conflicts). | A content hash of the card's deliverables (§16.3.3); ready unless a deliverable has conflict markers the check option names. |
| **isolation** | Parallel working folders for cards. | Worktrees: slots (§16.10). | Not in 1.0 (OP-16): everyone works in the project folder. |
| **integration** | Combine an approved change into the target, and **advance the target atomically**: move it from an expected revision to the result, or fail without changing it. | Merge (merge commit or squash) by Combwork's merge queue (§16.9) or the agent; the target is a branch, advanced with compare-and-swap (§16.9.2). | **Acceptance**: an approved revision is recorded as accepted; nothing is copied (OP-16). |
| **containment** | Is revision R (or its change) in target T? | Ancestor of the target, or a target commit with the same change (a squash) (§16.3.4). | R has an Accepted fact. |
| **sameness** | Is R2 the same change as R1? | Replay equivalence: replaying the reviewed change onto the new base gives exactly the new tree (§16.3.2; patch-id as a first test, OP-33). | Same hash (any edit is a new revision) [#1112 B]. |
| **authorship** | Who made the change? | Combwork's records of which agent worked the card, plus each commit's author identity (§16.3.4). | Combwork's records (edits attributed by hooks and file locks). |
| **observe** | Tell Combwork when the content changes outside an intent. | Watch the repository's refs and HEAD (§16.4.4). | Watch the deliverables (the Files tab's watcher). |

Every adapter answer is a value or **unknown** (git missing, a failed read, a folder gone). **Unknown never satisfies
a rule** [P1, following §8's "fail safe"]: a gate whose fact is unknown refuses, saying what couldn't be read and the
fix (Provider Setup, Retry).

The adapter's interface (P2 proves it, P3 builds it; names are the builders'):

```ts
interface PlatformDescriptor { id: 'none' | 'git'; capabilities: Capability[]; revisionShort(id: string): string }
interface PlatformAdapter {
  detect(folder): Detection                               // §16.3.5
  head(where: Folder): Revision | Unknown                 // revisions: reads without side effects (no snapshot)
  snapshot?(where: Folder): Revision | Unknown            // platforms that record the working copy (jj): explicit, at submit
  readiness(rev: Revision): Ready | Conflicted(files) | Unknown
  dirty(where: Folder, paths?: string[]): Dirty | Unknown // the folder's uncommitted state, optionally only some paths
  change(base: Revision, head: Revision): Change | Unknown // files changed, candidate key (sameness is a replay, §16.3.2)
  contains(target: Target, rev: Revision, change?: Change): Containment | Unknown
  authors(change: Change): Author[] | Unknown
  isolate?(card, line, base): Folder; release?(folder)    // isolation (slots, §16.10)
  testIntegrate?(target, rev, style): TestResult          // integration (§16.9)
  advance?(target, expected: Revision, result: Revision): Advanced | Moved(actual) | Unknown  // atomic, never partial
  observe(onChange): Disposable
}
```

Platform words stay out of the facts: a card works on a **line** (Git branch, jj or hg bookmark), integrates into a
**target** (a line), and integration produces a **result revision** (a merge commit in Git, a rebased commit in jj).

All Git calls go through the `git()` runner (`src/main/git.ts:47`); the two bypasses move onto it in P3:
`checkGit`'s `git --version` (`gitTool.ts:57`) and `excludeCopies`'s `rev-parse --git-common-dir`
(`providers/common.ts:344`) [#1119]. SPEC §8's "Git only" is retired: Git is the first platform [#1112 plan].

#### 16.3.2 Git adapter

- **Revision:** the commit id of HEAD in the card's folder (its slot, or the project folder). Shown as 7 characters.
- **The card's line and base.** With slots, each card has its own branch, created at start from the target's head
  (`prepareSlot`), so its **base** is that head, stored in `Started`. A lane's next card gets a new branch from the
  target's head when it starts, in the lane's slot, once the previous card is Done (§16.11.2): cards of a lane are
  separate changes, reviewed and merged one by one, and card 2's review never includes card 1's work. Work that needs an earlier card waits for it (`blockedBy`,
  G14: merged first). A lane-wide cumulative branch is not a 1.0 mode (OP-34) [P1]. Branch names whose title gives an
  empty slug (no ASCII letters) are just the key: `cw/AM/AM-12`.
- **The change** of a card is the whole diff from a **base** to its revision (decision B: the change, not single
  commits). Its endpoints are **fixed when submitted**: `Submitted` stores `base` (the merge base with the target at
  that moment, `git merge-base <target> <head>`) and `head`, and the change's keys and files are computed from those
  two revisions and stored. Later reads never recompute a submitted change from the target's current state, so a
  target that moves, contains the change already, or is rewritten doesn't alter what was reviewed [P1, answering
  HR2's round 1 finding 3]. **Files changed** per revision (`git diff --name-status -z <base> <head>`) are part of the
  Submitted fact (#945) [#1119 c].
- **Same change: replay equivalence** (sameness) [OP-33; P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 4 and round 2 finding 3].
  A pass on revision R1 (base B1) carries over to a later revision R2 (base B2) only if **replaying R1's change onto
  B2 with git's own three-way merge gives exactly R2's tree**: `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<B1> <B2> <R1>`
  succeeds without conflicts and its tree id equals `<R2>^{tree}`. Trees are compared whole, so whitespace, file modes,
  binaries and *where* in a file a change lands all count: changing the first of two identical blocks is not the same
  change as changing the second, because the replay puts R1's edit where git's merge places it, and R2's tree differs.
  If B2 is B1, it reduces to "the same tree". Anything the replay can't settle (a conflict, a merge base that can't be
  read, an object gone) is **not** the same change: the pass goes stale (unknown never carries over).
  - **Candidate key:** `git patch-id --stable` of the whole change **with no context lines** (`git diff -U0 <base>
    <head>`), stored with each submission, is a cheap first test only: different patch-ids mean a different change at
    once; equal ones go on to the replay. patch-id alone ignores whitespace (HR2's probe: two patches differing only in
    Python indentation share an id), and a hash of the changed lines without their positions can't tell repeated
    blocks apart (HR2's round 2 finding 3), so neither decides on its own. **Why no context** [P2]: patch-id hashes
    the context lines too, so with git's default three a clean rebase onto a target that changed a line within three
    lines of the card's gets another patch-id, and the first test would call it another change (the spike's
    `gitAdapter` test shows it); without context the key changes only with the lines the change adds and removes.
  - **Why replay:** it is the correspondence a rebase itself uses, so a clean rebase or a squash of an unchanged
    change passes (decision B's intent), and a conflict resolution that yields exactly the replayed tree passes
    because the merged content is then exactly what the replay of the reviewed change produces. The replay is of the
    **whole change**, so this is a rebase that conflicted **commit by commit** (an early commit touching a line the
    target changed, a later one taking it back) and was resolved to the whole change's replay; when the whole
    change's replay itself conflicts, there is no replayed tree, and nothing carries over [P2]. With "Exact revision
    only" (G4), only R2 = R1 carries over.
  - **Stored per submission:** base, head, the candidate key and the changed files, so later comparisons use the
    reviewed endpoints, never the target's current state.
  An empty change (head = base, or an empty tree diff) has no key, and submitting it is refused ("nothing to review")
  unless the card is no-code [P1].
- **Containment,** in order: `merge-base --is-ancestor <rev> <target>` (a merge, or a fast-forward); else a commit C on
  the target since the card's base whose parent P replays the change exactly (`merge-tree --merge-base=<base> <P>
  <rev>` gives C's tree: a squash, or a cherry-pick of the whole change; patch-id narrows which commits to try); else
  the existing whole-target test (`alreadyMerged`, `worktrees.ts:417`) for a squash split across commits. The first
  that answers yes says how (`method: merge | fast-forward | squash | same-tree`) [P1, extending `branchWatch`'s
  detection]. Containment reads stored endpoints and pinned revisions (§16.9.3), so it still answers after the card's
  line is deleted. **What is kept between passes** (HI-2182, HI-2189): a merge or fast-forward is the history's alone,
  kept for the revision and the target's head. A squash or same-tree answer goes through git's diff and merge, which
  attributes, config and drivers can change: a found one is never kept, and a **not found** is kept for **30 s** from
  when git computed it (never extended by being used; an answer that took longer isn't kept), for the same repository,
  folder, git, target, target head, base, revision and key, and never from a git the merge queue's host runs. So a new
  commit on the target or the card is looked at once, while a change only to attributes or config, with the same
  commits, can take up to 30 s to count for every caller (an outside merge found, a merged line deleted, a slot
  released), and for those 30 s a git that would now fail isn't asked. The user's decision (HI-2189, B).
- **Shared-folder cards** (G11 = the project folder: agents commit on the folder's line, often the target itself)
  [P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 1, round 2 finding 2 and HB3's findings 5, F, G]:
  - **Attribution is recorded once, when a commit is seen,** and never recomputed: Combwork writes `CommitAttributed`
    (commit, card, how) for each new commit on the folder's line. The rule, in order: a commit whose message carries a
    card's trailer (`Combwork-Card: AM-12`, §16.12, OP-14) is that card's; otherwise, if exactly one card of the folder is
    **unfinished** (Active, Review or Approved: not just Active) it is that card's (`how: only card`); otherwise it
    belongs to no card (`how: unattributed`) and is listed in the Version Control tab for the user to assign or leave.
    Combwork keeps the last head it attributed up to per folder line; the first look starts from the oldest `Started.base`
    of the folder's unfinished cards, so commits from before any card started are nobody's [P2].
    The folder's line is its first-parent history (HI-2382, Darren's decision): a branch merged into it (another line,
    the target merged into main) brings in commits that stay with their own cards and are never attributed in the
    folder, while the merge commit itself is one of the line's and is attributed by the rule above (its trailer, else
    the only unfinished card).
    New commits are attributed in batches of at most 100, each batch one transaction (its records, the cards' facts
    and the folder's cursor) with the folder's cards checked once under its lock, and main's thread given back between
    batches (HI-2379: a merge bringing 3,536 commits into the line, one transaction each, held it for 40 s).
    So A entering Review never hands A's commits to B: they were attributed when made, and a commit made while A and
    B are both unfinished needs a trailer.
  - **A card's change** is the ordered list of its attributed commits. With one card unfinished since its start, that
    list is exactly `base..HEAD`, and Combwork uses that range as a shortcut. With several, the change is the combined
    diff of its own commits applied in order (sameness: each commit replays, §16.3.2); containment needs every one.
  - **Two revisions, kept apart:** the card's **revision** (what is submitted and what a verdict names) is its newest
    attributed commit, which needn't be the folder's head; a **tested checkout** is the revision a check or a review
    copy actually had (§16.13). Submit takes the card's revision, not the folder's head (§16.8.1's "must equal the
    head" applies only to a card with its own line).
  - `submit.trailer` holds when an unfinished other card shares the folder and the agent's commits since its last
    submission include one attributed to no card, with the fix `git commit --amend --trailer "Combwork-Card: AM-12"` for
    the newest commit, or a non-interactive `git rebase --exec` for older ones (not on the target line itself once
    other agents' commits follow: then the user assigns it in the tab). Only commits made since the card started and
    still on the folder's line count (HI-2562: one an amend replaced is not), and the refusal names the newest. It
    gives the amend only when that commit is the folder's head; with commits after it (another card's among them), an
    amend would rewrite the head instead and a rebase others' work, so it tells the agent to do neither and report it
    with `cw_cannot_within_rules`, for the user to decide (HR1's HI-2562 round 1). A card
    with no commit of its own but such a commit gets this refusal, not `submit.empty`, whatever the rules hold (with
    every rule off too, where the submit would be refused as empty): its work is most likely that commit, made without
    the trailer.
  - **Review and checks see the folder as it is:** a review copy at the card's revision contains other cards' earlier
    commits, and a check run on it tests them too; the reviewer reviews the card's own commits (their diff is what
    `start review` lists). The option's description says so; slots are the answer when that matters.
  - When the folder's line is the card's target, its commits are **working revisions**, not integrations: they are on
    the target by construction, and Done waits for the card's rules (review, approval) instead (§16.4.4, §16.7.2).
- **Dirty:** `git status --porcelain=v2 -z` (already `--no-optional-locks`, §8), tracked changes and untracked files
  that aren't ignored. In a shared folder only the paths the agent holds or held file locks on since the card started
  count; others' changes are listed as "not yours" and don't refuse [P1, from #1112 down's "commit only your own
  changes"].
- **Readiness:** a Git commit can't store unresolved conflicts, so a revision is always ready; a folder mid-merge,
  mid-rebase or with conflict markers staged is dirty.
- **Authorship:** for no-self-review, the agents Combwork recorded working the card (Started, Submitted, build holds), not
  the commit author, since agents often share one identity [P1]. For the identity rule, each commit's author email
  (`%ae`) against the project's identity (§16.6.2, G12).
- **Observe:** a watcher on the repository's `HEAD`, `refs/heads`, `packed-refs` and `logs/HEAD` (common git dir and
  each worktree's), debounced, plus today's minute refresh and window focus (§8). Events are reconciled (§16.4.4).
  The watcher also records, per folder, every write to a tracked file and every HEAD reflog entry, which checks use to
  prove their content didn't change while they ran (§16.13).

#### 16.3.3 None adapter

[P1, answering HB3's round 1 finding 6 and round 2 finding C, HR2's round 2 finding 6]
- **Deliverables** (N4, §16.6.1): where a None project's work may be. By default the project folder except `.combwork`
  and folders the option excludes (`node_modules` and `.venv` by default; no build output folders are found, #1482); a
  card can narrow it to paths (OP-17), never widen it (#1511, decided: refuse): **declare paths** and `submit`'s
  `paths` refuse a path any part of which is `.combwork`, `.git` or an excluded folder (`paths.excluded`, naming the path
  and the folder); a declared folder leaves such descendants out, as before; paths stored before #1511 under one are
  left out of the revision (`NoneAdapter.leftOut`), and submit's reply says what it left out; a starting manifest
  recorded before is compared without them too (`covering`: the submission's change, unclaimed changes), so no such
  path shows as changed or deleted. So a write there is never a card's work, as N4's watcher and checks already held
  (`isDeliverable`, the same rule). Names match as the file system resolves them: on Windows whatever their case
  (`NODE_MODULES`, `.COMBWORK`), in a declaration, a folder's walk, a stored path and N4 alike; a refusal names the path
  as given.
- **A card's paths** are **declared, not guessed**: the card's list of files and folders its work covers, kept on the
  card from its start, which the builder sets at any time (the **declare paths** intent, §16.8.1, or `submit`'s
  `paths`), and the user when they submit it (below). Combwork **pre-fills** it from what
  it saw: edits by the card's agents through Combwork's hooks and file locks, and deliverable writes the watcher saw while
  that agent's turn ran and no other agent or the user was active in the folder. Everything else written in the
  deliverables since the card started (a formatter's output during overlapping turns, the user's editor, a
  hooks-free session, §16.15) is listed at submit as **unclaimed changes**, for the builder (or the user who
  submits it) to add or leave out. Hooks only make the pre-fill better; they are never needed for a
  correct revision. In a hooks-free session the list starts empty and the builder declares it.
  **Built (HI-2339)** for agents: the pre-fill sets the paths only while the card has none, so a code card's submit
  that gives no `paths` names, in its reply's warnings, its pre-fill beyond its paths (*its paths leave out files it
  recorded as its agents' edits*) and the unclaimed changes (*in neither its paths nor what it recorded as its agents'
  edits*: worded without saying who wrote them, as an overlapping write may be an agent's). The same warnings go with
  the two refusals they explain, `submit.unchanged` and `submit.sameRevisionNote` (a refusal's `warnings`, in the Agent
  API's body and the Combwork tools' text). Nothing is claimed: to include them, the builder submits with `paths` listing
  every file of the work (or declares them). The paths cover a file when it is one of them or under one, as the file
  system names them (`src` covers `src/x`, never `src-other/x`). Git cards and no-code cards are unchanged.
  **Built (HI-2352)** for the user: their move that submits a started None code card (a drag or **Move to** from
  Doing, or back from On Hold to Doing, to Review or past it: §16.8.4's submit step) first asks, when its paths
  leave files out (counted as above: its paths, else its pre-fill; its pre-fill beyond them, then the unclaimed
  changes), **Include files {card}'s paths leave out?**, listing every file, with **Include Them** (submitted with
  `paths` = its paths and those files, kept as its paths), **Leave Them Out** (submitted as it is) and Cancel
  (nothing written). The question is read-only (`tasks:move` replies `leftOut`; the runtime's `Ask` carries it with
  no rules), comes before the rules a move would skip, and the choice goes with that question's confirm too. It
  says a changed file may be another card's or the user's own. Nothing else asks: a drag from Todo (started in the
  same move: nothing changed since), a move to Done (a move, not a submission: Solo's), the Assistant's moves and
  agents' intents (their warnings, above). **Not built:** the window shows no card's paths, and has no editor for
  them; the Version Control tab lists no unclaimed changes.
- **The start's baseline, off main's thread** (HI-2340): a code card's start keeps every deliverable's hash
  (`Started.deliverables`, what its unclaimed changes are found against), and its unclaimed changes read the project
  whole again. Both reads run in a worker thread (`noneBaseline.ts`), never on main's, where they held typing 0.4–4 s
  on a few thousand files. A read takes at most **No version control: longest read of the project** (Settings →
  Advanced, `cw.none.baselineSeconds`, 120 s); past it, or if the worker ends, the card goes on with no baseline and
  no list, as with a project too large to read. What changed during a read is checked as before: the card's paths and
  their content, and its kind (the evidence, again at the write), its column (`stillAt`), and the folders left out (the
  adapter's generation: a start read under others is gathered again, once; an unclaimed list is read again, else
  none). **A no-code card reads nothing of the project**: no baseline, no hash of its declared paths (its base is
  none, its evidence its kind), and its unclaimed list is empty. **A check's points too** (HI-2358): a None check's
  start and end (`runChecks`' `checkStart` and `checkEnd`) read its declared paths' revision on a fresh adapter (cold:
  the whole project for a card declaring `.`) and, at the start and where the watcher's record isn't complete at the
  end, the stat snapshot of every deliverable, in the same worker (`readCheckPoint`: never shared or dropped, the same
  bound and endings), in the same order as before: the start's after `t0` and before the command, the end's after the
  watcher's record. The snapshot's lines are one function (`snapshotLine`), so a snapshot taken in the worker compares
  exactly with one taken on main. No answer, or a walk that couldn't be read, is null, never an empty snapshot: the
  run doesn't count (`revisionChanged`, or `changed`). The run's link reads the card's revision first, before its
  check starts (`cardRunRevision` → `NonePlatform.runRevision`): a revision-only point there too, never a hash on main.
- **Revision:** SHA-256 over the sorted list of (relative path, SHA-256 of content, or "deleted") of **the card's
  paths** (a folder means every deliverable file under it), together with the path list itself. It can be computed
  **at any time** from the card's current paths, not only at submit: a check run computes it when it starts and ends
  (§16.13), and submit computes it again and must find the same value for the run to count. Any edit to one of the
  paths, or a change to the list of paths, is a new revision: sameness is equality [#1112 B; answering HR2's round 3
  finding 1]. Whoever made it (the card's agent, another card's, the user) doesn't
  matter: the content is the revision.
- **A file in two cards' paths** (two cards working on one file in turn) belongs to both: an edit to it after A's pass
  makes A's pass stale (its content changed), which is correct; files outside A's paths never affect A.
- **No dirty state, no snapshot step:** None has nothing between "edited" and "submitted", so `submit.clean`,
  `submit.ready` and `submit.trailer` aren't in None rulesets (they need the Git capabilities `dirty` and
  `revisions` with commits); the revision is computed when submitted.
- **Change:** the card's paths with their content hashes at `Started` (a manifest stored with the fact: paths and
  hashes, never contents) and at the revision.
- **Acceptance** (None's integration): the approved revision is accepted only if **the card's paths still hash to it
  when it is accepted**; if anything in them changed since the pass or the approval, the pass is stale and the card
  goes back to Review (an edit before your approval means you'd approve something you haven't seen). So `Accepted`
  always names content that was reviewed and is what's in the folder at that moment [HR2's round 2 finding 6].
  Nothing is copied or published in 1.0 (OP-16). After acceptance, a later edit to those paths belongs to no card
  until a card starts on them.
- **Authorship:** the agents whose edits the pre-fill saw; for no-self-review, Combwork's records of who worked the card.
- **Hashing is incremental and write-driven:** a cache of (path, size, modification time) → content hash per
  project, which a watcher write event for a path invalidates even when size and time didn't change. At most 20,000
  files and 2 GB per card; beyond that the revision is unknown and the option row says to narrow the paths.

#### 16.3.4 Paper check: Jujutsu, Mercurial, Subversion

The capability model must take these later without changing facts or rules [#1117, note "Core model v2"]. Each row
says how the platform would answer, and where it is weaker than Git.

| Capability | Jujutsu (jj) | Mercurial (hg) | Subversion (svn) |
|---|---|---|---|
| revisions | The commit id (not the change id, which survives amends with new content). **jj records the working copy as a commit on most commands, reads included**: `head` reads with `--ignore-working-copy` (no side effect), and `snapshot` (an explicit `jj` command, at submit) makes the revision the card submits. | Changeset hash. | Revision number; local changes have none until committed to a branch path. |
| readiness | **jj can store unresolved conflicts in a commit** ([conflicts](https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/conflicts/)): `readiness` asks for the revision's `conflict` template keyword and lists the files; a conflicted revision is refused at submit (`submit.ready`) and as a test-merge result. | Always ready (a merge with unresolved files can't be committed). | Always ready (`svn commit` refuses conflicted paths). |
| isolation | `jj workspace add` (each workspace has its own working-copy commit). | `hg share -B` (bookmarks shared with the source: without `-B` a share keeps its own bookmarks and the target couldn't be read; [share](https://www.mercurial-scm.org/help/commands/share)). | A second checkout. |
| integration | Rebase onto, or a merge commit with, the target bookmark; the **result revision** is the new commit. | `hg merge` + commit (or `hg rebase`); the result is the new changeset. | `svn merge` + commit (or commit straight to trunk). |
| advance (atomic) | `jj bookmark set <target> -r <result>`: jj operations are atomic, and two concurrent ones never lose an update; a racing change leaves a **conflicted bookmark**, which `advance` reports as `Moved(actual)`. | **Weaker:** no compare-and-swap for a bookmark on the command line ([bookmarks](https://www.mercurial-scm.org/help/commands/bookmarks)). The adapter checks the bookmark, moves it, reads it back, and reports `Moved(actual)` if another writer moved it; it holds Combwork's repository lock, which excludes Combwork but not other clients. To settle when hg is built (git-support's sibling list). | The commit itself is the advance, and the server refuses an out-of-date working copy (`svn: E155011`), which is a compare-and-swap. |
| containment | jj integrates by **rebase**, which rewrites revision ids, so ancestry (`jj log -r 'R & ::T'`) answers only for a merge; the main test is a target commit that replays the change exactly (the change id as a hint), as Git's squash row. | Ancestry for `hg merge`; after `hg rebase`, the obsolescence markers (`hg log -r 'successors(R)'`, with evolve) or an exact replay. | R ≤ the target's head on the same branch path; merges through `svn:mergeinfo`. |
| sameness | Replay: rebase R1's change onto the new base in a temporary workspace and compare trees (the change id only a hint) [#1112 B]. | Replay with `hg graft` or a merge in a temporary share, comparing manifests. | Exact revision; there is no rebase. |
| dirty | **jj has no dirty state:** the working copy is a commit that commands snapshot. `submit.clean` means the working-copy commit `@` is empty (its changes were moved into the card's revision), and the watcher debounces `op_heads` so every snapshot isn't a new revision. | `hg status`. | `svn status`. |
| authorship | Author field + Combwork's records. | Same. | Same. |
| observe | `.jj/repo/op_heads` (each operation), read with `--ignore-working-copy`. | `.hg/store`, `.hg/dirstate`, `.hg/bookmarks`. | `.svn/wc.db`. |

**Fits:** jj and hg fit every capability, with two contract points the Git adapter doesn't exercise but the
interface now carries: **readiness** (jj stores conflicts in commits) and **explicit snapshots** (jj records the
working copy when read). hg's target advance is not atomic from the command line: a known weakness for when hg is
built, written down here so it isn't discovered then. Subversion has no local commits, so "submit a revision" means
committing to a branch path, and isolation is a checkout per slot: it fits with a "revisions are server commits" note,
and is not planned. The facts and the piece library say revision, line, folder, target, integrate and result
revision; Git's words (branch, commit, merge commit) appear only in the Git adapter and in the window's Git text
[P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 11].

#### 16.3.5 Detecting version control

[#1122 detect] Version control is a fact, detected, and never switched silently.

| Case | What Combwork does |
|---|---|
| A project is added in a Git repository | Git is selected, and the tab says "This folder is a Git repository at <root>". One step asks "How do you work? Solo / Pair / Team", suggesting a preset from the project's agents (Solo for one or none, Pair for a builder and a reviewer, Team for more). Nothing is applied until the user chooses. |
| A project is added in a folder with no version control | None, with its own preset step. |
| Upgrading to 1.0 | Git projects get Git and None projects None, with options matching how they work today (§16.17); a one-time notice offers the presets. |
| A None project gets `git init` (by the user or an agent) | Combwork notices (the refresh that ensures `.combwork`'s exclude, §8) and offers to switch to Git, with the switching warning (§16.6.5), from the next card. |
| The repository disappears (`.git` removed or moved) | Combwork says so and offers None. Until the user switches, Git's rules hold rather than pass: their facts are unknown (§16.3.1). |
| Mercurial, Jujutsu or another system is found (`combworkVcs.ts` `vcsOf`/`otherVcsOf`) | "Mercurial found: not supported yet, so this project uses None."
