A colocated jj+git repository (`.jj` beside `.git`) is Jujutsu too, so None: jj keeps git's HEAD detached there, which would break the Git adapter's line facts; `otherVcsOf` already treats it so for Initialise repository (§8) [P1, answering HB3's round 1 finding 16]. |
| A subfolder of a larger repository | Git, showing the repository root; the tab says branch and merge actions affect that whole repository. (Today the Git view refuses actions there, §8; 1.0 keeps refusing Combwork's merges into a parent repository unless the project's options name its target explicitly: OP-29.) |

Everything is visible in the Version Control tab itself, not only through the Assistant [#1122 c].

**Built [#1419]:**
- **Offers** (`ProjectPlatform.offer`) show under the tab's header: `gitFound` "Git found at <root>: switch to Git?"
  with **Switch…** and **Not Now**; `repositoryGone` "The Git repository is gone. Git's rules hold until you switch…"
  with **Switch to None…**; `otherFound` "Mercurial found: not supported yet, so this project can only use None" with
  **Switch to None…**. Not Now hides an offer until Combwork starts again (in memory). The fact is said once: while an
  offer shows, the fact line beside the choice is hidden, and after Not Now it says what was found ("Mercurial found in
  this folder: not supported yet." while Git is in force). The once-per-start notice (`sayPlatform`) gains **Open
  Version Control**, one per project (`platform:<path>`): a newer detection replaces the one before it. Initialise repository… (HI-1905: on Git's page, chosen before the folder has a repository) switches the
  project to Git after it; a switch cancelled there brings the `gitFound` offer without a restart (the refresh after it). Each switch goes through §16.6.5's warning.
- **The tab never contradicts itself [#1492]:** detection is the workspace refresh's, but the tab reads git again on
  window focus. When that read finds a repository where detection has none, or none where it has one (`.git` moved
  away, then back to Combwork), the tab asks for one refresh, so its fact, its offer and the notice follow at once, never
  "This folder is a Git repository" over a page saying there's none. Once per answer: where detection decides
  otherwise for good (a jj repository colocated with git, Mercurial beside it) nothing more is asked.
- **The repository gone (S20):** Git's rules hold. A Git card's start or submit refused for what can't be read
  (`platform.unknown`) carries `offer: repositoryGone` while detection finds no Git repository, and its next step is
  the offer: "The project's Git repository is gone: ask the user to restore it, or to switch the project to None in its
  Version Control tab (from the next card)."
- **A subfolder of a larger repository (OP-29):** when Combwork or the agent merges, the target branch (G7) must be set by
  the project itself, not inherited: the contradiction `subfolderTarget` ("This project is inside a larger repository:
  name the branch its work merges into"), checked when options are saved (the form, the settings tool), with the
  project's folder among the check's inputs. Who named the target is part of the ruleset: resolving the options sets
  `targetOwn` (never set by a level) when the project's own options name a Git target, so a card, or a lane's next
  card after a switch or a target edit, keeps it with the rest of its rules. The queue's backstop: in a subfolder
  project, an entry whose card's ruleset lacks `targetOwn` (no target, or one inherited from the workspace's or Combwork's
  defaults) pauses its queue (`subfolderTarget`), saying how to go on.
- `cw_project_status` gives `versionControl`: the platform, what is found, and any offer.

**Built [#1423], "How do you work? Solo / Pair / Team":**
- **Who asks, per platform** (`asksPreset`, `src/shared/workflow/presetStep.ts`): a project whose platform in force has
  no preset, no options of its own and no answer (`workflow.presetAsked`). That is a project added since 1.0 (New
  Project, a folder found when the workspace is read, its project.json made then as opening makes it, one the
  Assistant or the Agent API adds) and one switched to a
  platform it never had (#1419: nothing in `kept`), even with its other platform answered. A project from before 1.0
  (no platform recorded) never asks, also before its upgrade has run: the upgrade writes its options (it gets the
  one-time presets notice, §16.17).
- **The answer is the platform's:** `chosen` (any save from the Workflow section, the step's Choose included) or
  `notNow` (for the platform the step showed: one switched meanwhile isn't answered for it), written with
  `setPresetAsked` (`projectWorkflow.ts`) under the project's lock; it goes into `kept` with the
  platform's options when the project switches away and comes back with them, so each platform asks once. The settings
  tool's saves keep it.
- **The step**, under the Version Control tab's header (`PresetStep.tsx`): Solo, Pair and Team (for Git, Pair is Combwork
  merging), the one suggested from the project's agents marked (Solo for one or none, Pair for a builder and a reviewer
  counted as the upgrade counts one, Team for more; worked out again as agents are added) and previewed with what it
  sets and why (#1418's preview). **Choose** checks it as the Workflow section's save does and asks once ("Nothing is
  in flight yet…"), then saves; **Customise…** opens the Workflow section with the preset filled in, not saved; **Not
  now** writes `notNow` and no options, so they stay inherited (the workspace's and Combwork's defaults, else all off), and
  the header says "no preset chosen". Nothing is applied before Choose.
- **Where:** New Project opens the new project's Version Control tab at the step; a project found when the workspace
  is read, or added by the Assistant or the Agent API, gets a notice in the presets notice's look ("<project> was
  added: how do you work?", **Choose…** to the step, **Not Now** answers `notNow`); after a switch to a platform with no
  answer, the tab shows the step. All of it works with the Assistant off.

### 16.4 Facts

#### 16.4.1 The log

Each card has an append-only **fact log** [note §4, #1119]. A fact is `{ seq, card, kind, at, actor, source, data }`:
- `seq`: per card, increasing; `at`: when Combwork wrote it.
- `actor`: who caused it: `user`, `assistant`, `agent:<id>` (with its name then), `combwork` (Combwork's own action, e.g. the
  merge queue), `outside` (observed, no actor known). From the token as today (`taskActor`, `servers.ts:1737`).
- `source`: `recorded` (Combwork saw it happen, through an intent, a move or its own action) or `observed` (read back from
  the platform). Observed facts are always checked again when used; recorded ones aren't rewritten.
- `ruleset`: the id of the compiled options the fact was decided under (§16.5.4).
- `data` holds platform-neutral fields (revision, line, target, result revision, keys, files); anything only one
  platform has (Git's ref names, a merge commit's parents, the merge method's git details; jj's change id) goes in an
  opaque `data.platform` object that only its adapter reads [HB3's round 1 finding 16].

The log lives in `combwork.db` in its own table (`card_facts`), written in the **same transaction** as the card change it
causes (`boardWrite`, `boardStore.ts:536`), so a fact and the move it caused can't diverge [#1025, #1119]. Facts are
never edited or deleted, except with the card itself (Delete permanently) [P1]: a repeated refusal appends another
`Refused` fact, and the window collapses repeats when it shows them.

**Cards from before 1.0** [note §11]: a card that is Done, On Hold or Todo at the upgrade gets no facts and is marked
**before 1.0** (`preWorkflow: true`); Combwork invents none. A card in flight gets only observed evidence, marked
`adopted`: an **`Adopted`** fact (Doing, Review, Passed) and, for a card in Review, an adopted submission at its line's
head; never a verdict history can't prove (§16.17) [P1, answering HR2's round 1 note and HB3's finding 1]. Such a card
that starts after the upgrade loses the mark and is a 1.0 card from then on [Darren, #1119 decision 4]. **Fixed in rc.4** [HI-1674]: a
  start through an intent (cw_start_card) kept the mark, only P3's recorder cleared it, so the user's and the
  Assistant's later moves of the card took P3's path around its rules: on rc.1 two such cards went to Done in the column
  and stayed Active in the stage, their agents' questions still For you. Now any stage the workflow writes clears the
  mark (factStore's `setStage`), so such a move goes through the rules (recorded with the stage, its questions closed by
  `closeSettled`, or refused). Each time a workspace opens, `workflow/stageRepair.ts` clears the mark of every card with
  facts, and brings a card the board has in Done while its stage isn't into line: a `Moved` to done with cause `repair`,
  its asked questions closed, "Recorded as Done, as the board had it" in its history.
  **Fixed in rc.10** [HI-1966]: the user's and the Assistant's Start of such a card (`cw_start_task`, the board's move
  to Doing), and its agent's old move to Doing, took P3's recorded start: no slot was lent, and the `Started` fact named
  the agent's 0.9 worktree (or the project folder). On rc.9 the Assistant's Start of HI-1612 launched HB2 in the main
  checkout, on main. Now its start (into Active from Todo, or from Done) goes through the runtime, as an intent's does:
  its slot is lent where the project builds in slots, the mark clears, and its decisions from before become facts in that
  write, as P3's start recorded them. Its other moves keep P3's path until it starts. As well, a Start whose card still
  started with no slot in a project that builds in slots (not a slot's folder, nor its builder's 0.9 worktree not yet
  migrated) is undone, the card back where it was, "wasn't started: its project builds each card in a slot…", never its
  agent launched in the project folder. A Start of a card already Active with no slot (a start from before this fix) is
  refused the same way, the card left Active: "Put it back to Todo, then start it again" [HR2's round 1]. The user's
  Start across the rules, with its reason, starts where the agent is. A no-code card is never such a start: it takes no
  slot (HI-2335), so its Start (the user's, the Assistant's or a lane's) starts where its agent is [HI-2395].

**P3 records facts from today's moves, refusing nothing** [#1216]: every card change writes its facts in its own
transaction (into Doing with an agent `Started`; into Review `Submitted`; a review's start and verdict; each column change
`Moved`, cause `user` from the window, `intent` from an agent's or the Assistant's tools; blocked and unblocked; each
decision change, each a new generation; and what an agent was given of the decisions, by reading the card or receiving
a decision line, `DecisionsReceived`). A card's work cycle starts once (none yet, or reopened from Done): fixes after a
failed review, through Doing or not, go on in it. The platform is read before the change; a value that couldn't be
read never refuses the move: its field is empty and the fact's `platform.unknown` says what couldn't be read. A fact
that can't be written fails the change whole.

#### 16.4.2 Kinds

| Kind | Data | Written when |
|---|---|---|
| `Started` | folder (slot lease or `project`; under slots a no-code card's is `project`, HI-2335: no folder of its own, its agent left where it runs), line, base revision, target, ruleset, builder agent, kind (code / no-code); None: manifest, and the deliverables' manifest (hashes) that its unclaimed changes are found against [P2] | The start intent or the user's Start passes its rules. |
| `Adopted` (observed) | as `Started`, what could be read; followed by a `Moved` to the stage it was in (cause derived), since the stage is the last `Moved`'s [P2] | The upgrade, for a card in flight (§16.4.1). |
| `Submitted` | **submission id** (its seq), revision (none for no-code), base, head, candidate key, files changed (#945), round, the decision generation the builder had received, same-revision (bool), summary comment id | The submit intent passes (§16.8.1). |
| `CheckRan` | name, command, revision, result (passed/failed/stopped), run id, duration, by, counted (bool), why not counted | A run naming the card finishes (§16.13, P3) [#1119 c]. |
| `ReviewStarted` | reviewer, submission id, revision, review copy | The start-review intent (§16.8.1). |
| `Verdict` | reviewer, submission id, revision, pass/fail, kind of fail (content / explanation), round, decision generation the reviewer had received, comment id | The verdict intent passes. |
| `CarriedOver` | from revision, to revision, how (replay, same revision) | A pass is kept for a later revision that is the same change; with same revision, a stale pass holds again once its line is back at exactly the approved revision (#1623). |
| `Updated` | entry id, from revision, to revision, how (merged target in, rebased), carried (bool) | Strict: the queue brought the approved revision up to date on its own ref (§16.9.1). |
| `LineMoved` | line, from, to, why (squash continuation) | Combwork moved an agent's branch to the target between cards (§16.19.2). |
| `LineRenamed` | from, to, why (repair) | Repair renamed the agent's branch the card works on, named after an old place (#1305): the fold's `started.line` is the new name from here (only when it was `from`), so the card's view and its reconciliation follow it, never finding it gone. |
| `FolderMoved` | from, to, why (repair) | Repair relinked or recreated the agent's worktree the card works in at a new place (#1343), written before the agent's record: the fold's `started.folder` is the new place from here (only when it was `from`), so the card's view and its reconciliation read it there. Reconciliation writes it too, for an unfinished card whose folder is gone and whose builder's recorded worktree is elsewhere on the card's line, or on the new name of its line's pending rename (a Repair cut short before it; `LineRenamed` follows in the same run). It records no `Gone: folder` while the builder's record still names the folder and the project or its workspace has a move Repair hasn't recorded, while that worktree or its branch can't be read, or while its line has a rename pending to another name. |
| `CommitAttributed` (observed) | commit, card (or none), how (trailer, only card, unattributed, assigned by the user) | A new commit on a shared folder's line (§16.3.2). |
| `Stale` | approved revision, current revision, why (another change; a decision since; exact-only) | A newer revision that isn't the same change appears after a pass, or a decision is recorded after it (§16.4.6). |
| `ApprovalRequested` | request id, kind (approve, decide, test, sign-in, other), gate, revision?, text | The ask-the-user intent, or a rule waiting on the user. |
| `RequestClosed` | request id, why (`done`, `carriedOn`) | A request closed unanswered (#1638): its card reached Done, or the agent that asked moved the card on itself. |
| `Approval` | request id, user, gate, submission?, answer (approved / declined / answered), note, decision generation | The user answers the request (in the card, the For you list, or a pane reply counted under #922). An answer is never a `Decision` (§16.4.6). |
| `IntegrationRequested` | **entry id**, revision, candidate key, target, style | The card enters the merge queue (again, after a failure, with a new entry id). |
| `IntegrationCancelled` | entry id, by, reason | **Remove from queue**, a stale pass, a card moved out by the user, a follow-up posted on the queued card (#1623). |
| `IntegrationStarted` | entry id, expected target revision, result revision | The queue is about to advance the target (written **before** it does, §16.9.2). |
| `IntegrationPhase` | entry id, phase (files, ref, rollback) | Before each step of a checked-out target's advance (§16.9.2). |
| `IntegrationFailed` | entry id, revision, target, reason (conflict, checks, target moved, folder busy, not up to date), files, log, transient (bool), conflicts (HI-1181: a conflict's hunks) | The queue's test merge or checks fail. |
| `Integrated` | entry id?, revision, target, result revision, method, by (combwork, agent, outside), the rules skipped when merged by hand before they passed (the **outside the rules** mark) | The target moved with the change in it (recorded) or containment found it (observed). |
| `MergedInPart` (observed) | revision (the merge base now in the target), target | Some of an unfinished card's work found in the target: the **merged outside, in part** mark (§16.4.4) [P2: a mark needs a fact]. |
| `InTarget` (observed) | revision, target, submission (its `Submitted` fact) | A card in Review whose submitted change is in its target already: the **already in main** mark; it stays in Review (§16.4.4) [HI-2709]. |
| `LeftTarget` (observed) | revision, target | A Done card's revision no longer in its target: the **no longer in main** mark (§16.4.4) [P2]. |
| `Accepted` | revision (None code cards) or submission id (no-code cards, which have no revision) | None's integration, and a no-code card's acceptance on either platform. |
| `Moved` | from stage, to stage, cause (intent, user, derived, override) | Every stage change. |
| `Refused` | intent or move, rule, message ids, values | A refused intent or move (agents' and the Assistant's; the user's refused drags are not logged unless overridden). |
| `Override` | rule(s) skipped, move, by (user / assistant), reason | §16.8.4. |
| `Blocked` / `Unblocked` | reason | As today's `blocked`. |
| `Decision` | decision id, **generation** (1, 2, 3… per card) | A decision is recorded (the decision itself stays on the card). |
| `DecisionsReceived` | agent, generation | The agent received the card's decisions up to that generation (§16.4.6). |
| `FilesLocked` | agent, paths (relative to the project folder) | The card's builder took file locks on paths not yet recorded this cycle, while the card was its current one (G16, §16.6.4, #1481). |
| `CannotWithinRules` | rule, why | The agent's "I couldn't do it within the rules" intent (#686) [#1120 c]. |
| `ReviewerRequest` | text | The reviewer's request to the builder mid-review (#912) [#1120 c]. |
| `LoopStep` | step, text, design?, until?, waitMinutes?, of? | A card loop's step that moves nothing (#1382, #1467): the builder's design for its reviewer's check (`design`: its id, `<key>/s<seq>`, and when its check is due, `until`, by `waitMinutes`) or going ahead with it unchecked (`proceed`), the builder's follow-up of reviewed work for the check (`followUp`: its id, no due time), or the reviewer's answer (`ok`, `gaps`); an answer and going ahead name the step they are about (`design`; `of`: its kind). A design or follow-up waits (`CardState.step`) until answered, gone ahead from (a design), replaced by another, or the card moves, is submitted or given a verdict. |
| `HeadMoved` (observed) | line, from, to, candidate key of the new change | A new revision in the card's folder outside an intent. |
| `TargetMoved` (observed) | target, from, to | |
| `Gone` (observed) | what (line, folder, repository, deliverables) | |
| `LaneChanged` | lane, cards before/after | Combwork owns lane lists (§16.11). |
| `Undone` | the fact or change undone, by | §16.14. |

A card's history text (`TaskHistoryEntry`) stays, for people; the facts are the data [note §4].

#### 16.4.3 Derived state

- The card's **stage** is a function of its ruleset and facts: the last `Moved` fact's stage, where every `Moved` is
  written only by the runtime after its guards [#1112 E, note §14 q8]. The `cards` table keeps the stage and its
  category as columns (a cache, written in the same transaction), so the board, watches, lanes and the Agent API keep
  reading a column: `column` stays the **category id** (`hold`, `todo`, `doing`, `review`, `passed`, `done`) for
  compatibility, and a new `stage` field carries the stage id [P1].
- Badges and marks on the card come from facts: revision under review, last verdict and on which revision, checks on
  it, stale, override, returned, For you, outside Combwork, decision since.
- **Shown in P3** [#1224]: the card dialog's **Work** section (`CardWork.tsx`, from #1223's work view): branch (Git),
  base, folder and target; this cycle's revisions newest first, each with its round, builder, time, files (expandable,
  opening in Files), verdicts (dimmed once they no longer count) and checks (not counted, with why); the marks (stale,
  carried over, outside the rules, merged in part, left the target, an override); how it was integrated or accepted.
  A card from before 1.0 says it has no work record; an adopted one says so; a work view that can't be read says why,
  with Retry. The board card shows, in one line, the revision, the last verdict, the checks on it and a stale or
  outside-the-rules mark, each an icon with its words as its accessible name. None's revisions show once P4 reads them
  ("No revision recorded" until then). What a fact names as not read (`platform.unknown`: a revision, its files, a
  line or base) is shown as not read, with why, never as none. The English there is agents': the window words why
  itself [#1477]: what a platform couldn't read from the reason kept beside it as data (`platform.unknownText`), and
  Combwork's own notes (nothing read before the change, as for a card sent to Review with no agent: "No revision recorded:
  Combwork didn't read one when the card went to Review") in sentences of their own. A revision's files open in the folder
  recorded for it (the agent whose worktree it is now), else are listed as text, saying the folder is no longer an
  agent's [#1224 round 1].
- **Restart** resumes from the log. The merge queue rebuilds from `IntegrationRequested` entries with no
  `IntegrationCancelled`, `IntegrationFailed` or `Integrated` for the same entry id; an entry with `IntegrationStarted`
  and no outcome is reconciled first (§16.4.5) [note §4; P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 8].

#### 16.4.4 Reconciliation

[#1112 C] Observed facts are reconciled against recorded ones, never refused. Reconciliation runs on an observe event,
on window focus, when a card is read for a rule, and once at start. **P3 only recorded** [#1217]: the observed
facts below are written (each once across copies of Combwork, by its dedupe key). **From P4 it acts** [#1263]: the table's moves,
queue cancellations, wakes and lane ends follow, through the project's runtime, while **workflow rules are enforced**
(Settings → Advanced → *Workflow rules are enforced*, `cw.workflow.enforce`, on by default). Turned off, it records
only, as in P3: a card merged by hand stays where it is, with its `Integrated` fact. What follows an observation is
applied apart from recording it, once: an observation recorded while the rules were off is acted on at the next
reconciliation once they're on again (an integration until the card is Done; a stale pass once, its builder's wake
tied to its `Stale` fact) [HR2's #1263 round 1]. Its rules:

| Observed | Then |
|---|---|
| A new revision in the card's folder while it is Active | `HeadMoved`; nothing else. The card shows its current revision. |
| A new revision after Submitted, while in Review | `HeadMoved`. The review is of the submitted revision, and its verdict is **always recorded** [answering HB3's round 1 finding 8]: a fail stands as it is; a pass is recorded on the submitted revision and, if the head is now a different change, made `Stale` at once (the card goes to Approved with the stale mark, the builder is woken: "stale: submit again"). |
| A new revision after a pass that **is** the same change (a clean rebase, a squash) | `CarriedOver`; the card stays Approved [#1112 B]. With "Exact revision only" (G4), it is `Stale`. |
| A new revision after a pass that isn't the same change | `Stale`; the card stays in Approved with a **stale** mark until the builder submits again (it then goes to Review); its queue entry is cancelled (`IntegrationCancelled`); the builder is woken, and its lane shows "paused: stale, submit again" [#1120 c; HB3's round 1 finding 8]. |
| A stale pass's line back at **exactly** the approved revision (the same commit: a follow-up taken back) | `CarriedOver` (how: same revision), once per return, written only while the head it follows is still the newest observed: the reviewer passed that commit, so the stale mark goes and the pass holds again. Where Combwork merges, the Approved card with no queue entry is queued again (unless a follow-up waits for its reviewer's check, whose `ok` queues it, or the OK before merging is still to come, which is asked again); the builder is woken: no need to submit again. Where the agent merges, the builder is woken to merge it. Recorded while the rules are off, this is done once they're on [#1623]. |
| **Integration needs a change** [answering HB3's round 1 finding 2] | Containment and observed integration count only a card with a **non-empty change**: its revision differs from `Started.base` and isn't an ancestor of it. A card just started (its revision is its base, an ancestor of the target) is never found "in the target". |
| A card with its own line, in **Approved**: the approved revision (or one that replays to it) found in the target, not by Combwork | `Integrated` (observed, `by: outside`) → Done; the queue cancels its entry; the lane counts it [#1112 C]. |
| A card with its own line, in **Review**, whose submitted change is found in its target before its review passed: merged by hand, or carried in another card's merge (HI-2684 carried HI-2682's commits) | `InTarget` (observed: revision, target, the submission it was read for), a mark, once per submission: the card **stays in Review** and its review decides, with the rules on or off. The Work section says its code is already in main. Once its review passes, the queue finds the change in the target and closes it as merged (`Integrated`, by outside, as for an Approved card above), or the agent's merge report does; the user can also move it. A later submission has no mark until it is found in the target too. Before HI-2709 such a card was closed at once, outside the rules: a merge outside its review is no reason to skip it [HI-2709]. |
| A card in **Active** (or Todo) with some of its work found in the target (a partial hand merge) | A **merged outside, in part** mark with the revision; the card stays where it is and its agent goes on. Its work is its line's own commits (first-parent since its base): the target merged into the card (an update) is not its work in the target [P2]. Its later change is computed from its line as usual; the merged part is then in the target and drops out of the diff [HB3's round 1 finding 2]. |
| A card's line deleted **after** Done | Nothing: its facts and pin (§16.9.3) keep what was reviewed, and no slot is recreated [HB3's round 1 finding 11]. |
| A **shared-folder** card whose line is the target: its commits | `HeadMoved` only. These are working revisions, on the target by construction, never an integration: the card reaches Done only through its rules (§16.7.2's "Committed is done" row), so a Pair project working in its folder still reviews before Done [P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 1]. |
| A shared-folder card's commits interleaved with another card's | Each card's change is its own trailer's commits (§16.3.2); the other card's commits are in neither change. |
| A Done card's revision no longer in the target (the target was reset) | A warning mark "no longer in main"; the card stays Done [P1]. |
| The card's line deleted, its slot folder gone | `Gone`. A slot is recreated from the last known revision if it still exists (§16.10.2); otherwise the card shows the problem and its rules hold. Containment of a submitted change still answers from stored keys (§16.3.2). |
| A slot card's line before its slot's preparation (its cycle's `Started` with a lease, no `SlotPrepared` of that lease yet) | Nothing: the preparation makes the line (§16.10), so until then it isn't gone and its head isn't read. Once prepared, a deleted line is `Gone` as above [#1551]. |
| The repository gone | `Gone`; rules hold; §16.3.5. |
| A commit with a card's trailer on the target while the card is in Todo | `HeadMoved` on that card; it isn't moved [P1]. |
| An entry with `IntegrationStarted` and no outcome (Combwork stopped mid-advance) | §16.4.5. Reconciliation leaves the card alone meanwhile: the queue's recovery settles it. |
| **None:** an edit to a card's paths after a pass, while it waits in Review (for the user's approval, or a second reviewer) | `Stale`; the card stays in Review with the stale mark, its builder woken; the builder submits again from Review (None has no Approved stage, so §16.7.2's "Approved · submit after a stale pass" is "Review · submit after a stale pass" there). An edit outside its paths changes nothing [P2]. |

#### 16.4.5 Side effects and recovery

[P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 8] A fact and the side effects it causes can't be in one transaction (the
side effects touch git, processes and other agents), so they are tied by **durable actions**:

- Every action the runtime queues (wake an agent, notify, prepare a slot, prepare a review copy, enqueue, release a
  slot) is a row in `card_actions` (`id`, card, kind, payload, state `pending | done | failed | cancelled`, attempts,
  the fact seq that caused it), **written in the same transaction** as the facts. After the commit, a worker runs
  pending actions in order and marks each done or failed; at start it runs every pending one again.
- **Each action is safe to run twice:** it checks its effect first (a wake is a delivery with the action's id, and
  deliveries are deduplicated by id; a slot is prepared only if it isn't already for that card at that base; a
  notification carries the action id and isn't shown twice). An action that can't tell (a notification already shown
  before a crash) may repeat at most once, never more. **Built** (#1266): a wake's delivery carries the action's id
  (`deliveries.action`, unique), which is the record that it was made: the worker runs a delivering action until it is
  marked, and every run after the first finds its delivery.
  **Notices: the guarantee is the durable record, not the toast** (the Assistant's calls on #1266, 21 Oct). Each
  notice is a **line in its card's history** (*Notified you that it's blocked: Which logo?*, translated; with what it
  said: why it is blocked or stalled, as written, or the request's question, Combwork's own kept as its message; a lane's
  own events on the lane's current card), written by Combwork **in the same transaction as its action** (`notify` in the runtime's change,
  `laneNotice` in the lane notices' change), so after any crash the user can still read it on the card, whatever became
  of what it told. The banner or Windows notification itself is **best effort**: attempted after the record commits, repeated at most once more after
  a run that ended uncertainly, never claimed to be exactly once. A notice is **repeatable**: one claim at a time runs
  it, holding its **lease** (`lease_owner`, a token unique to the claim, and `lease_until`: taken by a conditional update
  only one writer wins, renewed while its handler runs); its dispatch is counted (`attempts`) under that token while the
  lease holds, and the toast is shown at once after that commits (a dispatch not followed by its mark is
  **uncertain**). A dispatch refused (its lease expired or taken, the workspace gone) shows nothing and leaves the
  action pending, retried: an action is done only once its dispatch was attempted under a valid lease (or it had
  nothing to show), and its completion is fenced by the token. Two claims never show it at once, and it is never
  dispatched past two uncertain dispatches. A kind with no handler yet is marked done by the one run that finds it
  pending.
  `card_actions.delivered` (#1215's stand-in) is gone (the 1.0 group's step 10). A host's deliveries are saved by
  **compare-and-set**: a save writes only the deliveries its change made or changed, each from the row as this Combwork
  last read or wrote it; another Combwork's receipt, ack or cancel since makes it read the rows again and plan the change
  again on them (never written over), its rows are never deleted, and a new delivery whose id it took takes the next
  free one. A delivery's record and the row it checks against come from one read (one SELECT, in one read
  transaction with the values beside them), on loading and on every read again.
- **The target advance** is the one step that can't be repeated blindly. The queue writes `IntegrationStarted`
  (expected target revision, result revision) and commits it, **then** advances the target, **then** writes
  `Integrated`. After a restart, an entry with `IntegrationStarted` and no outcome is reconciled from the platform,
  never assumed: for a target not checked out, the ref at the result → `Integrated` (`source: observed`), at the
  expected revision → the entry runs again from the test merge, anywhere else → `IntegrationFailed` (target moved) and
  containment decides; for a checked-out target, the journal's phases and §16.9.2's recovery table, whose last row is
  a terminal "needs you" state that pauses the queue for that target. An entry that runs again keeps its entry id and
  writes a new `IntegrationStarted` (the log stays append-only; the fold takes the newest) [P2].
- **The swap that loses a race:** between the queue's last check that the target is at the expected revision and the
  compare-and-swap, another writer can move it. The swap then fails having written `IntegrationStarted`, so the entry
  needs an outcome: `IntegrationFailed` (target moved, transient) and at once a new `IntegrationRequested` for the
  same revision, which the queue tests against the new head. That requeue is Combwork's, not the builder's: it never
  counts toward `requeue.allowed`, and it counts toward the 3 retests before a pause (§16.9.1 step 6) [P2].
- **Removing an entry** writes `IntegrationCancelled`; a rebuilt queue skips it, so a removed card can't merge after a
  restart.

#### 16.4.6 Decisions and the work they apply to

[#587, note §1; P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 6] A wake alone doesn't prove that work reflects a decision. So
decisions have a **generation** per card (the `Decision` fact's number), and Combwork records which generation each agent
has **received** (`DecisionsReceived`: the decision delivery received, the reply flag it carried, or the agent
reading the card after the decision; today's `decisionsNotice` and decision wakes, `decisionWakes.ts`, already know
these moments).

- **Submit** records the builder's received generation. If a decision is newer than that, submit is refused
  (`submit.decisionsReceived`): "AM-12 has a decision you haven't read: read it, check your work against it, then
  submit."
- **Verdict** records the reviewer's received generation, and is refused if the reviewer hasn't received the newest
  (`review.decisionsReceived`). A submission made before a newer decision shows "decided since this was submitted"
  to the reviewer, who judges whether the work meets it (passing it says it does).
- **Approvals are not decisions** [HR2's round 2 finding 5]: answering a request (Approve, Decline, a test result, a
  sign-in) writes `Approval`, never `Decision`, so it can't make the work it approves stale. Only a decision the user
  records on the card (the card's Decisions) bumps the generation: an agent's question approved with a note records
  the note as one too (HI-2286), beside the `Approval`.
- **Passes and approvals belong to a generation:** each `Verdict` and `Approval` records the generation current when
  it was given. They count only at the **current** generation: the quorum (G1b) is the number of **distinct reviewers**
  with a pass on this submission (or a change that replays to it) at the current generation, never the number of
  `Verdict` rows; `approval.given` needs an `Approval` at the current generation.
- **A decision after a pass or an approval** makes them stale (`Stale`, why: decision since):
  - with review in the ruleset, the card returns to **Review** for the same submission; the reviewers confirm it with
    new verdicts at the new generation (no new commit needed, §16.8.1), and the user's approval, if the ruleset needs
    one, is asked again after them;
  - with no review in the ruleset, the card returns to **Active**, its builder woken to check the work against the
    decision and submit again;
  - its queue entry is cancelled; a test merge already running finishes its checks but doesn't advance the target.
- **The last check before the target moves:** the queue re-checks `integrate.approved` (generation included) inside
  the advance, after the merge checks and before writing `IntegrationStarted` (§16.9.2), **in the transaction that
  writes it**: the entry still the card's open one, the card in Merging, approved at the current generation and not
  stale. If it no longer holds, nothing is written and git isn't touched [P2: a decision that landed while the queue
  read where the target is checked out still advanced it]. A decision recorded after
  `IntegrationStarted` is too late to stop that merge: the merge completes, and the card gets For you (Decide:
  "decided after it merged: does it need a follow-up?").
- **Content-stale and decision-stale differ** [HB3's round 2 finding G]: a new revision that isn't the same change
  keeps the card in Approved with the stale mark until its builder submits (the builder has work to do); a decision
  sends it back to Review (the reviewers have work to do). The Approved category reads "approved, or its pass is stale
  and waits for its builder".
- **Checks** aren't affected: they are about content, not decisions.
- The rule is part of review and approval (on whenever a reviewer or the user checks the work) and can't be switched
  off apart from them [P1].

#### 16.4.7 Done: one finish path

A card reaches Done by several routes: the merge queue, a builder's merge report (checked, or under Not checked), the
user's move with an override, the Assistant's with the user's reason, a no-code card's acceptance (or Accept's), a hand
merge reconciliation finds, and a plain board move (rules off, no workflow). Every one of them ends the same way
(HI-2014): the move into Done records one `Finished` fact, in the move's own transaction, and one durable `finish`
action, and everything that follows a Done hangs off that action, never off the route.

- **What it records.** `how` (`queue`, `reported`, `unchecked`, `accepted`, `override`, `board`), `verified` (the merge
  commit the target was found to hold, the cycle's `Integrated` result, else null) and, under Not checked, `claimed`
  (the result the builder reported: a claim, never read as containment), with an override's `by` and `reason`. Out of
  Done, the finish is over; Done again is another finish.
- **What follows, each once** (`FinishStep` facts, keyed by the finish):
  - *Requests*: the card's open questions closed (as any write in Done closes them), and the Assistant's unread
    requests on it cancelled. Combwork's own requests stay (a merge stopped part way, a dirty slot below).
  - *Dependents*: an override's Done counts as accepted for the cards that depend on it (Darren's option A), so they
    start without its work in the target; each is told so by a comment of Combwork's, once. Any other Done counts as before:
    accepted, or its work found in the target (an unchecked claim never counts).
  - *The slot and the line*: the project's slot pass, from what is on disk each time. The card's lease ends (a lane's
    stays while the lane runs); a slot still on the card's line is **detached at its target's head** when clean (a
    released one as the pool looks at it, before it is lent again; a running lane's by the pass), so the line is no
    longer checked out and, once its target contains it, is deleted (§16.10.1). **Which target** (HI-2185): the card's
    (where it merged, else where it started to), so a waiting slot sits at the head of the line its last card worked to,
    not the branch the slot was first made from (a slot made from main for a lane working to 1.0.0 waits at 1.0.0's
    head, and the next card's line starts from there). The pool, which doesn't read cards, uses the target the slot
    records: the target its last card's or lane's start named, else the one it was made from. A start records it once it
    has its slot, however it got it (lent, lent again, an adopted slot handed over, the one its builder's run still
    writes in taken over, or a lease its lane already held, as a lane lent while it waited for a slot, with no target
    known then), only while the lease it chose is still open and its builder's: one ended or replaced meanwhile records
    nothing and the start waits. A dry start records nothing, and a start with no target leaves the slot's. Its clean-up
    checks the slot's head is in that same target. Committed work that isn't merged stays
    on its line, which is kept. **Uncommitted changes** keep the slot on its line: the user is asked once on the card
    (For you, Combwork's own gate `slotDirty`), and the question closes once the slot is clean (then detached) or another
    lease's. A lane's next card waits while its finished card's slot is in that state. It is asked only of changes
    really left there (HI-2170): never while an operation holds the slot (the pool's look and detach of a released one
    is one, in every Combwork), its builder still works or drains there, the pool hasn't looked at a released one since its
    lease ended, or a later card of the running lane is under way there (its own start moves the slot on, or tells its
    builder); the slot as read is checked again after git's reads, right before asking.
  - *The lane*: read again (one whose cards are all Done ends).
  - Watches on the card end or fire as every board change makes them; stalls are read from the column.
- **Put back and an abandoned lane** aren't finishes: their slot is released and detached the same way, its line kept,
  and nothing else follows (no acceptance, no dependents).
- **Recovery.** A finish's steps are run after its commit and again as its workspace opens, for each Done card whose
  current finish still owes one; each step finds what was done (its fact, the comment's id, the slot as it is). A step
  whose finish is over is recorded as superseded and does nothing. The old `releaseSlot` and `endLaneIfDone` actions
  keep their own meaning when an older one is still pending.

### 16.5 Stages, categories and the piece library

#### 16.5.1 Categories

[#1112 A] Six fixed categories, the board's machinery works on them (lanes, watches, the start view, the Overview,
the Agent API's columns). Their ids are today's column ids, unchanged in the Agent API: `hold`, `todo`, `doing`,
`review`, `passed`, `done`. English names (OP-1, agreed 20 Oct): **On Hold, Todo, Active, Review, Approved,
Done** (`locales/glossary-1.0.md` §2.2).

| Category | Meaning (every platform) |
|---|---|
| On Hold | Parked by the user. Only the user and the Assistant move cards in or out (today's rule, `checkHold`, `tasks.ts:681`). |
| Todo | Not started. |
| Active | Being built. |
| Review | A revision is submitted and waits for, or is in, review or the user's approval. |
| Approved | The current revision is approved and isn't integrated yet, or its pass is stale and waits for its builder to submit again (§16.4.6). |
| Done | Integrated (Git: in the target), or accepted (None), or for a no-code card accepted by its reviewer or the user. |

#### 16.5.2 Stages

A **stage** is a column of the board [#1112 A]. Each sits in one category; a category may hold several stages; a
category the options don't use is hidden. The options produce the stages (§16.6); the user may rename a stage
(OP-30). Default stage names and when they exist:

| Stage (English, agreed) | Category | Exists when |
|---|---|---|
| On Hold | On Hold | Always. |
| Todo | Todo | Always. |
| Active | Active | Always. |
| Review | Review | A reviewer or the user's approval is required (G1/N1 not "No review"). |
| Approved | Approved | Review exists and something follows it (a merge, or an approval before merging). |
| Approved | Approved | Your OK before merging (G10) is asked, with or without review, and a merge follows [#1417, decided]. |
| Merging | Approved | Combwork merges (G5). Shown while the card is in the queue. |
| Done | Done | Always. |

A stage the options no longer produce stays visible while any card is in it (§16.17). Stage ids are stable strings (`active`, `review`, `approved`, `merging`…), the names messages. The panel and board
keep the category's colour and pattern; hovers and accessible names use the stage name [#1122 c].

**Built [#1417]:** the stage model is `src/shared/workflow/stages.ts`, which every view that names a stage reads
(`stagesOf`, `stageName`, `stageOf`, `stagesShown`; IPC `workflow:stages`, with a `workflow-changed` event whenever a
project's workflow is written). The stages are the ruleset's, compiled as the table says (decided on #1417): Review
with any review; Approved when a review or your OK before merging (G10) approves the work and something follows it: in
Git a merge (Combwork merges, the agent merges, or Not checked: G10 asks under each, decided on #1592), in None your OK after the reviewer agent (N1's "a reviewer
agent, then you"); Merging when Combwork merges. Committed is done has nothing after its review, and with neither a review
nor G10 there is no Approved (the agent merging comes from Active). Before #1417 the engine gave None no Approved and gave "the agent merges"
Approved without a review; 1.0 wasn't released, so no stored ruleset keeps that. A card keeps the stages of its own
ruleset; a stage no longer produced is shown while a card is in it.
**Names aren't rules** (N5, OP-30): `stageNames` is resolved global → workspace → project like the options, but left
out of the compiled ruleset and its hash, so a rename never marks anything old rules and applies at once
(`workflow:check` says `appliesNow`, removing the last rename too). Each name is trimmed, at most 24 characters, has no
control character and differs (ignoring case) from every other stage's name, produced or not (a stage kept for a card
under old rules is shown too): its rename, else its default name in English and in the language Combwork shows (so Active
can't be called *Erledigt* while Combwork is in German); a bad one is refused with its reason. Categories keep their names:
renaming the Active stage leaves the category Active. The user's names are for the user's side (the window, the
project's status lists them beside the ids); agents keep the ids. In the window the `doing` and `passed` categories read
**Active** and **Approved** (OP-1; glossary §2.2); the ids, the Agent API and the English agents read don't change.
That includes a card's history and the board's messages the window shows (#1458): a history line is stored in agents'
English ("Moved to Doing", which agents, Combwork's code and the scenarios read) and as its message, which the card dialog
shows as "Moved to Active"; Archive All's reasons and Start's refusals say Active and Approved. Refusals only agents get
(an agent's placement, ordering or review of a card) keep Doing and Passed.

**Built [#1420]:** the board's columns are stages (`src/renderer/src/boardStages.ts`, laid out from each project's
stages and each card's stage from its facts). The stages come with the board's cards (`board:stages`, read with them
when a workflow was written or the projects changed since), so every column is there in the board's first paint and
none is added after it (HI-1682); a board opened before that read shows its frame without columns. The toolbar's
workflow link ("Workflow: Git · …") comes in the same read (each project's `workflow:form`, HI-1852): arriving after
the first paint, it could wrap the toolbar in a narrower window and move every column down. Each category in its fixed order shows its stages as columns: those the shown
projects' current options produce, and any a card of theirs is in (a card under old rules keeps its stage shown).
On Hold, Todo, Active and Done always show; Review and Approved only with a stage, or all six while Settings →
Advanced → *Workflow rules are enforced* is off (cards move freely then). Approved with Merging is two columns
under one Approved heading, in the category's colour: a line over them in the gap above the columns with the name on
it, as a fieldset's legend, taking no row of its own (every column starts at the same height with a group or without). With several projects shown the columns are the union of their
stages; a column takes a project's rename when one project is shown or every shown project names it alike, else its
default name, and a card's project chip then says its own project's name for the stage. A drop into a stage is its
category's move; **Merging is no drop target** (its hover says cards come through the merge queue), and a card in
Merging leaves it by Remove from queue, never by a drag into Approved; Approved's Archive All takes Approved's cards only (a
card that moves on to Merging meanwhile stays: main checks its stage again), and Merging has none. When every card an
open Archive All dialog took leaves its column, stage or project, the dialog says none is left to archive, with Archive
disabled, rather than that agents are on them (#1463). Folds are kept per column id: a category's
apply to its stage, Merging keeps its own (`merging`). The toolbar links each shown project's workflow ("Workflow: Git ·
Team", or a **Workflows** menu with a line per project), opening its Version Control tab at Workflow.

#### 16.5.3 The piece library

[#1112 D] Rules are built only from these pieces, implemented and unit-tested in code. A piece declares the
capabilities it needs. Options pick pieces and their parameters; nothing else can run.

**Guards** (refuse unless…), each with its rule id, the capability it needs and the option that turns it on. A guard
whose option is off isn't in the ruleset at all, so it can't refuse.

| Rule id | Holds when | Needs | Option |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start.notBlocked` | The card isn't blocked. | — | G14 / N6 (with "Cards start only when…"); off in all-off, where a blocked card starts with a warning |
| `start.dependenciesIntegrated` | Every `blockedBy` card is **Done by facts** (integrated or accepted), not just Approved. | containment | G14 / N6 |
| `start.slotAvailable` | A slot can be lent (or the project folder is the card's folder). Never holds a no-code card, which takes no slot (HI-2335). | isolation | G11 = slots |
| `submit.notDuplicate` | This revision (or, for no-code, this card) has no submission still waiting for review or approval, and no open queue entry. A revision that failed review may be submitted again unchanged, with a note (§16.8.1) [answering HR2's round 1 finding 7 and round 2 finding 1]. | revisions | Always (it can't refuse an ordinary move: it only stops a second copy of a submission already waiting) |
| `requeue.allowed` | Re-entering the queue with an **unchanged** approved, unstale revision: its last entry ended with `IntegrationFailed` marked `transient` (or was cancelled by a hold or by the user), and fewer than **2** unchanged requeues **after transient failures** have followed the last new revision; a hold or the user's own cancel resets that count, so holding a card never strands it [HB3's round 3 finding 3]. A conflict, red checks or a failing hook need a new revision. At the limit the card gets For you (Decide: retry once more, take it over, or send it back) [HB3's round 2 finding E]. | integration | Combwork merges |
| `submit.ready` | The revision is ready (no stored conflicts; jj's snapshot taken) (§16.3.1). | revisions | Any rule that needs the card's change (as `submit.clean`); not in all-off rulesets |
| `submit.clean` | The card's folder has no uncommitted changes (shared folder: none in the agent's own paths). | revisions | Any rule that needs the card's change: review, "Committed is done", Combwork merges, the agent merges |
| `submit.trailer` | Shared-folder commits carry the card's trailer. | revisions | G11 = project folder, another agent works in the folder, and a rule needs the card's change |
| `submit.checksPassed` | Every configured pre-review check has a passing, counted `CheckRan` on this exact revision (§16.13). | revisions | G3 / N3 |
| `submit.identity` | Every commit of the change is authored with the project's identity. | authorship | G12 |
| `submit.ownRunsStopped` | The agent has no runs or background processes it started still running (Progress, background tasks). | — | G13 |
| `submit.decisionsReceived` | The builder has received every decision on the card (§16.4.6). | — | Any review, and **any ruleset with a merge step** (Combwork merges, the agent merges), so a no-review card a decision returned to Active reads it before submitting again; all off and Solo (committed) stay free [#1118 20 Oct; HI-2275 applies it] |
| `review.notAuthor` | The reviewer isn't among the card's builders (Combwork's records). | authorship | G2 / N2 (forced on with a reviewer) |
| `review.decisionsReceived` | The reviewer has received every decision on the card (§16.4.6). | — | Any review |
| `verdict.reviewing` | The reviewer started a review (`ReviewStarted`) of the submission it names. | — | Any reviewer agent |
| `verdict.currentSubmission` | The verdict names the latest submission. (A head that moved since is handled by recording the verdict and then `Stale`, §16.4.4, not by refusing it.) | revisions | Any reviewer agent |
| `approval.given` | An `Approval` (approved) answers the request the rule made, for this submission (or one that replays to it), at the current decision generation. | — | G1/N1 "You" or "…then you", G10 |
| `integrate.approved` | The revision has passes from the required number of distinct reviewers (G1b) and the approvals its ruleset needs, all at the current decision generation, none stale. | sameness | G1 ≠ No review |
| `integrate.upToDate` | The revision contains the target's current head. | containment | G8 (strict) |
| `integrate.checksPassed` | The merge checks passed on the test merge (target + change). | integration | G9, G20 |
| `submit.focusedChosen` | The submission's focused tests are chosen: its project's picker answered at exactly the revision, or its builder named them (`tests`) in place of a pick that failed, timed out or said every test. | integration | G20 |
| `done.contained` | The revision to finish (the approved one, else the submitted one) or the same change is in the target, and the change is non-empty (§16.4.4). | containment | G5 = Combwork merges, the agent merges, or Committed is done |

**Actions** (Combwork does…):

| Action | Does |
|---|---|
| `recordStart` | Writes `Started` (folder, line, base, target, ruleset). |
| `prepareSlot` | Lends a slot; creates the card's line from the target's head; runs setup (and installs when the lock file changed) [note §5]. |
| `recordSubmitted` | Writes `Submitted` with endpoints, keys and files. |
| `wakeReviewer` | Tells the lane's reviewer or the pool (§16.10.5). |
| `prepareReviewCopy` | Checks the revision out in a review copy (§16.10.5). |
| `recordVerdict` | Writes `Verdict`. |
| `askUser` | Writes `ApprovalRequested`, sets For you, notifies. |
| `enqueue` | Writes `IntegrationRequested` with a new entry id, adds the card to the target's queue. |
| `cancelEntry` | Writes `IntegrationCancelled`. |
| `testIntegrate`, `runMergeChecks`, `advanceTarget` | The merge queue (§16.9). |
| `returnToBuilder` | Writes `IntegrationFailed`, moves to Active, wakes the builder with the output. |
| `recordIntegrated` | Writes `Integrated`, moves to Done. |
| `accept` | None and no-code: writes `Accepted` (None) and moves to Done. |
| `releaseSlot` | Returns the slot when the card (or lane) ends (§16.10.2). |
| `wakeOnDecision` | On a `Decision`: wakes the builder; the reviewer too if the card is in Review or Approved [note §5, closes #587's manual step]; marks a pass stale (§16.4.6). |
| `endLaneIfDone` | Ends the lane when every card is Done **by facts**, with the result revisions from `Integrated` facts (no agent-supplied `mergeCommit`) [note §5]. Emits the verified lane-end event (#1088) [#1120 c]. |
| `notify` | A banner or Windows notification per the user's settings. |

#### 16.5.4 Compilation

- The project's options (§16.6), resolved global → workspace → project (§16.6.6), compile to a **ruleset**: the stages,
  and for every move (§16.7) the ordered guards and actions. A ruleset is plain data with a content hash as its id,
  stored once in `combwork.db` (`rulesets`).
- **The compiled table is total** [P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 2]: every supported combination of options
  (§16.7.2's dimensions) has a path from Todo to Done for each card kind, and every refusal names a next step that is
  possible under the same ruleset. Combinations the table doesn't support are **contradictions**, refused when saved
  with the reason (a few: "No self-review can't be off while a reviewer is required"; "Combwork merges needs each card in
  its own folder"; "Committed is done needs everyone in the project folder"; "Your OK before merging is already part
  of review by you"; "Combwork merges needs Git") [note §6]. P2 proves it with a test that enumerates every combination of
  the review, quorum, merge, folder and kind dimensions and walks each to Done, through each refusal and its next step,
  and through approvals and quorum.
- **Every card keeps the ruleset it started with** (`Started.ruleset`) until it's Done; a card in Todo uses the current
  one. A lane started under the old options keeps its ruleset until it ends ("old rules") [#1112 UI, #1122 c].
- **A card's target is its start's** (`Started.target`, HI-2674): its queue entry takes that one, and neither a change of
  G7 nor applying the options to the card (an Override) moves it; a running lane's cards still to start take what a
  start under its ruleset, for its builder, would (`startTarget`: an empty G7 can give a builder worktree's base).
  So a change of the target says which cards in flight and running lanes keep another one, with it: Workflow's Save…
  dialog (`WorkflowCheck.targets`) and the settings tool's reply (`keptTargets` in `optionsForm.ts`). Moving them onto the
  new target is HI-2556's.
- **A lane's or card's Merges into** (HI-2556, OP-12 built; Darren's decisions of 7 Nov on design s14). One effective
  target is decided at a card's start and recorded (`Started.target`): the card's own (`cards.target`), else its lane's,
  else G7. From then on that one value is the branch it is made from, its queue and merge, its dependency check and its
  slot. A **lane's** target is recorded in its ruleset: a lane started on another branch records the rules in force with
  G7 set to it (`targetedOf`, id the base's with `~target:<branch>`), so its cards take it as any rule, and old rules
  compare the base ids (`rulesBaseId`): a lane on 1.2.0 isn't on old rules for that. It is fixed for the lane's life
  (a start naming another is refused), set by the user, the Assistant or a script, never its own builder, and only
  with the rules enforced. **A lane is one target**: a card whose own target isn't its lane's is refused into it (on a
  start, an edit or a placement), and a lane's card can't be set to another. A **card's** own target is the user's or the
  Assistant's (`tasks.setTarget`, the card dialog, `cw_create_task`/`cw_update_task`, the Agent API's `target`), only
  while its branch has no work (never started, or each line it had is gone or already in its target, and the folder it
  worked in holds nothing uncommitted, tracked or not: its slot while still on its line, the project folder whatever is
  there: `ownWork`): no rebase of started work. Its old lines, empty, are deleted with the change (`dropEmptyLines`,
  each only at the head `ownWork` found empty, compare and swap: one moved since is refused and kept; refused while a
  folder has one checked out; only its own slot lines, never a target), so its next start makes a fresh line from the
  new target. Both name only
- **Retargeting when Work merges into moves on (HI-2680, design s14 after s8/s11).** A change of G7 from `A` (a release
  shipped) to `B` previews what still points at `A` (`retargetPreview`, read-only): Todo cards whose own target is `A`
  with no own work move; free slots recording `A` (or none, `A` being the target they fell back to) that are clean with
  nothing `A` lacks move; cards with work, cards started on `A`, running lanes on `A` and slots lent, busy, dirty or
  holding unmerged commits stay, each with why. The apply (`retargetApply`) is bound to that preview: each card only
  from `A` (`tasks.setTarget`'s `expect`, under the board's lock), each slot only as seen (its folder, recorded target and
  head: the pool's `retarget`), and before each the project's target still `B` and the caller still allowed, checked
  again at each one's write: a card's under the board's lock (`expectDefault`; a save changing G7 writes in the board's
  write too, so the two are serial), a slot's under the repository's lock (which every save of the options holds); each
  item says moved or why not (a failure part way included: `failed`, never thrown past what already moved), never all
  or nothing. A slot's move is its pool's operation (`op_kind` warm, its intent in
  `board_meta` `slot_retarget:`): reserved by compare and swap, then under the repository's lock and outside any
  database write the folder checked (clean, at its head, in `A`), the caller rechecked, detached at `B`'s head and
  checked, the intent marked `switched`; every exit, a crash's recovery too, settles it from the folder against the
  intent: clean at `B`'s head once switched → `B`; clean at its old head, not switched → its recorded target (none stays
  none); gone → `gone`; anything else → `dirty`, set aside (`board_meta` `slot_aside:`, with what it was moving to and
  what was found): no later look makes it ready, and it is never lent, carried or renamed (a rename that met one carries it to the new name), until it is removed. A store failure
  at its end leaves its operation and intent recorded, settled by the next refresh's recovery. A branch taken out of G7b is refused while anything records
  it (`referencesTo`: cards' own targets, cards in flight started on it, open queue entries, running lanes, slots),
  checked under the lanes' lock and in the board's write, so a lane start on it (which picks again under the lanes'
  lock) and the removal are serial; it is never taken out by itself. The window: Save…'s preview with **Also retarget
  what can move**, applied after the save; the Assistant: the setting's reply lists what can move with a preview id
  (`offerRetarget`: kept in memory, the newest 50 for a day), applied with `cw_queue` `retarget` (`POST
  /v1/workflow/retarget`, the id and the items named: only those that preview listed, each as it was seen then; `from`
  and `to` alone make a new preview, moving nothing).
  the default (stored as none) or a branch G7b lists that exists now (`pickTarget`, `branchExists`). A lane start's
  target is checked before anything changes (an `applyNow` put back included), and again under the lanes' lock.
- A ruleset can't run arbitrary code: pieces are looked up by id, and an unknown id or parameter refuses to compile
  (a ruleset from a newer Combwork opens read-only, like `combwork.db`, §4) [#1112 D].

### 16.6 The Version Control tab: options and presets

The project's **Git** tab becomes **Version Control** [#1112 UI]. Its id stays `changes`, so saved tabs keep working
(§8 kept it for the Git rename too). At the top: the version control (None or Git), detected (§16.3.5), with the
header "Workflow: Git · Team" (or "· Custom"), also linked from the board [#1122 c]. Under it, **Workflow** (the
options, this section), then for Git the platform's own sections: Changes, History, Branches & remotes (each branch
next to its card and the revision under review), and the **merge queue** (§16.9) [#1122]. The whole page changes
with the selection [#1112 down].

**Built [#1416], the tab's shell:** the tab (id `changes`, Alt+8, "Go to Version Control") is `VersionControl.tsx`:
its header (`VersionControlHeader.tsx`) shows the recorded platform as a **None · Git** choice (the other value
disabled, its tooltip saying Combwork offers a switch when it detects one: switching is #1419's), §16.3.5's fact line
(a Git repository at its root; a subfolder, whose branch and merge actions affect the whole repository; no version
control; another system found, so None; the repository gone), and **Workflow: Git · Team** (· Custom (from Team), ·
no preset chosen, from `workflow:form`), which opens Workflow. The sections (`VC_SECTIONS`, `vcSections` in
`gitRepo.ts`, kept per project while Combwork runs) are Workflow, then Git's Changes, History, Branches & remotes
(`GitBranches.tsx`) and Merge queue (#1357's section, placed as it was); a project opens at Changes for Git and at
Workflow for None. The sections are tabs (HI-1837: the shared `Tabs` component, `components/Tabs.tsx`; the body is
their tab panel). When the sections' names don't fit the tab's width beside the status line [#1461], they fold to
their icons (each name in its tooltip and for screen readers), the selected section keeping its name; narrower still,
the row scrolls with the selected section in view. **None's page:** Workflow (no Initialise repository…: HI-1905 moved it to Git's page, below); and **Merge queue while an old Git ruleset's queue is still there**, by #1356's actual-state rule
(`queueShown`: an entry testing or queued, a pause, a return not seen yet, a runner, or a card in flight whose own
ruleset has Combwork merge), with its controls and the links to it, until that state is clear. The section list is a pure
function of the platform and that state. Workflow hosts P4's form (§16.6.6's Built note) unchanged until #1418;
Project Settings → Workflow kept one row, **Open Version Control**, until HI-1766 removed the section; the hidden
`project.workflow.*` rows stay for `cw_update_setting` (their path: Version Control → Workflow → the option). The presets notice's **Choose…** opens the first project's tab at Workflow.

into the 7 locales per `locales/glossary-1.0.md` §2.6.

Not a rule, as G18: in no ruleset, read as the options are when the queue merges (HI-1697). |

An option the platform's capabilities can't support isn't shown (None has no G5–G9, G11, G15). Every option shows

#### 16.6.3 Presets

[#1112 UI, down] "Defaults are the product." Solo, Pair and Team fill every option in one click; changing any option

| G7 target | The repository's default branch (the folder's own line) [#1482] | `main` | `main` | **Built [#1355]:** the repository's default branch, by name (`main`, else `master`, else the branch it is on; `main` when it can't be read), filled in when the preset is chosen and shown before saving, so a repository whose default is another branch isn't given one it lacks. |
| G8 strict | — | Off | Off | The queue tests target + change anyway and a clean update keeps the pass, so strict mostly changes the history's shape; it is on offer for teams that want every merge up to date (OP-18; HB3's round 1 finding 4). |
| G9 merge checks | — | Quick checks | Quick checks + unit + each card's focused tests, dependencies installed clean | #1010's merge gate; #187 (§16.9.1 step 5). **Built [#1361], narrowed for now** (Darren, point 1 on #1121): Team's G9 is quick checks + unit tests, installed from scratch before every merge (`mergeInstall: always`); each card's focused tests are G20 [HI-1367], on in Team when the project has its runner. |
| G10 your OK | Never | Never | Cards labelled `ui` or `release` | Darren's practice (screenshots, release steps). |
| G11 where | Project folder | Slots | Slots | Pairs and teams build in parallel. |
| G12 identity | Off | On | On | #809. |
| G13 stop own runs | Off | On | On | |
| G14 deps merged | On | On | On | Cheap, prevents building on unmerged work. |
| G15 slots up to date | — | On | On | **Built [#1445]:** On in Pair, Team and Pair (the agent merges) since P7 (#1355 had it Off while agent worktrees stood in); a value saved before P7 is settled once (§16.6.6). |
| G16 shared-folder warning | On | — | — | Only matters in a shared folder. |
| G17 reviewers | — | One per lane | One per lane | A pool is the 6+pool template's choice (§16.10.6). |
