None's presets fill every option: Solo = N1 No one, N2 —, N3 none, N4 the whole folder except `.combwork`, `node_modules` and `.venv`, N5 default names, N6 On, N7 as set; Pair = N1 A reviewer agent, N2 On, N3 the quick checks, the rest as Solo; Team = N1 A reviewer agent, then you, N2 On, N3 quick checks + tests, the rest as Solo. (N7 is shown, not set: its owner is Settings → Agents.)

**G19's default since HI-1997** (Darren's decisions, 29 Oct): the branch's own in every preset and All off (`BASE`), since card titles name people and details a public history shouldn't keep. A project keeps Combwork's only by a proven choice: its `workflow.commitMessageChosen` mark (`writeWorkflow` sets it when a write changes G19 to Combwork's, and it stays while G19 is Combwork's) or its merge-choice record saying Combwork's (HI-1697; limited evidence, as the record isn't written for every save), which, where the project only inherited Combwork's, the step writes into its own Git options (marked), those in force or those it keeps while on None, before any default it inherits from is dropped. A one-time step (`commitMessageStep.ts`) switches every other stored Combwork's: a project's own Git options, in force and kept, at the workspace's open (each with its `stepsDone` in the same locked write, then the workspace's own defaults with workspace.json's `stepsDone`, then the board's mark `workflow.commitMessageDefault`), and Combwork's own defaults at startup (with `settings.stepsDone`, the save confirmed). A stored 'branch' is never touched. An ambiguous saved Combwork's is the old default and switches (Darren, 09:31); the hive project, with nothing proving its choice, switches too and is set back to Combwork's in Version Control → Workflow once the build is installed (Darren's answer, option ii), a choice made after the switch and so kept. The upgrade's merge question (HI-1697) starts on the branch's own, with Combwork's marked as how it merged until now.

The Version Control tab documents each preset's choices and why (P6, from this table) [#1122].

#### 16.6.4 All off, and several agents in one folder

[#1112 down] With Git, every option can be off: no review, Not checked, project folder, no checks. Then:
- **Off is really off.** Cards move freely, as today. Combwork still records facts (commits, who did what), so the card
  shows them, but it gates nothing.
- **What never turns off** (data safety): file locks (their own setting; Off there is the user's), never deleting
  `index.lock`, no destructive git (checkout, reset, branch switch, pull) while an agent works in the folder (§8's
  fence, #646), and the merge queue's compare-and-swap on the target (§16.9) [note "What all off means"].
- **Several agents in one folder.** File locks stop two agents editing one file. The remaining risks and helpers:
  commits sweeping in another agent's half-done files (G16 warns, from file-lock records: the paths each agent locks
  while it works a card are recorded on that card, `FilesLocked`, and count while it is the agent's current card, the
  one it started last, until it is Done or back in Todo or on hold; with file locks Off nothing is locked, so G16 has
  nothing to warn of, #1481; `submit.clean` there leaves another agent's recorded files out too); which card a commit
  belongs to (the `Combwork-Card:` trailer, §16.3.2); builds and tests seeing others' unfinished changes (inherent: the
  option's description says so and suggests slots); branch switches and pulls (already held, #646).

#### 16.6.5 Switching

[#1112 down, #1112 UI, #1122 c] Changing the version control or any option shows a warning first: what changes, that
it applies from the next card, and the running lanes and cards in flight it won't affect yet (they finish under their
ruleset, marked "old rules"). Confirming saves the options; nothing running is changed. Switching Git → None (or
back) works the same: cards in flight keep their platform's ruleset; a Git card can't finish under None's rules.

**Built [#1419], switching the version control:**
- **Where:** the header's None · Git choice (`VersionControlHeader.tsx`), the offers (§16.3.5), and the Assistant's
  settings tool (`project.workflow.platform`, within Control, never project agents). One switch for all of them,
  `workflow:setPlatform(projectPath, to, { expected })` (`src/main/workflow/platformSwitch.ts`), under the project's lock
  (`mutateProjectConfig`), with the detection read again there. `workflow:checkPlatform` gives the warning first.
- **Who can pick what** (Darren, 22 Oct, on #1419): **None is never refused for what is detected**, also for a folder
  that is a Git repository (the warning adds that Combwork then records no commits or merges for its cards), or one with
  Mercurial or Jujutsu. **Git** only where a Git repository is found and no other version control is ("Mercurial
  found: not supported yet"). **Git before a repository** (HI-1905, Darren, 27 Oct: "move Initialise repository under
  git. Make Git selectable but only show this option as active until git is initialised locally"): in a None folder
  with no repository of its own (none, or one around it), no other version control and no git problem, Git can be
  chosen as a view (`VersionControl`'s `previewFor`, never saved; gone with None, another project or the tab): Git
  checked in the choice, the fact and the workflow link None's, and only "This folder isn't a Git repository yet" with
  Initialise repository… and its hint, no sections and no preset step. Inside another repository it offers **Use that
  repository…** (the switch, with its warning) and **Initialise its own repository…**. The view stays through an init
  stopped before its first commit (Make first commit…) and the dialog's last failure stays on it once closed
  (`InitRepoEvents.onFailed`); it ends once the folder has a repository of its own with a commit. Init succeeded from
  it (`onInitialised`), `switchAfterInit` switches that project to Git: quietly when nothing keeps None's rules, else
  this warning (cancel leaves it None, with the `gitFound` offer); refused, changed meanwhile or failed, a notice says
  the repository is made but wasn't switched. A switch whose `expected` (the
  platform the window showed) isn't the one in force is refused ("Changed meanwhile"), and so is an options save read
  before a switch (`setWorkflowOptions` checks the platform under the lock). The window greys Git out with the same
  reason; `project:updateConfig` refuses `platform`.
- **The warning:** what changes, that it applies from the next card, the running lanes and the cards in flight
  (`cardsInFlight`, as for options) that keep their platform's ruleset; for a Git card in flight, that its merge queue
  carries on and stays in the tab and the panel until clear. **No "Apply to cards in flight"** across platforms.
- **Each platform keeps its own options and answer:** project.json's `platform` and `workflow.platform` change together;
  `setKept` (`projectWorkflow.ts`, beside `writeWorkflow`) puts the platform left into `workflow.kept[<it>]` (its
  preset, options and `presetAsked`, when it has any) and brings the one chosen back from `kept` (its entry removed),
  else no preset, no options and no answer, so #1423's step offers its presets. Ordinary saves change only the platform
  in force and keep `kept`. A project the upgrade hasn't given `workflow` yet changes only its `platform`.
- **After a switch:** the project is read again (its offer gone), and `workflow-changed` and `queue-changed` tell the
  windows. A card in flight keeps its own ruleset in the runtime (each card's adapter is its ruleset's platform), and
  the merge queue starts a workspace's queues with open entries for a None project too, so an old Git queue drains
  after Git → None (its merge commit's identity: git's own, HI-2266). The tab's Merge queue section stays while
  #1356's actual-state rule shows a queue (§16.6, #1416).

#### 16.6.6 Where options live

- **Storage** (OP-5): the project's options in `project.json` (`workflow: { platform, preset, options }`), written with
  `workspace.mutateProjectConfig()`; **[#1417]** `workflow` also keeps `kept` (the other platforms' preset, options and
  answer, #1419) and `presetAsked` (the answer to "How do you work?" for the platform in force, #1423), and has **one
  writer**: `writeWorkflow` (`src/shared/workflow/projectWorkflow.ts`) sets the platform, preset and options and keeps
  every other field, for the form's Save, presets and Paste and for `cw_update_setting`; `kept` and `presetAsked` are
  written by helpers beside it, never by replacing the object; workspace defaults in `workspace.json`, global defaults in config — resolved
  global → workspace → project like other settings (§5; the card loops' rounds and wait too, since HI-1766: §16.6.7)
  [note §11]. An option unset at a level inherits. **Built [#1263]:** the global and
  workspace defaults are per platform (`workflow: { git: {…}, none: {…} }` in Combwork's config and in `workspace.json`),
  over the platform's all-off (§16.6.4), each option with its origin (platform, global, workspace, project). They are
  checked as they are read: an unknown option, a value it doesn't take (its type, or one of its choices: a `finish`
  of `typo`), a project's options for another platform or a contradiction (§16.5.4) makes the project work with every rule off (all-off), logged once, never an error at a
  move. The upgrade (#1218) writes a project's options whole, so its own values win until the Version Control tab
  (#1278) lets an option inherit again.
- **One switch for every rule** [#1263, #1120's table]: Settings → Advanced → *Workflow rules are enforced*
  (`cw.workflow.enforce`, on by default) turns every gate off at once, in every project, whatever their options:
  facts are still recorded, nothing is refused or asked, and reconciliation records only (§16.4.4), as in P3. Each
  rule has its own option too.
- The resolved options and their origins are readable by agents (`cw_project_status`) and settable by the user, and
  by the Assistant within Control (as settings are, `cw_update_setting`), never by project agents [note §3].
- **Export**: a project's options can be copied as JSON from the tab and pasted into another project (OP-5).
- **Built [#1422], the defaults at each level**: since HI-1768 both in **Settings → Version Control** (section id
  `workflow`, after Board): **Combwork defaults** (`workflow.defaults`, "for every workspace") and **Workspace defaults
  (<name>)** (`workflow.workspaceDefaults`, shown while a workspace is open; before HI-1768 Settings → Workflow defaults
  and Settings → Workspace → Workflow defaults; the values stay where they were, config.json and workspace.json). Since
  HI-1837 they are two **tabs** under the section's intro line, each showing only its own form and its own line; both
  forms stay mounted while the section shows, so switching (or a search offering one tab) keeps each draft, and a tab
  with an unsaved draft is marked. The tab last chosen is remembered (`ui.tabs['settings.workflow']`); a search offers
  only the tabs it finds; a **From Combwork defaults** or **From the workspace** origin (an option's, or the copied files')
  links to its tab (`showWorkflowDefaults`). Each with a None · Git choice of which platform's it shows,
  in #1418's editor in a level mode (`WorkflowLevelForm`): the same groups, labels, presets, All off and live
  contradictions; a value set at the level says *Set here*, and Inherit goes back to the level below (the workspace's
  to Combwork's, Combwork's to the platform's all-off). G12 (the project's identity) and the rows shown elsewhere aren't at a
  level. `workflow:levelForm`, `workflow:levelCheck` and `workflow:setLevel` (`src/main/workflow/levels.ts`):
  - a level is resolved on its own and checked as a project's save is;
  - its check lists each project inheriting a changed option (Combwork's level: every open workspace's projects; a project
    setting an option itself isn't), what changes for it, its running lanes and cards in flight (they keep their rules:
    from the next card);
  - **a level that would make an inheriting project contradictory is refused**, naming the project and its reason (an
    `inheritor` problem), rather than leaving that project at all-off; the all-off fall-back stays for files edited by
    hand;

    `saveWorkspaceConfigWith` (workspace.json, kept with a backup), its base checked again as it is written.

  `workspace.workflow.<git|none>.<option>`, workspace scope; null inherits), saved through the same checks.

#### 16.6.7 Card loops and file locks as options (HI-1766)

Darren's decisions (26 Oct): Card loops' options and File locks move into the workflow options, for None and Git, and
Project Settings loses its **Card loops** and **Workflow** sections (the second was only a link to this form).

- **The options:** `loopWakes` (Wake reviewers and builders, on), `loopRounds` (Rounds, 10, 1–50), `loopWaitHours` (Wait
  in hours, 6, 1–24), `loopStepWaitMinutes` (Design check wait in minutes, 30, 1–240) under a group of their own, **Card
  loops**, and `fileLocks` (File locks: Block, Ask me, Warn or Off) under Where cards are built (Git) or The work
  (None), always shown, with "Applies to agents working in the same folder, outside a slot." Inherited Combwork (Settings →
  Version Control → Combwork defaults) → workspace (its Workspace defaults) → project (Version Control → Workflow), each row saying where its
  value comes from, and saved with the form's Save at every level (`shared/workflow/options.ts`).
- **Preferences, not rules** (`PREFERENCE_OPTIONS`): left out of every ruleset (`ruleOptions`), so a change applies at
  once and makes nothing "old rules", and no ruleset id changes; no preset or All off sets them; they never make the
  options Custom; choosing a preset or All off keeps the draft's own (`withUnpreset`); options holding only them don't
  answer "How do you work?" (`asksPreset`).
- **Read when used**, each resolving on its own (`shared/workflow/preferences.ts` `preferencesOf`; main's
  `projectPreferences`), so options whose rules contradict (which fall back to All off) keep their loop settings: the
  wakes (loop wakes, tasks, card watches, the loop check), a lane's rounds and wait as it registers (a running lane keeps
  its own; a request's still win), a design's wait as it is posted (a step waiting keeps its `until`), the board's
  stall, and the file locks of every edit. The Assistant's home isn't a project: its locks stay off.
- **Moved once, nothing lost:** config.json's `agents.fileLocks` becomes Combwork's default for None and Git; workspace.json's
  `loops` the workspace's `loopRounds`/`loopWaitHours` for both; a project's `loopWakes` (false), `loopRounds`,
  `loopWaitHours`, `loopStepWaitMinutes` and `fileLocks` its own options, for the platform in force and each kept
  platform. A value already in the new place wins (key presence); a default saved into every file (Block, wakes on,
  nothing set, Inherit) is no choice and isn't carried. Each is pure on read and written with the file's next save, so
  an old key goes only with its replacement. A project with no workflow options keeps its old keys, read as its own
  (the form shows them so), until it has options: giving it some would choose a workflow for it, and the 1.0 upgrade
  and "How do you work?" go by whether it has any.
- **Removed:** Settings → Workspace's Card loop rounds and wait (`workspace:setLoops`), Settings → Agents → File locks,
  Project Settings → Card loops, → Agents → File locks and → Workflow. The settings tool's rows are the options'
  (`workflow.<p>.loopRounds`, `workspace.workflow.<p>.…`, `project.workflow.loopRounds`…); cw_lane's rounds and wait
  left out are "the project's workflow options (Card loops)".

#### 16.6.8 Maximum agents (HI-2001)

Darren's decisions (29 Oct): the number of agents a project has is its team, recorded in its workflow; it doesn't
need to be in Advanced. A new user asking the Assistant to "get this done fast" shouldn't suddenly have six more agents.

- **The option:** `maxAgents` (**Maximum agents**, 1–24) for None and Git, first in the Workflow section under a group
  of its own, **Team**, inherited Combwork → workspace → project like the card loops (§16.6.7) and resolved the same way
  (`preferencesOf`: options whose rules contradict keep it). Not a rule: left out of every ruleset (`ruleOptions`), so
  no ruleset id changes and a change applies at once. **Set by the presets and All off** (`PRESET_PREFERENCES`, the
  one preference they set): Solo 1, Pair 2 (both Pairs), Team 12, All off 12; 12 where no level sets it. Changing it
  never makes the options Custom: a team of another size works the same way.
- **Whom it binds:** the Assistant and every Agent API caller (`cw_add_agent`, `POST /v1/projects/:name/agents`, the
  Assistant's template load) add agents only up to it, checked again under the project's lock; at it, a refusal (409,
  never a 500: HI-1952) naming it, its value, that it is the user's team size and where the user raises it, so the
  Assistant can pass that on. Combwork enforces it rather than adding guidance (HI-2010): the refusal is the rule, and the
  settings tool lists the option as sensitive, read-only to the Assistant, at every level, so it can't raise it. **It binds
  the user too** (HI-2058, Darren's decision of 29 Oct, replacing HI-2001's "the user adds past it by hand"): at it, the
  window's every way to add one (+ Add ▾'s entries, the Add Agent dialog, the shortcut's quick add, the Project
  Settings agent list's Add, Sessions' resume in a new agent, Add Agent from Template) is greyed out or refused, saying
  *This project's workflow allows n agents: raise Maximum agents in Version Control → Workflow*, with **Open Workflow
  Options** where there is room (the quick add's warning, the dialog's banner). Main refuses it too, under the lock.
- **Saved as the other options are** (HI-2058): its box in the Workflow form, and in the workspace's and Combwork's
  defaults, stages each value in range as it is typed or stepped, so Save lights and the row is marked before the box
  loses focus; Discard Changes drops it, and Save writes it at the page's level. A blank or invalid box waits for blur.
- **Lowering it removes no agents:** a project with more keeps them, its row saying none is removed but none can be
  added until it has fewer. Above 12 the row has the note on what more agents cost (the one Settings → Advanced's Agents per project had).
  The project's slot pool is its builders, at most its Maximum agents (§16.10).
- **Templates carry it** (`TEMPLATE_CARRIED`): a saved template's workflow has its project's; Combwork's own carry their
  size (Team 6 + pool: 8). **A load raises it by itself** (HI-2058, Darren's decision): the user's load with its
  workflow applied saves the template's own Maximum agents (`loadedMaxAgents`: the section's value, never under the
  agents loaded, as the project's own even when it equals the inherited one, so a later change to the defaults leaves it;
  with none it can take, the agents' count, only ever raising the project's) with the agents, in the same
  write of project.json, checked under its lock against the final list. The Load dialog says *Maximum agents goes from n
  to m for this project, saved with its agents*; the rest of its workflow is filled in for Save… as before (the option
  isn't in that overlay, so Discard Changes keeps it). Without its workflow, a load with more agents than the maximum is
  refused before anything changes: Load is greyed out, saying so, with **Open Workflow Options**. Past 24 it is refused
  either way. The Assistant's load is refused over the maximum, and the workflow it saves never changes Maximum agents.
- **Moved once, nothing lost:** Settings → Advanced → **Agents per project** is gone. advanced.json's value becomes
  Combwork's Maximum agents for None and Git at startup, where they don't set it, and is then dropped from the file
  (`migrateAgentsPerProject`, kept until then as `LEGACY_ADVANCED`); a workspace's own (workspace.json `advanced`)
  becomes the workspace's, on read, written with its next save. A project already over its new maximum keeps its agents.

### 16.7 Moves and gates

Every change to a card's stage goes through the runtime at the single place every card change passes
(`tasks.ts` update → `boardWrite`) [note §11]. Today any column can go to any column (`isTaskColumn` alone,
`tasks.ts:1002`), and an agent's unplaced `column: 'done'` patch isn't refused (only creates, placements and reorders
are, `tasks.ts:854`, `:705`, `:752`): 1.0 closes that.

#### 16.7.1 Who moves cards

| Actor | How | Refused |
|---|---|---|
| Project agent | Intents only (§16.8). `cw_update_task` keeps edits that aren't moves (comments, labels, blocked, description, links); its `column` is refused with the intent to use instead [#1112 E]. | By the ruleset's guards; never overrides. With every option off the ruleset has no guard that can refuse an ordinary move (only `submit.notDuplicate`, which stops a second copy of a waiting submission), so intents always succeed: start → submit → Done, the free flow of today [#1112 down]. |
| The user (window) | Drag or menu, as today. | Never refused: a move that skips a rule asks first, then records an `Override` (§16.8.4) [#1112 C]. A move that skips nothing just moves. |
| The Assistant | `cw_update_task` column moves, within Control, as today; a move that skips a rule needs `override: { reason }` explicitly, else refused with the rules it would skip [note §3]. | |
| Combwork | Actions (§16.5.3) and reconciliation. | — |

**Built [#1265]:** the user's and the Assistant's column moves go through the card's runtime (`tasks.ts` `gateOf` →
`Workflow.move`) when the rules are enforced (§16.6.6's switch), the card is from 1.0 and its ruleset has the stage
moved to; the runtime writes the move's facts (the recorder writes none of them for such a change: one owner per fact),
and the card's 0.9 fields (column, place, history, agent, review) follow in each of its writes' transactions. **Interim
until #1290 and #1275:** the user's moves don't ask yet (every one runs confirmed: a move that skips a rule records its
`Override` with no reason), and a move to a column the ruleset doesn't have (Review with no review) keeps P3's recorded
move; the window's `tasks:move` already returns the question (`ask: rules`) when not confirmed. **A drag is decided
whole** [HR2's #1265 round 1]: its steps (start, submission, the review skipped) are gathered first, outside the lock,
the submission on the state the start would leave; the rules they skip together are one question, one refusal or one
`Override` (written after the submission it approves, past Review); then every step is written in one transaction,
which a rule not decided on undoes (asked again). A submission refused for what no override makes true stops the drag
after its start (§16.8.4), the start written alone. With the rules not enforced, the runtime runs no guard for any
intent (`cfg.enforced`). A batch's card is a part of the batch's change undone on its own when refused (savepoint),
its `Refused` kept. **Built [#1290]:** the window's move (`tasks:move`) has §16.8.4's drag semantics whole: the
question names only the rules that refuse; a stage the card's ruleset lacks is refused with why (`move.noStage`: the
stages it has, and that they follow its Version Control options); a Done card dragged past Todo is reopened and started
in one write (a new cycle, nothing skipped by the reopening); On Hold's returns as above; with the rules not enforced,
every move just moves. Until the window asks through it (#1275), its drags (`tasks:update`) stay confirmed, and a column
the ruleset lacks keeps P3's move there. Agents' column moves and reviews are their intents (§16.17's transition,
**built [#1268]**). A builder with its own worktree starts there whatever the folder option says (it stands in for a
slot, §16.19.1; P3 recorded it so too), with no `prepareSlot`.

#### 16.7.2 The total table

[P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 2] The table is written over five dimensions; every supported combination has a
path to Done, and the rest are contradictions refused when the options are saved (§16.5.4).

| Dimension | Values |
|---|---|
| **R** review (G1/N1) | none · agent · agent then you · you |
| **Q** reviewers (G1b) | 1 · 2 (only with an agent) |
| **M** who finishes (G5) | Git: Combwork merges · the agent merges · committed is done · not checked. None: accept. |
| **F** folder (G11) | slots · project folder (Git); project folder (None) |
| **K** card kind | code · no-code |

**Contradictions:** M = Combwork merges or the agent merges needs each card in its own folder (F = slots, or before P7 an agent's worktree, §16.19.1); M = committed is done needs F = project
folder (the folder's line is the target); G10 is hidden when R includes you; Q = 2 needs R with an agent.

**The moves**, for every combination (a move not listed for the current stage is refused with the move that is):

| From | Event | Guards (only those the ruleset holds) | To, and actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Todo | **start** (builder, or the user's Start) | `start.notBlocked`, `start.dependenciesIntegrated`, `start.slotAvailable` | Active · `recordStart`, `prepareSlot` (F = slots) |
| Active | **put back** (builder) | — | Todo · `releaseSlot` |
| Active | **submit** (builder) | `submit.notDuplicate`, `submit.ready`, `submit.clean`, `submit.trailer`, `submit.identity`, `submit.checksPassed`, `submit.ownRunsStopped`, `submit.decisionsReceived` (K = no-code: only the last two and `notDuplicate`) | R ≠ none: **Review** · `recordSubmitted`, `prepareReviewCopy`, then `wakeReviewer` (R = agent…) or `askUser(approve)` (R = you). R = none: **Finish** (below). |
| Review | **start review** (reviewer) | `review.notAuthor`, `review.decisionsReceived`; an agent's start also `review.inProgress` (HI-2487, enforced with the rules on, not a ruleset's guard: read in the write): refused while another agent reviews the submission (started, no verdict since, still one of the project's agents with its session running), as many as G1b's passes still needed may review at once; it names that reviewer and for how long. A review the user started counts too, until its verdict (HR1's round 1). The user's start takes any review over; one whose reviewer left or stopped is free. Who is present unread, a review in progress refuses it as unknown (`platform.unknown`, "whether the reviewers of … are still running"), never taken for its reviewer gone. Seen 3 Nov: HR1, on a stale wake, took HI-2444's review from HR2 mid-review. The board's verdict patch that starts a review checks it too | Review · `ReviewStarted` |
| Review | **submit** with `followUp` (its builder; HI-1832), unstale | as Active's submit, and `submit.followUpNotBuilder` (an agent other than the card's agent on the board now, or, given to nobody, its cycle's builder), read again in the write | Review (no move) · `recordSubmitted` (`followUp`, the same round), `prepareReviewCopy`, wake the reviewer to start again; a plain submit there is `move.notFromHere` (its builder told of `followUp`) |
| Review | **verdict pass** | `verdict.reviewing`, `verdict.currentSubmission`, `review.notAuthor`, `review.decisionsReceived` | passes on this submission (or the same change) < Q: Review ("1 of 2 passed"). ≥ Q and R = agent then you: Review · `askUser(approve)`. Else **Finish**. |
| Review | **verdict fail** | the same | Active · wake the builder; a round (§16.11.4) |
| Review | **user approves** (R = you, or agent then you after the quorum) | `approval.given` | **Finish** |
| Review | **user declines** | — | Active · wake the builder; a round |
| Approved | **user approves** (G10's request) | `approval.given` | **Finish (merge step)** |
| Approved | **report merge** (builder; M = the agent merges, or not checked) | `done.contained` (not with not checked); `approval.given` when G10 applies, and with not checked a stale pass refuses it too (`integrate.approved`, cause stale: nothing checks what was merged, so the OK must be for the work there) (#1592) | Done · `recordIntegrated (by agent)`; with not checked, Done with no `Integrated` (nothing was checked, and §16.8.4 never fakes one; a later observed integration adds it) [P2] |
| Approved | **submit** after a stale pass | as Active's submit | Review |
| Approved | **retry merge** (the user's, or the Assistant's with a reason; Combwork merges, no queue entry, no follow-up waiting) | `integrate.approved` (a stale pass refuses it, naming **submit** as the way on) | Merging · `enqueue` [#1623] |
| Merging | queue: merged | `integrate.*`, `done.contained` | Done · `recordIntegrated`, `releaseSlot`, `endLaneIfDone` |
| Merging | queue: returned | — | Active · `returnToBuilder` (§16.9) |
| Active | **submit** after a queue failure, same approved unstale revision, no submission since the failure (HI-2504: one since, such as a conflict's merge commit reviewed and failed, is resubmitted as after any fail) | `submit.notDuplicate`, `requeue.allowed`, `integrate.approved`, `submit.decisionsReceived` (HI-2275) | Merging · `enqueue` (no review, no round) |
| any | a decision recorded | — | `wakeOnDecision`; an Approved or Merging card: Review if the ruleset has review, else Active (stale, why: decision since), and `cancelEntry` (§16.4.6) |

**Finish** (after review, or straight after submit with R = none):

| K, M | Then |
|---|---|
| code, Combwork merges | G10 applies: Approved · `askUser(approve)`, then the merge step. Else **Merging** · `enqueue`. |
| code, the agent merges | Approved; the builder merges and reports (above). G10 asks first, as above. |
| code, committed is done | `done.contained` on the folder's line (its revision is on the target by construction) → Done · `recordIntegrated (method: committed)`. A Pair project in its folder thus reviews before Done; the work is on the target meanwhile, which the option's description says. |
| code, not checked | R ≠ none, or G10 applies: Approved, then report merge (unchecked) or the user's move; G10 asks first, as above, and report merge waits for its OK (#1592). Else Done. |
| None, code | `accept`: `Accepted` of the submitted revision if the card's paths still hash to it, else Stale → Review (§16.3.3) → Done. |
| None, no-code | `Accepted` of the submission → Done. |
| no-code (Git) | `Accepted` of the submission → Done; no `Integrated` fact. |

**Stale passes:** an Approved card whose pass becomes stale (§16.4.4) stays Approved with the mark (a Merging one's
entry is cancelled and it shows in Approved), until its builder submits again → Review.

#### 16.7.3 No-code cards

[#1112 plan "no-code kind… from day one", note §5] A card's **kind** is `code` (default) or `no-code`, set when the
card is created, by the user or the Assistant (the kind is adopted "from day one" [#1112 plan]; OP-6 confirms who
sets it, and OP-7 whether agents may propose it in the create call for the user or the Assistant to confirm).
No-code cards have no revision: a submission is a summary (its submission id is what a verdict names), and they skip
`submit.ready`, `submit.clean`, `submit.trailer`, `submit.identity`, `submit.checksPassed`, `done.contained` and the
queue. With review they finish when the review (and approval, if any) passes; without review, submit finishes them.
Changing the kind later is the user's, recorded as an override.

**Built (#1277).** The kind is the card's `kind` column. The user (the New Card dialog's **No code (a decision, a
write-up, a trial…)**) and the Assistant (`kind` on `POST /v1/tasks` and `cw_create_task`) make a no-code card at
once; a project agent's `kind: "no-code"` is only **proposed** (OP-7: a `KindProposed` fact, the card stays code): its
tile marks it ("No code?") and its dialog asks **Confirm No Code** / **Keep as Code** (the Assistant: `confirmKind` on
`PATCH /v1/tasks/{n}` and `cw_update_task`), answered by a `KindDecided` fact. Changed later, the user's change asks
first (the rule *A card's kind is set when it is made*, `card.kind`; a reason; **Change Anyway**) and the Assistant's
needs `override.reason`; either records one `Override` (`card.kind`); agents never change or answer it (`403`). The
card shows **No code** on its tile and in its dialog's **Kind** (with **Make It Code…** / **Make It No Code…**); the
Agent API's card adds `kind` and, while one is open, `kindProposed` after its document's fields, just before `stage`.

**Review: Skip (#1625; Darren, 25 Oct).** Any card, code or no code, can skip its review, decided when it is made or
before it is submitted: not a project option, and Pair and Team still review everything else. Set, the card runs under
its rules with no review (`skipReviewOf`: its ruleset compiled with `review: none`, its id the base's with
`~skipReview`, so the base is found again and *old rules* compares the base), whenever the skip was set: its submission
finishes it. A no-code card is Done; a code card goes on as its finish says (Combwork merges: straight to the merge queue,
whose merge checks and `done.contained` still hold; G10's OK before merging still applies, as it isn't a review). Who:
the user (the New Card dialog's **Skip review**, with an optional note; the card dialog's **Review**: **Skip Review…** /
**Review It**), and the Assistant only with the user's reason (`skipReview` on `POST /v1/tasks`, `PATCH /v1/tasks/{n}`,
`cw_create_task` and `cw_update_task`; `false` sets it back). A project agent's (or the workspace token's)
`skipReview` at creation is only **proposed** (a `ReviewSkipProposed` fact with its reason; the tile shows *Skip
review?*, the dialog **Skip Review** / **Keep Review**), answered by the user or the Assistant, the Assistant with the
user's reason, never the agent's (kept in the fact as `proposed`, for history); agents never set or answer it (`403`).
Each decision is a `ReviewSkipSet` fact (`skip`, `by`, `reason`). Refused where the card's rules have no review
(nothing to skip), and once a submission waits for review or later (in Review: the way past it is the user's override
of the move; approved, merging or Done: nothing left to skip). The tile and the dialog show **Review skipped** with who
set it and why; the Agent API's card adds `reviewSkipped: { by, reason }` and `reviewSkipProposed` when there is one.

#### 16.7.4 Other moves

[P1, answering HB3's round 1 finding 15]
- **No review with Combwork merges:** submit → Finish → Merging (§16.7.2's Finish table): Active → Merging directly.
- **Reopening a Done card** (the user moves it back, or the Assistant within Control): no rule is skipped, so no
  override. Its next start is a new cycle: a new `Started` with a new line from the target's head; the earlier facts,
  pins and `Integrated` stay in its history.
- **On Hold** (the user's) for a card in Approved or Merging cancels its queue entry (`IntegrationCancelled`, reason
  hold) and keeps its slot's lease; leaving On Hold returns it to the stage it was in, and an Approved card of a
  Combwork-merges ruleset is queued again. A held Active card keeps its lease too; the lane pauses ("AM-12 on hold").
- **Your approvals carry over** by the same rule as passes (G4): a clean rebase by the queue keeps them.
- **Dependencies and per-card targets** (OP-12): `start.dependenciesIntegrated` checks each `blockedBy` card in **the
  dependent card's target**: integrated into that target, or found in it by containment (merged into `release`,
  then `release` into `main`); a card integrated only elsewhere still blocks [P2, #1118 20 Oct].
- **A new project before a preset is chosen:** the detected platform's all-off options (§16.6.4), the free flow of
  today, until the user picks a preset or sets an option.

### 16.8 The Agent API: intents, refusals, overrides

#### 16.8.1 Intents

[#1112 E] Agents act by intent; Combwork moves the card. Each intent is an Agent API route and a Combwork tool (the tool
packaging, one tool per intent or one tool with actions, is P4's to settle by the scenarios' results: §16.20 OP-8).
Each takes a card reference (§16.12) and replies with what moved, lean (`shared/toolReplies.ts`), or a refusal
(§16.8.3).

| Intent | Who | Arguments | Effect (§16.7.2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **start** | The card's builder (or an agent given it) | card | Todo → Active. Replies with the folder (slot path), line, base and target. |
| **put back** | The builder | card, why | Active → Todo; the slot is released. |
| **submit** | The builder | card, summary (comment), revision (optional: default the card's revision: its folder's head for a card with its own line, its newest attributed commit in a shared folder, §16.3.2), note (required when the revision was already reviewed: what changed in the answer, if not the code), paths (None: the card's paths, pre-filled, with any unclaimed changes to add or leave, §16.3.3). "Submit" is always **submit for review**: it hands committed work over and never commits (Darren, HI-1618). Nothing committed is refused in git's words (`submit.empty`: "Nothing committed to review."), its next step by the card's folder (HI-2227): uncommitted changes are committed by an agent doing the card, while one asked only to submit it asks the user before committing (HI-2257, Darren's decision: both rules, said only in the refusal), and with none a card that needs no change is no-code, asked for with `cw_ask_user` (action noCode) or, already decided, `cw_ask_assistant`; and a None card with no file changed by `submit.unchanged`. followUp (HI-1832): from Review, its builder's commit the reviewer asked for | → Review, or → Finish without review, or → Merging after a queue failure; a follow-up stays in Review. |
| **declare paths** | The builder (None) | card, paths | The card's paths (§16.3.3); replies with the pre-fill, the unclaimed changes and the current revision. |
| **start review** | A reviewer | card, submission (optional: default the latest) | `ReviewStarted`; replies with the review copy's path, the revision, base and files. |
| **verdict** | A reviewer | card, submission, pass/fail, kind of fail (content / explanation), comment | §16.7.2 |
| **report merge** | The builder (M = the agent merges, or not checked) | card, result revision | Combwork checks containment (unless not checked), then Done. |
| **ask the user** | Builder or reviewer | card, kind (approve, decide, test, sign-in, other), text, revision? | For you (§16.8.5) |
| **couldn't within the rules** | Builder or reviewer | card, rule, why | `CannotWithinRules`: a For you of kind decide; never a failed round, never a stall [#1120 c, #686] |
| **request to builder** | The reviewer | card, text | `ReviewerRequest`; wakes the builder now (#912) [#1120 c]. Codex reviewers get the tool (#913). |
| **card loop step** | The builder (design, followUp, proceed) or the reviewer (ok, gaps) | card, step, text | `LoopStep`; moves nothing; wakes the other side (§16.8.2) [#1382, #1467]. |

**The same revision again** [P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 7]: a revision that failed review may be submitted
again unchanged, with a note (the reviewer asked for an explanation, or a check failed for a reason outside the
code); it is a new submission and its review a new round. After a **queue failure**, an approved and unstale revision
is submitted again straight into the queue, no review, no round, but only after a failure marked transient (a check
that didn't start, a network error, a timeout) and at most twice in a row (`requeue.allowed`); a red check is a result,
so it needs a new revision, or the user's **Retry merge** on the queue card (recorded as an override) for a check the
user knows is flaky [HR2's round 2 finding 1, HB3's E]. Only verdicts count as rounds, fails of either kind; queue failures and the
user's approvals don't (a user's decline does).

**Built in P4** [#1267]: each intent is `POST /v1/tasks/{card}/<intent>` (`put-back`, `submit`, `declare-paths`,
`start-review`, `verdict`, `report-merge`, `ask`, `cannot`, `request`; **start** is `POST /v1/tasks/{card}/start`
called by a project agent with its own token, the Assistant's call there still starting a card on an agent) and a Combwork
tool each, OP-8's starting point (`cw_start_card`, `cw_put_back`, `cw_submit`, `cw_declare_paths`,
`cw_start_review`, `cw_verdict`, `cw_report_merge`, `cw_ask_user`, `cw_cannot_within_rules`,
`cw_request_builder`). Every agent has them, Codex's included (its enabled tools are the server's whole list, #913);
the Assistant has them all but `cw_start_card` at Control agents, through `assistantChange()` (listed in its actions,
refused at Look and advise). Each runs on the board's one intent path (#1265's `runIntent`), so the runtime's guards
decide, its facts are written once, and the card's board fields follow in each write: start gives the card to the agent
that starts it; a reviewer's verdict, request and the rest keep it its builder's; submit's summary, a verdict's and a
request's text are comments. Replies are a line (`intentText`): the card, the stage it left and the one it is in, what
the intent says (start: folder, line, base, target; start review: revision, base, files), what comes next on the card
(#1530, `shared/workflow/nextStep.ts`, from its state and rules after start, put back, submit, a verdict, report merge
and the queue's two: what its agent can do now, as the Combwork tools, the verdict after start review; or a reviewer's
verdict, the user's OK asked under For you, its builder's merge and report, Combwork's queue, or done. Agents follow it
rather than infer the step from a column; the user is next only while Combwork has asked them) and submit's warnings (G16:
another agent's files in a shared folder, never a refusal; the card's work view shows them with the submission). Put
back's why is a comment and the `Moved` fact's `why`; ask's revision (default the latest submission's) and Test
checklist are the `ApprovalRequested` fact's `revision` and `checklist`, for For you to show (P5). Every write of an
intent but start keeps the card's agent as it is then, under the board's lock (`keepAgent`): a reviewer's verdict
never takes the card, nor undoes a reassignment made while the intent read its platform. The Agent API's contract
version is 6.

The `review` parameter of `cw_update_task` maps onto the intents for one release (P4): `start` onto **start review**
(of the latest submission), `passed`/`failed` onto **verdict** on that submission; it is retired in P8 with the skills
[P1]. Tool descriptions say the arguments and side effects; skills say the workflow (AGENTS.md's one owner per rule).

#### 16.8.2 Card loops on intents

- **Combwork arms the watch at a lane's handoff** (#1639, built). On 25 Oct two builders submitted their lane's card and
  ended their turn with no card watch, and their lanes showed as stalled (#376's check) until the Assistant asked each to
  watch: card-loop's "watch, then submit" was missed. The step is Combwork's now (`main/intentWatch.ts`): an agent's
  `cw_submit` of a card in its running lane (active or paused) where it is the builder, leaving the card in Review,
  arms its card watch for the review (`changes: verdict, column, comment`, `column: passed`), and its failing
  `cw_verdict` as the lane's reviewer arms one for the next round (`column: review`, `fresh`), each for the lane's wait
  (at most a watch's longest). The watch starts from the card as the intent left it (`registerWatch`'s `start`), so a
  verdict given before it is armed still fires it. An agent with a watch of its own keeps it: one that includes the card
  is said so, one on other cards (or an agent or lane watch) isn't replaced, since it isn't stalled and the loop wake
  tells it of the verdict. The intent's reply says what was armed (`watch`: "Combwork watches HI-12 for you, for its review
  …: end your turn, and it wakes you."); card-loop says to end the turn on it, and to start the watch itself only where
  the reply says none was armed. Not for the pool's reviewers (no lane of theirs) or the Assistant.
- The builder's watch wakes on a verdict, a `Moved` into Approved or Done, a `ReviewerRequest`, a `Decision`, and the
  user's pane reply when relayed (#922) [#1120 c].

  **Built in P4** [#1272]: a card watch (or a bounded wait) that counts a verdict, a move or a comment also counts a
  reviewer's request (its history line, "Asked the builder: …", written with its comment) and a decision recorded,
  changed or removed; one waiting only to see a card in a column (a reviewer waiting for its arrival) doesn't, nor the
  watcher's own. Its line says so ("(its reviewer asks you something; a new decision from the user: read its
  decisions)"). Each event wakes once: where an agent's watch counts it, or its line has told it, the loop wake for a
  request and the decision line for a decision stand aside (`watchCovers`, `watchToldDecisions`). A lane watch counts a
  card's block lifted (`unblocked`, by default) and names the lane's merge commit at its end; the user's pane reply to a
  lane's agent is told to the Assistant on its own (#1099).
- **A design first** (#1382, built [#1382]). The Assistant often asks a builder for a design before it builds (a recurring
  finding, a card with open questions), and on 21 Oct #1305's sat six hours: its builder posted the design as a comment
  in Doing, and its reviewer's watch counted only arrivals in Review. It is a step Combwork knows: the **card loop step**
  intent (`cw_loop_step`, `POST /v1/tasks/{card}/loop-step`) writes a `LoopStep` fact, its text as a comment and a
  history line ("Posted a design for the reviewer to check: …", "Checked the design: OK: …", "Checked the design:
  gaps: …", "Went ahead with the design unchecked: …"), and moves nothing. The builder posts `design` in Doing: it is
  named (`<key>/s<seq>`) and its check is due the project's workflow option **Design check wait** (Card loops, §16.6.7) after its post (30
  minutes by default), both kept in its fact and returned (`design`, `until`, `waitMinutes`); a start's reply gives the
  wait (`designWaitMinutes`), so the builder arms its watch before posting. The reviewer answers `ok` or `gaps`; with no
  answer by `until`, the builder sends `proceed` and builds as posted. An answer and `proceed` name the design they are
  about (`design`), and one about another design is refused (`loop.staleStep`), so a late answer never settles a newer
  design; posting again replaces the one waiting. A design's comment starts with a line naming it ("Design HI-12/s40, for
  the reviewer's check (an answer names HI-12/s40):"), so the reviewer has its id however it hears of it: the loop wake,
  its own watch's line (which quotes a comment's first line) or `cw_read_task` with `latestComment`. `proceed` before the check is due is refused (`loop.tooEarly`), and a
  design's deadline never moves (a changed setting, a watch started again, a restart). Each side only its own
  (`loop.stepNotYours`): the builder's steps by the card's builder; an answer by its reviewer, the reviewer of its running
  lane, else the agent of its latest review started or verdict (by id: a rename doesn't lose it; for a card from before
  1.0, the agent whose board name last started reviewing it), while it is one of the project's agents (a removed one
  can't be woken), never its builder; the user and the Assistant take either. One rule decides this for acceptance and
  for delivery (`loopReviewerOf`, `loopReviewer.ts`), read inside the step's own board change (the runtime's `prepare`,
  before its transaction). Every change that takes an agent out of a project (a removal, a merge's clean-up, a template's
  load, any `agents` patch) publishes under the same board lock: `mutateProjectConfig` sees an agent id leave and,
  outside a board change, writes nothing and runs again inside one (lock order: agent names, board, project.json). So
  a removal is either before a design's read (refused) or after its write, never between. A design with no reviewer to check it is refused (`loop.noReviewer`), as is one outside Doing
  (`loop.stepNotHere`), and an answer or `proceed` with nothing waiting (`loop.noStep`); with the rules off, none is.
  Each step is a loop wake: a design (`step`, asking for a check, naming the design) and going ahead (`stepNotice`, a
  notice with nothing to answer) to the card's reviewer, an answer (`stepAnswer`) to the builder. They are delivered
  whatever the agent's own watch counts, so a reviewer waiting only for Review is woken; a watch that counts a verdict, a
  move or a comment hears a step as it hears a request (`step` among its changes: "a card loop step: read its latest
  comment"), and then the loop wake stands aside. A design's wake waiting for its reviewer is dropped once nothing waits
  (answered by someone else, posted again: the newer one is told). Off with the workflow option Wake reviewers and builders (Card loops). A
  design left waiting is a stall (beside #1410's deadlock, `loopStepWait` in `shared/tasks.ts`): the card in Doing, not
  blocked, its builder only watching it five minutes after its check was due (the deadline its history line kept, never
  restarted by a new watch) ("HB5 posted a design on #1305 for its reviewer to check and has waited 40 min: nobody has
  answered it, and it hasn't gone ahead as posted"), on the board, in the Agent API's `stalled` and in lane watches'
  `stalled` events. The card-loop skill says when to post one and how each side answers.
- **A follow-up checked** (#1467, built [#1467]). On 22 Oct #1417 and #1419 stalled the same way in Review and Approved:
  the Assistant's screenshot OK asked for changes for the reviewer to check, the builder posted its fixes as a comment,
  and the reviewer watched for a move into Review that never came. The card loop step has a `followUp`: the builder's,
  on a card in Review or Approved, queued included (`loop.stepNotHere` elsewhere; on a queued card it first takes its
  entry out of the queue, `IntegrationCancelled` with reason follow-up, so the queue can't merge the approved revision
  while the follow-up changes its line, and the reviewer's `ok` queues it again while its pass holds; refused once the
  queue has begun merging it, `loop.followUpMerging`, #1623). **A follow-up's `ok` is only the reviewer's check of it:
  it approves nothing (HI-1763, the Assistant's design call, 26 Oct).** A pass covers only the revision submitted, while
  it is the card's head or the same change: a line moved on to another change since the submission (a follow-up commit,
  OK'd or not) refuses a pass (`review.headMoved`, naming both revisions; next: a commit the reviewer asked for is
  submitted as a follow-up, else a failing verdict so its builder submits the head; either runs its checks, the user's
  gates and a review copy as any submission). **A follow-up submitted in Review** (HI-1832, the Assistant's card after
  HI-1772, 27 Oct, where HR3 moved the card to Doing to have a follow-up reviewed, which gave it to HR3 and ended HB3's
  watch): `cw_submit` with `followUp`, its builder's: the card's agent on the board when the write decides (a card
  given to another in Review keeps its `Started`: HR4's round 1), given to nobody its cycle's builder, the user or the
  Assistant either way (`submit.followUpNotBuilder` otherwise, checked in the write; the same revision
  `submit.notDuplicate`), makes the commit the revision under review: a `Submitted` fact
  (`followUp`, the same round), its pin and `prepareReviewCopy`, no move, no one reassigned, the board's line "Follow-up
  submitted for review at <commit>", and the reviewer woken (a `review` loop wake due until it starts again or gives a
  verdict, though it is already reviewing). The earlier submission's review doesn't carry: a verdict on it is refused
  (`verdict.currentSubmission`, or `review.headMoved` for a pass), one on the follow-up needs its review started on it
  (`verdict.reviewing`, which moves the review copy), and passes given before it no longer count (`passingReviewers`).
  The loop step's `followUp` stays for Approved and for a change with no commit (a screenshot's). On 26 Oct HR4 OK'd HB4's
  follow-up commit and passed the submitted one: the pass went stale at once and HI-1737 sat in Approved, nobody told.
  **A pass that goes stale afterwards is never silent:** its builder's wake names what was passed, where the line is and
  what to submit (`staleWake`), the card's merge line and a refused merge or move say so (queue state `stale`,
  `merge.combworkMerges` next `nextStale`), and a lane watch is told `stalled` once it has stood 10 minutes from its `Stale`
  fact (`staleSince`, never moved by later notices), its builder idle or only watching (`staleWaitReason`). Named as a
  design is (`<key>/s<seq>`, its comment
  headed "Follow-up HI-12/s41, for the reviewer's check (an answer names HI-12/s41):"), with the same reviewer rule
  (`loop.noReviewer` with none), the same `step` loop wake to the reviewer whatever its watch counts, and the same
  answers (`ok`, `gaps`, naming it; history "Checked the follow-up: OK: …"). It has no due time and no going ahead:
  `proceed` on a follow-up is refused (`loop.followUpChecked`). A design or follow-up waits until answered, replaced,
  returned for review, given a verdict or moved to another column (`pendingStep`, by its history lines' columns): a
  change of its place in its column ("Moved to the bottom of Approved") keeps it, its wake and its stall's age. The
  column it was posted in is kept on its history line (`column`, a value its words don't show, #1495): the history keeps
  only its last 300 lines, so the line saying where the card was may be gone, and a move into another column at its top
  ("Moved to the top of Review", the same words as a reorder there) then still ends it; a line from before keeps reading
  the lines before it. Unanswered, it is a stall (`loopStepWait`): the card in
  Review or Approved, not blocked, its builder only watching it REVIEW_WAIT_STALL_MS (15 minutes) after the follow-up
  ("B1 posted a follow-up on #333 for its reviewer to check and has waited 20 min: nobody has answered it"; the board's
  hint asks the reviewer to answer it). The card-loop skill has the builder post it, and the reviewer watch comments as
  well as columns while one it was asked to check is due.
- **A late message can't reopen a pass** (#699, #703): only a submission or a decision (§16.4.6) moves an Approved card
  back to Review; comments and messages never do [note §10].
- **Verified lane end:** `endLaneIfDone` replaces the agent's `mergeCommit` (`servers.ts:1556` checks only its format
  today). `cw_lane end` keeps `abandoned` for the user and the Assistant; `mergeCommit` is ignored with a note [P1].

#### 16.8.3 Refusals as instructions

[note §3, #1120] A refusal is HTTP 409 with:

```json
{ "refused": true, "rule": "submit.checksPassed",
  "message": "Review refused: checks failed on a3f2c1d (unit: 3 failures).",
  "next": "Fix the failures, commit, run `npm test` with cw-progress --card AM-12, then submit again.",
  "change": "This rule is set in Version Control → Checks pass before review.",
  "override": "the user" }
```

- **One contract for every refusal** [answering HR2's round 1 finding 12]: three parts, each a **whole sentence of its
  own message** (`workflow.refused.<rule>.message`, `.next`, `.change`), with placeholders; never one sentence built
  from pieces. The agent's reply carries the three English sentences as fields; the window shows them as three lines
  (the Progress hover, the card, a notification), each translated. Messages follow AGENTS.md's Translations rules:
  `msg({ id, defaultMessage, description })` kept as data and shown with `tr()` (`tRich()` for markup) when rendered,
  never at module scope; a description for translators naming the rule; numbers as `{n, number}` or plurals;
  `npm run i18n:extract` after adding them [#1120 c, `locales/glossary-1.0.md` §1].
- **Read by both** [#1264, HI-1585]: a sentence that means the user says *the user* to agents and *you* in the window
  (glossary §1 rule 10): it is one message with both whole-sentence wordings, `{reader, select, you {…} other {…}}`, the
  reader given by the format (`refusal()`'s English for agents: `agent`; the window's lines: `you`), never kept in the
  refusal's values, so a refusal recorded before it is shown either way. A `change` says where the rule is set ("This
  rule is set in Version Control → …"), and `override` who can skip it. A
  value that is a name in the code (`{move}`, `{intent}`, `{moves}`, `{rule}`, `{rules}`) reaches agents as it is
  (the intents they call) and the window through its own message (`shared/workflow/texts.ts`: stage, move and rule
  names, the rules worded as the Version Control options); a stage (`{stage}`, `{stages}`) reaches both by the name the
  board shows, agents in English ("Active", never the id `active`, #1604); what a platform couldn't read (`{what}`) is
  a message of its own, kept as data (`StoredText`) beside its English. `refusal()` builds the agent's English,
  `refusalLines()` the window's lines. A `move.notFromHere` with nothing possible from the stage says so as its next
  step, never an empty list; one whose stage's intents are the other side's gives the refused agent's own (#1604, its
  `whose` value): a reviewer's review or verdict on a card no longer in Review hears that its review is over (back for
  more work: leave it with no verdict and wait for its return to Review; moved on: leave it), and the card's builder
  refused a move while the card waits in Review hears to wait for the verdict.
- **The user's own move** (a drag on the board, the card dialog; HI-1851): its toast's title names the card and the
  column ("HI-12 can't move to Review"), and a rule whose sentences are worded for the agent (`submit.empty`'s "if you
  were asked only to submit it (not to do the card), ask the user before committing") has its own for the user (`FOR_USER` in `refusals.ts`, the format's
  `forUser`): "Nothing is committed to review yet. Commit the card's work, then move it again." An agent's refusal
  shown in the window (the Progress panel) keeps the agent's words.
- `next` is the exact next step the agent can take, possible under the card's ruleset (§16.5.4); `override` says who
  can override (never the agent).
- Every refused intent appends a `Refused` fact (so the lane shows it) [#1120 c]; the window collapses repeats.

#### 16.8.4 Overrides

[note §3, #1120, #1112 C]
- **Who:** the user always; the Assistant when Settings → Assistant → Control allows card changes, with a reason it
  must give; agents never (OP-9 asks Darren to confirm).
- **How:** the user's drag across a rule shows "This skips: <rules>. Reason (optional)" with **Move anyway**; the
  Assistant passes `override: { reason }`. One `Override` fact names every rule skipped.
- **Shown:** an override mark on the card and its lane segment, with who, which rule and why in the hover; overrides
  are never invisible [#1120 c].
- **Recorded actions still run:** a user moving a card to Done without a merge writes `Override` and `Moved`; it
  doesn't fake an `Integrated` fact. A later observed integration adds it.
- **A drag that stands for an intent runs it** [P2]: a forward drag into Active, Review, Approved or Merging runs the
  intents it stands for, in order: Start (`Started`, its line and base), then submit at the card's revision (by the
  user, with an empty summary; a no-code card too), then, past Review, an `Override` naming `integrate.approved`,
  which counts as approved for that submission (the queue merges it). A step that skips nothing just happens; one
  whose guards refuse **asks first, naming only the rules that refuse**, and its `Override` names exactly those. A
  step refused for something no override can make true (nothing to submit, a fact that couldn't be read) stops the
  drag there, so a card never sits in Active with no start, in Review with nothing to review or in Merging with no
  entry. Done is a plain move (no `Integrated` faked), and a stage the card's ruleset doesn't have isn't a place to
  drag to. Out of On Hold, a drag back to where the card was returns it there (queued again if it was queued, its
  gate asked again if still unmet); a drag past it returns it there first and then runs the intents of a drag from
  there; a move behind it counts the rules it skips from where the card was, not from Todo. A drag into Merging of a
  card already approved just queues it (nothing skipped).
- **Nobody on it (HI-2062):** the Assistant's move into Active (Doing) that would leave the card with nobody on it (no
  agent on it already, none named, or `agent` empty) is refused, `move.doingNobody`, naming the user's three choices:
  nobody on it, an agent on it (`agent`), or an agent started on it (`cw_start_task`). Nobody on it passes with the
  user's reason as `override`, recorded as an `Override` naming `move.doingNobody` (with any other rule the move skips:
  the refusal names those too, and one reason covers them all). Through the rules it is a rule of every move into
  Active (a start, or back from Review or On Hold) that names no builder, and the move's write checks the card again
  as it leaves it: an agent taken off meanwhile, or by the same change (a change of project), undoes the write and the
  move is decided again on the card as it is. With the rules off, P3's move checks it on the card as it is in its
  change and records the `Override` with it. A card the Assistant makes in Doing with no agent is refused the same way (made in Todo, then moved). The Agent
  API checks it before asking the user to approve the change, and the change checks it again; the user's moves (the
  Move to Doing dialog asks) and project agents' (into Doing gives it to them) aren't asked.
- **In the window (#1275):** every move the user makes on the board (a drag, Move to, Review (next round), the Move to
  Doing dialog with its agent, the card dialog's Column) goes through `tasks:move`; `tasks:update` from the window
  no longer skips a rule unasked (one that would is refused, naming the rules). A move that asks shows the question
  (*"Move AM-12 to Done anyway?"*, each rule it skips by its name, **Reason (optional)**, **Move Anyway** / Cancel),
  then moves with `confirm` and the reason. A window **Start** (the Start dialog, Move to Doing's Assign and start) asks
  the same before anything is done (`tasks:start` returns `ask` from the runtime's dry move, `startAsks`: no agent
  added, nothing launched), then starts with the reason kept on its `Override`. Cancel, or a step refused for something no override can make true, puts
  the card back where it was or where the drag stopped, with the refusal's three sentences in a toast. As a drag
  starts, the window asks which columns the card's rules have (`tasks:columns`: its ruleset's stages as columns, On
  Hold always; a reopened Done card's next cycle's; none when no rule applies): a column they don't have takes no
  drop and isn't highlighted. The **override mark** on a card's tile (an open lock, in the info colour) and a line in
  its lane segment's hover say who moved it past which rules and why: the card's latest `Override` since its work was
  last Done (`WorkBadge.override`).

#### 16.8.5 For you

[#439, #1120 c] Cards waiting on the user carry **For you**, from `ApprovalRequested`, a blocked question
(`CannotWithinRules`), or a gate waiting on the user's approval (G10). It shows as a chip on the card, a **For you**
board filter, a count on the activity bar and in the Progress panel's paused reasons; answering (Approve/Decline, a
decision, a reply) clears it and **wakes the waiting agent**. Kinds (OP-11, agreed 20 Oct): **Approve**,
**Decide**, **Test**, **Sign in**, **Other**; only an Approve satisfies an approval gate. A "Test" request may carry a
checklist (what to try, on which build) [P1]. The field records a person (`for: 'user'`) so "for <person>" can be
added later [#439]. A request Combwork makes (the user's review, the OK before merging, a decision after a merge) keeps its English `text` for agents and its message as data (`requestText`) for the window [#1264]; an agent's own question is its words. **A request belongs to its submission** [P2]: a new submission retires the requests made for an
earlier one, and an answer is checked under the transaction (the request still open, the card where it was, the
generation current then), and its gate evaluated before anything moves on, so an old request can never approve
newer work. A gate's request (the user's review, or the OK before merging) is bound to its submission, the stage it
was asked in and the decision generation it was asked at: a new submission, the card leaving that stage or a newer
decision retires it, and an answer begun before that is refused. The user is asked again when the gate is reached
again: at once under "You" review in Review, after the reviewers' confirmation under "…, then you", and when the card
comes back from On Hold to the stage whose gate is still unmet [P2].

**A decision that answers requests (HI-1932, Darren's decision of 28 Oct).** The user's answer given in a chat with the
Assistant, recorded by it as a decision in the user's words, may name the card's open requests it answers
(`cw_update_task` / `PATCH /v1/tasks/{n}`: `decision` with `answers`, up to 20 ids, as `cw_read_task`'s `forYou`
lists them); Combwork closes them with it. `forYou` comes just after the card's decisions in every form of
`cw_read_task` (`GET /v1/tasks/{n}`, with `comments`, `summary`, and the latest comment's), each request with its id,
who asked, its words and when (HI-1992: an Assistant reading only comments missed a question asked there); answered and
closed ones are only in the card's history. Only the user and the Assistant (never a project agent, so none closes its own
request); only a question (`decisionAnswers`: not an approval, Combwork's own gates, the round limit's choice or the merge
queue's merge choice); never without the decision. Checked in `tasks.ts` and again under the write
(`Workflow.answerByDecision`): every request still open and answerable, or none is answered and nothing is written, the
decision included. The decision (its id fixed beforehand), an `Approval` per request (`note`: the decision's words,
`byDecision`: the decision's id, who recorded it, the authenticated recorder, and when) and a history line each are one
write; each asker (else the builder) is woken once it commits, with the requests it answers. A lane's waiting for the
user clears as with any answer. The card dialog's For you section lists them (`WorkView.resolvedByDecision`, the newest
10: the question as asked, Combwork's own in the window's language, the decision by its id, *recorded by …*, when).

**Answering, main side (#1269).** Only the user answers (Darren's point 7, as recommended: never an agent or the
Assistant, which relays and asks; HI-1932's decision the Assistant records in the user's words is the user's answer): the window's `tasks:answer(n, request, answer)` on the intent path, the answer
checked under the transaction as above. What an answer may be follows the request (`answerFits`, checked in `tasks.ts`
and again by the runtime, before anything is written): an approval (kind Approve) is **approved** or **declined** (a
reply may say why), never answered with a reply or a decision alone; any other question is **answered** with a reply (kept with the answer, `Approval.note`) or
a decision (recorded on the card, a new generation, its agents told as any decision is); at the round limit (§16.11.4)
the answer is a choice, **carry on** (with 1 to 50 more rounds), **split it**, **accept it with follow-ups** or **take it
over**; anything else is refused before anything is written. Only an approval of a gate's request (the user's review,
the OK before merging) moves the card on; a decline of one is a round and returns the card to its builder; an answer to
an agent's own question (ask the user, couldn't within the rules) moves nothing, is never a round, and an approval of
it is recorded (`Approval`) as the OK it asked for (#922's push or release OK). **Answering wakes the waiting agent**,
once (the runtime's durable `wake`, `about: 'answer'`): the agent that asked (its request records it, `asker`), else the
card's builder; at the round limit the builder and the lane's reviewer, with the user's choice; an approval of a gate's
request (the user's review, the OK before merging) its builder, whatever it led to (finished, queued, or waiting on
another gate), its wake saying the answer first. An answer moves the card only through its gate: one that moves
nothing leaves its column as it is (a failed card in Review isn't returned for review by it). An answer's wake needs
no loop: it reaches an agent working on its own, with no lane or reviewer (*"…The user answered: carry on from where you
asked"*), and the card's history says so (*Told B1 (web) of your answer*), as long as the project's loop wakes are on. Each request records whom it is for
(`for: 'user'`). The window lists what waits with `tasks:forYou` (a project's or the workspace's: each request's card,
kind, gate, English text and Combwork's message for it, when it was asked and who asked; a count), read again on
`tasks-changed`. **In the window (#1276):** a card with requests shows a **For you** chip (a bell, the kind; the accent colour,
pill-shaped). Its tooltip is short (#1635): for each of the first two requests who asks for what ("HB5 asks you to
decide") over its first sentence or two as plain text (Markdown's marks taken out), a count of any more, and where to
answer (a click opens the card, whose For you section has each in full); its accessible name gives each request's kind
and start. The chip sits on its tile, folded or not; the Task Board
icon on the activity bar counts the cards (its accessible name "3 cards wait for you"; Review's count stays in the board
sidebar's Waiting for review); the board's toolbar has a **For you** filter (remembered per board view, composing with
the search); the card dialog's **For you** section lists each request (its kind, its text in the window's language or
the agent's words rendered as Markdown the way card comments are, sanitized, single line breaks kept, folded to about
ten lines with **Show all** (#1637), who asked and when, a Test request's checklist) with its answers: **Approve** / **Decline…** (a
reason, required) for an approval, Approve with an optional note beside it (HI-2286, `approveNote`: on an agent's question,
gate `ask`, the note is the answer's reply and the user's decision on the card, so the asker works to it and a reviewer
checks it; on one offering a single action, that action's reason; on Combwork's own gates, a reply only, since approving
moves the card on at once; the box's hint says which; empty, Approve is one click), a reply (**Send Reply**: the user's comment on the card, and to the agent waiting
on it an `answer` delivery from the user quoting the reply whole, its question quoted short, #1626) or **Record as
Decision** for a question (each with a tooltip saying what it does), and the four
ways on (carry on with its rounds) at the round limit. **Actions an agent offers (#1630):** an agent's question may
offer up to three things only the user can do on its card (`actions`: `done` Move to Done, `noCode` Make It No Code,
`unblock` Unblock; `skipReview` Skip Review, HI-1734), each with a suggested reason. Each the card allows now (not Done; a
code card; blocked; Todo or Doing) is a button with its reason, editable; one click does what the board does, as the user, with the
reason (Move to Done through the card's rules, the rules it skips an `Override` as Move Anyway's; Make It No Code the
`card.kind` override; Skip Review the review skip set as the user's; Unblock with the reason as the user's comment), then
answers the question (`Approval.action`, the reason its `note`), and the asker is told which. An action refused, or no
longer allowed, leaves the question open. **An answer that needs someone other than its agent (HI-1734; on 25 Oct
Darren's answer agreeing to move HI-1449 to Done reached only HB3, which can't, and it sat in Approved for two days):**
with one action offered, **{Action} With This Reply** does it with the typed reply as its reason, and approving an Approve
question that offers one does it too (the reply, else the agent's reason); Combwork never reads consent into a reply's text.
Any other answer to an agent's own question (gate `ask`) that Combwork didn't carry out, a bare Approve or Decline too, is
given to the Assistant as well as the asker (`answerRelay.ts`, a `control` delivery, `answer-relay`, once per request),
saying how the user answered (approved, declined, answered) apart from what they wrote, the question and the reply
each whole (never cut: a condition at a reply's end reaches it), and where both stay (`cw_read_task`); a decline is
worded as one ("nothing is to be done for it"), never as a grant; otherwise "This needs you … {asker} can't
{move it to Done / make it no code / skip its review / unblock it} by itself" where the card shows it (an action offered,
an open no-code or review-skip proposal, a card in Passed its agent doesn't merge, a block), else "For you to check … if
it grants a change {asker} can't make itself, make it". It is given only while the Assistant's Combwork tools are on and
Settings → Assistant → Control lets it change cards, checked at each offer and hand-out; one it can't be given, or that
ends unread, says so on the card and in a notice ("… couldn't be told of your answer"). **An agent asking the
Assistant (HI-1866; on 27 Oct HB6 asked it in a comment to park HI-1865 and move HI-1759 to Done on the user's answer,
and a comment reaches no inbox: it sat an hour unseen):** `cw_ask_assistant` (`POST /v1/tasks/{card}/ask-assistant`,
`text`), a project agent's only (the Assistant and scripts are refused, 403), on a card of its project not archived or
in Done (another project's is unknown to it), for what only the Assistant or the user may do on it (park a card On
Hold, move one past its rules on the user's recorded answer, unblock, reassign). It moves nothing and counts no round:
the text is the agent's comment (at most a comment's 20,000 characters, refused rather than cut) with a history line
("Asked the Assistant: …"), and a `control` delivery to the Assistant (`assistantAsk.ts`, `assistant-ask`, from
the agent: sender kind `agent` with its project and id) quoting it whole as an agent's request, not the user's
decision, with the card's key, offered at once: an idle or watching Assistant (its lane watch, which carries on) is
woken by the doorbell, a busy one told at its next tool call. The Assistant acts on it only within its Control and what
the user decided or answered on the card, and tells the agent with `cw_message_agent`. Refused before anything is
written (409, saying to ask the user with `cw_ask_user`) while the Assistant can't act on it (the same check as the
relay's); one that ends unread (cancelled when Control is turned down before it is handed out, expired) says so on the
card and in a notice ("The Assistant couldn't be told of {agent}'s request …"). The card-loop skill says when to
use it (what only the Assistant may do, already decided; a decision still the user's goes to them), coordinate-agents
how the Assistant answers. **No code, proposed:** a code
card that passes review with its change already in its target (nothing to merge) is proposed no code by Combwork
(`KindProposed`, once; the user confirms). Skip Review is dropped from a question's actions on a card whose rules don't
review it (nothing to skip). A refused answer (answered or retired meanwhile) is said in a
toast and the board read again; an answer clears the chip at once (`tasks-changed`). **A request settled another way
is closed (#1638):** in the same write, a question still open once its card is in Done (one an agent or the Assistant
asked: any request not under Combwork's own gates, `askedQuestion`; an agent that asked is told it no longer stands, unless
it made the move), and an agent's own questions once it moves the card on itself (a submit, a put
back: answered some other way, such as in its pane), each `RequestClosed` and a line in the card's history; For you lists
no question on a card in Done however it got there (Combwork's own requests stay: a merge stopped part way, a decision after the merge), and a
lane no longer waits for the user on a closed request.

#### 16.8.6 A refused commit (#907)

[#1117 c3] When the agent's CLI refuses its own commit (Claude Code's auto-mode check, "Modify Shared Resources"),
the commit never reaches Combwork, so no intent is refused. The agent uses **couldn't within the rules** with the
refusal's text; Combwork shows a For you of kind **Approve** with the fix: approve in the agent's pane, or add an allow
rule for `git commit` in the agent's folder (`.claude/settings.local.json`, never Combwork's edit of the CLI's config,
§10). After P5 merges are Combwork's, so only commits and release pushes remain [#907]. Guidance (P8) tells agents to
report it this way rather than retry.

### 16.9 The merge queue

[note §9, #1121] Combwork performs merges. The merge slot becomes a **queue per target** (a project and target line).

**Built [#1348], for a target checked out in no folder:** a card whose ruleset says Combwork merges is queued as it is
approved, and its target's queue runs in the app with the Assistant off: one host per open workspace, project and
target, started by the card's queuing and, as a workspace opens, for every target with entries; it runs on the target's
runner (§16.9.3), recovers its own target's entries first, then takes them in order through steps 1–2 and 4–8: the
test merge in the runner's worktree, the merge checks as Combwork's runs on exactly that result, and the advance by
compare-and-swap under the repository lock, the lease checked inside it. A conflict or a red check returns the card to
its builder with the files or the log; a check that couldn't start is transient, and the builder's resubmission of the
same revision goes straight back into the queue (at most twice); a target that moved is tested again (three times in a
row pause it); a hand merge meanwhile is observed, never merged twice. The card's ruleset decides, never the project's
options now: a card started under Combwork merges is merged by the queue after the options moved to another finisher. With
workflow rules off nothing reaches an advance: open entries pause (**rules off**) before it, an advance already begun
finishes, and they carry on when the rules are on again. A target checked out in a folder is advanced there by
§16.9.2's journaled update (**Built [#1351]**), automatically, or asked first while Merge into a checked-out branch
says so (OP-40). A
card's test-merge ref goes once its entry has an outcome, and its submissions' pins once it is archived.

#### 16.9.1 An entry's way through

1. Take the next entry (`IntegrationRequested` not cancelled, failed or integrated, in order) whose card **isn't
   waiting for a blocker** (HI-2709): a card blocked by a card that isn't Done (or that can't be read) stays in the
   queue, in its place, shown as **waiting for HI-x** (the queue's list, the card's Work section and its agents' card
