   reads), and the entries behind it go on. Its blockers are read again at each run, before its test merge and before
   its advance, and finally in the write of `IntegrationStarted`, the advance's authority: a blocker that isn't Done
   there means nothing begins, the entry stays open, and it is tested again once unblocked. A dependency added in
   Review, while queued or while it is tested holds it so. One added once `IntegrationStarted` is written (its advance
   begun, no outcome yet) is **refused** ("being merged into main now"), since nothing can hold that merge any more; a
   blocker reopened from Done after that point doesn't stop it either. A blocker moving into Done, or a dependency
   taken away, runs its queue again (`enqueue`): the entry is still the approved one, so there's no new approval.
   **Every route that closes a card as merged** keeps the same rule, one check (`closeWaitsFor`) read in its own write: reconciliation's close of a
   passed card whose change is in the target writes nothing while a blocker isn't Done (the card waits, Merging), the
   queue's already-in-the-target step (a forward merge's own close too) says `waiting`, and an agent's merge report is refused (`merge.waitsForBlockers`,
   two messages in 7 locales). The queue's own `Integrated` follows its advance, decided in `IntegrationStarted`'s write.
2. Check `integrate.approved` (quorum, approvals, not stale), and **check containment first**: if the change is
   already in the target (merged by hand meanwhile), record `Integrated` (observed) instead of making an empty merge
   [HB3's round 1 finding 19]. An entry that isn't approved any more gets an outcome, never a skip that leaves it
   open (it would hold up every card behind it): `IntegrationCancelled` (stale), the card back to Review (or Active
   with no review), its builder woken [P2].
3. **Strict** (G8), redefined [P1, answering HB3's round 1 finding 4 and round 2 finding B]: if the revision
   doesn't contain the target's head, the queue **brings it up to date itself, on its own ref only**: in its worktree
   it merges the target into the approved revision (or rebases it, per the merge style) and keeps the result on
   `refs/cw/queue/<entry>`, pinned; it **never moves the card's line**, which is checked out in the builder's leased
   slot. If the result replays to the approved change (§16.3.2), the pass carries over (an `Updated` fact records the
   new revision and why) and the entry goes on with it; a conflict returns the card. The builder's slot is unchanged,
   and when the card is Done its line is no longer needed. (OP-18: Team's default.)
   **Built [#1352]** (`MergeQueue.upToDate`): with the card's ruleset strict and the reviewed revision not containing the
   expected head (`merge-base --is-ancestor`), the queue's worktree is set at the reviewed revision and the target merged
   into it (`Merge <target> into <card>`, with `Combwork-Card` and `Combwork-Revision`), or with merge style Squash the change
   rebased onto it, made as Combwork's commits are (#1350: the project's identity, the repository's hooks and signing, no
   prompt). The result must be the same change (§16.3.2's `sameChange`: the candidate key, then the replay's tree), else
   the card returns (`IntegrationFailed`, reason `notUpToDate`: a conflict with its files, or a different change, such as
   a target that already holds part of it, with a line saying so); a failing hook returns it as `hook`, and the other
   failures pause as the test merge's do. The same: kept on `refs/cw/queue/<entry>` (dropped with its card's queue ref
   once the entry has its outcome) and recorded as `Updated` (`how` `mergedTarget` or `rebased`, `carried`), which
   folds onto **its entry** (`QueueEntry.updated`), never the card's approved revision: that stays the reviewed one, the
   builder's line, which reconciliation compares with and a requeue queues, so an update never makes the pass stale.
   Each test merge updates afresh from the reviewed revision (a retest after the target moved never builds on an earlier
   update); its message keeps `Combwork-Revision:` as the reviewed revision and adds `Combwork-Updated:`. The containment check
   (merged by hand meanwhile) uses the reviewed revision. G8's `integrate.upToDate` guard has no input from the queue:
   the queue brings the work up to date instead of refusing it.
4. **Test merge** in the queue's own worktree (a merge slot, kept warm like other slots): `git worktree add --detach`
   at the target's head (the **expected** revision); `git merge --no-ff <rev>` (or `merge --squash` + commit) with the
   message `AM-12: <title>` and trailers `Combwork-Card: AM-12`, `Combwork-Revision: <rev>`, `Combwork-Reviewed-By: <reviewer>`;
   the result on a temporary ref `refs/cw/queue/<entry>` [P1].
   **The branch's own message (G19, built [HI-1697]):** with *Commit message* set to the branch's own, the merge commit
   or squash commit takes the messages of the branch's own commits (`git log --no-merges <base>..<rev>`, oldest
   first): one commit's message as it is; several, each one's in turn, the first one's subject first, as git joins a
   squash's. Any `Combwork-…:` trailer line in them is left out (one of an earlier name is history, kept); a branch with no message of its own takes the card's
   title. No card key and no trailer, and strict's update (step 3) is git's plain `Merge branch '<target>'`. Which card
   it was is never read from the message: the `Integrated` fact names the merge's result, and containment and the
   board read that. Read as the project's options are when the queue merges (G19 isn't a rule). Commits on the card's
   own line keep whatever their builder wrote.
   **Rebase and fast-forward (G6, built [#1184]):** the test merge is a rebase, under the **linear landing** policy:
   every commit the advance adds to the target (`expected..result`) has exactly one parent, and `expected` is an
   ancestor of `result`. In the queue's worktree, detached at the reviewed revision, `git rebase --onto <expected>
   <base>` with Combwork's identity and `commitEnv` (no prompt, signing bounded), merge preservation always off
   (`-c rebase.rebaseMerges=false --no-rebase-merges`, overriding the repository's setting for this command only;
   `--force-rebase` whenever the reviewed suffix `base..revision` holds a merge, which git would otherwise take as up to
   date and keep) and no other ref moved (`-c rebase.updateRefs=false --no-update-refs`, as strict's update). A linear
   suffix already on top of the target lands as it is, with no rewrite. Before the merge checks the result is checked:
   on top of the target, no commit with two parents in `expected..result`, and `sameChange` with the reviewed change;
   failing one, the card is returned (`notUpToDate`, its log saying which: a merge resolution that changed the work
   can't survive flattening); a conflict returns it with its files; a read git couldn't answer pauses (never taken for a
   pass or a mismatch). The checks then run on exactly that result, and the advance (§16.9.2, unchanged) moves the
   target from `expected` to it: a fast-forward, recorded as `Integrated` with method `fastForward` (by recovery after
   a restart too, from the style the entry was queued with, as for the other styles). The queue's worktree is set at the
   reviewed revision first even when nothing is rewritten, so the merge checks always run on exactly the result. G8 (strict) needs
   no separate update with it. The rebased commits keep their own messages, authors and dates, with Combwork as committer:
   there is no merge commit, so no `Combwork-Card`, `Combwork-Revision` or `Combwork-Reviewed-By` trailers, the price of a linear
   history; the reviewed revision stays pinned (§16.9.3), and containment finds the change spread over several commits.
   No preset sets it.
   **Combwork's commits** [HB3's round 1 finding 11]:
   - authored and committed with the project's identity (git's configured identity for the repository, read each time, G12 on or off: HI-2266);
     with no identity the entry pauses ("set a commit identity for this repository");
   - the repository's hooks run (no `--no-verify`, AGENTS.md); a hook that fails returns the card with the hook's
     output (`IntegrationFailed`, reason `hook`);
   - **a conflict's hunks** (HI-1181, rc.4; design HI-1181/s8 and s10 checked by HR4): before the test merge, strict's
     update or the rebase is aborted, `main/workflow/conflictRead.ts` reads each conflicted file (named as git lists them with
     `diff --name-only -z`, never C-quoted: HR4's round 1) in the queue's own
     folder, bounded before anything is read (20 files, 256 KB a file, 1 MB in all, each read into a buffer of that size,
     never whole) and confined to it (a path that is absolute or climbs out, a link anywhere on the way, a parent whose
     real place is outside, missing, binary or not UTF-8 text: recorded with why, never read; a character cut at the
     budget is the cut's). `shared/workflow/conflicts.ts` parses each region (markers of 7 or more, a diff3 base, a stray
     marker as text) with 2 lines of context never shared with a neighbour, at most 8 hunks a file, 40 lines a side (the
     rest counted), lines cut at 400 characters (counted) and 16,000 characters in all, and says what stopped it
     (`partial`: read in part, the hunks, the room; an exact `more` only when the file was scanned whole). Kept on
     `IntegrationFailed` as `conflicts`, with which side git wrote first (`oursIs`: the target in a test merge and a
     rebase, the card in strict's merge). The card's Work section unfolds each file's hunks whenever they were captured
     (strict's not-up-to-date return too), read-only, its sides named
     (the target, the card's key, the common ancestor); "no text conflict" only for a file read whole with no markers,
     else why or "may have more". The builder's wake names where each file's conflicts are ("a.ts (2 conflicts, lines
     10 and 40)", "b.png (not read: binary)"), within its note's room. The queue's folder is reset straight after, so
     there is no diff to open; the Progress panel keeps Show log.
   - with `commit.gpgsign`, signing runs as configured; if it would wait for a passphrase (a pinentry window), the
     entry pauses with "signing waits for you" rather than failing, and a signing error pauses it with git's message.
   **Built [#1350]:**
   - **Identity:** the repository's own (`git config user.name` / `user.email`: local, then
     global), G12 on or off (HI-2266: G12's saved value never stands in for it), passed to the merge with `-c`. With none, the entry pauses `identity`, naming the project folder: the
     window says to set a commit identity for this repository (`git config user.name` / `user.email`).
   - **Hooks:** they run (no `--no-verify`).
   - **Who said what** [HR4's rounds 1 and 2 on #1350]: a failure is told by which part failed, and a decision reads
     only that part's own words, never the whole output (a hook can print anything).
     - Combwork's commits run with `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT=2`, so git writes its trace2 events into its own stderr, in order
       with what its hooks and its signer write there. A child's text comes after its `child_start` and before its
       `child_exit`: a hook writes before it exits, and git writes `child_exit` only once it has waited for it.
     - Each piece of text belongs to the top git's child running then: a hook (`child_class: hook`, its name) or the
       signer (gpg's or gpgsm's `-bsau`, ssh-keygen's `-Y sign`). Text while none runs is git's own. A git that a hook
       runs (its sid `<parent>/<own>`) is never a source.
     - An event is only a complete JSON record with the fields its kind needs, starting `{"event":"` and running to
       the line's end, from git's own session: the top git's (begun by its `version` record, with no parent's
       prefix) or a git it runs (`<top>/…`). Anything else is text: an event-looking fragment, or a hook's own
       structured log with a session of its own (#1397). Events never appear in a message.
   - **Hook failure:** a hook that exited non-zero (`pre-merge-commit`, `commit-msg`, or `pre-commit` for a squash's
     commit) returns the card with its own text, then git's (`IntegrationFailed`, reason `hook`).
   - **Other failures:** anything else (an index lock, a broken repository, a worktree it couldn't check out) pauses
     `needsYou` with git's own lines, never a return.
   - **A read that fails for a moment** (HI-2019): before anything is touched (no `IntegrationStarted`), a git read or
     worktree step that fails (the identity, the target's head, the queue worktree's listing, add or checkout, the test
     merge's head, strict's and Rebase's ancestry reads, the checked-out folder's branch, staged files, status and the
     merge's files) isn't a pause yet: the entry goes round again, the lock and fence released, after 250 ms × the try,
     up to 3 times (a budget of its own, apart from a target that moves). Before it goes round it is admitted afresh: still
     approved (a decision or Remove from queue meanwhile takes it out), no pause saved meanwhile (the user's stands, and
     the entry waits, open), the rules on, the lease held; so nothing more is merged or checked once one of those changed.
     Only a read that keeps failing pauses, `needsYou` with git's own words. A commit identity git couldn't read is that,
     never "no identity" (`identity` pauses only when git says the name or email isn't set). The queue's worktree is
     reused only when this repository's worktree list names it; a folder there that git doesn't list is used only if
     empty, else left as it is and paused, named; nothing of it is ever removed or pruned. After the advance, only the
     folder's branch is read again (3 times, 100 ms apart, in the lock): the advance is never redone. A git that didn't
     run to an exit of its own (Node's `EAGAIN` on a busy machine, Combwork's git worker ending, the output bound, a signal) is
     never git's answer anywhere in Combwork: its result has code -1 (never 1, which callers read as git's "no": a key not
     set, HEAD detached, not an ancestor) and `notRun` naming why, and it doesn't mark git as missing.
   - **A commit of the test merge whose git never started** (HI-2020: the merge, a squash's commit, strict's update,
     Rebase's rebase): nothing ran, so there is nothing to tell a hook, a signer or a conflict from. The queue's worktree
     is put back as after any failure and the entry goes round again, admitted afresh, within the same budget; then
     `needsYou` with the start's error. "Never started" is only ever positive: Node's start error with no process (in
     tests, the queue's own spawn); in the app, the runner's launcher that couldn't start, or the launcher's own line,
     marked with the launch's nonce, saying the command's start failed. An exit code never says it: a command that ran
     and exited 127 is that command's 127. A git that ran and failed is classified as before.
   - **No trace** (a git older than 2.24): only git's own "Not committing merge" is a hook, and signing is never read
     from text.
   - **Signing:** the repository's config (never overridden). Combwork's commits run with no terminal: no input,
     `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`, `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never`. In the app they go through the
     queue runner's recorded spawn (#1360). When `commit.gpgsign` is on, the commit (hooks included) has a bound:
     Settings → Advanced, `cw.queue.signSeconds`, 60 s. At the bound the whole tree (git, its hooks, the signer) is
     ended.
     - **Ended at the bound:** always a pause, decided by what was running when it was ended (the stream as far as
       it had come then). Ending a hook may make it exit non-zero, and that is never its rejection. A hook running
       then pauses `hookTimedOut`. The signer, or nothing known in a repository that signs, pauses `signingWaits`,
       "signing waits for you".
     - **A signer that exited non-zero:** pauses `signingWaits` when **its own** text says it needs a passphrase, a
       pinentry or a terminal, and `signing` otherwise, with its text and git's. Its own text is what it wrote while
       it ran (Git for Windows 2.45 lets the signer write to stderr), and git's text right after it exited, before any
       other child starts (HI-2399: a newer git, such as Git for Windows 2.56, captures the signer's stderr and reprints it then, as
       `error: gpg failed to sign the data:` and gpg's lines). A hook's text is never either.
   - **After any of these:** the queue's worktree is left clean at the expected revision (`merge --abort`,
     `reset --hard`, `clean`), and nothing in the target changes.
   - **The pause:** keeps git's message in its own words (`workflow_queue_pauses.message`, the 1.0 group's 15th
     step). Only a conflict, a hook or red checks return a card; every other cause is a pause.
   - Resuming after fixing the cause is #1353's; signing without a prompt stays #1185.
5. **Merge checks** (G9) run on that worktree as runs attributed to "Combwork (merge queue)", named for the card and the
   result revision (§16.13). The worktree is the queue's own and no one else writes in it, so the checks run on
   exactly the result. **Dependencies from scratch** [HB3's round 1 finding 12]: when the result's package manifests or
   lock files differ from those the worktree last installed, the queue runs the project's install in a clean state
   (the setup script with a clean flag; for npm, `npm ci`) before the checks, so a dependency missing from the manifest
   fails here (#187). Team's merge checks always install clean.
   **Built [#1349]:** the runner (`queueChecks.ts`) runs each G9 check's configured command (OP-24) one after another
   in the queue's worktree, stopping at the first that isn't green, hidden, with a session command's environment (never
   `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` or a session's `CW_*`; one of its own, `CW_CHECK_BASE`: the target's head the test merge is
   made on, so a check can look at what the card adds, HI-2617), and ends its whole tree at a time limit (Advanced
   `cw.queue.checkMinutes`, 90 minutes). Each check is a progress run of `source: 'combwork'` ("Combwork (merge queue)"),
   titled "AM-12 · typecheck · a3f2c1d", with its output in a bounded log (its first 2 MB and last 64 KB). The queue
   brackets each one and writes `CheckRan` at the **result** revision: green only if it exited 0 **and** counted (§16.13:
   at exactly that revision, clean at the start and the end, nothing written to a tracked file and no HEAD reflog entry
   between, by stat snapshot since the queue's folder isn't watched). Exit 0 but uncounted isn't green: the entry is
   tested again from a fresh test merge, and after `MAX_RETESTS` (3) it pauses `uncounted` (the card's `CheckRan`
   says why). The install is G9's **`mergeInstall`**: `onManifestChange` (the default, Pair's: a clean install whenever
   the manifests' hash differs from the folder's last install, which holds whatever the option says) or `always`
   (Team's: before every entry's checks). It is the worktree setup command in its clean form where Combwork knows one (a
   package manager's install with only known flags after it, those that change what it prints, how it fetches or which
   scripts run: `npm install --no-audit` → `npm ci --no-audit`; pnpm and yarn with their frozen lock file), else **as
   written**, which its run's details say (Combwork has no clean form of a compound command, one naming packages, one with
   another flag such as `--dry-run`, `--prefix` or `-g`, or another tool's). **Before every install** the queue folder's
   `node_modules` is removed (a link removed as a link, never through), so no warm package outlives an install that
   installed nothing: the checks then fail on what's missing rather than pass on what was there [HR3's #1349 round 2]; `npm ci` for a lock file with no setup command; or nothing, which the first check's run
   says once. The install is a run too, titled with its command line, which can hold a token, so it is
   `titleFromCommand` and the Agent API never gives its title out (#620). A log that can't be written (a full disk)
   never stops a run: it is closed and given as no log, and every run started is finished. G9 and G20 empty: no checks
   and no install, so a clean test merge alone merges.
   **Each card's focused tests (G20, built [HI-1367]; design HI-1367/s11–s24 with the user's decisions of 28 Oct).** A
   project gives two commands, `focused.pick` (optional) and `focused.run`, in its `commands`. A selection never passes
   by default:
   - **At submit** (`submit.focusedChosen`): Combwork reads the change path by path (`git diff --raw` with full blob ids,
     modes and rename endpoints) and runs the picker in the card's folder under a check's bracket (§16.13): at exactly
     the revision, clean at both ends, nothing written in between, else its pick is `unknown` (a check copy has no
     dependencies, and Combwork's own picker needs them; its submission's **operation** ends it with its tree, `cancelled`: each submit call makes one operation, which ends the card's operation before it, and its workspace closing ends any; every retry of the call (a re-gather after the evidence changed) carries that operation and never makes one, so a superseded call never ends its replacement; it is checked after gathering, after the evidence is checked again and under the write's lock, and an ended call is refused there, with the builder's own list or not). Its stdin is the paths, `CW_FOCUSED_BASE` the base; its stdout
     JSON lines `{"test", "needs": [unit | fake | real | packaged]}` or `{"every": true}`, its stderr kept apart as
     diagnostics, bounded (256 KB, 500 tests), ended with its tree at Advanced `cw.focused.pickSeconds` (180 s). A

   - **At the merge**, after G9's checks and the same install (G20 alone installs too): the approved selection stands for

     never run in the queue (realProof = review, the user's decision): each counts from its standing run at the

     counted run there, not the queue's, its configured command (if any) unchanged, which must have passed (an earlier
     pass never stands behind a later counted failure; HI-2660). That run is by the card's lane reviewer or an agent whose
     pass approved it (`CheckRan.agent`), or (HI-2660, the user's decision, 7 Nov) another agent's (the builder's) that
     such a pass accepted by its run id (`cw_verdict`'s `accept`, at most 50 test ids, each checked at the verdict the
     same way: `Verdict.accepted`, `{ test, run, agent }`, the original run and its agent, never relabelled; an id it
     can't stand behind is a warning, accepting nothing). A builder's own run never counts unaccepted. It is accepted as
     review evidence (`FocusedAccepted`, with `acceptedBy` when it came by acceptance), never a run at the result, and read again from the card's facts at the queue's last check and in `IntegrationStarted`'s write (HI-2660: a proof gone since, by a counted failure or its acceptance gone, sends the entry round again, whose checks return the card for it); one missing returns the card (`noProof`, which may go back unchanged once that run exists), and one
     only the merge's pick adds returns it (`newProof`). The rest run once as the check `focused tests`, bracketed like a
     G9 check, the list in a file (`CW_FOCUSED_TESTS`), the results written to another (`CW_FOCUSED_RESULTS`), and
     Advanced `cw.queue.focusedJobs` (2) as `CW_FOCUSED_JOBS`: green only when the runner exited 0, it counted, and the results (read at most 1 MB) hold
     exactly one result per test, none failed; a runner exits 0 when nothing failed, skips included. A failed test, a missing, duplicate or unknown record, or a runner failure returns the
     card with its output. A test **skipped** for its environment pauses the queue (`focusedSkip`) and asks the card's
     reviewer agent (`cw_focused_skip`) and the user under For you (`FOCUSED_SKIP_GATE`), the user able to answer
     first; the request and its decision are bound to the entry, the tests, the target's head and the merged tree, so
     the entry is tested again and takes that decision only for exactly that result (a moved target is asked again).
6. **Advance the target only on green** (§16.9.2), after writing `IntegrationStarted` (§16.4.5). If the target moved
   since the test (it isn't at the expected revision), the entry goes back to step 2 against the new head; after
   **3** such retests in a row the entry pauses ("main moves faster than its checks: retest or merge by hand") [HB3's
   round 1 finding 19].
7. Record `Integrated` (the result revision, method), move the card to Done, release its slot, end the lane if done.
   **Push after merging (G18, built [#1179]):** with *Push the target branch after merging* on (the project's options
   as they are then: G18 is in no ruleset), the same write records that the target's push is owed (store meta
   `queue.pushOwed:<target>`: the result, card and entry), in recovery's `Integrated` after a restart too, so the card
   is Done and the push owed, or neither. Then, and before the queue's next entry (first thing in every run, so after a
   restart or Resume too), the queue settles it: the option off by then (read again just before the push begins), or
   the target no longer holding the result (reset since), drops it with no push; a read of the target that fails is
   never taken for settled: it pauses `pushUnreadable` (Combwork's own words, translated), still owed, so no later merge goes ahead of it; else it pushes `refs/heads/<target>` to what the target tracks
   (`branch.<target>.remote` and `.merge`), or with nothing tracked to the only remote or `origin` under the same name,
   never `--force` and never `--set-upstream`, with no prompt (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, no askpass, the credential
   manager non-interactive) and within the Git view's 5 minutes. Pushed, or up to date already (a retry after a crash
   before the clear), it is cleared, only if still the same result (a newer merge's stays owed). Refused (the remote
   has commits the target lacks), failed (git's message: a sign-in, the network, the bound) or with no remote: the
   queue pauses (`pushRejected`, `pushFailed`, `pushNoRemote`, naming the merged card, which stays Done), the next entry
   waits, and the pause says what to do: pull (or fix it) and Resume, or turn G18 off and Resume to keep merging
   locally. Combwork never pulls by itself, and agents never push.
8. **Conflict or red checks:** `IntegrationFailed` with the files or the check output and log, `transient` when the
   failure was the environment (a check that failed to start, a network error, a timeout) rather than a result; the
   card goes to Active, back to its builder. A conflict, red checks or a hook failure need a new revision (review
   again unless it's the same change); a transient failure is resubmitted unchanged, straight into the queue, at most
   twice (`requeue.allowed`, §16.8.1)
   [note §9; answering HR2's round 1 finding 7]. **Built [#1349], the certain cases** (`classifyCheckFailure`): a check
   that couldn't start (a spawn error, or its program not found, told before it starts on Windows, where cmd exits 1 for
   it), one ended by its time limit, or one killed from outside (a signal, Windows' interrupt status) is transient;
   anything else is red. A process another program ends with TerminateProcess exits with the code that program gave,
   which can't be told from the check's own, so it counts as red. **Built [#1362]** (Darren, 21 Oct, #1121 point 3:
   (a) and (b)): a check that exits **75** (EX_TEMPFAIL: the project's own script saying "a temporary failure, try
   again", a way to mark its own environment failures) is transient, and so is a failed check whose **last 40 lines**
   (trailing blank lines aside) have one of Node's and npm's network error codes (`ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`,
   `ECONNRESET`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `ETIMEDOUT` as whole words: Settings → Advanced, **Merge queue: network errors that
   count as temporary**, a pattern with samples recorded from npm 11.17.0 and Node 24.19.0; `(?!)` turns it off). A code
   only earlier in the output, or in a check that passed, is nothing. Why is recorded as codes, never text: the
   `IntegrationFailed` fact's `cause` (`spawn`, `notFound`, `timeout`, `killed`, `exit75`, `network`) and `code` (the
   network error code found), and the check's run says it in its details. Transient only permits: the card is still
   returned to its builder (`returnCard`), and the builder's resubmission puts the same revision back; nothing retries by
   itself. Codes are looked for as the output comes (`TailCodes`), each line whole as it ends, so the 40 lines are the
   check's real last lines, not the short output a result carries. The answer depends on the output, never on how it was
   chunked: a line still being written past 64 KB is settled only as far as its text decides (a match counts once 256
   real characters follow it; one running closer to the unfinished end is searched again from its start), and only the
   undecided part is kept, after 512 real characters before it, so a word boundary or lookbehind sees the real text,
   never a start the trimming made. Bounded: a code per line for the last 40 lines, a line in progress up to about
   64 KB; the limit is a match and what decides it within 256 characters (a code). **Pauses are not failures:** a busy or dirty target folder, a missing
   identity or a signing wait pauses the entry with its reason and never returns the card [HB3's round 1 finding 3].

**Forward merges (HI-2679, design s10; Darren's decisions of 7 Nov on HI-2556's s14).** Bringing one of a project's
targets up to date with another (Bring Up to Date… on the destination's queue card; `cw_queue` `forward`;
`POST /v1/queue/forward`), the user's or the Assistant's alone, is an entry of the destination's queue on a card Combwork
makes for it (`forwardMerge`, queueControls.ts; one per pair while open). The open card looked for, the caller's
authority checked, the card made and started with its facts and entry are one board change (one transaction, under the
board's lock another Combwork takes too): refused or stopped part way, none of it is kept.
- its authority is its `ForwardRequested` {from, to, source, by}, written only by that request, right after its
  `Started` {folder project, line **null**, target = to, builder combwork}: with no line, nothing that updates, attributes
  or cleans up a card's line can touch the source;
- it runs under its own rules (`forwardOf`, its id the base's targeted one marked `~forward`, old rules comparing the
  base): no review (its fact is its approval), a merge commit always (G6), G8 off (the source never brought up to date
  with the destination), no focused tests (G20); every other gate stays (rules off, pauses, Ask each time on a
  checked-out target, the lease, the compare and swap);
- each attempt's source is its entry's frozen `revision`: a source that moves while it waits changes nothing; found in
  the destination already, that very commit is recorded `Integrated` (by outside);
- a conflict or a red check returns the card to Active (no builder is woken: it says so on itself), both branches as
  they were, and so does its advance declined (Ask each time on a checked-out destination); **Retry merge** freezes the source again at its head then (a new entry, its own checks); **Remove from
  queue** ends it in Done with `IntegrationCancelled`, never an `Integrated` (refused while it advances);
- a project agent's every intent on it is refused (`forward.notAgents`).

Each target's queue card lists how far it is behind each other target of the project (`QueueView.forward`): the commits
along the other's first-parent history it lacks (`git rev-list --count --first-parent to..from`: a card merged with a
merge commit or squashed counts once, a rebased one per commit), kept by both heads (at most 64 pairs), null when a head
can't be read; the window's listing includes every existing target, so a destination with nothing queued shows while it
is behind. Automatic forward merges are later (they would refuse cycles).

#### 16.9.2 Advancing the target

[P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 9 and round 2 finding 4] The advance moves the target from the expected
revision to the result, or leaves it where it was. Two cases, with different guarantees, stated exactly.

**Target not checked out in any folder** (`git worktree list` shows no folder on it): one command,
`git update-ref refs/heads/<target> <result> <expected>`, which git applies only if the ref is at `<expected>`. This is
a true compare-and-swap: nothing else is touched, and a crash leaves the ref either moved or not.

**Target checked out in a folder** (the project folder usually has `main`). Moving the branch means updating that
folder's index and files too, which git can't do in one atomic step with an expected value (`read-tree` updates the
index and files, `update-ref` moves the ref; HR2's probe showed the state between them: HEAD at the expected revision,
index and files at the result). So it is a **journaled** operation, with conditions checked before anything is
touched:

- **Before touching the folder** (Combwork holds the repository lock and the folder fence: #646, nothing of Combwork's is typed
  into the folder meanwhile), all of these must hold, else the entry **pauses** with the reason and nothing is
  changed:
  - no agent **builds** there: holds file locks in that folder or has a run going with it as its working folder (an
    idle agent, or a reviewer whose session lives there but works in a review copy, doesn't count) [HB3's round 1
    finding 3];
  - `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` names `refs/heads/<target>`, and the ref is at `<expected>`;
  - **the index equals the expected revision's tree** (`git diff --cached --quiet <expected>`: nothing staged), and none
    of the files the merge changes has unstaged changes (the rest of the user's edits are left as they are). The
    journal records the list of files the merge changes.
- **The journal** is the `IntegrationStarted` fact (§16.4.5) followed by an **`IntegrationPhase`** fact (entry id,
  phase) appended and committed before each step; nothing is rewritten (the log stays append-only):
  1. `phase: files`, then `git read-tree -m -u <expected> <result>` (index and the listed files to the result);
  2. `phase: ref`, then `git update-ref refs/heads/<target> <result> <expected>`;
  3. `Integrated`.
- **Failures while running** (git refuses, or the swap finds the ref moved): Combwork rolls the files back with
  `git read-tree -m -u <result> <expected>` (`phase: rollback`), which git refuses rather than overwrite if anything
  changed meanwhile; then back to the test merge. A rollback git refuses is a **terminal state** (below).
- **Recovery after a crash,** from the journal, never assumed: Combwork reads HEAD's branch, the ref, the index tree for the
  listed files and their working copies.

  | Journal phase | Found | Then |
  |---|---|---|
  | `files` | ref at `<expected>`, index and files at `<expected>` (read-tree never ran) | Run from step 1 again. |
  | `files` or `ref` | ref at `<expected>`, index and listed files at `<result>` (read-tree ran, swap didn't) | Re-check the conditions for the swap (branch, ref); if they hold, run step 2 (the result is the journaled commit, never a new merge, so hooks or time can't make it differ). If the ref moved meanwhile, roll the files back as above. |
  | `ref` | ref at `<result>` | Write `Integrated` (observed). |
  | `rollback` | index and files at `<expected>` | Back to the test merge. |
  | any | anything else (the branch switched, files edited, a rollback refused) | **Terminal: needs you.** The queue pauses for that target, the card shows the exact state (branch, ref, the listed files and which side each is at) and the commands that finish or undo it; Combwork changes nothing more on its own. |

- **What this does not guarantee** [HR2's round 2 finding 4]: another git client acting in the same instant, between
  Combwork's checks and `read-tree`, is outside Combwork's lock. git's index lock and `read-tree`'s refusals stop it from
  overwriting a changed file; the one case they don't stop is **a branch switch in that instant to a branch whose
  index matches the expected tree for every listed file**: then the merged files would be written into that other
  branch's working copy, as uncommitted changes (no commit or ref of it moves). Combwork detects it right after (HEAD no
  longer names the target), pauses with the terminal state above, and lists the files to restore. Whether to accept
  that residue for automatic merges into a checked-out target, or to ask the user before each such update, is
  **OP-40**; P5 ships the journal and its crash-injection tests (before and after each step and the rollback) either
  way, and until they pass the checked-out case asks the user (**Update main now** on the queue card).
- `git merge --ff-only` is not used: it has no expected value [HR2's round 1 finding 9].

**Built [#1351]** (`mergeQueue.ts`, `queueHost.ts`):
- **Where:** the target's folder is the one `git worktree list` names for it, read again under the repository lock
  (switched while the queue waited for it: looked at again, the right way). Checked out nowhere by then, it is the
  compare-and-swap above; a folder on another branch means exactly that.
- **The authority** [HR4's #1351 round 1]: Combwork writes to a target (`IntegrationStarted`, an `IntegrationPhase`,
  `read-tree`, `update-ref`, recovery's `Integrated` or `IntegrationFailed`, the queue's pause) only inside the repository
  lock and, for a checked-out target, its folder's fence, after deciding again there, from state read there, the
  target's saved pause, Ask or Automatic with the matching approval, the rules, the card's open entry and approval, and
  where the target is checked out. A check before the lock is an early-out only. A pause Combwork writes for what it saw in
  the lock (a condition, the terminal state, the ask) is written before the lock is released, and never in place of a
  pause saved meanwhile (the user's Pause queue stands, and nothing is asked under it; decided in the pause's own
  write), except the terminal state, which the user must settle anyway. Whoever caused the run
  (the card's own queue, another card's enqueue, a workspace reopening, another Combwork), the same holds. **A needs-you
  pause naming a card freezes its target:** recovery reads it first, in the lock, and writes nothing until the user
  lifts it (Resume, or the answer to its For you, which check first); other pauses (Pause queue, rules off, approval)
  stop new advances but let a begun one finish or roll back.
- **Under the lock and the fence:** the conditions, the journal and its rollback run holding the repository lock
  (#1347) and the folder's fence (#646: `changingFolder`, so no line of Combwork's is typed into an agent there and none
  starts there meanwhile). The test merge and the merge checks run without either: a user's commit, or a Git view action
  that takes the lock, during an hour of checks is never held up, and the swap's expected value catches the moved
  target, which is tested again (S42).
- **The conditions**, each a pause naming its files, nothing touched (the entry stays queued, never returned):
  `folderBusy` (an agent holds file locks in the folder, or a run of an agent, the Assistant or a script is going with
  it as its working folder: the locked files and the run's folder named; an idle agent, or one whose session lives
  there but works in a review copy, doesn't count), `wrongBranch` (the folder named), the ref no longer at the expected
  revision (tested again), `staged` (the staged files named), `unstagedChanges` (the listed files with a change in the
  working copy or index, untracked ones included, from the folder's whole status, so a long list never makes a command
  line too long). The user's other edits are left as they are. Resume (#1353) checks each again.
- **The journal:** `IntegrationStarted` with the listed files and the folder, then `IntegrationPhase` `files`,
  `read-tree -m -u <expected> <result>`, `IntegrationPhase` `ref`, `update-ref`; each phase's fact is written through
  the runner's lease fence (#1360), and the lease is checked again just before each git step, so a runner that lost its
  lease writes nothing more and touches nothing. A `read-tree` git refuses having written nothing (the index still at
  the expected revision) fails the entry as target moved and queues it again, a file edited since the check pausing
  `unstagedChanges`, named; anything else is the terminal state. A swap that finds the ref moved rolls back (`rollback`,
  `read-tree -m -u <result> <expected>`) and tests again; a rollback git refuses is the terminal state. A rerun after a
  restart begins a journal of its own: an earlier attempt's phases never count.
- **After the swap:** HEAD is read again. Not naming the target (the race above): `Integrated` (the target did move,
  so nothing is merged twice), then the terminal state with phase `done`, listing the merged files left in the other
  branch's working copy and the command that puts them back.
- **Recovery:** the table above, read from the journal's last phase, HEAD's branch, the ref and each listed file's side
  (its index entry and working copy both at the expected revision, both at the result, or neither: `other`), under the
  lock and the fence. Ref at the result: `Integrated` (observed), and the terminal state when the folder is on another
  branch with merged files in it. Ref at the expected revision, on the target: phase `files` (or none, or `rollback`)
  with the files at the expected revision runs again from the test merge; phase `files` or `ref` with the files at the
  result finishes the swap from the journal (writing phase `ref` first), rolling back if the ref moved in that instant.
  Ref elsewhere: files at the result are rolled back; files at the expected revision (read-tree never ran, or the
  rollback finished) fail the entry as target moved and queue it again. Anything else is the terminal state.
- **The terminal state** (`needsYou`, a typed record: the 1.0 group's 17th step adds the folder, HEAD's branch, the ref,
  the revisions and the phase to `workflow_queue_pauses`, each file's side to `workflow_queue_pause_files`, and
  `workflow_queue_pause_commands` with each command's arguments in `workflow_queue_pause_command_args`, never a shell
  string): the commands are generated from the journal as the state allows, only revisions and ref names, each run in
  the project folder or the target's folder, and shown as a PowerShell line (`shellLine`: an argument of anything but
  letters, digits and `._/:=+-` single-quoted, `'` doubled, so a ref such as `topic$part` reaches git as written; a ref
  with `"`, which Windows PowerShell can't hand a program as written, gets no command naming it): on the target with the ref at the expected
  revision and every file at the result, **finish** `git update-ref refs/heads/<target> <result> <expected>` and **undo**
  `git read-tree -m -u <result> <expected>`; the ref at the result and the files at the expected revision, finish
  `git read-tree -m -u <expected> <result>`; the ref moved and the files at the result, or the merged files left in
  another branch, undo; a file at neither side, none (git would refuse them). The queue's model (`queue:list`, `GET
  /v1/queue` without the folder, `cw_queue`) carries it as the pause's `stuck`, for #1356 and #1357. The card also
  asks the user (For you, Decide, gate `queueStuck`): its words say what to run, or to put the files right by hand;
  answering looks again as Resume does (`recheckStuck`), lifting the pause once recovery can carry on, and any other
  pause stays.
- **Ask each time** (OP-40): Settings → Advanced, **Merge queue: merge into a checked-out branch**
  (`cw.queue.checkedOutTarget`): *Ask each time* · *Automatically* (the default since the crash-injection tests
  passed in #1351's review). Under Ask, an entry whose test merge and checks
  are done, ready to advance into a target checked out in a folder, asks "<card> is tested and ready to merge: update
  <target> in <folder> now?" (For you, Approve, gate `queueAdvance`, bound to the entry, the expected revision and the
  result) and the queue pauses `approval`, naming the folder. The answer is an `enqueue` of its target: approved, the
  advance runs at once on that test merge (the target moved meanwhile: tested again, and asked again, the earlier
  request retired); declined, the entry leaves the queue as Remove from queue leaves it (Approved), and the queue goes
  on. Resume doesn't stand in for the answer. The setting turned to *Automatically* wakes a queue waiting for its
  Approve: it advances the asked test merge as an approval would, and the question is retired with the entry's
  outcome. A target checked out nowhere never asks.
- **Crash injection** (S34d): test copies (unpackaged) take `CW_TEST_QUEUE_CRASH` = `afterStarted`, `beforeFiles`,
  `afterFiles`, `beforeRef`, `afterAdvance`, `inRollback` or `afterRollback` (Combwork ends at that point, no quit handler)
  and `CW_TEST_QUEUE_RACE=beforeRef` (the target moved by another client just before the swap, once per run): the
  e2e suite `mergequeuecrash` restarts after each and checks the card is merged exactly once with the folder clean, and
  the terminal state; `mergequeuefolder` has S27, S34a–c, S42 and Ask each time (the crash restarts in a suite of
  their own, so a failure in one never hides the other's).

#### 16.9.3 Around the queue

**Locks** [note §12; HB3's round 1 finding 3 and round 2 finding G; #1338's round 1 finding 3] **Built [#1347]**: a
**repository lock** across processes (the dev and installed Combwork can't merge into or advance a target at once). It is
a row, not a file's existence: one row (`repo_lock`: `id` 1, `token`, `pid`, `process_start`, `profile`, `taken_at`;
a typed table) in a small SQLite database in the repository's common git dir (`cw-merge.lock`, so its worktrees
share it; `repoLockCore.ts`). Taking it is `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (SQLite's own cross-process lock) then: no row, or a row
whose holder is **dead** (its pid gone, or running with another process start time: a reused pid), judged before the
transaction and replaced only if the row is still the one judged (its token: compare and swap), so of two contenders
on one dead holder exactly one takes it. A **live holder is never taken over**, however long it holds: the waiter's
bound (Settings → Advanced, **Merges: wait for another Combwork**, 30 s) only ends its own attempt, with "Another Combwork is
merging into this repository (<profile>)", which it also shows after a moment's wait. Release deletes the row by its
token, so a late release after a takeover removes nothing of the new holder's. Why not a lock file taken with
exclusive create: stale takeover by rename or unlink isn't atomic (two contenders can both judge it stale, and a late
release can unlink a successor's file). It **replaced** the in-process merge lock of 1.0 (`withFileLock`, which
still serializes this Combwork's own takes of the row): the Git view's folder actions (§8), a worktree's merge (the Merge
dialog, agents' and unused worktrees' merges) and the line updater's move of an agent's branch (§16.19.2, which waits
quietly and tries again on its next pass) take it. No off switch: it is data safety (§16.6.4). It is held **only for
the advance** (§16.9.2), seconds. The test merge
(which runs the repository's hooks and may wait on signing) and the merge checks (an hour on Team) run without it:
they write only the queue's worktree and `refs/cw/queue/*`, and the advance's expected value catches anything that
moved meanwhile. A paused entry holds no lock. One queue per target still runs one entry at a time.

**The runner** [Built #1360]: exactly one Combwork runs a target's queue, across every Combwork on the workspace (the dev and
the installed one share its `combwork.db`, S50). It holds the target's **lease** (a row in `combwork.db`: the holder's profile,
pid and process start time, when it was taken and last renewed). Another Combwork takes the lease over **only once the
holder process is gone** (its pid gone, or given to a process that started at another time), never because its
renewals stopped: a stalled but living Combwork keeps its queue, and the panel says "run by <profile>". A Combwork that finds
the lease held **watches the holder's process** while the target has open entries (every 30 s, the renewal period: the
pid first, then its start time) and, once it is gone, runs the queue itself, taking the lease over with no other
prompt [#1455, built in #1358: before it, the queue waited for a new entry, Resume or a reopened workspace].

Each lease has a **Windows job object** that owns every process the runner starts for the life of its whole tree (a
check's detached server too: nothing may break away from it), held by Combwork's process supervisor (the one agents'
launches use), which ends with its Combwork; closing the job ends everything in it. What escapes a job anyway (a packaged
app's process, such as the Store's PowerShell, starts its children outside every job) is adopted into it or followed,
as for agents; a process it follows is first written to the lease's journal (a file the supervisor flushes to disk),
and one it can't write down is ended at once and the queue pauses (needs you). A command starts only once it is in the
job and recorded in `combwork.db`.

**The runner's git** (HI-2079): its git commands with no time bound (reads, and its writes in its own folder and refs)
run in one **git host** per lease, a process put in the job and recorded as a launcher is, before it runs anything; each
git is its child, so in the job from its start. A git then costs git's own start only (about 80 ms less per command,
and one process start instead of two). Its bounded commands (a push, a signed commit) keep a launcher of their own, whose
bound ends their whole tree. A host that goes, or says something it shouldn't, is never taken for an answer: what was
waiting is unknown (the step goes round again), the runner gives its lease up (its job ended, as a release does), and
the queue takes a new lease, which settles what the old one left and recovers its begun entries. A second runner in a
row whose host fails pauses the queue (needs you).

**Its reads too** (HI-2078): every git the queue's run makes while it recovers and drains, the reads it asks of the
repository included (where the target is checked out, the folder's status, containment, the identity), runs in that
host, within the same output and time bounds as Combwork's other git (the host ends a command past them). So a read stuck in
a filesystem, a filter or a hook ends with the lease, as the queue's own git does. Once its runner no longer holds the
lease, a read of that run starts nothing and is never an answer.

**A runner works on a target only once every earlier lease of it is settled**, or the queue is paused (needs you),
naming what couldn't be ruled out. Settled: its job, ended by its name (never the supervisor holding it, which may
serve a living Combwork's other targets and agents), is empty or gone; its journal is sealed (closed to writers for good:
a supervisor that outlived its Combwork can't write down anything more, and ends what it can't write down instead), then
read, and could be; every process its records and its journal name is gone (ended by pid and start time, never by
name); and its folder is removed, in that order, its duty dropped only after all of them. What a runner owns stays
recorded as a duty of the target until then, however many runners crash in between; a journal that can't be read, or
isn't whole, is never taken for empty; a folder that can't be removed pauses the queue naming it, until a later try
removes it. A clean release (closing a
workspace, quitting) ends and confirms its own job first, and leaves as duties what it couldn't confirm.

Each fact the queue writes, reconciliation's included, checks the lease in the same write, so a runner that lost its
lease stops at once, writing nothing. Each lease has **its own worktree** (`queue-<hash of project and target>-<lease>`,
in the project's Combwork worktrees folder): a takeover makes a new one, never an earlier runner's. A target's worktree is
kept while the queue needs it (an open entry, an unfinished advance, an in-flight card whose ruleset says Combwork merges
into that target, a run in it) and removed when nothing does, or with its project. Unused Worktrees never lists a
living runner's worktree.

**Accepted (a limitation, not a guarantee):** a process that escapes a job and that the supervisor hasn't yet seen
(about a second, or until the next process of the job ends) has no identity anywhere if Combwork crashes in that moment,
so a takeover can't end it, and it may go on doing whatever its command does. Worktrees share the repository and its
refs, and a command can use any path: such a process isn't confined to the old lease's folder, needn't take Combwork's
repository lock, and could move a ref, the target's included. What Combwork itself does stays safe: the takeover removes
the old folder or pauses naming it, the queue's facts and pauses are fenced by the lease, and Combwork's own advance is a
compare-and-swap against the head it tested, so it never builds on a target that moved under it unseen.

**Pins** [HB3's round 1 finding 11]: every submitted revision is pinned by a ref, `refs/cw/cards/<key>/<n>` (the
submission's number), until the card is archived, so a deleted line, a force push or garbage collection can't lose
what was reviewed or approved. Ref paths compare keys case-insensitively (NTFS).

**`mergeWorktree`** (`worktrees.ts`) [note §9, #1121] **Built [#1347]**: it returns the merge commit
(`MergeResult.mergeCommit`), takes a target (default: the project folder's checked-out branch; a branch checked out
nowhere is merged without touching a folder, the merged tree committed and the branch moved only from its tip; one
checked out in another folder is refused; a target is the branch git keeps under that name in any case, since Windows'
ref store is one ref for `main` and `MAIN`, and two branches differing only in case are refused), and never auto-commits a dirty worktree (before 1.0 it ran `add -A` and
committed): it refuses with the files counted and the next step ("commit or stash them in the worktree, then merge"),
which the Merge dialog shows before Merge (greyed out); a dirty slot refuses submit instead.
The **Merge… dialog** stays for the user's own merges outside cards; for a card's line it shows the queue instead
(OP-13).

**"The agent merges, Combwork checks"** (G5): the builder merges itself (as today's merge-ready), then reports the merge;
Combwork checks containment (`done.contained`) before Done, and refuses with the fix if the approved revision isn't in the
target [note §9 alternative].

**Observed merges:** a merge done by hand is observed (§16.4.4); the queue cancels that entry.

**Agents under Combwork merges** **Built [#1354]**: a builder never merges a card Combwork merges, and is told at each queue
outcome what to do. What decides is the card's own ruleset (the options it started under, or the user's change applied
to it, OP-38), never the project's current options: a card started under Combwork merges stays so after the project
switches to "The agent merges", and one started afterwards reports its merge.
- **Refusals** (`merge.combworkMerges`, three messages in 7 locales; agents get the English): `report merge` (and an
  agent's `cw_update_task` move to Done, translated or not) and a merge-slot claim naming the card are refused with
  where it is in the queue as the next step (`QUEUE_NEXT`: queued with its position, being merged, paused, returned,
  merged; otherwise "once it is approved"; paused, with what the pause waits for, #1406: `pauseWait` of the saved pause,
  the user's Resume, their answer in For you (`approval`; `needsYou` with a stuck advance), what stopped it fixed and
  Resume (`needsYou` with no question: git's error, an earlier runner's process), the checked-out folder put right and
  Resume (`wrongBranch`, `staged`, `unstagedChanges`, `folderBusy`), or the rules enforced again, which resumes it
  (`rulesOff`; Resume for one left paused with them on), as the agent's queue line says too), and "set in Version Control → Who merges. A card keeps the rules it started
  with." The claim is refused before the slot is touched; one naming no card, or cards the agent merges, is unchanged,
  and so is the Merge dialog's. Each is a `Refused` fact; `override` is none.
- **Wakes**: a returned card's (`returnCard`) says what came back (a conflict: its files; checks: which check, `install`
  for the install before them, its log's path and the output's last lines; a hook) and the next step (merge the target
  in and resolve; fix, commit and submit; for a transient failure, submit the same revision again, at most twice in a
  row), within 600 characters: a wake line quotes Combwork's own note up to 600, a reviewer's request still 200. What came
  back and the next step are always whole (a branch, check or code name in them cut at 80 characters, marked "…"),
  fitted first; the rest takes the room left: the files, as many of the first 8 as fit and how many more; the log's
  path whole, or else "Its log path: cw_read_task" (a card read has room for it); the output's last lines, cut from
  their start ("…"). `IntegrationFailed` keeps `check` and `logPath`, and of the output (`log`) its start and its end
  within 4,000 characters, the middle replaced by a line saying how many characters were left out, so the last lines
  quoted are the output's own. **The return leads every line about it** (HI-2087: on 30 Oct HB2's watch for Done
  read "HI-2046 is in Doing; latest comment by HR1: Round 2: PASSED", and HB2 took the card as merged): a card watch's
  line for a card moved back to work by the queue (`queueReturnOf` in `watches.ts`, `WakeAbout.queueReturn`) is the
  return's own words in place of where it is and its latest comment, with others or alone; an inbox item telling
  several of a card's events leads with its latest return ("… (with 2 more changes: read the card)"). Its **reviewer is
  woken when the builder submits it again** (HI-2143: HR2's watch on HI-2122, any move counted, began in Review before its
  pass; the card left and came back, and the watch, comparing only where it was, never fired, while Combwork's loop wake left
  it to that watch): a watch on any move counts a card that left and came back unless every move since was the watcher's
  own, and a card watch's line or loop wake to anyone but the builder for a card back in Review, submitted after the
  queue's return with no verdict since (`resubmittedOf` in `queueReturn.ts`, `WakeAbout.resubmitted`), leads with "HI-12
  is back in Review after the merge queue returned it (a conflict with main in …); HB1 resolved it and submitted it
  again: review the resolution" ("changed it … review what changed" for another return). And the queue
  leaves a **comment of Combwork's on the card** (a `comment` action after the change commits, written once by the action's
  id): its English is the return's words with more room (1,500 characters, 10 of the output's last lines), what agents
  read with `latestComment`; the window shows a message of its own (`tasks.history.queueReturned`: why, the target, the
  check, up to 10 files), pointing at the card's Work section for the run. A card that left the queue (`skip`)
  says why: its pass stale (`IntegrationCancelled` reason `stale`), or a decision since its approval (`decision`, no
  pass at the current generation).
- **Card reads**: the Agent API's card has `merge`, a sentence from `queueState.ts` (where a card is with the queue,
  from its facts and `queueOrder`, the order #1353's window model (`queueView`) shows: the entry testing now at its
  step, those waiting behind it): who merges it, and queued (position, 1 next after the one testing), testing (its
  merge, its checks, or advancing the target), paused (why), returned (what came back and what to do), left the queue, or
  not approved yet; absent once it is Done and for cards the agent merges. `cw_lane next` names the lane's passed
  cards Combwork merges with that line, and the next card waits for them.
- **Skills**: work-on-card, card-loop and merge-ready say, where they tell an agent to merge a passed card, "unless the
  card says Combwork merges it (`cw_read_task`: its `merge`): then the merge queue merges it; wait for Done or a return"
  (P8 rewrites the guidance whole).
- **Workflow rules off** (Settings → Advanced): nothing refuses; a card Combwork merges is reported as before 1.0, approved
  or waiting in the queue, whose entry is cancelled (`integratedOutside`, as S7's hand merge); the card read says to
  merge it and report the merge.

**User controls:** **Pause queue** / **Resume** (the user; the Assistant within Control), saved and shown; **Remove
from queue** on an entry, recorded as an override and as `IntegrationCancelled`. The slot's **Release** goes away
[#1121 c].

**Built [#1353]** (the controls and the model; the panel is #1356's, the card's queue state #1357's):
- **One model** of each target's queue for every control: the card testing now (its revision, the target's head it is
  tested on, its step: test merge, checks or advance, since when, and its check's run), the cards waiting in order, the
  latest 20 outcomes (merged with the result; returned with why, the files and the log; cancelled), the pause (why, the
  card, the files, who and when) and which Combwork runs it. The window reads it with `queue:list` and is told of each change
  (`queue-changed`); the Agent API with `GET /v1/queue` (a project agent its own project's; outcomes say whether there is
  a log rather than carry it); the Assistant and agents with `cw_queue` (`list`).
- **Who may (OP-9):** the user from the window; the Assistant within Settings → Assistant → Control (Control agents),
  through its change boundary (its actions, the per-message limit), with a reason for Remove from queue and Retry merge;
  a project agent never (403, saying whose they are), nor a script (403).
- **Pause queue** is saved per project and target (the pause tables: reason `user`, who and when: schema step 15
  `queue pause by`), so it holds across a restart and in every Combwork on the workspace. The queue stops before its next
  entry; an entry mid-check finishes its checks and waits, open, without advancing, also when the pause lands while its
  advance waits for the repository lock (decided again in `IntegrationStarted`'s write). A queue Combwork paused already keeps
  its own pause, which says more.
- **Resume** clears any pause once the user says its cause is fixed, and runs the queue, which starts again from a fresh
  test merge. Where Combwork can see the cause it checks first, and pauses again, saying so, when it still holds: the rules
  still off, §16.9.2's conditions on the checked-out folder (the branch, nothing staged, the listed files), the user's
  answer to "update it now" still awaited (#1351: Resume doesn't stand in for it), an interrupted advance still in its
  terminal state (the recovery table, read only), an earlier runner's process still running or its folder still there.
  A `checkedOut` pause, from before #1351, resumes.
- **Remove from queue** (an override and `IntegrationCancelled`): the card back to Approved and its builder woken; never
  merged, after a restart too (S33a). Refused once its advance has begun (`queue.advancing`): it is being merged, and
  its recovery finishes it.
- **Retry merge** (an override): a card the queue returned, a red check included, is queued again with its approved
  revision unchanged, once per revision (S32's last part). A card in Approved with no entry (taken out of the queue, or
  for a follow-up), approved and not stale, is queued again too, overriding nothing (#1623); a stale one is refused with
  **submit** as the way on, never **report merge**, which is the agent's own merge, not Combwork's. While a card loop's
  step waits for its reviewer (a follow-up), it is refused: the follow-up's check queues the card again itself.
  **The window offers it only where it runs [HI-1667]:** after a return, while it hasn't been used since the latest
  submission (the work view's `retried`), its confirmation saying once per revision, and once used a line saying the
  next way is a new revision; in Approved, not while a loop step waits (`loopStep`: a line says Retry merge comes back
  once the reviewer has checked it), its confirmation with no such limit.

**Built [#1357]** (the queue on the card, in the Git tab and in the Merge dialog):
- **The card's Work section** (`CardQueue.tsx`) shows the card's newest entry this cycle, from its facts (the work view's
  `queue`, which now carries a return's files, output, whether temporary, when, and a requeue) and its target's queue
  (`queue:list`): queued with its place and the approved revision; testing with its step and Show the run; merging;
  returned with why (a conflict's files, the check by its run's name, the output's last 12 lines, Show log: the run's log,
  else the whole output), and **Retry merge…** (a confirmation: the approved revision requeued unchanged, once);
  taken out with why; the queue paused with why and Resume queue; the OK an update of a checked-out target waits for
  (**Approve** with an optional note, the user's comment / **Decline…** with a required reason, HI-2286: the For you
  answer itself); and §16.9.2's terminal state for its card: the folder, its
  branch, the target's ref, the expected and result commits, each listed file and its side, and the commands that
  finish or undo it, each copyable, none run. It shows whatever the project's options are now. The terminal state's
  For you request (`workflow.forYou.queueStuck`) counts the files and names the Work section, and its row in the
  card dialog has **Show the files and commands**, which opens a folded Work section and brings that part into view once
  read (the Assistant's requirement).
- **The Git tab's Merge queue section** (`GitQueueSection.tsx`, a section of its own for P6 to move): per target, the
  Progress panel's queue card (reused) and its history (`queue:history`: the latest 50 outcomes, each with its card,
  revision, the result or why, and when), a `DataTable` as the archived cards' (#1641): a line a row, the title
  ellipsised, the outcome a short label with the result or why as its tooltip, the merge commit its own column
  (left to the tooltip when narrow), the headings and filters sticky over a box of its own that scrolls. A target shows by #1356's rule, or while it has a history. The panel's
  *Queue in Version Control* opens it.
- **The Merge dialog** (OP-13): for an agent's worktree branch whose card in flight has Combwork merge it under its own
  ruleset, with the rules enforced (`worktrees:branchCards`), it says so and where the card stands (not queued yet,
  queued with its place, testing; the queue paused), and Merge is off with why. **Merge anyway…** (a confirmation)
  merges it and records an override on the card (`merge outside the queue`); the merge is then observed (§16.4.4).
  Merge stays off until that lookup has answered, and when it fails (said, with Retry); main decides again at the
  merge (`agents:merge`), refusing a plain merge of such a card and Merge anyway for another card than the one there
  now, so a dialog's pending or stale state never merges it plainly (HR3's #1357 round 1). Branches with no such card:
  unchanged.

**None:** no queue; Accepted is immediate [#1121 c, OP-16].

Later, not 1.0: batching, speculative merges, stacked cards [note §13].

### 16.10 Slots, review copies and sessions

#### 16.10.1 The pool

[note §7, #1123] A project's **slots** are worktrees at `<Workspace>.worktrees/<Project>/<slot>` (today's location,
§15.12) with generic names (OP-31: `slot-a`, `slot-b`… recommended). A slot is **lent** to a card or a lane and
returned when it ends; free slots stay **ready** (set up, dependencies installed). Lines are named after the
**card**, `cw/<KEY>/<KEY>-<n>-<slug>` [#704 19 Oct] (slug: the title, lower case ASCII letters, digits and hyphens,
at most 40 characters) [P1].

#### 16.10.2 Leases and lifecycle

- **A lease** is one loan of a slot: (lease id, slot, card or lane, builder agent, from, to), a row in `combwork.db`. A
  slot has at most one open lease; lending is done under the slot's lock, so two launch requests for one slot can't
  both get it (the second is refused: "slot-b is in use by HI-B1 for AM-12") [P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 10].
- **Setup and archive scripts** per project (the old `worktreeSetup` and `worktreeCopy`, moved into the Version
  Control tab's slot options), and a per-slot name and port range in the environment (`CW_SLOT`, `CW_SLOT_PORT_BASE`
  with a block of 10 ports) [note §7].
- **Warming** a slot is a run attributed to "Combwork (slot <name>)" [#1123 c].
- **A lease ends** when its card is Done or put back, or its lane ends or is abandoned. Combwork then lets the builder's
  turn finish and stops its session in the slot (the conversation stays resumable while the slot isn't lent again);
  the slot isn't lent again until no session of the old lease is running.
- **Guarded clean-up:** never with a running session in it, unmerged commits (by containment), uncommitted or
  untracked files that aren't ignored, an open lease or a queue entry in flight [note §7; HB3's round 1 finding 11].
- **Squash merges** are detected (§16.3.2); a slot **gone from disk** is recreated (today's `recreateWorktree`,
  `agentWorktree.ts:77`).
- **One writer per slot,** enforced at launch through the lease: only the lease's builder starts a session in it
  [note §7].
- **Pool size:** as many slots as the project has builder agents, at most the project's agent cap; idle slots beyond
  that are removed after a day [P1].

**Built [#1429], the pool (main only; #1438 lends for a card's start):** `src/main/slots.ts`, tables `slots` and
`slot_leases` (the 1.0 group's `slots` step). A slot's state is `creating`, `ready`, `lent`, `dirty`, `gone` or `removing`.
A lease's kind is `card` or `lane` (a dispatch lease) or `carried` (#1441's adopted worktree, which protects its slot
while open, even while its agent holds a dispatch lease elsewhere). One open lease per slot, and one dispatch and one
carried lease per agent, are partial unique indexes: a second fails in SQLite. Lending prefers the slot the builder
last had, then the most recently used; a slot named that is in use is refused "slot-b is in use by HI-B1 for AM-12"
(in English to agents; #1438 words the window's). A new slot is a detached worktree at the target's head, with the
project's copied files and its setup run; a slot whose lock files changed since its last install is installed again;
a failed setup leaves it `creating` with the error and the run's log, and lending skips it. The pool's size is the
project's builders (`setBuilderCount`: its builder and either agents, #1438), at least one, at most its Maximum agents (HI-2001; before, Agents per project).
- **Options:** `project.json` `slots: { setup, archive, copy }`, each left out read from `worktreeSetup`, none and
  `worktreeCopy` (left as they are; the copy then inherits the workspace's and Combwork's, HI-1765).
- **Environment:** `CW_SLOT` and `CW_SLOT_PORT_BASE` (from 41000, 10 ports a slot, unique in the project) for its
  runs now and its sessions from #1434.
- **Runs:** setup, install and archive are Combwork's runs attributed to "Combwork (slot slot-b)" (the window's language;
  the stored name stays English), each in a job of its own on the process supervisor, logs in Combwork's `logs/slots`,
  bounded by Settings → Advanced, **Slots: longest a setup command runs** (`cw.slots.setupMinutes`, 60 min).
- **Released:** a slot left with uncommitted or untracked files that aren't ignored is `dirty`, not lent until clean;
  a free slot gone from disk is recreated when next lent, a leased one marked `gone`. A free slot is looked at again
  when it is next lent (changed since, a session or a process in it: marked or passed over, another tried; a slot
  asked for by name is refused once, *busy*).
- **Operations** (HR1's round 1): warming for a lease and removal own the slot from the write that starts them to the
  write that ends them (`op` on its row: a token every one of their writes checks, and the holder's pid and start).
  Nothing lends, adopts or removes a slot meanwhile; the same card asking again is told it is being set up. Another
  Combwork takes an operation over only once its holder process is gone (or this Combwork's own, left by a workspace closed
  meanwhile), after settling its job: a warming taken over is failed (*its setup was interrupted*, never ready), a
  removal looked at again. A command's job on the process supervisor is recorded on the slot before it starts and
  cleared only once its processes are seen ended, by #1360's protocol (`slotJobs.ts`: the job ended by name, its
  journal sealed before its one read, what it names ended and seen gone, only then cleared); until then the slot isn't
  lent. With no supervisor nothing runs. An operation is its Combwork's from before the write that reserves the slot.
  A workspace closing ends its slots' commands and awaits their operations.
- **Clean-up** is guarded as above, a process in the folder proved absent by renaming it aside and back; the archive
  command runs first and a failure keeps the slot; git removes the worktree, never forced. Combwork's skill copies in
  `.agents/skills/cw-*` are git-ignored, so the guards don't count them [#1500]: just before git removes the folder,
  Combwork removes its own unchanged copies (`removeCopiesIn`, `always`), and a `cw-*` folder still there (a copy edited
  since, or the user's own folder with Combwork's prefix) keeps the slot; any other folder there is untracked, which keeps it too (`editedSkillCopy`, naming the folders). Settings → Advanced,
  **Remove idle slots after a day** (`cw.slots.removeIdle`, on) removes free slots beyond the pool's size unused for
  a day, and failed ones, every hour.

**Built [#1447], Repair and project removal on slots** (`projectFolders.ts`, `workspaceMove.ts`, `agentWorktree.ts`,
`projectRemoval.ts`; they read #1429's and #1435's tables, #1441's homes and `legacyWorktree`, never `AgentDef.worktree`):
- **Repair a Moved Workspace** finds, beside agents' 0.9 worktrees (only those the migration hasn't taken over), each
  slot, copy and retired home, the same way (linked already, Locate…, then the moved-along places), named in the What
  column "slot-b (HI-B1, AM-12)", "hb2 (carried, HB2)", "copy-1", "HR4's old folder". Relinked: `git worktree repair`,
  then, in this order, the move its sessions' folders and Claude Code's per-folder store follow (pendingCopies, as for
  agents; not for copies, whose reviewers run in the project folder), its cards' `FolderMoved` (slots) and its record (a
  slot's or copy's row, in one write only while no operation or job holds it, else Repair tries again; a home's path):
  cut short anywhere, the pending move is still there for the next Repair. Not found: a leased slot offers Recreate (its
  own operation and intent, `slot_recreate:`, taken only while the row is as the plan saw it (that lease, that folder,
  no other holder or writer); the old and new folders checked absent, the prune refused if it would forget another
  worktree, `git worktree add <folder> <line>`, checked on its line; one cut short is finished or put back by the next
  holder, the lease kept either way) or Release (its lease ended); a free slot or a copy is marked
  gone at its place in the moved pool and made again at its next lease (no Locate for a copy); a home offers Locate… or
  Forget. Carried slots' branches named after the old place are renamed as agents' are (#1305). The queue's folders are
  left to its own recovery (#1360). While the workspace or a project waits for Repair, the slots' pass waits too (no
  preparing, placing or deleting on recorded folders that moved), and a card's folder isn't taken for gone.
- **A slot gone from disk** outside a move: its agent's Start says so (`agents:missingWorktree` names the slot) and
  offers **Recreate and Start** (on its line, the lease kept) or **Release the Slot**.
- **Project removal**: Remove from Combwork removes its slots and copies through the pools' guarded clean-up and keeps,
  listed with why, those with work, retired homes and folders outside `<Workspace>.worktrees/<Project>/`. Delete sends
  every slot, copy and retired home in that folder to the Recycle Bin with the project, work included, and is refused
  while one is outside it or busy, holding them all in one write first (`reserveDelete`) so no claim begins meanwhile
  (Darren's decision, 24 Oct; §6).

**Built [#1450], the views that list and merge worktrees** (`unusedWorktrees.ts`, `branchMerge.ts`; they read only #1429's
`slots` and `slot_leases`, #1435's copies and #1434's folder facts and `legacyWorktree`, never `AgentDef.worktree`):
- **Unused Worktrees** lists, besides worktrees no agent works in (as before): a slot left `dirty` with no open lease
  (with Open: the Changes tab shows a detached slot's changes too); free `ready` slots beyond the pool's size, least
  recently used first; a slot whose newest lease is an ended `carried` one; a retired home once no session record of an
  agent the project still has is in it. Never a lent slot, one with an open carried lease, one with an operation, an
  unsettled job or a writer, anything in the project's `copies` folder, or a queue folder its queue uses (#1644: by its record, a living lease, or
  `queueFolderNeeded` on the project's workflow, the folder a released runner keeps warm; not known, used). A recorded
  queue folder its queue no longer needs, and one named as the queue names them with no record, are listed as
  `queue` ("merge queue's old folder, not needed now"); while the records can't be read, neither is. Right before a
  queue folder is deleted, removal claims it in one board write, the lock runners take their lease and record their
  folder under: refused ("the merge queue is using it") while a living runner holds its target's lease or its lease
  has processes not seen gone, else its record is dropped so no runner takes it after (HR4's round 1). A slot
  row's Remove is `SlotPool.remove` (the archive command first; kept with the guard's reason, worded in the window's
  language), its verdict shown before as `SlotPool.check` (the same guards without the rename probe); never Remove
  anyway (its preview is refused). No row offers Give to an agent any more (#1555). "Remove all merged" takes the same rows. Every removal and
  Remove anyway's preview checks again that the folder is still a listed row (a home a conversation resumes in, a copy
  or a live queue folder is refused, by HR3's round 1), and refuses when what it decides from can't be read (session
  records that can't be read keep every retired home, unlisted, HR3's round 2); right
