  before anything is deleted, a session running in the folder keeps it.
- **Branches & remotes' Worktrees** (HI-1710): Combwork's own worktrees are groups of their own, read-only, with no
  button: **Review copies (Combwork's)**, each copy with who uses it ("copy-1: HR6 reviewing HI-12 at a3f2c1d", "… checking
  …" for an isolated check's lease, or "copy-2: idle in the pool", from `copies:list`), and **Merge queue (Combwork's)**, the
  queue's folders (named as the queue names them). `git:info` marks each row `combwork: 'copy' | 'queue'`
  (`combworkWorktreeOf` in `unusedWorktrees.ts`); the Worktrees list keeps agents', slots' and unused ones, never these.
- **The Merge dialog for merges outside cards** (OP-13) picks a branch, a card's line (with its slot), a carried slot's
  branch or any other local branch, and a target (any local branch, the project folder's by default), and merges it as
  an agent's merge (`mergeWorktree` with the target, the target's merge slot, #350): committed work only, refused while
  a session in the branch's folder is mid-task. A line whose card isn't Done (`started.line`, any stage but done) says
  so with a link, and main merges it only when the request names that card, after the window's confirmation; the merge
  is then observed as one outside the rules (§16.4.4; a card in Review is only marked, HI-2709). A card the queue merges takes Merge anyway (#1357). Every merge
  route (`agents:merge`, `worktrees:mergeUnused`, `worktrees:mergeBranch`) goes through one check in main
  (`authorizedMerge`), so the older Merge dialog (an agent's 0.9 worktree, an unused worktree's Open, kept until #1452
  removes the field) shows the same note and asks the same; a slot row's Open → Merge opens Merge a branch.
- **Branches & remotes** reads `slots:list`: a slot's row names its lease (card or lane, its agent; carried for whom; not
  lent), a branch checked out in a slot shows the slot's name, and a folder's agent is its slot lease's, else the agent
  whose session runs there (#1424's worktree badge becomes the slot's).
- **Update from <target>** (HI-1180, rc.4; the design checked by HR4, the conflict rule from Darren's OK via the
  Assistant): a local branch that lacks some of the target's commits (`git:info` counts both ways, `rev-list
  --left-right --count`, as `toTarget` and `fromTarget`; for a branch merged into the target, what it lacks on a
  count of its own) shows how many it lacks and an **Update** action when it has commits of its own, or none but is in
  use (a card's line, a slot's or a worktree's: HR4's round 1). A merged branch nothing uses is Clean Up's, not offered.
  `git:updatePlan` says what it would do: the counts; where it runs (the project folder, the slot or worktree it is
  checked out in, or a temporary detached worktree in the project's worktrees folder, `update-<id>`, when it is checked
  out nowhere); the card whose line it is; the agents working there; for a Passed card whether its pass carries over
  (the project's `sameness`); and why it can't run now. It can't run while an agent there is in a turn, the folder has
  uncommitted changes to tracked files, git is mid-operation there, or the card is in the merge queue (which brings it
  up to date itself, G8). The dialog (`GitForm`) offers **Merge <target> in** (the default: `merge --no-ff`, "Merge
  <target> into <branch>", with `Combwork-Card: <key>` for a card's line) or **Rebase onto <target>** (`--no-update-refs
  --no-autostash`, `rebase.updateRefs=false`; it says the commits are rewritten, and that a pushed copy then differs);
  for a branch with no commits of its own, only **Fast-forward to <target>** (`merge --ff-only`, whichever main is
  given). Git is given the target branch's commit, `refs/heads/<target>` read under the locks, never its name (a tag
  of that name would win), and the branch is checked to contain it afterwards.
  `git:updateBranch` runs it as switch and pull do: one action at a time, the branch's merge slot held as the user's, the
  repository locked, the folder fenced (#646), the plan checked again under them. It commits as the repository's own
  identity, hooks and signing. A conflict, or any failure, is aborted at once (`merge --abort` / `rebase --abort`) and
  then checked: no operation left, HEAD where it was, no tracked change. Only then does the error say the branch is as
  it was (naming the conflicting files, or git's words). An abort that fails (HR4's round 1: a hook that left
  `index.lock`) is said as it is: the folder named, still mid-merge or mid-rebase or left changed, with how to finish it
  there; never "as it was". In a temporary worktree the branch is moved only from the commit it was updated from
  (`update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`); the worktree is removed after, except when its abort failed (kept as git left it,
  the branch not moved, the error naming its path to look at and remove in Unused worktrees), and one that can't be
  removed is said (the reply's second line, or after the error). A card's pass then follows §16.4.4's reconcile (carried over or stale). A user
  action only: no Agent API route or Combwork tool.
- **A branch row's layout** (HI-1897): its name (no minimum of its own, at most 45% of the row), its middle (`.git-branch-info`: badges, card, status, last commit; `flex: 1 1 0`, the last commit giving way first, each part cut with …, the whole in its tooltip, joined with ·), and its tail (`.git-row-tail`, `flex: none`): the time, then each action in a place of its own on every row (an empty slot where a row has none, the current branch's Switch kept unseen), so the time and actions never shrink, leave the row or move, with or without a remote's Track and Stop tracking. Remote branches likewise.
- **Branches by state, and Clean Up Merged Branches** (#1642; Darren's decision: the list stays a list, its rows as they
  were). `git:info` measures each branch against the project's target (its options' `target`, else the default branch;
  none counted when that branch doesn't exist): merged into it (`for-each-ref --merged`), else how many commits it has
  that the target hasn't (`rev-list --count`, the first 60 such branches). `shared/branchCleanup.ts` groups them, In use
  (the target, the default branch, the folder's, a worktree's or slot's, an open card's line: any stage but Done),
  Merged, Not merged, the remote branches too (In use: the remote's HEAD, the target, the default branch), and makes
  the offer: merged local branches nothing uses, ticked; apart, under a warning, merged remote branches whose local
  branch isn't in use, none ticked (outward-facing, the Assistant's requirement; one whose local branch is ticked says
  so). Main checks each again: `git:deleteBranches` under the repository's lock (where slots are made), at the commit
  the window was shown (`update-ref -d <ref> <sha>`, compare-and-delete; never `branch -D`, nor `-d`, which measures
  against HEAD, not the target),
  merged unless it is one unmerged branch the user confirmed with the commits
  it drops (`git:branchDrops`); `git:deleteRemoteBranches` with `push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha> :<ref>`, so one
  that moved on the remote is refused there. Each one kept is said, why. What a branch is to the project (the target,
  read from its options again; the folder's branch, the worktrees and slots, the board's open cards) is read for each
  branch right before it goes (HR1's round 1), and the check and the deletion are one hold (round 2's finding): the
  repository's lock, across copies of Combwork (slot preparation, merges, branch switches, and every workflow options write that can
  move a Git project's target: a project's, a level's for each Git project it reaches, a setting's tool, a platform
  switch, through `withRepoLocks`, each repository once in its git folder's order; round 4's finding), then this Combwork's
  turn of workflow writes (`workflowWrite`), held through a remote's push. The same order everywhere. A branch moved by a git outside the lock meanwhile is refused by git and kept (round 3's finding); one
  checked out in a worktree after all is put back at that commit and kept, said as in use. The dialog keeps what it deleted, so Try Again after a remote's
  failure, or a tick changed after one, asks only for what is left. A card's own line is deleted by
  `deleteMergedLine` (#1438) once the card is Done and no worktree has it checked out: in a lane that is when its slot
  moves to the next card's line, so until then it shows In use.

#### 16.10.3 Agents unbound from folders, and resuming

[note §7, #1123] Agents lose their `worktree` field (`AgentDef.worktree`, `types.ts:964`) and gain "in slot X" while
they hold a lease. **An agent keeps its slot for a whole lane or card** (OP-10, recommended yes): CLIs file
conversations by folder and Combwork refuses to resume from another folder, so work in another slot starts a fresh
conversation.

Combwork records each session's provider, folder **and lease** [answering HR2's round 1 finding 10]:
- **Resume** of a session whose lease is open resumes in its slot, as today (and after a restart: leases are kept).
- **Resume** of a session whose lease ended, while its slot is lent to other work, is refused there: "This
  conversation's slot now holds AM-14's work." The window offers to read its transcript (Sessions tab) or start fresh
  with a handover. A conversation can't be resumed in another folder (CLIs file it by path), so Combwork never tries.
- If the slot is free and still at that session's last revision, the session may resume there under a new lease for
  the same agent.
- **Resume All** resumes only sessions whose lease is open (or that have no slot); the rest are listed as "slot
  reused".
- **Reviewers have a stable home:** their sessions run in the project folder (never a slot), and they read and run
  commands in review copies by path (§16.10.5), so their conversations always resume.

**Built [#1434], the folder contract** (`shared/agentFolders.ts`, decided there only; `main/agentFolders.ts` reads what
it decides from: the project's slots and leases in `combwork.db`, #1441's migration and retired homes):

| | Where |
|---|---|
| A new conversation (`launchFolder(agent, purpose)`) | `review`: the project folder. `build`: the agent's open dispatch lease's slot, else its carried slot, else the project folder. Before #1441 has migrated a project, an agent with a 0.9 worktree keeps working there. Reviewer-role agents never start in a slot. A start's purpose is its role's (builder and either: `build`) unless its caller says. |
| A conversation (`resumeFolder(session)`) | Always the folder it recorded (an older row without one: the project folder). Never moved. |
| Where the agent works now (`currentFolder`) | Its running session's folder (a retired home included), else where a new conversation would start. |

Whether a conversation may resume there is its **hold** (none: it may):

| Its slot, now | `canResumeNow` (Resume All, startup) | `canResumeByUser` (its own Resume) |
|---|---|---|
| The project folder, a retired home, or no slot | yes | yes |
| Its bound lease open, the agent's | yes | yes |
| The agent's own under a later lease | no | yes: the session is rebound to that lease |
| Free, set up, clean and at the head its lease ended at (recorded once its last writer has drained), no other lease since | no ("resume by hand") | yes: a new carried lease of it for the agent, and the session rebound to it, in one write |
| Its carried slot while the agent builds a card or lane elsewhere | no ("HB2 is on AM-14 in slot-a: resume this after AM-14") | no, until that lease ends |
| Lent to other work (open, or since), or another agent's session still draining there | no ("This conversation's slot now holds AM-14's work") | no |
| Free but changed (files, revision, not set up), gone, or the agent a reviewer now | no | no |

- **What a session records:** its folder always (the project folder too), and `lease`, the lease it is **bound** to
  (`combwork.db`'s `sessions.lease`, the 1.0 group's `session leases` step, with `slot_leases.end_rev`, the slot's head once
  its ended lease's last session has drained): set when it starts in a slot. `rebindSession` changes only that column, never the folder or the
  provider's id, only to a lease of the same agent whose slot is the session's folder, and only inside the same board
  write as the lease change that needs it (the user's Resume taking a free slot; #1441's carried → dispatch handoff).
  A record's save never writes it.
- **One writer:** a session starts or resumes in a slot only through one board write (`claimPlace`) that decides again
  from `combwork.db` as it is then (the slot's lease is its agent's; the resume authority, the agent's leases included; the
  user's Resume's new lease or rebinding) and reserves the slot's **writer** for that start's run: its run id, lease,
  agent and Combwork. [#1434 round 3, the design agreed with HR2 on the card:]
  - Its run's token is among this Combwork's live ones (the pools' `holder.live`, as #1429's operations') from before its
    claim can be seen; the claim is the project's pool's tracked work, so a closing workspace's pool waits until the
    start has spawned its process or released the writer, and makes no claim once closing.
  - The claim needs the slot set up and lent, with no operation (warming, installing, removal) and no unsettled job:
    a slot still being set up is refused ("slot-b is still being set up"). No operation starts while a writer is set.
  - The writer stays through the start's preparation, the launch and the session's whole run. A start given up before
    any process of it ran releases it at once. Once a process ran (its CLI, or the agent's own worktree's first setup,
    which runs in its carried slot but never in a slot the pool set up), it is released only when its launch's process
    job shows everything it started has ended (`ended`: the job's whole membership seen empty, a member not described
    counting as one; after End, only once a later look sees the job empty, since a kill is only asked, and `unknown`
    after 30 looks): leftovers kept running by the user, a launch that couldn't be tracked, or a job that couldn't be
    read leave it **held**. A run counts as having a process only once `spawnPty` has returned one.
  - While it is set the slot isn't lent, adopted, taken by hand or removed, and another start there is refused ("slot-b
    still has another session in it, or processes one left running there"); two at once give one writer.
  - A writer whose Combwork is gone is never taken over, nor cleared from a snapshot of its processes: it is settled only
    when its run was seen ended (HI-1886, `goneWriterSettles`), else it stays held until the user releases the slot
    (#1506).
    A refresh clears this Combwork's own writer whose processes are proven ended but whose release couldn't be written.
    Combwork's quit therefore waits, after the leftovers' look that tells each stopped run's outcome, for those releases
    to be written (at most 3 s, `sessions.writersSettled`) before its workspaces close (HI-1801: a quit that closed
    them first left the slot held, and the next start there was refused). So does a workspace's own close (Close
    Workspace, a switch, or closing a window that isn't the last), for its projects' writers, after stopping its agents (at most 5 s: each waits for its run's job to be seen empty, about 2 s)
    (HI-2299: Tools' slots stayed held, their releases tried after it had closed: "No workspace is open").
  - **A gone Combwork's writer settled by itself** (HI-1886: after a restart for an install, every builder's resume was
    refused, its slot held by its own ended run, and a lane's slot stayed held after its lease had ended). The proof is the
    one a release needs: the run's job seen empty (its whole membership, what its processes started joining it). Combwork
    keeps in its profile's `leftovers.json` (`ended`) the runs it saw end, each run whose release couldn't be written
    (its workspace closed), and, as it quits, the stopped launches whose jobs it sees empty: their jobs are looked at
    until empty for at most 5 s (`recordEndedLaunches`), so a CLI slow to exit as Combwork quits for an install still
    counts, and so do the leftovers the quit has just ended (`confirming`, HI-2055: rc.11's slot-d stayed held by a run
    whose leftovers the quit ended, as nothing looked again); only from the helper that held its job as the look began, never a run lost meanwhile (a helper started in
    its place has none of the old jobs and lists any as empty: HR2's round 2). Only runs that took a slot's writer and haven't had its release written (HI-2299: every ended run of a busy day, 130, went past the bound and pushed out a closed workspace's records, kept first). Kept forward until the writer is settled, at most 100; never offered as leftovers. When a writer's Combwork is
    known to have gone (`alive` false) and its run is kept as ended, it is cleared and drained. A list of the run's
    processes taken earlier (the last run's marker, a crash's) never settles it, even with none of them still running:
    what they started after it isn't in it (HR2's round 1). Nothing kept, a job not seen empty by the quit's end, or
    its Combwork still running or unknown: held, as before; Release Slot… lists what it knows still runs, including what
    the run left running kept from before this start (#614's `restored:<run>`). Settled as a start claims the slot (`claimPlace`), at each
    pool's refresh (a lend), as a pool is made, and at the hourly tidy; a slot freed so tells the lanes waiting for one.
    The Version Control tab's Worktrees list marks a held slot too (*Held by B1's ended session*, **Release…**).
  - **The keeper** (HI-2055: after rc.10's install six slots stayed held, though every process their runs had left
    ended seconds later). The helper holding the launches' jobs is the only one that can tell a job complete (its whole
    membership: what its processes start joins it, and what escapes is adopted or followed by its sweeps), so it
    outlives its Combwork: when its input ends (a quit, a crash), the merge queue's jobs close at once as before (ending
    what is in them), and while an agent launch's job it holds still has a process it stays, hidden, sweeping as before,
    and writes that job's state to the profile's `keeper\keeper-<run>.json`: `live` with its members (id, start time and
    name, never a command line) while it has any, `ended` once it sees it empty (a job it can't read is looked at again,
    never taken for empty, and its membership is taken only after a sweep that was sure of everything: a failed
    snapshot, an enumeration of it that stops part way, a failed listing, or an escaped child whose checks Windows
    refused, could hide a process; and what ties an escaped child to its job is kept until such a sweep: an exited
    process's identity and a followed one's are let go only after one, a followed one whose state can't be read never,
    and past 4096 exits kept the jobs concerned can no longer be told complete), then lets it go; it exits once it holds none, and says `keeping` first, so a quit doesn't
    wait for it. It ends nothing. A quit whose agents kept nothing running leaves none behind.
    - It is started through a launcher, a small PowerShell of its own (HI-2314): Node puts each process Combwork starts in
      one job that ends them all once Combwork ends (a quit or a crash), and lets their own children leave it, so a helper
      started directly died with its Combwork and kept nothing. The launcher ends with Combwork, the helper it starts stays. It
      hands the helper only its pipes to Combwork (a handle list), never what Electron itself could hand down (its own
      standard handles, such as a test's pipes to it, which a helper outliving Combwork would hold open). It waits for the
      helper and exits with its code. A helper Combwork must end (stuck, or not ready as Combwork quits) is ended by its
      launcher, told on a control pipe of its own (Node's fourth, never handed on), through the handle it holds, never
      by an id (#603); that pipe's end (Combwork gone) ends nothing. Not Node's `detached`: PowerShell 5.1 started
      without a console runs nothing.
    - Each tracked run is bound to its helper (`leftovers.json`'s `helpers`, "pid:created") as it is given its job.
      Bindings are kept by need, never by age (HI-2303: kept to the newest 100, a busy day's launches pushed out the
      binding of a run still holding a slot's writer, so its keeper's `ended` freed nothing): each stays until settled,
      that is its writer released or cleared (its own release, Release Slot…, a refresh, or settled at a start), its run
      known to have taken no writer (its outcome known), its helper revoked, or, at a start, an earlier Combwork's helper gone
      with no state written for the run (only that helper writes one, before it exits). What stays is bounded by the
      running launches and the held slots; past 100 it is logged, and none is ever cut.
      A gone Combwork's writer is settled by a state only when it is whole and its own: the run's file, at most 64 KB,
      version 1, its run, its Combwork (the writer's "pid:started"), the helper its run is bound to and not revoked,
      `observed: complete`, and `ended` with no member and total 0 (`keeperState`). The clear checks that binding again
      inside its write, and the state is removed only once the writer is cleared. Logged: *slot-d … settled: HB5's ended
      run left nothing running*.
    - A helper lost while Combwork runs is revoked (`revoked`) at once, its bindings going with it (so the bounded list
      never gives one back), and the revocation is written before its replacement is given a launch, however late the
      loss (before the launch, while its helper is made ready, or while its job is made): a launch can't be tracked
      while it can't be (the tracker notice says so). A run is bound only to the helper configured as its keeper that
      made its job, with no loss between.
    - What settled a writer is that attempt's own (its run and helper), carried to its clear's guard: another check of
      the same run never changes it.
    - `live`: held; Release Slot… lists its members still running, each checked again by id and start time (one that
      can't be is never listed as running). A keeper ended before its jobs empty (killed, a logoff) leaves `live` or
      nothing, and no state, a run from before this change or bound to no helper, leaves the writer held, as before.
      States older than 7 days are removed at the start.
    - This replaces recording each process as it starts (the card's first idea): a record can't hold what a process
      started after it through one that has since exited; the job's own holder sees it.
  - **Windows' own brokers don't hold a slot** (HI-2304: MB1's connection switch never resumed, its slot held by
    `WindowsSandboxServer.exe`, which the windows-sandbox server's Sandbox had started and which outlived it).
    **One rule, in one place** (HI-2309, Darren's decision): `agentProcesses.nothingHolds(processes)`, true when nothing
    is left, or when every process left is a known system broker (`systemBrokers.ts`) with none of what it serves
    running on the whole machine. Every path that decides from what Combwork sees now whether a run's processes have ended
    uses it:
    - the CLI's exit and each 10 s look at the leftovers (the run settles `ended`, so its writer is released);
    - restored leftovers (#614): not listed at the start, and dropped by a later look;
    - the quit's record (`recordEndedLaunches`, HI-1886), which now also looks once at launches whose leftovers are
      listed;
    - a gone Combwork's keeper, only by its answer now (HI-2313). Its `live` receipt is a snapshot, never proof, since a
      writer may have joined after it while a later sweep or write of its failed (HI-2309, HR1's rounds 1 and 2). So the
      next Combwork asks the keeper itself:
      - The keeper, once its Combwork is gone, serves a named pipe, `\\.\pipe\combwork-keeper-<pid>-<created>`, named after
        its identity, which the run's binding names. Only this user's processes can open it, never a remote client, and
        only as its first instance (one taken already, it serves nothing).
      - It takes one client at a time, each asking one line, `observe <run>`, and reading its answer within 2 s, then
        let go.
      - Its answer is observed for the asking, by the same observation its states use (`Look`): a sweep sure of
        everything and the job's membership read whole. That gives `now` with `observed: complete` and its members
        (none: empty now), or `unsure` (a sweep or read that wasn't sure, or its ancestry let go unsure), or `unknown`
        for a job it doesn't hold. Nothing a client sends ends or changes anything.
      - `keeperObservation` asks the helper the run is bound to (unrevoked), within 5 s, and takes the answer only when
        it is whole and its own: version 1, its run, that helper, the writer's Combwork, `now`, `complete`, every member by
        id, start time and name, its total no less than those described (console hosts counted, not listed).
      - Then the rule decides on that answer alone (`nothingHolds`: nothing, or only idle brokers, each still running as
        the same process). Settled, the clear checks the binding again inside its write, as for `ended`.
      - No answer, any doubt, an extra or undescribed member: held. Then, when the processes its receipt lists that
        still run are only idle brokers by the rule, the user is told once (a notice naming them, *slot-a is held by
        WindowsSandboxServer*: no Sandbox is running, so releasing it is safe, with **Release Slot…**). Release Slot…'s
        question says the same (`HeldWriter.idleBrokers`) and leaves "End these processes first" off. A receipt that
        describes only some of its members (its total above them) is never called safe (`KeeperState.more`, HR1's
        round 3).
      - The keeper's own `ended` is unchanged. Members are named without `.exe` (`ProcessName`), so the broker's name
        filter takes either form.
    The broker is never ended, and a job it is the last of is let go. The decision (a known list plus a confirmed
    "nothing it serves is running"):
    - A broker is known only by its executable's full path, asked of the helper by id and start time (`paths`:
      `QueryFullProcessImageNameW`), directly in its package's folder in `%ProgramFiles%\WindowsApps`. Only Windows
      writes there, so an agent can't put a look-alike there. Its file name only rules others out, before anything is
      asked.
    - It counts as the agent's while any of its `active` processes runs, because a Sandbox's mapped folders, which can
      be in the slot, can be written from inside it. The Sandbox's are `WindowsSandbox.exe`, `WindowsSandboxClient.exe`,
      `WindowsSandboxRemoteSession.exe` and `vmmemWindowsSandbox`, checked from one whole process snapshot (the
      helper's `running`).
    - It fails closed: no start time, a process gone or whose path can't be read, a path elsewhere, another process
      beside it, a member not described, or a snapshot not read whole, and the slot stays held as before.
    - Not a check of working folders or open handles: reading another process's handles needs rights that are often
      refused, and a Sandbox's writes come through Hyper-V's share, not through the broker's handles.
    - The list is code, not an Advanced setting, so a typo can't make a writer not one.
  - **A held slot is waited on, not retried** (HI-2304: the lane resumed MB1 every ~20 s, each try spending 15 s and a
    cancelled delivery).
    - A placement whose builder isn't running first asks what holds its slot (`slotHeldWords`: a run of this Combwork's,
      its session there or the processes it left, named). Held, it starts nothing and makes no delivery. It tells the
      card and its builder once (`resumeHeld`, "slot-a is held by WindowsSandboxServer, left running by MB1's last
      run"), and records the wait on the agent (`agentStarts.startWaits`). The card then stalls with *B1 waits to
      start: …* on the board and in lane watches, and the pane's status says *Waiting for its slot*.
    - It looks again when a slot of the project is freed, when leftovers change, or when its builder's status changes,
      and otherwise after 5 min.
    - A connection switch whose resume is refused for a busy slot (`busySlot`) waits the same way. It looks first at
      what holds the slot, cheaply, so a look while the slot is still held starts nothing. It looks again at each
      change and at each slot freed, tells the user once in a notice (*MB1's switch of connection waits for slot-a*),
      and resumes once the slot is free. It gives up after a day.
  - **Release Slot…** (#1506, the user's recovery, `agentFolders.ts` `heldWriter`/`releaseHeldWriter`): a writer is
    *held* when its run isn't live in this Combwork (its token ended: the session over and its leftovers kept, untracked
    or unreadable) and its Combwork is this one or one known to have gone (`writerHeld`). The agent's ⋯ offers Release
    Slot… for it (`AgentInfo.heldSlot`, before a carried slot's own Release Slot…, which waits while both name the same
    slot), and the Version Control tab's slot list marks the slot *Held by B1's ended session* with **Release…**. The
    question names the slot, the agent, its Combwork (this one, or the process that is gone), and what Combwork lists of the
    run's processes (with **End these processes first**, on by default) or that it doesn't know which still run: the
    run's leftovers, or, its Combwork gone and nothing listed for the run, that run's own launch in the last run's marker
    (`running.json`'s `runId`, the agent and project too: another launch, or a marker from before launches named their
    run, is never taken for it) whose processes still run (`lastUnexpectedClose`, `stillRunningOf`). The question
    names the run and its Combwork's process and state (this Combwork, running; or gone). Once
    confirmed, the listed processes are ended first if asked (that run's leftovers only, or those exactly, by id and
    start time; an end Windows refuses releases nothing), then the writer is cleared in a write
    fenced by its run, and drained (the ended lease's last revision, the slot looked at). Refused, in the dialog,
    while its run is live here (stop the agent, or End or Keep Running its leftovers, which release it themselves),
    while another Combwork holding it still runs or can't be told, and when the writer is no longer that run (a claim or
    another release meanwhile: one outcome).
  - **Release Slot for the Agent API and the Assistant** (#1561, `slotRelease.ts`, Darren's decision on #1506 that it
    follows the window's): `GET /v1/projects/{name}/slots/releasable` lists the project's carried slots and held writers
    (those the window offers Release for: the run over here, or its Combwork gone), each writer with its run, its Combwork and
    what Combwork lists of its processes; `POST /v1/projects/{name}/slots/{slot}/release` releases one by slot name (`kind`
    `carried` or `writer`, left out when the slot has only one). A carried slot goes through `releaseCarried`. A held
    writer needs `confirm` naming the slot and the run the user agreed to (the window's question, as data; `400`
    without it), `end` ends the listed processes first, and `releaseHeldWriter` refuses as in the window (live here,
    another Combwork still running or not known, the writer no longer that run: one outcome when racing a claim or another
    release). Releasing is the user's and the Assistant's within Control agents (`assistantChange`, kind
    `release-slot`, not undoable: `UNDO_FINAL.slotReleased`); a project agent and a script are refused (`403`). The
    Assistant's `cw_release_slot` (`list`, `release`) tells it to get the user's agreement before a writer's release;
    the scenario `assistant-release-slot` has it release a slot whose Combwork crashed once the user agrees.
- **Its environment:** `CW_SLOT` and `CW_SLOT_PORT_BASE` (#1429's `slotEnv`) while it runs in a slot; like every
  `CW_*`, never inherited.
- **Refused, with offers:** the window says why and offers **Read Transcript** (the Sessions tab, on it) and **Start
  Fresh with a Handover** (Hand Over to… for its agent; the new conversation starts where the agent works now).
- **Resume All and startup** use `canResumeNow` only: the rest are left and listed after them ("B1 — resume by hand",
  "slot reused", "after AM-14"), so a free slot stays for new work.
- **A lease's end** (#1429's `release`): the slot's writer under that lease drains. Combwork lets its turn finish (not in a
  turn, no prompt waiting, no run or background task going), then stops that run (a start of it still being prepared
  gives up); never another run of the agent's, in that slot under a new lease or elsewhere. Once the run's processes
  are known to have ended and its writer is released, the lease's last revision is recorded (its final commit
  included) and the slot looked at.
  A run of another Combwork is that Combwork's to stop; the slot stays its until it exits. No off switch: one writer needs it
  (with workflow rules off, leases aren't ended by rules, so nothing is stopped).
- **A lane's end lets its builder finish** (HI-1706, Darren 26 Oct: "Who the heck wants cut off like that."; design
  HI-1706/s10, agreed with HR1). A lane's lease ending (`laneEnded`, `laneAbandoned`) never cuts its builder off
  mid-turn, and ends it cleanly (`slotsApp.ts`'s `laneEnd`). Other lease ends, Stop and restarts are as above.
  - **Told first:** a note for that run alone (a `control` delivery, `source: 'lane-end'`, `ref` the lease id,
    `forRun` the writer's run, its conversation): *Lane X is finished: HI-1 merged at <sha>; HI-2 not merged. Your
    session ends once this turn does; Combwork resumes it for your next lane…* (*was abandoned* for an abandoned lane), at
    most 20 cards named and 2,000 characters. It is made once per lease end, whatever became of one made before. None
    is made for an agent without an inbox.
  - **Its turn over, as states say, no settle time** (`laneEndWaitsFor`): not in a turn as its status or its hooks say
    (a Stop the inbox drain carried on keeps the turn ledger's turn running), no line of Combwork's or the user's waiting to
    be taken, no Progress run or background task, and nothing still to reach that run (queued, offered or uncertain,
    given by the gate yet or not: the note among them until it is read), all read at one moment with nothing awaited
    (`laneEndHeldNow`), and asked again by the quit at each key and before Enter (HR1's round 1). Looked at again at
    each status, Progress and saved delivery change (`onDeliveriesChanged`, after the save) and every 5 s.
  - **Ended by the CLI's own exit** (`sessions.quit`, only here): its `quitLine` typed, then Enter (Claude Code
    `/exit`, Codex `/quit`, recorded exiting by themselves with code 0 on 2.1.310 and 0.164.0:
    `tests/fixtures/advanced/exit-*.json`, and the real-tier suite `cliquit`), Copilot its Ctrl+C keys; killed only
    if that run still runs after the exit grace. Never typed while the user types, over their draft, over a line of
    Combwork's not taken, or while Combwork types; any input of the user's or prompt its CLI takes once it has begun (whatever
    the typing pause), or its turn found open again, stops it before the next key and before Enter, what it typed
    cleared again unless the user typed since, and it is tried again later.
  - **Fenced** to that run, that lease and the workspace's lifetime, checked at each look, after each await and before
    each key and the kill: a restart, a closed workspace, a newer run or the slot's writer changing ends the wait with
    nothing typed or killed, and retires the note if unread.
  - **Bounded:** at `cw.lanes.endWaitMinutes` (10) after the lease's end, set once and never moved, it is ended
    whatever it waits for: its exit command once its input is free, killed instead where its prompt can't be typed
    into; logged with why. The deadline and the fence never wait for work in flight (a note being made, the states
    being read): each change, recheck and the deadline's own timer checks them first, and what a look still awaits
    then acts on nothing (a note made late is retired); a quit already typing is waited for, never a second one beside
    it. The slot stays the writer's until the run exits, as above.
  - **Its next lane or card takes that slot over** (HI-1762: HB5's next lane, started in the turn its lane's end waited
    for, found no slot free, its own run holding the only idle one): a start for the agent whose own run still writes
    in a slot with no open lease takes it over in one write (`SlotStore.takeWrittenSlot`, checked in that write: no open
    lease, operation or job, lent, its writer that agent's run and this Combwork's, no other lease of the agent's): the lease
    begins on it, the writer moves to it and the run's conversations are rebound to it. The old lease's end then no
    longer owns the run (the fence above, and a card's plain end, which looks at the writer at the idle moment): it
    ends nothing. The slot moves to the new line as any lent slot does, once its builder is quiet. One agent, one slot:
    that slot busy just then (an operation or job, not ready, its run held by another Combwork, or changed while taken)
    makes the start wait, looked at once more, never lent a second slot; the window's dry start says the same, asking
    the takeover's own conditions without writing (HI-1787). The same rule as a carried slot's
    takeover (§16.10.8).
  - **Off switch:** Settings → Advanced → **Lanes: let the builder finish when its lane ends** (`cw.lanes.gentleEnd`):
    off, it is stopped at its first idle moment, as before. A reviewer holds no lease, so a lane's end never stops it:
    it goes idle.
- **The Agent API:** an agent's row and detail give its running session's `folder` (when not the project folder) and
  `slot`, and a session's usage its `folder` and `slot`.

**Built [#1438], cards on slots** (`src/main/slotCards.ts`; the runtime's start in `gitPlatform.start`):
- **Start:** under G11 = slots, with the rules enforced, a card's start asks `leaseForStart(card, builder)`, the one
  function that chooses its lease: a lane's card, the lane's dispatch lease (lent if the lane has none yet, kept for the
  whole lane, OP-10); any other card, its own `card` lease. Only a builder or either agent gets one (#1430's roles); a
  reviewer's start, or the rules off, starts where the agent is, as P3. None free (or a slot being set up):
  `start.slotAvailable` refuses, *waiting for a slot* (the lend's reason in English for agents). A user's start across
  it works where the agent is. A lease lent for a start that isn't written (refused, undone) is given back; a window
  Start that only asks lends nothing. `Started` records the slot and lease; the start's reply tells an agent where it
  continues and to end its turn.
- **A no-code card takes no slot** [HI-2335; Darren, 2 Nov: "we were able to create agents that worked in the project
  folder rather than a worktree before"]: it changes nothing, so its start never asks `leaseForStart` and
  `start.slotAvailable` never holds it. It starts as with no slot here: `Started.folder` is `project`, which for it means
  *no folder of its own*: its agent stays where it runs (the project folder, or a lane's kept slot), and no line is made
  or prepared. Its lane's dispatch lease isn't taken or ended by it (a lane's lease ends with the lane), and putting it
  back has no lease to give back. Code cards are unchanged. Solo (F = project) and no version control never lend, so
  they start as before. **Not covered:** a no-code card made code while Active (the user's or the Assistant's override,
  §16.7.3) keeps its project-folder start until it is put back and started again, which lends it a slot.
- **A lane of only no-code cards takes no slot** [HI-2338; Darren, 2 Nov, "as recommended"]: a lane whose cards still to
  do (not Done, not archived) are all no-code (`openCardsNoCode`, one board read, no await) is lent nothing as it starts,
  from the window (`startLaneFromWindow`) or recorded by the Assistant or a script (`launchRecordedLane`): it records no
  `slotWait`, and its agents start where they are (the project folder by default; the brief says so). A lane already
  waiting for a slot whose cards are all no-code by now is started the same way by slotCards' waiting-lanes pass, its
  wait cleared, nothing lent, even behind a code lane waiting before it: once no slot can be lent, the pass lends no
  later lane one but still starts those that need none [HR1's round 1]. A code card coming up later in it (added, or made code) is lent the lane's slot as it
  starts (`leaseForStart`), as a lane an agent registers is at its first card: none free, that start waits
  (`start.slotAvailable`). A board with no kinds (waiting for its 1.0 upgrade) lends as before. Solo and no version
  control are unchanged.
- **The line** is `cw/<KEY>/<card key>-<slug>` (slug: the title folded to ASCII, lower case letters, digits and
  hyphens, at most 40), from the target's head (HI-2593: every branch and ref Combwork names starts with `cw/`; a
  line named `hive/…` from before 1.1 is still the line its card recorded, but the clean-up of Done cards' branches
  passes it by); a line the card already has (started again after being put back) is
  checked out as it is, its base where it left the target. The spike's `.combwork/slots` folders are its unit tests' only.
- **What a start owes is decided from durable state** [HR1's round 1]: the card's facts and the slots' lease rows, read by
  one pass per project (`settleSlotCards`), never by an action's run. `prepareSlot` and `releaseSlot` only ask for it; it
  also runs as a workspace opens (after a crash: what was owed is done then), when lanes change, when a slot's writer
  drains, when the rules are switched, and hourly. Per card cycle (its last `Started`): `SlotPrepared` → `PlacementClaimed`
  → `BuilderPlaced`; the lease row's end; `LineDeleted` after Done.
  - **Prepare:** once the lease's builder is quiet (not in a turn, nothing typed or queued, no Progress run or background
    task; an idle CLI may stay open), `SlotPool.prepare` as #1429's warming operation on the lent slot (fenced by its token,
    taken over once its holder is gone; only with no writer but the lease's own), under the folder's fence (#646: nothing
    typed into or started there meanwhile) and, for the switch, the repository's lock. The builder's quiet, the cycle and
    the rules are checked again at the boundary, inside the lock after any wait for it, before the files change (and
    again before an install). A slot already on its line is prepared as it is. With
    **G15** on it installs again when the lock files differ from its last install (a run of "Combwork (slot slot-b)"); off,
    nothing is installed (a lend never reinstalls for a card). Then `SlotPrepared`, in a write that finds the cycle the
    same.
  - **Place:** once quiet again, claimed in a write (`PlacementClaimed`: another Combwork's left to it unless its process is
    gone), the card given to the builder there: typed in where it already runs in the slot, else a new conversation
    started there (`launchWith`; the old one kept). Its delivery's identity is the cycle and lease (`slot-placement`): one
    made before a crash counts only while it was given or is still on its way under the deliveries' own policy (queued,
    offered, uncertain: never made again; its agent not running is started where it is offered), and one that ended
    without being given (cancelled, refused, expired, stale), or a launch that couldn't start, is made again by a later
    pass [HR1's round 2]; then `BuilderPlaced`. A window Start hands its prompt (note, Read first)
    to that instead of typing it where the agent is.
    **A lane's brief** (HI-1795: `cw_lane start`'s `brief`, kept with the lane, `brief: { text, rev, out }` in its
    row's `extra`): every placement of one of the lane's cards, in every mode (typed, resumed, started, a new
    conversation), carries the brief as it is when its delivery is made, after the card's own prompt (the window's or
    offered one kept whole), in that one delivery; fixed once made, so a retry or a restart that finds it gives what it
    carried, and an edit applies to the next placement made. Nothing records which conversation saw it. A start without
    `brief` keeps the lane's (a list change, queued or not); the same text changes nothing; a new text or `''` (a clear)
    takes the next rev, never one used before. Outside slots (no placement) it is delivered to the builder once per rev
    (`lane-brief`, ref `<lane>:<rev>`, a `rebrief`), the lane recording the rev made (`out`) so one owed after a crash is
    made by the next look (`laneBriefs.ts`, on lanes written and as a workspace opens), never twice; a replaced or
    cleared brief's delivery not yet received is cancelled, and refreshed before it is offered, so it never arrives as the
    current one. It is never offered into the builder's conversation running as its lane began (`notIn`: the one a
    new lane's start replaces), only to its next one, or to any while it wasn't running; an edit keeps that exclusion and
    takes no other, so an edited brief reaches the lane's working conversation.
    **A start racing its lane's end** (HI-2097: a changed list sent as the lane's last card merged): with no running lane
    the start makes a new one; given no `brief`, it carries the brief and name of the builder's lane that ended (all
    merged, never abandoned) in the last 10 minutes, as a new rev 1, and its reply says so. A new lane leaves out a card
    already Done, its reply naming it; a list of only Done cards starts nothing (`409`).
    **Its builder starting a lane card itself** (HI-2092: `cw_start_card` rather than ending its turn for Combwork's start,
    as Codex did): where no placement follows (outside slots), the start's reply ends with what Combwork's start would have
    given it, "Use the card-loop skill as this lane's builder." and the lane's brief as it is now, so the lane's
    instructions reach it either way; a start in a slot gets both with its placement.
    **Its builder stopped** (HI-1746: Combwork quit between the card's start and its placement), the placement resumes the
    builder's newest conversation of its provider bound to the card's lease (a handover or a takeover binds it there),
    the card's prompt that launch's own line (`BuilderPlaced` `how: 'resumed'`); a new conversation only when there is
    no such record or its transcript is gone. It never starts the builder meanwhile: while this run's restart resume will
    bring it back (queued, starting, or pending to resume by itself) it waits, woken as that resume settles, then types
    the card in (a failed or cancelled resume leaves it to resume the conversation itself); while that conversation is
    held (its slot's hold), or its resume refused for now (the slot's last run's processes not known ended, a setup under
    way: a conflict, never a counted try), it waits, the card told once, never an older or a new conversation instead,
    looking again at its builder's status, a run, its restart resume or a slot freed (else every 30 s); after three failed
    resumes it stops, the card told, and types the card in once its builder runs there (the user's Resume, a start by
    hand; a Combwork started again tries again). A start of the builder by another wins over its own: the restart queue
    counts a start under way as running (skipped, never failed), the window's Resume All counts the same conversation
    live, or a start of it under way once it has started, as resumed (its failure or cancellation is Resume All's; a
    different conversation is refused as before), and the placement's refused launch gives its delivery to nobody, so the
    next try types the card in: one launch, the card's prompt once.
  - **Release:** a card's own lease its current cycle doesn't use (Todo, Done, or a later start's), ended in the write
    that reads the card, so a release can never end a later start's lease; a lease lent for a start not written yet is
    left two minutes. A lane's when the lane has ended or been abandoned. Releases run with the rules off too.
  - **Merged lines:** a Done card's line, by the card (never a number read from the line's name), once its target
    contains it (§16.3.2's containment, squash by its key), under the repository's lock: the worktrees read, the intent
    recorded (`LineDeleting`, with the head checked), the ref removed at that head (`update-ref -d`), then settled from
    what is on disk: a checkout of it that came in has the branch put back at that head and checked (`LineDeleteUndone`),
    none has `LineDeleted`. A deletion cut short by a crash is settled the same way by the next pass, first and whatever
    the switches say (they gate new deletions only), found from the project's facts whatever the card has done since or
    how long ago it began [HR1's round 3]; a branch that can't be put back leaves the intent for the next pass, never claimed kept [HR1's round 2].
    A lane's previous line goes once the next card's line is out.
    Off switch: Settings → Advanced **Delete a card's branch once it's merged** (`cw.slots.deleteMergedLines`, on).
- **The pool's size** is the project's builders and either agents (`setBuilderCount`).
- **Lanes:** Start Lane lends the lane its slot before starting its agents, and the brief names it ("works in slot-b, a
  new branch per card"); none free, the lane is recorded with its wait (`slotWait`, kept with the lane, so through a
  restart), shows *waiting for a slot* (`LaneWaitReason` `slot`, pausing) and is lent one by the pass once one is free,
  its agents (the lane's builder and reviewer then, re-read) started once (their brief's delivery identity is the lane
  and role) and its wait cleared. A lane ended or abandoned while it waits is never started. `cw_lane` names the
  lane's slot.
  **A free slot held** (HI-2466): a lend passes over a free slot with a session in it, or one a process holds (a file or
  folder in it open, so the pool can't rename it: often the last builder's processes still closing after its session
  ended). With no other to lend, the refusal is `busy`, naming the slot and what holds it (`held`: `session` or
  `process`), never "every slot in use". A waiting lane so refused keeps that for its status (*waiting for slot-a:
  B1's session is still in it*, *…: a process still has a file or folder in it open*) and its project's pass looks
  again after a pause (1 s, doubling, at most 30 s) and at once when a session there ends or goes idle, until the lane
  is lent one or no slot is held: a process ending tells Combwork nothing. While the slot is still held and is the only
  one it could have, the look writes no lease. Its cached holder and retry belong to the workspace's current lifetime:
  closing the workspace or removing the project forgets them, without clearing another live workspace's holds;
  stopping the slot-card service clears all of its held-slot status and retries (HI-2469). Reopening looks afresh.
  **Windows Sandbox's broker in a held slot** (HI-2467): Windows refuses to rename a folder that is a process's current
  folder, and Windows Sandbox's broker (`WindowsSandboxServer.exe`) keeps the folder it was started in as its own long
  after the Sandbox and the session that started it have ended: a Sandbox started through the windows-sandbox MCP
  server from an agent in a slot so holds the slot (the server starts `wsb.exe` in the agent's folder; its fix is the
  mcp project's MC-1484). When a held slot's rename fails, Combwork looks at each process running a known broker's
  executable (systemBrokers.ts), through its process helper (never on main's thread): its executable's path and its
  current folder, read from its PEB (x64 only; anything else, or an inconsistent read, is unread). One counts only when,
  in that one look, its path is the broker's in WindowsApps and its current folder is the slot or inside it; it is then
  named (`held`: `broker`, with its process name and whether one of the Sandbox's own processes runs: idle, a Sandbox
  running, or unknown), else the slot is held by a `process` as before. Each retry looks again, so what is said follows
  the broker starting, stopping or ending. It only names what holds the slot: whether the slot can be lent is still the
  rename alone, and Combwork ends nothing (HI-2309).
  **A refused start, its slot held** (HI-2468): a lane recorded over a builder that is still running isn't waiting for
  a slot. Combwork's own start gives it its first card (`laneStarts.ts`), and that start can be refused for its slot
  (`start.slotAvailable`). The start's wait (`startWait`, `why: "refused"`) then names the slot and what holds it
  (`startSlotHold` in `slotCards.ts`):
  - its lend passed over a free slot as held (`busy`): what the lend found, which the lend keeps for that lane: a
    session in it, a process, or the broker;
  - no slot free, as the builder's own last run still holds one as its writer (the usual case for a builder stopped
    after starting something that outlives it): what that run left running there, named from the slot's writer
    (`heldWriter`: *B1's last run left node running in it*), or that the run isn't known to have ended.

  For example: *HI-12 waits to start: its start was refused for now, slot-a still in use (B1's last run left node
  running in it); Combwork tries again*. The status keeps its builder as `agent` and puts the holder's agent in `heldBy`.
  Between tries (every 30 s, as before) each look checks the slot again (a session, the rename, the broker, the
  writer), so the status follows what holds it. Once nothing can be told, it says only that the start was refused, as
  does a start refused for any other rule. The retry and the start's own rules are unchanged.
- **The stand-in** (an agent's 0.9 worktree as the card's folder, `existing: true`, the line updater) acts only for an
  agent whose `legacyWorktree` is still its folder: until #1441 migrates the project (then its carried lease).
- **Off switches:** G11 another value: nothing of this. `cw.workflow.enforce` off: nothing is lent, refused,
  prepared, placed or deleted, and a waiting lane stays waiting (each step checks it again after its waits); leases still
  end (data safety).

**Built [#1451], the Agent API and main's readers** (the window's are #1442's; `AgentDef.worktree` leaves the type with
#1452):
- **No agent is pinned to a worktree.** Adding an agent (the Agent API, the IPC, a template) adds it with its workflow
  role and no worktree: `location` other than `project`, `worktreePath`, `branch` and `base` are refused
  (*Agents aren't pinned to worktrees in 1.0: slots are lent per card or lane.*, `400`), never ignored; so are the Agent
  API's `worktree`, `existingWorktree`, `branch` and `base`, and a card's start on a new agent with `worktree: true`. Combwork's
  making, reusing (#456) and bringing up of an agent's worktree are gone; a 0.9 agent's worktree is still removed,
  checked and merged as before, read through `legacyWorktree`.
- **Where an agent is** (`agentPlaces` in `shared/agentFolders.ts`, `agentPlace` in main): where it is now (`currentFolder`:
  its running session's folder, else where a new conversation would start) and where its next new conversation starts

  with why (`session`, `lease`, `carried`, `project`), and `branch`, the line of the slot it is in (the card last
  started under its open lease; a carried slot's or 0.9 worktree's own branch).
- **The Agent API:** `cw_project_status`'s agents give `folder`, `slot` and `branch` in place of `worktree`; the agent's

  reply says where the agent is. A project agent's own doc reads (`cw_read_section`, `cw_doc_outline`) read the

- **Main's readers:** the Git view's agents in the project folder (`folderAgents`) are those whose current folder it

- **Tests:** suites that need a 0.9 agent with its worktree make it as an upgraded project has one (test copies'

**Built [#1442], the window** (`AgentInfo.place` from `shownPlace` in `shared/agentFolders.ts`, made in `sessions.liveInfo`
over #1451's `agentPlace`; the window's helpers in `renderer/src/agentPlace.ts`):

- **Shown:** "in slot-b" beside the agent's name on its pane's header (a link to Version Control → Branches & remotes),

**Built [#1452], the type's removal:** `AgentDef` no longer has `worktree` or `needsSetup`, and `AgentWorktree` is gone
