  notice after the upgrade lists the keys.
- **Keys only, rc.3** [HI-1661; Darren, 26 Oct: "We should reference cards only by key"]: the key and the workspace
  number had drifted apart (HI-1660 is `#1662`), so a number quoted found another card. Every text that names a card
  names it by its key alone, never "HI-1230 (#1240)": the Combwork tools' replies, wakes, the inbox, lane rebriefs, task
  prompts, review-copy notices, refusals, errors, history lines, the Assistant's activity and start view, notifications
  and the window. One formatter (`nameWithKey`/`cardName`/`cardRef`, `shared/projectKeys.ts`) holds the rule; main names
  cards by key in its window's work too, not only in agents' requests. `#N` is left only for a card with no key (a
  workspace card, a project with no key yet) and for another project's card in a confined agent's text (as before).
  History lines stored before keep the `#N` they were written with. The tools' descriptions ask for the key; the tools
  that take `number` still take a bare number as the old number, silently; the intents still refuse an agent's plain
  number, their hint naming only the key. The skills, the agents' contract ("each named by its key") and AGENTS.md say
  to name cards by key.
- **The window, built in P3** [#1221]: one label everywhere a card is named (`cardLabel`: its key, `#12` for a card with
  none), on the board, the card dialog, card chips, agent panes, the Assistant, lane segments, the Progress panel,
  Performance, stall reasons and notifications; history lines and main's errors keep `#N` (agents read them, until P8).
  New Project… has a key box, suggested from the name until the user types, checked as typed, left empty for the
  suggestion; Project Settings → General → Project key changes it (the old one listed as an alias). The compact
  sidebar's tiles show the key, 3–4 letters smaller. The board's search, Archive All and the command palette find `AM-12`,
  `am-12`, `AM-` (the project's cards) and old keys (`#N` as before); a key form no project has (`re-`) is searched as
  words. **Changed in rc.3** [HI-1661]: a bare number (`12`) finds the cards whose key has those digits, in every
  project (AM-12, HI-12), never the workspace number; `#12` still finds the card with that old number, and a card with
  no key by its number either way. Card references link in a card's description and comments (rendered Markdown, never in code) and in
  terminals (keys in capitals only) beside `#N`; `#N` stays the old global number. A moved card's names in the projects
  it left (`card_aliases`, read with the board) find it in links, search and Depends on/Related. A key chosen in New
  Project… is reserved until the project has it: a key change or another new project meanwhile is refused it.
- **Everywhere else the key appears** [#704]: board and palette search by `AM-`; notifications; lane rows; handover and
  plan file names; Apiary rooms. Keys compare case-insensitively in ref paths (NTFS) [HB3's round 1 finding 18].
- **Tables** [#1025]: cards with typed columns; comments, history, decisions, links, holds, and facts in their own
  tables; aliases; `store_rows` retired (sessions, lanes, watches, deliveries get typed tables); the Agent API's JSON
  kept identical or versioned; a backup first (`db.ts` backs up before migrating, `:124`). Holds in their own table
  bring the cost reads down (#1107's measurement) [#1119 c].

### 16.13 Checks and the Progress panel

**Runs become checks** [#1119 c]. A run can name its card and revision (`cw-progress --card AM-12 [--revision …]`,
`/v1/progress` fields; default from the agent's current card and, at start, that card's revision read through its
platform's adapter (Git: its folder's head on its own line, its newest attributed commit in a shared folder; None: its
declared paths' hash), or the folder's head for a run for no card or for one not started [#1233]; backwards compatible).
A finished run naming a card and revision writes `CheckRan`. The gates read the same facts the panel shows, so they
agree by construction. Its end reads the folder again before the write (the watcher settling, git), so the record can
come after cw-progress has exited: a submit waits for its project's records still being written, and a check that
passed counts the moment its run finishes [#1651].

**Reused at review** [HI-2660]. Start review's reply names the card's checks recorded at the reviewed submission's
revision (`checksAtRevision`: an earlier submission chosen with `submission` has its own revision's), for its reviewer
to reuse instead of running them again: the latest counted run of each name there (a failure after a pass says
failed), never an uncounted attempt, another revision's run, the merge queue's own (`entry`), or a configured check
whose command has changed since its run. Names are data, as `checks` are (HI-2276). Only those checks: what else the
change needs is the reviewer's to judge (review-agent-work), and a record in a summary's text is checked by the
reviewer, never read by Combwork. A focused test proved by review (G20, realProof = review) counts from the reviewer's
own run, or from another agent's run that its pass accepts (below).

**When a run counts for a revision** [P1, answering HR2's round 1 finding 5 and round 2 finding 2, HB3's F]: a green
run proves something only about content it ran on. A run records its **tested checkout** (the revision checked out
where it ran) and counts for a card's submission only if all of these hold; otherwise it is recorded with
`counted: false` and why:
- it was started as that check: `cw-progress --check <name> [--card AM-12]` runs **the project's configured command
  for that name** (the agent doesn't pass the command), so `npm run typecheck && npm run lint` or `npx vitest run`
  never has to match a string; a run without `--check` counts only if its command is exactly the configured one
  [HB3's round 1 finding 17];
- **the tested checkout contains the card's revision:** for a card with its own line, it *is* the revision; in a
  shared folder, the card's revision is an ancestor of it (other cards' later commits may be in it too, which the
  option's description says). An explicit `--revision` must equal the checkout at the start (else refused at once,
  "a3f2c1d isn't what's checked out here: b71e09a4c3d2 is"; None: the card's paths' hash, its tested checkout). As for
  `cw_submit`'s `revision`, a start of the commit's id of 7 or more hex characters names it, any case, where git finds
  only that commit for it (HI-2671: one it finds more for is refused as ambiguous, asking for more of it);
- the folder was clean when it started (§16.3.2's dirty), and is clean and at the same checkout when it ends;
- **nothing changed in between**: the watcher (§16.3.2 observe) saw no write to a tracked file in the folder and no
  HEAD reflog entry during the run (a checkout and back, a reset to the same commit, an edit undone all show), and no
  agent's edit hook fired there. A build writing ignored outputs (`out/`, `node_modules`) doesn't count against it.
  Writes anywhere in the tracked tree count, not just the card's files: its checks can depend on any of them. A write
  is the run's by the file's own times, not when its event came in (HI-1767): a check copy's reset or the target merged
  in just before the start, whose events came in after it under load, isn't (its file last written before the start,
  100 ms of clock slack aside); a link by its own and its target's, the later; a file shown gone (ENOENT, ENOTDIR) by
  its folder's; one that can't be read counts;
- **None:** `cw-progress --check <name> --card AM-12` computes the card's current revision from its declared paths
  when the run starts and when it ends (§16.3.3); the run counts for a submission whose revision is that same value
  (same paths, same contents), and the watcher saw no write to a deliverable in between. So the builder declares its
  paths, runs the check, then submits: no circle. Changing the paths, or editing one of them, after the run makes a new
  revision, and the run no longer counts [HR2's round 3 finding 1].

**Where checks run, and the remedy when a folder is busy.** Merge checks always run in the queue's own worktree, which
no one else writes in (§16.9.1). Pre-review checks run where the builder runs them (its slot, or the shared folder)
and count under the rules above. In a shared folder, another agent's edit during a run makes it uncounted, which is
the honest answer, so a refusal always offers a remedy that can be met: **`cw-progress --check <name> --isolated`**
runs the check in a **check copy**, a detached worktree at the card's revision from the same warm pool as review
copies (§16.10.5), leased to that run and written by nothing else, so it counts whatever happens in the folder. The
refusal's next step names it ("another agent changed files during your run: run it isolated"). **Said where it
happens [#1654]:** a run that didn't count keeps what stopped it (`changes`: up to 5 paths, `:reflog` or `:edit`, for
`changed` and `dirty`), the finish's answer says how it counted, and `cw-progress --check` prints one line with the
reason and the remedy. `submit.checksPassed`'s refusal names the reason of the check's newest run on the revision when
that run passed and didn't count, and its next step is that reason's remedy (commit or remove changes; run it again
with nothing else writing, or `--isolated` on Git; run it in the card's own folder). A reviewer's runs in a
review copy count for the revision it holds (§16.10.5). None has no check copies (no isolation, OP-16): its remedy is
running again when the deliverables are quiet, which the refusal says. **Named on the card [HI-2276]:** a code card's
read (`cw_read_task`, the Agent API's `checks` and `checksHint`) lists its rules' pre-review checks by name, as data,
with a fixed hint, `cw-progress --check <name> --card …` (and `--isolated` where the platform has check copies), until
it is past Review: agents that never read work-on-card ran the check in the shared folder by hand. No shell command is
built from a configured name (free text: quoting it for every shell failed review twice). The rule stays in work-on-card.
**Built [#1435]:** `--isolated` (with `--check` only, by an agent, on Git) asks resolve for a check copy. It is leased at
the card's revision apart from the request (`IsolatedRequests`: a first setup takes longer than any request may): resolve
answers within 2 s, with the copy or 409 `wait` and a ticket, and cw-progress asks again with the ticket every 2 s
for the wait's first minute, then half as long again each time up to every 10 s (HI-1831: well inside the minute a
ticket is kept unasked; resolve's wait is recorded as the `waiting` outcome, not a client error), saying what it waits for once (*waiting for a check copy*, *… to be set up*); a copy leased for a ticket nobody asks
about for a minute is given back (`abandoned`). At most 100 requests wait at once (the oldest is dropped); a request
dropped that way, or by its workspace closing, while its copy is still being set up gives that copy back once it comes,
exactly once [#1499]. The lease's job is opened on the process supervisor (`copy-<lease>`,
recorded on the lease first). cw-progress then starts the command's launcher (#1360's, `workflow/launcher.ts`) in the
copy and has Combwork put it in that job (`POST /v1/progress/isolated`) before it runs anything: only by the lease's agent,
once per lease, and only a process of that agent's own (in its launch's job, started in the window it names). The run's start takes the lease,
its finish returns it after its `CheckRan` (`isolated: true`), and **Stop** on its row in the Progress panel
(`progress:stop`) ends the job, so the whole tree ends, and the run is recorded as stopped. Any run whose folder is in a leased copy of the caller's own
project is linked to the lease's card and revision (runLink's `copyAt`), never the agent's card in Doing; naming another
card there is refused. Another project's copy is no copy to an agent: nothing of its lease is read or shown.
The run's details name the copy (`ProgressRun.copy`). A lane waiting for a copy has the status `checkCopy` (*waiting
for a check copy for HI-12*). Combwork running pre-review checks itself is OP-27.

**The queue's runs, attributed to Combwork** (§16.9.1 step 5). **Built [#1349]:** a run Combwork starts itself has
`source: 'combwork'`, is the card's project's, and shows as **Combwork (merge queue)** (`defaultName: 'mergeQueue'`, in the
window's language; no provider, no agent to show). Only Combwork updates or finishes it (a script's token gets `404`, as for
another caller's run), it never goes stale (no reporter to fall quiet: Combwork ends it itself, its time limit included), and
it is kept in the run history like other runs, with its log path (Show log) and its `counts` once the queue has
bracketed it. Its `CheckRan` is for the card at the test merge's result revision, `by: 'Combwork (merge queue)'`, counted or
not by the rules above; it never counts for a submission (its revision is the result, not the card's). `noInstall`
marks the first check after an install that had nothing to run. The window's side (the row in Runs and Pulse) is
#1356's e2e; the queue in the app is #1348's.

The Progress panel stays; its 1.0 changes per phase are on the phase cards and are part of this spec:
- **P3** [#1119 c]: run rows show "AM-12 · a3f2c1d" (links the card, copies the revision); details show Card, Revision
  and "counts as check: typecheck"; a run's default card is the agent's card in Doing only when it has exactly one (a
  run counted for the wrong card is worse than none); cw-progress resolves the card, revision and check before the
  command starts (`POST /v1/progress/resolve`), so a refusal runs nothing; `--isolated` is refused until P7's check
  copies [#1220]. **Combwork slow to answer (HI-1892):** cw-progress waits for the resolve, and for its run's start to
  be taken, as Settings → Advanced → *cw-progress: Combwork's reply time* says (`cw.progress.replySeconds`, 15 s,
  1–120 s, handed to sessions as `CW_PROGRESS_REPLY_SECONDS`; a fixed 5 s gave up on a busy Combwork's checks). A check
  needs the answer, so an ask that got none (slow, or an error) is asked once more after 1 s (never an isolated
  check's first ask, which may lend a copy) before it runs nothing, saying why: *Combwork is slow to answer: no reply … in
  N s, asked 2 times* (try again, or give it longer), or, the connection refused or not allowed, at once and asked
  once, *Combwork couldn't be reached … (connection refused at <url>)* with the hint that a sandbox blocking local network
  access (Claude Code's Bash sandbox) does the same. A check's finish that got no reply is sent once more (a `409` then
  says the first arrived), and cw-progress says when its result may not be recorded: its start never taken, no
  reply to its finish, or a finish refused; its exit code stays the command's. The lane hover gains the revision under review, the last verdict and on which
  revision, checks on it and the merge commit.
- **P4** [#1120 c]: a refused move marks the segment (a notch, red, by pattern and colour) with the one-line reason and
  next step; a stale pass is marked ("Pass was for a3f2c1d; now at b71e09a"); overrides marked with who, rule and why;
  no-code cards say so; paused lanes say why; a failed run that blocks a gate says so ("blocks review for AM-12").
  **Built [#1279]:** a running lane's segment marks come from its card's facts (none on an ended lane's, whose facts
  may be a later cycle's), each a shape of its own beside the state's colour and pattern, and each said in the
  segment's hover and accessible name: a **refused** request since the card last moved (its latest `Refused`) is a red
  notch in the segment's end corner, its hover the refusal's reason and next step in the window's language (the
  agent's English from the same messages, §16.8.3), "(refused 3 times)" when the same rule refused it in a row, cleared
  by the card's next move; a content-**stale** pass is amber dashed top and bottom edges over a paler fill, "Pass was
  for a3f2c1d; now at b71e09a" (revisions through the project's descriptor), until it is submitted again or Done; the
  latest **override** since it was last Done is a ringed dot in the start corner, its hover who, which rules by name
  and why (§16.8.4's note); a **no-code card**'s hover says so and has no revision or merge lines. A lane with a status
  (#1270) says why in its header, in the room the lane's name had (every lane keeps one height; paused in the paused colour, others faint; its whole text in its title), and in its accessible name:
  *waiting for you (approval): AM-12* (the open request's kind), *waiting: AM-11 not merged*, *waiting: AM-11
  merging*, *stale: AM-12 must be submitted again*, *waiting for a reviewer on AM-12*, *list changes after AM-12*, the
  round limit, a card blocked or On Hold; the Lanes bar counts the lanes waiting for you (an open request or the round
  limit). A finished check run for a card whose result failed and whose name is one of the card's ruleset's checks
  before review (`blocks()`, `checks.ts`) records `blocks: review` with how it counted (`RunCheck`, kept with the
  run), and its row says **Blocks review for AM-12** under the failure, for as long as the failed run shows.
- **Tabs** [#1309, Darren 21 Oct]: the panel's header has a segmented control, Pulse · Merges · Runs · Lanes, words
  that fold to icons below about 360 px (a container query on the panel), a tablist (arrow keys, Home, End), the tab
  kept per workspace. Badges: agents waiting for a merge slot, lanes, and in red the **unresolved failures** (a failed
  run with no later run of the same thing, a card's check or a command, that passed; dismissing doesn't resolve one).
  Pulse lays out top to bottom, its lanes at the bottom of the panel growing upwards (#484; HI-1673 brought it back
  after #1309 had them follow the runs, which left empty space under them), and holds no finished runs (the Assistant for Darren, 21 Oct: a run
  that ended stays a few seconds, then lives in Runs): the merge, a line for the unresolved failures (it opens Runs on
  them; above the runs and outside their scrolling list, so it stays in sight however many there are: HI-1923), the
  runs going on, then the lanes, each with a dot for its current card's latest run. Runs: what runs on top,
  scrolling in what's left; every kept run docked at the bottom (HI-1925, Darren 28 Oct: "make today fixed to the
  bottom like lanes on the pulse panel"), behind Pulse's lanes edge (one splitter, `DockEdge`: the lanes snap to whole
  lanes, this one doesn't), by day, Today first, then Yesterday and older, scrolling in its own height: about 6.5 lane
  rows by default, 1 to 10, unsnapped, kept per workspace (`progress-runs-today:<workspace>`), and on a short panel
  what fits while the runs going on keep RUNS_KEEP_PX (its height back as the panel grows; its separator's range and
  value say what shows). Today always heads it: "No runs today", "No runs match." (a filter matching only older runs),
  or the dock's one line "No finished runs" when there are none; days roll over at midnight by the panel's clock. Every
  run in the dock is its own line, only its details folded (several open at once, closed whenever Runs leaves the
  screen or the workspace changes; nothing kept). The same thing's runs on a day fold into one line ("AL-12 cardwork ×4 · 2 failed, then
  passed"), with search and filters (failures, a lane's cards, an agent). Each day is grouped by card (HI-1701, Darren
  26 Oct): a heading per card, the card with the newest run first and **Other** (runs for no card) last, with its key
  (it opens the card), title, how many runs and how they went ("7 runs · 1 failed", "all passed", " · running" while
  one runs) and when the last ended; its icon shows a failure (✗ when a run's last try failed, ⚠ when one failed before
  it passed). A card's runs always show (HI-1925: never a whole card folded). Under it a line per run: its icon, who,
  what (the card's key left out of the title), how long and when it ended; a run's retries fold as before ("B1 unit ×3 · 2 failed, then passed", the same failure-aware
  icon), and the merge queue's checks for the card into one line ("Combwork (merge queue) lint, typecheck"). The commit,
  the copy, the command go in the hover, all of it in the details. The filters filter runs within cards and hide a card
  left with none; what runs stays on top, ungrouped. Merges and Lanes show theirs alone. #1228's
  fold of Recent is gone with Recent. The word stays **Runs** (Darren); `/v1/progress` is unchanged. A run's details
  give times relative, the date and time in full on hover.
- **P5** [#1121 c]: the merge slot card becomes the queue's summary per target (testing now, queued, just merged,
  returned with Open card and Show log), Pause/Resume and Remove from queue, the queue's runs attributed to Combwork, the
  full queue view in the Version Control tab, state changes announced politely.
  **Built [#1356]** (the panel; the card's Work section and the Git tab's section are #1357's): the **Merges** tab lists
  a card per merge queue target and the merge slot's cards side by side, by project then target; the slot's keep
  **Release**, the queue's have none. A queue's card (`ProgressQueue.tsx`, its model `shared/progressQueue.ts`, which
  #1357 reuses) says, each state with its own icon and words: **testing now** (*HI-61 + main @ 1cd2592 → check:
  unit*: the card, the target's head it is tested on, the step: test merge, merge checks or the check running by its
  run's name, merging), the time so far against an **estimate**, the median of the target's last five merges' check
  times from Combwork's own runs (a merge's runs are those on its result revision, all passed; none shows no estimate);
  **queued** in order, each with its approved revision (copies) and a link to its card, and **Remove** (a confirmation,
  then #1353's intent); **just merged** (*✓ HI-61 merged as 9e1f0aa*) for 8 s; **returned** (*✗ HI-108 returned to
  HB1: conflict in tasks.ts*, *checks failed: unit*), with **Open card** and **Show log** (the failed check's run log,
  else the output the outcome kept), shown **until seen**: the Merges tab shown in a focused window, with no dialog over
  it, marks seen the returns it shows (the project filter applies; `queue:seen`, kept in `combwork.db` for every window and
  Combwork: `workflow_queue_seen`, 1.0 group step 18 `queue seen`), then each goes 10 s later. **The returns policy** (HR3's #1356 rounds
  1 to 4) is one invariant: every return not seen is reachable (shown, or counted on the card: *2 more returned
  cards*), a return shown and seen stays shown and usable for at least its 10 s whatever arrives meanwhile, and the
  read is bounded. A return is its card's newest outcome, the card not queued or testing again (left out before
  anything is filled or counted). The window's model lists at most 50 returns, apart from the latest 20 outcomes (the
  Agent API's): those seen in the last 10 s first, by seen time, holding their places, then those not seen, newest
  first, in the places left, and the exact count of the rest. Only rows shown get seen, so nothing displaces a row
  seen; the next ones come as rows fold, the window reading the queue again then by itself (an idle or paused queue
  pages on, a page at a time, each its full 10 s). Each window also keeps the rows it showed and marked seen until
  their own 10 s are up, merged with main's list (the Assistant, #1356 round 6): two windows marking different
  snapshots can leave main's bounded list without one of them, and a row main lists as seen earlier (another window
  saw it first) still shows until this window's own 10 s are up, with main's latest data (#1427); **paused**, each pause reason a sentence (git's own message under it), with **Resume
  queue**, and Open card for needs you; **run by <profile>** for another Combwork's queue; and **Queue in Version
  Control**, which opens the project's Git tab (#1357 points it at its Merge queue section). **When a queue shows**
  (item 0, round 2 of #1338) is decided from its actual state, never the current options alone: an entry testing,
  queued or paused, a return not seen (or seen in the last 10 s), a merge of the last 8 s, a lease, a pause, or a card
  in flight (started, not Done, not archived) whose own ruleset has Combwork merge into that target; and, empty (*Nothing
  queued.*), while the project's current options have Combwork merge into it (`queue:list` gives the window those targets
  too, with `combworkMerges` and `inFlight`; the Agent API's listing is unchanged). So after a switch to "The agent merges",
  or Git → None with an old Git ruleset's cards in flight, the old queue stays controllable until its cards are merged,
  out of flight, and their outcomes seen. Under **All projects** (HI-2165, Darren 30 Oct: "we shouldn't show details
  from inactive projects") a queue shows only for a project being worked on (the sidebar's Working on) or while it is
  busy (`queueBusy`: an entry testing or queued, a pause, a return not seen, or a merge in the last hour), so an
  inactive project's idle *Nothing queued.* card is left out; chosen in the filter, its queue shows as above. While a
  queue is left out the filter is offered, even with one project to choose (`activeFilter`'s `offered`). Pulse's
  queue lines, the merge cards, Runs and Lanes need no such rule: each lists only what is going on or just happened (a
  queue testing or paused, a slot taken, a run reported, a lane running or ended in the last hour). Pulse has a line per queue testing or paused (*main: testing HI-61 · 2
  queued*), which opens Merges; the Merges badge counts queued entries plus agents waiting for a slot; the project
  filter offers the projects with a queue shown. A polite live region (`role="status"`) says each change once: a card
  merged or returned (with why), a queue paused or resumed. The Runs tab's Agent filter has **Combwork (merge queue)** for
  Combwork's own runs, which fold by card and check like any run. Display only: it follows the queue's state; the controls
  are #1353's.
  **Recent merges [HI-1924]:** under each queue's card and the project's merge slots (the slot for its target, else
  under the project's first queue: what merges now first, history after), its latest outcomes (merged with the merge commit, which copies;
  returned with `returnWhy`; taken out with its reason) and pauses (why in a few words, the sentence as its tooltip; how
  long it lasted, or still paused), newest first, at most 20, then *More in Version Control* when there may be more.
  A return names the check its own outcome recorded (`IntegrationFailed.check`, carried as `QueueRecent.check`), and
  its run (Show log's, and the check's name when the outcome has none) is the one with the log that outcome recorded
  (`logPath`), never another attempt's red run found by time; the queue's card, the card's Work section and the
  Version Control history read it the same way.
  A row has the card's key and title, its time (how long ago on hover) and how long the queue took over the entry: from
  the start of its first merge check (the queue's `CheckRan` names its `entry`) to the outcome, else from its
  `IntegrationStarted` (no merge checks), else none (it ended before anything ran; old facts without `entry` count the
  queue's checks between the entry's request and outcome only when no other entry of the card was open then). With G18
  on, a Combwork merge says Pushed, Not pushed yet, Not pushed (pushing turned off, or the target no longer had it), or Push
  not recorded (none kept: an older merge), never inferred from an owed push's absence. A click opens the card; the
  panel's project and agent filters apply (an agent: its cards' rows; a pause on no card always shows); *No merges yet.*
  when empty. From the queue's model (`queue:list`, read again on each queue change; nothing new to read, nothing
  drawn while the tab is hidden): `QueueRecent.tookMs` and `push`, and `QueueView.pauses`, window-only (the Agent
  API's listing is unchanged). Recorded in `board_meta` beside the owed push, no schema step: `queue.pauseLog:<target>`
  (the newest 20, written in the pause row's own write: a pause begins a row, lifted or replaced it ends; saved again
  as it was, it carries on), `queue.pushPending:<target>` (each merge owed a push, in the `Integrated` transaction; not
  bounded, it drains) and `queue.pushLog:<target>` (settled, the newest 20). A push goes by the target's commit read
  before it, and settles the pending merges captured before it, in the write that clears the owed push: those that
  commit holds pushed, the rest reset; pushing turned off settles them off; a target without the owed merge settles
  as reset only those it no longer has (the rest stay pending for the next push); a failed push leaves them pending.
- **P6** [#1122 c]: stage names in hovers and accessible names over the categories' colours and patterns; the legend
  by stage; Solo shows no lanes section unless a loop runs; links to the Version Control tab; "old rules" marks.
  **Built [#1421]:**
  - A segment keeps its category's colour and pattern (no stage gets one of its own). Its hover and accessible name
    say the card's **stage** (`WorkBadge.stage` through `stageName`, with its project's renames from
    `workflow:stages`). Where its category shows two stages (Approved and Merging), its hover lists both with a thin
    divider and the card's own in bold. A card's category's stages are its own ruleset's (`WorkBadge.stages`, §16.5.4),
    else its lane's recorded one (`LaneInfo.stages`, for its cards in Todo), else its project's now; names are always
    the project's now (names aren't rules). So a lane under old rules keeps its stages when the options now produce

  - **The legend** is on the Lanes bar's hover and keyboard focus (Esc closes it; screen readers get it as the bar's

  - **Solo:** Pulse leaves out a project's lanes while its preset is Solo (or Custom from Solo), unless one of them

  - **The Lanes tab** (HI-1926, Darren 28 Oct): every lane, Pulse's row (`LaneRow`), stacked from the bottom and growing

    `endedAt`, the Integrated or Accepted time, and `merged`) how long it took and its merge commit (copied with a
    click) or how long so far. An ended lane shows only what happened before it ended: a cycle started or finished

  - **A lane's queued list change** (HI-2151, Darren 30 Oct: "I didn't see it on the lane"): a running lane with one

    HI-12 is Done: HI-14 added, HI-9 moves to HB6’s lane*. None when nothing is queued (it goes once it applies) or the
    queued list is the same; Pulse keeps its one-height row and its *list changes after* header. Editing it is HI-1927's.
  - **A lane's wait time** (HI-1926): main stamps each running lane's status when its key (reason, card, ask) first

    `atLeast`, shown "23 min+" with a tooltip saying so. The header shows it after the wait's text, amber past
    Settings → Advanced's bounds: for you or a round limit `cw.lanes.waitYouMinutes` (60), a reviewer

  - **Links:** a lane's header names its project, a link to its Version Control tab at Workflow. The Merges tab's

  - **Old rules** (§16.5.4): `LaneInfo.oldRules` for a running lane whose recorded ruleset (`lane_runs.ruleset`) isn't
