### 16.14 Undo for the Assistant's changes

[#1120 c, #1170] The Assistant's 30-changes-per-message cap (`MAX_ACTIONS_PER_TURN`, `assistantControl.ts:24`) goes,
with its refusals and every text that states it; `MAX_CHANGE_BATCH` (100 cards per call) stays. In its place, **undo**,
built on the fact log and the Assistant's activity list:
- **What:** card edits (labels, column, blocked, title, description, links, agent), cards it created (archived on
  undo), lane records, agent settings and Combwork settings.
- **Not:** prompts and messages sent, and work an agent did after it was started; undo can stop an agent it started.
  The panel says so.
- **Changed since:** if the user or an agent changed the same thing afterwards, undo skips it and says so; it never
  overwrites a later change.
- **Grouped** by the user's message ("Your message at 08:14: 61 changes · Undo"), with Undo per change. Kept on disk
  across restarts for **7 days** (OP-15; the card says "at least a day").
- **The Assistant can undo its own** changes with a tool limited to them, recorded in its panel; never the user's or
  agents' changes.

**Built in P4** [#1282] (main side; the panel is #1283):
- **Recorded:** every change the Assistant makes through `assistantChange()` (and its batches) is kept in `combwork.db`'s
  `assistant_changes` and `assistant_change_values` (a 1.0 group step), as it is made (`assistantChanges.ts`).
  - A card's fields are recorded as the card is saved, in the same transaction.
  - A lane is recorded in its own save's transaction (lanes.ts), from the lane as read under its lock.
  - An agent's settings are recorded from what its change saw under the project's lock. A Combwork setting is recorded by its
    route. An agent it started is recorded with the launch it started.
  - What can't be undone is recorded with why: a prompt or message, and a card's decision, comment or place.
  - Each change keeps what it replaced and what it wrote, per field, as typed rows (a list or table as a row per member,
    never JSON). It is grouped by the user's message (`assistantControl`'s turn) and pruned after 7 days.
- **Undone** (`assistantUndo.ts`) one change or a message's, newest first.
  - A field goes back only while it still holds what the change wrote, checked at the write under that thing's own lock
    (a card's, the lanes', the project's for an agent's settings, a setting's guard). One changed since is skipped and
    said, the rest still go back. A price table's removed models are a field of their own.
  - Every value a write changes, implicitly too, is checked: a card's project goes back with its agent in one transaction
    (both or neither), only while its agent and review are as the move left them. A column move back never stops a review
    started since. A provider goes back with everything a provider change resets (model, effort, permission mode, context,
    its last conversation), each as the change left it, never while the agent runs; one it inherited is inherited again.
  - What is reported is what the write saved, read inside it. A change is marked undone only when every field ended undone
    or skipped for good; one that failed stays to be tried again.
  - A card it made is archived only while its history goes no further than the change left it.
  - A column move goes back through the rules with `override: { reason: "undo" }`.
  - A lane it started is abandoned; its list, reviewer, rounds, wait and name go back through the lane record. A lane
    that ended stays ended.
  - An agent it started is stopped only while the launch the start returned still runs.
  - A template it loaded [HI-1502] is two changes of the project (kind `agent`, act `load-template`): its agents and
    layout, put back through the load's own replacement (`restoreProjectAgents`) only while they are exactly those the
    load left (ids, names, roles, pairing, connection and settings; the layout) and none runs or is starting, the old
    names checked against other projects' under the names lock (one another project has now is never renamed: the change
    fails, said, to try again), the project's starts fenced throughout; the restored agents keep their ids, so their
    conversations come back. Its workflow options go back through the Workflow form's save, only while they are those
    the load saved (`base`). The agents' cards and lanes stay as the load left them (said: `UNDO_FINAL.templateCards`).
  - Every successful change is listed: one that recorded nothing undoable gets a final row with why. An intent's facts
    (a submission, a verdict, a question) stay beside its card fields' undo, and that is said. Undo itself isn't recorded.
  - An undo's own writes aren't recorded. Each change is marked undone as soon as it is undone.
- **The user** undoes from the window (IPC `assistant:changes`, `assistant:undo`: the panel's, #1283).

**Built in P4** [#1170]: the cap is gone: no count of changes per message, no 429 for it, and no text (Settings →
Assistant's Control and Change settings tips, the batch tip, the Assistant's guidance and skills, the tool descriptions)
states it. `MAX_CHANGE_BATCH` stays.

**The panel's undo** [#1283] (`components/AssistantChanges.tsx`, `renderer/assistantUndo.ts`):
- **Done by the Assistant** lists the changes kept (`assistant:changes`, loaded with the panel and again on each of its
  actions) by the user's message: a heading each, "Your message at 08:14: 61 changes" (a date too before today), newest
  first, the newest open and the others folded (a click opens or folds one). The actions that aren't changes (a refusal,
  a failure, an undo, the user's or its own `cw_undo`'s) are listed with their message too (`AssistantAction.group`,
  the turn they were recorded in); one that changed something is listed by its changes. "Done by the Assistant (n)"
  counts the rows.
- **A row** is a change: a card's by its card ("#12 Fix the login: labels and column", "Made #12 …") with its fields
  named in the window's language; another by the Assistant's line for it while the window has it (the nearest action of
  its kind in its message), else as recorded. Each has **Undo** where Revert was (settings' Revert is this Undo: one
  control). One undone is struck through with when ("Undone 2 minutes ago") and offers no Undo; one that can't be undone
  says "Can't be undone", its why in its tooltip. Why is worded in the window's language from codes (`finalWhys` reads
  them from the English kept, `UNDO_FINAL` in `shared/assistantActivity.ts`; the IPC adds `finalWhy`).
- **Undo of a message** asks first ("Undo 61 changes? Changes made since by you or an agent are kept.", and how many
  can't be undone), runs in the dialog, then says under its heading what it did: undone n, each change kept with why
  (its fields changed since, gone, the lane ended, failed) and each that can't be undone with why. A change's own Undo
  runs at once. A failure keeps Undo offered, with why.
- **What undo did is kept with the change** (round 2: `assistant_change_outcomes`, a 1.0 group step, v13): when a change is
  marked undone, each of its fields is recorded as put back or kept (changed since, gone, the lane ended), whoever undid it
  (the window or the Assistant's `cw_undo`). The row says Undone (struck through, with when), Partly undone or Kept,
  why in its tooltip, after a reload or restart too (`AssistantChangeRow.outcome`). A change marked before outcomes were
  kept reads as undone; a failure isn't marked, so it has none.
- **The Assistant** undoes its own with `cw_undo` (`GET /v1/assistant/changes`, `POST /v1/assistant/undo`, Control
  agents, its activity kind `undo`). Its control level and launch are checked again at each write: turned down or ended
  partway through, the undo stops there. It undoes a Combwork setting only while Change settings is on.

### 16.15 Override switches for the CLIs

[#966, #1120 c, #1123 c, #1167, #1174] Every Combwork override of a CLI's own behaviour has a switch, or a recorded reason
it can't. One owner per switch; each defaults to today's behaviour; never written into the user's CLI config.

| Group / rows | What | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| A (1, 3–8) | Inherit the CLI's own permission policy (badges, resume state and Control kept honest); pre-approval of Combwork's tools (Copilot `--allow-tool=combwork`, Claude Assistant `--allowedTools`), separating availability, CLI trust and API authorization; MCP isolation per CLI (Claude `--strict-mcp-config`, Codex `.enabled=false`, Copilot `--disable-builtin-mcps`/`--disable-mcp-server`); the Assistant's non-Combwork servers; Copilot's `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` strip (displayed and running account agree) | P4 |
| B (10–14) | Claude's `--settings` merge, widened hook allowlists and the `disableAllHooks` refusal; Codex's hook replacement and trust; Claude's status line (keep or chain the user's); guidance and the Assistant's role injection (Codex `developer_instructions`). Built in #1285 (below): rows 12 and 13 have switches; rows 10, 11 and 14 have their recorded reasons, with no hooks-free mode | P4 |
| E (24, 26–30) | Ctrl+C/V passthrough; all-keys passthrough; the OSC 52 policy; prompt fidelity (Ctrl+U clearing a draft, collapsed whitespace, stripped characters); raw variants of Combwork's wrapped prompts | P4 |
| #1167 (19–23, 25, 34) | Copilot auto-update (both suppressors, every path); right-click for Claude Code and Codex; Codex terminal title omitted; `--system-prompt-snapshot off`; `--allow-all-mcp-server-instructions`; Codex `--no-daemon` (only if verified); model/effort flags (check first) | P4 |
| #1174 | Codex: the Assistant pre-approves only its Control subset of Combwork tools (parity; built in #1281, §9.3) | P4 |
| C (15, 16) | Skill delivery per slot and choice of skills (row 15 **Built [#1431]**, §16.10.7); carrying on (inbox, checkpoints, Stop continuation, idle wakes): row 16 **Built [#1432]** (below) | P7 |
| F (31–33, 35–38), probes (39–42) | No switch: they are the integration itself (reasons on #966) | — |
| 9, 17, 18 | Already switchable (file locks, background sessions, 200K): one owner, no duplicate | — |

**Group C's row 16, carrying on** (#1432; `shared/inboxSwitches.ts`): how Combwork gets an agent to read its inbox, three
booleans in Advanced under Combwork, each on by default and read at each use, with a project's own in Project Settings →
Sessions (`inboxCheckpoints`, `inboxStopContinuation`, `inboxIdleWakes` in project.json: inherit, on or off; the
Assistant's home has no project, so it follows Settings', which its Control tip says). Whether an agent can read an
inbox at all stays the Agent API's (its Combwork tools, `agentReadsInbox`): Advanced links to it beside them, no second
switch.
- `cw.inbox.checkpoints`: off, `noticeFor` gives no notice at the end of a tool (and doesn't count one as told).
- `cw.inbox.stopContinuation`: off, no drain: the Stop gets no reply, so Codex and Copilot aren't blocked and Claude
  Code gets no context; the turn ends as the CLI ends it.
- `cw.inbox.idleWakes`: off, `offerOnce` types no doorbell for what waits, of any kind (messages, card events and
  loop wakes, watches' wakes, decisions, mode notices). A task given now (`deliverNow`: a card started on a running
  agent, a prompt through the Agent API's `…/agents/{agent}/prompt`) and a launch's own prompt (`launchWith`) are no wakes and are typed as before. The pane's
  unread menu says nothing is typed by itself and offers **Deliver Now** (`session:deliverNow`: one offer, as asked).
  Its line put off as it is typed because what it was made from changed (#1504: a loop wake's board and lanes, which the
  card's own arrival in Review updates a moment later) is made again at once from things as they are now and typed, up
  to OVERTAKEN_TRIES times, never over the user's own typing: the retry a wake gets later types nothing with this switch
  off, so the ask would be lost. Why an asked line was put off is logged (`whyOfferFails`).
- **No delivery dropped**: with any of them off an item stays in the inbox, unread, with the overdue rules as before;
  with checkpoints and Stop continuation off an idle wake still tells the agent once its turn ends
  (`tests/carryingOn.test.ts` lists every combination by the agent's state).

**Group E's plain switches** (#1286; rows 24, 28, 29): Combwork's own handling, the same for every CLI, so each is one row
under Combwork in Advanced (no CLI's recording to check it against), defaulting to what Combwork did before:
- `cw.terminal.ctrlCVToCli` (off; at once): on, an agent pane's Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V go to the CLI as xterm sends them
  (^C, ^V), selection or not; Combwork's copy and paste stay on right-click (`shared/terminalInput.ts` `copyPasteKey`).
- `cw.journal.builds` (on; at once): off, a build of Combwork itself isn't written into the journal, and a marker left while Combwork was closed is dropped (§ the journal's Builds).
- `cw.assistant.startView` (on; at once): off, `assistantStartView` gives none, read at each start and compaction, so
  a running Assistant takes a change at its next one.
- `cw.prompt.asTyped` (off; at once): on, `sendPrompt` keeps the prompt as written: in a bracketed paste its line
  breaks go in as CR (as a terminal pastes them) and tabs and spacing are kept; typed key by key (a CLI without
  `bracketedPaste`, a slash command) each line break or tab becomes a space: Codex's prompts stay flat with the switch
  on (the Assistant's decision on #1286). Other control characters stay out either way,
  so nothing in a prompt can end a paste or press a key (`promptInput`).
- `codex.prompt.newlineKey` (HI-1327; `auto`, `spaces`, `alt-enter` or `ctrl-j`; default `auto`): with
  `cw.prompt.asTyped` on, a prompt typed into a CLI whose descriptor lists `typedNewlines` gets each line break as
  the key its adapter's `typedNewline(version)` picks.
  - **Tried in real Codex:** the real-tier suite `codex-newline` (Codex test home, its non-admin sandbox; Darren's OK, 28
    Oct) saw Alt+Enter and Ctrl+J prompts each recorded as written in one prompt by Codex 0.164.0.
  - **Gated by version:** `auto` is Alt+Enter only for a version in the adapter's `NEWLINE_TRIED` (0.164.0); another
    version, or one not known, gets spaces. A key chosen (`alt-enter`, `ctrl-j`) applies to any version. The version
    is the one the running agent was launched with (`LiveSession.cliVersion`), never the CLI installed since.
  - **Stopped part-way:** Codex's Ctrl+U deletes only to the line's start, or the line break before it at a line's
    start. So taking back a multi-line prompt Combwork stopped typing (`sendPrompt`'s catch, the same conditions as
    before: the same run, nothing the user typed since) presses Ctrl+U once for each line of it with text and once
    for each line break (`rollbackKeys`, from what `typeSegments` recorded as written). Each press is its own key,
    and none goes past Combwork's own text, so nothing of a stopped prompt can go out with a later one.
  - **Enter once drawn:** Enter waits to see the last piece with visible text drawn. With none (lines of spaces), there
    is no wait.
  - **The keys:** Codex 0.164.0's editor takes `ctrl(J)`, `ctrl(M)`, `shift(Enter)` and `alt(Enter)` as a new line;
    its composer sends only on plain Enter (`tui/src/keymap.rs`). Windows' console turns a written LF into
    Ctrl+Enter, which Codex doesn't bind. It delivers `ESC CR` as one Alt+Enter key, and win32-input-mode Ctrl+J as J
    with Ctrl (HI-1327's probe, `tests/fixtures/advanced/newline-keys-codex-0.164.0.txt`).
  - **Building the prompt:** `typedPrompt()` splits on CRLF, CR or LF, puts each line through `promptInput`'s typed
    filter (a tab becomes a space; controls and escapes are left out), and puts Combwork's fixed key between the lines
    (`TYPED_NEWLINE_KEYS`, its one source). `typeSegments` writes each key whole, checking that the agent is still
    there before each write.
  - **Unchanged:** a slash command, and the switch off, still go on one line. A user who remapped Codex's new-line keys
    chooses `spaces`. Combwork never edits Codex's config.
- `cw.prompt.clearDraft` (on; at once): off, no Ctrl+U on any of `sessions.ts`'s paths (before a prompt, taking back
  one stopped part-way, before `/compact`). Codex's `/permissions` menu steps keep theirs: the menu can't open behind
  a draft.
  - **A wrapped line stopped part-way** (HI-1974): Claude Code 2.1.312's Ctrl+U deletes only the row the cursor is on
    of a line wrapped onto several (Codex and Copilot clear the line: each tried in a 50-column terminal). A wake put
    off as it was typed (no longer wanted, the agent busy) kept its first rows in LB1's input, and the next wake was
    sent after them. A CLI whose descriptor says `ctrlUClearsRow` (Claude Code) gets the stopped line taken back with
    Backspaces instead, one for each code point Combwork wrote (`backspaceKeys`), eight to a write as typing goes. A
    Backspace deletes a character however wide it is drawn and wherever its rows wrapped, so no count of rows or
    cells is needed (a count of rows missed wide characters: HR6's round 1). Tried on 2.1.312: 150 CJK characters, an
    emoji sequence, a decomposed é and long words, pasted or typed, all cleared, and the next text went alone. A
    character of several code points can make it press a few more, which delete only a draft the switch was clearing
    anyway, and nothing in an empty input. The same guards hold: the same run, nothing the user typed since.
  - **Still checked as it is typed:** a line's `wanted()` (deliveries.ts) is asked before each piece and before Enter,
    as before: idle wakes turned off, Deliver Now made again (#1504) and a user's own task whose reason changed stop
    it part-way, and it is taken back. The suites `wakeputoff` (fake Claude Code and Codex) and `wakepaste-codex` /
    `wakepaste-copilot` (the real CLIs) hold a wrapped doorbell before its Enter (`CW_TEST_HOLD_TYPED`) and turn
    idle wakes off.
  - **A wrapped draft before Combwork types** (HI-1979; HR6's design s9, option (a)): one Ctrl+U left a wrapped draft's other
    rows in Claude Code's input, and the prompt went after them. For a `ctrlUClearsRow` CLI with an input-box reader
    (`adapter.promptBox`/`promptText`, the Advanced pattern "Screen: input box"), `clearInput` (sendPrompt and
    `/compact`) presses Ctrl+U a key at a time, each its own write, until the box reads empty. Rules:
    - **Success is only what a key of Combwork's draws now, never a box already on the screen** (HR6's round 1: a redraw
      can be late). A box read as empty gets a letter typed (`CLEAR_PROBE`, `x`: `/`, `?`, `!`, `#` and `@` each open
      something in an empty Claude Code input). The letter must show alone, then the Backspace that takes it back
      must leave the box empty. A draft drawn late shows the letter at its end instead, and is cleared with it. A
      letter left by a try that stops is taken back, unless the user has typed since.
    - **Each key must be answered within "Clearing the input: wait for each key"** (Advanced, Claude Code, 2 s): the
      box reading differently (as drawn: a deleted line break's empty row counts), or, while the box can't be read
      (a draft taller than the screen, its top rule off it), the screen changing. That can only go on, never end it.
    - **Failure refuses what was to be typed, and nothing of it is written:** a key not answered, 200 keys
      (`CLEAR_KEYS_MOST`), or a box it can't read at all. A wake is put off and tried again (retrySoon); `/compact`
      fails with the reason. The log names the cause.
    - **The guards run before every key:** the same run, and the caller's guard (wanted, idle, the user not typing,
      folder steady). The user typing mid-clear stops it, the rest of their draft theirs; nothing is taken back,
      as nothing was written. `/compact`'s guard is its run and the user typing since it began, checked before
      every key, before the command is typed and before its Enter: it fails with "You typed in the agent's
      terminal…" (HR6's round 1).
    - Codex and Copilot keep one Ctrl+U.
    - **Tried on 2.1.312:** a typed draft of four rows took four Ctrl+U, then read empty
      (`tests/fixtures/advanced/input-clear-claude-2.1.312.txt`). A multi-line paste is one row there (`[Pasted text
      #1 +44 lines]`), cleared by one.
    - **The box read is the bottom one.** "Screen: input box"'s default takes its closing rule as a lookahead, so a
      rule can close one box and open the next. A stray rule and prompt mark higher on the screen no longer swallow
      the bottom box's top rule into a span of their own, which read an old prompt as the input.
    - **The fake Claude Code draws 2.1.312's box by default** (Darren's decision on HI-1979; `fake-plain-prompt.txt`
      for the old prompt), as the real CLI keeps it:
      - only one, always at the bottom: what it prints while idle goes above the box, and a prompt sent or a turn
        begun takes it away;
      - empty under its spinner while it works (typing then goes after the busy lines, as before);
      - redrawn whole after each change, top rule included, and replaced by its own question;
      - the cursor moved back to the line's end relatively, as a line feed at the bottom scrolls.
**Group E's rows 26, 27 and 30** (#1292; Darren's choices on #1120 point 5), each as Combwork did by default, at once:
- `cw.terminal.allKeysToCli` (off): on, every key in an agent's pane goes to its CLI but the command palette's
  shortcut (Show All Commands, as the user bound it), so every command stays in reach (`appTakesTerminalKey` in
  `shared/terminalInput.ts`). A two-step palette shortcut: its first key starts the window's chord (so it no longer
  reaches the CLI alone), its second completes it while the chord is pending; any other key then goes to the CLI and
  ends the chord (HR4's round 1). Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V keep their own switch (row 24).
- `cw.terminal.osc52` (a choice: `allow` as before, `ask`, `block`): what a CLI's OSC 52 clipboard write gets, of those
  the gate takes (the pane in use, a valid payload of at most 1 MiB): written; shown to the user first, one question
  at a time, a write meanwhile refused; or refused (`osc52Decision`). A read is never answered, whatever the policy.
  The `choice` kind is Advanced's own (its values in advanced.json and the tools, their names in Settings' select).
- `cw.prompt.rawCardStart` (off): on, a card started on an agent is its title, the user's note and its description
  alone (`rawTaskPrompt`), without Combwork's wrapper (its board name, dependencies, Read first, the skill to follow). Only
  the card's start has a raw variant: wakes, deliveries and Combwork's other prompts stay wrapped (Combwork's protocol). The
  leading-dash `Task:` guard of a first prompt passed as an argument stays: without it the CLI would read an option.

**Group A's rows 1 and 7** (#1284; Darren's decision on #1120 point 3):
- **Row 1, the CLI's own setting** (`shared/cliOwnMode.ts`): a permission choice every descriptor lists last
  (`cli-own`, `cliOwn`), for an agent, a project or a provider's default like any mode, and needing no opt-in. Combwork
  passes no mode flag (Claude Code no `--permission-mode`; Codex no `-s`/`-a`/`--approve-for-me`; Copilot no mode flag
  or edit rule), so the CLI's own config decides. The session's mode is `cli-own` for the whole launch, in the window,
  the Agent API and what a restart or resume starts in (the settings'); the mode a footer, hook or status line shows is
  recorded only as seen (`modeObserved`). What depends on the mode the CLI is in reads that one (`modeInEffect`):
  Codex's reviewer answering its permission requests (`reviewed` in the status rules and the safeguard check) and the
  no-guardrails warnings (the badge, the project's warning and its sidebar mark). The badge says "CLI's own" (`short`), its tooltip that the CLI's screen shows
  the mode. No live switch to or from it (`canSwitchModeLive`): a choice restarts the session, and the running menu
  says why. The dangerous-mode confirmation doesn't apply (the user's config chose). **Never the Assistant's**: not in
  its pickers or its settings' options, one set anyway is its provider's `assistantMode` (`assistantProjectConfig`),
  and switching or restarting it into one is refused (`session.mode.assistantCliOwn`): Control relies on its mode.
  Combwork's tool pre-approval stays row 3's switch.
- **Row 7, the Assistant's other MCP servers setting**: retired by HI-1472 (§7.2, the Assistant's own choice per server in each
  workspace). No longer listed; kept in advanced.json (`LEGACY_ADVANCED`, never "unknown") only so a workspace opened
  later moves an "on" to its choices. Its CLI's own servers follow that CLI's `mcpIsolation` either way. Control governs
  only Combwork's tools; another server's ask per the CLI.

**Group B's rows 10–14** (#1285; Darren's decisions on #1120 point 4 and on #1285):
- **Row 10, Combwork's hooks: no switch and no hooks-free mode** (Darren, 21 Oct): Combwork's hooks are how it knows what an
  agent is doing (its status, waiting for you, file locks, the lines Combwork types and their taking, inbox notices, a new
  Codex conversation's id); without them it isn't Combwork, and a user who can't run them is better served by a plain
  terminal. Mapped on #1285: without the hooks no status reaches Combwork at all, since its screen readings only follow a
  turn a hook opened. Claude Code's `--settings` merge stays as it is (§6.1: the user's settings and hooks kept, the
  allowlists widened for Combwork's), and `disableAllHooks: true` stays refused, the message saying why and what to change
  (`providers.settings.hooksOff`). Hooks that stop arriving later are said by the hooks health check (#1336, §6.3).
- **Row 11, Codex's hooks: no switch**, nothing to keep (Darren, 21 Oct). Codex keeps each config layer's hooks
  apart: the user's (their `config.toml`, keyed by that file) and Combwork's (`-c hooks.<event>`, the session flags'
  `C:\<session-flags>\config.toml:<event>:0:0`) both run, and Combwork's `-c hooks.state` table merges into the user's, whose
  trust records stay (Codex 0.163.0, its app server's `hooks/list`). Combwork names only its own keys. `codexownhooks`
  asks the installed Codex, so a Codex that starts displacing them fails there; a unit test pins Combwork's keys. A
  `-c hooks.<event>` in the user's Extra arguments comes after Combwork's and replaces Combwork's for that event.
- **Row 12, `claude-code.override.statusLine`** ("Combwork's status line in place of yours", on; sessions started
  afterwards): off, the status line in the user's Claude Code settings (the first scope that sets a command one,
  highest first: managed, their `--settings`, the project's local and shared files, theirs; `ownStatusLine`) runs after
  Combwork's: `curl … "<hook URL>&statusline&echo" | (`, their command on lines of its own, then `)`, with their padding.
  Combwork's hook server answers the `echo` form with the JSON it was sent, so their command gets Claude Code's input whole
  on stdin, and its output is the status line; Combwork still reads the status. Claude Code runs status lines with bash (Git
  Bash on Windows): the subshell on its own lines keeps any command that runs alone whole (a comment at its end, several
  lines), tested by running the chain in Git's bash. With none of theirs, Combwork's alone. `claudestatusline` checks it on
  the real Claude Code (2.1.306).
- **Row 13, `cw.guidance`** (each connection's since HI-2670, §11.2's Launch settings; "Combwork's guidance for agents", on; sessions started afterwards), separate from Settings →
  Agent API → Provide Combwork tools, without which there is no guidance either: off, project agents get Combwork's tools
  without it: `sessions.combworkGuidance` gives none (Codex's `developer_instructions`, Copilot's custom instructions), and
  the combwork server answers `initialize` with no `instructions` (`CW_GUIDANCE=0`). On Codex, Combwork's guidance (and the
  Assistant's role) now follow the `developer_instructions` Codex itself would give the session, instead of replacing
  them. Combwork parses no profile and ranks no layer (the Assistant's design on #1285, after three rounds of corners):
  Codex renders the session's prompt offline with the agent's own Extra arguments in its folder (`debug prompt-input`,
  no sign-in or model), twice side by side, as is and with `-c developer_instructions=""` (an empty value clears every
  layer below it). What the first's developer message has in front of the second's is the value; the same renders mean
  none (missing, empty or blank); anything else, or a render failing or passing `codex.promptInput.timeoutSeconds`
  (Advanced, 15 s), means Combwork can't tell (`developerInstructionsOf`). It is read at every launch Combwork adds some to,
  with the launch's own Extra arguments, folder and environment, never cached (only Codex knows what it depends on:
  `-C`, ancestors, managed layers), about 200 ms. Combwork's combined value is the last `-c developer_instructions` on the
  command, after the Extra arguments, so a user's own `-c`/`--config developer_instructions=…` there is in it and never
  overrides it. **Never anything in place of an unread value** (the Assistant's decisions on #1285): Codex unable to say,
  an agent gets no override at all (its own apply, without Combwork's guidance) and the Assistant its role alone (without it
  there is no Assistant), each with a notice once per agent and folder while Combwork runs (`launchNotice`). What Combwork keeps
  between a launch's preparation and its command is bounded (the latest 16). `codexownhooks` checks the reading against
  the installed Codex at every layer (the user's, a selected profile in each form Codex takes, a trusted and an untrusted
  project), each missing, empty, blank or set: Codex 0.163.0 gives a trusted project's over the profile's over the
  user's, an empty one clearing those below it, and refuses two profiles. With none of Combwork's, Combwork passes nothing and
  Codex's own apply. Combwork never writes Codex's config.
- **Row 14, the Assistant's role and its guidance: no switch** (Darren, on #1120 point 4): the Assistant is its role and
  its Control; without them it is no Assistant, only an agent. `cw.guidance` doesn't reach it.

### 16.16 Other 1.0 rules

- **Resume's busy state** [#1177]: every button that starts a session (Resume, Resume All, Start, the Sessions tab,
  the Assistant's panel, tiles, the agent list) is disabled and shows that it's working ("Resuming…") from the click
  until the launch; a launch never waits for the one-time usage import.
- **Translations** [#1117 c]: every phase ships its text in all 7 locales in the same change, using
  `locales/glossary-1.0.md`; a final review (#1126) before 1.0.0.
- **Logical CSS** in every new 1.0 rule (#908) [#1117 c6].
- **Stable user-guide anchors** (#860) and **builds as facts** (#1062) in P8 [#1124 c].
- **Every phase ends with an RC** for Darren to install, except P2 (a spike with no UI) [#1112 release plan, #1118].
  **Changed** [Darren, 21 and 22 Oct]: P3–P7 ended with checks only, and the first install is the 1.0 baseline at P8's
  end (#1288, §16.19).

### 16.17 Upgrading to 1.0

[#1112 plan, #1122 c, #1123 tpl, #704, #1025; P1, answering HB3's round 1 findings 1, 7 and 9]

**The migration.** One upgrade, backed up first (`db.ts`, `.combwork/backups`): card tables, keys and aliases, the fact
log, actions, rulesets, typed tables for sessions, lanes, watches and deliveries. **Built as several steps that run as
one** [Darren, 20 Oct, #1119 decision 3]: each part is its own step in the board's **1.0 group** (`Migration.group:
'1.0'`, `BOARD_MIGRATIONS`; P3's steps each take the next version as they merge), and a file that needs any step of the
group runs **all of its pending steps in one transaction**, after one ask, one backup and one exclusive lock: to the
user it is one upgrade, and a crash leaves the file at 0.9. The group's first step (#1207, v3) records
`board_meta.format = 1.0`. A new file has nothing to upgrade: it takes every step unasked. So does a file in the group
already (at or past its first version), for the group's later steps: it was asked when it joined, or made by 1.0, and
they run under the group's lock with an ordinary copy before them (HI-1718: a board an earlier release candidate
upgraded waited for the upgrade again, as if from 0.9, and failed to open). **The cards step** (#1209,
v5, `schema/cardsStep.ts`) moves every card out of its JSON document into #1208's tables (typed columns in `cards`,
labels, links, context, comments, history, decisions and holds in child tables), checks each card composes back to its
document byte for byte before the group commits (a card that doesn't, or a row that isn't a card's document, stops the
upgrade naming the card, and the file stays 0.9), and drops the documents: from then on the board's readers compose
each card's JSON from its rows (`schema/cardRows.ts`), the same bytes as before, so the Agent API's cards and Export
Board are unchanged. A 0.9 board waiting for its upgrade is read from its documents as before. Sessions and deliveries move from `store_rows` into
typed tables (#1211, v6, the last of its stores: `store_rows` goes with it), every record read back equal as JSON;
deliveries keep their in-memory store (published after each transaction), the table its durable copy [Darren, 20 Oct,
#1211].
- **Before it runs, Combwork asks** ("Upgrade this workspace's board to 1.0? Combwork 1.0 needs to upgrade this workspace's
  data. Version 0.9 can then no longer open it; a backup of the board is kept, and Help → Restore the 0.9 Board Backup…
  puts it back. Back up first: there's no going back to 0.9.3 once your agents' worktrees become slots." [the Assistant
  for Darren, #1207 20 Oct; reworded on #1209, Darren 20 Oct: the cards step drops the cards' documents, which 0.9
  reads; its last sentence since the upgrade is one-way, Darren 22 Oct on #1123]). Until the user agrees, the board opens read-only, as for a newer
  file (writes refused with "This board is from version 0.9: it is read-only until it is upgraded to 1.0"; what would
  change a card is off, saying why in its tooltip: the board's add-card buttons, dragging cards, a card's menu but Open, the
  card dialog's fields, Save, Start…, Archive, Delete, comments and decisions, with the reason as a banner in the dialog
  [#1230]; for a newer file too), with a banner at the top of the window offering **Upgrade…**; **Not Now** holds
  until Combwork starts again. A test copy (unpackaged, `CW_TEST_BOARD_UPGRADE=yes|no`) answers before it is asked
  [#1207]. **Meanwhile nothing that `combwork.db` must record starts** [HR1's #1207 round 1 finding 1]: the whole file is
  read-only, so an agent's or the Assistant's start (every path: a click, Resume All, the Agent API, the Assistant) is
  refused before anything runs ("This workspace is from version 0.9: upgrade it to 1.0 before starting agents"), and
  reading the workspace's stores moves no old file in (a host's `sessions.json` waits for the upgrade). The workspace
  stays open for reading; the banner says the board is read-only and agents can't start, and New Session and Resume in
  the session view and the agent's menus are off with that as their tooltip [#1230]. The opening's steps that write the
  board (the merge queues, the cards', lanes' and watches' project ids, the projects' keys, archiving old Done cards,
  ending the reviews of sessions that ended, sweeping idle skill copies, the adoption) skip it quietly, logging nothing,
  and **run once the upgrade completes**, in the same session (`onBoardUpgraded`) [#1621: the merge queues had failed
  with "no such table: card_facts" and started only after a restart]. **Nothing else runs against it either** (HI-1694,
  `boardWaits()`): the line updater passes over a workspace whose board waits (it had failed with "no such table: lanes"
  on every agent's change in another window), metrics keep what they observe unsaved ("attempt to write a readonly
  database"), and the opening's board steps (the stage repair too) wait for the upgrade. **The opening shows its steps**
  (HI-1694): from the click until the window shows the workspace, and from Upgrade until the adoption and the slots are
  done, a steady view over the window names the workspace and the step (reading its projects; upgrading its board, the
  0.9 board kept as a backup; adopting its cards and projects; adopting its agents' worktrees as slots), and the window
  opens, makes or closes no other workspace meanwhile (refused, saying why). The log says when the board waits for the
  question, times each schema step and the copy before them, the upgrade, and each step of the opening. **Every open
  shows the workspace as soon as its projects are read** (HI-1705: an ordinary open took 4–11 s while other windows'
  agents kept main's file calls queued): what it reads for the window is read at once, not one after another (the
  projects, each project's parts, its agents), and its bundled skills and modes (§7.1) are brought up to date after the
  window has it, in the background; an agent's launch waits for them, and the .combwork folder is watched once they are (a
  watched folder can't be swapped on Windows). What the open starts in the background is timed, each part, in one
  "after opening" line of the log once all have ended. **When the file is replaced
  under the services** (the upgrade, Restore) [HR1's round 2 finding]: what they keep from it in memory (deliveries,
  card watches, metrics, lanes' and sessions' "moved in" marks) was read before, and a 0.9 may have written since
  (while the upgrade waited), so each reads it again from the file as it is then; the workspace database's
  **generation** (`dbGeneration`) moves on, and a save made from something read in an older generation is refused
  (`saveStore`'s guard), never written over the file.
- **No other Combwork may have the workspace open while it runs** [HB3's round 2 finding D, HR2's round 2 finding 10].
  0.9.x writes no workspace presence marker, and its single-instance lock is per profile (`index.ts:115`), so the dev
  and installed Combwork can't see each other that way. What every running Combwork does hold is a connection to the
  workspace's `combwork.db` for as long as the workspace is open. So the migration opens `combwork.db` with SQLite's
  `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` and takes the exclusive lock **for the whole migration**, not one transaction: SQLite grants
  it only when no other connection has the file open, and while it is held no other process can open it. If it can't
  be had, the migration doesn't start and says "Another Combwork has this workspace open: close it first". After the
  migration, a 0.9 opening the file sees a newer schema and opens it read-only (`db.ts:147`), but **can't read its
  board** [Darren, 20 Oct, #1209 option 1]: its cards are no longer JSON documents (0.9.3 prepares `SELECT doc` and
  `INSERT … doc` as it opens the board), so it says "The board couldn't be opened"; the way back is Restore, below. The stores' steps (#1211, #1212) likewise
  leave 0.9 nothing it can read [the same decision]. P3
  proves this with a two-process test (a 0.9 build holding the workspace, a 1.0 build migrating; and a 0.9 build
  started *during* the migration, recording what it shows the user, which the RC notes then describe) before relying
  on it; if SQLite's lock can't be relied on for the WAL setup Combwork uses, the fallback is a presence marker added to
  0.9.x (now a 0.9.4 patch, 0.9.3 being released), which is outside this lane and needs Darren's say (OP-41).
  **The group's copy is kept for good** (`combwork-before-1.0-v<n>-<time>.db`, a family of its own that `BACKUPS_KEPT`
  never prunes) [#1207].
- From 1.0 on, every Combwork also writes a **workspace presence marker** (`.combwork/open/<profile>.json`, pid and a
  heartbeat), so later migrations and the queue's lock have a second signal. [#1207] `<profile>` is the profile
  folder's name and a hash of its path; the heartbeat is renewed every 30 s while the board is open, the file removed as
  it closes, and a marker is stale once its heartbeat is 90 s old or its process is gone. The upgrade refuses, as for
  SQLite's lock, while another profile's fresh marker exists.
- **A way back:** Help → **Restore the 0.9 Board Backup…** puts the pre-migration backup back (after its own backup of
  the 1.0 file), for a user who returns to 0.9.x; the RC notes say so. Nothing is deleted. [#1207] It brings back the
  board's cards and their history only: once slots have moved agents' worktrees, nothing promises that 0.9.3 carries on
  with worktrees, sessions or lanes (Darren, 22 Oct on #1123: the upgrade is one-way; the release notes say to back up
  first). The 1.0 file is
  copied first by a connection holding the file's exclusive lock (refused, as the upgrade is, while another Combwork has it
  open), kept for good as `combwork-before-restore-v<n>-<time>.db`; the board is closed, the 0.9 copy put in its place,
  and the board opened again: read-only in the 1.0 build (its upgrade waiting again), writable for 0.9. The copy put
  back is the newest of the group's family **made before the group's first step**, its file checked to be a 0.9 board
  (a schema before the group); the copy before a later step of the group, on a board in the group already, is an
  ordinary one of the file's three [HR1's round 1 finding 2]. Refused while any of the workspace's agents (or its
  Assistant) runs or starts: the board put back takes no writes here, so they would go on unrecorded.
- **Two copies of Combwork on one workspace** (the dev and the installed one, after the migration): both observe the platform, so
  an observation is deduplicated as **the same transition**, not the same value [HR2's round 2 finding 7, HB3's G]:
  every observed fact names the observed fact it follows for that card and kind (`prev`: its seq, or the cycle's
  `Started` for the first), and (card, kind, prev) is unique. Two processes seeing the same change compute the same
  `prev`, so the second write is a no-op; a real later change (A→B→A→B) follows a different fact and is written.
  **When the write conflicts** (another process already wrote a fact after the same `prev`), the loser never drops
  its view or writes an old snapshot: it reads the fact that won and the platform's state **now**. If the state now
  equals the winner's `to`, nothing more is written; if it differs, it writes a new fact following the winner (`prev`
  = the winner's seq) with the state it has just read. So when one observer saw B and the other C (both from A), the
  log reads A→B→C or A→C→B with C or B as the current state, whichever is true now, never a missed or stale value
  [HR2's round 3 finding 2]. An
  observed `Integrated` is also unique per cycle and entry (card, the cycle's `Started` seq, entry id or revision), so
  reopening a card and merging the same revision in a new cycle is recorded again.
  - **One key for every observed fact** [P2]: the store keeps a dedupe key per observed fact, unique per card and
    kind: `prev:<seq>` for transitions (`HeadMoved`), `cycle:<seq>` for an observed `Integrated`, `commit:<id>` for
    `CommitAttributed`, the mark's own (`part:<cycle>:<revision>`, `left:<cycle>:<target head>`), and for a pass's
    `Stale` and `CarriedOver` the head observation they follow (`stale:`, `carried:`, `back:<cycle>:<HeadMoved seq>`,
    #1623: a line away, back and away to the same commit again is observed each time). One unique
    index covers them all.
  - **The view comes first** [P2]: an observer takes the fact it follows (its view of the log) **before** it reads the
    platform. Read after, a loser that saw B would find the winner's C as its `prev` and write C→B, a stale value
    following the winner: the race S62 describes, which the spike's test hit until the order was fixed.

**Old cards** (§16.4.1): Done, On Hold and Todo cards get no facts (**before 1.0**). Cards in flight get evidence, never
an invented history:

| At the upgrade | Gets | So that |
|---|---|---|
| Doing | `Adopted` (agent, folder, line, head, base = merge base with the target) | it can be submitted. |
| Review | `Adopted` and an **adopted submission**: a `Submitted` fact marked `source: observed, adopted: true` at the line's head, with endpoints and keys computed then | its reviewer reviews that revision as usual. If the head isn't what the builder meant, the review says so. |
| Passed | `Adopted` with `passedBefore1_0: true` (what the column said), **no `Verdict`**: a pass can't be tied to a revision history doesn't prove | under the upgrade's options (G5 Not checked, below) nothing needs a verdict: the builder reports its merge or the user moves it. A later stricter ruleset applies only from the next card [#1112 down]. |

The adoption (#1218, `workflow/adoption.ts`) runs in the background once the migration has committed, and again at each
start until it has handled every card once (board_meta `adoption`). It handles only the cards from before 1.0: the
upgrade's transaction records the highest card number (board_meta `adoption_upto`; 0 on a board made by 1.0, which so
adopts nothing), so a card made since is never marked. Archived cards, workspace cards and the cards of a project no
longer in the workspace are **before 1.0** whatever their column. A card's folder is its agent's worktree (target: the
branch it came from) or the project folder (target: its branch); git is read outside the board's lock. `Adopted` keeps
the folder's head as observed (`head`, null when unknown) apart from `base`, and the fold's head is that head (a
`Started` fact's head is its base). Each card is checked again inside the change that writes it: one started, adopted
or marked meanwhile (by another Combwork, or a rerun) is left as it is; one changed meanwhile (moved, archived, given another
agent, its agent's folder changed) is never written from the stale reads but classified again by another run (up to
three in a row, else at the next start), and the adoption isn't finished until none is left. So it is safe to repeat
and to run in two copies of Combwork at once, and a project's options are written only when project.json has none. Nothing moves on
the board: each adopted card is already at the stage its column stands for. A project's agents count as reviewer agents
when a role or name says *review*.

**Options at the upgrade** [#1122 c: "options matching how they work today, so nothing changes overnight"]:
- Git projects get Git with G5 **Not checked**, G11 as their agents work (slots if any agent has a worktree, else the
  project folder), every check off, and **G1 = A reviewer agent if the project has reviewer agents or a lane**, else No
  review. None projects get None, with N1 the same way. (Everything off would hide the Review and Approved stages that
  running lanes are in, HB3's finding 1.)
- **A stage stays visible while any card is in it,** even if the options no longer produce it; the card finishes under
  its own ruleset.
- A one-time notice offers the presets. This reads the clean cut-over as "everyone moves to the layer at once, no warn
  mode", with options starting where the project is (OP-22). **Built [#1278]:** a banner after the upgrade names the
  projects with no preset chosen; **Choose…** opens the first one's Project Settings → Workflow, **Not Now** dismisses
  it. Either answer is recorded in `board_meta` (`workflow.presetsNotice`), so it shows once per workspace, and never on
  a board made by 1.0 (no card from before it: `adoption_upto` 0).
- **[#1423]** Only projects from before 1.0 get the upgrade's options: those whose project.json records no platform
  (Combwork records it as it makes a project.json, which no version before 1.0 did), whatever the board (an upgraded board
  with no cards included). A project made by 1.0 gets none, and asks "How do you work?" (§16.3.5) instead.
- **[HI-1697] The merge style and commit message are asked, never set silently.** A Git project given the upgrade's
  options is marked `mergeAsk` in project.json's `workflow` (for good). Its question is open while it has the mark and
  the board has no choice recorded for it (board meta `workflow:<project>:mergeChoice`). Its first card to reach the
  merge queue (once the project has Combwork merge it, a preset or a save later) pauses the queue (`mergeChoice`) with a
  Decide on the card in For you: "How should Combwork merge <project>'s cards into <target>?", with G6 (Merge commit, as
  until now; Squash; Rebase and fast-forward) and G19 (Combwork's, as until now; the branch's own; not shown with Rebase)
  and **Save and Carry On Merging** (`workflow:chooseMerge`).
  **The board records the choice atomically; the file follows it and is repaired on start.** The answer and a Workflow
  save that chooses (changes G6 or G19 as they resolve, while the question is open) are one function
  (`saveWorkflowOptions`), under the repository's lock and in its turn of workflow writes, and the options are checked
  against the project's as they are now, as any save is. Then one change of the board (its lock and transaction, which
  every answer, move and retirement of a request takes, from this Combwork or another): an answer's request checked still
  open, of the gate and bound to the card's open queue entry (else refused, nothing written: a stale dialog, or one
  answered or retired while the save waited); the choice recorded, its file write pending; the cards' rules (Overrides
  under the chosen options: an answer's, the project's cards in flight; a save's, those ticked and the card waiting
  with the question); then the request answered as the user, or the question closed. Only once that has committed is
  project.json written (G6 and G19 over its options as they are, the rest kept), and the record marked written. Stopped
  inside the board's change, nothing is kept and the question is still open. Stopped after its commit, the waiting
  card already merges by its Override's style, and a pending record is written to project.json at the workspace's
  open, before the queue goes on (`QueueConfig.settle`, which then reads the options again, so the merge's G19 is the
  one chosen; a save still writing it holds the same locks, so the queue waits for it) and before the next save. Once
  chosen, a project's saves are ordinary ones and the record never takes them back (it is written to the file only
  while pending). The queue then lifts its pause, closes any question still open, and merges the card as chosen.
  Answered in words, the queue asks again. A project marked with no card in the queue is never interrupted. Projects
  upgraded before HI-1697 have no mark.

**Agents' old moves, for one transition** [HB3's finding 7]: from P4 until P8 rewrites the skills, an agent's
`cw_update_task` column move is translated into the matching intent instead of refused: `review` → submit, `passed`
→ verdict pass (on the latest submission, by its reviewer), `done` → report merge, `doing` → start; each through the
same guards, and its reply names the intent to use next time. P4 also updates the lines of card-loop, merge-ready,
work-on-card and review-agent-work that its gates change (columns → intents), so the guidance agents follow on the P4
and later RCs matches what ships; P8 then shrinks the skills to describe the rules [P1]. **Built [#1268]:** a project
agent's `cw_update_task` (its own token) with the rules enforced, on a card from 1.0: `column` `doing`, `review`,
`passed`, `done` and `todo` are start, submit (the comment its summary), a passing verdict on the latest submission (its
review started first), report merge and put back (the comment its why); `review` `start`, `passed` and `failed` are start
review and a verdict on the latest submission (§16.8.1), the comment the verdict's, a failed card back in Active as the
verdict moves it. Each on the board's one intent path (`runIntent`), so the runtime's guards decide (a refusal is
§16.8.3's, the Agent API's `409`) and the card's 0.9 fields follow; the change's other fields go with its first write,
its comment with the write recording the intent. The short reply adds "As submit: next time call cw_submit". A batch
translates each card's; a card an agent creates in Doing, Review or Passed is made in Todo and moved by its intent in
one change (in a column its rules lack, made there as before: HR2's round 2). **Every new cycle is a start, through Start's guards** [HR2's #1268 round 1]: from Todo, a Done card moved
back to Doing (reopened: back to Todo and started in one write), a card On Hold never started, and a start naming
another agent (started for it: its builder). **Each translation is one write** (a verdict with the review it starts),
undone whole when refused or failing part way, the comment checked before anything is read or written. P3's path
stays for: a column the card's ruleset lacks (Review with no review), a review there, and any move of a card in such a
column or On Hold while being worked on (as the user's moves, until the skills use the intents); a move back into
Doing from Review or Passed (fixes or more work in the same cycle: nothing started, no rule to skip); a move to the
column a card is in (but a failed card from before returned to Review is its submission); another agent's card in
Doing moved on (P3's refusal); scripts (the workspace token); cards from before 1.0 until they start, their start
itself the runtime's (as the user's, §16.7.1; HI-1966); and every agent move with the rules off (§16.6.6). An adopted card's stage is its column's until a rule moves it (no `Moved`
written at adoption): the runtime folds a card's facts from its cached stage, so an adopted card's intents work (S40).
With the old moves translated, a lane's next card waits until the one before it is Done (§16.11.2, OP-36) also for
a builder following today's card-loop skill: its move of the next card to Doing is refused (`lane.oneAtATime`) until it
reports the previous one merged (#1274's skill lines say so).

**Other:** templates v1 wiped; agents' worktrees become slots (§16.10.8, **Built [#1441]**: adopted in place, renamed later
with Repair's steps, one-way); keys suggested (§16.12).

#### 16.19.2 Agent worktrees between cards (P4–P6)

**In 1.0** [#1579, the Assistant's call]: this applies only to a lane carried over the upgrade on its builder's 0.9
worktree (S56, #1441's carried leases), which runs there until it ends. 1.0 adds no worktree agents, and a lane on slots
gives each card a line of its own, so nothing moves (S54 and S55 since #1573). The e2e suite `linecarried` covers it on
the dev build, with a 0.9 worktree builder made through the test channel: a merge commit, two squashes (the builder
busy, then the worktree dirty) and a commit made past approval.

[P1, answering HB3's round 3 finding 2 and HR2's round 3 finding 3] In agent-worktree mode a builder's branch carries
on from card to card, so after each Done Combwork checks, **before the lane's next card starts**, that the branch is an
ancestor of the target (a merge commit or a fast-forward leaves it so). If it isn't (a squash):
1. **Wait for a safe moment:** the builder's session isn't in a turn (idle, or stopped), and no run of it is going in
   the worktree; the lane shows "waiting: bringing HI-B1's branch up to date".
2. **Check what would be lost:** every commit on the branch since the card's base must be in the target by the
   squashed card's replay (§16.3.2: the squash commit replays the card's change), and the worktree must be clean
   (no staged, unstaged or untracked-not-ignored files). Anything else, such as a commit made after the card was
   approved, stops here: the lane pauses with "HI-B1's branch has work that isn't in main: <commits>", For you
   (Decide), and nothing moves.
3. **Move it:** today's `moveBranchTo` (`git reset --keep <target>`, `worktrees.ts:479`), which git refuses rather than
   overwrite a local change; it is recorded as a `LineMoved` fact (§16.4.2) on the card just Done, written **before** the
   next card's `Started`, whose `base` is the `to` of that fact [HB3's round 4, HR2's round 4].
4. If git refuses, the lane pauses with git's reason; nothing else is tried.

So two squashed cards in a row each review only their own work (S54, S55).

**Built [#1271]:** the runtime refuses the lane's next card's start while its builder's own worktree (the last card
before it in the lane worked there, Done) has a head not in that card's target (`lane.lineBehind`, 7 locales; the user's
drag isn't refused), and Combwork's line updater (`workflow/lineUpdates.ts`, after board changes and an agent's status
changes, one pass per workspace at a time) does the steps above between cards: the builder busy (in a turn, starting,
asking a permission, its background tasks running, or a prompt not yet taken), a Progress run of it going, or the
worktree dirty, the lane's `status` is `lineUpdate` ("waiting: bringing the builder's branch up to date", not pausing;
the Progress panel's lane header says so, #1287);
the line's change since the card's approved base not in the target (containment, as `done.contained` checks it), a For
you **Decide** on the next card naming the commits after the approved revision; git's refusal, a For you **Decide** with
git's reason. Each is asked once for the branch's head (bound to it), so a branch nobody touches isn't asked about twice.
The move goes through the platform (`lineNow`, `moveLine`: `git reset --keep`), then `LineMoved` on the card just Done
and a wake to the builder ("<line> is up to date with <target> …: <next> can start"); the next card's start then reads
its base as `LineMoved.to`. **The move is checked again at its boundary** [HR2's round 1]: just before it, the line,
its head and the target's head are read again (the worktree still clean), and the rules on, the switch (or the user's
approval), the builder idle with no run and the workspace open checked again. The platform's move [HR2's round 2] is
serialized with the worktree's own git work: it holds the worktree's index lock (a commit or other git write there
meanwhile is refused by git, nothing lost), checks the branch, head, target head and a clean worktree under it, asks
those conditions once more at that boundary, brings the files from the head's tree to the target's through a separate
index (`read-tree -m -u`, which won't overwrite a local change), then moves the branch only if it is still at that
head (`update-ref <to> <head>`, compare and swap; else the files go back and nothing moves). Never a reset of a branch
that may have moved on. Anything changed: nothing moves or is recorded, and the next pass looks again. While the move
runs, the next card is reserved: its start is refused (`lane.lineBehind`, also inside its own write) until the
`LineMoved` is saved, and a `LineMoved` that can't be saved has the move undone the same way. **A failure after the
move's first change** [HR2's round 3] is put back conditionally: the new index is staged in the held lock and published
only once the branch has moved (a refused rename tried a few times); unpublished, the branch is swapped back (only if
still where the move put it) and the files restored from that index. A `LineMoving` fact is written before the move
and its outcome after it: `LineMoved`, or `LineMoveUndone` when nothing was made (the platform put everything back).
One with no outcome (a move that couldn't be put back, or Combwork stopping during it) holds the next card wherever the head
is [HR2's round 4: a head back where it began proves nothing of the files and index]; the next pass records `LineMoved`
once the line is at its target and clean, `LineMoveUndone` once it is back where it began and clean, else asks the user
once (For you, Decide), that question the unfinished move's (answered, it doesn't stop the next move). What waits is each workspace's own (forgotten when it closes). **Settings → Advanced → Bring an agent's branch up to date after a squash merge**
(`cw.workflow.updateAgentBranch`, default on): off, the user is asked every time, a For you **Approve** on the next
card (approve: Combwork moves it once, by the steps above; decline: the user does it). With workflow rules off, nothing
moves, nothing is asked and nothing waits: P3's behaviour (Darren's decision on #1120, point 2; the Assistant on #1271),
and the Merge dialog's squash still moves the branch itself, as before 1.0 (tested).

So the contradiction "Combwork merges and the agent merges need each card in its own folder" (§16.7.2) is met before P7
by an agent's worktree, and "Committed is done" still needs the project folder.

Git capabilities found missing go into the phase that needs them or On Hold labelled git-support [#1117 git]
(P1's list: §16.20's last table).

| OP-41 | The migration detects a running 0.9 by SQLite's exclusive lock (§16.17). If P3's two-process test shows that can't be relied on, add a workspace presence marker to 0.9.3 (a fix on main, merged forward)? | **Agreed [#1117 20 Oct].** Yes, only if needed; P3 reports which. |

**Git support (P1's list)** [#1117 git]. Capabilities the spec needs, and where they go:

| Capability | Where |
|---|---|
| Patch-id sameness, squash containment, refs watcher | P3 (in scope) |
| `mergeWorktree` returns the merge commit, takes a target, no auto-commit; cross-process merge lock | P5 (in scope) |
| Branches shown next to their cards and revisions | P6 (in scope). **Built [#1424]:** Branches & remotes shows, on each branch a card's current cycle works on (`WorkBadge.line`), that card (the one in flight, else the latest; how many earlier), its stage (its project's name, its category's colour), in Review the revision under review (`WorkBadge.underReview`, copyable) and, Done, merged with `Integrated`'s result; the cards of a reused branch by when each one's current cycle started (never by a later fact). Worktrees name their agent's card (Doing, else Review, else Passed) the same way, whatever they have checked out |
| Push the target after Combwork merges (an option) | **Built [#1179]:** G18 (§16.6.1, §16.9.1's push after the merge) |
| Update a branch from its target (merge or rebase) as a user action in the Version Control tab | **Built [HI-1180]** (rc.4): Branches & remotes' Update from <target> (§8) |
| Conflict help on a returned card (the conflicting files and hunks from the test merge) | **Built [HI-1181]** (rc.4): the Work section's hunks and the wake's places (§16.9.1, Combwork's commits) |
| Submodules and Git LFS in slots and review copies | On Hold, git-support: #1182 |
| Remote targets: fetch before testing, push after (Team with a shared remote) | On Hold, git-support: #1183 |
| Rebase and fast-forward as a merge style | **Built [#1184]:** G6's third value (§16.9.1 step 4, linear landing) |
| Signed queue commits without a prompt | On Hold, git-support: #1185 |
| Pin refs for submitted revisions; hooks and signing pauses in the queue; Combwork's commit identity | P5 (in scope, §16.9) |
